roles.title: Electrical and Electronics Installers and Repairers, Transportation Equipment
roles.description: Install, adjust, or maintain mobile electronics communication equipment, including sound, sonar, security, navigation, and surveillance systems on trains, watercraft, or other mobile equipment.

tasks.label: Inspect and test electrical systems and equipment to locate and diagnose malfunctions, using visual inspections, testing devices, and computer software.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail maintenance shop/depot: a locomotive or transit railcar is written up with an electrical fault (door control circuit, HVAC, cab signaling, PA/CCTV, lighting, propulsion control). Technician reads schematics, plugs a laptop into the vehicle's diagnostic network, then physically opens control cabinets, checks connectors and relays, and probes points with a multimeter under-car, on the roof, and in the cab to isolate the failure.

Marine electronics service aboard a vessel at a dock, marina, or boatyard: intermittent radar/GPS/VHF/autopilot/sounder or DC-power fault on a boat of unique layout and age. Technician crawls into lockers, helm consoles, and engine spaces, inspects for corrosion, chafe and water ingress, and tests wiring, grounds, antennas and NMEA networks with meters and analyzers.

Fleet garage or upfitter bay: bus, transit van, emergency vehicle, or heavy truck with a malfunctioning mobile-electronics system (camera/DVR, two-way radio, lightbar, farebox, GPS/telematics, security system). Vehicle parked in a bay; technician runs scan-tool/PC diagnostics, then traces harnesses behind panels and probes circuits to find the fault.

Bench work in the shop: a removed unit — control module, printed circuit board, radio, display, power supply — is brought to a test bench, connected to a test set or interface adapter, powered and stimulated, and tested to confirm the fault and localize it to a component or sub-assembly before repair or scrap.

In-service / field emergency troubleshooting: train disabled on the line or in a station, vessel with dead electronics at anchor or underway, or a vehicle down at a remote site. Technician works in poor light, weather, and time pressure with hand test gear to find the malfunction quickly enough to restore service.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers (e.g., 4080)
sources.title: Flying Probe Tester for electronic boards PCB | SPEA
sources.claim: Commercial automatic flying-probe testers physically move measurement probes to contact points on an electronic board and are used not only for post-assembly test but for troubleshooting defective units and verifying repairs, generating in-circuit test programs automatically from CAD data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is board/unit-level electrical fault localization in electronics manufacturing rather than on transportation equipment; it transfers to the bench-test instance because the object (a removed PCB/module of the same class found in rail and marine electronics), the measurements (continuity, resistance, voltage, component values) and the output (fault isolated to a component) are the same, and the machine performs the probing itself.

sources.system: SPEA Board Handling Equipment with 4080 flying probe tester
sources.title: SPEA 4080: 8-Probe Flying Probe Tester | SPEA
sources.claim: Flying-probe test cells are supplied with automatic board handling equipment that loads and unloads units under test without an operator, allowing unattended test runs.
sources.transferJustification: Supports the 'limited intervention' requirement for the bench-test instance: the unit under test is presented to the machine automatically in a purpose-built cell, as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: Seica Pilot 4D V8 'Pass Through' flying probe tester
sources.title: Flying Probe Tester "Pass Through" Pilot 4D V8 - Automatic Test Equipment | Seica Spa
sources.claim: Seica flying probe testers are offered in fully automated configurations with magazine loaders that feed boards through the tester without manual loading.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the SPEA items: automated in-circuit probing and fault localization on removed electronic assemblies, with the work presented to the machine by an automated handler.

sources.system: Automated Bench Test Equipment (BTE/CABTE)
sources.title: Automated Bench Test Equipment | Wabtec Corporation
sources.claim: Rail-industry automated bench test equipment automatically sequences electrical and electro-mechanical stimulation of a locomotive/railcar unit under test through custom interface test adapters and troubleshoots the fault to the module or sub-component level.
sources.transferJustification: Directly in-domain (rail electronic modules) but bench-level: the unit is fixtured onto an interface test adapter and the equipment runs the diagnostic sequence, matching the bench-test instance's start-to-accepted-output (fault isolated to module/sub-component).

sources.system: ANYmal quadruped inspection robot (with Stadler Service AG)
sources.title: Exploring the future of train maintenance with robots - ANYbotics
sources.claim: The most advanced legged inspection robot work in train maintenance is exploratory data collection alongside and beneath stationary rolling stock; the partnership is framed as exploring potential rather than performing electrical fault diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the frontier for on-vehicle inspection: the robot captures inspection data on rolling stock but no source shows it locating and diagnosing an electrical malfunction with test instruments.

sources.system: Spot with thermal/visual payload (Consumers Energy substations)
sources.title: How Spot Helps the ENR Sector | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Deployed quadruped inspection robots in utility facilities autonomously capture thermal scans and gauge readings of electrical assets and flag high-heat anomalies, but do not troubleshoot circuits with test instruments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous electrical-asset condition inspection in a fixed-layout facility; cited to bound what mobile robots do in situ — anomaly detection on fixed plant, not probing vehicle circuits, opening panels, or isolating a reported fault.

tasks.label: Reassemble and test equipment after repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench, common current-production unit (marine VHF/chartplotter, bus PA/radio head, locomotive display or control module) that was opened and repaired: reseat boards, reconnect internal ribbon/board-to-board connectors, refit gaskets/knobs, close housing with screws to torque, then power up on the bench and run a functional/RF or diagnostic test before returning it to service.

Shop bench, legacy, obsolete or damaged unit: corroded or stripped fasteners, mismatched replacement hardware, soldered flying leads, missing shields, model the shop has seen only a few times; reassembly requires improvised fixes and the test is an ad hoc bench setup with a service monitor or simulator.

Rail maintenance facility: reinstall a repaired/replaced electronic module (cab display, radio, PTC/event recorder, camera or sensor) into a locomotive cab console or equipment cabinet — lift into place in a cramped enclosure, mate multiple existing harness connectors, refit brackets, covers and trim, then power up and run built-in self-test plus functional checks with the vehicle's systems.

Aboard a vessel at a marina, dock or boatyard: reassemble a helm console or below-deck electronics after repairing radar, GPS/sonar or SSB gear — re-route and reconnect cabling and antenna feeds, refit panels and sealing hardware, then test transceivers, transducers and displays, sometimes with an on-water check.

Fleet garage for buses, trucks or other mobile equipment: after repairing a security/surveillance camera system, navigation head unit or PA/intercom, refit dash panels, kick panels and wire looms, reconnect connectors and grounds, reinstall fasteners, then power up and verify with the vehicle diagnostic tool and functional checks.

Field/emergency call at a customer site, rail yard track-side, roadside or on deck: reassemble and reconnect equipment after an on-the-spot repair in ad hoc conditions (weather, poor light, awkward access, no fixtures), then test with hand-held meters and portable test gear.

sources.system: KUKA KR AGILUS robots in Schnaithmann Chaku-Chaku assembly and end-of-line test system
sources.developer: KUKA / Schnaithmann Maschinenbau (for an automotive supplier)
sources.title: Assembly automation and end-of-line tests for supercomputers using KUKA robots | KUKA Global
sources.claim: A production cell of seven KUKA KR AGILUS robots at Schnaithmann assembles automotive high-performance computers (vehicle electronic control units) fully automatically with no human staff in the cell, and two of the robots carry out the end-of-line functional testing with a vision system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembly plus end-of-line functional test of automotive electronic control units. It transfers to bench reassembly-and-test of a repaired mobile-electronics unit because the objects (ESD-sensitive vehicle electronic units), the precision (millimetre placement, controlled mating of housings and boards) and the accepted output (unit verified by a functional test) are the same; under the E1 counterfactual the repaired unit arrives fixtured and presented as this cell presents its parts.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR5e with Robotiq Screwdriving Solution (integrated by Vikaso/Raruk)
sources.developer: Universal Robots / Robotiq / Vikaso, at Panorama Antennas
sources.title: Cobot Automates Screwdriving at Electronics Company | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Panorama Antennas runs a UR5e cobot with the Robotiq Screwdriving Solution that automatically picks screws from a feeder and fastens the cover panel of a network ... (an electronic assembly) to controlled torque, with screw-presence and torque error-proofing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closing an electronics enclosure with fasteners on a production bench. Reassembly of a repaired radio/navigation unit ends with the same act — refitting a cover panel and driving small screws to a controlled torque on an RF/electronic assembly — at comparable size and precision, in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: AppMuTT AI-based connector-mating framework on an industrial robot (KIT/Bosch-affiliated authors)
sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology / ArtiMinds / University of Bremen
sources.title: AI-based Framework for Robust Model-Based Connector Mating in Robotic Wire Harness Installation (arXiv:2503.09409)
sources.claim: An industrial robot using a learned force-controlled search strategy autonomously mates five different electrical connector types when installing a wire harness into an automotive center console in real-world experiments; the same paper states that wire harness installation in vehicles remains largely manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating vehicle harness connectors, a sub-step of both bench reassembly and in-vehicle reinstallation. It supports connector mating in a fixtured robot cell (E1) only; the paper's own framing that harness installation stays manual shows no system performs whole in-vehicle reconnection and refitting.

sources.system: MATT (Standard and Extended) device test automation robot
sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: MATT is a commercially sold desktop/6-DoF test-automation robot that physically actuates buttons, knobs and touchscreens of a device under test to run repeatable hardware and software functional test scenarios at a bench.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional testing of a finished electronic device by physically operating its controls. This is the 'test' half of the task for a bench unit — same objects (consumer/industrial electronic units with buttons and displays) and same acceptance criterion (device responds correctly) — performed in a fixtured bench cell.

tasks.label: Adjust, repair, or replace defective wiring and relays in ignition, lighting, air-conditioning, and safety control systems, using electrician's tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Transit bus, truck or other fleet vehicle in an institution-run maintenance garage: technician traces an intermittent lighting/HVAC/ignition fault to a chafed, corroded or broken wire behind the dash, in the engine bay or in a roof HVAC unit, cuts out the damaged section, strips, crimps/solders and heat-shrinks a splice, re-looms and re-secures the harness, then retests the circuit.

Locomotive or rail car in a railroad maintenance shop: replacing defective wiring, relays and contactors in control cabinets, cab consoles and equipment lockers; removing ring-lug terminations, pulling replacement conductors through confined raceways, torquing terminals, re-tagging wires and function-testing lighting, HVAC and safety-control circuits.

Watercraft at a marina, dock or boatyard: repairing corroded or failed wiring and relays for nav lights, blowers, AC/refrigeration and safety circuits in bilges, engine compartments and behind helm panels; every boat is a different vintage and layout, access is cramped, and the vessel is taken as found.

Field/roadside repair of disabled mobile equipment where it sits (rail yard, yard tractor, off-road or emergency-vehicle upfit): locate the failed relay or damaged harness segment, replace or splice it outdoors under variable weather and lighting, with limited access and only the tools carried in the service truck.

Straightforward modular swap in a shop bay: an accessible fuse/relay center or removable control module on the vehicle, where the defective plug-in relay or lighting driver is identified and simply pulled and replaced (or a relay/switch adjusted), followed by a power-on functional check.

sources.system: AI-based connector mating framework (Multimodal Trajectory Transformer, ArtiMinds/KIT-affiliated authors)
sources.developer: Kienle, Alt, Schneider, Pertlwieser, Jäkel, Rayyes (ArtiMinds Robotics / academic collaboration)
sources.title: AI-based Framework for Robust Model-Based Connector Mating in Robotic Wire Harness Installation
sources.claim: A research framework automates mating of automotive wire-harness electrical connectors with force control and visuotactile learning, running as programs on standard industrial controllers, validated on a fixtured center-console assembly; the paper also states that harness installation itself remains largely manual in industry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating/unmating electrical connectors on a fixtured automotive assembly. It transfers partially to plug-in relay and module swaps (same connector geometries, similar insertion forces and tolerances) but the same source states full harness installation remains manual.

sources.system: Recirculate robotic battery-disassembly cell (KUKA KR10 on linear track)
sources.developer: Centria University of Applied Sciences (Recirculate project)
sources.title: Recirculate tests AI-driven robotic system for EV battery disassembly
sources.claim: A purpose-built robotic cell with a KUKA KR10 autonomously detects, unscrews and removes fasteners, connectors and wiring from used EV high-voltage battery packs using a depth camera and trained ML models.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening an as-built electrical assembly in a fixtured cell — removing covers/screws and disconnecting connectors and wiring. Transfers to accessing a fixtured relay/fuse panel and extracting a plug-in component; it is disassembly only, with no re-wiring, splicing or functional restoration.

sources.system: Komax Zeta 620/630/640/650 (and Zeta 633/656 with Kiesling) control-cabinet wiring machines
sources.date: commercial; Zeta 633/656 reported 2014, current Zeta range 2024-2026
sources.title: Control Panel Manufacturing Gets Automated (Komax Zeta) / Komax Zeta 620 story
sources.claim: Commercial fully automatic machines wire control cabinets — cutting, stripping, labelling and ferruling wires, with variants able to insert wires automatically into spring-loaded terminal blocks with ... — inside a purpose-built machine enclosure, including cabinets for trains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: new-build panel wiring in a purpose-built machine. It shows automated wire preparation and terminal insertion under full fixturing, but not fault location, removal of an existing defective conductor, splicing, or re-looming inside a vehicle, so it does not cover repair instances.

sources.system: Dual-arm robotic wire harness assembly system (research)
sources.developer: Malvido Fresnillo et al., Tampere University
sources.title: A dual-arm robotic system for automated multi-branch wire harness assembly in automotive industry
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed work of December 2025 presents a dual-arm robotic system for multi-branch wire harness assembly and reports that wire harnesses are still assembled manually in industry, with robots proposed as a possible future solution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation of harnesses (deformable linear objects). Cited as state-of-the-art context showing even factory harness work is research-stage, so it cannot substantiate autonomous in-vehicle harness repair.

tasks.label: Splice wires with knives or cutting pliers, and solder connections to fixtures, outlets, and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop workbench work: technician builds or repairs a cable assembly/pigtail for a radio, sonar head, camera or nav unit that has been removed from the vehicle - cuts and strips conductors, splices leads, solders them to connector pins, terminals or lugs, and insulates with heat-shrink or solder sleeves.

In-situ wiring in a road-vehicle cab (bus, truck, transit coach, RV) inside a service bay: technician reaches behind the dash, under seats and through panels, splices new sound/security/camera/nav feeds into an existing loom, and solders connections in a confined, poorly lit space with the harness unfixtured and live circuits nearby.

Marine electronics install/repair aboard a customer's boat at a dock or in a yard: splicing and soldering sonar, VHF, radar and instrument wiring in a helm console, bilge or mast conduit - cramped, damp, corroded conductors, boat-specific layout, heat-shrink solder sleeves required for water resistance.

Rail car or locomotive in a maintenance shop/yard: splicing multi-conductor cables and soldering terminals inside junction boxes, control cabinets and under-carbody enclosures for PA, security-camera and train-control wiring, standing on ladders or in pits.

Field/emergency repair on a disabled vehicle or a vessel underway or moored remotely: locate the damaged conductor, cut out the bad section, splice and solder in place, outdoors or in an engine space, with only hand tools and no shop support.

sources.system: Comau Racer-3-0.63 robotic soldering cell (with ETNEO soldering technology)
sources.title: Precision Robotic Soldering for Electronics Manufacturing - Comau
sources.claim: Comau deployed a fully automated robotic soldering cell (Racer-3-0.63 with dispensing-soldering head and vision inspection) in a high-volume electronics manufacturing facility; it replicates manual soldering movements with sub-millimetre accuracy and inspects every joint.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as the task's soldering half - melting solder onto small terminals/pads to worker-quality joints with automated quality check - but on fixtured workpieces inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Kurassem-SR / Kurassem-WH robot package (KURASENSE C100FX 3D vision)
sources.title: Robot Package (Kurassem) Kurassem-WH (Wire Harness Manufacturing) / SR (Automatic Soldering)
sources.claim: Kurabo's commercial Kurassem-SR/WH robot packages use a 3D vision sensor and a 6-axis robot inside a safety fence to pick individual lead wires from a bundle, correct their bend, position them and solder them to sensor terminals, board pads or harness connector ends; the WH package also crimps terminals and inserts them into connectors.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the task's core objects (loose wires, terminals, connector ends) and the soldering operation, executed autonomously in a fenced cell rather than in a vehicle.

sources.system: Komax Alpha 560 / Gamma 450 automatic wire-processing machines
sources.title: Automatic Crimping | Komax
sources.claim: Komax fully automatic wire-processing machines carry out cutting, stripping, crimping, seal insertion, ... of conductors in one machine on a production line, with in-process monitoring that rejects defective wires.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the preparation steps of the task (cutting and stripping conductors, tinning ends, terminating) on the same gauge of transport-equipment wire, in a machine-fed purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Schunk Sonosystems Minic III / L-Splice ultrasonic splice welders
sources.title: Schunk: Inside Ultrasonic Technology - Wiring Harness News
sources.claim: Schunk Sonosystems ultrasonic splicing machines (Minic III, L-Splice) make wire-to-wire splices from 0.26 mm2 up to 300 mm2 to harness-industry quality standards, and are designed for integration into fully automated production systems, as well as wire-to-terminal welding with fixtured tooling.
sources.transferJustification: This is the splice half of the task - joining two or more conductors to an accepted mechanical and electrical standard - performed by machine on fixtured wire ends.

sources.system: TE Connectivity RBK X1 / X1C heat shrink processing machine
sources.title: Heat Shrink Machines for Raychem Heat Shrink Products from TE Connectivity
sources.claim: TE Connectivity RBK heat-shrink processors seal and insulate splices automatically: splice sensors verify wire position, the machine centres the assembly, installs the sealing product and ejects the finished, insulated, strain-relieved joint.
sources.transferJustification: Supplementary: covers the insulation/sealing finish of a splice; operator-loaded in standalone use, so treated as non-autonomous and not decisive for any judgment.

sources.system: Review of collaborative and semi-automated automotive wire harness assembly (state of the art)
sources.title: Review of Current Status and Future Directions for Collaborative and Semi-Automated Automotive Wire Harnesses Assembly
sources.claim: A 2024 review of automotive wire-harness assembly reports that despite research prototypes and collaborative-robot solutions, the industry has not adopted any method that automates in-vehicle harness assembly fully or partially; robotized harness handling remains at the research stage.
sources.transferJustification: Supports the negative finding that no fielded system performs unfixtured in-vehicle wiring, splicing or soldering work inside human work facilities (E2).

tasks.label: Locate and remove or repair circuit defects such as blown fuses or malfunctioning transistors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Protective-device fault: a piece of onboard equipment (bus PA/camera system, rail car HVAC control, boat navigation display) is dead; in the garage/depot bay the tech opens the power distribution panel, tests blade fuses, breakers and plug-in relays with a meter/test light, pulls the opened device, installs a replacement of correct rating, and verifies the circuit works.

Bench component-level repair in the shop's electronics room: a removed module or circuit card (marine radio, sonar/chartplotter, locomotive control or door card) is placed on the bench; the tech uses schematics, meter, scope and known-fault knowledge to find the failed discrete (transistor, diode, capacitor, regulator, board-mounted fuse), desolders it, solders in a replacement, and functionally retests the board.

In-situ wiring circuit defect on the vehicle/vessel in the depot or shop bay: intermittent short, open, chafed conductor, corroded ground or damaged connector behind panels, under floors or in cable runs; the tech traces the circuit with meter and prints, then repairs by splicing, re-terminating, replacing a connector or re-routing, and reassembles trim.

Afloat or field repair: vessel at a dock or underway, or mobile equipment in the yard/roadside; cramped engine room, bilge or console space, salt corrosion, moisture and non-standard as-built wiring; the tech locates the defect (water-damaged board, corroded fuse holder, failed component) and repairs or replaces it on the spot to restore service.

Commissioning fault after a new installation: newly fitted equipment repeatedly blows a fuse or does not power up; the tech must diagnose across the installed system (wrong feed, miswired harness, defective supplied unit), correct the defect on the vehicle, and re-test the whole installation.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers (e.g. 4060 series)
sources.title: Electronic Board Testing: ICT, Flying Probe & Functional | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA automatic flying-probe testers are sold as dedicated solutions for repair centers that automatically probe a loaded board and identify the faulty component, producing a component-level diagnostic report — the machine performs the 'locate the circuit defect' step inside a purpose-built test cell.

tasks.label: Install fixtures, outlets, terminal boards, switches, and wall boxes, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail vehicle build or mid-life overhaul at a railcar plant or transit maintenance shop: installing terminal boards/terminal strips, switch and breaker panels, receptacles and junction/wall boxes in locomotive cab consoles and electrical lockers; drilling and tapping into car structure, mounting boxes, landing conductors on terminal blocks, torque and continuity checks.

Bench/shop prefabrication before installation: building up terminal boards on DIN rail or panel plates, populating switch/outlet subpanels and boxes on a bench or jig in the shop, labeling and pre-wiring them for later fitting into the vehicle or vessel.

Upfitting an emergency vehicle, bus or work truck at an upfitter facility: cutting openings and mounting switch panels, 12 V and 120 V outlets, fuse/terminal boards and wall boxes in consoles, cabinets and body compartments, then terminating circuits with hand tools.

New boat production at a boatbuilder: installing breaker/switch panels, outlets, terminal blocks and junction boxes into helm consoles and bulkheads on the production line, working to the builder's standard layout with prepared harnesses.

Marine retrofit aboard a customer's vessel at a marina, dock or on the hard: adding a switch panel, outlet, terminal block or junction box in an as-found boat, working in confined lockers, bilges and behind the helm on varied, non-standard construction.

Field replacement/repair on in-service mobile equipment (transit bus at a depot, railcar in a yard, ferry, off-highway machine): removing a failed switch, outlet, terminal board or box, mounting the replacement and reconnecting it to existing, sometimes corroded or unlabeled wiring.

tasks.label: Install new fuses, electrical cables, or power sources as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fuse/circuit-protection work on a vehicle in a maintenance shop: locate the fuse or distribution panel (under a locomotive desk, in a bus electrical locker, behind a truck dash), select the correctly rated fuse, fusible link or breaker, seat it, and verify the circuit powers up. Cramped, reach-limited access around existing bundles.

Running a new cable run for added electronics inside a locomotive, transit bus, truck cab or vessel at a shop/yard: pulling power and signal cable through existing bundles, conduits, cable trays and firewall/bulkhead grommets, drilling or using existing penetrations, dressing and clamping the run clear of heat and moving parts.

Terminating and landing conductors: cutting to length, stripping, crimping lugs and connector pins, populating connector housings, landing wires on terminal blocks, breakers and equipment studs to torque, labeling, and continuity/insulation checking. Done partly on a shop bench, partly aboard the equipment.

Installing a power source: mounting and connecting a battery bank or battery box, DC-DC converter, inverter, power supply or breaker/distribution panel for newly installed radio, navigation, surveillance or sonar gear - bracket mounting, bolting heavy items, landing feed cables and grounds.

Field/mobile install at a customer site: a recreational or commercial boat in a slip or on a trailer, or a customer truck in a lot, where a fused power lead, battery isolator or new supply cable must be added for a radar, radio or camera in a vehicle whose wiring layout is found as-is.

sources.system: AFRA Automatic Fuse and Relay Assembly (Fuse Insertion Station / Screw Station)
sources.title: AFRA Automatic Fuse and Relay Assembly
sources.claim: Commercial standalone station uses a SCARA robot to insert fuses into fuse ... already mounted in wire harnesses, with load-cell force monitoring detecting missing or faulty insertions; a companion station screws nuts onto fuse-box studs with torque traceability.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the fuse-installation part of the task: same objects (blade fuses, automotive fuse boxes) and same acceptance check (insertion force/contact), performed by machine on fixtured work.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing and securing electrical cables for transportation equipment (aircraft harnesses). Same deformable conductors and routing/clamping precision as running cable in a vehicle, but with the route fixtured on a form board.

sources.system: Komax Alpha series automatic crimping machines

sources.transferJustification: Covers the termination step of installing electrical cables (strip, crimp lug/terminal, seal) at production quality, with the wire fed to the machine.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating electrical connectors in vehicle wiring. Same connector hardware and insertion-force tolerances as landing a newly installed cable's connector.

sources.claim: Automated swap stations remove and install a traction battery pack in a vehicle - aligning, unbolting/bolting and mating power connections - in about three minutes with no human handling, across thousands of deployed stations and over 100 million swaps.

tasks.label: Cut openings and drill holes for fixtures, outlet boxes, and fuse holders, using electric drills and routers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Marine electronics install on a customer's boat at a marina/boatyard: cutting a flush-mount rectangular opening in the fiberglass or acrylic helm dash for a multifunction display or VHF, plus hole-sawing and drilling fastener holes, working in the cramped helm area of a boat taken as found, templating around structure behind the dash and protecting the gelcoat.

Vehicle/RV/bus/emergency-vehicle install in a shop bay: drilling holes through interior trim, headliners, roofs, firewalls and sheet-metal bulkheads for antennas, cameras, speakers, sirens and fuse blocks with step drills and hole saws, avoiding hidden wiring, tanks and structure behind the panel.

Bench fabrication in the shop: cutting cutouts and drilling holes in a blank aluminum/plastic mounting panel, junction box or equipment enclosure for fuse holders, breakers, switches and connectors before it is installed in the vehicle, laid out from a drawing or by marking around the components.

Rail/transit retrofit in a maintenance depot: drilling and routing openings in equipment cabinets, mounting rails, car-body panels and floor pans for surveillance, PA and communication gear; heavier steel/aluminum stock, mag-drill or router work, clearance and safety-critical structural restrictions.

Field service call with awkward access: drilling a pass-through in a transom, bulkhead or console and mounting a fuse holder/connector plate while kneeling in an engine compartment or reaching overhead behind a dash at the customer's site, with no fixed layout and limited light and space.

sources.transferJustification: Cited only to bound the in-situ (E2/E3) case: it drills anchor holes in building ceilings from a model at anchor-hole tolerance and cannot enter a vehicle cabin or boat helm, template around hidden structure, or router a flush-mount instrument opening, so it does not transfer to this task.

tasks.label: Install electrical equipment such as air-conditioning, heating, or ignition systems and components such as generator brushes and commutators, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fleet/truck/bus/RV shop bay: install or replace a cab air-conditioning or heater unit (evaporator/blower assembly, compressor, control head). Worker removes dash/kick panels, mounts brackets, routes refrigerant hoses and wiring harness, terminates and plugs connectors, fuses circuits, evacuates and charges the system, then function-tests. Vehicle on a lift or floor bay, mixed makes/model years.

Marine work at a marina, dock, or boatyard: install A/C or heating units, ignition-system components, or other electrical equipment on a vessel. Confined engine compartments and lockers, bespoke cable runs drilled and sealed through bulkheads, no two boats laid out alike, work often afloat and in motion.

Rail maintenance shop: install electrical equipment on transit railcars or locomotives — roof- or underfloor-mounted HVAC/heating package, cab heaters, control boxes. Unit craned or hoisted into position, bolted to mounting rails, gaskets seated, power/control cables landed in junction boxes and lugged, then tested.

Shop bench or in-place service of rotating electrical machines: install new generator/traction-motor brushes and brush holders, fit or replace a commutator/slip-ring assembly, set spring tension and brush seating, clean and undercut, reconnect leads, test output. Machine may be on a bench fixture or accessed through inspection covers on the equipment.

Shop/engine bay: install ignition-system components on propulsion or auxiliary engines (bus, truck, marine, locomotive genset) — coils, magnetos, ignition modules, plugs and plug leads, wiring harness sections — using hand tools and torque wrenches, followed by continuity/spark and run testing.

sources.system: KUKA KR CYBERTECH nano ARC HW robots in Liebherr-Verzahntechnik battery-pack assembly cell (with KOSTAL plug-in module connectors)
sources.developer: KUKA / Liebherr-Verzahntechnik GmbH / KOSTAL Kontakt Systeme
sources.title: Automated battery pack assembly for high-voltage batteries | KUKA Global
sources.claim: In a production cell, paired KUKA industrial robots autonomously plug flexible high-voltage module connectors into battery modules, i.e. automated mating of real electrical connectors with non-rigid cables in a fixtured, fenced cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated electrical connector mating during battery pack assembly. The instances here require plugging vehicle wiring connectors and landing power leads on comparably sized automotive connectors, so demonstrated autonomous connector mating on fixtured product transfers to the electrical-connection step of an installation performed in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Nissan Intelligent Factory line (automated cockpit module and headliner installation robots)
sources.title: Nissan Intelligent Factory | Innovation | Nissan Motor Corporation Global Website

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation of the cockpit/HVAC module into a vehicle body on a fixtured line. It involves the same class of object (a heater/AC module plus harness) placed into a vehicle to tight tolerance, so it substantiates HVAC-unit installation when the vehicle is presented fixtured to the machine.

sources.system: Comau automated range-extender engine assembly line (SmartCell)

sources.system: HONEST Automation brush-motor assembly lines (water-pump motor, 370 motor lines)

The instance's objects (carbon brushes, brush holders, commutators/slip rings, spring tension seating) are the same components handled on these lines, so the capability transfers when the machine is fixtured and parts are presented.

sources.transferJustification: Directly related: connector installation into a vehicle is a core step of every instance. The measured success rate bounds what is achievable outside highly engineered cells and supports negative judgments at E2/E3.

It marks the ceiling of mobile/humanoid capability in a human-standard vehicle facility — part insertion into fixtures, not multi-step electrical installation with hand tools — supporting negative E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Repair or rebuild equipment such as starters, generators, distributors, or door controls, using electrician's tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench rebuild of a rotating electrical machine (starter motor, alternator/generator, blower or auxiliary motor) removed from a locomotive, transit car, bus or vessel: teardown of a worn, greasy core with hand and power tools, cleaning, growler/megger testing of armature and fields, commutator turning/undercutting, replacement of brushes, bearings, solenoid or regulator, reassembly and bench test to spec.

Repair/rebuild of transit rail-car or coach door control equipment in a shop bay: door operator motor/actuator, control relays, limit and safety switches, obstruction-detection wiring and control card, working inside the door pocket and control cabinet with electrician's hand tools, then adjusting and cycle-testing the doors.

On-equipment repair of starters, alternators/generators, ignition/distributor and charging components on buses, trucks or rail equipment in a fleet garage bay: removing the unit from the engine bay or underframe, bench-servicing or replacing internals, reinstalling, re-terminating cables and load testing.

Repair aboard a vessel or in the field: engine-room generator/starter, deck machinery controls or navigation-equipment power supplies serviced dockside or under way; cramped, vessel-specific access, vibration, moisture and corroded terminals, layout differing boat to boat.

Bench repair/rebuild of electronic control units and control cards (door controllers, voltage regulators, relay/contactor panels): opening the housing, diagnosing to the failed component or connector, desoldering and replacing components or rewiring terminals, reassembly and functional test on a test fixture.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of used starter motors for remanufacturing. It is the teardown sub-step of the bench rebuild instance; it does not carry over to the whole instance because inspection-driven part replacement, reassembly of worn cores and bench testing are not demonstrated.

Rail vehicles in a transit/railroad maintenance shop or car-builder plant: fabricating and installing mounting frames, wireway/conduit runs and junction boxes on locomotives and rail cars for PA, CCTV, event recorder or PTC equipment - working in the cab, in equipment lockers, under the carbody and along roof lines, drilling and bolting into existing structure.

On-site field work outside any controlled shop: dockside, rail yard, jobsite or customer premises, often in weather or on an in-service vehicle/vessel - measuring a run, cutting and bending conduit, fabricating a bracket, and installing boxes and supports with hand tools where layout and existing structure are taken as found.

roles.description: Repair, test, adjust, or install electronic equipment, such as industrial controls, transmitters, and antennas.

tasks.label: Test faulty equipment to diagnose malfunctions, using test equipment or software, and applying knowledge of the functional operation of electronic units and systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Line-down troubleshooting of installed industrial/material-handling controls at a factory or distribution center: technician goes to the machine, opens an energized control cabinet, checks supply and I/O voltages with a DMM/clamp meter, scopes sensor and drive signals, connects a laptop to the PLC/VFD to read fault codes and force I/O, and traces the fault through field wiring, photo-eyes, encoders and contactors to a specific failed device or wire.

Bench diagnosis of a returned printed-circuit assembly from a known product line at a repair depot or shop: board is placed on the bench/tester, powered or probed, compared against known-good data, and the failure localized to a specific component, trace or pin before rework.

Depot/shop fault isolation of a complete faulty unit (radio/transmitter chassis, industrial controller, power supply, instrument): unit is connected to a test station or manufacturer test set, functional/self-test routines are run, measurements taken, and the fault isolated to a replaceable module or assembly.

On-site diagnosis of commercial electronic equipment at a customer's premises (building-automation controllers, commercial machines, security/AV, lab or gaming devices): unfamiliar installation, tight or occupied spaces, technician meters power and control circuits, runs vendor diagnostic software, and determines whether the fault is in the controller, a peripheral, wiring, or the supply.

Diagnosis of transmitter and antenna systems at a broadcast/land-mobile/microwave site: rooftop, tower base or remote shelter, sweep/VSWR and return-loss tests on feedlines, RF power and modulation measurements, spectrum checks, weather and access constraints, isolating the fault between exciter, PA, filters, feedline or antenna.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers (4060/4080 family)
sources.title: Load Board Testing: how to ensure accuracy and reliability | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA flying probe testers are commercial automatic test machines whose moving probes contact a board placed in the machine and, running an automatically generated program, localize the failure to the specific defective part on a board that has failed in service - i.e. diagnosing a fault on faulty equipment brought to the machine.

tasks.label: Inspect components of industrial equipment for accurate assembly and installation or for defects, such as loose connections or frayed wires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inside a plant or commercial facility, the tech opens a de-energized control cabinet, MCC bucket or switchgear panel and inspects terminations, terminal blocks, relays, contactors and internal wiring: tugging conductors, looking for discoloration/arc tracking, chafed or frayed insulation, missing lugs, and modules not fully seated. Cramped enclosures, dust, plant noise, PPE.

In a repair shop, a removed unit (VFD, PLC I/O card, controller, transmitter, power supply) is opened on the bench and inspected under light/magnification for burnt or cracked components, cold or lifted solder joints, corroded or loose connectors, damaged internal leads, and confirmation the board was assembled correctly.

Field inspection of installed devices and wiring in process areas of a plant (indoor or outdoor): transmitters, sensors, motor terminal boxes, junction boxes, conduit, cable trays and cordsets. Checks external condition, corrosion, water ingress, loose glands, chafed or frayed cable, then opens covers to check terminations. Work at height, in tight spaces, in weather.

Routine scheduled condition round of energized electrical equipment in an operating plant or substation: walking a fixed route, visually checking equipment and indicator lights, and thermographically scanning switchgear/MCC exteriors and IR windows for hot spots that reveal loose or high-resistance connections; anomalies logged for follow-up.

Commissioning / acceptance inspection of newly installed or newly assembled equipment at a facility: verifying the panel or skid was built and installed per drawings - correct components and ratings, correct point-to-point terminations, labeling, grounding, torque marks, cable dressing - before energizing.

Service call at an unstructured customer site (rooftop HVAC controls, remote pump/telecom or antenna site, building under construction, small shop): inspect as-found installed equipment and its wiring for defects and installation errors, with no fixed layout, variable access, weather and clutter.

Install repaired RF/communications gear at a broadcast, dispatch, or tower site: rack-mount a repaired transmitter or amplifier, or remount a repaired antenna on a tower or rooftop mast — coax connectors, weatherproofing, grounding, sweep/power test, often outdoors at height in variable weather.

Install repaired electronic equipment at a military establishment: shipboard compartment, vehicle/aircraft bay, radar or comms shelter — confined space, escorted access, mil-spec circular connectors and bonding straps, securing hardware, functional check with the host system.

Bench/shop work in the repair facility: reinstall the repaired module, board, or power supply back into its host chassis or slide the repaired unit into a customer rack/test stand — fasteners, ribbon/blade/circular connector mating, then final functional test before return to service.

instances.label: At a customer plant, technician runs a malfunctioning machine's control system through its operating cycles (HMI screens, pushbuttons, jogging a drive, forcing I/O) to reproduce a reported fault and isolate it to a drive, controller, sensor or board; standard industrial equipment, plant floor conditions.

Plant-floor chase of an intermittent or system-level fault: run the line under production conditions, cycle it repeatedly, trip sensors, watch interactions of mechanics, field wiring, power quality and process; hypotheses change as behavior is observed.

Repair-shop bench: a returned unit or board (VFD, power supply, industrial controller, instrument, transmitter card) is powered up on a bench, exercised through its functions and probed to localize the fault, then re-operated after repair to verify performance before return.

After install or repair, operate the equipment in front of the customer's operators/maintenance staff to demonstrate proper use, correct settings and safe start-up, answering their questions until they can run it themselves.

Field-sited RF/telemetry equipment: at a tower shack, rooftop or remote site, key up a transmitter, run test transmissions, exercise exciter/amplifier controls and sweep lines/antennas to characterize a malfunction; weather-exposed, site-to-site variation.

Small or varied commercial customer sites taken as found (retail back rooms, clinics, small shops, temporary installations): operate a piece of commercial electronic equipment to reproduce the customer's complaint and determine what is wrong.

In-situ field calibration of installed process instruments in an industrial plant or utility: locate the pressure/temperature/level/flow transmitter or loop, isolate and bypass it, connect a pressure/temperature source and a documenting calibrator or HART communicator, run 5-point up/down checks, trim zero and span to prescribed tolerance, restore the loop and file the certificate. Hot, noisy, congested piping/panel environments.

Post-repair bench calibration and alignment of industrial electronic equipment in the repair shop: after replacing components on a drive, controller card, weight indicator, transmitter or two-way radio/RF module, place it on the test bench, apply reference signals, adjust trim pots or write digital calibration constants, and verify output meets the manufacturer's published specification before return to service.

On-site calibration at customer commercial/light-industrial premises of installed but removable instruments and sensors (building automation temperature/pressure sensors, scale load-cell indicators, portable analyzers, bench instruments in customer labs): setting varies site to site, access is as found, the technician works around occupants and equipment in service.

In-place calibration/alignment of installed systems that cannot be taken to a bench: aiming and tuning an antenna/transmitter on a rooftop or tower to prescribed signal specs, calibrating an installed weighing or batching system in place with certified test weights, or aligning machine-mounted sensors and limit devices on running production equipment. instances.label: In-plant repair of industrial control/power gear: at a manufacturing plant's electrical room or machine line, lock out and replace a failed contactor, relay, VFD, power supply, sensor or terminal block inside a control panel or MCC bucket — releasing, landing and torquing existing field wires, re-labelling, restoring and verifying operation.

Bench repair in an in-house or third-party industrial electronics shop: open the housing of a returned drive, PLC module, instrument or power supply, replace the defective parts (electrolytic caps, IGBT module, fan, relay, connector, worn contacts), clean, reassemble with gaskets and fasteners, and retest before return to service.

Board-level component rework at the shop bench: a single identified defective SMD/BGA/fine-pitch device on a control board is desoldered, the pads cleaned of residual solder, flux/paste applied, a new component aligned and soldered, then the board is electrically verified.

Swap of a standardized plug-in / hot-swappable module in racked control or communications equipment (rack power supply, redundant I/O or line card, disk) in a controlled control room, telecom/broadcast rack room or data hall: locate the failed unit, extract it, insert the replacement, confirm status.

Replacing worn sealing and wear parts on installed equipment in the field: renew gaskets/O-rings in watertight, washdown or explosion-proof enclosures and junction boxes, seals on submersible/outdoor equipment, motor brushes and worn contacts — scrape and clean the sealing face, fit the new seal, refit and torque the cover, verify ingress protection; often outdoors, wet, cramped or at height.

Field service call at a customer or remote site: repair or adjust transmitters, antennas, weighing systems, traffic controllers, commercial or medical equipment in varied buildings, rooftops, towers, vehicles or pump stations — layout differs each visit, access is improvised, weather and clutter vary.

Modification or installation of electronics at a remote/outdoor or non-standard site (transmitter and antenna site, pump or lift station, outdoor skid, utility yard cabinet): mount and wire the new device per spec in cramped, weather-exposed, site-specific conditions with no fixed layout.

Develop a one-off circuit, interface board or test fixture to available specifications: build the circuit (perfboard/prototype board or wired assembly), integrate it with connectors, switches and indicators in a housing, then bring it up with meter/scope/power supply and adjust component values or wiring until it meets spec.

instances.label: Routine preventive-maintenance inspection round of a distribution/transmission substation: walk the fenced yard and control house, visually inspect transformers, breakers, buswork and insulators, run an infrared thermographic scan for hot connections, read oil-level/temperature and SF6 gauges and panel voltmeters/ammeters, and log/flag defects for follow-up. Utility owns and controls the site.

Periodic test and calibration of protective relays (electromechanical or microprocessor): isolate the relay at test switches per the schematic, land test-set leads on the relay terminals, inject secondary currents/voltages, verify pickup values, timing curves, targets and output contacts against settings, and identify defective or out-of-calibration elements. Done in a substation control house or in the relay shop.

Troubleshooting a reported malfunction in station control, protection, DC, or auxiliary circuits (breaker fails to close, DC ground alarm, blown fuse, faulty auxiliary switch, alarm misoperation): open cabinets, follow as-built wiring diagrams, ring out wiring and check voltages/continuity at cramped terminal blocks with a multimeter, and isolate the defective component or wire.

Electrical testing of primary apparatus during a maintenance outage: insulation resistance (megger), contact resistance (ductor), CT/PT ratio and polarity, transformer turns ratio and power factor on 15 kV-345 kV breakers, transformers and instrument transformers — grounding, clamping heavy test leads to bushings/terminals in the yard, running the test set, and comparing results to prior data.

Routine inspection/condition round of electrical equipment inside a generating station: walkdown of switchgear rooms, MCCs, station service transformers and battery rooms; IR scanning of energized gear through viewing ports, reading panel meters and instrument readings, listening for abnormal noise, and reporting abnormalities.

instances.label: Substation control house: a microprocessor/solid-state protective relay in a panel has failed. Tech opens FT-1 test switch paddles (trip, CT-shorting, PT) to isolate it, tags out, unscrews/unplugs the relay from the panel cutout and terminal blocks, installs a like-for-like replacement, restores wiring, closes test switches and verifies with a relay test set.

Metal-clad switchgear room (substation or plant): defective relay or auxiliary relay associated with a breaker cubicle. Tech racks the breaker out to test/disconnect position, opens control-power switches/fuses, works on the cubicle-door-mounted relay, replaces or adjusts it, functionally trip-tests, then racks the breaker back in.

Outdoor substation yard: to free a defective relay's protection zone, tech operates motor-operated or manually cranked disconnect switches, verifies de-energized, applies safety grounds, then repairs/replaces the relay and control wiring in an outdoor control cabinet; gravel yard, weather, energized HV equipment nearby.

Electromechanical relay (induction-disc overcurrent, plunger, differential) found out of calibration or with pitted/misaligned contacts. Tech isolates it with test switches, withdraws it from its case (or takes it to the relay shop bench), burnishes contacts, adjusts spring tension, contact gap, drag magnet and taps, recalibrates against a test set, and returns it to service.

Generating station / powerhouse: protection or auxiliary relay in unit control panels, MCC or excitation cabinets. Tech coordinates the clearance, opens control switches and pulls fuses to isolate the relay, replaces or adjusts it in a congested panel with other trades working nearby, then restores and proves the trip path.

After-hours trouble call at an unmanned substation: a relay is misoperating and causing spurious trips. Tech must diagnose which element is at fault, block/isolate the scheme by opening trip test switches or lifting leads, make a temporary fix or swap, and restore service quickly under outage pressure.

tasks.label: Repair, replace, and clean equipment and components such as circuit breakers, brushes, and commutators.

instances.label: Scheduled maintenance/repair of a high-voltage circuit breaker or switch in an outdoor transmission substation yard: de-energize and ground, open cabinets, clean bushings/insulators and arc-interrupter parts, inspect and replace worn main/arcing contacts, seals and springs, lubricate the operating mechanism, reassemble, torque hardware, and verify timing/contact resistance before returning to service.

Brush-rigging and collector/commutator work on a generator, exciter or large DC machine on the powerhouse floor: measure brush wear and spring pressure, pull and fit new carbon brushes (often with the machine running or on a short outage), seat/sand brushes, wipe and dress collector rings or commutator, clean carbon dust from the rigging, check for sparking and ring eccentricity.

Low/medium-voltage switchgear and MCC maintenance in a plant electrical room or substation control house: rack out a draw-out breaker, remove arc chutes and covers, vacuum/blast out dust and carbon tracking, inspect and replace contacts, springs, coils and auxiliary switches, lubricate the stored-energy mechanism, reassemble, re-rack and functionally test.

Protective/auxiliary relay and control-panel work in a control house: replace a failed electromechanical or microprocessor relay, control switch, fuse block or auxiliary device — remove wiring landed on the old device, mount the new device on the panel/rack, land and torque wiring per the schematic, burnish or clean contacts on in-service electromechanical relays, then test with a relay test set.

Bench/shop reconditioning of a removed DC machine armature or slip-ring assembly in the plant or utility repair shop: chuck the armature, turn/face the commutator, undercut the mica, deburr and polish the bar surfaces, and clean the part so it meets the shop's surface and runout standard.

Emergency repair after a fault, fire or storm at a generating station or substation: damaged, sooty, partially collapsed or flooded equipment in non-standard condition, temporary lighting or night work, improvised access, replacing burned components and cleaning contamination to restore service under time pressure.

sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the 'commutator' element of this task: reconditioning a worn commutator (turn, undercut, deburr, polish) on a machine that holds the workpiece, i.e. the work brought to the machine.

tasks.label: Run signal quality and connectivity tests for individual cables, and record results.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Substation control house and yard: technician rings out and meggers individual multiconductor control, trip and CT/PT cables running between relay panels and outdoor breaker/junction boxes — landing test leads on labeled terminal-block points, coordinating with a partner at the far end, checking continuity, phasing and insulation resistance, then recording readings on the utility's test form or asset software.

Fiber-optic and communications cable testing at a substation or plant: OTDR traces, optical loss/continuity and connector endface checks on SCADA, teleprotection and LAN fiber links terminated at patch panels in the control house or comm room; results logged into circuit records.

Generating station (powerhouse): continuity and insulation-resistance/hipot checks on individual instrument, control and motor-feeder cables terminating at MCCs, junction boxes and instrument racks; hot, noisy, congested cable-tray environment; results entered on the work order.

Relay/electronics shop bench: testing individual cable assemblies, jumper harnesses, coax/patch cords and test leads before installation — continuity, opens/shorts, resistance, insulation/hipot on a bench tester; results printed or logged to the job record.

Field troubleshooting/fault location on an installed or damaged cable: TDR, megger or thumper work from a manhole, pull box, cable trench or pad-mounted cabinet, often outdoors in weather and traffic; identify the suspect conductor, locate the fault distance, record findings.

Pilot-wire/telemetry and leased communication circuit testing between two substations: injecting tones, measuring levels, noise and loop resistance end to end, coordinating with the far-end technician or carrier, recording circuit test results.

tasks.label: Maintain inventories of spare parts for all equipment, requisitioning parts as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled cycle count / annual physical inventory of racked, labeled stock in a utility service-center or generating-station warehouse: walking pallet racks and open shelving to count boxed relays, meters, breaker parts, spare modules, wire reels; reading location and part labels and reconciling counts against the ERP/CMMS, flagging discrepancies and shortfalls.

Checking the relay shop's loose and enclosed stock: parts in cabinet drawers and closed bins (contacts, fuses, terminal blocks, hardware, test leads, legacy components often unlabeled or in mixed bins); verifying quantities and usable condition and updating the stock record.

Receiving and put-away: opening delivered cartons at the storeroom/dock, verifying items and quantities against the packing list and purchase order, tagging them, placing each in its bin/shelf location, updating stock records, and reporting shortages or shipping damage.

Point-of-need withdrawal and requisition: pulling a needed spare (relay, aux module, fuse, contact kit) from stock during or after a repair, recording the issue against the job, and raising a requisition/purchase order when the item hits its minimum level; following up with the vendor on delivery.

Field/vehicle stock: checking and replenishing the crew truck and substation control-house stock of consumables (fuses, terminals, wire, tape, test leads, small spares) before or after jobs, and noting what must be reordered.

Large/critical spares: verifying presence, serial numbers and storage condition of bulky spares staged in a yard or high-bay (spare power transformer, circuit breaker, relay panels, cable reels) - checking heaters/desiccant/damage, updating the critical-spares list and initiating procurement of long-lead replacements.

tasks.label: Construct, test, maintain, and repair substation relay and control systems.

instances.label: Periodic maintenance testing of installed protective relays in an energized substation control house (PRC-005 program): open test switches/test plugs, connect a secondary-injection test set to the relay, run pickup/timing/element tests, verify trip outputs and targets, restore the relay in service and document results.

Troubleshooting and repairing relay/control system failures and misoperations: tracing DC control and trip circuits through panels and terminal blocks, checking fuses, aux relays, switches and CT/VT circuits with meters, finding loose or chafed conductors, replacing failed auxiliary relays and re-terminating wires, often under time pressure after a fault, sometimes at night or in poor weather.

Relay and control-system retrofit/upgrade in an existing substation panel: de-energize and isolate, remove electromechanical relays and their existing field wiring, mount and land wiring on new microprocessor relays, add test switches, load settings, and prove the modified scheme.

Acceptance/commissioning testing of new or expanded substation relay and control systems at an active construction site: point-to-point wire checks between panels, yard devices and marshalling cabinets, CT/VT circuit polarity and ratio verification, functional trip checks to breakers, SCADA/RTU point verification, punch-list corrections.

Shop fabrication of new relay and control panels: machining/mounting DIN rail, relays, test switches and terminal blocks on a mounting plate, then cutting, ferruling and landing hundreds of wires per the schematic and wire list on a bench in the utility's relay/panel shop.

sources.claim: CIGRE's survey of substation robotics describes teleoperated patrol robots that inspect equipment and operate a disconnect switch with a mechanical arm, and live-maintenance robots for cleaning insulators — i.e., inspection and gross switching, not relay or control-circuit work.

tasks.label: Test insulators and bushings of equipment by inducing voltage across insulation, testing current, and calculating insulation loss.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor substation, scheduled outage: power-factor / tan-delta (Doble) test of power-transformer bushings. Worker verifies isolation, applies working grounds, disconnects line leads, shorts H and X bushing terminals, isolates neutral, shorts bushing CTs, connects HV/LV test leads and guard leads at height, energizes 10 kV, records watts/current/capacitance and computes power factor with temperature correction.

Outdoor substation: insulation-resistance (megger), DC hipot and leakage-current tests on circuit breakers, current/potential transformers, disconnects and station post insulators; leads clipped to terminals in a live yard beside energized apparatus, results computed (polarization index, dielectric absorption, insulation loss) and trended.

Generating station indoors: insulation testing of generator and large motor windings, switchgear buses and cables — megger/PI, AC or DC hipot, and power-factor tip-up on stator insulation; access through cable boxes, terminal cabinets and collector rings in a plant kept to housekeeping standards.

Utility repair shop or test laboratory: bench testing of bushings, insulators, arresters or CTs removed from service — mount on a stand, connect test set, apply voltage, measure charging and loss current, calculate capacitance and dissipation factor against nameplate.

Energized overhead line / switchyard structure: condition testing of insulator strings and station post insulators from a bucket, ladder or structure using a hot-stick insulator tester or contact resistance probe to find punctured or zero-value units, in weather and at height.

sources.system: Marposs in-line electrical test station for cylindrical battery cells (robotic loading + HV insulation test)
sources.title: In-Line Electrical Test Of Cylindrical Battery Cells | Marposs
sources.claim: Marposs supplies commercial in-line test cells in which a robot picks cells from a pallet, makes the electrical connection itself, and the station performs a high-voltage electrical insulation test — a fully machine-executed apply-voltage/measure-current insulation test in a purpose-built production cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated end-of-line insulation (hipot) testing of manufactured electrical parts. It transfers to this task's E1 counterfactual because the machine itself makes the high-voltage contact to a fixtured workpiece, impresses test voltage across the insulation and evaluates the resulting current — the same physical operation as testing a bushing or insulator presented in a test fixture.

sources.system: Marposs e.d.c. AST320/W automatic testing system for stators and windings
sources.title: Automatic Testing System for Stator and Windings - AST320/W | Marposs
sources.claim: Marposs e.d.c. AST320/W is a commercial automatic test system for production testing of windings, coils and stators, performing AC high-pot, surge and partial-discharge measurements to identify winding-to-ground and turn-to-turn insulation problems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dielectric/insulation testing of rotating-machine windings on a production line. Same electrical quantities (applied HV, leakage/partial-discharge current, pass-fail on insulation condition) as powerhouse generator and motor insulation testing, with the workpiece presented to the machine.

sources.system: Marposs PEM fuel cell stack assembly module high voltage test bench
sources.title: Electrical Test - PEM FUEL CELL STACK ASSEMBLY MODULE HIGH VOLTAGE TEST | Marposs
sources.claim: Marposs builds fully enclosed single-station benches whose measurement principle is insulation resistance and dielectric strength via an integrated hipot tester, with automatic door and automated cycle, for high-voltage testing of fuel-cell stack assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated insulation-resistance and dielectric-withstand testing of an assembly inside a guarded test cell. Demonstrates that, with the workpiece fixtured and guarded, energizing insulation and evaluating current is a routine machine operation, as required for the E1 counterfactual of the substation and shop instances.

sources.system: Megger DELTA4000 series 12 kV power factor / tan delta test set
sources.title: DELTA4000 12 kV Tan Delta & Power Factor Diagnostic System | Megger
sources.claim: The Megger DELTA4000 is a fully automatic 12 kV insulation power-factor / dissipation-factor (tan delta) test set that energizes the insulation, measures the resulting current and computes loss for transformers, bushings, circuit breakers, cables and rotating machinery — i.e., the induce-voltage/measure-current/calculate-loss core of the task is machine-executed once connected.
sources.transferJustification: Not a manipulator: cited only for the measurement-and-calculation portion (voltage application, current measurement, dielectric-loss computation) on exactly the apparatus named in the task — bushings, transformers, breakers, rotating machinery — once leads are presented as a purpose-built cell would present them.

sources.system: Avangrid/United Illuminating 'Sparky' (Boston Dynamics Spot) substation inspection robot
sources.title: Avangrid Pilots Mobile Robot Dog to Advance Substation Inspections with AI
sources.claim: Mobile robots actually deployed in US substations perform camera, thermal and acoustic inspection of transformers, breakers and capacitor banks; the robot was initially driven by an on-site operator with a tablet. No contact electrical testing or test-lead connection is performed.

sources.system: Insulator detection robot for 500 kV / UHVDC insulator strings
sources.developer: Chinese grid research institutes (State Grid affiliated), published in Electric Power Systems Research / EAI Energy Web
sources.title: Design and construction of a new insulator detection robot for application in 500 kV strings: Electric field analysis and field testing
sources.claim: Research robots that climb energized 500 kV / UHVDC insulator strings to measure per-disc resistance and identify zero-value insulators have been field tested, but they are placed on the string by workers and their motion is monitored/controlled remotely via video, so end-to-end autonomy is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field analogue to insulator condition testing, but autonomy is unclear and the robot must be installed on the string by a worker, so per the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Schedule and supervise splicing or termination of cables in color-code order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Planning and scheduling: in the substation control house or a district office, the repairer sequences control-cable termination work for a relay panel replacement against outage windows, crew availability, and cable-pulling completion, and issues the work schedule.

Pre-job briefing: the repairer walks the termination crew through the elementary and connection diagrams and the applicable color-code/wire-numbering convention before work begins at a new or retrofitted relay panel, assigning which conductors each person lands.

On-site oversight during termination: the repairer observes crew members landing multiconductor control cable on terminal blocks in an energized substation control house, monitors progress against the schedule, answers questions on ambiguous conductor identification, and directs rework where the color code was not followed.

Acceptance and sign-off: the repairer reviews completed terminations against the as-built point-to-point wiring list, notes discrepancies for correction, and documents completion for the outage record.

Coordination with outside parties: the repairer schedules and oversees a contractor or telecom crew splicing fiber or pilot-wire cable entering the substation, coordinating access, timing, and color-code/fiber-buffer conventions.

tasks.label: Test oil in circuit breakers and transformers for dielectric strength, refilling oil periodically.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled oil sample drawn from an in-service oil-filled power transformer at an outdoor transmission/distribution substation: locate and open the bottom sampling valve, flush/purge waste oil, draw an air-free sample into a syringe or glass bottle, seal, label and log it, close the valve, wipe up drips, and deliver the sample for dielectric-strength testing. Energized equipment nearby, gravel yard, weather, PPE and clearance rules.

Running the dielectric breakdown test (ASTM D877/D1816, IEC 60156) on a collected oil sample with a portable or bench oil test set in the substation control house, a test van, or the utility shop lab: clean and reassemble the test vessel, polish and set the electrode gap, pour the sample, let it settle, run the sequence of breakdowns, read and average the result, record it against the asset, drain and clean the cell.

Outage maintenance on an oil circuit breaker or load-tap changer in a generating station or substation: draw oil from the breaker/LTC tank drain valve, test its dielectric strength, judge carbon/moisture contamination, then filter or replace and refill the tank to the correct level and re-seal.

Periodic refilling/topping off of insulating oil on a substation transformer or breaker: position drums or an oil filter/degassing cart, connect hoses to the fill valve, pump (often under vacuum) to bring the level gauge into range, bleed air, monitor pressure and level, disconnect, and clean up spills.

Oil check and sampling on smaller oil-filled units away from a controlled yard - pad-mounted or pole-top transformers, reclosers or regulators on public right-of-way, customer premises, or units pulled after storm damage - with variable access, terrain, clutter, and no fixed layout.

sources.title: OTS PB vs OTS AF: Which Megger oil test set is right for you? | Megger

sources.claim: A commercial PLC/SCADA-controlled transformer oil treatment and filling plant dries, degasses and filters oil to restore dielectric strength and performs oil filling and transfer into transformers, running unattended with safety interlocks once hoses are connected, including on energized units.

sources.title: Robotic Fuelling System | Haul Trucks, Mining Trucks, Trains and AGVs
sources.claim: A containerized robotic fuelling station autonomously positions itself to a vehicle's fill port, attaches a dry-break nozzle, transfers hundreds of litres per minute of fluid and disconnects; in service at mine fuel bays.

Robotic coupling of a nozzle to a vehicle fill port and metered dispensing is the same physical operation as connecting to a transformer fill valve and pumping oil to level - comparable object scale, coupling precision and dirty outdoor-but-controlled bay conditions.

tasks.label: Disconnect voltage regulators, bolts, and screws, and connect replacement regulators to high-voltage lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Replacing a failed single-phase step voltage regulator in a bank at an outdoor distribution substation: after switching/bypassing, de-energizing and grounding, the tech breaks bolted bus/riser terminal connections and the ground strap, disconnects the control cable at the conduit, unbolts the ~2-8 ton oil-filled unit from its pad or steel stand, rigs it out with a boom truck/crane, sets and bolts down the replacement, torques the aluminum/copper terminal bolts to spec with anti-oxidant, reconnects the control cable, and tests before re-energizing. Gravel yard, energized adjacent equipment, weather exposure.

Replacing a pole- or platform-mounted line voltage regulator on a 12-25 kV distribution feeder in a road right-of-way or rural easement: bypass switching with cutouts/bypass switch, bucket truck plus digger derrick, removing bushing terminal bolts/hot-line clamps and jumper leads, unbolting the regulator from its pole bracket or platform, hoisting down the old unit and hoisting up the replacement, bolting connections to primary conductors and neutral, landing the control cable. Traffic control, uneven ground, variable pole framing.

Shop/service-center work on regulators in a utility test bay: a spare or rebuilt regulator is set on a stand, high-voltage leads and control cabling are bolted/screwed to its bushings and terminal board for test or for prep before field installation, and the tech breaks and remakes those connections. Indoor, fixtured lifting equipment, controlled conditions.

In-place replacement of a regulator's control and accessories rather than the tank: opening the control cabinet, removing mounting screws and panel hardware, disconnecting the multi-pin control cable and terminal-block wiring, swapping the electronic tap-changer control or position transmitter, re-landing the small-gauge wiring, and verifying tap operation. Performed in a substation yard on the regulator's cabinet.

Emergency storm/outage replacement of a burned or leaking regulator: night or bad weather, oil spill containment, heat-damaged or seized bolts and clamps that must be cut or torched off, bent mounting hardware, damaged jumpers of unknown condition, roadside or easement location with crews working under time pressure to restore load.

sources.system: Fori Automation Robotic Chassis Marriage system
sources.title: Robotic Chassis Marriage - Fori Automation
sources.claim: Commercial robotic chassis-marriage cells lift heavy vehicle modules into position and perform automated fastening in a fixtured, fenced production cell — the closest analogue to setting a heavy apparatus on a mount and bolting it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing a heavy sub-assembly onto a structure and torquing its bolted joints. It transfers to setting and bolting a regulator only under E1 conditions — the workpiece fixtured and presented in a known position, as in this cell.
