sources.transferJustification: Related task: torquing a bolted mechanical joint to spec under vision guidance. Comparable fastener sizes and torque control to regulator terminal/mounting bolts, but demonstrated only in a fixtured production cell.

sources.system: Inbolt GuideNOW with FANUC streaming motion
sources.title: Fanuc and Inbolt launch AI-powered robots for real-time assembly line automation
sources.claim: A commercially launched AI vision system for FANUC robots supports bolt rundown, screw insertion and part insertion on assembly lines with variable part position.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving bolts and screws into parts whose position varies. Supports the fastening portion of regulator replacement at E1, where the unit is presented in an industrial work station.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Battery Disassembly: The Design and Implementation of a Battery Disassembly Autonomous Mobile Manipulator Robot (BEAM-1)
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile manipulator removes bolts of multiple types from used, non-pristine end-of-life EV battery packs, perceiving and planning without pre-programmed sequences, with 98.78% success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unbolting a used piece of equipment whose fasteners vary in type and condition — the 'disconnect bolts and screws' half of this task — demonstrated in a fixtured disassembly station, i.e. an E1 setting.

sources.system: Averex wiring center (Rittal/Kiesling); Rittal collaborative-robot wiring cell
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems

sources.transferJustification: Related task: landing small-gauge wires on cabinet terminals and screw terminals — the control-wiring portion of a regulator/control swap — but only in a purpose-built machine that holds the cabinet in a fixed position.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: breaking and remaking bolted high-voltage bus connections in a substation. It covers only a sub-step: it handles light steel plate fittings, not rigging, mounting or control wiring of a multi-ton regulator, so it cannot complete the whole instance.

tasks.label: Estimate costs of repairs, based on parts and labor charges.

tasks.label: Install equipment and accessories, such as stereos, navigation equipment, communication equipment, and security systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail 12-volt / car-audio shop bay: install an aftermarket head unit plus speakers or an amplifier in a customer's car. Pry off dash bezel, kick panels and door cards without breaking clips, fit a dash kit, connect a vehicle-specific harness adapter (crimp/solder in older cars), route power and signal cable under carpet to a trunk amp, ground to chassis, reassemble trim rattle-free, test.

Aftermarket security system / remote start / alarm install in a shop bay: work upside-down under the dash, tap the ignition harness or CAN data bus with an interface module, hide the brain behind the dash, mount the siren in the engine bay, route valet switch, hood pin and LED, program the immobilizer bypass and key, verify no stored fault codes.

Fleet telematics / GPS tracker / dash cam installation on vans, pickups and trucks at a fleet depot or service shop: mostly hardwired (fuse-box or ignition-harness tap, ground, sometimes CAN connection), plus camera or antenna mounting, wire routed behind A-pillar and headliner, loomed and zip-tied, device activation confirmed; a minority are plug-in OBD-II dongles.

Emergency-vehicle or commercial upfit at an upfitting facility: install mobile two-way radio and control head, roof or trunk-lid antenna (drill and seal a hole), console, siren and lighting controller; run heavy-gauge power through the firewall to the battery, fuse and ground it, secure cables clear of airbags, then function-test the radio and program channels.

New-vehicle accessory installation at a dealership prep area or port: repetitive same-model kits (remote start, backup camera, navigation/telematics module, satellite radio), partial dash/console/trim disassembly, plug-and-play kit harness, module mounting, then programming/configuration with a factory scan tool and a road-ready quality check.

Mobile installation at the customer's driveway, office parking lot or a job site: same head-unit, camera, radio or tracker work performed outdoors from a service van, in variable weather and light, on whatever vehicle is parked there, with no lift and only a portable toolkit.

sources.system: Nissan Tochigi six-axis headliner installation robots / automotive final-assembly automation state

sources.transferJustification: Closest industrial analogue to in-vehicle equipment installation: even in a purpose-built fixtured line (E1) running identical vehicles, automated installation of interior electronics is not done; robotic interior work is limited to placing large modules such as headliners.

tasks.label: Inspect and test electrical or electronic systems to locate and diagnose malfunctions, using visual inspections and testing instruments, such as oscilloscopes and voltmeters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop install bay: customer vehicle with an aftermarket audio system fault (amp in protect, one channel dead). Tech pulls kick panels/seat trim, back-probes power, ground and remote-turn-on leads with a DMM/test light, checks RCA signal, isolates the failed wire, connection or component.

Shop install bay: aftermarket security/remote-start or keyless module malfunction. Tech works behind the dash in confined space, scopes CAN/LIN or door-trigger signals with an oscilloscope, back-probes module connector pins against a wiring diagram, and localizes a bad splice, T-harness pin or failed module.

Dealership or fleet service stall: factory/aftermarket nav, backup camera, telematics or upfitter electronics fault. Tech connects a scan tool at the OBD-II port, pulls DTCs, then confirms with a voltmeter at the module connector and inspects connectors/grounds for corrosion or damage.

Mobile service call at a customer driveway, curbside or employer parking lot: diagnose a dead stereo, alarm or fleet camera install with a handheld meter and test light, in variable weather, lighting and vehicle positions, with no lift and limited tooling.

Shop bench: unit removed from the vehicle (amplifier, head unit, aftermarket module). Tech powers it from a bench supply, checks for protect/no-power, then uses DMM and oscilloscope on the board to find blown fuses, shorted output devices or a failed supply rail before repair or replace decision.

Vehicle-wide visual inspection plus continuity checks of a previously installed harness in a van, truck or bus: crawling under the vehicle and behind panels looking for chafed insulation, corroded connectors, loose grounds, and confirming circuits with a meter.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers (e.g. SPEA 4080) / in-circuit testers
sources.title: In-Circuit Testing: How ICT Detects PCB Defects [2026] | SPEA
sources.claim: Commercial flying-probe in-circuit testers autonomously move probes over an assembled board inside the machine and contact test points to detect electrical board defects, without a custom fixture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating electrical faults on an electronic assembly with contact instrumentation. It transfers to bench diagnosis of a removed car-audio/module board because the objects (populated PCBAs), the measurements (continuity, resistance, powered checks) and the required probe precision are the same; it does not transfer to work inside a vehicle.

sources.system: Seica Pilot V8 flying probe tester
sources.title: How flying probe testing works for PCB assembly | Sierra Circuits
sources.claim: A flying probe tester in production use at a PCB assembler tests for opens, shorts, resistance, capacitance, ... and micro-shorts under program control, i.e. it locates the specific defective net or component.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fault localization on electronic assemblies by instrumented probing. Same class of hardware and measurements a technician makes on a removed head unit or amplifier board at the bench; environment is the machine's own load area, not a vehicle interior.

sources.system: Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System (Dobot Magician + Arduino measurement platform)
sources.title: Implementation of a Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System (IJARIS)
sources.claim: A research system pairs a robotic arm with an instrumentation module to autonomously probe PCB test points, measure voltage and resistance, and identify open circuits, short circuits and wrong component values.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as bench electrical testing with a voltmeter: robotic probing of defined test points and comparison against expected values. Probe positions are taught in advance and the board sits in a fixed jig, so it supports only a purpose-built bench cell.

sources.system: Rocsys ROC-1 / M1 autonomous charging robot
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M | Electrek
sources.claim: Robotic systems can autonomously locate and mate a connector on a parked vehicle in an institutional facility (ports, depots, robotaxi charging bays), but the function is charging, not instrumented fault diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connector mating on a vehicle exterior. It shows the boundary of current capability — a large standardized exterior port under good access — and does not substantiate under-dash trim removal, back-probing harness pins, oscilloscope work, or reasoning to a root-cause fault.

sources.system: SmartBay robotic tire change platform
sources.title: Automated Tire, Inc. Emerges from Stealth, Reveals SmartBay, the World's First Robotic AI-Powered Tire Change Platform
sources.claim: The only robotic system reported working inside a US vehicle service bay handles tire changing; no comparable service-bay system performs electrical or electronic fault diagnosis on vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to characterize the state of service-bay robotics: it is wheel/tire manipulation at the vehicle exterior and involves no electrical measurement, connector back-probing or fault reasoning, so it cannot substantiate this task.

tasks.label: Diagnose or repair problems with electronic equipment, such as sound, navigation, communication, and security equipment, in motor vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bay: customer complains of intermittent/no sound from an aftermarket audio system. Tech verifies the symptom, pulls kick panels, dash trim and under-dash covers, probes power, ground and speaker leads with a DMM, isolates a chafed wire, bad ground or failed amplifier, repairs by solder/crimp/heat-shrink, reassembles trim and re-verifies.

Dealer/independent shop bay: OEM infotainment, navigation or telematics fault (frozen screen, no GPS, module not communicating). Tech connects a factory-level scan tool, reads DTCs and network status, checks module power/ground and CAN lines at the connector, then reflashes software or removes and replaces the module behind the dash and configures/programs it.

Shop bay: failed component swap on a vehicle — blown door speaker, dead backup camera, broken antenna or damaged tweeter. Tech removes door panel or hatch trim (screws, hidden clips, connectors), unplugs and unmounts the failed part, fits the replacement, routes/secures wiring, reinstalls trim without rattles or damage, verifies operation.

Shop bay: security/alarm, remote start or keyless-entry troubleshooting on a previously installed system — tracing add-on wiring spliced into the vehicle harness under the dash, finding a miswired or failed control module or immobilizer bypass, correcting the wiring, reprogramming remotes and confirming arm/disarm and start functions.

Mobile/on-site service in a customer driveway, parking lot or fleet yard: diagnose and fix a two-way radio, GPS tracker/telematics unit, dash camera or upfit electronics in a work truck or van. Varied vehicle types, no lift, ambient weather and lighting, tools carried to the vehicle.

sources.system: survey of automotive-service robots (RoboTire, 3M Finesse-it, Rolls-Royce snake robots, Audi telepresence, Kitov)
sources.title: Robots are primed to replace auto mechanics (or are they?) | Electronics360
sources.claim: Trade-press review of automation in vehicle service concludes there is no automated system that performs full-service vehicle maintenance/inspection; shops would need many separate machines to cover what one mechanic does.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about automation of vehicle diagnosis and repair, the same work domain as this task; establishes absence of whole-job automated diagnostic repair systems.

sources.system: Kitov-CorePlus
sources.title: Robots are primed to replace auto mechanics (or are they?) | Electronics360
sources.claim: Kitov-CorePlus autonomously performs visual inspection of automotive electronics defects (bent connector pins, missing components) on the vehicle production line — narrow defect detection in a purpose-built inspection cell, not fault isolation or repair of installed audio/navigation systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated inspection of automotive electronics. It covers only camera-visible surface/connector defects on production-line units; it does not remove trim, probe circuits, reason to a root cause, or effect a repair, so it cannot complete a diagnose-and-repair instance.

sources.system: RoboTire System (4th generation)
sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced automation actually running in customer-facing automotive service bays changes wheels/tires; RoboTire's system removes, lifts and installs wheel assemblies at Discount Tire stores while technicians oversee it and perform the remaining service steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated work on customer vehicles in a shop bay (E2). It shows shop-bay robots exist, but only for a single fixture-friendly mechanical operation on the vehicle exterior; nothing transfers to interior trim removal, harness probing or electronic fault reasoning.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: As of May 2026 the newest service-bay robotic platform still targets only tire changing plus vehicle inspection, and its first generation does not fully automate even the mounting/airing/balancing sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic servicing of customer vehicles in a service bay. Current-generation capability is limited to wheel/tire work and visual inspection, indicating no shop robot performs electronic-system diagnosis or repair.

sources.system: Figure 02
sources.title: BMW Group bringing Physical AI to Europe — Pilot project at BMW Group Plant Leipzig (BMW Group PressClub)
sources.claim: The frontier of humanoid robot work in automotive facilities is repetitive, precisely specified part handling at a fixed station: Figure 02 spent ten months at BMW Spartanburg removing and positioning sheet metal parts for welding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose humanoid manipulation in an automotive facility. Demonstrated scope is single-step pick-and-place of known parts at an engineered station, far short of open-ended electrical troubleshooting, trim disassembly and repair inside a vehicle cabin.

tasks.label: Splice wires with knives or cutting pliers, and solder connections to fixtures and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop install bay: 12V installer works under the dash/steering column of a customer's vehicle integrating a remote start, alarm or stereo interface — identifies specific circuits in the factory loom by color/test light, cuts and strips them with a knife or cutting pliers, splices and solders the module leads, heat-shrinks and tapes, then loom-wraps and secures. Cramped, inverted access around live 12V wiring, ducts and airbag modules; harness layout differs by make/model/year.

Workbench in the shop: installer pre-builds harness adapters and leads off the vehicle — strips and Western-Union/lap splices conductors, solders joints with an iron, applies heat shrink, terminates ring/spade terminals and connector pins for radio, amplifier power/RCA and camera leads. Work held in a vise or helping hands on a lit bench.

In-vehicle body work: splicing and soldering speaker leads at door panels, kick panels, A-pillars and rear cargo areas — panels partly removed, wires fed through grommets and behind trim, joints soldered and insulated in confined, poorly lit cavities of the customer vehicle.

Fleet/upfitter facility: repetitive batch installs of two-way radios, lightbars, telematics and cameras in identical vehicles at a dedicated upfitting bay — same documented splice points on each unit, power/ignition leads soldered or crimp-spliced to the factory harness, sealed and secured to a fleet standard.

Mobile/field service: technician works at a customer's driveway, fleet yard or job site — splices and solders connections in a truck, RV, trailer or boat harness (trailer lighting, backup camera, radio power), outdoors with variable light, weather, dirt and no fixed bench.

sources.system: Komax Omega 740/750 with ultrasonic splice module
sources.title: Omega 740/750: Now fully automatic ultrasonic splicing | Komax
sources.claim: Komax Omega 740/750 wire-assembly machines produce automotive wire harnesses fully automatically, including cutting/stripping, terminal insertion into housings and ultrasonic splicing, with automatic splice quality checking — the splice step of this task performed by machine in a fixtured production cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical operation as the task (cutting, stripping and splicing insulated automotive-gauge wire), performed on harness wires identical in kind to those an installer splices, but with the wires presented in machine fixtures.

sources.system: MRC500 automatic wire soldering cell
sources.title: MRC500 automatic wire soldering cell
sources.claim: A commercially offered robotic cell cuts, strips, positions and solders a wire automatically, combining an automatic wire-stripping unit with a collaborative robot and a 150 W soldering iron head.

sources.system: Apollo Seiko tip and laser soldering robots
sources.title: New Benefits with Automated Soldering Innovations - Wiring Harness News
sources.claim: Apollo Seiko soldering robots are used in production for wire-lead assemblies — filling solder cups on connectors and soldering wire leads to boards and connectors — the soldering-to-fixtures-and-equipment half of this task, done in a fixtured machine cell.
sources.transferJustification: Soldering stranded wire leads into connector solder cups and onto boards is the same joining operation, on the same conductor sizes, as soldering connections to fixtures and equipment in a vehicle.

sources.system: KURASENSE Kurassem-WH / SR robot package
sources.title: Robot Package (Kurassem) Kurassem-WH (Wire Harness Manufacturing) / SR (Automatic Soldering) | KURASENSE
sources.claim: A vision-guided robot package singulates one wire from a bundle, crimps a terminal and inserts it into a connector in about 10 seconds, and can be configured with soldering stations in the same cell.
sources.transferJustification: Picking an individual wire out of a bundle and terminating it is the manipulation an installer performs when isolating one conductor from a loom, here done by 3D-vision robot with the bundle presented in the cell.

sources.system: KK1012 heat shrink tubing machine
sources.title: Heat Shrink Tubing Machine – Automated Wire Protection - Cablemachineries
sources.claim: Machines automate the feeding, cutting and shrinking ... sleeving onto wires for automotive harness work, covering the insulate-and-seal finishing step that closes out a soldered splice.
sources.transferJustification: Insulating the completed splice with heat shrink is the closing step of the human task; this machine performs it on the same wire types in a fixtured feed.

sources.system: Skill-based robotic connector installation system
sources.title: Automotive Wire Harness Connector Installation Using Skill-Based Robotic Programming
sources.claim: Robotic wire-harness work inside an actual vehicle body remains a research demonstration: a force-controlled connector installation skill validated on a car door reached only 76.7% success.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available in-vehicle wiring work; cited only to show that harness manipulation on a real car body is demo-stage and below worker reliability, not to support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Run new speaker and electrical cables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aftermarket audio upgrade in a customer's car in a shop bay: run new speaker wire from the head-unit/amp location to four door speakers — pop off sill plates and kick panels, pull back carpet, feed wire through the rubber door-jamb boot into the door cavity, tuck the run away from moving parts and factory harnesses, secure with loom/zip ties and leave service slack at each end. Vehicle model and interior layout differ with every job.

Run heavy-gauge amplifier power cable in a shop bay: locate or drill a firewall pass-through, install grommet, feed 4- or 0-gauge cable from the battery through the firewall, route it the length of the cabin under sill trim/carpet to the trunk amp location, separated from the RCA/signal runs, plus ground cable and remote turn-on wire; fuse near battery.

Accessory retrofit wiring at the shop (backup camera, dash cam hardwire, remote start, radar detector, subwoofer): run a small-gauge cable from the tailgate/rear of the vehicle forward through headliner, A/B/C-pillar trim or under carpet to the dash, threading through existing grommets and body pass-throughs without disturbing airbags or factory harnesses.

Mobile install at the customer's driveway, workplace parking lot or street: same speaker/power cable runs performed on an unfamiliar vehicle outdoors, with variable light, weather, ground surface and no bench, lift or fixed tooling.

Fleet/commercial upfit at an upfitter or fleet garage: run power, antenna and speaker/siren cables for two-way radios, telematics units, light bars or PA speakers in a batch of identical vehicles to a standard build sheet, using pre-made harnesses and dedicated bays; still routed through the assembled vehicle's firewall, sills, pillars and headliner.

Bench prep of the cable run before it goes in the vehicle: measure, cut and sleeve speaker/power cable lengths, bundle and loom them into a made-up run with terminals/connectors fitted, on a workbench in the shop.

sources.system: Robotized wire harness assembly (state-of-the-art survey of vision-based robotic systems)
sources.title: Overview of Computer Vision Techniques in Robotized Wire Harness Assembly: Current State and Future Opportunities
sources.claim: Survey of robotized wire-harness assembly based on observation in a car manufacturing plant reports that routing the harness inside the car body and fixing/connecting it are still done manually, even though upstream steps are automated; this is the purpose-built (E1) version of running cables through a vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing/routing automotive wire harnesses in the car body. Same objects (flexible insulated cable bundles), same vehicle interior geometry and clip/grommet precision as running speaker and power cable; it is the most automation-friendly version of the task and it remains manual.

sources.system: Dual-arm robotic wire harness assembly system (ROS/Omron safety-PLC cell, dual-arm robot)
sources.developer: Tampere University (Malvido Fresnillo et al.), Journal of Manufacturing Systems
sources.title: A dual-arm robotic system for automated multi-branch wire harness assembly in automotive industry
sources.claim: State-of-the-art dual-arm robotic cell for automotive multi-branch wire harness assembly, evaluated in a purpose-built industrial cell, achieved only 55% and 73% end-to-end success; the paper states harness assembly remains largely manual and existing solutions are fragmented and economically unviable for high-mix work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly and routing of automotive wire harness branches. Same deformable insulated cables and clip/branch routing precision required to run speaker and power cable; reported success rates are far below the reliability a shop would accept.

sources.system: Multi-stage cable routing hierarchical imitation learning system (Franka arm, wrist+top cameras)
sources.developer: Berkeley AI Research (UC Berkeley) with Intrinsic Innovation LLC
sources.title: Multi-Stage Cable Routing through Hierarchical Imitation Learning
sources.claim: Best-known learned system for autonomously routing a cable through a sequence of clips works on a benchtop fixture with three clips; per-clip insertion succeeds 46% of the time and full-task performance reaches only about 85% after per-configuration finetuning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing a cable through a series ..., the canonical laboratory analogue of running a cable along a fixed path. Even on an open benchtop board with visible clips — far easier than a vehicle's hidden channels, boots and grommets — reliability is well below worker quality.

sources.system: Q5D CY1000 wiring automation cell
sources.title: Automated EV Wiring Harness Assembly | Q5D CY1000 Robot
sources.claim: Commercial 5-axis robotic cell that automatically lays insulated conductors and connectors onto fixtured parts and sub-assemblies, terminating wires into connectors; as of 2025 it is being used to build the wiring in the roof lining of ... in a small production run.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated laying, securing and terminating of insulated conductors along defined routes on a fixtured automotive part. Comparable objects (speaker/power gauge wire), comparable routing/termination precision, performed in a purpose-built cell — this matches bench-made-up cable runs, not routing inside an assembled vehicle.

tasks.label: Remove seats, carpeting, and interiors of doors and add sound-absorbing material in empty spaces, reinstalling interior parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-cabin sound treatment on a customer's passenger car in a 12-volt/car-audio shop bay: unbolt and lift out front and rear seats (disconnecting airbag/occupancy-sensor and seat-belt buckle connectors), pull console trim and carpet, clean the floor pan, cut and roll butyl/foil damping mats plus closed-cell foam into footwells and transmission tunnel, then reinstall carpet, console and seats to torque with no fault lights, rattles, or trim damage.

Doors-only treatment done with a speaker or door-speaker upgrade in the shop: remove door trim panels of a specific make/model (hidden screws behind trim caps, plastic clips, window switch and courtesy-light connectors, cable-operated handles), peel back the factory vapor barrier, apply damping to the outer and inner door skins around window regulator cutouts, reseal the barrier, and reinstall the panel without broken clips or wind noise.

Trunk, hatch cargo area, or rear deck treatment accompanying a subwoofer/amplifier install in the shop: remove trunk liners, spare-tire cover, rear-deck speaker grilles and quarter trim, apply damping mats to sheet metal panels and wheel wells, then reinstall all trim panels and fasteners.

Commercial fleet or specialty vehicle work at a fleet/upfit shop: cargo van, box truck, ambulance or RV in which floor covering, bulkhead and wall panels are removed, insulation/sound-absorbing material is added into cavities and empty spaces, and panels, flooring and seats are reinstalled around wiring runs and equipment racks.

Mobile installer working at the customer's location (driveway, office parking lot, or parking garage) with a portable tool kit: removes door panels or seats and carpet on the spot, applies sound deadening, and reinstalls, working in variable weather, lighting, and uncontrolled surroundings.

sources.system: Industrial robots in vehicle final trim & assembly (FTA)
sources.developer: Automotive OEMs / robot suppliers (reported by Automotive Interiors World)
sources.title: Exclusive: Improving interior assembly using robots that 'feel'
sources.claim: Even inside purpose-built automotive final trim and assembly lines — the most structured possible setting for interior work — robotic automation of interior fit-out remains below 5%, versus up to 95% in body-in-white and paint, because of fit/finish complexity and damage risk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing vehicle interior trim, carpet and seats on an assembly line. It involves the same objects and precision as the reinstall half of this task, in a fully fixtured E1 line; the reported <5% automation rate shows no cited system performs it, and removal from an already-assembled used vehicle is strictly harder.

sources.system: Automotive final assembly trim lines
sources.title: Beyond the Welding Line: Robots and Automotive Assembly
sources.claim: In automotive final assembly, carpeting, door trim, instrument panels and seats are installed manually by operators; interior trim work is described as the remaining frontier of automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fitting carpet, door trim and seats into a car body on a fixtured line — the same handling and fastening skills this task requires when reinstalling interior parts. It is still manual even at E1, so no cited system supports the instance.

sources.system: ABB Liquid Applied Sound Damper (LASD) robotic application
sources.title: Paint solutions for Automotive | ABB
sources.claim: Robotic application of sound-damping material is deployed and autonomous, but only as liquid spray onto empty painted bodies-in-white in paint shops; adhesive damping pads of the kind used in retrofit interiors are applied manually.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying sound-deadening material to vehicle sheet metal. Transfer is only partial — the robot sprays an empty, fixtured body shell in a paint booth and performs no removal, cutting, rolling, or reinstallation of seats, carpet and door trim, so it cannot complete this task's whole instance.

sources.system: Damping pad vs. LASD application in vehicle body construction
sources.developer: Automotive body shops / material suppliers (reported by ASSEMBLY Magazine)
sources.title: Liquid applied sound deadening materials | Assembly Magazine
sources.claim: Damping pads (the mat-type material used in aftermarket sound-deadening jobs) are applied manually; only the liquid spray variant is robotized.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching sound-damping mats to vehicle panels — exactly the material handling in this task. The source shows pad application remains manual labor even in OEM paint shops, so no cited robotic system does it.

sources.system: Figure 03 humanoid robot
sources.title: BMW deploys Figure humanoid robot at US factory
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid robots deployed in automotive plants as of mid-2026 are doing parts sorting and sequencing and sheet-metal part loading, not interior trim removal or installation inside vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general dexterous manipulation work inside a car plant. The deployed scope (sorting/sequencing parts) shows current general-purpose humanoids are not performing confined-space trim disassembly, connector handling, or fastener removal inside vehicle cabins.

sources.system: Manual interior trim panel removal practice (baseline human method)
sources.title: Learn how to remove interior trim panels — Dent Hero
sources.claim: Interior door panel removal is a model-specific, learned manual skill involving hidden fasteners, fragile appliqué and sensors, with methods that vary greatly from vehicle to vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Baseline description of the task itself rather than a robotic system; used only to characterize the object variability and delicacy that no cited robotic system has been shown to handle.

tasks.label: Replace and clean electrical or electronic components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a shop bay, replace a failed in-dash head unit / navigation-infotainment unit in a customer's vehicle: pry off dash trim and bezels, remove mounting screws and brackets, unplug wiring harness, antenna and camera leads, swap in the replacement unit, reassemble trim, verify function.

In a shop bay, replace an amplifier, speaker, subwoofer, alarm/remote-start or telematics module mounted under a seat, behind a door panel, in a kick panel or in the trunk: remove interior panels and fasteners, disconnect and re-dress harnesses, mount and connect the replacement, refit panels.

On the vehicle, clean and service electrical connections: corroded battery terminals and ground straps, oxidized connector pins, fuse-box and relay-socket contacts, ground points behind panels; brush/contact cleaner/dielectric grease, re-terminate or replace damaged terminals, retest circuits.

In a shop bay, quick swaps of small electrical parts on the vehicle: blown fuses, relays, inline fuse holders, antenna masts and GPS/satellite antennas, backup-camera modules, lamp/LED assemblies, small pigtails - accessed in fuse boxes, engine bay, under dash or on exterior body.

Bench work in the shop: on a unit removed from the vehicle (car amplifier, radio, module), replace a failed board-level component (capacitor, MOSFET, connector) by desoldering and resoldering, and clean the board and contacts before reinstallation.

Mobile/field service at a customer's driveway, home garage, or a fleet yard: replace a failed component (radio, remote-start module, dash camera, corroded connector) on-site with a portable kit, in whatever lighting, weather and vehicle condition is found.

sources.system: Ersa HR 600P automatic rework system
sources.title: New high-end rework system with automatic residual solder removal
sources.claim: Commercial automated SMT rework systems desolder a failed component from a fixtured circuit board, remove residual solder, dispense paste/flux, place the replacement with vision alignment and reflow it automatically to plus/minus 50 um placement quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = board-level rework in electronics manufacturing/repair. It transfers to bench-level component replacement on a car amplifier or radio board: same class of objects (SMD/through-hole parts on a PCB), same or finer precision, and the board is fixtured in the machine exactly as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: I.C.T-5600 PCBA cleaning / defluxing machine
sources.title: PCBA Cleaning Machine / PCB Defluxing - For Best Coating and Bonding Effect - I.C.T SMT Machine
sources.claim: Batch PCBA cleaning machines run the full clean-rinse-dry cycle on loaded boards automatically, covering the 'clean the board/contacts' portion of bench-level electronic component servicing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = defluxing/cleaning assembled boards in electronics production. Same objects (populated PCBs) and same acceptance criterion (residue-free board) as cleaning a removed automotive audio board on the bench.

sources.system: NIO Power Swap Station 4.0
sources.title: NIO's New Battery Swap Station 4.0 Is Faster, Bigger And Automatic
sources.claim: A vehicle electrical module can be exchanged fully automatically only where both vehicle and module are engineered for machine handling: NIO's swap station removes and installs a traction battery pack in about 144 seconds with the car parked on a purpose-built platform.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = replacing an electrical component in a motor vehicle. It does NOT transfer to this task's instances: the pack has a standardized quick-change interface at a known underbody location designed for swapping, whereas head units, amplifiers and connectors require trim/panel disassembly, hidden fasteners and harness handling on arbitrary used vehicles.

sources.system: RAPID (Robotic Agentic Platform for Intelligent Disassembly)
sources.developer: Correll Lab, University of Colorado Boulder
sources.title: Robotic Agentic Platform for Intelligent Electric Vehicle Disassembly | Correll lab
sources.claim: Removing fasteners and components from a real vehicle assembly is still a research problem even inside a purpose-built gantry cell; the CU Boulder RAPID platform investigates perception-driven fastener removal on an EV battery pack and is described as working toward increasingly autonomous workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic disassembly of vehicle assemblies. Cited to show the state of the art for machine removal of vehicle-mounted components is a lab gantry cell with human-in-the-loop programming, not repair-quality component replacement.

sources.system: Figure 02 humanoid at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg
sources.title: BMW Group bringing Physical AI to Europe - Pilot project at BMW Group Plant Leipzig
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid deployment inside automotive plants performed only pick-and-place of sheet-metal parts into fixtures; no deployed humanoid performs vehicle interior disassembly, connector work or electronic component replacement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = humanoid manipulation on an automotive line. Cited as an upper bound: even the best-documented plant deployment handles rigid panels presented in fixtures, far short of prying trim, unplugging locking harness connectors and swapping modules in a used car.

sources.system: RoboTire robotic tire changer
sources.title: RoboTire's tire-changer aims to evolve service bay | Tire Business
sources.claim: The only robotic system working on customer vehicles inside service bays at commercial scale handles wheels and lug nuts, not electrical or electronic components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic vehicle service in a shop bay. Cited to show shop-bay vehicle robotics is limited to a standardized mechanical operation on the wheel face, providing no capability for interior trim removal, connector handling or electronic module replacement.

tasks.label: Cut openings and drill holes for fixtures and equipment, using electric drills and routers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Speaker/subwoofer install in a 12-volt shop bay: installer removes a door panel, rear deck trim or kick panel from the customer's car, marks the driver location, and cuts or enlarges the mounting opening with a jigsaw/rotary tool plus drills the screw holes, then cuts a matching adapter baffle. Panel material and hidden window mechanisms vary by vehicle.

Wire pass-through work on an assembled vehicle in the bay: drilling holes through the firewall, floor pan, trunk bulkhead or inner fender for power, ground and antenna leads, working in cramped engine-bay/under-dash spaces, avoiding hidden harnesses, fuel and brake lines, then deburring and grommeting the hole.

Head-unit, display or camera-monitor fitment: cutting and routing the dash bezel, sub-dash bracket, glovebox or center console plastic so an aftermarket radio kit, tablet screen or switch panel drops in flush; involves repeated test fitting and trimming on the specific vehicle's trim piece.

Fleet/emergency-vehicle upfitting at an installation facility: drilling holes in the roof or body sheet metal of vans, patrol cars and trucks for antennas, GPS pucks, light bars, sirens and camera brackets, plus bolt holes for consoles and equipment racks; holes must be deburred and sealed against corrosion.

Bench fabrication in the shop: cutting subwoofer enclosure panels, amplifier racks, speaker baffles and equipment mounting boards from MDF, plywood or ABS with a router, jigsaw and hole saw, including driver cutouts and bolt-circle holes.

Mobile on-site install at a customer driveway or fleet yard: drilling small holes in trim, headliner or body for a telematics unit, dash camera or antenna mount, working outdoors around the parked vehicle with hand power tools and no shop fixtures.

tasks.label: Build fiberglass or wooden enclosures for sound components, and fit them to automobile dimensions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the shop's fabrication bay: build a sealed or ported MDF/plywood subwoofer enclosure for a car trunk or SUV cargo area. Worker measures the available space, computes net internal volume/port tuning, cuts rectangular panels on table saw or CNC, glues and screws the carcass, adds bracing, seals the joints, cuts driver and terminal-cup holes, wraps in carpet or vinyl, and trial-fits the box in the vehicle.

In the shop: build a behind-seat or under-seat wedge enclosure for a pickup cab or a stepped box for a hatch, with compound-angle and contoured panels templated off the cab wall, seat backs, window motors and wheel arches; cut, assemble, seal, finish, and trial-fit repeatedly until it drops into the space with clearance.

In the shop: build a fiberglass enclosure molded to a vehicle cavity (wheel-well, spare-tire well, trunk corner). Worker masks the cavity, forms a shape with cardboard rings and stretched fleece, wets it out with resin, adds mat layers, grinds and trims the shell, bonds an MDF baffle, fills and sands, finishes, and fits it back into the car.

In the shop: fabricate small fiberglass speaker pods — A-pillar tweeter pods, kick panels, or door pods — molded directly against factory trim panels so the pod blends into the interior contour, with on-axis driver aiming, body filler blending, and vinyl or paint finish.

Mobile installer working at the customer's driveway, parking lot or fleet yard: builds or adapts an enclosure on site with portable tools out of the van, cutting and assembling wood to fit the specific vehicle's available space in uncontrolled conditions (weather, no bench, no dust collection).

In the shop: modify or adapt a prefabricated enclosure or build a simple flat panel/amp-rack board — re-cut the baffle for a different driver, trim the box to clear a floor hump or strut tower, add bracing or a divider, re-cover, and fit.

sources.system: ShopSabre CNC routers (Audio Intensity Proline X enclosure production)
sources.title: CNC Subwoofer Enclosure: How It's Built
sources.claim: Vehicle-specific subwoofer enclosures are commercially produced by cutting every panel on CNC routers from CAD data to 0.005 in tolerance, with boxes contoured to a specific vehicle to work around window motors, vents and the cab wall.

sources.transferJustification: Assembling a wooden cabinet carcass from flat panels is the same operation as assembling a wooden speaker enclosure carcass: same material, same panel sizes, same squareness requirement.

sources.transferJustification: Glue-and-place assembly of dimensionally varying wooden members to a data-defined geometry is the same operation as gluing up an enclosure carcass whose dimensions are set per vehicle.

sources.transferJustification: Surface preparation and finishing of a speaker enclosure shell is the same finishing step required on a car-audio enclosure before carpet, vinyl or paint.

sources.title: Automating swimming pool production | CompositesWorld
sources.claim: A gantry-mounted robot fitted with a chopper gun sprays chopped glass and resin into moulds in commercial fibreglass pool production, but technicians still roll out the sprayed laminate by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Open-mould spray-up of chopped glass and polyester resin is the same lamination process used for fibreglass car-audio enclosures, at larger scale; it establishes what part of that process is robotised and what is not.

sources.system: Sea Ray Deck and Hull Trim Cell (robotic FRP trimming and sanding)
sources.developer: Sea Ray (Brunswick) with FANUC robots / BRM NamPower brushes
sources.title: Robotic Hull Cutting, Sanding Speeds Luxury Boat Production
sources.claim: A boat manufacturer runs a robotic Deck and Hull Trim Cell that cuts holes and trims moulded fibreglass parts and robotically sands hull interiors, while the fibreglass laminate itself is still hand-rolled in layers by workers.
sources.transferJustification: Trimming and hole-cutting of moulded fibreglass shells is the same finishing operation a fibreglass enclosure needs; the article also documents that the layup step itself remains manual.

sources.system: RoboCraftsman / RoboForming
sources.title: Capabilities | Machina
sources.claim: A containerized robotic cell makes one-off custom-geometry parts from CAD: robots load and fixture the blank, form it, scan the formed surface with a robot-mounted laser, and use the scan-derived datum to trim edges and drill features adaptively.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: batch-of-one fabrication of a custom-shaped part to a specified geometry. It shows a purpose-built cell can take per-part dimensions (here scan/CAD-derived) and produce a matching one-off part, which is what 'fit to automobile dimensions' requires; the material is sheet metal rather than wood, so it is supporting rather than decisive.

roles.description: Install, repair, or adjust audio or television receivers, stereo systems, camcorders, video systems, or other electronic entertainment equipment in homes or other venues. May perform routine maintenance.

tasks.label: Install, service, and repair electronic equipment or instruments such as televisions, radios, and videocassette recorders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-home install of a TV / home-theater system: locate studs, drill and fasten a wall mount, lift and hang a 40–85" panel, level it, fish and conceal cables in the wall, connect sources/soundbar/receiver, power up, configure inputs and remotes, and demonstrate to the customer. Furniture, pets and occupants present; every room layout differs.

Commercial/institutional AV install (conference room, classroom, house of worship, bar): mount displays and ceiling projectors to structure, hang speakers, pull and terminate cable above ceilings and through walls/conduit, rack-mount and wire amplifiers/switchers/control processors, then commission and test the room.

On-site service call at a customer premises (home or small business): a system is dead or intermittent — diagnose by testing cables, connections, power and devices; re-terminate or replace a cable, swap a failed component/module, reseat or reconfigure equipment, verify operation with the customer.

Bench repair at a shop/service depot: a receiver, TV, or similar unit is brought in; open the enclosure, diagnose the fault (power board, backlight driver, ribbon, bad cap/solder joint), replace the module or component (screws, connectors, sometimes desoldering), reassemble and functionally test.

Routine preventive maintenance at a venue: clean/replace projector filters and lamps, dust and reseat rack gear, dress and label cables, check connections, apply firmware updates and re-calibrate audio/video, log the visit.

sources.system: Molg robotic microfactory (with ABB Robotics)
sources.title: ABB Robotics and US start-up Molg tackle data center e-waste with robotic microfactories
sources.claim: Molg's robotic microfactory autonomously assembles and disassembles complex electronic products (laptops, servers, industrial electronics) in a purpose-built robotic cell built with ABB robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown/rebuild of consumer and IT electronics. It shares the objects (screwed plastic/metal enclosures, ribbon and board connectors, plug-in modules) and the precision of bench-level electronics service, and is done in a fixtured cell, so it substantiates module-level open/replace/reassemble work at E1, not on-site work.

sources.system: Molg Microfactory
sources.title: Molg Raises $5.5 Million in Seed Funding to Tackle Electronics Waste Through Circular Manufacturing
sources.claim: Molg's disassembly microfactories are installed and operating in commercial IT-asset-disposition facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the ABB item: establishes that robotic teardown of electronics runs in real facilities, in purpose-built cells, rather than only in the lab.

sources.system: DTI laptop refurbishing robot (RoboSAPIENS project)
sources.title: Search-based Robustness Testing of Laptop Refurbishing Robotic Software
sources.claim: A robotic refurbishing cell at the Danish Technological Institute automates laptop refurbishment steps — unscrewing, component removal, cleaning and reassembly — using vision and a robot arm in a fixed workcell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: refurbishing consumer electronics on a bench. Same object class (screwed consumer electronics with screens, boards and connectors) and same fine-manipulation precision as shop repair of a TV or receiver, in a fixtured workcell.

sources.system: RLDG (RL-distilled generalist policies) on a Franka arm
sources.title: RLDG: Robotic Generalist Policy Distillation via Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: Autonomous learned policies perform sub-millimeter connector insertion (USB, Ethernet, VGA) with a fixed female port fixture in a lab cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step: mating AV cables/connectors. It shows connector mating is solved only with the port rigidly fixtured at a known pose in a lab cell — a sub-step, not the whole install or service instance.

sources.system: In-contact robotic desoldering system
sources.title: An in-Contact Robotic System for the Process of Desoldering PCB Components
sources.claim: Robotic desoldering and extraction of components from PCBs has been demonstrated with force-controlled contact tooling in a laboratory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step of bench repair: component-level removal from boards. Same objects and precision as shop-level board repair, demonstrated only with the board presented in a fixtured setup.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Hilti unveils BIM-enabled construction robot for mobile ceiling work
sources.claim: The most capable jobsite installation robot in service performs only BIM-guided ceiling hole drilling under operator direction; it does not mount or wire equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead drilling for MEP installation, the closest fielded analogue to drilling mounts and running AV cable in venues. It covers only hole drilling under operator control, so it cannot substantiate completion of an AV install.

sources.system: 1X NEO
sources.title: For $20,000, a humanoid robot will do your household chores for you… but it still needs help
sources.claim: The leading home humanoid robot cannot perform non-trivial household manipulation autonomously; tasks are completed via a remote VR operator.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that general-purpose manipulation in private homes — the setting of residential AV installs and service calls — is still teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment there.

tasks.label: Calibrate and test equipment, and locate circuit and component faults, using hand and power tools and measuring and testing instruments such as resistance meters and oscilloscopes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commissioning/calibrating a newly installed conference-room or classroom AV system in an office or school: verifying every source-to-display signal path with test patterns and an HDMI/cable tester, checking mic and speaker wiring with a meter, setting gain structure, EQ and AEC in the DSP with an RTA/measurement mic, then documenting the results. Ladder work above ceilings and behind racks; furniture and occupants present.

Setting up and calibrating a residential home theater or whole-house audio system: placing/aiming speakers, running level and distance calibration with a measurement mic at seating positions, calibrating the display with a colorimeter, testing in-wall cable runs for continuity/shorts with a toner and meter. Layout, furniture, and gear differ from house to house.

On-site fault diagnosis of a failed installed system at a business, school, courtroom, or house of worship (no image, hum/buzz, intermittent dropouts, dead mic channel): isolating the fault by substitution, measuring continuity and DC voltages at connectors and power supplies, checking amplifier outputs and speaker-line impedance, then repairing or replacing the offending cable, connector, or unit.

Bench work in a shop/service depot: a returned amplifier, receiver, projector, or DSP is opened, the board is inspected and probed with a resistance meter and oscilloscope to locate the faulty circuit/component (shorted output device, open fuse resistor, bad supply rail), and the fault is identified and documented for repair.

Tuning and testing a large venue sound/video system (auditorium, stadium bowl, worship space): sweeping and measuring loudspeaker arrays with measurement mics at multiple audience positions, verifying amplifier channels and 70V line impedance with an impedance meter, checking long cable runs, aligning and calibrating projectors/LED walls.

Residential service call for a failed component: tracing why one zone, TV, or subwoofer is dead in an occupied home, testing the wall plate and cable with a meter/tester, checking the power supply of the device, and confirming the repair with the homeowner present.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers (4060/4080 series, 'Repair Test' configuration)
sources.title: Electronic Board Testing: ICT, Flying Probe & Functional | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA sells flying-probe systems configured specifically for repair centers that automatically probe a loaded board and identify the faulty part(s) with a component-level diagnostic report — i.e., automated electrical fault localization on a board presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-circuit/flying-probe board test. It performs the same electrical acts the worker performs with a resistance meter — continuity, resistance, capacitance and component-value measurement at pads and vias — and outputs the located faulty component, which is the deliverable of 'locate circuit and component faults'.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers
sources.title: Flying Probe Tester for electronic boards PCB | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA flying probers accept boards loaded automatically by an input conveyor into the test area and then recognize faulty components, opens, shorts, and out-of-spec parts without an operator — a purpose-built machine cell with the workpiece presented to it.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; this item establishes that the board arrives fixtured/conveyed and the fault-finding runs unattended, matching the E1 counterfactual of work brought to the machine.

sources.system: Keysight Medalist i3070 In-Circuit Test System
sources.title: In-Circuit Test Systems | Keysight
sources.claim: Keysight's i3070 in-circuit test system is a widely deployed fixtured board tester that automatically detects structural defects (opens, shorts, wrong components) and includes tools to identify the location of a failing component.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bed-of-nails in-circuit test. It makes the same resistance/continuity/component measurements a technician makes with a resistance meter and reports which node or component fails, i.e. component-level fault localization on a fixtured board.

sources.system: OptoFidelity FUSION
sources.title: Automated Audio Testing in Pre-Owned Phones: Ensuring Quality | OptoFidelity
sources.claim: OptoFidelity FUSION is a commercial robot-assisted automated test system that measures speaker and microphone audio quality and volume of devices placed in the test cell, repeatably and without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated acoustic/functional test of a consumer device inside a purpose-built robotic test cell. It shows that 'test the equipment' can be done autonomously when the unit is presented to the machine, though only for units fixtured in the cell, not for equipment installed in a room.

sources.system: Autonomous Robot Twin System for Room Acoustic Measurements (ARTSRAM)
sources.developer: Aalto University (Götz, Martinez Ornelas, Schlecht, Pulkki)
sources.title: Autonomous Robot Twin System for Room Acoustic Measurements (ARTSRAM)
sources.claim: ARTSRAM is a pair of autonomous mobile robots (one carrying a loudspeaker, one a microphone array) that capture large sets of room ... at varying positions inside a room; it measures acoustics only and does not connect to, configure, or calibrate an installed AV system, and it relies on an external tracking system and random-walk positioning in a research lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-room acoustic measurement, the measurement sub-step of AV calibration. Cited to bound the field-work judgments: it covers only mic/source placement and impulse-response capture, not signal-path testing, DSP tuning, display calibration, or fault isolation.

sources.system: Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System
sources.title: Implementation of a Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System (IJARIS)
sources.claim: A university lab built a Dobot Magician arm with an Arduino measurement module that probes predefined PCB test points to take voltage and resistance readings, but positions are set by teach-and-playback and errors reach 6% (resistance) and 12% (3.3V rail) versus a calibrated multimeter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic probing of a PCB with meters. Cited only as supporting context for machine-cell probing; its teach-and-playback positioning and large measurement errors mean it is treated as scripted and cannot by itself support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Confer with customers to determine the nature of problems or to explain repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Position or mount speakers, and wire speakers to consoles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential home theater / whole-house audio install: cut openings and mount in-ceiling or in-wall speakers into drywall and joists, hang surround speakers on wall brackets, fish and terminate speaker wire through finished walls back to the AV receiver in a rack or cabinet. Ladders, furniture, pets, homeowner present; every house differs.

Corporate conference room, classroom or huddle space in an occupied office/school building: mount a soundbar over a display or drop ceiling-tile/pendant speakers into a suspended grid, route plenum-rated cable above the tile to a DSP/amp rack or credenza, land conductors on Phoenix/screw terminals and verify levels.

Distributed background-music system in a retail store, restaurant or gym: install dozens of near-identical 70V ceiling speakers with tile bridges and safety wires, daisy-chain and tap the 70V line, terminate at the amplifier rack. Repetitive but performed on ladders/lifts amid fixtures and often during business hours.

Live-event / portable sound reinforcement setup at a venue: carry and place powered mains on pole stands and subs on the floor or deck, set stage monitors, run and dress XLR/NL4 cabling to the front-of-house console, at load-in under a schedule with crew and gear moving around.

Large permanent venue install (house of worship, auditorium, stadium, ballroom): assemble and fly line-array modules or point-source boxes from steel or truss with rigging hardware, aim them, and run/terminate speaker feeds back to the amp room. Overhead work at height, often from a lift during a fit-out.

Service call to replace or re-position an existing speaker: remove a blown or damaged unit, remount a replacement in the same location, re-terminate the existing wire at the speaker and at the console/amplifier, and test. Mostly homes and small businesses with unknown existing wiring.

sources.system: FANUC M-20iD/35 and SR/LR Mate assembly cells (chair assembly; rotary-dial place/screwdrive cell)
sources.developer: FANUC America with integrators (Paramount Tool, RND Automation)
sources.title: Assembly Robots | Assembly Line Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Commercially integrated FANUC assembly cells autonomously place parts and drive screws and inserts into CNC-cut ... on fixtured lines, i.e. mechanical mounting of a component with fasteners in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fastening of hardware into wood/panel workpieces. Mounting a speaker or its bracket onto a fixtured baffle, cabinet or panel uses the same object class (wood/composite panels), the same fasteners and the same few-millimetre placement precision, in a fenced cell.

sources.system: ASG AX-10 robotic assembly cell (Cartesian or six-axis cobot with X-PAQ screwdriver)
sources.developer: ASG, a Division of Jergens Inc.
sources.title: Robotic Cell Automates Screwdriving Process | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Off-the-shelf robotic screwdriving cells with modular fixtures and automatic screw feeders are sold as standard products for assemblies needing several screws driven from one side.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated screwdriving of fixtured assemblies. Mounting a speaker to a bracket, baffle or enclosure is a four-to-eight-screw, single-side fastening job of exactly the kind these cells are built and sold for.

sources.system: Stäubli TX2-60L robots in Eberhard AG assembly system
sources.title: Robot-assisted assembly of high-voltage connectors for electric vehicles | Stäubli
sources.claim: A deployed six-robot, vision-guided cell assembles and inspects five million high-voltage electrical connectors per year, showing production-grade robotic handling and mating of electrical connector parts on a fixtured line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of electrical connectors. Landing a speaker cable on a connectorised terminal in a fixtured cell requires the same sub-millimetre insertion of small electrical parts under vision, at production reliability.

sources.system: Rocsys M1 hands-free charging robot (earlier Rocsys units at APM Terminals Maasvlakte II)
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M | Electrek
sources.claim: A commercially deployed robot autonomously locates a vehicle inlet, opens the port, mates a high-current charging connector and disconnects it, with a claimed >99.9% plug-in success rate in ... depot and port environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mating of a keyed multi-pin power connector into a socket while managing a heavy flexible cable — physically the same act as plugging a speaker cable into an amplifier/console panel or an NL4 into a cabinet.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR10 at Paradigm Electronics
sources.title: Collaborative Robot Polishes Speaker Cabinet | Assembly Magazine
sources.claim: A collaborative robot works on loudspeaker cabinets in the speaker manufacturer's own production cell, applying force-controlled tooling to the cabinet surface since 2015.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled robotic work on loudspeaker enclosures in a work cell. It establishes that the actual object class of this task — speaker cabinets — is handled by robots to accepted production quality when presented in a fixture.

sources.system: Microsoft Research datacenter dexterous modular robots
sources.title: Future AI Infrastructure — Robotics | Microsoft Research
sources.claim: Research robots manipulate optical transceivers and cables inside datacenter racks, but this is a co-designed research program covering cable handling only, with no mounting of equipment to walls or ceilings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cable connection inside a structured facility. Cited to show that in-facility (E2) cabling robotics is still a research demo confined to purpose-designed racks and covers none of the speaker mounting work.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Hilti unveils BIM-enabled construction robot for mobile ceiling work | Construction Dive
sources.claim: The most capable in-building installation robot in field use drills and marks anchor holes from BIM data under operator attendance; it does not mount devices or make electrical connections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead anchor drilling inside buildings. Cited as the ceiling of field capability: even this semi-autonomous, operator-attended machine only makes holes, so it cannot substantiate mounting-and-wiring a speaker at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Instruct customers on the safe and proper use of equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Make service calls to repair units in customers' homes, or return units to shops for major repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: technician drives to a customer's living room, interviews the customer, and troubleshoots a home theater/TV system that is dead, has no picture or sound, or drops HDMI/network sources; resolves by reseating or replacing cables, swapping a failed source device or soundbar, reconfiguring inputs, updating firmware, and verifying operation with the customer.

Residential service call on mounted or concealed equipment: wall-mounted TV, in-ceiling or outdoor speakers, ceiling projector, or in-wall cabling; requires ladder work, dismounting heavy panels, fishing or re-terminating wire in walls/attic/crawlspace, then remounting, leveling, and testing in an occupied home.

Service call at a commercial or institutional venue (conference room, classroom, house of worship, bar/restaurant): diagnose rack gear such as amplifiers, matrix switchers, DSPs, and control systems; replace a failed unit, re-terminate connectors, reload configuration, and confirm the system passes the site's acceptance check.

Unit needs major repair: technician disconnects and removes it from the customer's site, transports it to the shop, benches it for diagnosis and repair over days, then returns, reinstalls, and re-integrates it into the customer's system.

Shop bench repair of a customer-delivered unit (receiver, amplifier, TV, projector, camcorder): open a varied unfamiliar chassis, probe with meter/scope, isolate a failed board or component, desolder and replace parts or swap the board, reassemble, burn-in and functionally test before release.

sources.system: Daisy (with Dave and Taz)
sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy robot autonomously disassembles a fixed set of iPhone models on a purpose-built line for materials recovery; it performs no fault diagnosis, component-level repair, reassembly, or functional testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of consumer electronics in a fixtured cell. It marks the frontier of E1 electronics handling but does not transfer to this task: it works from a closed list of known models, never diagnoses a fault, never replaces a part, and never reassembles or tests a working unit.

sources.system: NEO
sources.title: 1X Neo Home Robot Teleoperation Today, Autonomy Tomorrow | Hiverlab
sources.claim: The only consumer humanoid entering private homes performs its harder household tasks through VR teleoperation by a remote pilot, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general manipulation inside private homes. It is the closest precedent for a machine working in a customer's residence, but the demonstrated work is teleoperated and consists of tidying-grade tasks far below AV fault isolation and repair, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: UR10e + RealSense D405 + custom mechatronic screwdriver unscrewing cell
sources.developer: I. Diaz et al. (Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing | ScienceDirect / Zenodo record
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous electronics-disassembly research covers only the screw-removal sub-step on fixtured devices, at research-grade reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening electronic devices by removing fasteners, a first step of bench repair. It does not transfer to the whole instance: no diagnosis, no board or component replacement, no reassembly or functional test, and first-pass reliability below shop standards.

sources.system: Jaibot
sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: The leading jobsite installation robot drills BIM-specified anchor holes semi-autonomously after an operator positions and supervises it; it performs no diagnosis, device handling, or cable termination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead MEP installation work involving ladders and ceilings. It does not transfer: the robot only drills pre-planned holes under operator setup, whereas the instance requires dismounting and remounting equipment, pulling and terminating AV cable, and verifying a working system.

tasks.label: Tune or adjust equipment and instruments to obtain optimum visual or auditory reception, according to specifications, manuals, and drawings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential: after installing a TV, projector or video wall in a customer's living room or dedicated theater, set and calibrate the picture — picture mode, brightness/contrast, gamma, grayscale/color point (often with a probe on the screen and the maker's spec sheet), adjusted for the room's lighting; customer views and signs off.

Residential: set up and tune a surround-sound or whole-house audio system — position and aim/toe-in speakers, set levels, distances and crossovers on the AVR/processor, place a measurement mic at listening positions to run and verify room correction, then listen and re-adjust until the customer accepts.

Home or small business: aim an off-air antenna or satellite dish (roof, attic, mast) and peak azimuth/elevation/skew against a signal-strength/quality meter until reception meets spec on all required channels or transponders, in whatever weather and obstruction conditions the site presents.

Commercial conference room, classroom or courtroom commissioning per drawings/spec: focus and set projector or display geometry and brightness, tune DSP audio (gain structure, EQ, AEC, mic gating, zone levels), set camera framing presets, then verify the whole chain against the design documents with the room in service.

Large venue (arena, theater, house of worship, ballroom): tune the installed sound system with a measurement mic and analyzer (EQ, delay/time alignment, array zone balance, gain structure) and align/color-match the image system (multi-projector blend or LED wall), verified against the designer's specification.

Shop bench: align or adjust a unit brought in for repair or pre-deployment setup — amplifier, tuner/receiver, camera, wireless mic system — using signal generator, oscilloscope/analyzer and the service manual, trimming internal adjustments or settings until measured response meets published spec.

tasks.label: Disassemble entertainment equipment and repair or replace loose, worn, or defective components and wiring, using hand tools and soldering irons.

instances.label: Bench repair at a service shop: technician opens a consumer AV unit (flat-panel TV, AV receiver, amplifier, turntable, game console) with hand tools, traces a loose/burnt/failed part (cold solder joint, bulging capacitor, cracked HDMI or power jack), desolders and replaces it, dresses wiring, reassembles the chassis and function-tests before return to the customer. High model mix, mostly without manufacturer CAD data.

Commercial venue service call (school auditorium, house of worship, conference room, bar/stadium): pull a rack-mounted amplifier, DSP, matrix switcher or projector, open it on a work cart, replace a defective fan/board/connector, resolder loose internal wiring or a broken terminal, reassemble, reinstall in the rack and verify signal.

In-home service call: work on a home-theater receiver, soundbar, subwoofer or TV on the customer's floor or a table; disassemble the enclosure, resolder a loose speaker lead or replace a defective board/connector, reassemble and test, working around furniture, carpet, pets and existing cabling.

Cable and connector repair/re-termination: replace worn or broken speaker leads and interconnects, solder XLR/RCA/banana/phono connectors, repair wall-plate or patch-panel wiring; strip and tin conductors, solder, heat-shrink and continuity-test. Done at the shop bench or on a work surface at the job site.

Elevated or large-display field repair: LED video wall module, digital signage, or ceiling-mounted display/projector; from a ladder or lift, remove a panel/module, replace a defective module, ribbon cable or connector, resolder a broken lead, reassemble in place and verify the picture.

tasks.label: Install, maintain, or repair security systems, alarm devices, or related equipment, following blueprints of electrical layouts and building plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction commercial/institutional building (school, office, warehouse): fire alarm rough-in and device installation from blueprints — locating device positions from prints, mounting back boxes to studs/deck, drilling anchors, running FPLR cable through conduit, sleeves and J-hooks above ceilings, mounting pull stations, horn/strobes, duct and smoke detectors, terminating and addressing at the FACP. Active construction site with other trades, debris, ladders/lifts, changing layout.

Occupied single-family home: burglar alarm and camera install — mount control panel and keypad, door/window contacts, motion detectors and sirens, drill through exterior walls, fish or staple wire in attic/crawlspace or mount wireless devices, dress and terminate at the panel, test and walk-test with the homeowner. Furniture, pets, varied construction, no two houses alike.

Retrofit or expansion of a fire alarm/access control system in an occupied commercial or institutional facility (hospital wing, office floor, retail store): swap out control panel, add or relocate devices, pull cable above suspended ceilings and through existing walls, splice into existing circuits, work around occupants and after-hours schedules, verify per as-built and code.

Service/repair call at an existing commercial or institutional building: diagnose a trouble/ground-fault or false-alarm condition using as-built drawings and a meter, access devices above ceilings or in electrical rooms, replace a faulty detector, module, power supply or damaged cable segment, then retest the circuit and clear the panel.

Exterior/perimeter work on an existing controlled campus or facility grounds: mount CCTV cameras on soffits, walls and poles from a lift, install card readers, gate contacts and request-to-exit hardware, run and seal exterior conduit, terminate and aim/focus cameras per the site plan, in outdoor weather.

tasks.label: Mount and fasten control panels, door and window contacts, sensors, or video cameras, and attach electrical and telephone wiring to connect components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential burglar/fire alarm install in an occupied single-family home: screw-mount the control panel/enclosure in a closet or garage, fasten door and window contacts to varied wood/vinyl frames, mount motion detectors in ceiling corners and a keypad by the door, and land low-voltage conductors on panel screw terminals and device leads. Layout differs house to house; furniture, pets and occupants present.

Small commercial retrofit (retail store, restaurant, office suite) during or after business hours: mount the alarm panel on a back-room wall, install door contacts and glass-break/motion sensors, mount 4-16 IP cameras to drop-ceiling tiles, grid or walls, and terminate cabling (RJ45/BNC/screw terminals) at cameras, panel and NVR.

Fire alarm / security rough-in and trim-out in a commercial or institutional new-build or major renovation (school, hospital wing, warehouse): fasten backboxes and the FACP to studs/masonry, mount pull stations, smoke/heat detector bases, horn-strobes at ceiling height from ladders or lifts, and terminate device wiring per code. Active jobsite with other trades, dust and changing conditions.

Exterior/perimeter work: mount cameras, housings and brackets on building facades, parapets, parking-structure decks and light poles from a lift or ladder, mount weatherproof enclosures/power supplies, and terminate cabling in wet-location fittings. Weather, height, uneven ground.

Service call in an occupied commercial facility: replace a failed detector, contact, camera or power supply on an existing system - dismount the old device, fasten the replacement to the existing backbox/bracket, re-land the existing conductors on the new device's terminals and verify the circuit.

Shop prefabrication at the contractor's bench: build a control panel/backboard - fasten the panel board, power supply, terminal strips and expansion modules to an enclosure or plywood backing and run and land the interconnecting wiring - before the assembly is taken to site.

It is the same physical act as the task's second half - landing prepared conductors on the screw/clamp terminals of mounted devices - on comparable components (terminal blocks, breakers, contactors) at comparable precision, with the workpiece fixtured in the machine.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
