sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic selective coating removal from airframe surfaces. It substantiates machine-controlled stripping of coatings from aircraft structure to a specified layer, the 'strip' element, but only inside a purpose-built laser bay.

sources.system: Xyrec Laser Coating Removal (LCR) robot
sources.title: Laser Coating Removal Robot (LCR) - Xyrec
sources.claim: Xyrec's Laser Coating Removal robot, developed with SwRI, is a mobile 8-DOF laser robot with closed-loop color recognition that strips metal and composite aircraft surfaces selectively; the developer states it is fully autonomous, supervised by one operator behind glass in a custom-built facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective robotic stripping of coatings from installed aircraft skins. Shows machine-controlled stripping on real airframes, but only in an enclosed, purpose-built laser bay with people excluded.

sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System
sources.title: 3M Finesse-It Robotic Paint Repair System Fixes Paint Defects on Assembly Lines - The Robot Report
sources.claim: 3M's Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair ..., commercialized in 2021, uses a vision system to locate individual surface defects and then robotically sands and polishes those localized spots on production vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: localized, defect-targeted robotic abrasion of a coated surface. It transfers to locally stripping and sanding a bond area of a defined size at a location found by inspection rather than sanding a whole part.

tasks.label: Determine repair limits for engine hot section parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Line/heavy maintenance borescope inspection of an installed engine's hot section in an airline hangar or at the gate: technician inserts a measuring borescope through the ports, motors the engine, examines combustor liner, HPT nozzle guide vanes and blades, sizes cracks/burns/coating loss/tip damage, and determines against AMM/engine-manual limits whether the engine is serviceable, on watch, or must come off wing.

Engine overhaul shop piece-part inspection after teardown and cleaning: cleaned hot-section hardware (HPT blades, nozzle segments, combustor liners and domes, seals) examined visually and by FPI on a bench; cracks, burn-through, oxidation, sulfidation, coating spallation judged against engine-manual serviceable and repair limits; each part dispositioned serviceable, repairable (to a specific repair scheme) or scrap, and the finding recorded.

Dimensional/metrology evaluation of individual cleaned hot-section parts against published service and repair limits in the engine shop inspection area: blade height, chord, tip and trailing-edge thickness, untwist, liner wall thickness, nozzle throat area/distortion, measured with gauges, micrometers, CMM or optical scanners and compared to the limits tables.

Hot section inspection on a small turbine engine (PT6A, TPE331) at a regional or general-aviation turbine shop: gas generator case split, combustion liner and vane ring removed, compressor-turbine blades inspected in place on the disc; sulfidation, cracking, erosion and burning judged against the manual's limits, with repair/replace decisions made on the spot for a low-volume mixed workload.

Verification of a repaired hot-section part against limits before release: after a blend of a nick, a weld/braze repair, or a coating strip-and-recoat, confirm blend depth, radius, blended-away material, restored wall/chord dimensions and surface condition are inside the manual's allowable repair limits, and accept or reject the part.

sources.system: White light inspection robots (Gen 2)
sources.developer: GE Aerospace (Research Niskayuna / Global Automation and Robotics Center, Bromont)
sources.title: Dance of the White Light Robots: A Closer Look at the Newest Inspection Technology in MRO
sources.claim: GE Aerospace deployed AI-guided 'white light robots' in its STAC MRO shop in fall 2024: two articulated industrial robots with white-light optical scanners scan a fixtured high-pressure-turbine disk and run unattended once started, recording and numerically valuing every anomaly.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: automated capture and measurement of damage on a hot-section rotating part (GE90 HPT disk) that a technician would otherwise inspect by hand against manual limits.

sources.system: White light inspection robots (Gen 2)
sources.title: Dance of the White Light Robots: A Closer Look at the Newest Inspection Technology in MRO
sources.claim: In the same deployed GE system, the accept/repair/reject engineering disposition — the determination of whether damage is within limits — is explicitly retained by the human inspector after five years of development.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point: this is the disposition step of hot-section part inspection, i.e. determining whether observed damage falls inside repair limits.

sources.system: AutoInspect
sources.title: Digital inspection procedure for engine components industrialized
sources.claim: Lufthansa Technik industrialized AutoInspect, a robot-based automated crack inspection of engine combustor components (CFM56/CF34 families), in productive use since 2018, producing digital repair-relevant data on each part.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated crack detection/sizing on combustor hot-section parts in a robot cell) supplies the measurement input to the repair-limit determination, on the same parts and precision class.

sources.system: AutoInspect
sources.title: A4A NDT Forum 2016 - AutoInspect: Innovative Inspection System for Engine Components
sources.claim: Lufthansa Technik qualified AutoInspect with a probability-of-detection study against manual FPI and visual inspection, and positioned it as the inspection front end of an automated weld/mill repair chain for combustor parts.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the robotic cell's crack-detection performance was formally shown equivalent-or-better than the manual FPI/VI a technician performs before applying manual limits.

sources.system: ZEISS ScanBox Series 5 (5110) with ATOS 5 for Airfoil
sources.title: ZEISS ScanBox Series 5 is an all-in solution for automated inspection and digitization of complex parts
sources.claim: ZEISS/GOM ScanBox automated optical metrology cells are commercial, robot-driven enclosed cells with automated measuring procedures, marketed for gas-turbine airfoil inspection and used directly in production environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional verification of turbine airfoils against nominal geometry and tolerance bands — the same measure-and-compare-to-limits operation the technician performs with gauges against service/repair limits tables.

sources.system: ATOS ScanBox 5108 with ATOS Triple Scan
sources.title: Videos - ATOS ScanBox 5108 - Turbine Blade Automated Inspection
sources.claim: Automated ScanBox cells are used specifically for dimensional verification of turbine blades/airfoils with blue-light 3D scanning.
sources.transferJustification: Turbine blade dimensional verification in an automated cell is the machine equivalent of measuring a hot-section airfoil and comparing it against the manual's dimensional limits.

sources.system: Automated defect detection + decision support tool (DST)
sources.developer: Aust & Pons (Victoria University of Wellington), published in Aerospace (MDPI)
sources.title: Automated Defect Detection and Decision-Support in Gas Turbine Blade Inspection
sources.claim: A rule-based decision-support tool has been demonstrated that takes automated defect detection output and applies engine-manual limits from a lookup table to return a serviceability decision for a gas turbine blade.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the limit-comparison logic of this task, but software only (no embodied capture) and research-stage; used only as supporting logic alongside a robotic measurement cell.

sources.system: Sensiworm
sources.title: GE Aerospace is developing a robotic worm to inspect and repair jet engines
sources.claim: GE Aerospace's in-situ engine crawler robot for on-wing inspection is remote-controlled by operators, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as negative evidence for in-situ hot-section assessment: the only in-engine crawler is teleoperated and does not produce a limits determination.

sources.system: AI-assisted / robotic borescope inspection (industry state of the art)
sources.developer: MRO Business Today (industry analysis of OEM and MRO systems)
sources.title: Beyond Inspection, how AI, data and advanced RVI are reshaping the future of engine MRO
sources.claim: Industry assessment as of 2026: moving from AI damage detection to a serviceable-limits determination requires validated, OEM-certified disposition logic tied to specific engine manuals, and fully autonomous borescope inspection is not ready for line deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence bearing exactly on determining whether hot-section damage is within serviceable limits.

sources.system: AI-enabled Blade Inspection Tool (BIT)
sources.title: GE Aerospace deploys AI-enabled tool to enhance aircraft engine inspections
sources.claim: GE Aerospace's deployed AI blade inspection tool assists technicians in capturing turbine blade images across a dozen-plus MRO facilities; the technician remains in the loop for capture and judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence: the most widely deployed AI inspection aid for turbine blades is a technician-operated tool, not an autonomous system producing limit determinations.

sources.system: Optomec/Acme automated turbine blade repair work cell (CS-250 laser cladding + robotic grinding/finishing)
sources.title: Industry's First Fully Automated Work Cell for the Additive Repair of Turbine Parts
sources.claim: A commercially available, certified multi-robot work cell repairs turbine blade tips automatically, measuring each worn blade and adapting tool paths to its actual as-worn geometry, running largely unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated per-part measurement of worn/repaired blade geometry inside a fixtured cell, the same metrology needed to verify a repaired part against its dimensional repair limits.

tasks.label: Disassemble engines and inspect parts, such as turbine blades or cylinders, for corrosion, wear, warping, cracks, and leaks, using precision measuring instruments, x-rays, and magnetic inspection equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Turbofan/turboshaft engine shop visit at an MRO: technician strips an engine mounted on a horizontal build stand — removes cowls, tubing, harnesses, accessories, splits modules with hoists and slings, breaks lockwire and seized/corroded fasteners, de-stacks rotors — and visually/dimensionally inspects parts as they come off, logging findings.

Piece-part inspection station in the engine shop: after cleaning, technician inspects turbine/compressor blades, vanes, disks and seals for cracks, corrosion, erosion, warping and wear using loupes, borescope optics, micrometers, gauges and go/no-go fixtures, and dispositions each part serviceable / repairable / scrap.

NDT of engine piece parts in the shop's inspection lab: fluorescent penetrant inspection, magnetic particle inspection, and radiographic (x-ray) inspection of blades, disks and cases; interpreting indications and recording accept/reject per the engine manual.

General-aviation piston engine at a repair-station hangar: mechanic pulls cylinders from a Lycoming/Continental engine (baffles, exhaust, intake, pushrods, base nuts), then measures bore wear/out-of-round with a dial bore gauge, checks valves, guides and crank journals with micrometers, and inspects for corrosion and leaks.

On-aircraft partial disassembly and inspection during line/base maintenance: removing an accessory gearbox component, igniters, combustor access covers or a cylinder/QEC part on an installed engine in a hangar or on the ramp, then borescope and visual/dimensional inspection for cracks, wear and leaks in cramped, cluttered access.

Field/austere setting: military flight-line or deployed maintenance, remote AOG, or ag-aviation strip — partial engine teardown (module or cylinder removal) and inspection outdoors with portable tools, variable light, weather and no fixed layout.

sources.system: GE Aerospace AI white light inspection robots (Gen 2)
sources.developer: GE Aerospace Research / Global Automation and Robotics Center
sources.title: Dance of the White Light Robots: A Closer Look at the Newest Inspection Technology in MRO | GE Aerospace News
sources.claim: GE Aerospace deployed AI-guided 'white light robot' inspectors — two articulated industrial robots in a universal workstation with white-light optical scanners — into an MRO shop in fall 2024 to inspect high-pressure turbine disks/parts, scoring anomalies such as dents, cracks, corrosion and fretting.

sources.system: AI White Light Inspection (robotic FPI)
sources.title: GE Aerospace developing Service Technology Acceleration Center
sources.claim: An AI-powered robotic system performs the large majority of fluorescent penetrant inspections of CFM56 engine airfoils at GE Aerospace's Singapore engine shop, applying a data-derived technical standard to the accept/reject call.

sources.system: AV&R robotic inspection and repair system (FANUC LR Mate 200iD / M-20iB)
sources.title: Fan Blade Inspection and Repair Courtesy of AV&R | Tech-Labs
sources.claim: AV&R built a robotic inspection-and-repair cell for aerospace MRO customers in which a FANUC LR Mate 200iD ... inspects large, heavy engine turbine parts (fan ..., shafts), cutting a multi-day manual inspection to 30 minutes to two hours.

sources.system: AV&R automated visual inspection system with OwlVision
sources.title: Robotic Automation of Fan Blade Visual Surface Inspection – Metrology and Quality News
sources.claim: AV&R's automated visual inspection cell for MRO fan blades has the robot manipulate the blade in front of 2D imaging and 3D scanning heads and automatically detects and dimensions defects (nicks, dents, erosion, deformation, tip curl, wear, rub marks, fretting) per pre-established criteria, generating inspection reports.

sources.system: Multi-robot FPI inspection system with deep neural nets
sources.title: Multi-Robot System for Automated Fluorescent Penetrant Indication Inspection with Deep Neural Nets - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A multi-robot cell developed by GE and partners automates fluorescent penetrant inspection of gas-turbine parts end to end: autonomous image acquisition with full coverage, robotic wipe-off, and deep-neural-net discrimination of true defects from non-relevant indications.

sources.system: North Star Imaging RobotiX (X25/X7000, efX-ADR)
sources.title: Automated X-ray CT Scanning with RobotiX™: Raising the Bar in Aerospace, Automotive & Medical Manufacturing
sources.claim: North Star Imaging's RobotiX cells integrate industrial robots with digital X-ray and CT scanners for fully automated part loading, scanning and defect analysis, and are used in aerospace on parts such as turbine blades to find cracks, porosity and inclusions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is production/quality radiographic and CT inspection of turbine blades; it transfers to the mechanic's x-ray inspection instance because the objects (turbine airfoils, castings), the modality (radiography/CT with automated defect recognition) and the fixtured cell environment are the same.

sources.system: YOLO-SAM vision-based robotic aircraft engine disassembly pipeline
sources.title: Vision-based robotic disassembly of aircraft engines with YOLO-SAM: a novel method for task orientation estimation
sources.claim: State of the art in robotic aircraft-engine disassembly is a research pipeline: a dual-arm setup detects removable bolts with YOLO+SAM and unscrews accessible ones, running in automatic and semi-automatic modes, ... many bolts flagged as non-removable because of surrounding inaccessible components.

sources.system: Remote Boreblending robot / SWARM / snake-arm robots
sources.title: Rolls-Royce robots promise maintenance revolution - The Engineer
sources.claim: Rolls-Royce's most mature on-wing engine maintenance robot, the Remote Boreblending robot, attaches to an installed engine and is operated remotely by a human specialist rather than autonomously; swarm and snake concepts remain research.

tasks.label: Remove, inspect, repair, and install in-flight refueling stores and external fuel tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Remove and install external fuel tanks (e.g., F-16 370-gal, F/A-18 330-gal, A-10/F-15 tanks) on wing or centerline pylons in a base hangar or on the flight line: defuel/purge, disconnect fuel, vent and electrical connections, back off sway braces, release suspension hooks, lower onto a tank lift trailer/jammer; on install, hoist and align 14/30-inch lugs, engage hooks, torque sway braces, mate plumbing and electrical, install pins/safety wire, then leak and fuel-transfer functional check.

Remove and install in-flight refueling stores - buddy refueling pods (e.g., D-704 ARS), KC-135 wing air refueling pods, HC-130/helicopter hose-reel pods, probe and boom components - typically several hundred to over a thousand pounds, rigged with hoists or a lift trailer in a hangar, with hydraulic/fuel/electrical interfaces mated and a post-install functional and leak check.

Routine visual condition survey of installed tanks and refueling stores during pre-flight, post-flight or phase inspection in a hangar or on the flight line: walking the aircraft looking for dents, cracks, punctures, paint/skin damage and fuel staining on the store's external surfaces, documenting findings.

Detailed hands-on inspection of installed tanks/stores per technical order: check security of attachment and sway brace torque, safety wire and pins, condition of lugs and pads, drain valves, disconnect fittings and seals, wet leak checks at couplings, and functional check of fuel transfer/jettison circuitry.

Shop/back-shop inspection and repair of a removed tank or refueling pod on a stand or bench: purge and open, replace o-rings, seals, valves, pumps, hose/reel components, apply sealant, make minor structural or composite repairs, treat corrosion and touch up paint, then pressure/leak test and return to serviceable.

Deployed or shipboard removal/installation of tanks and refueling stores: carrier hangar bay or flight deck, or an expeditionary/deployed airfield - confined space around parked aircraft, weather and night conditions, limited support equipment, tight turnaround timelines.

sources.system: Donecle Iris autonomous inspection drone
sources.title: Donecle's €10M Inspection Drone Raise Meets America's Aircraft Mechanic Shortage
sources.claim: Donecle's autonomous inspection drones fly programmed scans around a parked aircraft in a hangar and use AI to detect exterior surface damage; the product is in commercial service with airlines, MROs and air forces, with autonomous inspection recognized by the airframers and regulators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated general visual inspection of an aircraft exterior. It transfers to the visual-damage-survey portion of inspecting installed external tanks/stores - the same painted external surfaces on the same aircraft in the same hangar, and the same defect classes (dents, cracks, paint and fluid staining).

sources.system: Donecle military aircraft drone inspection
sources.title: Military Aircraft Inspection by Drone - Donecle
sources.claim: Donecle fields the automated drone inspection on combat and transport military aircraft, including scheduled depot maintenance and post-flight inspection after in-flight refuelling, at home bases and on deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above, on the military fleets (Rafale, AWACS, maritime patrol) that carry external tanks and refuelling stores, performed in the air force hangar/depot where this task's inspections occur.

sources.system: MHU-TSX robotic loading system
sources.developer: Square One Systems Design / USAF Global Strike Command
sources.title: US Air Force Tests Robotic Aircraft Weapon Loading System
sources.claim: The only robotic aircraft store-loading system tested by the US Air Force, the MHU-TSX, is a human-operated loader: an operator drives it with a controller at the aircraft pylon, and autonomy would require a sensor package that had not been added.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hanging a heavy store on an aircraft pylon (a B-52 CALCM pylon). It is the closest fielded attempt at the mechanical part of installing an external store, and it is operator-controlled, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: RAMLS (Robotically Assisted Munition Loading System)
sources.developer: Sandia National Laboratories / US Air Force (research)
sources.title: A robotically assisted munition loading system
sources.claim: A research prototype, RAMLS, used a hydraulic six-DOF fine-motion mechanism to load a 500 lb bomb onto a tactical aircraft in laboratory testing, with the load crew reduced from three to one rather than eliminated; it covers only the lift-and-mate motion, not fluid/electrical connection or leak checks, and was never fielded.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating a heavy store to an aircraft suspension rack, mechanically similar to hanging an external fuel tank on a pylon. It is an assisted laboratory prototype with an operator in the loop and no plumbing/electrical mating, so it is treated as non-autonomous.

sources.system: Wilder Systems robotic aircraft wash system
sources.title: US Air Force Unveils Robot Jet Washer for F-16s
sources.claim: Wilder Systems built an automated robotic wash system that cleans an entire F-16 in about an hour with robotic spray arms; airmen at the 149th Fighter ... demonstrated it as an autonomous machine solution in a base wash facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic surface work on a whole fighter inside a base facility. It shows robots can register to and cover an aircraft's exterior, but it involves no disassembly, fastener work, fluid-line mating or torque, so it does not carry over to removing or installing stores.

sources.system: Robot-deployed laser-ultrasonic / PAUT NDT system
sources.title: Robot deployed Laser-Ultrasonic NDT system for inspection of large aircraft structures
sources.claim: Robotic ultrasonic/laser-ultrasonic NDT of large aerospace structures is performed by fixed six-axis arms scanning a component presented to the cell; the reported systems are prototypes for composite part flaw detection, not whole-component serviceability decisions or repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated flaw scanning of an aerospace component fixtured in a cell. It covers only the NDI sub-step of shop inspection of a removed tank or pod, not disassembly, seal/valve replacement, sealing, repair or pressure testing.

sources.system: Automated robotic sealing system for aircraft components
sources.title: DEVELOPMENT OF AUTOMATED SEALING SYSTEM FOR AIRCRAFT COMPONENTS
sources.claim: Robotic sealant application for aircraft components remains at laboratory development stage, with work focused on establishing dispensing parameters rather than fielded repair of assembled fuel-carrying structures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying sealant to aircraft structure, a sub-step of fuel tank repair. It is a laboratory parameter study on a purpose-built rig and does not cover the disassembly, seal/valve replacement and leak testing that complete a tank repair.

tasks.label: Trim and shape replacement body sections to specified sizes and fits and secure sections in place, using adhesives, hand tools, and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aluminum structural skin repair in a maintenance hangar: mechanic cuts out damaged fuselage/wing skin, lays out and trims a replacement skin section or doubler from sheet stock (shears, nibbler, band saw, file, die grinder) to the specified size, edge distance and contour, fits it, drills and deburrs the pattern, applies sealant/adhesive, and installs solid or blind rivets with pneumatic tools, often overhead or in awkward access on the parked aircraft.

Composite/bonded secondary structure repair in the MRO component shop with the part removed from the aircraft (fan cowl door, thrust reverser panel, radome, flap/fairing): damaged skin and honeycomb core cut out, replacement core plug and skin/ply plies trimmed to fit the scarf or cutout, bonded with film/paste adhesive and cured, then edges trimmed and fasteners reinstalled.

In-situ composite repair on the aircraft in the hangar: scarf or cut out damage on a wing, fuselage or nacelle panel, cut and fit the replacement plies/patch to the prepared area, bond with adhesive and cure under a heat blanket, working on a curved, sometimes overhead surface at height on stands.

Line-maintenance or general-aviation field work on a ramp or small shop: replacing or patching a fairing, wingtip, access panel, belly skin or fiberglass tip; trimming the replacement piece by hand (snips, files, sanders, hole saw) to match the existing installation, then securing it with screws, rivets, clips and adhesive, under varying weather and time pressure.

Cabin interior panel and trim replacement: sidewall, ceiling, floor and galley/lav liner panels trimmed to fit around existing cutouts, brackets and wiring inside the confined cabin, then secured with adhesive, tape, camlocks and screws using hand and power tools.

sources.system: Airbus Hangar 245 fuselage assembly robots (KUKA Titan + Alema end-effectors; MTM Robotics Flextrack)
sources.developer: Airbus / KUKA / Alema Automation / MTM Robotics
sources.title: Special feature: Tour of Airbus’ advanced manufacturing facility in Germany
sources.claim: At Airbus Hamburg's Hangar 245, fenced production cells of robots automatically drill, countersink, seal and insert thousands of rivets to join fuselage skin sections, and MTM Robotics Flextrack units drill longitudinal joints — i.e., securing large body sections in place with power tools and sealant in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production joining of fuselage skin sections. Transfer holds because the objects (aluminium/composite skin panels), the joining method (drill, countersink, seal, rivet) and the hole/edge tolerances are the same ones a mechanic must meet when securing a replacement skin section.

sources.system: IPAC (Integrated Panel Assembly Cell) / MPAC
sources.title: IPAC - Broetje Automation
sources.claim: Broetje-Automation sells the Integrated Panel Assembly Cell, a widely installed automated riveting cell that fastens skin and wing panels; such cells hold the panel in flexible tooling and drill, seal and set fasteners without an operator in the work zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated riveting of skin panels in manufacturing. Comparable workpieces (aircraft skin panels), comparable fastening tools and precision to the securing step of this repair task, performed with the work brought to the machine.

sources.system: LHT/iSAM automated adaptive composite repair robot (ARC workshop)
sources.title: Gallery: How Robots Are Revolutionizing MRO
sources.claim: Lufthansa Technik, with iSAM, runs an automated adaptive robot cell in its airframe-related-component workshop that repairs removed components (radomes, fan cowl doors, inlet cowls) by scanning them and machining away damaged composite skin and honeycomb core — the trim-and-shape half of the repair — with technicians supervising from a control desk.

sources.system: CAIRE mobile scarfing/repair robot
sources.title: CAIRE repair robot – Lufthansa Technik
sources.claim: Lufthansa Technik's mobile CAIRE robot works in situ on an aircraft wing or fuselage: it is clamped to the component, scans the damage, computes the scarf geometry and mills out the damaged material — but the replacement plies are then bonded to the structure by hand, so the securing half of the task is not automated on-aircraft.

sources.system: MobileBlock (MB) milling robot; REPLY.5 waterjet robot
sources.title: Field & Onsite Repair of Composite Structures – Development Center for Maintenance of Composites
sources.claim: In a Dutch DCMC/NLR field-repair project, the DMG MORI MobileBlock milling robot prepared a damaged composite fuselage panel and a matching patch was milled from a ... panel to fit, then bonded with film adhesive — a robot-machined trim-to-fit of a replacement section in a fixtured laboratory/shop setting.

sources.system: KMT/Shape Process Automation robotic waterjet and RoboTrim router cells
sources.title: Aerospace uses 5-axis or 6-axis waterjet robotic systems – KMT Waterjet
sources.claim: Six-axis robotic waterjet and router cells are standard commercial equipment for trimming aerospace parts — aluminium, titanium and composite panels and interior parts — to net shape on three-dimensional contours inside fenced cutting cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production trimming of panels to net shape. It is the same operation as "trim and shape replacement body sections to specified sizes", on the same materials and contours, performed with the workpiece fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: F-150 body shop robotic SPR/adhesive cells (Dearborn/Kansas City)
sources.title: Fabricating the F-150 – FFJournal
sources.claim: In Ford's aluminium F-150 body shop, robotic cells apply structural adhesive and set self-piercing rivets to join aluminium body panels — automated adhesive-plus-mechanical securing of trimmed sheet sections in a fenced production cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing aluminium body panels with adhesive and rivets. Objects (thin aluminium panels), consumables (structural adhesive, rivets) and joint tolerances are close analogues of bonding-plus-riveting a replacement aircraft skin section in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Wilder Systems agile manufacturing robot (aircraft defastening)
sources.title: US Air Force RSO | Automation & Robotics
sources.claim: Wilder Systems' robots automate rivet drill-out on real aircraft in Air Force depot facilities using lasers and vision, but the demonstrated in-situ capability is fastener removal and hole drilling, not fitting and securing a replacement skin section.

tasks.label: Cure bonded structures, using portable or stationary curing equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: MRO hangar, on-aircraft external composite patch repair (fuselage skin, wing panel, control surface, radome): after layup the technician builds the bagging stack (peel ply, release film, breather, caul), tapes thermocouples around the patch, positions a silicone heater blanket, seals a vacuum bag over a curved contour, connects a portable hot bonder, runs and monitors a ramped multi-hour cure cycle with vacuum and temperature checks, then debags and inspects.

Composite/bond backshop: a removed component (flight control surface, honeycomb sandwich panel, nacelle part, radome) with a bonded repair or bonded assembly is bagged, vacuum and thermocouple leads connected, loaded into a walk-in oven or autoclave (or clamped into a heated bonding press/fixture), the programmed cure cycle is run and logged, the part is unloaded, debagged and verified.

Shop bench cure of small bonded items: bonded metal doublers, interior/decorative laminate panels, small honeycomb plug repairs and bonded fittings cured with heat lamps, a small hot bonder, a heated platen press or a bonding fixture; short cycles, several parts per shift.

Awkward-access on-aircraft cure in the hangar: repair inside the cabin/under floor, in a wheel well, inside empennage or on top of a wing/vertical stabilizer from a lift; blanket, thermocouples and bag applied in a confined or elevated position, with heat management around heat sinks, adjacent systems and temperature-sensitive structure.

Line maintenance/ramp or remote-site cure: portable hot bonder used at the gate or on a remote stand, often under tenting, with ambient temperature, wind and humidity affecting heat-up and dwell; time-pressured turnaround and logbook sign-off.

sources.system: CAIRE scarf-joining robot (Composite Adaptable Inspection and Repair)
sources.title: Lufthansa Technik unveils robot that can scan and fix a plane's outer layer tiles
sources.claim: The most advanced on-aircraft composite repair robot (CAIRE scarf-joining robot, Lufthansa Technik/Airbus) scans damage and mills the scarf on the airframe, but the repair plies are then bonded and cured by hand — no robot performs the bonded-repair cure on aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Same work object (bonded composite repair on an aircraft in an MRO hangar); the source shows the cure step of that repair remains manual even where a robot performs the adjacent machining step.

sources.system: Schmidt & Heinzmann automated bonding cell (Automated Bonding of Composite Parts)
sources.title: An SMC machinery provider adds automation | CompositesWorld
sources.claim: A commercial automated bonding cell joins multiple FRP and metal components and cures the adhesive in a heated pressing tool inside a reconfigurable, purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: curing an adhesively bonded composite/metal assembly in stationary heated curing equipment. Same physical operation (heat + pressure applied to an adhesive bondline to an engineering cure schedule) on comparable composite/metal parts, executed unattended in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Multi-kinematic gripping system for vacuum bagging (3 independent manipulators on a 6-DOF industrial robot)
sources.developer: DLR Center for Lightweight Production Technology (ZLP)
sources.title: Introduction of a Multi Kinematic Gripping System for the Vacuum Bagging Process of Complex Shaped Aerospace Composite Structures
sources.claim: A robot-mounted multi-kinematic gripping system demonstrated automated placement of vacuum-bagging consumables (peel ply, release film, membrane) onto doubly curved aerospace tooling, the setup step that precedes cure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vacuum bagging of aerospace CFRP structures, the consumable-stack and bag application that a technician performs before running a cure cycle; same materials and comparable doubly curved surfaces.

tasks.label: Prepare and paint aircraft surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Spot touch-up after a structural or corrosion repair on an in-service aircraft in a line/base maintenance hangar: mechanic locates the repaired area on the skin, feather-sands and scuffs the surrounding paint, solvent-cleans, masks a local patch, brushes/sprays primer and matching topcoat, and blends the edge so the repair is invisible and sealed.

Full exterior repaint of an airframe in a dedicated paint hangar to a single-color/base scheme (e.g., military gray, all-white corporate base, cargo fleet standard): wash and sand/scuff the whole skin, solvent wipe, mask antennas/probes/windows, spray primer and topcoat over the entire fuselage, wings and empennage to spec film thickness.

Full repaint with a complex multi-color commercial or corporate livery in a paint hangar: repeated masking and unmasking for stripes, logos and gradients, plus hand-laid stencils, registration marks, walkway/no-step markings and decals, with hand touch-up of edges before acceptance.

Priming/painting removed components in a shop paint booth: access panels, cowlings, fairings, landing-gear parts, brackets and fabricated repair patches are stripped or scuffed, alodine/etch-primed, hung or fixtured, and sprayed with primer and topcoat, then inspected for coverage and cure.

Applying corrosion-inhibiting primer, sealant or CIC to structure in awkward or confined areas: wheel wells, wing/fuselage interior stringers and bilges, flap tracks, opened-up joints after corrosion removal, sprayed or brushed through access openings with wands and mirrors in a hangar or shop.

Stripping old coatings from a whole small aircraft or a large area of a larger airframe: chemical stripper application and scraping, plastic-media/laser blast, or sanding down to primer/bare metal in a strip bay or paint hangar, followed by rinse and surface inspection before repaint.

roles.description: Repair and refinish automotive vehicle bodies and straighten vehicle frames.

tasks.label: File, grind, sand, and smooth filled or repaired surfaces, using power tools and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rough shaping of cured body filler on an accessible outer panel (fender, door skin, quarter) still mounted on the customer's vehicle in a collision-shop bay: grinding/cheese-grating the high spots, then block and DA sanding through 40–180 grit to restore the panel contour and feather the filler edge into surrounding paint, checking by hand and guide coat.

Grinding and dressing welds and bare-metal prep on structural or panel-replacement repairs in the shop: grinding down MIG plug welds and seams on a replaced quarter or rocker, stripping paint/corrosion to bare metal around the repair, smoothing weld beads flush without gouging or overheating the base metal.

Final smoothing before refinish on the vehicle in the shop: sanding glazing putty, block-sanding primer-surfacer to a flat paint-ready surface, wet sanding and scuff-sanding adjacent blend panels through fine grits so the repair is invisible under topcoat.

Confined and detail areas on the vehicle: door jambs, panel edges and flanges, body-line creases, around handles, lamps, mirrors and trim openings, inside bumper-cover corners — worked mostly with hand files, small blocks, scuff pads and mini sanders where a machine cannot easily reach.

Detached parts worked off the vehicle in the shop's prep area: a new or repaired bumper cover, hood or door skin on a stand or bench, filler or plastic repair material sanded and feathered, part scuffed and smoothed for primer.

Mobile/on-site repair: a mobile bumper or dent-repair technician grinds and sands a filled scuff on a vehicle parked in a customer's lot, dealership row or driveway, in ambient weather and lighting with only portable tools.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: sanding cured putty (body-filler-like material) on large tooling to a target shape and finish. Transfers to sanding filler on a fixtured body panel — same abrasive media, force-controlled contact, scan-based shape correction, and comparable smoothness acceptance; only the workpiece differs.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-grit abrasive shape correction and surface prep in a robotic cell. The auto-body instance requires the same sequence of grind → coarse sand → fine sand with tool and grit changes on curved panels.

tasks.label: Inspect repaired vehicles for proper functioning, completion of work, dimensional accuracy, and overall appearance of paint job, and test-drive vehicles to ensure proper alignment and handling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Final refinish quality check in the shop's paint/detail bay: technician examines the freshly cleared and buffed repair area under shop lighting and daylight for dirt nibs, runs, orange peel, sand scratches, mottling and blend/color match to the adjacent original panels, on a customer vehicle of arbitrary make, age and color parked in a bay.

Pre-delivery walkaround of the assembled repaired vehicle in the shop bay or lot: verifying every part on the repair order is installed (moldings, clips, badges, lamps, fascia), checking door/hood/deck panel gaps and flush against the undamaged side, checking for overspray, tape lines, new dings or dirt, and confirming the car is clean and ready to hand over.

Functional check of the repaired systems in the shop: opening/closing doors, hood and hatch, cycling windows, mirrors and latches, checking lamps, wipers, horn, HVAC and seat belts, running a post-repair diagnostic scan for stored codes and confirming ADAS calibrations and warning-lamp status.

Dimensional verification after structural/unibody or frame repair: vehicle on the frame bench or lift, technician sets up the electronic measuring system (laser/ultrasonic targets) and compares control points, datum heights, and upper-body openings to OEM specification, documenting a final measurement report.

Post-repair road test on public streets plus alignment-rack check after suspension, steering or structural work: driving several miles in traffic to feel for pull, off-center steering wheel, vibration, brake behavior, clunks, wind or water noise, and confirming no warning lamps, then verifying toe/camber on the alignment rack.

tasks.label: Fit and weld replacement parts into place, using wrenches and welding equipment, and grind down welds to smooth them, using power grinders and other tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop bay/frame bench: replacing a welded outer body panel on a late-model unibody car or SUV (quarter panel, body-side section, rocker). Technician test-fits the new OEM panel to the cut opening, adjusts gaps to adjacent doors/lamps, clamps, makes squeeze-type resistance spot welds and MIG plug welds per OEM procedure, then grinds/dresses the welds flush before filler and primer.

Collision shop, vehicle on frame rack with electronic measuring: structural sectioning and replacement of rails, aprons, reinforcements or a truck frame section. Part is trimmed to the sectioning joint, positioned to measured spec, tacked, fully welded (MIG/silicon bronze) and welds ground smooth; heat control and weld quality checked against OEM specs.

Collision shop: bolted-plus-welded assembly work — door skin, radiator support, fender/bumper brackets, tabs and clips. Mostly wrench/socket fitting and alignment of bolted parts to correct gaps, with a limited number of MIG welds on brackets or skin edges and grinding of those welds.

Collision/restoration shop: rust or small-collision patch repair on an older vehicle. Technician cuts out corroded metal by hand, fabricates or trims a patch panel from stock or an aftermarket piece to the irregular hand-cut opening, butt-welds it in short stitches while managing burn-through on thin, uneven, corroded sheet, then grinds the welds flat.

Mobile/field or fleet-yard work: welding replacement panels, plates or body parts on trucks, trailers, buses or fleet vehicles at a customer site or open yard — variable access, outdoor conditions, vehicle not on a lift or fixture — followed by grinding the welds smooth.

tasks.label: Prime and paint repaired surfaces, using paint sprayguns and motorized sanders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refinishing a repaired panel still on the assembled vehicle in a collision shop: after filler/metal work the tech DA-sands and feather-edges the repair, masks, sprays primer-surfacer in the prep station, block-sands it, then in the downdraft booth applies sealer, basecoat blended into the adjacent panel, and clearcoat. Vehicle is rolled in by hand; make, color and damage location vary job to job.

Refinishing detached parts in the shop's booth: new or repaired bumper covers, fenders, doors, hoods, mirror caps hung on stands or racks — scuff/sand the part, apply adhesion promoter and primer, sand, then base and clear to match the mixed color.

Small spot repair / scuff-and-shoot: a scratch, chip or small dent on one panel — localized sanding, spot primer, spot blend of base and clear into the surrounding paint, then de-nib and polish to blend the edge.

Large multi-panel or full respray (heavy collision, fleet vans, older vehicles): extensive powered sanding over large areas, full-vehicle masking, primer over several panels, then full-body color and clearcoat in the booth.

Awkward substrates and areas: aluminum or plastic/SMC panels, door jambs, edges, inner structures, undersides and welded seams — epoxy/corrosion primer, chip guard or undercoat sprayed into recessed and inverted areas with small sanders used in tight access.

Mobile/on-site smart repair: a mobile refinish tech works at a dealership lot, fleet yard or customer driveway with portable sander and spray setup under a pop-up shelter — sand, prime and blend a small painted area outdoors in ambient conditions.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics Scan&Spray (GMR-AI robotic cell)

sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Spray robotic cells apply primers and paint with a pressurized spray gun to a controlled film thickness on high-mix parts, with toolpaths generated automatically from an onboard scan rather than programmed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray application of primer and topcoat on high-mix manufactured parts. It transfers to priming/painting repaired auto body panels because the objects (large curved painted panels), the tool (pressurized spray gun), the film-build/appearance standard, and the fixtured-in-a-cell presentation are the same.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic random-orbital sanding of raw and primer-coated vehicle bodywork before painting. This is the same operation (motorized sanding of primer/substrate on vehicle body panels to a paint-ready finish) that precedes and follows priming in collision refinishing.

tasks.label: Sand body areas to be painted and cover bumpers, windows, and trim with masking tape or paper to protect them from the paint.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop stall: prepping a repaired panel still on the vehicle — block-sanding cured body filler and primer to contour, feather-edging into the surrounding paint, scuffing the blend area, then masking the adjacent panels, glass, door handles, trim, lamps and wheels with tape and masking paper before the car goes into the booth.

Prepping detached/new parts (bumper cover, fender, hood, mirror caps) on a stand or paint rack in the shop: scuff-sanding the whole part for adhesion, sanding primer on any repaired areas, and taping off the areas that stay unpainted (textured lower valance, emblems, sensor bezels, mounting flanges).

Overall repaint: sanding/scuffing the entire vehicle body and fully masking it — wheels and tires bagged, glass and lamps covered with paper or plastic sheeting, jambs, weatherstrip and all trim taped — a multi-hour whole-car prep in the shop.

Spot repair / panel blend in the shop: sanding a small damaged area or scratch and scuffing the blend zone, then back-taping the blend edge, taping trim and emblems, and draping the rest of the car with plastic sheeting and paper.

Mobile or off-site prep (dealership lot, fleet yard, mobile smart-repair van): sanding a bumper scuff or small dent repair and masking the surrounding trim, glass and adjacent panels outdoors on an as-found vehicle, in variable light, wind and dust.

tasks.label: Chain or clamp frames and sections to alignment machines that use hydraulic pressure to align damaged components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop bay: unibody passenger car with moderate front-end damage is rolled onto a frame rack/bench; technician crawls under the vehicle to set and tighten four pinch-weld anchoring clamps at the rocker seams, then attaches pull clamps and chains to the damaged rail/apron, positions the pull tower, and runs hydraulic pulls with laser/mechanical measuring feedback, repositioning chains between pulls.

Shop bay: unibody car with side or rear-quarter damage needing multi-vector pulls. Technician anchors the vehicle, then bolts specialty clamps into structural holes / grips flanges, rigs two or three chains at different angles and heights, applies staged hydraulic pressure while hammer-and-dollying and re-measuring, and re-rigs several times before dimensions are accepted.

Shop bay: light truck, SUV or van with a full ladder frame. Technician raises the vehicle, fits heavy vise-type frame clamps to boxed/C-channel rails, wraps and hooks heavy chains at the specified anchoring locations, and applies high-force hydraulic pulls to correct rail sag/diamond/sway.

Shop bay, minor structural work: a single section pull — door opening, rocker, radiator support or quarter panel pinch weld — clamped to the rack or to a portable pulling post/porta-power, given one or two short controlled hydraulic pulls to restore gaps, with wood blocks or protective pads to avoid marring.

Shop bay, severe wreck: non-rolling vehicle is winched or forklifted onto the rack; anchoring points are themselves deformed so the technician improvises with plate clamps, straps and chains on undamaged structure, working around fluid leaks, glass, dirt and torn sheet metal before setting up multiple pulls.

Heavy-duty truck or trailer frame/section straightening done with portable pulling equipment, sometimes outside a dedicated bay (fleet yard, open shop apron): chains wrapped around frame rails and anchored to floor pots or a portable pulling post, hydraulic rams pressurized to correct bent rails or bumper/cab mounts.

sources.system: Celette frame anchoring clamps / frame straightening bench
sources.title: Full-Frame Machine Anchoring Clamps & Anchoring Systems | CELETTE
sources.claim: Frame anchoring is a manual, per-vehicle judgment task: technicians select and fit pinch-weld or ladder-frame clamps to grip the specific vehicle's seams or rails before hydraulic pulls; no automation of this step is described by equipment makers.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, described by the equipment vendor; establishes that clamp selection and fitting is performed by technicians on each vehicle, with no robotic product offered.

sources.system: Pinchweld clamp anchoring procedure (I-CAR Repairability Technical Support)
sources.title: Back-To-Basics: Pinchweld Clamps - Anchoring - UPDATE | I-CAR RTS
sources.claim: I-CAR technical guidance shows anchoring requires vehicle-specific inspection and judgment (some vehicles lack a usable pinchweld flange, requiring alternative equipment-maker-specified anchoring), i.e. the setup is not a fixed repeatable sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Same task; documents the variability and judgment required in clamping a damaged vehicle to an alignment machine.

sources.system: RoboTire robotic tire-changing system
sources.title: Robot Mechanic Could Automate the Tire Changing Experience | IoT World Today
sources.claim: The most advanced robot deployed on customer vehicles in retail auto service is a wheel/tire changing cell, which works on wheels at a known lift position — it does not anchor vehicles, rig chains, or apply structural pulls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work on a customer vehicle inside a service shop (E2). It does not transfer — it manipulates standardized wheels/lug nuts at fixed positions, not heavy chains, anchoring clamps and multi-ton hydraulic pulls on deformed, vehicle-specific structure.

sources.system: PaintGo intelligent spray painting robot
sources.title: Auto Body Shop Painting Robot California | Body Shop Automation - PaintGo USA
sources.claim: Robots sold into collision repair shops today perform non-contact spray painting guided by 3D vision; no vendor offers a robot that anchors vehicles or performs structural pulling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic work on damaged vehicles inside a body shop (E2). It does not transfer — painting is a non-contact, low-force surface-following operation, whereas anchoring and pulling requires heavy rigging, tool tightening and force-controlled structural manipulation.

sources.system: Galdabini automatic straightening presses
sources.title: Automatic straightening machines for gearbox shafts - Galdabini
sources.claim: Automatic hydraulic straightening machines exist as purpose-built cells with automatic clamping and closed-loop measurement, but they handle known-geometry rotationally symmetric workpieces such as shafts and railway axles loaded by gantry or 6-axis robots, not crash-damaged vehicle bodies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hydraulic alignment of bent components with automatic workholding. It does not transfer to this task — the machine accepts only standard, undamaged-geometry parts in dedicated tooling; it cannot receive a wrecked car body, choose anchoring/pull points on crumpled structure, or rig chains.

sources.system: Humanoid robots in industrial manufacturing (Figure, Apptronik, Digit and peers)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Industrial Manufacturing: What They Can (and Can't) Do in 2026
sources.claim: Humanoid robots in automotive settings as of 2026 are limited to a narrow set of pilot tasks (part handling, kitting, inspection) at a handful of sites, well short of heavy rigging and force-controlled structural repair.
sources.transferJustification: General-purpose mobile manipulation is the only candidate class for under-vehicle clamping and chain rigging; this source shows the demonstrated task envelope does not include such work.

tasks.label: Position dolly blocks against surfaces of dented areas and beat opposite surfaces to remove dents, using hammers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop repair bay: a small-to-medium dent or crease in an accessible outer steel panel (door skin, fender, hood) on a customer vehicle. Tech removes trim/inner panel or reaches through an access hole, holds a dolly behind the low, bumps or hammers-off-dolly working from indirect toward direct damage, then feels the surface by hand/file and metal-finishes so only a skim of filler is needed.

Vehicle on a frame rack or pulling post with major collision damage (quarter panel, rocker, A/B pillar area). Tech roughs out the damage with hammer and dolly while tension is applied, relieving stress in buckles and reshaping body lines and crowns; poor access, heavy blows, work coordinated with pulling and heat.

Removed panel or new replacement/salvage panel worked on a bench or panel stand in the shop: bumping out shipping/handling dents, straightening flanges and hem edges with dolly and hammer, tuning contour so the part fits gaps and body lines before installation.

Dings, creases and hail dents on high-strength steel or aluminum panels, worked in a shop's dedicated aluminum/clean repair area with dedicated non-ferrous hammers and dollies, controlled heat and OEM-limited repair procedures; very little tolerance for stretching or cracking.

Heavy-gauge work in a truck/fleet or agricultural body shop: dents in pickup beds, box-truck panels, bus skins, fenders and toolboxes; larger dollies and heavier hammers, cosmetic standard sometimes lower but access often awkward.

Mobile or catastrophe work off-site: technician works a dented panel with dolly and hammer at a customer driveway, dealer lot, parking-lot hail tent or fleet yard, outdoors with variable light, weather and no fixed layout.

sources.system: RoboCraftsman / RoboForming (Machina Labs)
sources.title: Machina Labs uses robots to manufacture titanium sheet metal parts - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Machina Labs' RoboCraftsman cells use two industrial robot arms on opposite sides of a fixtured sheet to incrementally form (not repair) metal panels to CAD geometry inside a purpose-built cell; this is the closest robotic analogue to two-sided dolly-and-hammer work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: two-sided incremental sheet forming of new blanks. It shares the object class (automotive-scale sheet metal) and the opposed-tool geometry of dolly-and-hammer, but it forms virgin blanks to CAD in a fixture rather than diagnosing and reversing collision damage in a work-hardened, painted, already-formed panel, so it does not substantiate completion of the repair task.

sources.system: RoboCraftsman (Machina Labs)
sources.title: Capabilities | Machina
sources.claim: Machina Labs states its cells hold the sheet in a frame and achieve roughly ±1 mm / ±0.3% accuracy with 125 µin Ra finish — coarser than the metal-finished contour an auto body repairer must deliver, and on new panels rather than damaged ones.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic sheet forming). Cited to show the precision and workpiece presentation of the nearest robotic system; the tolerance and the virgin-blank workflow fall short of dent removal to a paintable, metal-finished contour on a damaged vehicle panel.

sources.system: Mechatroforming (fixtureless automated incremental sheet metal forming)
sources.title: An automated solution for fixtureless sheet metal forming | The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
sources.claim: Research-grade 'Mechatroforming' uses a robot arm to manipulate a sheet under a controlled hammering tool inside an automated forming setup — robotic hammering of sheet metal exists only as a forming process for new parts in a machine-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic hammer-forming of sheet metal. It shows a robot can strike sheet metal under control, but the workpiece is a simple new part manipulated into a machine, not a dented panel on a vehicle; no dent diagnosis, dolly backing, or metal finishing is demonstrated.

sources.system: Robot-based machine hammer peening
sources.title: Robot based machine hammer peening using an electromagnetic driven hammering device (PDF)
sources.claim: Robotic machine hammer peening is an established robot application, but it is a surface-treatment/structuring process (residual stress, mold surfaces), not restoration of a panel's contour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic controlled hammering of metal surfaces. Confirms robots can apply repeated controlled blows, but the purpose is surface conditioning on rigid fixtured parts, not backing a dolly and reversing a dent to a paintable contour, so it does not transfer to this task.

tasks.label: Cut and tape plastic separating film to outside repair areas to avoid damaging surrounding surfaces during repair procedure and remove tape and wash surfaces after repairs are complete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop prep bay: before refinishing a repaired quarter panel or door, the tech cuts pre-taped masking film/plastic sheeting from a roll, tapes it along body lines to adjacent panels, covers glass, wheels, lamps and trim, back-tapes edges; after paint/cure, pulls all tape and film without lifting fresh paint and washes/wipes the surrounding surfaces.

Small spot or blend repair (bumper cover corner, mirror cap, small dent): fine-line tape at the blend boundary plus small pieces of plastic film taped over adjacent trim, badges and openings; after the spot repair, tape and film are removed and the area cleaned and washed.

Protecting surrounding surfaces during non-paint work (welding, cutting, grinding/sanding, seam sealing, glass or panel replacement, frame pulling): plastic film cut and taped over adjacent panels, interior trim and glass to catch sparks, dust and sealer; removed afterward and surfaces washed down.

Full or large-area refinish on a full-size vehicle (pickup, van, fleet truck, RV): extensive masking of the whole vehicle exterior, jambs, glass, wheels and trim with film and tape, often on a lift or in a large booth; complete unmasking and wash-down after cure.

Mobile/on-site repair at a dealership lot, fleet yard or customer driveway: masking film taped around the repair area on a vehicle parked outdoors in wind, dust and varying light, then tape/film removal and wash after the repair.

sources.system: Active Taping Kit (ATK) — Aerobotix / FerRobotics
sources.title: New End-Effector Applies Masking Tape | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: The Aerobotix/FerRobotics Active Taping Kit is a commercial force-controlled end-effector that lets a six-axis robot automatically lay masking tape lines on aircraft assemblies inside a robotic cell; it applies tape only, on rigid fixtured parts, and does not cut or apply plastic masking film, remove masking, or wash surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic masking-tape application for painting. It is the closest automated masking capability found, but it lays straight tape lines on rigid, fixtured aerospace parts in a purpose-built cell; the auto-body task requires cutting and taping limp plastic sheeting over compound-curved vehicle surfaces and then de-masking and washing, none of which this system does.

sources.system: PaintGo intelligent spray painting robot (ONEW Technology)
sources.title: A Robot that Paints Cars - Autosphere
sources.claim: PaintGo robotic refinish arms are in commercial service in body shops and dealership repair centers, spraying primer/base/clear autonomously after a human loads and programs the job — but the vehicle is masked by people and the robot simply avoids the masked sections, showing masking/unmasking is still manual in the most automated body shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated refinish spraying in the same body-shop setting. It shows that even where a robot performs the painting, the cut-and-tape masking of surrounding surfaces and its later removal remain human work; no masking capability is claimed for the system.

sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System (with FANUC robots)
sources.title: General Motors and 3M Partner on New Robotic Paint System | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: The 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint ..., installed at GM's Spring Hill plant, autonomously inspects and then sands and polishes topcoat defects on vehicles moving down an assembly line — automated vehicle-surface work confined to abrasive processing of rigid painted panels in a purpose-built line, not to masking with film and tape.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic surface work on painted vehicle bodies. It establishes the frontier for automated vehicle-surface operations (vision-planned sanding/polishing of rigid surfaces) and does not extend to handling, cutting, taping or peeling deformable masking film.

tasks.label: Review damage reports, prepare or review repair cost estimates, and plan work to be performed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Fill small dents that cannot be worked out with plastic or solder.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop bay, on-vehicle: after roughing/pulling a dent in a steel door, fender or quarter panel, the tech grinds to bare metal, mixes two-part polyester filler with hardener, spreads it over the low spot, waits for cure, then cheese-grates/board-sands and block-sands to the panel contour, feathers the edge, checks by hand and guide coat, and glazes pinholes until primer-ready.

Detached panel or replacement part on a stand or bench in the shop: filling small dings, weld seams and low spots on a hood, deck lid, fender or salvage panel removed from the vehicle; same mix-apply-cure-sand cycle, done at a comfortable working height.

Plastic bumper cover or other flexible plastic panel: gouges, scuffs and shallow dents filled with flexible/adhesive filler after sanding and adhesion prep, then shaped and feathered to the cover's contour, on a stand or on the vehicle.

Awkward exterior geometry on the vehicle: filling small dents on roofs, pillars, wheel-arch curves, near character lines, and on vertical or overhead surfaces, including aluminum panels that require dedicated aluminum-safe filler and segregated tooling.

Mobile / on-site repair: technician fills a small dent or ding in a driveway, dealership lot, parking garage or fleet yard, working out of a van with no fixed bay, with variable light, wind, dust and temperature affecting filler cure.

Restoration work using body solder/lead: heating and tinning the panel, wiping molten lead into the low area, then filing and shaping the solder flush with the surrounding sheet metal on a classic vehicle in the shop.

sources.system: Scan&Sand (GrayMatter Robotics)
sources.title: Scan&Sand helps automate labor-intensive ambulance manufacturing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Sand autonomous robotic sanding cell is deployed at ambulance maker Life Line Emergency Vehicles, sanding raw and primed emergency-vehicle bodies, handling complex geometries and sanding for shape correction with push-button operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sanding/shape correction of vehicle body panels to a paint-ready standard. This is the shaping half of dent filling, on the same class of objects (vehicle body panels) and to the same finish standard a body shop requires before primer.

sources.system: Robotic sanding / AI-enabled sanding system in Pierce paint facility
sources.title: The Optimal 7-Step Fire Truck Painting Process | Pierce Mfg
sources.claim: Pierce Manufacturing runs robotic sanding and preparation systems in its fire-apparatus paint process; the robots smooth applied body filler and metal surfaces ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sanding of applied body filler on truck bodies. Same material (polyester body filler), same substrate (sheet-metal vehicle bodywork) and the same paint-ready quality bar as the shaping step of this task.

sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System
sources.title: 3M and GM Partner on First-Ever Robotic Paint Repair System on Moving Assembly Line
sources.claim: 3M's Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair ... installed at GM's Spring Hill plant, where a vision system locates and classifies localized defects on each car body and robots then sand and polish them on a moving assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous detection and localized abrasive repair of small surface defects on automotive bodies. It shows machine localization of a small defect on a car panel and finishing it to Class-A appearance, matching the perception and finishing demands of filling a small dent.

sources.system: Aerones wind turbine maintenance and repair robot (Leading Edge Repair)
sources.title: Aerones introduces 'first' wind turbine maintenance and repair robot | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Aerones' wind turbine maintenance and repair robot is reported by its developer to perform Level 1-3 leading-edge erosion repairs autonomously, with attachments for surface preparation, primer application, filler application and protective coating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling eroded low spots in a coated composite shell with a certified filler and sanding it back flush. Same physical operation as this task (deposit filler over a defect, smooth it, cure, abrade to the surrounding contour) on a curved coated surface.

sources.system: Aerones Leading Edge Repair robot
sources.title: Leading Edge Repair - Robotic Wind Turbine Care Systems | Aerones
sources.claim: Aerones' commercial leading-edge repair service sequence has the robot prepare the surface, apply filling compound to the eroded area with a smoothing technique, then sand repeatedly to a smooth surface and apply coating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application and smoothing of filler over surface damage followed by sanding it flush - the same apply/cure/abrade cycle as filling a small dent with plastic filler.

tasks.label: Remove damaged sections of vehicles using metal-cutting guns, air grinders and wrenches, and install replacement parts using wrenches or welding equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop, late-model unibody car: remove damaged bolt-on parts (bumper cover, fender, hood, door, grille, headlamp) with sockets/wrenches and air tools — releasing clips, hidden fasteners and wiring connectors — then hang and align replacement parts to OEM panel-gap specs and torque fasteners.

Collision shop, structural sectioning: cut out a damaged quarter panel/rocker/rail/apron section with cut-off wheel, reciprocating saw or plasma cutter along an OEM-approved sectioning line, drill or mill out spot welds, grind flanges clean of e-coat and seam sealer, clamp and fit the service part, then MIG/squeeze-type resistance spot weld it in and dress the welds.

Collision shop, welded/bonded skin replacement: strip a roof panel or door skin (grind off welds or cut bonded flanges), remove the damaged skin, prep mating flanges with air grinder, then fit and weld/bond the replacement panel and finish the joint.

Heavy-duty / commercial vehicle body shop: cut away damaged truck bed, box, bracketry or frame-mounted structure with torch, plasma or grinder, unbolt heavy mounts, then bolt and weld in replacement sections on thicker-gauge steel, often working under or over a large vehicle.

Older or corroded vehicle in a general body shop: seized/rusted fasteners cut off with a cut-off wheel or torch, hidden rust and prior repairs discovered mid-job, patch panels trimmed and fitted by hand, welded in and ground smooth.

Mobile / on-site repair at a fleet yard, dealership lot or customer location: unbolt a damaged bolt-on panel, bumper or mirror assembly outdoors with hand and air tools from a service van and install the replacement.

sources.system: RoboTire (4th-generation tire changing system)
sources.title: RoboTire: The Next Frontier in Automotive Maintenance – Impact Lab
sources.claim: RoboTire's vision-guided robot arms autonomously locate wheels and lug fasteners on customer vehicles, unscrew and remove nuts/bolts and pull the wheels, with a human technician assisting; deployed in Discount Tire and Creamery Tire stores. This is the closest deployed system to unbolting a part off a customer car, but it handles only one standardized, undamaged interface and does not remove or fit body panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal/reinstallation of a bolted vehicle component (wheel) on a customer car using a powered torque wrench. It bears on the 'remove ... using wrenches, install replacement parts using wrenches' element, but covers a single standardized fastener circle on an undamaged hub, not deformed panels, clips, harness connectors or gap alignment.

sources.system: Path Robotics intelligent welding cells (Obsidian AI)
sources.title: The Technology / Intelligent Welding Cells – Path Robotics
sources.claim: Path Robotics' Obsidian AI scans each part and plans weld paths in a robotic welding cell without programming, handling imperfect fit-up and part-to-part variation — i.e., adaptive autonomous arc welding of fabricated assemblies inside a purpose-built cell, not welding of replacement panels onto a damaged vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous adaptive welding of variable metal parts. It speaks only to the joining sub-step in a fixtured cell on shop-fabricated steel assemblies; no cited deployment cuts out damaged vehicle structure or fits a service panel to a wrecked body.

sources.system: Figure 02 humanoid
sources.title: Successful test of humanoid robots at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg
sources.claim: Figure 02 humanoids at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg autonomously inserted sheet metal parts into welding fixtures during a multi-week trial — part placement into a fixture in a factory body shop, not removal of damaged sections or fastening/welding of replacement panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and placement of automotive sheet metal. It shows placement accuracy in a fixtured factory setting but not disassembly of a damaged vehicle, fastener removal, cutting, or panel fit-up and welding on a repair.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics Scan&Grind / robotic sanding cells
sources.title: Grinding and sanding go autonomous – The Fabricator
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' AI-driven cells perform autonomous grinding, sanding and weld blending on high-mix parts in fabrication shops, adjusting from onboard sensor feedback — the closest autonomous analogue to the air-grinder element, but on loose parts in a robotic cell, not on a damaged vehicle body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic grinding of variable metal surfaces, relevant to the grinding sub-step of weld dressing and flange prep; it does not include cutting out damaged vehicle sections or installing replacement parts.

sources.system: Kinetic robotic calibration facility
sources.title: The collision repair shop of the future opens in the Dogpatch
sources.claim: The most advanced robotics actually deployed in US collision repair as of 2026 are ADAS diagnosis and calibration hubs (Kinetic), which perform sensor calibration after body work; no cited system performs the body work itself.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to establish the state of collision-repair robotics: it covers post-repair electronic calibration, a different task, and confirms that panel removal and replacement remains manual.

tasks.label: Remove small pits and dimples in body metal, using pick hammers and punches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop bay: after roughing out a dent in a steel door/fender/quarter with hammer-and-dolly or pulls, the tech metal-finishes the area — runs a body file or bare hand over it, then picks up remaining low spots from behind with a pick hammer and knocks down high spots with a punch, iterating until the panel is true enough for a skim of filler and paint.

Shop bay, minor damage: door dings, small pits, shallow dimples and pock marks on an accessible panel (hood, roof, deck lid) with the back side reachable; tech picks each low spot over a dolly and files/checks by reflection until the surface reads flat before primer.

Shop bay, limited-access areas: pits and dimples on quarter panels, pillars, roof rails or double-walled panel edges; pick work done blind through drilled access holes or with long-reach picks, judged by feel, followed by hole sealing.

Shop bay, aluminum or high-strength-steel panel in a segregated aluminum repair area: picking small dents and pits with non-marring picks under OEM-limited heat, where over-picking cracks or stretches the panel and the repair must meet OEM procedure.

Restoration/custom shop: classic or hand-formed panel metal-finished with pick hammer, planishing hammer and file to near-perfect contour with no filler accepted; irregular, non-CAD panel shapes and often bare, previously repaired metal.

Mobile/on-site: technician at a dealership lot, fleet yard or customer driveway removing small dings and pits from a vehicle as found — variable lighting, weather, no fixturing, vehicle parked among others.

sources.system: RoboCraftsman / RoboForming
sources.title: Machina Labs – NCMS exhibitor page
sources.claim: Machina Labs' RoboCraftsman is a commercially available cell in which two 7-axis robots incrementally form sheet metal from opposite sides under closed-loop AI control, with autonomous sheet loading and fixturing.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing robotic analogue to hammer-and-dolly work: two robots deform sheet metal from opposite sides in a fixtured frame. It does not transfer to this task — it forms flat blanks to CAD geometry at roughly millimetre-scale tolerance, whereas removing pits and dimples means detecting and correcting sub-millimetre defects on an already-shaped, previously damaged panel to a paint-ready cosmetic standard; no demonstration of defect repair or Class-A finish is shown.

tasks.label: Remove upholstery, accessories, electrical window-and-seat-operating equipment, and trim to gain access to vehicle bodies and fenders.

Heavily damaged or corroded vehicle: fasteners seized or sheared, clips broken, panels crushed so trim is trapped or access is nonstandard; the repairer improvises — drills out bolts, cuts trim free where it is scrap, salvages reusable pieces, works around deployed airbags.

Unfamiliar, older, exotic or accessorized vehicle: technician consults OEM service data to find hidden fasteners, removes aftermarket accessories and upholstery (headliner, seat covers, custom panels) on a restoration or older car with brittle plastic and no standard layout.
Quick single-part removal in the shop: pull one molding, badge, splash shield, mud flap or door handle to expose a small dent or an area to be refinished, then set it aside undamaged for reinstall.
