tasks.label: Mix polyester resins and hardeners to be used in restoring damaged areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop bay: technician scoops a golf-ball-to-fist-sized dollop of polyester body filler from a gallon can onto a mixing board, squeezes a proportional ribbon of cream (BPO) hardener, and folds/knees it with a plastic spreader to uniform color, air-free, within a 3-5 minute pot life, then applies it to the prepped repair area.

Large repair (quarter panel, heavy dent, rusted-out section): worker mixes successive larger batches of heavy-bodied, lightweight, or fiber/aluminum-reinforced polyester filler, adjusting hardener slightly for shop temperature, keeping each batch workable while spreading over a broad damaged area.

Finish stage: worker mixes a small amount of polyester glazing/finishing putty with a tiny, carefully judged amount of hardener to fill pinholes, sand scratches and low spots; ratio errors cause staining, pinholing or slow cure.

Fiberglass/plastic panel or restoration work: worker measures liquid polyester (fiberglass) resin into a cup and adds MEKP catalyst drops at a percentage judged for temperature and batch size, stirs to homogeneity, then wets out mat or cloth over the damaged area.

Shop using cartridge-metered materials: worker loads a dual-cartridge filler/glaze cartridge into a manual or pneumatic dynamic-mixing applicator, purges, and dispenses pre-proportioned mixed filler on demand at the vehicle.

Transfer holds because the operation is identical in kind - metering a resin and a catalyst to a fixed ratio and mixing them homogeneously before a short pot life expires - and the machine is designed for exactly the short-pot-life chemistry class that polyester filler belongs to.

tasks.label: Adjust or align headlights, wheels, and brake systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Headlight aim on a customer's repaired car in a collision-repair shop: after a front bumper/fender/headlamp assembly replacement, the repairer levels the vehicle, sets up an optical aimer or wall screen, opens the hood, locates the vertical/horizontal adjuster screws (often in tight, obstructed engine-bay locations that vary by model), turns them until the low-beam cutoff meets spec, and re-checks.

Four-wheel alignment after suspension or structural repair: drive the vehicle onto the alignment rack, mount clamps/targets on four wheels, run the compensation and measurement routine, then adjust toe at the tie-rod sleeves and camber/caster at eccentric cams, strut slots or shims (frequently on corroded, road-grime-covered used-vehicle hardware), and re-measure to spec.

Brake system service after collision repair: bleed and refill the hydraulic system once a damaged hose/line, caliper or master cylinder has been reconnected, purge the ABS module, adjust the parking brake, and verify pedal travel and braking before release.

Alignment that will not come into spec by adjustment alone: diagnose bent/damaged parts, install a camber/caster correction kit, replace a bent tie rod, control arm or strut, or re-pull the structure on the frame bench, then re-align and re-verify.

Post-alignment electronic re-aiming: reset the steering angle sensor and perform static ADAS recalibration (forward camera/radar targets set at measured distances from the thrust line) plus, on many vehicles, a road-test dynamic calibration after wheel or headlamp work.

tasks.label: Replace damaged glass on vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bonded windshield replacement in a collision/glass shop bay on a customer's late-model car: remove wipers, cowl, A-pillar moldings and rearview/camera bracket cover; cut the cured urethane bead with cold knife or wire tool without scratching paint or cutting the dash; lift out the cracked laminated glass; trim the residual bead to a thin base, treat any bare metal, prime; lay a continuous urethane bead; set the new glass to gap/flush spec; refit trim; then perform the OEM-required static ADAS camera calibration and leak/water test before release.

Mobile windshield replacement performed at the customer's driveway, apartment lot or office parking space: same cut-out, prep, bead and set sequence, but done outdoors on uneven ground in whatever weather and lighting exists, with tools carried from a van, no lift or fixturing, bystanders and traffic nearby, followed by dynamic (drive) or mobile ADAS calibration.

Side door glass (tempered) replacement in the shop after a break-in or collision: pop the interior trim panel clips and screws, disconnect switch/speaker harnesses and the vapor barrier, vacuum shattered fragments from the door cavity and interior, lower the regulator, unbolt/unclip the broken pane, slide the new tempered glass into the regulator clips, torque, test up/down travel and reset the auto-up feature, reassemble panel without rattles.

Back glass, quarter glass or vent glass replacement in the shop: clean out shattered tempered fragments from the trunk/cargo area and headliner area, remove interior trim, unplug defroster grid and antenna leads, cut out bonded backlight or quarter glass, prep and prime the pinchweld, bond the new glass, reconnect defroster/antenna and verify function, reinstall trim.

Glass removal and reinstallation as part of a larger collision repair: the windshield or quarter glass is cut out so a damaged pinchweld, roof rail or quarter panel can be repaired, welded and refinished, then new glass is bonded to the freshly painted flange after cure; the vehicle is partially disassembled, panel fit varies, and the technician must judge flange condition, corrosion protection and adhesive cure/drive-away time.

It shares the object (windshield/backlight) and the set-to-aperture step of this task, but omits the defining steps of glass replacement — cutting out cured urethane, pinchweld cleanup and priming on a used vehicle, shard cleanup, trim/door disassembly and ADAS calibration — so it does not substantiate completion of the whole instance.

tasks.label: Remove damaged panels, and identify the family and properties of the plastic used on a vehicle.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision repair shop: remove a bolt-on damaged steel/aluminum panel (front fender, hood, door, deck lid) from a customer's wrecked vehicle — first pulling wheel-house liner, lamps, moldings and cowl trim, disconnecting harness connectors and grounds, then breaking loose bolts that may be bent, painted over or corroded, and lifting the deformed panel clear without marring adjacent finished panels.

Collision repair shop: remove a damaged plastic bumper fascia, grille, rocker cladding or mirror cap (dozens of screws, push-pin clips, hidden snap tabs, sensor/lamp connectors) and then identify the plastic family and properties — reading the molded ISO code on the backside (e.g. >PP+EPDM<, >TPO<, >PC+ABS<) or doing a grind/melt/adhesion test — to decide whether the part is repairable and which adhesive, welding rod or primer applies.

Collision repair shop: remove a welded panel (quarter panel, rocker, roof skin, sail panel, or sectioned rail) — locate the factory spot welds under sealer and paint, drill or grind each weld nugget, cut sealer/adhesive bead, saw at sectioning lines per OEM procedure, and separate the panel without damaging the underlying structure.

Collision repair shop teardown/blueprinting: strip damaged interior trim panels, seats, headliner edges, door trim, splash shields and inner reinforcements across a wide mix of makes, models and years, with clips that break, fasteners that seize, and parts to be bagged/tagged for reassembly or supplement estimating.

Off-site/mobile work: remove damaged panels or plastic parts at a customer's driveway, a fleet yard, or a salvage/recycling yard (harvesting a replacement panel), on uneven ground, in weather, with only portable tools and no lift or fixture.

sources.system: RoboTire System (4th generation)
sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: RoboTire's vision/AI-guided robotic system is installed and operating in tire retail stores, where it removes lug nuts and lifts wheel/tire assemblies off customer vehicles under technician oversight — the closest deployed case of a robot detaching bolted components from an as-presented consumer vehicle in a service facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wheel removal from a customer vehicle in a service bay. It shows vision-guided location and removal of threaded fasteners on an as-presented vehicle, but only for a standardized, fully exposed 4-6 lug pattern on an undamaged hub; it does not address deformed panels, hidden/mixed fastener types, clip and harness disconnection, or plastic identification.

sources.system: ABB automotive final-assembly robotic cells (door removal, lamp, glazing, tire mounting)
sources.date: current product page, retrieved 2026-07 (offering in market for years)
sources.title: Final Assembly - Robotics | ABB
sources.claim: ABB sells robotic cells for automotive final assembly that include 'door removal' — robots unbolting and lifting a door off a car body inside a fixtured, fenced line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing a bolted panel (door) from a car body. Transfer is limited: the plant case involves brand-new, undamaged bodies of one known model presented on a conveyor at a taught position with bare hinge bolts and no trim, liners or harness attached, whereas collision teardown involves deformed panels, shifted mounting points, damaged/corroded fasteners and prior removal of many attached parts.

sources.system: Robotic screw unfastening and collection cell (cobot + electric spindle + 3D camera + F/T sensor)
sources.developer: University of Birmingham / Wuhan University of Technology (Tan, Huang, Jiang, Fang, Liu, Pham)
sources.title: Robotic Removal and Collection of Screws in Collaborative Disassembly of End-of-Life Electric Vehicle Batteries (Biomimetics)
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed study demonstrated a collaborative-robot cell that automatically finds, unfastens and collects screws on end-of-life EV battery packs using 3D vision and force/torque control — a laboratory disassembly cell, semi-automated within a human-robot collaborative workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fastener removal during disassembly of an end-of-life automotive assembly. It substantiates only single-fastener-type unscrewing on one pack geometry in a lab cell with a human collaborator; it does not substantiate removing a damaged body panel, cutting spot welds, or handling mixed clip/harness attachments.

sources.system: AMP Cortex / AMP AI sorting robots
sources.title: Evergreen to install 15 AMP Robotics sorting systems across three locations | Recycling Product News
sources.claim: AMP Robotics' AI-guided sorting robots autonomously identify polymer families (PET, HDPE, LDPE, PP, PS) and pick the items on conveyor lines at recycling facilities, with 15 systems installed or planned across three Evergreen plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine identification of plastic family. It covers packaging resins presented singly on a purpose-built conveyor, not identification of automotive blends (TPO, PP+EPDM, PC/ABS, PUR) and their repair-relevant properties on a part still attached to a vehicle, and it includes no panel-removal capability.

tasks.label: Apply heat to plastic panels, using hot-air welding guns or immersion in hot water, and press the softened panels back into shape by hand.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision shop: a thermoplastic (TPO/PP) bumper cover removed from the vehicle and set on a bumper stand; technician plays a hot-air gun over a low-speed impact dent/crease until the plastic relaxes, then pushes and works it out from behind by hand (often with a wood block or gloved thumb pressure), checking contour by eye and feel, and cools it to set the shape before refinishing.

Collision shop bay: dent/deformation in a bumper cover, rocker cladding or air dam left on the vehicle; technician heats the area in place with a hot-air gun while shielding adjacent paint, lamps and sensors, then presses the softened panel back to its original contour by hand from front and back with limited access behind the panel.

Collision shop: cracked or torn bumper cover / broken mounting tab; technician plastic-welds the crack or reattaches the tab with a hot-air welding gun and rod, then heats the surrounding distorted area and hand-presses it back into alignment so the panel's gaps and mounting points fit the vehicle before filling and refinishing.

Collision shop: small plastic parts and trim — fender liners, mirror caps, spoilers, moldings, grille surrounds, mud flaps — warped, curled or bent; technician heats with a hot-air gun or immerses in hot water, then presses/holds them flat or to shape by hand (sometimes against a bench, jig or the vehicle's own surface) until cooled.

Collision shop: removed bumper cover immersed in or flushed with hot water (dip tank, hot-water bath or steam) to soften the whole panel, then lifted out and worked back to its original contour by hand, often needing two hands and body support on a large floppy part before it cools.

Mobile / on-site smart repair: technician works at a customer driveway, dealership lot or parking garage, heating a scuffed and dented bumper cover with a hot-air gun and pressing it back into shape by hand outdoors, in variable light, temperature and wind, with the vehicle parked as found.

sources.system: Robotized incremental polymer sheet forming (RoboForm), KTU / Sensors 2021 study
sources.developer: Kaunas University of Technology (Institute of Mechatronics)
sources.title: Investigation of Advanced Robotized Polymer Sheet Incremental Forming Process (Sensors)
sources.claim: Robot-guided incremental forming of polymer sheets with localized heating has been demonstrated in a laboratory: a clamped polymer sheet is deformed along a programmed tool path with laser heating. This is forming new small-batch parts from sheet blanks, not restoring a damaged, molded, painted automotive panel to its original contour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heated robotic forming of thermoplastic sheet. It shares the physics (heat plus tool force to change plastic shape) but works on flat clamped blanks to a pre-programmed CAD path; it does not sense unknown collision damage, judge when a molded cover has returned to its original contour, or protect an existing painted finish, so it does not substantiate completion of this repair task.

sources.system: Robotic plastic welding cells (FANUC, Motoman, Bosch Rexroth Cartesian robots)
sources.developer: FANUC Robotics America / Motoman / Bosch Rexroth (reported by A3)
sources.title: Industry Insights: Plastic Welding Robotics | Robotic Industries Association
sources.claim: Industrial robots routinely apply heat and force to thermoplastic automotive parts (hot gas, hot plate, hot staking, extrusion welding) inside fixtured manufacturing cells, but the operation is joining known, identical parts held in fixtures, not reshaping variable damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic heat-and-press operations on automotive thermoplastics (hot staking, hot plate, hot gas welding). Objects are comparable (bumpers, instrument panels), but each cycle is a fixed, pre-taught operation on an undamaged part in a fixture; no cited cell diagnoses a dent and iteratively works a softened panel back to a target contour.

sources.system: Path Robotics Autonomous Fit-up robotic welding cell
sources.title: Robotic cell picks, fits-up, and welds small parts autonomously | The Fabricator
sources.claim: Autonomous, vision-driven robotic joining cells exist for metal fabrication: a cell scans parts and welds them without part-specific programming. This is the closest autonomous 'repair-like' robotic capability found, and it is metal arc welding in a fenced cell, not heat-softening and hand-pressing plastic panels back to shape.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous adaptive robotic joining with 3D scanning. It shows robots can localize unknown workpieces and run an adaptive process, but it neither heats thermoplastic nor applies compliant forming force to restore a panel's contour, so it does not carry over to heat-and-reshape plastic repair.

sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System
sources.title: Robotic Paint Repair | 3M Abrasives
sources.claim: Robotic automation that has actually entered automotive finishing/repair work addresses sanding, polishing and painting of surfaces — not heating and reshaping damaged plastic panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic defect repair on automotive bodies in OEM paint lines. It demonstrates force-controlled robotic surface work on car panels, but only material removal/polishing on a rigid, fixtured body in a paint shop; nothing in it addresses thermal softening or plastic reforming.

tasks.label: Clean work areas, using air hoses, to remove damaged material and discarded fiberglass strips used in repair procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After grinding/sanding a body-filler or fiberglass repair on a vehicle in an open collision-shop bay: blow sanding dust, filler crumbs and grinding debris off the panel, seams and adjacent surfaces with a compressed-air hose and clear the immediate area before the next step. Vehicle sits on the floor or a lift surrounded by carts, cords, hoses and hand tools.

Pre-primer/pre-paint cleanup in the prep station or spray booth: blow out door jambs, wheel openings, panel edges, drip rails and body seams; clear masking scraps and sanding dust from the booth floor and grates so nothing contaminates the finish. Acceptance standard is a visibly dust-free vehicle and booth.

End-of-job bay cleanup: collect and dispose of discarded fiberglass mat/cloth strips, cured filler and resin scraps, used sandpaper, masking paper and tape, and metal cut-offs; blow and sweep debris out from around the lift, frame rack, toolboxes and carts; return the bay to a ready state for the next vehicle.

Cleanup after teardown/repair of a heavily wrecked vehicle: remove broken glass, plastic shards, torn trim, dirt, mud and loosened undercoating from the damaged area of the vehicle and the surrounding floor, using air hose and shop vacuum, often with the car on a frame rack and parts staged nearby.

Mobile/field repair work outside a fixed shop (mobile repair unit at a customer lot, fleet yard, RV/boat fiberglass job, driveway): clean the work area with a portable compressor and air hose and pick up fiberglass strips, resin scraps and dust from an uncontrolled surface, with wind, weather, uneven ground and bystanders present.

sources.system: Duerr EcoBlow-Off / EcoClean / EcoRS Clean F
sources.date: 2023-02 (page); technology in series use since late 1980s
sources.title: Car body cleaning - Dürr
sources.claim: Duerr's EcoBlow-Off automated cleaning system blows dust and dirt out of the inside of vehicle bodies ... painting; the companion EcoClean feather-duster machines have been in worldwide series use since the late 1980s. These run in conveyor-fed, fenced OEM paint-shop stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-paint blow-down of a car body in an OEM paint shop. Same object (a car body), same medium (directed compressed air plus feather rollers), and the same acceptance criterion the body repairer works to - a dust-free surface before refinishing.

sources.system: Duerr EcoRS Clean F cleaning robot
sources.title: Dürr equips first BYD plant in Europe with sustainable painting technology - Dürr
sources.claim: Duerr's robot-based EcoRS Clean F cleaning robot handles varying body shapes in any order on the line and is being installed in BYD's first European car plant, showing these cleaning robots are commercially deployed production equipment rather than demos.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated blow-off/dusting of differently shaped vehicle bodies before paint - the same operation the repairer performs by hand with an air hose on a repaired panel; it shows the machine copes with model-to-model shape variation, not one fixed part.

sources.system: DMG MORI AI chip-flushing (camera-guided nozzles)
sources.title: AI Chip Flushing Keeps the Lights Out - National Tooling & Machining Association
sources.claim: DMG MORI machine tools use camera- and AI-guided swiveling coolant/air nozzles that flush chips and keep the machining work zone clean without an operator, enabling lights-out running - automated clearing of loose waste material from a machine's own work area inside a purpose-built enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing swarf and debris from a machine's work zone with directed jets. The purpose is identical to the repairer's air-hose blow-down - removing loose waste material from a work area - and the perception problem (find residual debris, aim a nozzle at it) is the same, inside a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.system: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker / Fast Picker
sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics (Terex) Heavy Picker and Fast Picker robots autonomously identify and pick bulky, irregular construction and demolition debris and lightweight waste off conveyors in sorting facilities, running continuously in commercial plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking discarded irregular scrap (including composite and board offcuts and strips) out of a presented stream and dropping it into a chute. Comparable objects and grasp precision to removing discarded fiberglass strips and filler scraps, in a purpose-built conveyor cell - the E1 presentation of the cleanup.

sources.system: Tennant X16 SWEEP (BrainOS)
sources.title: Brain Corp: Tennant Company Unveils X16 SWEEP for Autonomous, Around-the-Clock Industrial Sweeping
sources.claim: Tennant's X16 SWEEP, launched April 2026 on Brain Corp's BrainOS, is an autonomous robotic sweeper sold for warehouses, logistics centres and light manufacturing; it sweeps open industrial floor areas and navigates around obstacles, but is a ride-on-class floor machine with no manipulator or air hose.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous removal of floor debris in a structured facility. Cited to bound the E2 judgment - it clears open floor lanes only, and cannot blow dust off panels or clear scrap from a congested repair bay around a lifted vehicle.

sources.system: Tesla robotaxi interior cleaning robot
sources.title: Tesla readies its autonomous Cybercab and Robotaxi cleaning service
sources.claim: Tesla has installed a fixed robotic cleaning arm with interchangeable attachments at its Austin robotaxi hub that vacuums crumbs and debris from vehicle interiors and wipes surfaces between rides at a dedicated station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing loose debris from inside a vehicle presented at a fixed servicing station - comparable to clearing glass fragments, dirt and torn material out of a damaged vehicle, with the vehicle brought to the machine as an E1 setting would present it.

tasks.label: Soak fiberglass matting in resin mixtures and apply layers of matting over repair areas to specified thicknesses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision-repair stall in a general body shop: cracked or holed fiberglass/SMC panel still mounted on the customer's vehicle (e.g., Corvette quarter, cab fairing, bedside). Tech grinds and feathers the damage, cuts chopped-strand mat, mixes catalyzed polyester/epoxy resin, wets out the mat and lays 2-3 layers over the backside/face of a curved, often vertical or overhead area, rolling out air to a specified thickness.

Same shop, part removed and laid on a bench or stand: hood, deck lid, spoiler, ground effects, fender flare or scoop. Tech backs up a crack or rebuilds a broken edge with resin-soaked mat layers built to spec thickness, using a mold or tape dam for contour, then lets it cure before grinding.

Heavy-truck, bus or RV body shop: large fiberglass front cap, roof cap, aero fairing or sidewall repaired in place on the vehicle, working from a ladder or lift over a large, gently curved area; several mat layers laid up wet over a scarfed area, thickness matched to the original laminate.

Restoration/specialty or race-body shop: structural fiberglass work on a classic Corvette, kit car or fiberglass race body — bonding panel sections, laminating overlaps and building the laminate to a specified ply count/thickness with matched contours, on the vehicle or on a jig.

Mobile/field repair at a fleet yard, dealership lot or customer site: portable resin kit and mat used outdoors or in a driveway to patch a fiberglass panel on a truck, trailer or RV, with variable access, wind, temperature and no fixed workstation.

sources.system: SAMBA Series Fiber Patch Placement cells
sources.title: Cevotec upgrades SAMBA Fiber Patch Placement cells for production of large aerostructures | CompositesWorld
sources.claim: Cevotec's SAMBA Fiber Patch Placement cells are commercially sold, fully automated robotic layup systems that place fiber patches (dry fiber or prepreg) layer by layer onto complex 3D tools with integrated process control, building laminates/preforms to a defined thickness inside fenced robot cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic multi-layer composite layup on contoured tooling. It places resin-impregnated (prepreg) or binder-tacked fiber layers onto curved surfaces to a specified stack thickness with process control — the same physical operation and materials class as laying resin-soaked glass mat to a specified thickness, at tighter precision than body-shop laminating requires; the demonstrated setting is a purpose-built robot cell, which is what the E1 counterfactual supplies (panel fixtured like a mold).

sources.system: Matrasur Robomat gantry robot with modified MVP High Volume PROGUN chopper gun (Ibazur pool plant)
sources.developer: Matrasur Composites / Magnum Venus Products (user: Ibazur)
sources.title: Automating swimming pool production | CompositesWorld
sources.claim: In a production FRP plant, a gantry-mounted Matrasur Robomat robot fitted with an MVP chopper gun sprays successive layers of chopped glass and catalyzed resin onto contoured molds to build laminate thickness; consolidation rollout between layers is still done by hand by technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray-up lamination. It deposits exactly the materials of this task (chopped glass reinforcement plus catalyzed resin) in successive layers to a controlled thickness on large curved surfaces inside a purpose-built cell; the caveat is that hand rollout is still used for consolidation between layers, so this item supports deposition-to-thickness rather than the full consolidated laminate on its own.

sources.system: Automated Ply Placement (APP) / Automated Laminating cell
sources.title: Aerospace - Airborne
sources.claim: Airborne sells robotised automated laminating and Automated Ply Placement systems that cut plies and pick and place them robotically to build tailored laminates; such cells have been contracted by Airbus (Getafe) and GKN Aerospace for production use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cutting and placement of composite plies into a stacked laminate. Cutting reinforcement to shape and stacking plies to a specified thickness is the core of the body-repair layup; the system operates in a fenced production cell (E1) with the workpiece fixtured, matching the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: ROMAIN Robotic Patch Applicator (RPA) on Aerones deployment platform
sources.title: Automating Wind Turbine Blade Repair with Robotic Patch Applicator (RPA) (CompositesWorld/ROMAIN)
sources.claim: In the EU ROMAIN project, a Tecnalia robotic patch applicator carried by an Aerones platform applied premanufactured glass-prepreg repair patches (also validated with liquid-resin wet patches) over prepared damage on operating wind turbine blades, conforming to curvature, vacuum-consolidating and curing; however, the patch plies themselves were cut, laminated and debulked by hand on the ground and the platform is deployed and vision-assisted by an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a multi-ply glass-fiber/resin patch over a prepared composite repair area on a real damaged structure. It is the closest field analogue to this task, but the lamination step remained manual and platform positioning is operator-mediated, so it is recorded as unclear autonomy and used only as context for why no in-situ (E2/E3) positive judgment is made.

sources.system: Automated planning and execution system for robotic prepreg layup
sources.developer: academic research team (Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing paper)
sources.title: Automated planning for robotic layup of composite prepreg
sources.claim: A published robotic layup system autonomously generates grasp, manipulation and robot trajectory plans for prepreg plies and executes multi-ply layup on an industry-inspired mold in a laboratory robot cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous planning and execution of composite ply layup, i.e. draping limp resin-impregnated fabric onto a contoured surface without hand guidance — the manipulation problem at the heart of applying resin-soaked matting — demonstrated in a fixtured robot cell (E1).

tasks.label: Read specifications or confer with customers to determine the desired custom modifications for altering the appearance of vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Cut openings in vehicle bodies for the installation of customized windows, using templates and power shears or chisels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Van-conversion / upfitter shop: technician marks a side or rear window opening on a cargo van (Transit, ProMaster, Sprinter) using a supplied template, drills a start hole, cuts the 18-20 ga steel skin with a pneumatic nibbler or electric shears while working around inner reinforcement ribs, then deburrs and primes the raw edge. Vehicle sits in a shop bay, already fully assembled and painted.

Aftermarket sunroof/moonroof installer: headliner and roof trim removed, template taped to the painted steel roof of a customer's assembled car or SUV, opening cut with air saw/shears, roof bows and reinforcements trimmed and re-braced, edges sealed. Single-vehicle job in a specialty installer's bay, zero tolerance for cutting the wrong structure.

Specialty/commercial vehicle work at a fabricator or upfitter: cutting window openings in a shuttle bus, ambulance/box body, RV or trailer sidewall, or armored/limousine conversion. Panels may be aluminum sheet, laminated composite sidewall, or fiberglass; openings are large and often cut before or during body build-up.

One-off custom or restoration job: chopped-top hot rod, custom van, or panel-truck quarter window where the opening shape is hand-drawn or made from a shop-built template, cut with chisel, air saw or shears in a fabricated/modified panel with no CAD data, then hand-fitted, flanged and welded to accept a custom-made window.

Mobile / on-site work: cutting a window or vent opening into a fleet van, service body or trailer at a customer's yard, driveway or lot, using a template and cordless shears, with uncontrolled lighting, weather and surroundings and no shop fixtures.

sources.system: Precitec SolidCutter (robot-mounted 3D laser cutting head)
sources.title: 3D robotic cutting with laser | Flexible & precise | Precitec
sources.claim: Commercial robot-guided 3D laser cutting heads are used in series automotive production to cut openings in car body components, including openings for roof rails and ... and contours in vehicle doors.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical operation as the rated task - cutting a shaped opening through vehicle body sheet metal to accept a fitted component - on the same class of workpiece (car/truck body panels) at equal or better precision, but in a fixtured production cell rather than a repair bay.

sources.system: Precitec FormCutter Plus (robot-arm mounted X/Y/Z cutting head)
sources.title: Highly productive 3D laser cutting | PRECITEC
sources.claim: Robot-mounted 3D laser cutting tooling is routinely used to cut antenna and roof-railing holes in vehicle bodies and design-specific holes and recesses in truck production.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting holes in an already-formed vehicle roof/body is the same operation as cutting a roof or body opening for a customized window; the robot positions the tool over the body and cuts the programmed contour, the function the human template and power shears serve.

sources.system: Staubli RX160L laser-cutting robots at Zhengzhou Yutong Bus
sources.title: Laser cutting sheet metal | Staubli United States
sources.claim: Six-axis laser-cutting robots have been in daily bus-body production since 2011, cutting doors, bumpers and other metal ..., from small circular cutouts to complex 3D free-form contours, at a plant producing over 340 buses per day.
sources.transferJustification: Bus door and body sheet-metal cutouts are the same material, thickness class and geometry as window openings cut by body repairers; the robot produces the finished contour to production quality with no human guiding the tool.

sources.system: Shape Process Automation 6-axis robotic waterjet cutting cells
sources.title: Robotic Waterjet Cutting | Shape Process Automation
sources.claim: Turnkey six-axis robotic waterjet cutting cells, supplied complete with product fixturing and ..., are sold and installed for cutting automotive parts.
sources.transferJustification: Provides the fixtured, purpose-built cell in which a vehicle panel is presented to a cutting robot; cutting large shaped openings in composite and metal vehicle panels is the same operation as cutting a window opening.

sources.system: KMT / Shape Process Automation robotic waterjet systems
sources.developer: KMT Waterjet with Shape Process Automation
sources.title: Automotive Industry: Use of Waterjet Cutting Systems
sources.claim: Robotic waterjet cells are used in the automotive industry to cut composites, steel, titanium, headliners and door panels, using six-axis robotic cells.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes machine cutting of the composite/fiberglass and metal panel materials found in RV, bus and specialty vehicle bodies - the materials the repairer cuts with shears or chisels when fitting custom windows.

sources.system: Blue Advanced Machinery CNC routers for RV/trailer manufacturing
sources.title: RV & Trailer Manufacturing | Blue Advanced Machinery
sources.claim: CNC routing machines are sold to RV and trailer manufacturers specifically to replace hand cutting, including cutting precise openings in aluminum ... and laminated walls.
sources.transferJustification: RV/trailer window and door openings in aluminum-skinned and laminated sidewalls are the same openings the repairer cuts by template and power shears; the CNC machine produces the finished opening from a program under machine control.

sources.system: Staubli robotic laser cutting (6-axis robots with trajectory generation)
sources.title: Robotic laser cutting | High Dynamic Precision with Staubli robot
sources.claim: Laser-cutting robot controllers provide trajectory generation for free-form and circular contours with optimized entry/exit strategies, so arbitrary one-off contours can be cut without a physical template.
sources.transferJustification: Custom one-off window contours are free-form paths; this shows the cell can execute an arbitrary programmed contour, the machine equivalent of a shop-made template.

tasks.label: Measure and mark vinyl material and cut material to size for roof installation, using rules, straightedges, and hand shears.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Body/trim shop bench work for a common late-model or classic vehicle with a known top pattern: pull bulk vinyl top material off a roll onto the bench, measure with rule and straightedge, mark panel dimensions plus seam/wrap allowance, and cut the main roof panel to size with hand shears.

Cutting from a template: the worker lays a manufacturer paper pattern, the old vinyl top, or a shop-made template on the new material, traces the outline (main panel, sail/quarter panels, listing pockets), and cuts the contoured pieces with shears.

Fitting on the car: material is draped over the roof of a vehicle in the stall, positioned to drip rails, A-pillars, backlight and door openings, trim lines marked in chalk/pencil against a straightedge, then pulled off and trimmed to size with hand shears (vehicle is a standard production model).

Small ancillary pieces cut from remnants or narrow stock: welting/beading strips, padding, filler and sail-panel inserts, or a patch piece for a partial vinyl-roof repair; measured, marked and sheared to size at the bench.

Custom/one-off job: chopped or modified roofline, street rod, restoration or unusual vehicle for which no pattern exists; the worker measures the actual roof, develops a paper pattern by hand, then marks and cuts the vinyl to fit.

sources.system: Zünd digital cutting system (S3/D3/L3 with camera registration)
sources.title: Zünd Cutter - GSD FabLab (Harvard)
sources.claim: Zünd digital flatbed cutters are a modular cutting and marking system that works with leather, fabric, foam and plastics, using a carriage camera to detect material edges and registration features so cuts align to the media — i.e., machine measuring, marking and cutting of flexible sheet stock.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: measuring/marking flexible sheet goods (vinyl, leather, fabric) and cutting them to size from patterns; the cutter substitutes for rule, straightedge and shears.

sources.system: Zünd S3 and D3 cutters with Mind software

sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting vehicle upholstery materials to size from vehicle-specific patterns. Same materials (coated fabric/leather/vinyl), same tolerances, and the same measure-mark-cut output the trim worker produces.

sources.system: Zünd roll-off / RollMaster material handling
sources.title: Roll-handling from Zünd - for your rolled material
sources.claim: Zünd roll-handling units feed rolled material such as vinyl to the cutter automatically, supplying material and rolling up finished work without operator intervention.

sources.system: Eastman automated cutting systems

sources.claim: Eastman machines cut vinyl, canvas and upholstery stock in simple and intricate patterns, including stacked plies.

sources.claim: Lectra's Versalis automated leather cutting system scans and digitizes each hide and CNC-cuts nested automotive interior parts; it is marketed and deployed for automotive seating and interiors.

tasks.label: Select appropriate tools, safety equipment, and parts, according to job requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile job at a customer's driveway, street or workplace parking lot: after confirming the vehicle/VIN and glass options (rain sensor, HUD, acoustic, heated wiper park, camera bracket), the tech pulls the correct windshield off the van's exterior rack, picks urethane and primer suited to the temperature/SDAT, chooses the cut-out method and tools (wire-out kit vs. cold knife vs. power tool), setting tools/suction cups, and PPE (cut-resistant gloves, safety glasses), and stages them at the vehicle.

In-shop windshield replacement at an auto glass shop bay: from the work order the tech walks the shop racks, locates and carries the correct laminated windshield, pulls matching moldings, clips, cowl fasteners, urethane cartridges/sausages, primer and glass prep, selects removal and setting tools from the bench/cart, and PPE, then stages everything at the bay.

Chip or crack repair job (usually mobile, sometimes in shop): tech assesses the break type and selects resin viscosity, injector/bridge, probes, drill bit, curing tabs, UV lamp, razor and polish from the repair kit, plus safety glasses and gloves, and sets them up at the damage.

Side, quarter or back glass and specialty jobs (door glass with regulator clips, tempered back glass with defroster tabs, RV/heavy-equipment or commercial vehicle glass): selecting the correct tempered/laminated part, setting blocks, butyl vs urethane, vacuum for cleanup of tempered fragments, trim/door-panel tools, and PPE.

Branch stockroom/warehouse pull at the start of a route or shift: matching part numbers on the day's work orders to inventory, pulling glass from A-frame racks, staging consumables (adhesive, primers, moldings, clips) into job kits, and loading the van, including checking stock and flagging substitutions.

tasks.label: Prime all scratches on pinchwelds with primer and allow to dry.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile passenger-car windshield replacement at a customer's home driveway, street or office parking lot. After cutting out the old glass and trimming the urethane, the tech inspects the pinchweld flange, finds a handful of hairline cut-through scratches in the paint, dabs black pinchweld primer on each with a dauber while leaning over the cowl, and waits the flash time. Temperature, wind, dust and lighting are whatever the site offers; vehicle model and flange geometry vary job to job.

In-shop passenger-car windshield replacement in an auto-glass shop bay. Vehicle driven into a fixed bay with controlled lighting and temperature; after cut-out the tech primes each scratch on the pinchweld with the urethane maker's specified primer and observes the specified dry/flash time before applying the bead.

Bonded back glass or quarter glass replacement in the shop: narrower, deeper flange, interior trim and headliner edge removed, defroster tabs and encapsulation nearby; scratches from the cold knife or wire are primed in a confined channel with limited hand access, then allowed to dry.

Heavy truck, bus, RV or fleet vehicle serviced at a fleet yard, dealership lot or roadside: large flange perimeter often reached from a ladder or stand, older painted or galvanized steel with more cut-through, primer applied at many scratch spots and allowed to flash before the glass is set.

Older or previously replaced vehicle whose pinchweld shows extensive cut-through, prior over-cutting or spot corrosion after removal; the tech must judge which areas are bare metal, prime every scratch (sometimes a second coat) and respect the full dry time before bonding.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-shop windshield (frontlite) replacement: after cutting out the broken glass in the shop bay, the tech vacuums glass chips and debris from the pinchweld, cowl and dash, trims the old urethane, wipes the flange and the new glass frit with cleaner/activator, applies black primer along the glass edge and to any exposed metal scratches, and waits the specified flash-off time before urethane.

Mobile windshield replacement at a customer's driveway, office parking lot or roadside: same prep sequence (debris removal from the aperture, cleaning the frit band, priming the glass edge and any bare metal, flash-off) performed on the vehicle where it sits, under ambient temperature, humidity, wind and dust, with the glass staged on a portable stand.

Side/door tempered glass replacement after a break-in or impact, usually mobile: vacuum thousands of tempered glass fragments out of the door cavity, window channel, seat rails, carpet and defroster vents, wipe dirt from the run channel and belt molding, and clean/prime bonded quarter glass edges where applicable.

Rock-chip or short-crack repair on the installed windshield (mobile or in shop): probe and clean loose glass and dirt out of the impact pit and crack legs with a carbide bur/pick, dry residual moisture, and prep the pit surface before resin injection and cure.

In-shop bonded back glass or heavy-truck/RV/commercial-vehicle windshield prep: clear old adhesive residue and loose glass from a large aperture, clean the encapsulated glass edge or gasket channel, apply primer along the glass perimeter, and allow it to dry.

tasks.label: Check for and remove moisture or contamination in damaged areas and keep areas dry until repairs are complete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-shop rock-chip/short-crack repair: at a glass shop bay, tech inspects the break with light and probe, judges whether moisture or dirt is trapped inside the impact point, drills/cleans loose glass, runs a moisture evaporator or heat plus vacuum cycles to drive water out of the legs of the break, then keeps the area dry and masked until resin is injected and UV-cured.

Mobile chip repair at a customer's driveway, street, or office parking lot: damp or cold glass, dew or recent rain; tech must confirm the break is dry, warm and dry the glass locally, shield the spot from wind, rain and sun with a cover or canopy, and keep it dry through injection and cure.

In-shop windshield/backglass replacement prep: after the old glass is cut out, the tech checks the pinchweld and glass channel for water, dirt, glass shards and old sealant residue, vacuums and wipes the bonding surface with cleaner/activator, blows or wipes it dry, spot-primes any bare or scratched paint, and keeps the opening dry and uncontaminated until the urethane bead is laid.

Mobile replacement prep at a customer site: same pinchweld cleaning and drying done in a driveway or lot with wind-blown dust, possible drizzle or damp cowl area; tech must dry the channel, protect the opening and cured-out bead area from moisture until the glass is set and the urethane reaches safe drive-away.

Water-leak / corrosion jobs: vehicle comes in with a leaking or previously botched installation; tech locates the water path, removes trim and dries a soaked channel, headliner edge or cowl, cleans out contamination and treats surface rust on the flange, and keeps the area dry until re-bonding.

tasks.label: Apply a bead of urethane around the perimeter of each pinchweld and dress the remaining urethane on the pinchwelds so that it is of uniform level and thickness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-shop windshield replacement on a common passenger car/SUV in an auto-glass shop bay: after the old glass is cut out, the tech dresses the residual urethane on the pinchweld down to a uniform thin layer (~1-2 mm) with a cold knife/utility blade, cleans and primes, then lays a continuous V-notch urethane bead of consistent height and width around the whole aperture with a pneumatic/electric cartridge gun.

Mobile service at a customer's driveway, apartment lot, or workplace parking area: same dress-and-bead sequence performed on the vehicle where it sits, outdoors, with ambient temperature/humidity affecting urethane flow and cure, uneven ground, wind and dust, no fixturing of the vehicle.

Shop replacement of back glass, quarter glass, or vent glass set in urethane: smaller, tighter-radius apertures, encapsulated glass and defroster tabs, residual urethane dressed on narrow flanges, bead applied around a short perimeter with limited access.

Heavy truck, bus, RV, or off-road equipment glass at a fleet shop or in the yard: large flat or two-piece windshields, wide pinchwelds, thicker/high-viscosity urethane beads run from bulk guns, sometimes two beads or a taller bead height.

Shop job on a vehicle with pinchweld corrosion, scratched e-coat, or a previous poor install (over-thick or contaminated old urethane): tech must judge how much old urethane to remove, dress it level without cutting to bare metal, treat/prime exposed metal, then apply the bead.

Dealership or fleet facility bay doing repeated same-model replacements (e.g., rental/fleet windshields): consistent vehicle geometry, indoor controlled bay, standard urethane and equipment, high throughput.

tasks.label: Obtain windshields or windows for specific automobile makes and models from stock and examine them for defects prior to installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-shop technician pulls the windshield for a specific make/model from the shop's A-frame racks/stockroom, matches part number and features (rain sensor, HUD, acoustic, ADAS bracket) to the work order, carries or carts it to the bay, and inspects surface, edges, frit and moldings for chips, scratches, distortion and shipping damage before install.

Mobile technician loading the day's route at a branch warehouse or distribution counter: locates several windshields and door glasses on warehouse racks by part number, verifies each against the dispatch list, inspects for cracks, edge chips and scratches, and loads them into the van's exterior glass rack.

Mobile technician at a customer driveway, street, or workplace parking lot takes the glass off the van rack, unwraps it, and inspects it in ambient outdoor light and weather before setting it on stands; rejects damaged glass and calls the branch for a replacement.

Retrieving small tempered side/door glass or a back glass, usually boxed, bagged or bin-stored on shelving, verifying part number, tint, and features (defroster grid, encapsulation, mounting buttons), and inspecting edges, encapsulation and attached hardware for chips or breakage.

Receiving a special-order or OEM windshield delivered on a supplier rack or crate at the shop: unwrapping, verifying the part matches VIN-specific options, inspecting for freight damage, then racking it or staging it for the scheduled job.

tasks.label: Install, repair, or replace safety glass and related materials, such as back glass heating elements, on vehicles or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile windshield replacement at a customer's home driveway, street, or workplace parking lot: tech removes wipers/cowl/moldings and interior trim, cuts the old urethane bead out with wire or cold knife, lifts out the broken laminated glass, trims and primes the pinchweld, transfers mirror bracket/rain sensor, lays a fresh urethane bead, sets and centers the new windshield, reinstalls trim, and checks for leaks - in whatever weather and space the site offers.

In-shop bonded windshield replacement in a glass shop or collision-shop bay on a late-model ADAS-equipped car: same removal/prep/set sequence indoors on a flat floor or lift, plus transferring camera brackets, gel pads and heated wiper-park elements, then static/dynamic recalibration of the forward camera and a safe-drive-away check.

Side/door tempered glass replacement (door or quarter glass shattered): remove door panel and vapor barrier, vacuum shards from the door cavity and interior, unbolt and align the new glass in the regulator sash, cycle and adjust the window in its run channels, reassemble trim without rattles or broken clips.

Back glass work: replace a bonded or gasket-set backlite and reconnect/solder defroster grid tabs and embedded antenna leads, or repair a damaged heating-element grid line or tab with conductive paint/epoxy and verify continuity and defrost function; usually in a shop bay, sometimes mobile.

Windshield chip or short-crack repair: clean and drill/probe the impact point, mount an injector bridge, vacuum and pressure-cycle resin into the break, UV-cure, scrape and polish the pit - done in minutes at a customer's parking spot or in a shop bay, with judgment about whether the damage is repairable.

Setting new glass into a bare, previously stripped opening: collision vehicles delivered with the glass already out and the pinchweld freshly painted, restoration bodies, and newly built or re-glazed truck/bus/equipment cabs at a fleet shop or upfitter - prime, bead, set and secure the glass with no old adhesive to cut out.

tasks.label: Install replacement glass in vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile service: technician drives to a customer's driveway, apartment lot or office parking space and sets a urethane-bonded replacement windshield into a passenger car or light truck — dry-fits/sets stops, applies primer and urethane bead to the glass, lifts and sets the glass into the pinchweld to OEM gap/height, installs cowl and moldings; done outdoors in variable weather with the vehicle parked wherever the customer left it.

In-shop windshield replacement in an auto glass shop or dealership service bay: vehicle driven onto a flat bay floor, urethane-bonded windshield (usually with rain sensor / ADAS camera bracket and encapsulated moldings) set into the aperture, glass held with setting blocks/tape until cure, followed by ADAS calibration on a target rack.

Bonded back glass (backlite) or fixed bonded quarter/vent glass replacement, usually in the shop: urethane set into the aperture, defroster grid tabs and antenna leads reconnected, trim and third brake light or wiper reinstalled.

Tempered door (side) glass replacement in shop or mobile: door trim panel and vapor barrier off, new drop-in glass fed down into the door shell, seated in run channels and bolted/clamped to the window regulator, glass squared and up-travel adjusted, door reassembled.

Heavy/commercial glass at a fleet yard, terminal or equipment site: truck cab, bus, RV or off-road equipment glass — large panels, often rubber gasket/locking-strip 'rope-in' sets or bolted frames, awkward access from ladders or the ground, one or two technicians.

sources.system: Bluewrist EzRG windshield insertion system (Gocator 2300 3D sensors, six-axis robot)
sources.date: 2022-09-29 (case study page); system in production use since ~2018
sources.title: 3D Vision Guided Robotic Windshield Installation — Bluewrist case study
sources.claim: Bluewrist's EzRG 3D-vision-guided robotic windshield insertion system, used on automotive assembly lines, has a six-axis robot pick the glass with suction cups, measure the actual body aperture with on-arm 3D sensors, and insert the glass at up to 0.2 mm guidance accuracy — the same set-the-glass-into-the-aperture operation as replacement glass installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: OEM final-assembly glazing. The object (a full-size windshield), the receiving feature (the vehicle body pinchweld aperture) and the required precision (sub-millimetre gap/flush setting) are the same as when an installer sets replacement glass; the difference is that the vehicle arrives fixtured on a conveyor rather than parked.

sources.system: Bluewrist EzRG + Gocator 2300 sensors on six-axis robot (photos courtesy Wuhan TopEagle)
sources.title: Sensors Make Robots Smarter When Inserting Vehicle Windshields — ASSEMBLY Magazine
sources.claim: Trade-press account of the same deployed system: robots insert both front and rear windshields into car bodies on the assembly line, with vision compensating for body-position variation, at ±0.2 mm accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic insertion of front and rear windshields on a vehicle assembly line. It covers backlites as well as windshields, matching the bonded back-glass instance; objects, adhesive process and positional tolerances match aftermarket glass setting.

It shows robots handling large glass gently, priming bond areas and coping with part-to-part glass variation and many part numbers, which are the prep steps preceding setting the glass.
