sources.system: Automated end-of-line (EOL) test cells
sources.title: End-of-Line Testing, Ensuring Quality in Manufacturing
sources.claim: Automated end-of-line test cells execute complete test sequences on production vehicles/units around the clock with minimal ... and produce the accept/reject verdict automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line functional verification of vehicles. Same purpose as the mechanic's 'ensure it is working properly' drive — run the vehicle through a defined operating regime and issue a pass/fail — performed by machine in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: HBK (Brüel & Kjær / Discom) Acoustic End-of-Line Test Systems
sources.title: NVH End-of-Line (EoL) Testing | HBK
sources.claim: Production acoustic/NVH end-of-line systems automatically detect mechanical defects in drivetrain assemblies from noise and vibration signatures, including defects hidden inside closed transmission modules.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine 'listening' for mechanical faults. It substitutes for the technician listening and feeling for noise/vibration during a test drive, on comparable drivetrain hardware, but only inside an instrumented test cell with reference signatures.

sources.system: Ford robotic test driving program (vehicle automation kit by Autonomous Solutions Inc.)
sources.developer: Ford Motor Company / Autonomous Solutions Inc. (ASI)
sources.title: Ford Using Robots to Improve "Built Ford Tough" Durability Testing of its Trucks
sources.claim: A robotic driving module installed in a production truck drives it unattended over punishing durability courses at Ford's Michigan Proving Grounds, controlling steering, throttle and brakes along a preprogrammed course with remote monitoring and onboard obstacle stopping; the same robotic driver program was used in 2025-2026 for Ranger Super Duty endurance testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-driven durability testing of trucks at a proving ground. It shows the driving half of a test drive can be done by machine in a controlled facility on an ordinary truck, but the failure findings are produced by engineers inspecting the vehicle and data afterwards, not by the robot.

sources.system: ASI Vehicle Automation Kit with Mobius command and control
sources.date: 2017-2018 (ongoing commercial service to Ford, Toyota and others)
sources.title: Autonomous Technology Improves Safety at Proving Grounds – ASI Robots
sources.claim: ASI's vehicle automation kit is OEM-agnostic hardware installed into a test vehicle to control steering, acceleration, braking ..., letting proving-ground vehicles run test paths without a driver on board.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrofitting a robotic driver into an arbitrary vehicle for track testing. It covers the driving actuation of a mechanic's test drive on any vehicle, but supplies no diagnostic judgment of noise, feel or driveability.

sources.system: Aurora Driver (SAE Level 4) on Class 8 trucks
sources.title: Aurora Expands Driverless Trucking Service from Fort Worth to El Paso
sources.claim: Aurora operates fully driverless Class 8 trucks in commercial freight service on Texas public highways, surpassing 100,000 driverless miles by October 2025 and expanding to multiple long-haul routes; the Aurora Driver's Fault Management System monitors vehicle health and pulls the truck over when a fault such as a tire blowout occurs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless highway operation of heavy trucks. It shows a machine can drive a truck on public roads and detect gross vehicle faults, but only on its own purpose-built AV trucks, and it does not evaluate repair quality or characterize driveability complaints.

sources.system: Taylor water-brake chassis dynamometer (shop dyno diagnostics service)
sources.title: Dyno (Dynamometer) - Overdrive Heavy Duty
sources.claim: Heavy-duty repair shops use a chassis dynamometer to diagnose trucks while running under load — cooling, drivetrain, fuel economy and component failures — establishing that a dynamometer cell is a valid substitute environment for a diagnostic road test.
sources.transferJustification: Context only (human-operated): establishes that heavy-truck diagnosis and load verification are routinely performed with the truck fixtured on a dynamometer instead of on the road, which is the E1 counterfactual form of this task.

sources.system: Driving pedal robot for indoor chassis dynamometer testing
sources.title: Development of a Driving Pedal Robot for Indoor Chassis Dynamometer Testing
sources.claim: A driving pedal robot developed for indoor chassis dynamometer testing actuates accelerator and brake pedals like a human, is quickly installable in a vehicle, and runs long test programs in place of a human driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pedal operation of an ordinary vehicle on a dynamometer. Shows the robot driver can be fitted to a vehicle brought into the cell rather than requiring a purpose-built AV, which is what the E1 counterfactual of this task needs.

tasks.label: Diagnose and repair vehicle heating and cooling systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Class 8 truck in a fleet or dealer shop with an overheating/coolant-loss complaint: read fault codes and coolant temp data, pressure-test the system, check coolant chemistry, inspect radiator, fan clutch, belts, hoses and water pump for leaks, then replace the failed part (thermostat, water pump, fan clutch, hose), refill, bleed air and road/dyno verify.

Cab air-conditioning diagnosis and repair on a truck or bus: gauge-set performance test, electrical/control checks, UV dye or electronic leak detection, recover refrigerant, replace compressor, condenser, receiver-drier, expansion valve or hose assembly, pull vacuum, recharge with oil and refrigerant, verify vent temperature.

Heavy remove-and-replace work on cooling components of an in-service vehicle: radiator, charge-air cooler, EGR cooler, or heater core. Drain coolant, remove shrouds, brackets, charge pipes and corroded/seized fasteners in a tight engine bay or behind the dash, install and re-torque, refill and leak-check.

Transit bus or motorcoach HVAC service in a transit garage: rooftop or rear-mounted unit accessed from an elevated platform or pit — replace blower motors, belts, filters, evaporator/condenser coils, find and repair refrigerant leaks, check heater valves and hoses, then verify saloon temperature control.

Mobile/roadside repair: a truck disabled by a coolant leak on a highway shoulder, customer yard, or job site. Technician diagnoses the leak (hose, clamp, radiator, water pump seal) at the vehicle with hand tools and portable equipment, makes the repair or a temporary fix, refills coolant, and returns the unit to service.

sources.system: Figure 02 humanoid robot
sources.title: Successful test of humanoid robots at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid deployment in an automotive setting to date is Figure 02 at BMW Spartanburg, which autonomously picked and inserted sheet metal parts into fixtures in the body shop of a new-vehicle assembly plant. This is repetitive, fixtured handling of new parts on an assembly line, not fault diagnosis or disassembly/repair of an in-service vehicle's cooling or HVAC system.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the frontier of robotic manipulation in vehicle work. It does NOT transfer to this task: the objects are new, fixtured sheet-metal blanks presented identically each cycle, whereas cooling-system repair requires open-ended fault isolation, tool use on corroded fasteners, and fluid handling on used vehicles of many configurations.

sources.system: SmartBay automated tire-changing system
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most automated vehicle-service bay currently offered (tire changing, a far simpler and more repetitive service task than cooling-system diagnosis) is still only semi-automated and requires a human operator for several steps; the earlier fully-robotic attempt, RoboTire, went bankrupt. No comparable machine exists for engine cooling or HVAC repair.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest-neighbour evidence from automated vehicle service (tire replacement in a service bay). It shows the state of the art in a shop environment still needs an operator for the manipulation steps, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of the far more variable diagnose-and-repair work on cooling/HVAC systems.

sources.system: Tele-robotic EV battery disassembly platform (Franka cobots / Phantom Omni haptic)
sources.developer: University of Birmingham / Faraday Institution ReLiB researchers
sources.title: Towards reuse and recycling of lithium-ion batteries: tele-robotics for disassembly of electric vehicle batteries
sources.claim: Robotic unbolting and disassembly of used automotive assemblies — the closest analogue to removing a failed water pump, radiator or A/C compressor from a service vehicle — remains a teleoperated research exercise on a single fixtured vehicle module, not an autonomous capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of used vehicle hardware (unbolting, cutting). It bounds the state of the art — even with the workpiece fixtured in a lab cell, these operations were teleoperated or human-assisted, so autonomous removal/replacement of cooling-system components is not substantiated at any tier.

tasks.label: Inspect, repair, and maintain automotive and mechanical equipment and machinery, such as pumps and compressors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fleet/dealer shop bay: replace or repair an engine-driven auxiliary component on a bus or truck — air compressor, water pump, power-steering pump, fuel/injection pump, A/C compressor. Tilt cab or open hood, drain fluids, remove belts, hoses and lines, unbolt in tight cluttered space, install and torque new unit, refill, run and leak-check.

Scheduled PM inspection of a vehicle's auxiliary mechanical systems in the shop: check air compressor build-up/governor cut-in-cut-out, air dryer, belts and pulleys, water and fuel pumps, A/C compressor, hydraulic pump; crawl under and over the unit, soap-test air leaks, feel belt tension, make minor adjustments, and document findings on the inspection form.

Bench overhaul of a removed pump or compressor in the shop: disassemble a dirty, corroded core, clean parts, measure bores/clearances for wear, decide reuse vs. replace, fit new seals, bearings and gaskets, reassemble to torque spec, and verify on a test stand.

Mobile/field service: diagnose and repair a failed pump, compressor or hydraulic component on a truck or piece of mobile equipment at a customer yard, jobsite or roadside — uneven ground, weather, limited tooling and no lift.

Service and repair of stationary shop and facility equipment: shop air compressor (oil and filter change, belt/coupling replacement, tank drain, leak repair), parts-washer and fuel-island pumps, lifts, pressure washers, standby generators.

Routine condition-monitoring round of the shop's/plant's stationary machinery: walk the facility, read gauges and sight glasses, check for hot bearings and overheating motors, listen for compressed-air and pump leaks, log readings and flag anomalies for follow-up work orders.

sources.system: ANYmal (ANYbotics)
sources.title: Automation and digitalization with ANYmal the case at BASF - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal, an autonomous legged inspection robot, performs routine inspection rounds in a BASF chemical production plant, reading gauges and taking acoustic and thermal measurements of pumps and compressors.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the inspection/condition-monitoring portion of 'inspect ... pumps and compressors' on stationary machinery in an institution-controlled facility.

sources.system: ANYmal (ANYbotics)
sources.title: TDK Ventures Invests in ANYbotics, a World Leader in Industrial Inspection Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: Roughly 200 ANYmal inspection robots are commercially deployed in industrial facilities of customers including BP, Equinor and Novelis, performing thousands of inspections weekly.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that autonomous inspection rounds of plant machinery (pumps, compressors, motors) are a fielded commercial capability, not a demo.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced automated vehicle service-bay system found, Automated Tire's SmartBay, is semi-automated: it changes tires with the wheels left on the vehicle specifically to avoid lug-nut work, and a human operator must handle the tire and the air line.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest fielded robotic work in a vehicle service bay (a related task: wheel/tire service). It shows fastener-level, under-hood component R&R on vehicles is not automated; used as context for negative judgments.

sources.system: DeMoBat disassembly demonstrators (KUKA robots)
sources.title: "DeMoBat" - Industrial disassembly of battery modules and electric motors - Fraunhofer IPA
sources.claim: Automated disassembly of used automotive assemblies (unscrewing, cutting, separating) remains at the demonstrator/research stage in purpose-built robot cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown of used, fastened automotive assemblies — the disassembly half of a bench overhaul. Its research-demonstrator status shows the E1 counterfactual for pump/compressor overhaul is not met.

sources.system: Experimental robotic disassembly cell
sources.title: An experimental robotic cell for the disassembly of electric vehicle battery modules | Journal of Remanufacturing
sources.claim: A robotic cell for disassembling used EV battery modules (unscrewing, pick-and-place, cutting, tool changing) is described as an experimental cell in the research literature, not a production system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of a used, bolted assembly in a purpose-built cell. Confirms that whole-cycle disassemble–inspect–replace–reassemble–test of worn units is not yet achieved at worker quality.

sources.system: Sensiworm
sources.title: GE Aerospace is developing a robotic worm to inspect and repair jet engines
sources.claim: GE Aerospace's Sensiworm crawler for in-situ engine inspection and prospective repair is remote-controlled by operators and at the demonstration stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ inspection/repair inside installed engines. Teleoperated and demo-stage, so it cannot support a positive judgment for hands-on engine-accessory repair.

tasks.label: Inspect and verify dimensions and clearances of parts to ensure conformance to factory specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Engine overhaul/rebuild bench metrology in a truck shop: measuring crankshaft main and rod journal diameters, taper and out-of-round with micrometers; cylinder liner/bore ID and out-of-round with a dial bore gauge; ring end gap, piston skirt, liner protrusion and head deck flatness; every reading compared to OEM service-limit tables to decide reuse, regrind or replace. Parts are used, cleaned cores from several engine families, handled loose on a bench.

In-chassis clearance verification on an installed diesel engine in a shop bay: setting and verifying valve lash, injector height/overhead adjustment and rocker clearances with feeler gauges and dial indicators, engine barred over to specific timing marks, reaching through the valve-cover opening in a cramped engine bay or under a tilted cab.

Wear-dimension checks on removable running gear during a PM or DOT annual inspection: brake lining/pad thickness, drum inner diameter, rotor thickness, hub and wheel-bearing condition, tire tread depth, measured with calipers, drum gauges and tread depth gauges on a truck raised on a lift or over a pit, wheels sometimes removed.

Play and clearance checks on the assembled vehicle: air-brake pushrod stroke at applied pressure, kingpin and tie-rod end play, wheel bearing endplay, u-joint/driveline slack, clutch free travel and steering wheel lash - the technician applies force with a pry bar or air pressure while reading a rule, dial indicator or scale against spec, chassis in a shop bay.

Driveline and transmission component bench metrology in the shop: ring-and-pinion backlash and tooth contact pattern with dial indicator and marking compound, carrier/pinion bearing preload, shaft endplay and runout, gear tooth and clutch disc wear measured on a removed assembly or bench fixture against factory specification.

Mobile/field service measurement: a road-service technician measures lining thickness, shaft runout, belt/pulley wear or a clearance on a disabled truck at a customer yard or roadside, working on uneven ground with handheld gauges in poor light and weather.

sources.system: Mitutoyo MiSTAR robotic measurement cell (Meca-Precis, with Engineering Data)
sources.title: Meca-Precis utilizes robotic measurement cell to eliminate inspection bottlenecks
sources.claim: A deployed robotic measurement cell (multi-axis articulated robot + Mitutoyo MiSTAR shop-floor CMM + 20-pallet automated storage) performs full dimensional inspection of machined parts autonomously, including during unattended shifts, in a purpose-built cell inside a machining workshop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: 100% dimensional inspection of machined parts against CAD/drawing tolerances. Transfers to verifying engine part dimensions because the objects (metal machined components), the micron-level precision, and the accept/reject-to-specification decision are the same; only the fixtured cell environment differs.

sources.system: Marposs M125 automatic gauge station
sources.title: MARPOSS automatic measuring machine for cylinder block and engine head inspection
sources.claim: Marposs M125 is an automatic gauge ... that performs dimensional and geometric checks on cylinder blocks and cylinder heads - the same bores, decks and journal features a diesel mechanic measures - in a production workshop setting.

sources.system: Marposs M110 automatic gauging machine
sources.title: Automatic Measuring Machine for Inspection of Shaft-like Components (Crankshafts, Camshafts, Gear Shafts)
sources.claim: Marposs M110 is an automatic ... that makes dimensional and geometric measurements on crankshafts, camshafts and transmission shafts - journal diameters, runout, lobe geometry - the measurements a mechanic makes with micrometers and dial indicators at overhaul.

sources.system: Marposs M100 automatic gauge station
sources.title: Automatic Measuring Machine for Inspection of Disk-Like Components (Brake Disks, Drums, Wheel Hubs)
sources.claim: Marposs M100 is an automatic ... for dimensional inspection of brake disks, drums and ..., i.e. automated measurement of exactly the friction/rotating components whose wear dimensions a truck technician checks against factory limits.

sources.system: Automated valve clearance adjustment machine (JSAE Review, Takase et al.)
sources.developer: Society of Automotive Engineers of Japan (Takase, Noro, Makino, Naito)
sources.title: DEVELOPMENT OF AUTOMATED ADJUSTMENT MACHINE FOR VALVE CLEARANCE OF AUTOMOBILE ENGINES - TRID
sources.claim: A fully automated machine measures and sets intake and exhaust valve clearance on every cylinder of assembled automobile engines using electric micrometers and motor-driven screwdrivers, running on the engine production line and eliminating skilled manual adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Same measurement: verifying valve lash against factory specification on an assembled engine, done by machine probes and electric micrometers rather than a feeler gauge; the engine arrives fixtured on a line rather than installed in a chassis.

sources.system: Valve lash adjustment apparatus (Atlas Copco / Utica Enterprises valve lash setting spindle)
sources.developer: Atlas Copco Tools & Assembly Systems / Utica Enterprises
sources.title: CA2434366C - Valve lash adjustment apparatus and method - Google Patents
sources.claim: A machine apparatus with contact probes, plunger and driven spindle measures rocker-arm valve lash directly and adjusts it at an automated assembly-line stop station, showing modern automated lash measuring hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that automated valve-lash measuring/adjusting machines are engineered for engine assembly stations; patent documentation only, so it supports but does not by itself establish deployment.

sources.system: Klingelnberg P 40 precision measuring center (P-series)
sources.title: Klingelnberg Group: P 40
sources.claim: Fully automatic CNC precision measuring centers inspect cylindrical and bevel gears, worms and general dimensional/form features of gear and shaft components against specification without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production gear metrology (tooth geometry, runout, general dimensions). Transfers to a mechanic's ring-and-pinion and transmission-shaft measurement because the same gear and shaft features are measured to the same tolerances against factory specification.

sources.system: UVeye heavy-duty vehicle inspection system (drive-through scanners)
sources.title: 'MRI for Vehicles' Now Available For Trucks - Heavy Duty Trucking
sources.claim: UVeye's drive-through AI scanners perform an automated 17-point inspection of Class 6-8 trucks and buses in seconds in fleet and dealer service lanes, covering exterior, underbody and tire condition, but not internal component metrology or applied-force clearance checks.
sources.transferJustification: Closest automated system operating in the technician's own environment (fleet/dealer service lane); cited to show that in-facility automated inspection today is camera-based external screening, not dimensional verification of parts and clearances.

tasks.label: Disassemble and overhaul internal combustion engines, pumps, generators, transmissions, clutches, and differential units.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Heavy-duty diesel engine overhaul in a fleet or dealer truck shop: pull or in-frame the engine, strip accessories, remove head(s), oil pan, pistons/liners, bearings; deal with seized, corroded, or heat-locked fasteners; clean and measure components; replace liners, rings, bearings, seals; reassemble to torque-plus-angle and clearance specs; set valves and injectors; run and leak-check.

Transmission or clutch job on a Class 6-8 truck in the shop: split the driveline, remove the transmission/clutch with a jack, tear down the gearbox on a bench or stand, inspect gears/synchros/bearings/shafts, press bearings on and off, reshim and reassemble, reinstall and align, road test.

Differential/final-drive or axle carrier overhaul on the bench: remove carrier, disassemble ring-and-pinion, bearings and diff case, inspect for wear/spalling, set pinion depth, backlash and preload by shim and gear-pattern checks, reassemble and reinstall.

Auxiliary component overhaul at the bench: injection pumps, water/hydraulic/air pumps, alternators/generators, starters, air compressors, turbochargers — teardown, cleaning, wear inspection, replacing bearings, seals, brushes or plungers, reassembly and bench test/calibration.

Field or mobile overhaul work: engine, clutch, or differential repair performed at a customer yard, quarry, farm, construction site, or roadside on a mobile service truck, with variable footing, weather, lighting, and no fixed lift or bench.

sources.system: Human–robot collaborative disassembly (review of state of the art)
sources.title: A comprehensive review on human–robot collaboration remanufacturing towards uncertain and dynamic disassembly
sources.claim: A 2024 peer-reviewed review of human–robot collaborative remanufacturing states that fully automated disassembly lines remain unrealized because of the uncertainty of end-of-life products; only semi-automated, human-in-the-loop disassembly is being implemented.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about disassembly of used engines and drivetrain cores, the first half of an overhaul; establishes that no fully automated line exists even in dedicated reman facilities.

sources.system: Human–robot collaborative disassembly cell, Autonomous Remanufacturing Laboratory
sources.title: An experimental human-robot collaborative disassembly cell
sources.claim: The most advanced demonstrated disassembly of an automotive powertrain component (a turbocharger) was done in a laboratory human–robot collaborative cell, i.e., a robot working alongside a human operator rather than completing the teardown alone.
sources.transferJustification: Turbocharger teardown is a used-core powertrain disassembly closely related to engine/pump overhaul; the demonstration still required a human partner and was lab-scale.

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing station (UR10e + RealSense D405 + custom mechatronic screwdriver)
sources.developer: Academic research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robotic disassembly is confined to a single sub-step — locating and unscrewing fasteners — on small electronic devices and EV battery packs, not to whole-unit teardown, inspection and rebuild.
sources.transferJustification: Unfastening is the entry step of any overhaul; the evidence shows autonomy today extends only to this isolated step on small, clean, non-seized fasteners.

sources.system: RoboTire automated tire-changing system
sources.title: AI-Driven Robots Have Started Changing Tires In The U.S. In Half The Time As Humans
sources.claim: Deployed autonomous robotics in vehicle service bays is limited to wheel/tire service: the machine removes lug nuts, dismounts and remounts a wheel and torques to spec, with no teardown of powertrain assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Wheel service is the closest deployed robotic analogue to shop mechanic work (unbolting/rebolting on a vehicle in a service bay); it involves one standardized fastener pattern and no disassembly of an internal assembly, so it does not transfer to overhaul.

sources.system: Robotic diesel cylinder-head processing cell
sources.title: Case Studies: Industrial Cylinder Heads Assembly Automation
sources.claim: Robotic automation of engine work in industry is confined to assembly and processing of new, fixtured components on a dedicated production line — e.g., a robot cell processing diesel engine cylinder heads through cleaning and peening within an existing engine assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Engine assembly automation covers new, uniform, fixtured parts; overhaul additionally requires teardown of a worn unit, condition assessment, machining decisions and fitting to measured clearances, none of which this cell performs.

sources.system: JASPER diesel engine remanufacturing line
sources.title: The JASPER Process: Diesel Engines
sources.claim: In purpose-built engine and transmission remanufacturing plants — the most machine-friendly setting this work occurs in — the teardown, machining and rebuild are performed by skilled human technicians using specialized equipment.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task (overhaul of diesel engines, pumps and injection components) carried out at high volume in a dedicated facility; it shows the work is still done by technicians, not robots, even where the environment could be built around machines.

tasks.label: Adjust or repair computer controlled exhaust emissions devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer/fleet shop bay: truck in for a check-engine/derate warning. Tech connects diagnostic laptop (JPRO, Cummins INSITE, DDDL) to the 9-pin connector, reads aftertreatment fault codes, inspects wiring/sensors and DEF quality, then runs a forced/parked regeneration, resets ash accumulator or SCR adaptations, clears codes and verifies the derate is gone.

Shop bay: replace a failed aftertreatment sensor or metering component (inlet/outlet NOx sensor, exhaust temp sensor, delta-P lines, DEF doser/injector, DEF pump or header) on a Class 8 truck. Work under the chassis or in a crowded engine bay, corroded/seized fasteners and fittings, torch/penetrant, harness routing and connector care, then code clear and verification regen.

Shop bay: DPF/DOC service. Loosen V-band clamps and brackets, disconnect sensors and harness, remove the ash-loaded filter (often 60-100 lb, sometimes with a lift), pneumatically clean and thermally bake it and flow-test (or replace), reinstall with new gaskets/clamps to torque spec, reset ash counters and verify with a regen.

Shop bay: EGR system repair on a diesel engine — replace EGR valve, EGR cooler or differential-pressure sensor. Drain coolant, remove intake/exhaust plumbing and heat shields, extract a heavy cooler from a tight engine valley, fit gaskets, torque sequence, refill and leak-check, clear codes and confirm EGR flow commands track.

Shop bay: full one-box SCR/DPF aftertreatment assembly replacement or overhaul on a truck or transit bus — unbolt frame-rail mounts, disconnect DEF lines, dosing unit and full harness, lower the assembly with a jack or hoist, fit the new/reman unit, re-plumb and re-harness, program the new unit's parameters, and run verification cycles.

Roadside or truck-stop mobile service call: truck derated with an SCR/DEF fault. Mobile tech works on gravel/pavement in weather without a lift, diagnoses with a laptop and hand tools, replaces a NOx sensor or DEF doser or thaws/repairs a DEF line, performs a stationary regen, and returns the truck to service.

sources.system: RoboTire tire-changing system
sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: RoboTire's robotic wheel-service system is installed in retail tire stores, where robot arms remove, lift and install wheel-and-tire assemblies on customer cars — the closest commercial case of robots performing bolt-level service work on in-service vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wheel R&R in a service shop. It shows robots can unbolt a standardized, externally accessible fastener pattern in a fixed bay, but it does not transfer to emissions-device repair: no fault diagnosis, no engine-bay or under-chassis access, no seized exhaust clamps, gaskets, DEF plumbing or harness work, and no post-repair regeneration/verification.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly platform (four industrial robots, unscrewing system with nutrunner adapter changing)
sources.developer: University of Birmingham (ReLiB/Automation journal case study)
sources.title: Robotic Disassembly Platform for Disassembly of a Plug-In Hybrid Electric Vehicle Battery: A Case Study
sources.claim: A four-robot laboratory platform automates non-destructive unscrewing and disassembly of a used plug-in hybrid EV battery pack, handling jammed screws and positional uncertainty — the most advanced demonstrated robotic disassembly of a used automotive assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal of fasteners from a used automotive assembly. Transfer fails for this task: the pack is removed from the vehicle and fixtured in a purpose-built cell, the screw set is known in advance, and the work is destruction-free teardown, not diagnosis, corroded exhaust-clamp work, gasket sealing, reassembly to torque and ECM verification on a truck.

sources.system: Rocsys autonomous charging robot (RCS-1 / M1)
sources.date: 2025-04 (port demo with DAF autonomous truck); 2026-04 (M1 multi-bay)
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic arms autonomously locate a vehicle's charging inlet, open the flap, insert and remove the connector at ports and charging depots — demonstrated autonomous connector mating with in-service commercial vehicles in a controlled facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous insertion of a connector into a vehicle port. It substantiates only the plug-in step of a diagnostic session; it provides no evidence for reading and interpreting aftertreatment fault codes, physically inspecting sensors/DEF quality, or commanding and validating a regeneration to a shop's acceptance standard.

sources.system: FSX TrapBlaster JR pneumatic DPF/DOC cleaning machine
sources.date: product page retrieved 2026-07 (product line in commercial use for years)
sources.title: TrapBlaster Jr | FSX Equipment, Inc
sources.claim: Commercial DPF/DOC cleaning is done with automated cleaning cabinets that run programmed pneumatic scanning-air-knife cycles, but an operator must remove the filter from the truck, load and unload the cabinet, and reinstall and verify it on the vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bench cleaning of a removed particulate filter. It is an operator-loaded appliance covering one sub-step; it performs no vehicle-side removal, reinstallation, ash-counter reset or regeneration verification, so it cannot complete the whole DPF service instance.

tasks.label: Rebuild gas or diesel engines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-frame overhaul of a Class 8 truck diesel (e.g., Cummins X15, Detroit DD15, PACCAR MX) in a fleet or dealer shop bay: truck on the floor or lift, hood and cooling package pulled, oil pan and head removed, cylinder kits (liners, pistons, rings) and rod/main bearings replaced in situ, cam and rocker gear inspected, liner protrusion and bearing clearances checked with dial bore gauge and plastigage, all fasteners torqued to sequence and angle, then valve/injector lash set and the engine run and leak-checked.

Out-of-frame rebuild in a truck shop: engine pulled from the chassis and mounted on a rotating engine stand, complete teardown to a bare block, parts hot-tanked or pressure-washed, crank and block measured and sent out for grind/bore/deck, cylinder head reconditioned, then selective reassembly with new bearings, gaskets and seals, oil pump priming, and run-in on the stand or after installation.

Transit or school bus engine overhaul in an agency maintenance garage: rear or mid-mounted engine removed on a cradle through a tight compartment, in-frame or out-of-frame overhaul performed alongside aftertreatment, turbo and EGR service, with agency inspection sign-off before return to service.

Bench work forming part of an engine rebuild: cylinder head torn down and reconditioned (valve springs, guides, seats, lash caps), and accessory assemblies such as turbocharger, oil pump, front cover, air compressor and injection components disassembled, measured against wear limits, cleaned of carbon and gasket residue, and rebuilt to spec at a workbench in the shop.

Field or mobile rebuild at the customer's site: marine diesel in a cramped engine room, off-highway or mining equipment engine at a jobsite, or a stationary genset in a mechanical room, with the mechanic rigging lifting gear, working out of a service truck, and doing teardown, cylinder pack replacement and reassembly in place under non-standard access, lighting and weather.

sources.system: Alfred robotic HPC rotor assembly cell
sources.title: Robot Assembles Aircraft Engines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A fenced robotic cell named Alfred at Pratt & Whitney's Eagle Services Asia MRO facility autonomously builds the high-pressure compressor rotor module of overhauled GTF jet engines after an operator loads hardware into ...; it is one module build within an engine overhaul, with the rest of the overhaul done by technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: engine module assembly inside an overhaul (MRO) shop, the closest deployed robotic analogue to rebuilding an engine. Transfer to the whole rebuild fails: parts arrive already stripped, cleaned, inspected and fixtured, the cell stacks one rotor of one engine model, and no teardown, wear measurement, condition judgment or selective fitting is done by the robot.

sources.system: robotic disassembly systems (general state of the art)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: Industry review of remanufacturing automation as of 2026: robotic disassembly of used products is only beginning to emerge and is blocked by the variability of worn hardware such as seized bolts and deformed parts, leaving most remanufacturing work with skilled human technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the disassembly and inspection stages that open every engine rebuild; establishes that no fielded robotic system tears down used engines with worn or seized fasteners.

sources.system: Track-mounted dual-robot cylinder head finishing cell
sources.title: Industrial Cylinder Heads Assembly Automation | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: A turnkey dual-robot cell processes four models of new diesel cylinder heads (vision part-ID, heated wash, shot peen, plug inspection, drying, cooling) on a three-minute cycle inside a purpose-built cell integrated into an existing engine assembly line, with one operator overseeing flow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling, cleaning and inspection of diesel cylinder heads in a purpose-built cell. It covers only clean/inspect handling of new machined heads presented by conveyor in known orientation; it does not disassemble a used head, measure wear, or reassemble a valvetrain.

sources.system: Optomec LENS + Acme Manufacturing robotic blade repair cell
sources.title: Aircraft Engine MRO: How Additive Manufacturing Plus Robotic Finishing Will Expand Capacity for Blade Repair
sources.claim: An automated production cell combining Optomec directed-energy deposition with Acme robotic finishing restores worn aircraft engine blade tips at high volume, illustrating that automated remanufacture of worn parts is achieved only for a single fixed-geometry part family.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated repair of worn engine parts. Transfer is limited: one simple fixtured geometry restored by deposition and grinding, versus a multi-hundred-part engine rebuild requiring teardown, condition judgment and assembly.

sources.system: Object-centric autonomous disassembly framework (research)
sources.title: Disassembly from scratch: An object-centric approach for robotic autonomous disassembly with zero contact/interference information
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic disassembly without predefined task models remains at laboratory-experiment stage, validated on generic structures rather than in production teardown of used machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the teardown stage of a rebuild; shows the capability exists only as lab feasibility work, not as a system that could strip a worn diesel engine to worker standard.

tasks.label: Specialize in repairing and maintaining parts of the engine, such as fuel injection systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-chassis fuel injection component replacement on a heavy truck or bus in a fleet/dealer service bay: remove valve cover, rocker shafts or fuel rail and high-pressure lines, extract carbon-seized injectors from bores, clean and inspect cups/bores, install new/reman injectors to torque and injector-height spec, prime and bleed the system, program trim codes, leak check and road test.

Fuel-system diagnosis and adjustment in the shop: return/leak-off flow tests, cylinder cutout and rail pressure tests, injector solenoid and harness checks, fuel filter/water separator and supply-pump service, then setting overhead — valve lash and injector adjustment (Cummins/Detroit style) with feeler gauges and torqued locknuts.

Bench overhaul and calibration of fuel-injection components in a specialty diesel injection or reman shop: disassemble used common-rail injectors or injection pumps (seized nozzle nuts, carboned parts), ultrasonic clean, measure lapped surfaces, replace nozzles/plungers/springs/seals, reassemble to precise torque, then flow-test/calibrate on a test bench and issue a test report.

Major internal engine component repair in the shop: cylinder head removal and reinstallation, valve/valve-seat and injector cup or sleeve replacement, head gasket and torque-to-angle head bolt sequence, or in-frame overhaul work involving liners, pistons, bearings and timing components on a truck engine.

Field/mobile service: fuel injector, injection pump, or supply-system repair performed on a truck at a customer yard or roadside, or on a marine diesel in a vessel engine room or a stationary genset at a remote site, with limited access, portable tools and variable weather.

sources.system: Human-robot collaborative disassembly cell (2x KUKA LBR iiwa 14 R820), Autonomous Remanufacturing Laboratory, University of Birmingham
sources.title: An experimental human-robot collaborative disassembly cell — Computers & Industrial Engineering
sources.claim: Robotic disassembly of used automotive engine components (an automotive turbocharger) has been demonstrated only as a human-robot collaborative laboratory cell, with an operator working alongside two collaborative robots — not as autonomous end-to-end component repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown of a used diesel-engine accessory (turbocharger) with threaded fasteners — the closest published analogue to bench overhaul of injectors/pumps. It shows the state of the art requires a human collaborator, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of engine-part repair.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly systems in remanufacturing (general survey of deployed/emerging systems)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: As of 2026, robotic disassembly for remanufacturing remains emergent, with condition variability — seized bolts, deformed parts — cited as a major unresolved obstacle to automating repair-type teardown of used parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown/repair of used mechanical assemblies in remanufacturing. Directly bears on whether a robot could remove and replace worn fuel-system parts; the cited obstacles (seized fasteners, variable part condition) are exactly the conditions of diesel injector and pump repair.

sources.system: Survey of robotic disassembly techniques and applications
sources.developer: Academic review (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: The future of robotic disassembly: a systematic review of techniques and applications in the age of AI
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of robotic disassembly finds the field limited by absence of disassembly standards and labelling, restricting generalization of robot behaviour across products — i.e., no general autonomous repair/teardown capability for used machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of end-of-life products, the enabling capability for automated component repair. Establishes that autonomous teardown of used hardware — the first half of every engine-part repair instance — is not a mature capability.

sources.system: Industrial robot with Bosch machine vision code-reading system, Bosch plant, Curitiba, Brazil
sources.title: Bosch Launches Vision System to Read Codes on Injector Nozzles
sources.claim: Deployed industrial robots handle new fuel-injector nozzles in a Bosch plant only for presentation to a vision inspection system; the demonstrated capability is pick-and-place of clean new parts, not repair of used injection components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling of fuel-injection components in a purpose-built manufacturing cell. It substantiates only part transport/inspection of new nozzles; it does not cover disassembly, part replacement, torqueing, or calibration of used injectors, so it cannot substantiate completion of any repair instance even at E1.

sources.system: SmartBay robotic service bay
sources.title: AI robot changes your tires and balances them too (Fox News)
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial robotic vehicle-service system in a purpose-built service bay is limited to tire mounting, balancing and inspection; no comparable commercial system performs engine or fuel-system repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated vehicle service in a purpose-built bay. Scope is wheels/tires — externally accessible, standardized interfaces — and does not transfer to confined under-hood fuel-injection work with seized fasteners, high-pressure lines and torque/calibration specs.

tasks.label: Recondition and replace parts, pistons, bearings, gears, and valves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-frame (in-chassis) overhaul of a heavy-duty diesel in a fleet or dealer shop bay: engine stays in the truck/bus; mechanic removes valve covers, rockers and cylinder heads, pulls worn liners and pistons, replaces rings, rod bearings, liner O-rings and seals, reinstalls with torque-angle sequences and clearance checks, in confined, oily, grime-covered access.

Out-of-chassis rebuild in the shop: engine pulled and mounted on a stand; complete teardown of a used, carboned/rusted engine, cleaning, micrometer and dial-bore measurement, deciding what to reuse or recondition, then installing new pistons, rings, main and rod bearings, valves and gaskets to spec.

Cylinder-head / valvetrain bench reconditioning: disassemble keepers, springs and stuck valves from a used head, pressure-test and inspect for cracks, replace valves, guides, seats and stem seals, grind or lap seats, reassemble the valvetrain and set lash.

Gear and driveline reconditioning: rebuild a differential carrier or transmission (replace worn ring-and-pinion, cluster gears, synchronizers, tapered bearings; set pinion depth, backlash and preload with shims), or replace wheel-end bearings, races and seals on a truck or bus axle.

Replacement of bolt-on engine and driveline components in the shop: turbochargers, injectors, water/oil pumps, air compressors, clutches, EGR coolers; fasteners often seized or corroded, gasket surfaces scraped clean, fluids drained and refilled, then function-checked.

Field or mobile repair: mechanic with a service truck replacing parts on a bus, truck or marine diesel at a customer yard, roadside, dock or job site, on uneven ground in weather, with limited lighting, tools and no fixtures.

sources.system: MWES robotic oven-tending and engine block liner insertion cell
sources.title: Case Studies: Engine Block Liner Insert Automation | Midwest Engineered Systems Inc.
sources.claim: A deployed two-robot production cell heats large engine blocks and inserts six or eight cylinder liners per block - the same liner-installation operation performed during a diesel overhaul, but on new blocks in a fixtured, purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: new-engine assembly. Installing cylinder liners into a block involves the same object and interference-fit precision as replacing liners during an overhaul, but the block is new, clean, fixtured and conveyor-presented, with no teardown or condition assessment.

sources.system: JR Automation automated piston assembly system
sources.title: Robotic Automation Case Studies - Association for Advancing Automation
sources.claim: An integrator-built automated piston assembly system installs pistons for multiple engine variants across two engine families on a 25-second cycle, showing that piston installation into fixtured blocks is automated in production settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: new-engine piston installation. Same components (piston, rings, rod) and bore clearances as piston replacement in a rebuild, but with new parts fed to a fixtured block and no removal of worn pistons or measurement-driven fitting.

sources.system: MWES industrial cylinder heads assembly/processing robot cell
sources.title: Case Studies: Industrial Cylinder Heads Assembly Automation | Midwest Engineered Systems Inc.
sources.claim: A fully automated robot cell processes four different models of diesel engine cylinder heads (cleaning and peening) as part of an assembly line, showing robotic handling and surface processing of diesel heads inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diesel cylinder-head production processing. It shows robotic handling of the same heads a mechanic reconditions, but covers only cleaning and peening of production parts, not valvetrain teardown, seat machining or reassembly of a used head.

sources.system: robotic disassembly systems for remanufacturing (industry state-of-the-art review)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: As of March 2026, robotic disassembly for remanufacturing is described as only beginning to emerge, with condition variability of used products the major obstacle to automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: teardown of used machinery for remanufacture, which is the disassembly half of every reconditioning instance in this task; the source establishes it is not yet performed autonomously at production quality.

sources.system: GE Aerospace robotic blade blending (Singapore automation lab)
sources.title: GE Aerospace turns to robots and 'Lean' methods to tackle jet engine repair crunch (Reuters)
sources.claim: At GE Aerospace's purpose-built component repair facility, restoring worn compressor blade tips to tolerance has been entirely manual, and a robot is only now being taught the process in an automation lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reconditioning worn engine components to tight tolerance in a highly structured industrial repair shop; the closest analogue to valve, seat and surface reconditioning, and it shows the operation is still manual where fixtures and process control are best-in-class.

sources.system: RoboTire automated tire-changing system
sources.title: Tire Changing Robot Installed at Second Discount Tire Store
sources.claim: Robotic vehicle-service systems deployed in commercial service bays are limited to wheel and tire work (locating and removing lug nuts, swapping and balancing tires); no comparable deployed system opens engines or driveline assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing and refitting a vehicle part in a service bay. It marks the frontier of in-shop repair robotics, but handles only standardized, fully exposed lug nuts and wheels, not buried engine or gear-train fasteners and components.

sources.system: Digital twin with model predictive control for robotic screw unfastening
sources.title: Digital Twin with Model Predictive Control for Screw Unfastening by Robots
sources.claim: Removing degraded screws and bolts from used products remains an active research problem, addressed in 2026 with digital-twin model-predictive control at laboratory scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic unfastening of corroded fasteners, the first step of nearly every part-replacement instance here; the work is laboratory-stage, so it cannot substantiate worker-quality completion.

tasks.label: Install or repair accessories.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fleet shop bay: bolt-on exterior accessory kits fitted to a batch of identical new/near-new trucks (mud flaps and hangers, fender extensions, cab steps, bug/deer guards, chrome trim, hose hangers) using existing brackets and pre-drilled provisions; torque fasteners, visual fit check.

Shop bay, in-service trucks of varied makes/ages: replace or install individual accessories such as heated/powered mirrors, marker and work lamps, backup camera, trailer light receptacle, wiper arms/motors, air horns; break loose corroded fasteners, splice or route wiring to the existing harness, weather-seal, function test.

Shop bay, in-cab electronics: install or repair telematics/ELD units, dash cams, two-way radios, inverters, auxiliary switch panels, radios/speakers; work under the dash and behind panels, route wire through firewall/headliner, fuse-tap or harness-tap power, mount hardware, configure and test.

Shop bay, comfort/climate accessories on in-service trucks and buses: diagnose and repair cab A/C, bunk or auxiliary heater, APU, blower motor/resistor, seat air suspension, defroster; remove the failed unit from a confined engine bay or cab interior, replace, evacuate/recharge or bleed, verify operation.

Shop or upfit bay, heavy mounted equipment: install liftgate, pintle hitch, snow plow, headache rack, PTO-driven pump, or bus wheelchair lift; measure and drill or weld frame mounts, run hydraulic lines and heavy electrical, adjust and test under load.

Mobile service call at a customer yard, terminal lot, or roadside: replace a broken mirror, lamp, or mud flap, or repair accessory wiring on a truck parked wherever it stopped, working from a service truck without a lift, in weather and traffic.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR5/UR10/UR10e cobot cells at Stellantis Mirafiori
sources.title: Stellantis | Cobot Case Stories - Universal Robots
sources.claim: Eleven Universal Robots cobots on the FIAT 500 line at Stellantis' Mirafiori plant automate bolt-on exterior part installation, including mudguard mounting, hood mounting, tailgate riveting and tightening of rear side-door hinges, on vehicles indexed on the assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: line installation of bolt-on exterior vehicle parts. Mudguards/fender guards and their fasteners are the same class of object, fastening and tolerance as fleet-spec bolt-on truck accessories (mud flaps, fender extensions, guards), with the vehicle presented in a fixed, known position as a purpose-built cell would present it.

sources.system: Volvo Trucks cab assembly glazing/hatch robots
sources.title: How a Volvo truck cab is assembled | Volvo Trucks Magazine
sources.claim: Two industrial robots on Volvo Trucks' cab assembly line install windscreens, side windows and ... onto FH truck cabs, with sensors ensuring the cab is exactly positioned and placement accurate to tenths of a millimetre.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fitting exterior fitments (roof hatches, glazing) onto truck cabs. Shows robots mounting truck-scale exterior parts to spec in a purpose-built, sensed and fixtured cell, the closest industrial analogue to bolting an accessory onto a truck cab brought to the machine.

sources.system: Inbolt GuideNOW 3D vision + FANUC CRX/industrial robots
sources.title: FANUC and Inbolt Automate Moving Assembly Lines With Robots - Control.com
sources.claim: FANUC robots guided by Inbolt's robot-mounted 3D vision perform vision-guided fastening on vehicles moving down general assembly lines, including inserting and tightening screws and running down bolts; the system has been installed and tested at ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fastening of parts onto vehicles. Supplies the bolt-driving and part-locating element of accessory mounting on vehicles inside an automotive plant, but only for pre-engineered fastener locations on new vehicles.

sources.system: Figure 02 humanoid
sources.title: Successful test of humanoid robots at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg - BMW Group PressClub
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid deployment in vehicle production to date ran roughly 11 months at BMW Spartanburg, where Figure 02 picked sheet metal parts and inserted them into welding fixtures; no accessory fitting, wiring or repair work was performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid part handling in a vehicle plant. Cited to bound what general-purpose robots do on vehicles today - fixtured part placement on new bodies - which does not extend to fitting, wiring or repairing accessories on in-service trucks.

sources.system: RoboTire robotic tire-changing system
sources.title: RoboTire Launches Tire Changing System in Second Discount Tire Location
sources.claim: RoboTire systems installed in Discount Tire and other tire stores remove and install wheel/tire assemblies on customer vehicles in a service bay; this is the extent of demonstrated robotic hands-on work on in-service vehicles in a human service facility and covers no accessory fitting, wiring or diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bolt-off/bolt-on work on customer vehicles in a service shop. Cited as the ceiling of E2 service-bay robotics - one highly standardized wheel interface with the vehicle spotted for the machine - far short of varied accessory fitting and wiring.

tasks.label: Repair or adjust seats, doors, or windows.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fleet shop bay: heavy-truck cab door repair — sagging/misaligned door from worn hinge pins and bushings, sticking latch or striker, broken outside handle or lock actuator. Mechanic diagnoses by feel and fit, pops interior trim panel clips, removes often-corroded fasteners, drives out hinge pins, installs new pins/bushings or hardware, then iteratively shims and realigns the door to gap and seal specs and verifies it latches and seals.

Fleet shop bay: cab window work — dead power window, broken regulator cable or motor, cracked door glass, worn glass run channels, or a leaking windshield. Requires removing door trim and vapor barrier, extracting the regulator through access holes, or cutting out urethane-bonded glass, cleaning and priming the pinchweld, setting new glass, and leak/rattle testing.

Fleet shop bay: seat work in a truck cab — air-suspension seat that won't hold air or bottoms out, broken swivel/slide track, torn cushion or worn bushings, loose pedestal bolts. Mechanic diagnoses, unbolts the seat from the floor inside a cramped cab, disconnects air line/wiring/belt anchors, replaces the seat or rebuilds the suspension, reinstalls to torque, and checks travel and belt function.

Transit or school bus garage: passenger door system service — pneumatic or electric door engine adjustment, worn linkage and rod-end replacement, sensitive edge/interlock and closing-force checks, seal and door glass replacement, plus passenger seat frame bolt tightening and cushion/back replacement inside the bus aisle.

Mobile/road service call: truck at a customer yard, terminal lot, or roadside with a door that won't latch or open, a broken side window to board up or replace, or a seat that has come loose — worked on outdoors in whatever weather, light, and parking position the vehicle is found in, with only the tools on the service truck.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced deployed automotive-service robot is a purpose-built robotic service bay that performs tire changes, wheel balancing and inspection; a technician still positions the vehicle and connects the air line, and its scope is the wheel/tire interface only — not cab door, glass, or seat repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wheel/tire service on vehicles in a shop bay. It does not transfer to repairing seats, doors, or windows: the wheel is a standardized bolt-circle interface on the vehicle exterior, whereas this task requires fault diagnosis, removal of clipped trim, work inside the cab, bonded-glass cut-out, and iterative fit adjustment, none of which the system performs.

sources.system: RoboTire robotic wheel-changing system
sources.title: RoboTire's automated wheel-changing system - Case Study | Zivid
sources.claim: Robotic wheel-changing cells have been installed in tire shops, again limited to removing and mounting wheels and tires with the vehicle presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vehicle wheel service in a service bay. Same limits as SmartBay — one standardized fastener interface on the vehicle exterior, with no demonstrated trim removal, in-cab work, glass bonding, or door alignment.

sources.system: Automotive final-assembly robots (windshield glazing, seat loading)
sources.title: Automotive Robots: Revolutionizing the Assembly Line | Wevolver
sources.claim: Industrial robots routinely install new windshields and seats on vehicles, but only in fixtured final-assembly lines where new, identical parts are presented to the machine on an indexed body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing glass and seats into vehicle bodies. Transfer to repair fails because assembly supplies a new, clean, dimensionally known body in a fixture and never requires fault diagnosis, removal of a worn or corroded assembly, cut-out of cured urethane, or iterative realignment of an in-service door.

sources.system: Robotic screw-removal / EV battery disassembly cell
sources.developer: University of Birmingham / Wuhan University of Technology research groups
sources.title: Robotic Removal and Collection of Screws in Collaborative Disassembly of End-of-Life Electric Vehicle Batteries
sources.claim: Automated removal of fasteners from used, in-service assemblies — the precondition for any repair — remains laboratory research conducted in fixtured cells with human-robot collaboration, because used hardware presents uncertain screw positions and conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of used vehicle assemblies. It shows the enabling step for repair — removing worn fasteners from used hardware — is still demo-grade in fixtured lab cells, so it cannot substantiate whole repair jobs on trucks or buses even at E1.

sources.system: Figure 02 / Figure 03 at BMW Spartanburg
sources.title: Humanoid Robots in 2026: What Is Actually Deployed - Technology Org
sources.claim: Humanoid robots deployed in automotive facilities are doing part handling and logistics sequencing in fixtured production settings, not vehicle service or repair work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose humanoid manipulation in automotive facilities. The deployed scope is part loading and sequencing, which does not substantiate diagnosis-and-repair of doors, windows, or seats at any tier.

tasks.label: Dismount, mount, and repair or replace tires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Class 8 tractor/trailer in a fleet maintenance shop: mechanic jacks the axle, breaks loose and removes 10 hub-piloted lug nuts (~450-500 ft-lb) on a dual position, pulls the 100-150 lb steel wheel/tire assemblies, breaks the beads and demounts the worn 22.5 in tires on a heavy-duty changer, inspects/cleans the rims, mounts new or retread tires, inflates in a safety cage, remounts the duals and torques to spec.

Mobile/roadside emergency service call: blown or flat tire on a truck or trailer stopped on a highway shoulder, at a customer yard, or in a truck stop lot; technician works from a service truck with jack, cordless impact and a spare or new tire, in traffic, weather and on uneven ground, then torques and returns the vehicle to service.

Tire repair in the shop: locating a nail hole or slow leak, demounting the tire from the rim, buffing and installing an inside patch/combination plug-patch or replacing a valve stem/tube, checking the casing for damage, remounting, inflating and balance/runout check before reinstallation.

Transit or school bus in a fleet garage: replacing worn steer or drive tires on Budd/hub-piloted wheels in confined wheel wells and skirted bodywork, demounting and mounting the tires on the rims, inflating, checking dual matching and spacing, and torquing fasteners.

Light- and medium-duty fleet vehicle (cargo van, box truck, service pickup) in the shop: remove the wheels, demount and mount 16-19.5 in tires on a tire changer, balance the assemblies, reinstall and torque.

Tire-room bench work in the fleet shop, no vehicle involved: building up spare wheel assemblies by installing valve stems, lubricating beads and mounting new or retread truck tires onto clean/new rims on a heavy-duty changer, then inflating in a cage to pressure spec and staging the assemblies.

sources.system: RoboTire System (4th generation)
sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: RoboTire's robotic cell, installed in Discount Tire retail store service bays, autonomously removes, lifts and installs tire-and-wheel assemblies on passenger vehicles, while store technicians still perform balancing and pressure monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passenger-car wheel removal/installation in a tire store. It bounds what deployed vehicle-side tire robots do - light-vehicle wheels only, with humans still doing the tire-to-rim and balancing steps.

sources.system: RoboTire System with Hunter Revolution changer
sources.title: AI-powered RoboTire can change 4 tires twice as fast as a human | Fox News
sources.claim: In RoboTire's deployed workflow the robot arms unscrew lug nuts and pull the wheels, then pass them to a Hunter tire changer, but a human technician loads the fresh tire into ... monitors the operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passenger-car tire replacement. Shows the dismount/mount-on-rim portion is not robot-executed end to end even in the most advanced deployed service-bay cell.

sources.system: RoboTire wheel-changing system (Zivid 2 3D vision)
sources.title: RoboTire's automated wheel-changing system - Case Study (Zivid)
sources.claim: The RoboTire cell used 3D machine vision and AI to locate lug nuts and remove/replace wheels; its vision supplier describes the system as fully autonomous and adaptable to the vehicles it encounters in shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive wheel R&R. Establishes the autonomy level of the leading service-bay tire robot, which is limited to light vehicles.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: SmartBay, the 2026 service-bay tire robot, is semi-automated: an operator removes the used tire, positions the new tire in the ..., connects the air line to inflate, and mounts the balance weights; it works on passenger vehicles with the wheels left on the car.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: light-vehicle tire dismount/mount. The newest system still requires manual steps, so no cited system completes a tire change end to end.

sources.system: Haul Truck Wheel Changer
sources.title: Haul Truck Wheel Changer | Lewis Australia
sources.claim: Heavy haul-truck wheel/tyre changing machines used at mine sites are remotely operated by a human rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: very large off-road wheel/tyre change. The only machines that handle truck-scale wheels are teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

sources.system: Ultimation truck tire changer / tire assembly machine
sources.title: Tire Assembly Machine | Ultimation Industries | Tire Mounting and Inflation
sources.claim: Conveyor-fed, PLC-controlled tire assembly machines produce a mounted and inflated heavy-truck tire/wheel assembly in under 30 seconds inside high-volume tire-and-wheel assembly lines; fully automatic models are offered for passenger, light commercial and heavy truck tires.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element (mounting a tire on a rim and inflating it to spec), performed on truck tires, but in a purpose-built assembly line rather than a service bay.

sources.system: Schenck RoTec wheel assembly lines
sources.title: Wheel Assembly Lines: individual & complete solutions | Schenck
sources.claim: Automated wheel assembly lines perform lubricant application, tire mounting on the rim, inflation and balancing as monitored automatic stations for car and commercial-car tires.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element (mount tire to rim, inflate, balance) executed automatically in a purpose-built line; corroborates E1 capability for mounting new tires on clean rims.

tasks.label: Align front ends and suspension systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steer-axle (front-end) alignment on an in-service Class 8 tractor in a fleet or dealer shop: truck driven onto the alignment bay/pit, sensor heads or laser gear mounted on the wheels, toe/camber/caster and thrust angle measured, total toe corrected by loosening the cross-tube clamp bolts and rotating the tube, steering wheel centered via the drag link, fasteners re-torqued, results printed and road-verified. Fasteners are often rusted and the linkage is worn.

Complete tractor-trailer alignment in the shop: after the steer axle, drive-axle thrust angle corrected by adjusting/shimming torque rods or loosening U-bolts and repositioning the axle, and trailer axles squared to the kingpin (slider or adjustable torque arms). Heavy under-vehicle work with 200+ ft-lb fasteners, heat/cutting of seized hardware, jacks and stands.

Transit or school bus alignment in a transit garage: air-suspension ride height set at the leveling valves first, then toe/camber/caster measured and corrected on the front axle (and tag/rear-steer axles on some coaches), working around low body panels, skirts, and tight bay clearance.

Suspension/steering geometry restoration that accompanies the alignment: dry-park inspection finds worn kingpins, tie rod ends, drag link, spring or torque-rod bushings, shackles, or sagged springs; the technician replaces the parts (press work, torch, hammer, press-fit kingpin bushings, ream) and then aligns the vehicle to spec.

On-site alignment check and correction performed with portable equipment at a customer terminal yard, quarry, or roadside — outdoor, unlevel gravel or asphalt surface, weather, no lift, portable laser/optical alignment kit and hand tools.

Alignment of a light/medium-duty fleet vehicle handled by the same shop (cargo van, step van, or small box truck with independent front suspension): toe set by loosening jam nuts and rotating the adjustable tie rod sleeves, camber/caster by cam bolts, on a conventional alignment rack.

sources.system: Dürr x-wheel / x-3Dprofile wheel alignment stand
sources.title: See and drive perfectly with x-light and x-wheel — Dürr Group

tasks.label: Maintain or repair vehicles with alternative fuel systems, including biodiesel, hybrid, or compressed natural gas vehicles.

instances.label: Scheduled preventive maintenance of a CNG transit bus or refuse truck in a fleet maintenance garage: raise the vehicle/use roof access, leak-check cylinders, lines and fittings with a gas detector, inspect cylinder mounts and shields, replace high-pressure fuel filters and coalescing filter elements, defuel/depressurize as needed, and document the inspection.

Diagnose and repair a driveability or fuel-system fault on a CNG/LNG or biodiesel-fueled truck in a shop bay: e.g., leaking pressure regulator, faulty high-pressure solenoid or fuel-rail sensor, plugged/gelled biodiesel filters, water in fuel, corroded fittings; involves scan-tool diagnosis, removing corroded fasteners and lines, replacing parts, priming, leak-test and road test.

High-voltage service on a hybrid transit bus or hybrid truck in the shop: de-energize and lock out the HV system, insulation/isolation testing, replace a battery module or pack, inverter, HV cable or cooling-loop component, refill and bleed coolant, torque terminals to spec, then reset and verify with the OEM diagnostic tool.

Bench-level component work in the shop after removal from the vehicle: rebuild or replace a CNG pressure regulator or high-pressure valve assembly, service injectors on a dual-fuel engine, or clean/replace a fuel pump, then bench-test/pressure-test before reinstallation.

Road call or on-site repair of an alternative-fuel vehicle: a CNG bus down at a curbside stop, a hybrid truck stalled in a customer yard or roadside; mobile technician works in traffic, weather and poor lighting with a service truck's tools to diagnose and either repair or make the vehicle towable.

tasks.label: Measure vehicle emissions to determine whether they are within acceptable limits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diesel smoke-opacity test on a heavy truck or transit bus in the fleet shop bay: technician clamps/inserts the opacity meter probe on a vertical stack or under-body tailpipe (heights, diameters and stack shapes vary by unit), climbs into the cab, warms the engine, performs SAE J1667-style snap accelerations while the meter captures peak opacity, then compares the reading to the state/fleet limit and prints the report.

Scan-tool / OBD emissions compliance check (e.g., California Clean Truck Check HD-OBD test, readiness monitors, emissions DTCs, NOx-sensor and DPF/DEF live data): technician reaches into the cab, plugs the tool into the diagnostic connector under the dash or in the kick panel, keys on and idles the engine, captures the data and judges whether the aftertreatment system is within limits.

Post-repair verification after aftertreatment or fuel-system work (DPF/DOC/SCR replacement, EGR, injector work, forced regen): technician runs the engine through idle and loaded rpm points in the shop while watching opacity or 5-gas analyzer output plus upstream/downstream NOx sensor values, confirming emissions are back within spec before releasing the unit.

Scheduled emissions test at an inspection lane — a state/agency heavy-duty lane or a fleet's own dedicated test lane: vehicle is driven onto the marked lane, probe inserted into the tailpipe, prescribed idle/2500-rpm or loaded-mode gas-analyzer or opacity procedure executed, pass/fail recorded against the regulatory limit (includes CNG buses and medium-duty diesels).

Field check outside the shop: a driver reports a smoking bus or truck, and the mechanic takes a portable opacity meter or gas analyzer to the yard, customer site or roadside, sets it up on uneven pavement in whatever weather, runs the engine and decides whether the unit exceeds limits and must be pulled from service.

tasks.label: Follow green operational practices involving conservation of water or energy or reduction of solid waste.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fleet/dealer shop bay, PM service on a Class 8 truck or transit bus: mechanic drains used engine oil, coolant, hydraulic and gear fluids into drain pans/evacuation units and transfers them into the shop's bulk used-oil and used-coolant recycling tanks without spills, so fluids are recycled rather than landfilled or sewered.

Shop floor and yard: mechanic segregates the solid waste from a job — drained oil filters into the filter drum, scrap steel/aluminum parts into the metal bin, cardboard boxes to the baler, used batteries onto the battery pallet, casings/cores to the core rack, tires to the tire stack, general trash to the dumpster — keeping streams uncontaminated.

Wash bay / parts-cleaning station: mechanic cleans a chassis, engine or removed components using water-conserving methods — closed-loop aqueous parts washer, reclaimed wash water, trigger-shutoff wands — rather than free-running hoses, and keeps rinse water in the reclaim loop instead of the storm drain.

Energy-conservation practices through a shift in the shop: shutting down air compressors, welders, lifts, battery chargers and bay lighting when not in use, keeping bay doors closed in heating season, and minimizing unnecessary engine idling during diagnostics and warm-ups.

Regulated/hazardous waste handling: recovering A/C refrigerant with a recovery machine, decanting used antifreeze and solvent for recycling, labeling and dating satellite accumulation containers, keeping absorbents and spill kits used correctly, and staging drums for the licensed hauler.

Mobile/roadside service call: mechanic performs a repair on the shoulder or at a customer yard, catches drained fluids and used filters in portable containment, and hauls the waste back to the shop instead of leaving it on site.

tasks.label: Operate valve-grinding machines to grind and reset valves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Complete valve job on a removed heavy-duty diesel cylinder head in a truck/bus shop machine area: mechanic cleans carbon off used valves, refaces each on the valve grinder, grinds/cuts the seats, laps, gauges margin thickness, stem wear and valve recession, discards out-of-spec valves, then resets the valves in the head with new stem seals, springs, retainers and keepers and vacuum/solvent-tests each seat for sealing.

Batch refacing operation: a tray of same-type used valves from one or several diesel heads is presented at the valve refacing/grinding machine; operator dresses the wheel, sets the face angle, chucks and grinds each valve face and stem tip to spec, gauges them, pulls bent or thin-margin rejects, and returns the finished set for assembly.

Valve seat reconditioning in the cylinder head on a seat grinder or seat-and-guide machine in the shop: head clamped and leveled on the fixture, pilots set in the guides, each seat ground/cut to specified angle, width and concentricity (occasionally after guide replacement), then checked with dye or a vacuum tester.

Resetting the valves after grinding: valve lash/clearance adjustment on the diesel engine (in-chassis in a fleet service bay or on an engine stand) — bar the engine to each cylinder's setting position, set intake and exhaust clearance with feeler gauge or dial indicator on the rocker adjusting screw, torque the locknut, recheck.

Field or marine work: grinding/lapping valves and seats on site with portable equipment — a bus in a fleet yard, a mobile service truck, or a marine diesel cylinder head in a vessel engine room — with improvised setup, poor lighting and no shop fixturing.
