roles.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul farm machinery and vehicles, such as tractors, harvesters, dairy equipment, and irrigation systems.

tasks.label: Reassemble machines and equipment following repair, testing operation and making adjustments, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/independent farm-equipment shop: after an engine or powertrain overhaul on a tractor or combine, the tech reassembles the unit — bearings and shims measured to spec, pistons, gaskets and seals, head torqued in sequence to torque-plus-angle, injectors, harness and hoses routed and clipped, accessories hung — then runs it on a stand or in the machine, checks pressures/leaks/valve lash and timing, and adjusts as needed. Mixed makes, models and decades of vintage.

Shop bench work: reassembly of a rebuilt subassembly — hydraulic cylinder resealed, gear pump, valve block, water pump, starter/alternator — installing elastomeric seals and O-rings into grooves, torquing glands/caps, then pressure/leak or bench test and setting relief or pressure adjustments before the unit goes back on the machine.

Field or farmyard service call during season: reassembling combine, header, baler or planter components (concaves, feeder chains, belts, sprockets, gearboxes, knotters, row units) after a repair, working on uneven ground in dust/mud with a service truck, then running the machine under load, listening/observing, and adjusting tension, clearance and timing.

Shop reassembly of tractor structure and subsystems after a repair: refitting cab or hood, fenders, wheels/duals, PTO and three-point hitch components, fuel/DEF plumbing, wiring harnesses and sensors; then function test (electrical, hydraulics, PTO engagement, diagnostic scan) and adjustment of linkages, sensors and clearances.

On-farm dairy or irrigation equipment: reassembling vacuum/milk pumps, pulsators, milking unit clusters, feed auger drives, or a center-pivot gearbox/drive and sprinkler package after repair, in a parlor, equipment room or open field; then running the system and adjusting vacuum level, pulsation rate, alignment or pressure regulation.

tasks.label: Maintain, repair, and overhaul farm machinery and vehicles, such as tractors, harvesters, and irrigation systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled preventive service on a customer tractor or combine in a dealership service bay: engine oil and filter change, fuel/hydraulic/air filters, greasing dozens of zerks, checking and topping fluids, inspecting belts, hoses and drivelines, torquing wheel lugs, running diagnostic software and clearing codes, writing up findings.

Major overhaul/rebuild in the dealership or independent shop: pulling and splitting a tractor for a clutch or transmission job, tearing down a diesel engine or final drive, measuring wear on used and contaminated parts, cleaning, deciding what to replace, reassembling to torque/clearance spec, and test-running under load.

In-season emergency field service call: technician drives a service truck to a muddy field or farmyard where a combine, planter or sprayer has failed; diagnoses on the spot and replaces a burst hydraulic hose, seized bearing, broken chain, belt, knife section or sensor, working under the machine on uneven ground in heat, dust or rain.

Irrigation system repair on the farm: rebuilding or swapping a center-pivot drive gearbox or motor, repairing leaking spans, replacing sprinkler heads and pressure regulators, fixing collector-ring and control-panel wiring, or servicing a well/booster pump and PTO drive, all outdoors in a crop field.

Electrical/electronic and precision-ag diagnosis and repair, mostly in the shop bay: tracing a wiring harness fault or intermittent short, replacing an ECU, CAN sensor, alternator or GPS/guidance component, calibrating and updating controller software, and verifying the fix on the machine.

sources.system: RoboTire automated tire-changing system

sources.transferJustification: Related task: wheel/tire replacement in an automotive service bay. It does NOT transfer to farm-equipment maintenance/repair: the workpiece is a standardized car wheel presented in a purpose-built bay, there is no fault diagnosis, no fastener corrosion/seizure handling on heavy machinery, no fluid service, and no disassembly/reassembly of powertrain or hydraulic assemblies.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive tire/wheel service. sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated disassembly of used, variant-rich mechanical/electrical assemblies. It bounds what is possible for machinery teardown at E1: even with the workpiece fixtured in a dedicated cell, complete autonomous disassembly is not achieved, and repair additionally requires diagnosis and reassembly.

sources.system: Industrial humanoid deployments (Figure, Agility Digit, Apptronik Apollo)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose mobile manipulation in factories. Cited to show the most flexible embodied systems deployed today handle totes and parts presentation, not tool-based diagnosis, fastener work and assembly/disassembly on heavy machinery, so they cannot substantiate any instance of this task.

tasks.label: Examine and listen to equipment, read inspection reports, and confer with customers to locate and diagnose malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership service shop bay: a tractor, combine or self-propelled sprayer is in for a customer complaint (loses hydraulic power when hot, engine surge, intermittent electrical fault). Tech reads the work order and prior inspection report, questions the customer, connects the OEM diagnostic laptop, starts and runs the machine, listens for knocks/whines, hooks pressure gauges to test ports, cycles controls, traces circuits, and names the failed component.

Emergency field service call during planting or harvest: service truck to a field or farmyard, machine down in mud, dust and heat with poor light and no fixed layout. Tech interviews the operator about symptoms, walks around the machine, listens while it runs, crawls under to find leaks or broken drives, meters circuits, and diagnoses on the spot.

Seasonal or pre-delivery multi-point inspection in the dealer shop: work through the OEM checklist on a tractor, combine or planter - fluids and oil samples, belts, hoses, bearings, tires, linkages, lights and electronics - run it up, review stored codes and the previous inspection report, and list existing faults and impending failures for the customer.

Specialty on-farm systems: diagnose a dairy milking system in the parlor during milking (vacuum pump, pulsators, receiver, plate cooler), a center-pivot irrigation machine in a wet field (gearbox noise, control panel, sprinkler pattern), or a grain dryer/auger - listening and observing while the system runs and conferring with the producer.

Bench diagnosis of a removed component or assembly in the shop: injection pump or injector set, hydraulic pump, engine or transmission on a stand - mount it on the test bench, drive it, measure and listen, and determine which element is out of spec or which internal part has failed.

sources.system: ANYbotics ANYmal X
sources.title: ANYmal X Tested for Autonomous Robot Inspections in Ex-zones at BASF
sources.claim: ANYmal X performs autonomous multi-sensor inspection missions (gauges, lever positions, thermal on tanks and pumps, pump frequency) at BASF's Ludwigshafen chemical plant - autonomous 'examine and listen' rounds on fixed assets in a structured industrial facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine condition-monitoring rounds. It substantiates autonomous sensing of running machinery (thermal/acoustic/visual) in an E2 facility, but only on preset routes over fixed assets, with no manipulation, no functional testing and no complaint-driven fault isolation, so it does not carry over to diagnosing an arbitrary malfunction on a customer's machine.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit and thermal/acoustic payloads

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot runs autonomous inspection rounds that read analog gauges and capture thermal and acoustic data, alerting on abnormal readings; Nestle Purina deployed it to automate thermal and acoustic ... on packaging lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acoustic/thermal anomaly detection on rotating plant equipment. It shows a robot can autonomously 'listen to equipment' and flag a failing bearing or leak in an E2 facility, but the output is an anomaly alert on a known fixed asset, not a located root cause of a reported fault on a mobile farm machine.

tasks.label: Dismantle defective machines for repair, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/independent shop: tearing down a major powertrain assembly on a tractor or combine (engine, transmission, final drive, hydro unit) — draining fluids, disconnecting wiring/hoses/linkages, splitting the machine, breaking loose corroded high-torque fasteners, slinging and lowering heavy castings onto stands, keeping parts and hardware organized for the rebuild; models and failure states vary machine to machine.

Shop bench teardown of a removed subassembly (hydraulic pump, planetary gearbox, PTO clutch pack, starter/alternator, injection pump): press/puller work, snap rings, seals, shims, torqued and sometimes seized or rounded fasteners, judging what is reusable while dismantling without damaging good parts.

On-farm field repair: dismantling a broken machine where it failed — combine header drive, baler knotter/pickup, planter row unit, mower conditioner — in mud, crop residue, dust or rain, on uneven ground, with only a service-truck kit of hand tools, often in a hurry during harvest or planting.

Shop access work: removing wheels/duals, hoods, side shields, belt guards, floor plates, cab panels, guards, hoses and lines to expose the defect — varied fastener types and locations across machine makes, heavy awkward panels and wheels, rust and thread damage common.

On-farm dairy or irrigation equipment: dismantling a center-pivot gearbox or drive, a well/booster pump, or milking-system vacuum pump and receiver plumbing in a farmyard, pump house or parlor — confined access, water/manure contamination, corroded fasteners.

sources.system: Daisy (Apple disassembly robot)
sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy is a deployed, purpose-built disassembly line robot that autonomously takes apart used iPhones at high rate, but only 23 known consumer-phone models in a dedicated facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of used/defective products. Transfer to farm machinery fails — Daisy handles palm-sized, fixed-geometry electronics on a bespoke line, not multi-hundred-kilogram cast-iron assemblies with seized fasteners, hoses and wiring on varied machine models.

sources.system: Molg robotic microfactory (with ABB robots)
sources.title: ABB Robotics and US start-up Molg tackle data center e-waste with robotic microfactories
sources.claim: Molg's ABB-based robotic microfactory autonomously disassembles laptops, servers and industrial electronics inside a purpose-built cell; it is the closest commercial autonomous disassembly of 'machines' and is confined to flat, screw-fastened electronics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous teardown of end-of-life equipment in a fixtured cell. Objects (rack servers, laptops, machine screws) are orders of magnitude lighter and more standardized than tractor powertrains; forces, fluids, corrosion and model variety of farm machinery are outside its demonstrated envelope.

sources.system: AUTOREMAN robotic disassembly research platform
sources.title: Disassembly demonstration key to robotic remanufacturing – The Robot Report
sources.claim: Academic state of the art on robotic disassembly of mechanical cores (engine-type components) is fundamental research on single operations such as pin removal; disassembly of returned cores is unsolved because of product variety and unknown component condition.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the related task (robotic disassembly for remanufacturing of engine-type components); it shows the capability is at the level of isolated primitives, not whole-machine teardown.

sources.system: DeMoBat robot-based disassembly demonstration platform (KUKA robots)
sources.title: New technologies for the disassembly of electric vehicle batteries and motors – Fraunhofer IPA
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IPA's DeMoBat work on disassembling EV batteries and electric motors — the heaviest mechanical assemblies with robotic teardown work — remains a robot-based demonstration platform, with tooling still being developed to grip parts and loosen screws.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic dismantling of a heavy bolted mechanical/electrical assembly in a fixtured cell — the nearest analogue in mass and fastener type to a tractor subassembly. It is a demonstrator on one known pack design, so it does not substantiate completion of varied farm-machine teardown.

sources.system: Fraunhofer automated electronics disassembly demonstrator
sources.title: Automated Electronics Disassembly – Fraunhofer
sources.claim: Automated electronics disassembly research reports that rusty or stripped screws and deformed components defeat robotic unfastening — the condition routinely encountered on defective farm machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic unfastening during teardown; establishes that degraded fastener condition, the norm on defective farm equipment, is outside current robotic disassembly capability even in a structured cell.

sources.system: RoboTire
sources.title: From Manual to Robots: RoboTire's Impact on the Tire Shop Floor – Tire Review
sources.claim: RoboTire is a shop-installed robotic cell whose vision system locates a passenger car's lug nuts and removes them and the wheel, then torques nuts to spec — an autonomous unbolting/removal task in a human service facility, limited to car wheels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal of bolted-on components in a vehicle service bay. Transfer to farm equipment is only partial — it is engineered for standardized passenger-car wheel geometry and does not remove guards, panels, hoses or heavy agricultural wheels, so it cannot complete the access-work instance.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly and remanufacturing automation (review)
sources.title: Robotic disassembly and remanufacturing automation | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: Survey literature on robotic disassembly notes it is common in machine repair and maintenance but is hard to robotise because of variability in the condition of returned products.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses the related task of robotic disassembly in machine repair and maintenance, confirming no fielded system covers it.

tasks.label: Clean and lubricate parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/independent farm-equipment shop, teardown for repair or overhaul: technician degreases and cleans removed components (gearboxes, hydraulic valves, bearings, housings, engine parts) caked with oil, grease, chaff and field dirt using a solvent/aqueous parts washer, wire brush, scraper and compressed air, then dries them ready for inspection and reassembly.

Shop bench reassembly: technician packs bearings with grease, coats splines, seals, O-rings and pins with the specified lubricant, applies anti-seize to fasteners, and oils chains and slides on subassemblies before installing them back on the machine.

Scheduled PM/inspection service in the shop service bay on a tractor, combine or baler: technician locates and wipes 30-60 grease zerks (driveline, pivots, U-joints, hidden points under the chassis), pumps grease until purge, replaces plugged fittings, oils chains, and blows out radiator screens and air filters.

Shop wash bay: pressure-washing / steam-cleaning a mud-, manure- and crop-residue-caked machine or large subassembly (combine head, planter row units, undercarriage) before or after service so components can be worked on and inspected.

On-farm field service call during planting or harvest: technician cleans and lubricates the machine where it sits in the field or farmyard - blowing chaff off screens and bearings, wiping and greasing fittings on a combine or sprayer - on uneven ground, in dust, heat or mud, with the machine parked as found.

tasks.label: Repair or replace defective parts, using hand tools, milling and woodworking machines, lathes, welding equipment, grinders, or saws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/independent farm-equipment shop service bay: remove and replace a defective major component on a tractor, combine, sprayer or loader (hydraulic pump, injector, water pump, alternator, clutch pack, final-drive or gearbox) using hand tools, impact wrenches, torque wrenches, hoists and jack stands. Machine is a used, dirty unit of variable make/model; fasteners may be seized or corroded; fluid lines, wiring harnesses and shields must be removed and reinstalled.

In-field or farmyard emergency repair during planting/harvest: replace broken parts on a combine, planter, baler or sprayer where the machine sits (mud, stubble, dust, uneven ground, poor light, weather), working from a service truck with hand tools, portable welder and torch; often improvising to get the machine running the same day.

Wear/consumable part replacement on implements and machines, in the shop or farmyard: sickle sections and guards, plow points and sweeps, chains and sprockets, belts, hoses, bearings, tires/wheels — bolted, riveted or press-fit components on the assembled implement.

Bench weld/torch/fabrication repair in the shop of a component already removed from the machine: welding a cracked bracket, frame member, tank or implement arm; gouging/cutting out cracks with a torch or saw; building up (hardfacing) worn surfaces and grinding the repair smooth; fabricating a replacement piece from plate or tube.

Bench machining of a replacement or reconditioned part in the shop machine-tool area: turning a shaft, bushing or spacer on the lathe, milling a keyway or bracket, cutting stock on the saw, grinding/resurfacing a worn part to spec so it fits the mating component.

On-site repair of stationary farm systems: dairy milking equipment (pumps, pulsators, vacuum lines), irrigation pump ends, center-pivot gearboxes and drivelines, grain augers and dryers — replacing defective parts in barns, pump houses and open fields, in confined, wet or dusty conditions.

sources.system: Optomec CS-250 LENS + Acme Manufacturing MRO blade-tip repair robotic work cell
sources.title: Optomec and Acme Manufacturing Showcase First Automated Workcell for Adaptive Repair of Turbine Parts at Formnext
sources.claim: Optomec and Acme Manufacturing sell a fully automated, turnkey work cell that repairs worn/damaged metal parts (aviation compressor blades) by robotic grinding, laser-clad weld build-up and robotic post-clad finishing, with automatic tool-path adjustment to each part's as-found wear and distortion; capacity 85,000 blades/year.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated repair of worn/defective metal parts by weld deposition and grinding. Transfers to a farm mechanic's bench repair of a worn or cracked component because the process chain (cut/grind out the defect, weld build-up, grind to spec) and precision demands are the same or higher; the part must be fixtured on a pallet in the cell.

sources.system: Path Robotics Intelligent Welding Cells / Obsidian
sources.title: Intelligent Welding Cells | Path Robotics
sources.claim: Path Robotics' Intelligent Welding Cells use the Obsidian AI model with vision-driven seam finding and path ... to weld high-mix parts held in heavy-duty positioners inside a fenced cell, without part programming and tolerating imperfect fit-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous arc welding of steel weldments in high-mix job-shop production. Transfers to bench weld repair/fabrication of farm-implement steel parts (comparable steel sections, fit-up tolerance and weld quality) provided the workpiece is fixtured in the cell's positioner.

sources.system: Path Robotics autonomous welding system with ALM positioners

sources.claim: Path Robotics' autonomous AI welding system has been deployed with customers in production, including TYCROP with ALM heavy-duty positioners, and a shipbuilder (LAD Services).

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-tended CNC turning/milling of small-batch and one-off parts. sources.system: Automated Tire SmartBay

tasks.label: Test and replace electrical components and wiring, using test meters, soldering equipment, and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership service bay: tractor or combine brought in with a no-crank, no-start or charging complaint. Tech does battery load and voltage-drop tests with a meter, checks starter, alternator, ground straps and cables, then removes and replaces the failed unit (heavy, bolted, cable-lugged) and retests the system.

On-farm field service call: machine down in a field, fencerow or farmyard with an intermittent electrical fault or rodent-chewed harness. Tech works off a wiring diagram, back-probes connectors with a meter in awkward positions, cuts out damaged wire, solders/heat-shrinks or crimps splices, reloams and secures the harness, retests in dirt, wind and variable light.

Shop repair of machine electronics on a combine, sprayer or planter: diagnostic software plus meter checks isolate a failed sensor, switch, solenoid, relay or control module; tech removes shields/panels, unplugs weather-pack connectors in tight cavities, installs the new component, routes and secures wiring, then calibrates and verifies.

Dairy parlor, grain-handling or irrigation-system electrical work on the customer's premises: test and replace motor contactors, overloads, pressure/level/flow switches, pivot collector rings and panel wiring; wet, dusty, manure-laden or livestock-occupied, layout differs at every site.

Bench work in the shop: making up replacement leads, pigtails and harness sections  crminp or solder terminals onto cut and stripped wire, seat terminals in connector bodies, apply heat-shrink, then continuity/function test the finished lead before it goes on the machine.

Shop lighting and accessory electrical work: test and replace work lights, beacons, cab switches, fuses and relays on a tractor; run and secure new wire through cab and frame, splice into existing circuits, check current draw and function.

sources.system: Kurabo Kurassem-WH / Kurassem-SR (KURASENSE 3D vision robot package)
sources.title: Robot Package (Kurassem) Kurassem-WH (Wire Harness Manufacturing) / SR (Automatic Soldering) | KURASENSE
sources.claim: Commercial vision-guided robot cell that pulls a single wire from a bundle, crimps a terminal, and inserts it into a connector in about 10 seconds, with soldering and electrical characteristic testing offered as customizations - i.e., building and testing terminated leads inside a fixtured factory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wire-harness manufacturing/soldering in a factory cell. It transfers to the mechanic's bench sub-task of making up and testing replacement leads - same objects (stranded wire, crimp terminals, connector bodies, solder joints) and same precision - but only when wire and connector are presented fixtured, as in the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Nissan / University of Tennessee robotic wiring-harness assembly robot
sources.developer: Nissan North America with University of Tennessee senior design team
sources.title: Robotic Wiring Harness Assembly: Nissan's Automation Breakthrough
sources.claim: Industrial robots programmed with a vision/insertion algorithm autonomously insert delicate wires into connector cavities, including a re-grip and second push to guarantee full seating - the terminating step of harness build.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive wire-harness assembly. Terminal/wire insertion into connectors is the same manipulation a technician performs when repinning or building a replacement lead; demonstrated only on fixtured parts presented to the robot in a cell.

sources.system: Eureka Robotics force-controlled connector insertion (Eureka 3D camera + robot)
sources.title: Automated Connector Insertion in Automotive Wire Harness Assembly
sources.claim: Force-controlled robotic mating of automotive wire-harness connectors using a 3D camera and force-torque feedback, in an industrial cell where the mating connector is presented on a slider.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connector mating in harness assembly. Plugging and unplugging locking electrical connectors is a core motion of electrical component replacement; the demonstration is confined to a fixtured cell with parts presented in known poses.

sources.system: Automated electrical cable harness testing system (modular automated test rig)
sources.developer: Ball et al., published in Robotics (MDPI)
sources.title: Automation of Electrical Cable Harnesses Testing
sources.claim: An implemented automated system for continuity/insulation testing of electrical cable harnesses, evaluated on actual products, showing that harness electrical testing can be executed by machine rather than by a technician with a meter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated harness continuity/insulation testing. It covers the 'test with meters' element of the bench instance for harnesses docked to a purpose-built test fixture; it does not extend to probing circuits on an assembled machine.

tasks.label: Tune or overhaul engines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership service bay: in-frame or out-of-frame major overhaul of a large agricultural diesel engine (tractor/combine). Technician removes hood/cab or pulls the engine, tears it down, cleans and measures cylinders, bearings and crank, replaces liners, pistons, rings, bearings, gaskets and seals, torques to spec in sequence, sets valve lash and injection timing, then run-in and load tests.

Dealership/independent shop tune and performance restoration on a modern electronic diesel: diagnose with service tool, replace injectors, fuel and air filters, turbo or EGR components, check compression/blow-by, adjust valve lash, flash ECU calibration, then verify on PTO dyno or under load.

Field service call at a farm during planting or harvest: tractor, combine or sprayer engine misfires, smokes, loses power or will not start. Technician works from a service truck in a farmyard, machine shed or muddy field, in wind/heat/dust, diagnoses, replaces injectors/filters/sensors, bleeds fuel, adjusts, and test-runs the machine.

Bench work in the shop on small gas or small diesel engines from irrigation pumps, generators, augers, skid units and utility vehicles: carburetor rebuild, plugs and ignition, compression/leak-down test, ring-and-valve overhaul, valve lapping, reassembly and test run.

On-site partial overhaul of a machine too large or too immobile to bring in: head gasket, cylinder head, liner or injector-pump work on a combine or self-propelled sprayer at the customer's farm, using a service truck, portable lift and improvised staging on uneven ground.

sources.system: Comau automated range-extender engine assembly line (Li Auto)
sources.title: Automated Line Assembles 'Range Extender' Engines for EVs | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Automated engine assembly lines with vision-guided cobots build NEW engines (spark plug and connecting-rod cap installation, head and piston lines) in a fenced/structured plant line; this is assembly of clean new parts in fixtures, not teardown, wear measurement or reassembly of a used engine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = new-engine assembly. It shares reassembly motions (threading plugs, torquing caps) but not the instance as a whole: parts are new, dimensionally known and fixtured, with no diagnosis, no removal of seized/corroded hardware, no wear measurement and no parts-selection decisions, so it does not transfer to tuning or overhauling a used farm engine.

sources.system: Industrial cylinder-head robotic assembly cell
sources.title: Industrial Cylinder Heads Assembly Automation | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: Robotic cylinder-head assembly cells are commercially built and run as fenced automation cells with conveyor infeed, vision part identification, robotic gluing, closed-loop torque tightening and press-fit, again only for new production parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = cylinder-head sub-assembly on a production line. Transfer fails for overhaul because the cell handles freshly machined, identical heads presented by conveyor, whereas overhaul begins with a dirty, worn, variably damaged core requiring inspection-driven decisions.

sources.system: Cat Reman engine remanufacturing (Corinth, MS facility)
sources.title: Cat Reman Engine Remanufacturing: First Steps | Cat | Caterpillar
sources.claim: Industrial engine overhaul/remanufacturing at scale is still performed by skilled human technicians who disassemble, clean, inspect and salvage the dirty core; automation in the plant is used for cleaning, machining and material deposition, not for the teardown-inspect-rebuild sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = industrial engine overhaul, essentially identical to the shop-overhaul instance. It shows the state of practice is manual skilled labor even inside a purpose-built plant, i.e. no robotic system completes the whole overhaul.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly research systems (UR10e unscrewing cells, ease-of-robotic-disassembly metric)
sources.developer: academic (multiple, incl. Univ. of Birmingham / ScienceDirect authors)
sources.title: Ease of robotic disassembly metric and information for digital product passports in flexible remanufacturing systems - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed work as of 2025 states that robotising disassembly of end-of-life products remains unsolved because of corrosion, rust and missing parts; demonstrations are limited to single operations such as unscrewing on lab specimens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic disassembly for remanufacturing, the teardown half of an engine overhaul. It establishes the negative: even fixtured, used assemblies are not reliably disassembled autonomously today.

sources.system: Rolls-Royce remote boreblending robot
sources.title: Rolls-Royce is Robotizing Jet-Engine Maintenance | American Machinist
sources.claim: The most advanced in-situ engine repair robots (Rolls-Royce boreblending for compressor-blade repair in an MRO setting) are remotely controlled by specialist engineers rather than autonomous, and address a single machining operation rather than a full overhaul.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = in-situ engine repair. Transfer fails on autonomy (continuous remote control by an expert) and scope (blade blending only), so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of a tune or overhaul.

sources.system: Humanoid robots in industrial manufacturing (Atlas, Optimus, Figure class)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Industrial Manufacturing: What They Can (and Can't) Do in 2026
sources.claim: As of 2026 humanoid robots that might plausibly use human hand tools in a service bay are limited to a handful of pilot sites doing narrow material-handling and simple assembly tasks, with reliability below traditional industrial robots; no reported deployment performs vehicle or engine repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = general-purpose factory manipulation. It bounds the state of the art: no cited humanoid performs multi-hour diagnostic, teardown and rebuild work with hand tools, so no transfer to engine overhaul exists.

tasks.label: Drive trucks to haul tools and equipment for on-site repair of large machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Highway/rural service call: technician loads the service truck at the dealership and drives 20-60 miles on state highways and two-lane county roads (often gravel the last miles) to a customer's farmstead, then pulls into the yard/shop area and parks beside the broken machine. Mixed traffic, weather, livestock/deer, directions given by phone or a GPS pin.

Field call: technician drives the service truck off pavement through an unmarked field entrance, across stubble, mud, ruts, terraces and waterways, to a combine or tractor stopped at an arbitrary point in the field, frequently at night during harvest, and positions the truck alongside it.

Truck-and-trailer haul: pulling a gooseneck/lowboy with heavy service equipment (portable welder, compressor, hydraulic press, jack stands) or towing a disabled tractor/implement over public roads and gravel approaches; backing the trailer into a farm lot and loading/unloading with ramps or a winch.

Local parts and tool run: short trips on town/city streets and rural blacktop between the dealership, a parts supplier or machine shop, and an ongoing job site; congestion, stop signs, parking, then unloading the parts at the site.

Moves on institution-controlled premises: repositioning the service truck within the dealership yard/shop apron, or driving through a dairy, feedlot, grain elevator or co-op yard on established lanes to spot the truck next to the equipment being serviced.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for hauling (autonomous Cat 789D/793F/797F haul trucks)
sources.title: Cat" MineStar" Command for hauling manages the autonomous ecosystem
sources.claim: Cat MineStar Command for hauling runs fully autonomous mining trucks that haul loads point-to-point over unpaved site haul roads, day and night, at dozens of customer mine sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous haulage of material on unpaved mine roads. It transfers to driving a truck loaded with tools/equipment to a machine on a controlled worksite - same vehicle class, unpaved and changing terrain, dust and darkness, dispatch to assigned destinations and spotting on arrival.

sources.system: Kodiak Driver driverless trucks operated by Atlas Energy Solutions
sources.title: Kodiak Announces Delivery of Two Additional Customer-Owned and -Operated Driverless Trucks to Atlas; Launches Driverless Service Up To 24/7
sources.claim: Customer-owned driverless class-8 tractor-trailers with the Kodiak Driver haul ... from a load-out to customer well sites across the Permian Basin with nobody in the cab, up to 24/7.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless hauling of a loaded trailer to remote worksites over an industrial site's road network. Same driving function as hauling tools/equipment to a machine at a remote site, including trailer handling and rough unpaved approaches.

sources.system: Kodiak Driver driverless trucks (Atlas Permian operation)
sources.title: Groundbreaking 2025 Milestone: Kodiak Driverless Trucks Revolutionize Permian Oilfield Logistics
sources.claim: The Kodiak/Atlas driverless operation runs on private, dirt lease roads inside the oilfield using pre-mapped routes; public-highway driverless operation was still ahead of it.
sources.transferJustification: Documents the environment of the decisive system: an operator-controlled network of dirt lease roads, i.e. a structured industrial site rather than open public road networks or untracked fields.

sources.system: Aurora Driver (Peterbilt 579 / International LT)
sources.title: Aurora Expands Driverless Trucking Service from Fort Worth to El Paso
sources.claim: Aurora runs commercial driverless class-8 trucks on public interstate corridors (Fort Worth-Houston, Fort Worth-El Paso, later Phoenix) terminal-to-terminal, surpassing 100,000 driverless miles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a heavy truck on public roads. It covers the highway leg of a service call, but the operating domain is mapped interstate corridors between purpose-built terminals, not rural county roads, farm driveways or fields.

sources.system: Gatik Autonomous Delivery Network (freight-only box trucks)
sources.title: Autonomous Trucking at Scale | Gatik Deploys Driverless Fleet
sources.claim: Gatik operates freight-only driverless box trucks making daily commercial deliveries on public roads over fixed, pre-mapped middle-mile routes between fixed customer sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless goods hauling on public streets. Shows repeatable point-to-point cargo runs, but only on fixed pre-mapped routes with fixed loading/unloading endpoints, unlike a service call to a different farm each time.

sources.system: Seegrid Tow Tractor S7 AMR
sources.title: Seegrid Tow Tractor S7 Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR)
sources.claim: Seegrid autonomous tow tractors haul heavy cart loads (up to 10,000 lb) point-to-point across industrial facilities, delivering parts to assembly lines and workstations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport of heavy material to a designated point of use inside a facility. Same function as hauling tools and equipment to a machine when the work occurs inside a structured, institution-controlled facility.

sources.system: Seegrid AMR fleet
sources.title: Seegrid AMRs Surpass 17 Million Autonomous Miles Driven in Customer Facilities
sources.claim: Seegrid's AMR fleet has accumulated over 17 million autonomous miles in real customer production facilities, evidencing sustained deployment rather than a demo.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment scale and reliability for the in-facility hauling evidence used at E2.

sources.system: Autonomous 9RX tractor with second-generation autonomy kit
sources.title: CES 2025 New Autonomous Machines Technology | John Deere US
sources.claim: John Deere's second-generation autonomy kit lets a 9RX tractor perform tillage unmanned in an open crop field, released in limited quantities from 2026; the operation is a pre-planned job inside a mapped field boundary.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned traversal of a crop field. It shows field-capable perception, but the machine is delivered and set up by an operator and follows a planned coverage job inside a mapped boundary, not ad-hoc navigation to a disabled machine.

tasks.label: Fabricate new metal parts, using drill presses, engine lathes, and other machine tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer/farm shop: mechanic turns a one-off replacement shaft, bushing, spacer or pin from bar stock on the engine lathe to match a worn or no-longer-available OEM part, measuring the old part with calipers/micrometer, facing, turning, boring and parting off, then test-fitting to the assembly.

Shop bench/drill press: mechanic lays out, center-punches and drills/reams bolt holes in steel plate or angle, taps threads and deburrs, producing a mounting plate, shim, spacer plate or repair piece for a tractor or implement.

Shop fabrication: cutting flat bar/angle/tube on the bandsaw or with plasma, drilling, grinding to fit and MIG-welding into a bracket, guard, hitch reinforcement or implement repair piece, finished to fit the machine.

Shop precision job: multi-operation part such as milling a keyway or flats, boring a housing to bearing fit, or building up and re-machining a worn shaft/spindle to tolerance on a mill or lathe, with fit verified against the mating component.

On-farm/in-field improvisation: machine is down in a field or the customer's own shed; the technician cuts, drills and welds a makeshift part from whatever stock is at hand using portable tools (grinder, torch, portable drill/mag drill) with no drawing and under time pressure to get the machine running.

sources.system: Hadrian automated precision machining factory (robotic CNC cells, Torrance CA)
sources.title: Report: Hadrian Business Breakdown & Founding Story | Contrary Research
sources.claim: Hadrian operates automated, software-driven precision machining factories in which robots load and tend CNC machines and software handles programming, machining and inspection, producing about 10,000 unique (one-off/low-volume) metal parts per month; human roles are largely reduced to placing the block of metal and starting the cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: machining one-off metal parts to print on CNC machine tools (turning, milling, drilling, inspection), the operations a farm-equipment mechanic performs on a lathe/mill/drill press, at tighter tolerances than farm parts require.

sources.system: Fastems FMS (robotic pallet-handling automation on CNC machining centers) at WALTER
sources.title: WALTER Automates High-Mix, Low-Volume CNC Manufacturing
sources.claim: Fastems flexible manufacturing systems automate high-mix, low-volume CNC machining with robotic pallet handling, allowing WALTER's shop to run unattended in lights-out mode with digitized work instructions and low failure rates.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates that milling/drilling of small-batch and one-off metal parts is completed with the workpiece fixtured on pallets and presented to the machine automatically, matching the drill-press/mill portions of this task.

sources.system: Fastems FMS with Okuma horizontal machining centers at L&R Precision Tooling
sources.title: Boosting Manufacturing Efficiency with Fastems Flexible Manufacturing Systems - L&R Precision Tooling, Inc.
sources.claim: A job shop's Fastems FMS with two loading stations, 52-pallet storage, three Okuma horizontal machining centers and built-in inspection runs lights-out to tight tolerances in exotic metals.
sources.transferJustification: Milling, drilling and boring of metal parts with automated presentation and in-cell inspection: the same operations and acceptance check (dimensional verification) as fabricating a bracket, plate or bored housing in a farm shop.

sources.system: CNC turning center with automatic bar feeder (Custom Tool, Cookeville TN)
sources.developer: Various machine tool/bar feeder builders (reported by Modern Machine Shop)
sources.title: The Unattended Effects of CNC Machine Shop Automation | Modern Machine Shop
sources.claim: Automatic bar feeders let CNC turning centers run unattended for extended periods, continuously feeding bar stock so turned components such as shafts and bushings are produced without an operator at the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the lathe portion of the task: turning shafts, bushings and pins from bar stock, with stock presented to the machine automatically, which is what the E1 counterfactual grants.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 and AF-1 autonomous robotic welding cells
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 autonomous welding cells scan each steel part, build a model on the fly and weld without programming or teach pendants; both are deployed in fabrication shops ... the AF-1 can pick, fit and weld ....
sources.transferJustification: Covers the weld-fabrication step of building a bracket/guard from cut steel stock; the cells handle variable, high-mix steel parts and imperfect fit-up, comparable to shop-fabricated farm implement pieces.

sources.system: Teqram EasyGrinder / EasyDebur with EasyEye vision system
sources.title: LEVELING UP // Job shops and midsized manufacturers gain a competitive foothold with the ability to access cost-effective, easy-to-use robots and cobots
sources.claim: Teqram's vision-guided EasyGrinder and EasyDebur robots, and its drilling and shot-blasting robots, work without programming: the EasyEye vision system detects part geometry, size and ... sequences and changes grippers and tools to suit the part.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the finishing/drilling operations of fabricating a metal part (deburring drilled plate, grinding cut edges) autonomously on varying one-off parts inside a robotic cell.

tasks.label: Repair bent or torn sheet metal.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/independent service shop: straighten a bent or dented large panel on a tractor or combine — hood, fender, side shield, grain-tank wall, cab panel — using pry bars, hammer and dolly, slide hammer/stud puller, hydraulic pulls and heat shrinking, then blend for paint. Damage geometry is unique to the machine; the technician judges by eye and feel how far to work the metal.

Shop weld repair of a crack or tear in a steel sheet-metal component removed from the machine and clamped to a bench or positioner (auger housing, grain tank panel, shield, hopper skin): grind the paint back, close the tear or weld a patch plate over it with MIG, dress the bead. Finish is functional rather than cosmetic.

In-season field or farmyard call: a torn sheet-metal panel on a machine down in the field is patched in place with a portable welder/generator — cut, fit and weld a plate over the tear so harvest can continue, working around the machine as it sits.

In-season field or farmyard call: bent sheet metal (shields, fender, feederhouse or hopper skin) is straightened in place with pry bars, hammer, come-along or torch heat, on the machine as found, in dirt, wind and daylight.

Shop fabrication and fitting of a replacement patch/section: cut out the rusted or torn area, cut a blank from flat stock, form it on a brake/rolls to match the panel contour, clamp and tack it into the damaged opening, weld out, grind flush and prep for paint.

Bench work on small removable pieces — guards, brackets, battery boxes, toolbox lids, step plates — bent back to shape in a vise, on an anvil or in a shop press, with hammer and heat as needed, then refitted to the machine.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 Robotic Welding Cells
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 autonomous welding cells scan parts, plan and execute welds without programming, and are commercially deployed in fabrication shops in the US and Canada — fenced industrial cells, i.e., purpose-built robotic work environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production/high-mix arc welding of steel parts. Transfers to repair welding of a torn steel farm-machine panel because the objects (mild-steel sheet and plate), the joint-finding problem (vision-located seam on a non-nominal part) and the required weld quality are comparable when the part is brought to the cell and fixtured.

sources.system: Path Robotics AF-1 Robotic Welding Cell
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The same product line includes a cell that picks, fits and welds parts without human intervention, indicating fit-up as well as welding is automated inside the cell for parts presented to it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fit-up and welding of nominal production parts; supports the tack/weld step of a patch repair once the patch and panel are presented, but does not cover forming a patch to a damaged panel's contour.

sources.system: Path Robotics welding AI (Obsidian) with ALM positioners at TYCROP
sources.title: Path Robotics and ALM Positioners Deliver Breakthrough Welding Automation for TYCROP
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AI welding system, paired with heavy positioners, is deployed on heavy, irregular, one-off parts in high-mix shops (trailers, construction equipment, agricultural chassis), adapting in real time to ... variation rather than running fixed programs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: welding heavy irregular high-mix steel weldments. Transfers to a one-off torn farm-equipment panel because the geometry is likewise non-repeating and located by scanning, and the weld sizes on sheet/plate steel are comparable.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics AI-powered finishing cells
sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics Unveils 100,000-Square-Foot AI Robotics Innovation Center in Carson
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' AI-driven robotic cells autonomously sand, grind, polish and blast high-mix parts of varied geometry, and are deployed at manufacturers such as Pierce Manufacturing — supporting the grind/dress step of a weld repair inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface finishing/grinding of varied parts in a robotic cell. Transfers to dressing a weld bead on a repaired steel panel: same abrasive tooling, similar force control and scan-then-plan approach on parts of varying geometry.

sources.system: Path Robotics Rove
sources.title: This autonomous welding robot may be the future of advanced manufacturing - Fast Company
sources.claim: Path Robotics' mobile welding robot Rove (arm on a Boston Dynamics quadruped) targets shipyards and construction-type sites, but as of mid-2026 it is in beta with market release planned for 2027 — no deployed mobile system performs weld repairs on machinery in the field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile field welding. Cited to show the state of the art for welding away from a fixed cell is pre-commercial beta, so it cannot substantiate completion of in-field sheet-metal repair.

tasks.label: Calculate bills according to record of repairs made, labor time, and parts used.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Install and repair agricultural irrigation, plumbing, and sprinkler systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-season field service call on a center pivot or lateral-move machine in standing crop: drive to the field, diagnose the fault (water spraying from a blown flex boot, plugged or broken sprinkler heads and drop hoses, leaking flange gasket, weeping drain valve, flat tower tire, oil-leaking or seized drive gearbox, electrical short in tower box), then replace or repair the affected parts on a machine standing in mud and wet crop, and re-pressurize and verify the pattern.

Installation of a new irrigation system or major component on a farm: setting the pivot point and its plumbing, erecting/aligning spans and drops, or trenching and laying buried PVC/poly mainline, gluing or fusing joints, installing valves, risers, hydrants, air vents and check valves, backfilling, then pressure-testing the line.

Pump-station, wellhead and farmstead plumbing work: pull and overhaul a centrifugal or vertical turbine pump (seals, impeller, bearings, packing), thread and fit steel pipe, replace foot valves, pressure tanks, pressure switches and filters, re-plumb suction/discharge and livestock or washdown water lines in an open-sided pump house or barn, then prime, start and set pressures.

Drip/micro-irrigation and solid-set sprinkler work in orchards, vineyards and row crops: locating and splicing punctured or rodent-chewed lateral lines among vines/trees and weeds, replacing emitters, micro-sprinklers, filters, flush and air-relief valves, repairing submain connections, flushing lines and checking distribution uniformity.

Bench work in the dealership/farm service shop on irrigation components brought in: tearing down and rebuilding pumps, center-pivot drive gearboxes, valves and pressure regulators; fabricating, cutting and threading pipe assemblies and testing them before return to the field.

sources.system: 360 RAIN
sources.title: Irrigation automation means no more cutting corners on farm fields - Agweek
sources.claim: 360 RAIN is a commercially offered autonomous in-field irrigation machine that navigates row crops on an RTK path and applies water and nutrients; it delivers water but performs no installation, fitting, or repair of irrigation plumbing hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest agricultural system operating in the same E3 field environment as irrigation service work; it substantiates autonomous mobility in crop fields only, and does not substantiate any diagnosis, disassembly, pipe-fitting or component replacement, so it cannot support completion of this task.

sources.system: Bluewhite autonomous tractor retrofit kit (with New Holland/CNH)
sources.title: New Holland, Bluewhite collaborate on autonomous orchard and vineyard solutions - The Packer
sources.claim: Bluewhite's retrofit autonomy kit makes conventional orchard and vineyard tractors driverless for field operations (spraying, mowing, hauling) and is sold through New Holland dealerships; it automates implement-pulling field passes, not plumbing installation or machine repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tractor field operations in the same orchard/vineyard settings where drip-irrigation service occurs. Transfer fails for this task because the kit only steers a tractor and actuates implements; it provides no manipulation of pipe, emitters, fittings or fasteners.

sources.system: Jaibot
sources.title: Jaibot Drilling Robot - Hilti USA
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a semi-automated construction ... installation trades; its actual work is marking and drilling anchor holes from BIM data on building sites, not assembling, sealing or repairing piping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic support for plumbing installation trades. Transfer fails because Jaibot drills overhead holes for hangers under operator setup inside finished buildings; it does not cut, join, seal, test or repair pipe, and is not shown outdoors on farms.

sources.system: Fraunhofer DeMoBat robotic disassembly cells (as reported in vision-guided dual-arm disassembly study)
sources.title: Vision-Guided Dual-Arm Humanoid Robotic Disassembly of End-of-Life 18650 Lithium-ion Battery Packs
sources.claim: Robotic disassembly of used assemblies for remanufacturing/repair remains a research activity: reported industrial-robot demonstrations remove bolts and cables from assemblies whose geometry is known in advance, and general disassembly under geometric uncertainty is still an open problem.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown/rebuild of used mechanical assemblies in a fixtured cell, the E1 counterfactual for shop overhaul of pumps and gearboxes. Transfer fails: demonstrations are lab-stage, single-product, and stop at disassembly of known geometry, with no worn-part inspection, replacement or reassembly to service quality.

roles.title: Mobile Heavy Equipment Mechanics, Except Engines
aliases: Heavy Equipment Field Service Tech (Heavy Equipment Field Service Technician)
Heavy Equipment Field Tech (Heavy Equipment Field Technician)
Heavy Equipment Service Technician (Heavy Equipment Service Tech)
Heavy Equipment Shop Tech (Heavy Equipment Shop Technician)

roles.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul mobile mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic equipment, such as cranes, bulldozers, graders, and conveyors, used in construction, logging, and mining.

tasks.label: Repair and replace damaged or worn parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field repair at a construction/road job site: a burst hydraulic hose, leaking cylinder, failed alternator/water pump, damaged wiring or sensor on an excavator, loader or dozer parked in dirt, mud or gravel; mechanic works off a service truck with jacks, cranes and hand tools in ambient weather, freeing seized and contaminated fasteners and returning the machine to service the same day.

Dealer or fleet shop service bay: major component removal and replacement on the machine — final drive, travel motor, hydraulic pump, transmission, radiator, swing bearing — using an overhead crane, stands, torque wrenches, draining fluids, breaking corroded bolts, shimming/aligning and re-torquing to spec, then testing.

Shop bench overhaul of a removed component: hydraulic cylinder reseal, pump/valve bank, starter, brake pack or gearbox — press out bearings/bushings, clean and inspect, measure wear, decide reuse vs. replace, replace worn parts and seals, reassemble to torque/clearance spec and pressure-test.

Undercarriage, running gear and wear parts in the shop or yard: replacing bucket teeth and adapters, cutting edges and wear plates, track chains, rollers, idlers and sprockets; pin-and-bushing turns on a track press; gouging and welding cracks or building up worn surfaces.

Routine small-part replacement in the shop or yard: filters, belts, hoses and fittings, batteries, lamps, mirrors, glass, air-conditioning parts, worn linkage pins and bushings on a variety of machine makes and models.

Mine, quarry or logging site change-out on rough ground: replacing a bucket cylinder, suspension strut, GET, drive shaft or haul-truck wheel assembly in the pit or on a hardstand, with a service crane or manipulator, in dust, heat and uneven footing.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly research platforms (Birmingham AUTOREMAN programme and related)
sources.developer: University of Birmingham / IEEE CASE authors
sources.title: Robotic disassembly and remanufacturing automation (IEEE)
sources.claim: Survey of robotic disassembly for remanufacturing/repair reports that disassembly of used machinery remains hard to robotise because returned products vary in condition and the manipulations require dexterity and complex contact handling.
sources.transferJustification: Disassembly of worn, used assemblies is the necessary first half of 'repair and replace damaged or worn parts'; the source states this step is not yet robotised for used products, which bounds capability on heavy-equipment repair.

sources.system: Object-centric disassembly (OCD) framework
sources.developer: academic (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Disassembly from scratch: An object-centric approach for robotic autonomous disassembly
sources.claim: State-of-the-art review accompanying a 2025 autonomous-disassembly method states that automation of robotic disassembly remains limited because of uncertainty in end-of-life products; the work itself is a laboratory framework on small assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Repair of worn machinery requires removing used, uncertain-condition parts; the cited autonomous work is confined to small lab assemblies, not multi-tonne fixtured heavy-equipment components.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial vehicle-service part-replacement robot is an autonomous tire-changing bay for passenger cars; its first generation still does not automate the full mounting, airing and balancing sequence, and the earlier RoboTire venture failed.
sources.transferJustification: Wheel/tire replacement is the simplest vehicle part-replacement task and the closest commercial analog; even here automation is partial and limited to light passenger vehicles in a purpose-built bay, not heavy-equipment component repair.

sources.system: Undercarriage roller/idler rebuilder (automatic welding rebuild machine)
sources.title: Undercarriage Track Repair & Rebuilding Equipment | JC-Hydraulic

tasks.label: Test mechanical products and equipment after repair or assembly to ensure proper performance and compliance with manufacturers' specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer/fleet service-shop functional test of a whole machine after a hydraulic or drivetrain repair (excavator, wheel loader, dozer): start the machine, cycle every implement and travel function, hook pressure/flow gauges to test ports, compare readings and cycle times to the service manual, watch repaired joints for leaks, verify no fault codes recur.

Bench/stand test of a repaired or rebuilt component or assembly before or after installation (hydraulic pump, control valve bank, cylinder, final drive, powershift transmission): mount on a test stand, run it up to rated speed/pressure/load, record flow, pressure, leakage and shift quality, and accept or reject against OEM specification.

Field test at a construction, logging or quarry job site after an on-site repair: operate the dozer/grader/excavator through real work cycles on the actual ground, check track/blade/implement response, drift, power under load, and listen and look for noise, smoke or leaks; conditions and terrain vary site to site.

Post-repair run check of a plant or mine conveyor / fixed material-handling system: belt restarted after idler, pulley or drive repair, then verify belt tracking, bearing and gearbox temperatures, noise and vibration on an inspection walk-down inside the processing facility.

Mobile crane, boom truck or aerial lift post-repair test: function-test boom, winch, swing and outriggers, verify load-moment indicator against the load chart, and perform a rigged proof/load test with certified test weights before returning the unit to service.

Travel/road test after brake, steering or drivetrain repair on a self-propelled unit (articulated dump truck, crane carrier, service truck): drive it on the yard, haul road or public road, check braking effort and pull, steering, shifting and warning lights against spec.

sources.system: Duerr x-road InLine roll, brake and ABS test stand
sources.title: Function checks in final assembly - Duerr
sources.claim: D"urr's InLine testing puts fully automated dynamic roll, brake and ABS function tests into vehicle final assembly; the conveyor delivers the vehicle and indexing pins fixture it, with no employee driving the vehicle onto the stand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line functional testing of a complete self-propelled vehicle after assembly. The O*NET task explicitly covers testing 'after repair or assembly'; the stand actuates drive and brake systems and grades results against specification in a purpose-built, fixtured cell, which is what a post-repair function test of a self-propelled machine requires.

sources.system: SuperFlow Axiline/Hicklin transmission dynamometers with PowerNet control
sources.title: Remanufacturing - SuperFlow

sources.claim: HORIBA's ADS EVO driving robot replaces the human driver in a chassis vehicle ..., executing standard test cycles repeatably.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled operation of a vehicle's pedals/controls through a prescribed test cycle in a test cell. A post-repair performance test also requires driving the machine through a defined sequence while instrumentation records conformance, so the actuation and cycle-execution capability transfers.

sources.system: Highland Hydraulic industrial-grade hydraulic test bench / YST380 excavator hydraulic repair test bench

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for hauling

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous driving, braking and manoeuvring of heavy mobile equipment on a controlled work site. sources.system: ANYmal legged inspection robot

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous condition verification of running conveyor equipment in an as-found processing plant.
