sources.system: Rocsys autonomous charging robot (M1)
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free robotaxi charging, raises $13M
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic arms autonomously locate a vehicle's port, open the flap and insert the connector in live port and depot environments, reporting a 99.9%+ plug-in success rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connection of a coupling to a port on a vehicle. Hooking a test/diagnostic line to a machine's quick-coupler test port is a comparable vision-guided insertion of a connector at comparable scale and tolerance, supporting the hook-up step of a bench or cell test.

tasks.label: Operate and inspect machines or heavy equipment to diagnose defects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer or fleet service bay: a customer complaint on an excavator/wheel loader (slow hydraulics, intermittent warning, drivetrain noise). Mechanic climbs in, starts the machine, cycles boom/stick/swing and travel functions, watches gauges and the service-tool laptop, listens and feels for cavitation, checks for leaks under load, and isolates the failing pump, valve, sensor or line.

Field service call on an active construction jobsite: a dozer or excavator is down in dirt/mud. Mechanic operates the machine where it sits to reproduce the symptom, walks around it, inspects undercarriage, hoses, linkage and electrical connections in weather, and determines the defect and whether it can be repaired on site.

Mine or quarry maintenance workshop / pit: a haul truck, shovel or production loader is brought in for a reported fault. Mechanic runs the machine through steering, brake, suspension and hydraulic function checks, road-tests it, and inspects while operating to localize the defect.

Fixed/portable conveyor system at a quarry, mine or processing plant: mechanic runs the belt and inspects drives, gearboxes, pulleys, idlers and belt condition (hot bearings, misalignment, belt damage, leaks) to identify the defect before shutdown repair.

Logging or remote off-road setting: feller buncher, skidder or forwarder in the woods (or farm/pipeline equipment in an open field). Mechanic operates the machine on uneven, cluttered ground to reproduce a hydraulic or drivetrain fault and inspects it in place.

Post-repair / pre-delivery functional test operation in the dealer or rental yard: mechanic operates the machine through its full range of functions, monitors instruments and listens/looks for leaks, abnormal noise or slow response, and certifies whether any defect remains.

sources.system: ANYmal (ANYbotics)
sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped has run fully autonomous inspection rounds at the Vigier Ciment plant since early 2025, covering 450+ checkpoints and finding real machine defects (cracked crusher foundation, bearing overheating, air leaks) that maintenance teams acted on.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous condition-inspection rounds on plant machinery. Transfers to inspecting conveyor/crusher drivetrains for defects — same class of rotating mechanical equipment, same thermal/acoustic/visual cues a mechanic uses, inside a controlled industrial facility.

sources.system: Spot + Orbit AIVI-Learning
sources.title: Boston Dynamics Spot uses DeepMind for machinery inspections
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot with Orbit AIVI-Learning (Gemini Robotics ER integration) autonomously inspects industrial assets including conveyor belt damage, sight glasses and gauges; several thousand Spot units patrol industrial sites globally.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous asset inspection rounds. Directly covers conveyor belt damage detection, the defect-finding part of the conveyor instance, in institution-controlled plants.

sources.system: Spot
sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Spot has been used on autonomous inspection routes collecting thermal condition and gauge data on pumps, motors and compressed-gas systems to support maintenance planning at industrial customer sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine machine-health inspection. Supports defect detection on fixed rotating equipment in structured facilities; it does not involve operating a machine's controls.

sources.system: Tessellate haul-truck inspection robot (MISA Vortex program)
sources.title: Automated Haul Truck Inspection by Tessellate Robotics | Groupe MISA
sources.claim: Tessellate Robotics is developing an autonomous mobile robot that inspects mining haul trucks during refuelling with visual, thermal and 3D sensing and generates a maintenance report; the project is still in prototyping/field-validation phases with a mining partner.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preventive walkaround inspection of mobile heavy equipment. It covers only static visual/thermal checks of a parked truck, not operating the machine or isolating a reported fault, and remains a pre-commercial prototype.

sources.system: ExACT autonomous excavator
sources.title: ExACT: An End-to-End Autonomous Excavator System Using Action Chunking With Transformers
sources.claim: A 21.5-tonne hydraulic excavator retrofitted with drive-by-wire can be actuated autonomously by a learned controller (ExACT), showing machine control of heavy-equipment hydraulics is feasible, though the work performed is excavation, not fault diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation of heavy-equipment hydraulics. It substantiates the 'operate' motion only; no evidence of perceiving symptoms or diagnosing a defect, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.system: UVeye Helios / Artemis / Atlas
sources.title: UVeye Expands AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Trucks, Buses, and Commercial Fleets
sources.claim: UVeye's drive-through automated inspection systems, used at hundreds of dealerships and by commercial fleets, detect tire wear and underbody defects such as leaks, cracks and structural damage on trucks and buses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect scanning of vehicles in a service facility. It is a fixed sensing gantry that neither operates the machine's controls nor isolates functional faults (hydraulic, drivetrain, electrical), so it does not transfer to diagnosing a reported heavy-equipment defect.

tasks.label: Read and understand operating manuals, blueprints, and technical drawings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Dismantle and reassemble heavy equipment using hoists and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer/fleet service shop bay: pulling a major component (engine, transmission, torque converter, final drive) out of a dozer, loader or excavator with an overhead crane and chain hoist — draining fluids, disconnecting hydraulic lines, wiring harnesses, driveshafts and mounts with impact guns and wrenches, breaking loose seized/rusted fasteners, then reinstalling, aligning, torquing to spec and refilling.

Field repair at a construction, logging or roadwork site: removing and replacing a hydraulic cylinder, boom/bucket pin, swing motor or pump on a machine parked outdoors, using a service-truck crane or portable hoist, on uneven muddy ground, in weather, with limited access around the machine and pins that must be driven out.

Shop bench teardown and rebuild of a removed subassembly (hydraulic cylinder, pump, final drive, differential, swing drive) — clamping in a fixture/stand, using a press and pullers, splitting the case, replacing seals, bearings and worn parts, then reassembling to shimming and torque specifications and pressure-testing.

Undercarriage work in the shop or fenced yard: jacking/blocking a dozer or excavator, breaking and re-joining track chains with a track press, and changing sprockets, rollers and idlers — very heavy, greasy, awkward sections handled with hoists and slings.

Mine-site maintenance workshop: change-out of a major module on a haul truck or shovel (wheel motor, suspension strut, engine/radiator module) in a large bay with overhead cranes, jib hoists and torque multipliers, following the site's standard work procedure.

sources.system: Human–robot collaborative disassembly (systematic review of the field)
sources.developer: Lee, Liang, Hu, Onel, Behdad, Zheng (Univ. at Buffalo / Univ. of Florida); published ASME J. Manuf. Sci. Eng.
sources.title: A Review of Prospects and Opportunities in Disassembly with Human-Robot Collaboration
sources.claim: State-of-the-art review of robotic disassembly of used products concludes that full automation of disassembly is not viable given the task's complexity and variability, with human–robot collaboration the practical direction; no autonomous system performs whole teardown-and-rebuild of used machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of end-of-life mechanical products. It is the closest research analog to dismantling used heavy equipment (worn, corroded fasteners, unknown internal condition); the review's finding that full automation remains out of reach bounds what could transfer to heavy-equipment teardown.

sources.system: AgiProbot automated disassembly demonstrator
sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) / Fraunhofer IOSB
sources.title: 6D Pose Estimation on Point Cloud Data through Prior Knowledge Integration: A Case Study in Autonomous Disassembly
sources.claim: A research cell autonomously disassembles end-of-life electric starter motors that are clamped in a fixture, using a multifunctional robot arm with vision-based 6D bolt pose estimation — a lab-scale, purpose-built cell handling small used motors, disassembly only, with no reassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of a used bolted electromechanical assembly in a fixtured cell. It is the nearest demonstrated analog to bench teardown of a heavy-equipment subassembly, but the objects are small starter motors, the work is disassembly only, and no reassembly to torque/shim specification is shown.

sources.system: ORNL robotic battery disassembly line
sources.title: Automated disassembly line aims to make battery recycling safer, faster
sources.claim: A purpose-built robotic line demonstrated automated removal of bolts and housings from spent EV battery packs, showing fixtured-line disassembly of a bolted heavy assembly at laboratory demonstration maturity, without any reassembly step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated unbolting and stripping of a large bolted assembly on a purpose-built line. It bounds E1 capability — even with fixtured presentation the demonstrated scope is destructive/one-way disassembly of a standardized pack, not reassembly of a repaired machine.

sources.system: SmartBay robotic tire-changing platform
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial vehicle-service automation, a robotic tire-changing bay, is only semi-automated: it avoids removing wheels from the vehicle and still needs a human for tire handling, air-line connection and weight placement — far short of general dismantle-and-reassemble mechanical work even in a purpose-built bay.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal/refitting of a bolted heavy vehicle component in a service bay. It is the closest commercial analog to shop dismantling work; its need for human steps on a single, highly repetitive operation shows the gap to multi-step heavy-equipment teardown.

sources.system: Robotic mining-truck tire changing machine (prototype design)
sources.developer: Academic/industrial research team (IEEE/VDE ISR conference publication)
sources.title: Automatic Tire Changing of Large Mining Vehicles with Industrial Robots
sources.claim: Automated changing of large mining-truck tires — a repetitive, high-value heavy-vehicle service operation — exists only as a proposed prototype machine design combining two industrial robots with a hydraulic parallel platform, not as a deployed autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal/refit of a very heavy bolted component on mining equipment. Same object class and scale as heavy-equipment dismantling; its prototype-only status indicates no fielded system for heavy-equipment component removal and reinstallation.

tasks.label: Overhaul and test machines or equipment to ensure operating efficiency.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer or fleet shop overhaul of a removed major component (hydraulic pump/motor, final drive, swing drive, transmission, differential) on a bench or rebuild stand: tear down a dirty, worn unit with seized fasteners, clean, measure and inspect parts for wear against specs, decide reuse/replace, install new bearings, seals, clutch packs and shims, reassemble to torque, backlash and end-play specs, then bench/dyno test for pressure, leakage and function.

Shop rebuild of hydraulic cylinders and smaller hydraulic/pneumatic assemblies: break loose a seized gland nut, extract rod and piston, inspect rod chrome and barrel bore for scoring, hone or replace, fit a new seal kit without damaging seals, reassemble, then stroke and pressure/leak test the cylinder on a test stand before return to service.

Machine-level overhaul in the shop (certified rebuild or major service of a dozer, excavator, loader or crane): rig and remove components with an overhead crane, rebuild or replace undercarriage/track groups, powertrain and hydraulic lines, harnesses and cooling package, reinstall and align, refill and bleed systems, then run all functions and load-test the machine.

Field overhaul/major repair at a construction, quarry, mine or logging site: machine sits on uneven muddy ground, technician works from a service truck in weather, removes and rebuilds a final drive, swing motor, pump or blade/boom cylinders in place, improvises rigging and access, then tests the machine under load on site.

Post-overhaul testing, adjustment and commissioning of the rebuilt machine: connect the diagnostic laptop, run each hydraulic and drivetrain function, measure relief and standby pressures, cycle times and temperatures, hunt leaks, adjust valves, linkages and brakes, road/load test, and document results before release to the customer.

sources.system: Robotic laser cladding system (CNH Industrial Reman facility, Springfield, MO)
sources.title: CNH Industrial Reman Adds Robotic Laser Cladding System to Expand Part and Component Production Capabilities
sources.claim: A remanufacturer of agricultural/construction equipment components installed a robotic laser cladding cell to restore worn surfaces on returned cores — an automated single step of component remanufacturing, not teardown, inspection, reassembly or testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: salvage/restoration of worn heavy-equipment cores in a remanufacturing plant. It is the closest deployed robotic work to overhaul, but it performs one fixtured metal-deposition operation on an already-disassembled, cleaned part; it does not disassemble, inspect, reassemble or test a component.

sources.system: CAD-to-POMDP robotic disassembly planner with manipulator (laboratory)
sources.title: From CAD to POMDP: Probabilistic Planning for Robotic Disassembly of End-of-Life Products
sources.claim: Robotic disassembly of end-of-life products — the analogue of overhaul teardown — is still a research problem; the field states such disassembly is currently performed mostly by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of used products. Overhaul begins with teardown of worn, contaminated assemblies; the state of the art here is laboratory planning research on far smaller, cleaner products, so it does not carry over to heavy-equipment overhaul.

sources.system: Object-centric autonomous disassembly framework (lab robot cell)
sources.title: Disassembly from scratch: An object-centric approach for robotic autonomous disassembly with zero contact/interference information
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed work on autonomous robotic disassembly identifies the exact conditions of overhaul cores — corrosion, rust, missing or altered parts, unknown internal relations — as the unresolved barriers, and demonstrates only laboratory-scale disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous disassembly of worn/corroded used assemblies, which is the first phase of any overhaul. The cited limits (rust, seized and missing fasteners, unknown internals) are the defining conditions of heavy-equipment cores.

sources.system: Cylinder test bench for hydraulic cylinders
sources.title: Cylinder test bench for hydraulic cylinder - hainzl.at
sources.claim: Automated hydraulic cylinder test stands can run a programmed test sequence on rebuilt cylinders, but the test heads are only semi-automated and the machine covers the verification step alone, not the rebuild.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-rebuild functional/leak testing of hydraulic cylinders. It substantiates automation of the 'test' half only; human operators mount and connect the cylinder, and no rebuild work is performed.

sources.system: SmartBay robotic tire-change platform
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay
sources.claim: The most advanced deployed vehicle-service robot performs tire removal, mounting and balancing on standard consumer vehicles inside a purpose-built service bay under light operator oversight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic vehicle service in a repair bay. It shows the current ceiling of service-bay robotics — a standardized bolt-off/bolt-on operation on light vehicles — which does not transfer to disassembling, measuring, rebuilding and testing heavy-equipment drivetrain and hydraulic assemblies.

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing and screw-collection system for EV battery disassembly
sources.title: Robotic Removal and Collection of Screws in Collaborative Disassembly of End-of-Life Electric Vehicle Batteries
sources.claim: Robotic unfastening of threaded fasteners during disassembly of used products is still being published as new laboratory method work on small screws in collaborative cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fastener removal on used equipment. Overhaul requires breaking loose large, torqued, rusted and thread-locked hardware; even small clean screws remain a research-stage capability, so the transfer fails.

tasks.label: Adjust, maintain, and repair or replace subassemblies, such as transmissions and crawler heads, using hand tools, jacks, and cranes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer or fleet maintenance shop: remove and replace a powershift transmission or torque converter on a dozer, wheel loader, or grader - drain fluids, disconnect driveshafts, hydraulic lines and harnesses, split the machine or drop the unit with an overhead crane and floor jacks, install a reman unit, torque to spec, refill, adjust and stall-test.

On-site field repair at a construction, logging, or quarry job site: replace final drives, sprockets, idlers, track chain or crawler-head components on a tracked machine using a service-truck crane, porta-power and jacks, on uneven ground in mud, dust, heat or cold, with the machine sitting wherever it failed.

Shop undercarriage/crawler-head rebuild: press pins and bushings, replace rollers, idlers and sprocket segments, rebuild track assemblies on a track press and benches, then reinstall on the machine and set track tension.

Field or pit change-out of other heavy subassemblies on mining and construction machines - hydraulic pumps, swing/travel drives, differentials, winches, conveyor drive gearboxes - rigged with a crane or boom truck, often on a machine that must first be jacked, cribbed and locked out.

Routine adjustment and maintenance of subassemblies in the shop or yard: track tension adjustment, clutch, brake and linkage adjustment, transmission/final-drive oil and filter service, re-torque checks, pressure tests and operational verification.

sources.system: RUSSELL 7 Model R AutoMotion Mill Relining Machine
sources.title: RME deploys world's first semi-automated mill relining system
sources.claim: RME's RUSSELL 7 AutoMotion mill relining machine performs heavy maintenance component exchange (grinding-mill liner removal and placement) in a mineral processing plant, but it is a semi-automated, operator-supervised, purpose-designed liner handler, not a general subassembly repair system for mobile equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy bolted-component removal and replacement during industrial maintenance. Transfer fails: the machine handles one standardised liner type inside a fixed processing plant with dedicated bolt-knocking hammers, is operator-directed (semi-automated), and cannot drain fluids, disconnect hoses and harnesses, or fit a transmission or crawler head on a mobile machine.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire unveils AI-powered robotic tire-changing platform for automotive service bays
sources.claim: Robotic tire-change bays change passenger-vehicle wheels autonomously inside a purpose-built service bay; this is the closest commercially offered robotic vehicle-service work, and it is confined to standardised lug-nut wheel removal on cars.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing and refitting a bolted component on a vehicle in a service bay. Transfer fails: wheels are light, standardised, externally accessible and held by uniform lug nuts, whereas transmissions, final drives and crawler heads weigh hundreds of kilograms and require fluid draining, line and linkage disconnection, crane rigging and model-specific torque and adjustment procedures.

sources.system: DeMoBat robotic EV battery pack disassembly cell
sources.title: Vision-Guided Dual-Arm Humanoid Robotic Disassembly of End-of-Life 18650 Lithium-ion Battery Packs
sources.claim: Automated heavy-component disassembly with industrial robots has been shown only for products of known, fixed geometry presented in a purpose-built cell; the authors state feasibility depends on removing geometric uncertainty.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic unbolting and removal of a heavy vehicle subassembly. Transfer fails: it requires a priori known geometry and a fixtured cell, while heavy-equipment repair presents worn, dirty, seized, model-variable assemblies whose condition is discovered only during teardown.

sources.system: Deep-reinforcement-learning robotic unscrewing system
sources.developer: University of Birmingham remanufacturing robotics group and collaborators
sources.title: Robotic disassembly of screws for end-of-life product remanufacturing enabled by deep reinforcement learning
sources.claim: Robotic removal of threaded fasteners from used products remains a laboratory research problem, with work focused on single-screw removal under dirt, rust and condition variability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automating fastener removal, the elementary step of any subassembly R&R. It shows the state of the art is single-fastener removal in a lab cell, far short of a whole transmission or crawler-head replacement at technician quality.

sources.system: Robotic parallel platform for automated tire changing of large mining vehicles
sources.title: Automatic Tire Changing of Large Mining Vehicles with Industrial Robots
sources.claim: A robotic machine for changing large mining-truck tires exists as a published machine-design/prototype study using two industrial robots on a hydraulic parallel platform; it is not a deployed maintenance system and addresses wheels rather than drivetrain subassemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic unbolting and handling of a heavy component on mining equipment. Transfer fails: it is a prototype for one standardised wheel operation with no evidence of autonomous field or shop deployment, and no capability for transmissions, final drives or crawler heads.

tasks.label: Repair, rewire, and troubleshoot electrical systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field service call at a construction site: an excavator, dozer or loader won't crank or won't charge. The mechanic works beside the machine in dirt/mud and variable weather, reads fault codes with a laptop, uses a multimeter to check batteries, grounds, starter/alternator circuits, traces the harness through the frame and engine bay, finds a chafed wire, corroded pin or failed relay, repairs the splice/connector, and verifies the machine starts and charges.

Dealer or contractor shop bay: machine driven/hauled in for an intermittent electrical fault (CAN bus communication errors, sensor circuit codes, erratic monitor readings). Mechanic pulls OEM schematics, back-probes connectors, performs pin-to-pin continuity and voltage-drop tests, isolates a broken conductor or water-intruded connector inside a harness, cuts in a repair section with solder/crimp splices and heat shrink, reroutes and secures the harness, clears codes and road-tests.

Mine or quarry maintenance shop: haul truck, shovel or crusher electrical work in a large bay with overhead crane access — repairing damaged high-current cables and battery/starter circuits, replacing burnt lugs and terminals, fixing lighting and camera circuits, testing 24 V systems, following lockout/tagout, on machines with heavy guarding and confined access.

Known-fault component replacement in a shop or equipment yard: replace an alternator, starter, solenoid, wiring pigtail, sensor or battery bank — remove guards/panels, disconnect and reconnect connectors and heavy cables, torque lugs, then load-test and verify charging/cranking output.

Installing or rewiring add-on electrical equipment in the shop: beacons, work lights, back-up cameras, GPS/telematics or grade-control kits — routing new wire through the machine, drilling/grommeting pass-throughs, terminating and fusing circuits, splicing into existing power/ignition feeds, loom and tie-down, and functional test.

Remote field repair in logging or agriculture: harness damaged by rodents, brush or a small fire on a skidder, forwarder or feller-buncher parked on uneven ground, often in rain, cold or after dark; mechanic diagnoses from a service truck, fabricates and installs replacement leads on the spot, and gets the machine running.

sources.system: Komax harness manufacturing / automatic crimping platforms (e.g., Omega 750 S, CrX-44HD)
sources.title: Harness Manufacturing | Komax
sources.claim: Automated wire-harness production equipment (Komax) exists commercially and performs cutting, crimping, housing insertion and routing of new harnesses inside purpose-built factory machines; it does not diagnose or repair harnesses installed on machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory fabrication of new wire harnesses from fixtured spools. It does not transfer to the mechanic's task, which requires diagnosing an unknown fault in an installed harness on a specific machine and making targeted in-situ repairs to an existing, deformed, dirty assembly.

sources.system: Behavioral-cloning robotic connector assembly cell (research)
sources.developer: euROBIN / Innovation Campus Future Mobility research groups
sources.title: Behavioral Cloning for Robotic Connector Assembly: An Empirical Study
sources.claim: Wire harness assembly/installation in vehicles remains largely manual; robotic connector assembly is still a research problem studied in lab cells with fixtured parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating electrical connectors in a fixtured lab cell. Even this narrow sub-step is at research maturity, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance diagnosis and repair of heavy-equipment electrical systems.

tasks.label: Diagnose faults or malfunctions to determine required repairs, using engine diagnostic equipment such as computerized test equipment and calibration devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field service call on an active construction site: a dozer/excavator/loader is down with an intermittent hydraulic or electrical fault. Tech drives a service truck to the machine, interviews the operator, opens panels, connects a laptop running OEM software (e.g. Cat ET, Service ADVISOR) to the diagnostic port, pulls active/logged codes, runs live data and solenoid actuation tests, tees pressure gauges into hydraulic test ports, probes harnesses with a multimeter, and concludes which component must be repaired/replaced. Mud, weather, machine parked where it failed.

Dealer or fleet shop service bay: machine hauled in, positioned over a pit or in a bay. Full diagnostic workup — ECM data download and code retrieval, electronic calibrations of sensors/valves, hydraulic flow and pressure tests, stall and drive tests, fluid sampling, partial teardown to confirm root cause — ending in a written repair recommendation/estimate the service writer accepts.

Mine or quarry, in-pit or on a haul road: a haul truck, shovel or dozer shows an engine derate, transmission or brake fault. Technician reaches the machine in a light vehicle, connects OEM diagnostic software, checks live parameters, temperatures and pressures, isolates the fault in dust/heat/cold, and decides whether the machine can be walked to the shop or needs field repair.

Logging or land-clearing site in the woods: skidder, feller buncher or grinder with a hydraulic/electrical malfunction. Diagnosis with a handheld or laptop diagnostic tool plus pressure and electrical checks, on uneven ground among slash and stumps, often with limited access to the machine and no shelter.

Scheduled PM / condition inspection at a customer yard, rental depot or municipal fleet garage: technician connects diagnostic equipment to download ECM/telematics data and stored codes, verifies calibrations, checks for leaks, undercarriage and hose wear, takes fluid samples, and produces a list of required repairs for the fleet manager.

sources.system: Spot (with Orbit/automated inspection payloads)
sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot, a commercially deployed quadruped, performs autonomous routine inspection missions in industrial facilities — gauge reading, thermal monitoring and acoustic leak detection — producing alerts on equipment health, but it senses rather than connecting diagnostic equipment or determining required repairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous equipment-condition inspection in industrial plants. It shares the mobility and sensing part of fault-finding, but not the defining acts of this task (plugging in computerized test equipment, running actuator/calibration routines, pressure and continuity testing, root-cause determination), so it does not substantiate completion.

sources.system: ANYmal
sources.title: ANYbotics Total Funding at $150 Million after Climate Investments Joins to Scale Autonomous Inspection in Hazardous Sites
sources.claim: ANYmal legged robots are deployed at scale for autonomous inspection of energy and industrial sites, detecting overheating, abnormal vibration and leaks; their output is anomaly detection, not diagnostic testing of machines with computerized test equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous condition monitoring of fixed industrial plant. Demonstrates rugged autonomous sensing in E2-type facilities, but no interaction with machine ECMs, test ports or calibration devices and no determination of required repairs, so it cannot substantiate this task.

sources.system: Automated haul truck inspection robot
sources.title: Mining industry - Tessellate
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile robot is being introduced at mine sites to perform visual and thermal inspection of haul trucks while they refuel, generating alerts for targeted human intervention rather than fault diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = pre-shift/condition inspection of mining haul trucks, the same machines as instance 2. It covers only external visual/thermal screening and explicitly hands off to technicians for intervention, so it does not carry over to instrument-based fault diagnosis and repair determination.

sources.system: Automated transfer-case test cell (robot load, automated engagement tooling)
sources.title: Test Cell Automation Soup to Nuts - RedViking
sources.claim: Purpose-built automated test cells load a fixtured driveline component with a robot and engage it mechanically and electrically to run full functional tests, i.e. automated pass/fail testing of a known product in a fenced cell rather than root-cause diagnosis of a worn in-service machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = end-of-line functional testing of a fixtured drivetrain component; this is the closest E1 analogue to 'bringing the work to the machine'. It verifies a new unit against spec and flags failures for human diagnosis; it does not isolate root cause across the varied failure modes of aged field equipment or specify required repairs.

sources.system: UVeye underbody/360 inspection systems
sources.title: UVeye Expands AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Trucks, Buses, and Commercial Fleets
sources.claim: Automated drive-through scanning systems installed at hundreds of dealerships and fleet sites inspect vehicles, including heavy-duty trucks and buses, for external and mechanical flaws in seconds, but they are fixed sensing gantries that do not interrogate control modules, run calibrations, or determine required repairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated vehicle condition inspection in a structured service lane, closest to the PM-inspection instance. It detects visible damage and wear only; it performs no computerized diagnostic testing of controllers or hydraulics and issues no repair determination, so it cannot substantiate this task.

tasks.label: Examine parts for damage or excessive wear, using micrometers and gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer or independent heavy-equipment service shop: a hydraulic pump, motor or cylinder has been torn down on the bench; the mechanic degreases the piece parts and measures rod diameter, bore ID, wear-plate thickness and clearances with outside micrometers, bore gauges and feeler gauges, comparing each reading to the OEM reuse/wear-limit table and marking parts reuse, salvage or scrap.

Shop component rebuild of a drivetrain assembly (final drive, transmission, swing gearbox, brake pack): mechanic measures bearing journals and bores, sets gear backlash and end play with dial indicators, gauges friction/brake disc thickness, and inspects gear teeth and bearing races for spalling, pitting and scoring against reuse criteria.

Field service at a construction site or quarry: technician measures undercarriage wear in situ on a dozer or excavator — link height, bushing OD, grouser/shoe height, roller and idler flange wear — with wear gauges, calipers and an ultrasonic depth gauge, kneeling in mud on uneven ground, and reports percent wear remaining.

Roadside/jobsite inspection of a failed or suspect component still mounted on the machine: checking pin-and-bushing joint clearance with a pry bar and dial indicator or feeler gauge, measuring a scored or bent cylinder rod, gauging sheave/track pad or blade wear, and deciding on the spot whether to repair in place, remove, or run.

Component rebuild / remanufacturing center: incoming used cores are washed and presented at inspection benches, where piece parts are measured against reuse tables and crack-checked (dye penetrant or magnetic particle) before routing to salvage or scrap.

Mine-site maintenance workshop: teardown of a very large component (final drive, wheel hub, large sheave, track roller frame) with overhead crane support; large-bore micrometers, telescoping gauges and dial indicators used on heavy, oily parts staged on stands.

sources.system: Engineering Data / Mitutoyo robotic measurement cell with MiSTAR CMM (Méca-Précis)
sources.title: Robotic measurement cells removes bottleneck in parts inspection process | Engineer Live
sources.claim: A deployed robotic measurement cell (articulated robot + Mitutoyo MiSTAR shop-floor CMM + pallet storage) at machining firm Méca-Précis autonomously loads fixtured metal parts and runs dimensional inspection programs unattended, in an enclosed, glass-panelled cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional inspection of machined metal components to tolerance. It transfers because the mechanic's act — measuring a metal part with a micrometer/bore gauge and comparing the reading to a limit table — is the same measurement at the same (micrometre) precision on comparable metal objects; the cell also renders the pass/fail verdict.

sources.system: CUBE-R (MetraSCAN 3D-R robot-mounted optical CMM scanner)
sources.title: Creaform Launches CUBE-R At-Line 3D Robotic Scanning CMM – Metrology and Quality News
sources.claim: Creaform's CUBE-R is a commercially sold turnkey, fully enclosed robotic scanning CMM cell that performs automated dimensional inspection of parts 1–3 m in size at metrology-grade accuracy on the shop floor, running several hundred parts a day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated whole-part dimensional inspection in a purpose-built cell. Transfers because heavy-equipment piece parts (cylinder rods, gears, track links, wear plates) fall inside the 1–3 m size range and the deviation-to-nominal colourmap output is the same reuse/replace decision the mechanic makes from gauge readings.

sources.system: Automated Vision Inspection (AVI) with robot-assisted parts handling
sources.title: Vision inspection system with robot assisted parts handling | Kistler INT
sources.claim: Kistler sells an Automated Vision Inspection machine in which vision-guided pick-and-place robots feed parts for 100% inspection of dimensions and detection of ... on metal and plastic components, down to the micrometre range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: combined dimensional gauging and surface-defect detection on metal parts with robotic handling. Transfers because 'examine for damage or excessive wear' is exactly dimension-versus-limit plus surface flaw (scoring, pitting, cracking) detection on metal components presented at a station.

sources.system: Vision-guided robotic ultrasonic inspection work-cell (Strathclyde)
sources.developer: University of Strathclyde (Khan, Mineo, Dobie, Macleod, Pierce)
sources.title: Vision guided robotic inspection for parts in manufacturing and remanufacturing industry | Journal of Remanufacturing
sources.claim: A robotic inspection work-cell combining automated 3D vision reconstruction with ultrasonic NDT tool-path generation was built and validated specifically for remanufacturing components that have seen decades of wear and therefore deviate from CAD models.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated NDT/geometry inspection of worn cores in remanufacturing. Directly comparable objects and purpose (used, worn heavy components assessed for damage before reuse), and it addresses the specific difficulty — worn parts departing from nominal geometry — that separates wear inspection from new-part metrology.

sources.system: SHINING 3D Automated Inspection System (OptimScan 5M Plus + collaborative robot)
sources.title: A New Method for Incoming Material Inspection – SHINING 3D Automated Inspection System
sources.claim: Shining 3D markets an automated incoming-material inspection system pairing a collaborative robot with an OptimScan 5M Plus scanner of 0.005 mm accuracy to check that received components conform to specification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic incoming-part conformity inspection at 5 µm accuracy. Transfers to core/piece-part inspection at a rebuild centre, where incoming used parts are measured against reuse dimensions — same precision class and same accept/reject output.

tasks.label: Weld or solder broken parts and structural members, using electric or gas welders and soldering tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop repair of a cracked or broken structural component that has been removed from the machine (loader bucket, dozer blade/push arm, ripper shank, cylinder mount, frame gusset): the mechanic finds the crack extent, drills stop holes, gouges/grinds the crack to sound metal, preheats, lays multi-pass FCAW/SMAW fill, sometimes fits a doubler plate, then grinds and checks the repair.

Field welding at a construction site, mine pit, quarry or logging landing on the machine where it sits: cracked bucket or blade, broken lift-arm weld, torn wear plate, cracked frame member. Out-of-position (vertical/overhead) welds with an engine-driven welder, dirt, grease, wind/rain, uneven ground and no fixturing; part usually cannot be moved.

Shop fabrication and wear-part work: torch/plasma cut and fit new cutting edges, wear plates, tooth adapters or a replacement bracket from stock steel, tack up, weld out multi-pass, and hardface/build up worn surfaces on buckets, blades and rollers.

Small hot-work joints: brazing or soldering hydraulic/fuel/AC tube joints and radiator or cooler leaks, and soldering battery cable lugs and wiring-harness terminals; work done on the bench in the shop or at the machine.

Small welds performed on the fully assembled machine in the shop bay: welding a nut onto a sheared bolt or stud to back it out, tacking a hose or guard bracket back on inside a crowded engine bay or under the frame, patching a crack in an installed tank or shield, working around hoses, wiring and painted surfaces.

sources.system: MaxQ Repair (with Fanuc welding robots)
sources.title: Automated Mining Component Repair with Metalleco
sources.claim: RAMLAB's MaxQ Repair workflow turns standard Fanuc welding stations into automated repair cells that scan worn mining components of inconsistent wear geometry and generate adaptive cladding/weld-build-up toolpaths, deployed with repair company Metalleco.
sources.transferJustification: Repair welding of worn/damaged mining machine components by robotic weld build-up is the same physical operation (deposit weld metal to restore a broken or worn heavy-equipment part) on the same class of objects as the task's shop repair welds.

sources.system: MaxQ Repair (cobot-based repair cell)
sources.title: Patch welding of large castings with MaxQ Repair
sources.claim: MaxQ Repair automates patch/defect repair welding of large castings end to end: an operator marks the defective area, and the system scans, plans and fills it with weld metal.
sources.transferJustification: Patch repair welding of defective areas in large rail/mining/maritime castings matches the task's core act of building broken metal back up; geometry is unknown in advance and is recovered by scanning, as with a cracked heavy-equipment part.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 intelligent welding cells (Obsidian AI)
sources.title: The Technology - Path Robotics
sources.claim: Path Robotics' welding cells scan each part, build a 3D model, locate seams and plan and execute welds autonomously without robot programming, handling high-mix parts with inconsistent fit-up.

sources.system: Path Robotics intelligent welding cell (Obsidian)

sources.claim: Path Robotics' intelligent welding cells are used in production by Mine Rite Technologies to make precision welds on massive mining-equipment structures such as shovel buckets and haul truck beds.

sources.title: Automated Solutions for Bucket Welding Help Keep Manufacturers and the Earth Moving (AWS Welding Digest)
sources.claim: A robotic cell configured for a 22,000-lb mining loader bucket combines a gantry-mounted welding robot, heavy 2- and 3-axis workpiece positioners, laser seam searching and light curtains to weld bucket plate and wear strips.
sources.transferJustification: Welding wear strips and plate onto excavation buckets in a fixtured cell is the same operation as the mechanic's shop work of cutting, fitting and welding replacement wear plates and cutting edges onto buckets and blades.

sources.system: Heavy-plate robotic welding cell (armored face conveyor pans)
sources.title: Mining Equipment Manufacturer Digs Robotic Welders' Productivity (A3/Automate case study)
sources.claim: Mining-equipment maker Bucyrus uses four heavy-duty welding robots that deposit about 150 lb of filler metal in multiple passes on thick-plate (40 mm) armored-face conveyor pans, cutting labor time versus manual welding.
sources.transferJustification: Multi-pass welding of very thick abrasion-resistant plate on mining conveyor structures matches the metallurgy, joint thickness and multi-pass technique of structural repair welds on heavy equipment.

sources.system: UltraFlex robotic induction brazing cell (SOLO / Dragon RoboStand)
sources.title: UltraFlex demonstrates automated robotic induction brazing for copper to brass assemblies
sources.claim: A robot-arm-mounted induction coil automatically brazes copper-to-brass tube joints, moving from joint to joint and completing each braze in seconds with controlled heat.
sources.transferJustification: Robotic brazing of copper/brass tube joints is the same joining operation as brazing repaired hydraulic, fuel, AC or radiator tube joints on heavy equipment, on comparable small-diameter metal tubing.

sources.system: Apollo Seiko soldering robots (desktop, in-line, laser)
sources.title: Apollo Seiko Robotic Soldering | Kaisertech Ltd
sources.claim: Apollo Seiko builds commercial iron-tip, laser and selective soldering robots that automate hand-soldering operations on presented workpieces in production.
sources.transferJustification: Automated soldering of fixtured joints covers the soldering half of the task (terminals, lugs, small connections) when the joint is presented to the machine in a cell.

sources.system: Rove (Obsidian on quadruped platform)
sources.title: Path Robotics Launches Rove, Bringing Mobility to Welding Automation Powered by Physical AI
sources.claim: Path Robotics launched Rove, a quadruped-mounted mobile welding robot intended for large assemblies that cannot be fixtured in a cell; a shipbuilder is one of the first ... evaluating it.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as the frontier of in-facility mobile welding on unfixturable assemblies; it is at early-adopter evaluation, so it does not substantiate completion of repair welds on assembled machines.

sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Welder, an autonomous column-welding robot, was deployed on the Toranomon-Azabudai high-rise construction site to weld massive steel columns, using laser shape recognition of the prepared groove.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field-welding deployment: it welds standardized, pre-prepared column groove joints from a dedicated collar jig, so it does not show locating, gouging and repairing arbitrary cracks on machine structures outdoors.

tasks.label: Fit bearings to adjust, repair, or overhaul mobile mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench overhaul of a removed drivetrain component (excavator final drive/planetary, dozer transmission, grader tandem, truck differential): pull worn tapered roller cups and cones with puller/press, clean and micrometer bores and journals, press or induction-heat new bearings into place, set endplay/preload with a shim pack and rolling-torque check, reassemble. Dealer or fleet repair-shop bay with overhead crane, press and hand tools.

Bench rebuild of hydraulic and pneumatic components (piston pump, swing/travel motor, cylinder gland bushings, air compressor/valve assemblies): fit close-tolerance bearings and bushings into housings and onto shafts, verify clearance and free rotation, in a clean area of the repair shop.

Undercarriage and linkage components removed and pressed on a shop or portable press: track roller, carrier roller and idler bearing/bushing replacement, bucket and pin-boss bushings pressed out and in on a hydraulic/track press at the bench, loose component handled by hoist.

In-situ pin-and-bushing/bearing work on the assembled machine at a construction, logging or pit site: drive out frozen pins, heat and press new bushings into boom, stick and bucket bosses in place, realign linkage, on mud/uneven ground with a service truck, portable press and torch, in weather.

Wheel-end and axle bearing service on haul trucks, wheel loaders and graders in a mine or fleet maintenance bay: break down the wheel end, drive old cups from the hub, pack and fit new bearings, reinstall on the spindle and adjust preload/endplay to spec on the machine.

Large in-place bearing replacement with crane assistance: excavator/crane slew (swing) ring bearing change, crane sheave and drum bearings, pulley/pillow-block bearings on a mobile conveyor or crusher at a quarry — heavy overhead work around and inside the assembled machine.

sources.system: Ahaus robot-integrated knuckle assembly cell (six-axis robot + bushing/sleeve press)
sources.developer: Ahaus Tool and Engineering (Ahaus Advanced Automation), for a tier-1 automotive supplier
sources.title: Knuckle Assembly Cell | Ahaus Advanced Automation
sources.claim: A purpose-built robotic cell autonomously presses a bushing and two sleeves into automotive steering knuckles (the wheel-end housing carrying the hub bearing), with a six-axis robot handling part and press, load-cell force monitoring of every press and automatic rejection of bad fits; the operator only refills the feeder.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: press-fitting bushings/sleeves into a cast steel wheel-end housing. Transfer: same objects (interference-fit steel rings into machined bores), same precision regime (press force/depth verified against a signature), and the same act a mechanic performs fitting a bearing race into a fixtured housing.

sources.developer: Ford Motor Co. with force-control suppliers cited in the article
sources.title: Force-Controlled Assembly With Robots | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Force-controlled industrial robots in daily production install clutch packs and gears deep into transmission cases at a high-mix plant building 70 transmission models, adjusting in real time from force feedback to seat parts without damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic insertion of precision rotating-assembly parts into gearbox housings under force control. Transfer: same objects and clearances as seating bearings and gear trains in a final drive or transmission, and the plant runs a high variant mix rather than one SKU.

sources.system: Robotic press-fit work cells (Promess servo press / Robot EMAP; Schmidt Technology SCARA-fed shuttle-fixture press cell)

sources.claim: Commercially supplied press-fit work cells combine robots, fixtures and servo presses so parts are picked from a conveyor, fixtured and driven into the press automatically, with force-versus-position signatures monitored on each press.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated interference-fit pressing into fixtured workpieces. Transfer: bearing fitting is a press-fit operation judged by force/depth signature; these cells perform exactly that motion and verification with the workpiece fixtured and the part presented.

sources.system: Simmons railway wheel set and bearing presses (NSH USA / Hegenscheidt-MFD wheel shop equipment)
sources.developer: NSH USA Corporation / NSH Group (Simmons, Hegenscheidt-MFD)
sources.title: Wheel Presses | NSH USA Corporation
sources.claim: Purpose-built press machines mount and demount bearings on wheelsets in railway maintenance (overhaul) facilities, integrated with other wheel-shop equipment for automated control of the pressing graph — removing worn bearings from used axles and fitting new ones is done by machine in a dedicated station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dismounting worn bearings from used axles and mounting replacements during overhaul. Transfer: same act on heavy interference-fit bearings; cited only as context for the removal half, since crane/operator loading leaves autonomy unclear and it cannot alone carry a positive judgment.

sources.system: Survey of robotic disassembly and remanufacturing automation research

sources.claim: Surveys of robotic disassembly for remanufacturing and repair report that disassembly of used machines remains hard to robotise because of variability and condition of returned products, with work still largely at research or human-robot-collaboration stage.
sources.transferJustification: Context for negative judgments: no fielded autonomous system performs teardown-and-bearing-fitting on used heavy machines outside purpose-built stations.

tasks.label: Clean, lubricate, and perform other routine maintenance work on equipment and vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled preventive-maintenance service (e.g., 250/500-hour) on an excavator, dozer or loader inside a dealer or contractor service shop: drain and refill engine oil, change oil/fuel/hydraulic/air filters, check and top off coolant and gear oils, grease all fittings, wipe down, record the service.

Field preventive-maintenance service from a lube/service truck at a construction, quarry or logging job site: machine parked on dirt or rock, mechanic climbs the machine, drains oil to a catch tank, spins off and replaces filters, greases pins and bushings, tops off fluids, blows debris out of coolers, in weather with no fixed layout.

Mine-site scheduled service of a haul truck or shovel at the mine maintenance facility / fuel-and-lube bay: refuel, refill grease and DEF, change engine oil and filters, check fluid levels and tire pressures, wash-down and inspection sign-off.

Lubrication-only routine (daily/weekly grease round) in the yard or shop: connect a grease gun coupler to dozens of zerk fittings on boom, stick and bucket pins, swing bearing, articulation joints and driveline, purge until fresh grease shows, replace damaged fittings, wipe excess.

Wash-down / pressure cleaning of a machine before or after repair: de-mucking the undercarriage, blasting caked mud and hydrocarbons off frame, tracks and body in a shop wash bay or wash pad at a shop, rental yard or mine site.
Cleaning removed components and assemblies in the shop: degreasing hydraulic parts, housings and covers in a parts washer, cleaning filter housings, radiators and coolers before reassembly.

tasks.label: Assemble gear systems, and align frames and gears.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer/independent service shop, component bench: rebuild-assembly of a planetary gear reducer from a mobile machine - dozer/excavator final drive, travel drive, swing drive or winch gearbox. Tech presses bearings onto the carrier and sun/planet shafts, indexes and meshes planet pinions into the ring gear, installs thrust washers, snap rings and seals, sets endplay with shims, torques housing bolts to spec and checks rolling torque. Parts weigh 25-400 kg, handled with hoist and rebuild stand.

Shop bench overhaul assembly of a powershift transmission or torque converter for a loader, articulated truck or grader: stacking clutch packs and gear trains onto shafts, aligning splines to drop shafts and the converter into the case, measuring clutch clearance/endplay and selecting snap rings or shims, then torquing case halves and covers to spec before test-stand run-in.

Shop bench setup of an axle carrier / differential for a haul truck, grader or loader: installing the ring gear on the case, setting pinion depth with shims, establishing ring-and-pinion backlash and bearing preload, and verifying the tooth contact pattern with marking compound, re-shimming until pattern and lash are in spec.

In the shop bay, on the machine: installing an assembled gear unit back into the equipment and aligning it - mating a transmission and torque converter to the engine flywheel housing and engaging splines, bolting a final drive onto a track frame or axle housing, or mounting a swing drive to an excavator upper frame and setting pinion-to-swing-bearing backlash. Work is done overhead, underneath and inside the machine with hoists, jacks and pry bars.

At a customer site (mine, quarry, pit, construction or logging site): aligning drive components in place - laser/dial-indicator alignment of a conveyor drive motor-gearbox-pulley train with shims under the baseplate, aligning drive shafts and carrier bearings, or squaring frames and undercarriage components after a field final-drive change. Uneven ground, weather, dirt, limited access, no fixed layout.

In the shop: fabricating a bent-and-welded item — belt guard, hydraulic hose shield, heat shield, battery box, step tread, bracket with flanges. Cut blank, bend on a press brake or box-and-pan brake, tack and weld corners/gussets, grind and prime the finished piece.

In the shop, working on the machine itself: cutting out a rusted/cracked area of a cab panel, fender, hopper, or shroud and making a patch to fit the irregular opening — trial-fitting, trimming with grinder/nibbler, hammering to match contour, tacking and welding it into the machine's existing structure.

In the shop: a complex contoured piece — curved fender skin, chute or bucket liner, rolled shroud or transition — requiring pattern development from measurements, rolling/forming compound curves, multiple welded seams and a trial fit to the machine.

Field service at a mine, construction site or logging landing: mechanic fabricates a discrete part (bracket, hose guard, guard panel, cover plate) from sheet stock carried on the service truck, using portable shear, grinder, plasma cutter and welder, then hands off/installs the finished part.

Field service on a downed machine: cutting and shaping a plate or patch and welding it directly onto the damaged machine in place (cracked fender, torn shroud, worn deck plate), fitting to as-found damaged geometry outdoors, often in mud, wind, or awkward positions.

tasks.label: Inspect the interior and exterior of rail cars coming into rail yards to identify defects and to determine the extent of wear and damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inbound freight train arrives at a Class I receiving yard; carman inspects the exterior/running gear of every car in the string (wheels, bearings, truck springs, brake rigging and shoes, air hoses and angle cocks, couplers, safety appliances, carbody), identifying defects and judging whether wear (wheel flange/tread, brake shoe, coupler) exceeds condemning limits. Outdoors, day/night, all weather, long strings of mixed car types.

A car bad-ordered on arrival or arriving damaged is placed on the repair track/shop; the repairer inspects it closely inside and out (crawling under, gauging wheels and couplers, checking sills, draft gear, doors, welds, hidden structural damage) to determine the extent of wear/damage and the repair scope to be billed.

Interior inspection of empty freight cars in the yard or at a loading facility — boxcar, covered hopper, gondola, auto rack — climbing in or on the car to check for holes, loose or broken interior fittings, protruding nails, residual lading, moisture, rust flaking and contamination before the car is released or reloaded.

Transit/commuter rail car arriving at the maintenance facility: undercarriage and running-gear inspection performed from the inspection pit/trench — wheels, axles, bolts and fasteners, brake units, traction motors, cables and underfloor equipment — checking for cracks, loose parts, leaks and wear.

Transit/commuter rail car incoming inspection of the interior and upper carbody — seats, floors, doors and door mechanisms, windows, grab rails, interior panels, plus roof-mounted equipment and exterior body damage or graffiti — in the maintenance shop.

Tank car or specialty car arriving at a repair/qualification facility: external visual inspection of shell, jacket, valves, manway, fittings and protective housings, plus interior visual inspection of the tank (confined space) when required, to identify defects and quantify corrosion, dents and wear.

tasks.label: Remove locomotives, car mechanical units, or other components, using pneumatic hoists and jacks, pinch bars, hand tools, and cutting torches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freight car in a repair shop or on a repair track: worker disconnects brake rigging, air hoses and safety appliances, raises the car body with pneumatic/hydraulic jacks or a car hoist, rolls the truck out, and lifts wheelsets/side frames/bolster apart with hoist and pinch bars. Multi-ton parts, decades-old car designs, rust and dirt.

Air brake and running-gear component removal under a car on a shop track or repair track: control valve, brake cylinder, reservoir, slack adjuster, brake shoes and keys, hangers, hoses and piping. Confined access under the car, seized/corroded fasteners, occasional torch or impact tools, awkward postures.

Draft-system and structural component removal in a shop: coupler, yoke, draft gear, carrier and striker parts pulled with pneumatic hoist and pinch bars; and torch-cutting off damaged or corroded appliances and structure (ladders, grab irons, running boards, hopper outlet gates, rivets, sill/plate sections) with an oxy-fuel torch, cutting only where the sound structure begins.

Locomotive or transit-rail-car shop: removal of large mechanical units — traction motor, air compressor, radiator/cooling module, HVAC unit, engine subassemblies, propulsion boxes — using overhead crane, pneumatic hoists, jacks and hand tools, with cables, piping and mounting hardware disconnected first.

Mobile/field repair of a bad-order car at an industry track, customer siding, or a remote yard track: worker arrives with a mobile repair truck, works on ballast in whatever weather and lighting, and removes wheelsets, brake parts, couplers or damaged appliances with portable jacks, hand tools and a torch, with no shop fixturing.
Wheel-shop dismantling of wheelsets already pulled from cars: bearings and adapters pressed off the axle journals and wheels pressed off axles, wheelsets rolled between machines on shop rails.

tasks.label: Test units for operability before and after repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freight car on a shop/repair track: after brake work (valve change, brake rigging, COT&S), the repairer performs a single car air brake test — couples the test device to the glad hand and/or the four pipe-bracket pressure taps, charges the brake pipe, cycles service/emergency applications and releases, operates cut-out cocks, retainer and bleed rod, checks leakage, verifies brake shoes apply/release, measures piston travel and rigging, and stencils/records the passing test.

Freight car arriving on the repair track before repairs: repairer applies air and diagnoses — listens/soaps for leaks in trainline, hoses and reservoirs, checks whether brakes apply and release, tests hand brake operation, checks slack adjuster and rigging travel, verifies the defect reported by the inspector so the correct component is removed.

Component/air-brake room of a car shop: removed or overhauled units (ABDX service and emergency valve portions, angle cocks, empty/load devices, slack adjusters, cushioning units, compressors) are mounted on a shop test rack, run through the specified pressure/function sequence, judged pass/fail, tagged and stocked or scrapped.

Transit/passenger car in a maintenance shop after repairs: functional test of the whole car — cab controls and diagnostic laptop used to cycle doors and check obstruction detection, run HVAC, verify lighting, PA, propulsion and brake response, air system leakage, coupler electrics; sometimes a test-track or shop-move run before release to service.

Transit component shop: repaired units (door operators, HVAC packages, brake control units, electronic boxes, contactors) are placed on dedicated test stands and cycled/measured against acceptance criteria before reinstall.

Field/mobile repair: repairer travels by truck to a customer's industry siding, interchange track, or a car set out on line of road; after repairs, runs an on-car air test with a portable device under weather, uneven ballast and no shop utilities, then releases the car.

tasks.label: Adjust repaired or replaced units as needed to ensure proper operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freight car repair track / car shop: after replacing brake shoes, rigging, cylinder or control valve on a bad-order car, the repairer adjusts brake rigging and dead-lever fulcrum, sets piston travel and hand-brake chain slack, then runs a single-car air brake test and re-adjusts until the car sets and releases within spec. Cars sit on outdoor or covered repair tracks over ballast; car types and rigging arrangements vary widely and components are rusty, greasy and worn.

Running repair in a rail yard or on an industry track: after replacing a knuckle, coupler, draft components, air hose or brake shoe, the repairer checks and adjusts coupler height (shims, carrier wear plate), aligns and adjusts the rigging, re-pins levers and verifies brake set/release by hand and by air, working outdoors between cars in all weather with switching movements nearby.

Transit/passenger rail car maintenance shop (heavy repair bay with pit, lifts, catwalks): after replacing door operators, brake units, pantograph or third-rail shoes, suspension springs/air bags or electronic control units, the technician cycles the system, adjusts door travel, closing force and locks, sets brake clearance, ride height and shoe pressure, and re-runs functional/diagnostic tests until acceptance.

Component/subassembly bench work in the shop's component room: an overhauled or replaced unit (air brake control valve portion, slack adjuster, door operator, hand brake, coupler assembly, compressor) is mounted on a test rack or bench and adjusted - turning threaded adjusters, setting linkage length, torquing and locking jam nuts, setting pressure/regulator settings - until it passes the test stand's spec.

Field / road repair away from the shop: mobile repair truck sent to a derailment site, customer siding, or an underground mine-car haulage way; after replacing a component the repairer adjusts it to working condition with hand tools on uneven ground, in poor light and with no fixed layout, then verifies operation before the car moves.

sources.claim: Fori Automation supplies robotic 'toe set' tooling used in automotive end-of-line alignment cells: a robot-carried gear-driven socket engages the tie-rod adjustment hex, sets toe automatically from the alignment stand's measurement, then torques the jam nut - a closed-loop measure-adjust-lock operation on a vehicle held in a purpose-built stand.

It is the same act as the bench instance of this task - measure a unit's setting, drive a threaded adjuster to spec, lock it with a jam nut, re-measure - on a vehicle presented in a fixtured cell, at tolerances finer than rail-car linkage specs. It transfers only where the unit is standardized and fixtured (E1), not to varied, corroded rigging on cars as found.

tasks.label: Repair, fabricate, and install steel or wood fittings, using blueprints, shop sketches, and instruction manuals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freight-car body repair inside an AAR-certified repair shop: a car spotted on a shop track has damaged steel fittings (ladder, grab irons, brake step, door fittings/tracks, corner post or sill patch). The repairer reads the car's blueprint/AAR rule sheet, torch-cuts or grinds out the damaged fitting and welds, fits the replacement to the existing distorted structure, tacks, welds out-of-position and at height, and grinds/inspects to gauge.

Bench/fabrication-area work in the shop: from a blueprint or shop sketch, the repairer lays out, cuts (torch, saw, shear), drills, bends and welds up a replacement steel fitting or bracket from plate, angle or bar stock, then verifies dimensions before it goes to the repair line.

Wood fittings work: replacing rotted or split flatcar decking, boxcar floor planks or gondola wood lining. Pry out and unbolt old planks, measure the opening, cut lumber/plywood to fit around stakes and fittings, drill, and bolt/nail the new boards to the steel underframe.

Mobile/field repair on a yard track or customer siding: a truck-based repairer diagnoses and repairs or installs steel fittings (grab irons, brake components' brackets, coupler carriers, placard holders) on a car in the open, in weather, with a portable welder and limited access under and around the car.

Transit/passenger rail car maintenance facility: fabricating and installing steel or composite/wood fittings per manufacturer manuals and drawings — seat frames and brackets, interior panel supports, handrails, floor sections and equipment mounting brackets — working in the confined car interior or under the carbody.

tasks.label: Perform scheduled maintenance, and clean units and components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freight car periodic/scheduled maintenance on a railroad repair track: carman jacks/chocks the car, lubricates hand brake and side bearings, checks and replaces worn brake shoes, air hoses, gaskets and cotter keys, performs a single-car air brake test, and wipes/blows dirt and grease off running gear and valve components before re-stenciling. Outdoor or canopy-covered repair track in a railroad-controlled yard, cars of many types and states of dirt.

Transit/commuter rail car scheduled preventive-maintenance inspection in a shop on a pit track or lift: check and lubricate couplers, door mechanisms and truck components, change HVAC and traction-motor filters, top off fluids, measure and replace brake pads, blow out and wipe down under-car boxes, electrical cabinets and roof equipment, then sign off the PM checklist.

Backshop cleaning of removed units and components before inspection or overhaul: wheelsets, roller bearings, truck/bogie frames, air brake control valves, traction motors and gearboxes are degreased and washed of bituminous gear lube, grease and road dirt so defects can be seen and parts reassembled.

Exterior cleaning of the car body: running coaches/units through the wash track or hand-washing car sides, ends, roof and undercarriage with brushes, detergents and high-pressure water at a yard wash rack or shop.

Interior cleaning of a passenger/transit car during scheduled servicing: sweep/scrub floors, vacuum and wipe seats, clean windows and interior panels, remove rubbish, spot-clean graffiti and service restrooms, on a layup track or in the depot.

Tank car or covered hopper interior cleaning at a repair/cleaning facility: remove product heel and residue by high-pressure washing so the car can be inspected, hot-worked or reloaded, with confined-space and hazardous-commodity precautions.

tasks.label: Examine car roofs for wear and damage, and repair defective sections, using roofing material, cement, nails, and waterproof paint.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freight car (boxcar / covered hopper) roof leak inspection and seal-and-patch repair on a shop repair track: the repairer climbs onto the car, walks the roof, inspects roof sheets, lap seams, hatch coamings and running-board fittings for corrosion, holes, cracked sealant and impact damage, wire-brushes/grinds the bad spots, applies roof cement/caulk, screws or rivets a small patch plate over holes, and spot-coats the repair.

Structural roof-sheet replacement in a heavy railcar repair shop: cut out a corroded or torn roof panel with torch/plasma, fit a replacement sheet placed by crane, weld or rivet it to carlines and side plates, seal all seams, then apply waterproof coating over the new section.

Running/field repair outdoors in a rail yard or on a customer siding: inspect the roofs of cars in a standing consist for wear and damage (punctures, dented roof sheets, missing or unlatched hatch covers, lifted seams), decide repair vs. bad-order, and make a temporary weather-tight patch with sealant and a bolted or nailed patch in whatever weather and lighting exist.

Passenger/transit rail car roof inspection and resealing in a transit maintenance facility with roof-access platforms and de-energized catenary: inspect roof panels, joints and sealant around roof hatches, vents and roof-mounted equipment, cut out failed sealant, reseal joints, and touch up the roof coating.

Full roof strip-and-recoat during car refurbishment in a blast-and-paint facility: inspection finds general coating wear and light surface corrosion with no structural defect, so the car is spotted in the blast room, the roof and body are abrasive-blasted to bare metal, and a waterproof primer/topcoat system is applied.

tasks.label: Paint car exteriors, interiors, and fixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full exterior repaint of a freight car (covered hopper, tank car, boxcar) during heavy repair/overhaul: car spotted inside the shop's blast/paint facility, blasted and then primed and topcoated over the whole body in a single color to shop coating spec (film thickness, cure).

Spray touch-up and priming of repaired exterior areas after running repairs — weld patches, replaced side sheets, doors, roof sheets, new sills — on a car in a repair bay or on the repair track; large accessible side/end/roof surfaces, color matched to the existing car.

Brush, roller or aerosol touch-up of underframe, truck side frames, brake rigging, couplers, draft gear, grab irons and safety appliances after component replacement; car over a pit or on an outdoor repair track, cluttered and occluded geometry, adjacent bearings/hoses to avoid.
Applying stencils and markings after painting: reporting marks and numbers, capacity/lettering data, load-limit and safety stencils, reflective marking placement, on the car body side and ends.

Painting removed parts and fixtures in the shop's parts paint area or small booth: hatch covers, doors, brake components, grab irons, brackets, truck castings — parts hung on racks or placed on a table/conveyor.

Interior painting/coating work: repainting interior walls, ceilings and panels of boxcar/hopper/transit car bodies during overhaul, and interior lining application inside tank cars via the manway; confined, enclosed surfaces.

tasks.label: Repair and maintain electrical and electronic controls for propulsion and braking systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Transit rail car (metro/light-rail vehicle) in a maintenance shop with a reported propulsion fault: technician connects a laptop to the train control/monitoring system, reads fault logs, then opens underfloor or roof equipment cabinets to megger cables, check contactors, gate-driver boards, current/speed sensors and harness connectors, isolates the failed element, replaces the control card or component, and test-runs the car before release.

Locomotive or transit car electronic brake system repair in the shop: diagnosing and repairing electro-pneumatic brake control equipment (e.g., microprocessor brake control units, EP valve driver boards, pressure transducers, trainline wiring, ECP/EOT electronics), replacing failed modules or wiring, then running a full air-brake/functional test to acceptance.

Field troubleshooting on a yard repair track or ready track, outdoors in whatever weather: a car or locomotive has cut out its propulsion or brakes; the repairer works from a truck with meters and spare modules, traces chafed wires, blown fuses, tripped breakers, failed contactors or speed sensors under and between cars, makes the repair on the spot, and releases the equipment.

Scheduled preventive maintenance of electrical/electronic propulsion and brake controls in the shop: insulation-resistance testing traction motor and high-voltage cables, cleaning and re-torquing terminations in HV boxes and control cabinets, dressing/replacing contactor tips and brushes, checking batteries/chargers and grounds, verifying control software/parameters, documenting results.

Bench work in a component shop: a removed propulsion control rack, brake control unit or logic card is set on a test stand, powered and functionally tested to isolate the fault, a faulty card, relay or (occasionally) board-level component is replaced or reworked, and the unit is retested and tagged serviceable.
