It is the closest published work to dismantling an engine, but only one elementary operation (pin extraction) was automated in a laboratory rig, so it does not substantiate whole-engine teardown, defect diagnosis, part repair or reassembly.

tasks.label: Connect test panels to engines and measure generator output, ignition timing, or other engine performance indicators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership or independent shop service bay: technician locates the bike's diagnostic connector (often under the seat, tank, or a side cover), plugs in the manufacturer scan tool (e.g., Harley Digital Technician, Yamaha YDT, BMW ISTA), starts the engine and reads fault codes and live sensor data (rpm, TPS, coolant temp, battery voltage) at idle and raised rpm on a late-model EFI motorcycle.

Charging-system test in the shop: remove seat/side panels, disconnect or back-probe stator and regulator/rectifier connectors, measure stator AC output at specified rpm, DC charging voltage and current under electrical load with a multimeter/load tester, plus resistance and leakage checks; bikes range from clean late models to dirty, corroded, crash-damaged, or heavily modified machines.

Ignition timing check on an older, carbureted, or points-equipped bike: remove the timing inspection plug, clip an inductive pickup timing light to the spark plug lead, run the engine at specified rpm and read the advance marks through the inspection window (or set static timing), adjusting the pickup/points plate as needed.

Cylinder condition measurement in the shop: remove spark plugs, thread a compression or leak-down gauge into the plug hole (sometimes with adapters), crank or run the engine with throttle held open, and record pressures/leakage across cylinders; may include a vacuum-gauge reading at the intake for a running engine.

Chassis dyno session in a shop dyno room: strap and fixture the bike on the rollers, connect rpm pickup, lambda/exhaust sniffer and any datalogging leads, run the engine through rpm sweeps under load and record power, torque and air-fuel ratio to verify a tune or a performance complaint.

Mobile or field service: check charging output, run a scan-tool read, or check timing on a bike at a customer's driveway, a rally, a race paddock, or roadside, using portable meters and a battery-powered scan tool in uncontrolled lighting, weather and space.

It is the same physical act the mechanic performs — mating a test panel's fluid, power and data lines to an engine and running a measurement sequence — on comparable objects (complete IC engines) at production precision, but with the engine fixtured on a pallet in a purpose-built cell.

The dyno session's physical demand — holding the vehicle at commanded speed/rpm through a sweep while instrumentation logs performance — is performed by the robot instead of a rider, in the same class of purpose-built test cell.

sources.claim: A one-arm robot autonomously locates an electric vehicle's charging port and inserts and removes the connector in a parking structure, but only for a single standardized port whose position the vehicle communicates; it performs no measurement or disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connector insertion into a vehicle in a human-standard facility (E2). Cited to bound E2: it shows only standardized-port mating on a car that reports its port location, not locating varied motorcycle diagnostic connectors, removing bodywork, probing stator leads, or running and reading an engine measurement sequence.

tasks.label: Listen to engines, examine vehicle frames, or confer with customers to determine nature and extent of malfunction or damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop-bay physical examination of a bike brought in with a complaint or after a crash: mechanic puts the machine on a lift or stand, inspects frame, forks, swingarm, welds and mounts for bends/cracks, checks chain, brakes, tires, fasteners and leaks, and judges the nature and extent of damage (e.g. 'steering head tweaked, fork tube bent, frame serviceable').

Running-engine diagnosis in the service bay: mechanic starts the engine, listens at idle and under throttle (often with a stethoscope or by ear near the cases, head and exhaust), localizes a knock, top-end tick, cam-chain rattle, bearing whine, misfire or exhaust leak, and rates severity.

Conferring with the customer at the service counter or on the phone at a dealership or independent shop: eliciting when and how the symptom occurs, riding history, prior repairs, walking around the bike with the owner as they point out noises or damage, then translating that into a diagnostic direction.

Road test: mechanic rides the motorcycle on public streets/highway to reproduce and characterize an intermittent complaint (wobble, clutch slip, surging, noise only under load, brake pulsation) in mixed traffic and unpredictable road conditions.

Field or mobile diagnosis with the machine as found: mobile mechanic at a customer's home garage or roadside, or a technician at a motocross track/rally, diagnosing a no-start, a strange noise or crash damage without a lift, without shop lighting and with whatever the site offers.

sources.system: Discom by HBK acoustic end-of-line (EoL) engine test system (ROTAS)
sources.date: 2020-12 (product page), product line in commercial use through 2026
sources.title: Combustion engine - Discom (HBK Acoustic End-of-Line Test Systems)
sources.claim: Discom (HBK) acoustic end-of-line test systems run combustion engines on production test stands and automatically detect specific mechanical faults from sound/vibration signatures - camshaft and crankshaft unbalance, cylinder knocking, valve rattling, mispositioned balance shafts - i.e. machine 'listening' that names the fault.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production end-of-line acoustic testing of engines. It transfers to 'listen to engines to determine nature of malfunction' because the machine judges a running internal-combustion engine by the same acoustic cues a motorcycle mechanic uses (knock, valve rattle, unbalance, bearing noise) and outputs a named fault; it requires the engine fixtured on a purpose-built test stand, which is exactly the E1 presentation.

sources.system: Discom by HBK NVH end-of-line test bench
sources.title: NVH End-of-Line (EoL) Testing / The Future of NVH End of Line Testing (Quality Magazine)
sources.claim: The same class of EoL acoustic system reliably detects internal defects in closed assemblies (gears, bearings, shifting mechanisms) on the test bench, and Discom engineers re-tuned an OEM's bench so it could catch faulty rotor-shaft bearings that the previous system missed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acoustic fault detection on drivetrain assemblies at a production test stand. Transfers to diagnosing engine/drivetrain noise on a motorcycle because the objects (bearings, gears, shafts) and the acoustic diagnosis are the same; only in a fixtured test-cell setting.

sources.system: Spot with Fluke SV600 / Sorama L642 acoustic imaging payload
sources.title: Acoustic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics sells an autonomous acoustic-inspection capability on the Spot quadruped: the robot walks a taught route in a facility, captures beamformed acoustic images of running equipment and flags leaks, abnormal vibration and failing bearings against a nominal baseline.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous acoustic condition monitoring of machinery inside a human work facility. It shows machine listening for faults at E2, but only on fixed assets already running, with a learned per-asset baseline; it cannot start or operate an arbitrary customer vehicle or diagnose an unfamiliar machine.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) at ST Engineering MRAS
sources.title: Boston Dynamics' robot dog patrols 1.5 million-square-foot factory
sources.claim: Spot is deployed in a 1.5-million-sq-ft aerospace manufacturing plant where it autonomously patrols and inspects fixed production equipment with thermal and acoustic sensors to catch abnormal vibration and leaks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous walk-around machine-health inspection in a structured facility (E2). Shows the environment ceiling actually achieved by mobile inspection robots - fixed, pre-taught assets - not free-form diagnosis of arbitrary vehicles brought into a shop.

sources.system: ZEISS ABIS III automated surface inspection (robot-guided)
sources.title: Revolutionize Your Factory with ABIS III | ZEISS
sources.claim: ZEISS ABIS III is a robot-mounted optical surface-inspection sensor used in press shops and body shops that automatically and reproducibly finds structural/surface defects on sheet-metal and body parts, including cracks, dents and necking, within seconds per part.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect inspection of welded/formed vehicle structures in a fixtured robotic cell. Transfers to 'examine vehicle frames to determine nature and extent of damage' because a bent or cracked frame is exactly a geometry/surface defect on welded metal, judged against a nominal, at comparable or finer precision.

sources.system: ZEISS ScanBox / ATOS ScanBox Series 8 robotic optical 3D measuring cell
sources.date: 2024-10 (listing); systems in OEM use for years

sources.claim: ZEISS/GOM ScanBox robotic measuring cells (up to two robots per cell) automatically digitize parts and complete vehicle bodies and compare the resulting 3D model against CAD, programming, scanning, inspecting and reporting automatically inside a purpose-built enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic full-vehicle/body dimensional inspection against CAD. Transfers to assessing frame/chassis damage extent, which a mechanic determines by checking alignment and geometry against spec; the cell requires the workpiece fixtured and presented, i.e. an E1 setting.

sources.system: UVeye Atlas/Helios/Artemis automated vehicle inspection systems
sources.title: UVeye's Vehicle Inspection Systems Keep Fleets Safe and On The Road
sources.claim: UVeye's automated drive-through inspection installations, in use in the service lanes of hundreds of US dealerships, scan a vehicle in seconds and automatically report undercarriage/frame damage, fluid and oil leaks, brake-line and exhaust problems, tire wear and body damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated condition/damage inspection of a whole vehicle at a service lane. Same purpose as the mechanic's walk-around examination (name the damage and its extent), but it is a fixed purpose-built portal the vehicle must be driven through, and it is built for cars/trucks, not motorcycles - so it supports only the E1 counterfactual.

tasks.label: Repair or replace other parts, such as headlights, horns, handlebar controls, gasoline or oil tanks, starters, or mufflers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership or independent shop service bay: replace failed lighting and simple electrical bolt-ons on a customer street bike (headlight bulb or assembly, turn signal, horn) - remove bezel/fairing fasteners, unplug connector, fit new unit, refit trim, test and aim the light.

Shop bay: replace a muffler/slip-on or full exhaust (rusted or damaged OEM unit, or an aftermarket accessory install) - break loose seized clamp and heat-shield bolts, remove old can, fit gasket and hangers, align, torque, run engine and check for leaks/fitment.

Shop bay: replace handlebar controls and related items after a drop or wear - switchgear housings, levers, mirrors, throttle/clutch cables and grips; route cables and harness, reconnect connectors, set free play, verify switch and kill-switch function.

Shop bay: remove and replace fuel tank or its hardware (tank, petcock, in-tank fuel pump, vent/fuel lines) - drain gasoline, disconnect fuel lines and sender wiring, unbolt and lift tank off frame, refit with new seals, refill, pressure/leak check.

Shop bay: starter motor or starter clutch replacement on a mid-size or touring bike - strip bodywork/exhaust/coolant hoses as needed for access, unbolt starter from engine case, seal and torque new unit, reassemble, verify cranking.

Mobile/field service: replacement of a failed part (headlight, muffler bracket, horn, starter) at a customer's driveway, garage, rally site, or roadside, with the bike as found, uneven ground, and only van-carried tools.

Transfer is only partial: objects are comparable (vehicle lighting, bolted body parts) but the work is single-model, fixtured, with new parts and known fastener condition, and excludes removal of a used part, connector work on a worn harness, and functional verification.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous unbolting of a used, variable product in a fixtured cell. Supports only the fastener-removal sub-step of replacing a motorcycle part; no replacement component is fitted, sealed, connected or function-tested.

sources.system: RoboTire automated wheel-changing system
sources.title: Discount Tire testing RoboTire system for use in stores | Tire Business
sources.claim: RoboTire, deployed in Discount Tire and other tire stores, autonomously locates the wheel with 3D vision and removes/installs lug nuts and the wheel assembly, but a human operator performs the tire demount/mount - the most mature vehicle-service robot handles only the standardized wheel, not other vehicle parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-vehicle bolt-off/bolt-on of a component inside a service facility. Objects are not comparable to headlights, mufflers, tanks or starters: lug patterns and wheels are standardized and externally accessible, with no connectors, gaskets, fluids or cable adjustment involved.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Automated Tire's SmartBay, unveiled May 2026 as an AI robotic service-bay platform, is semi-automated in its first generation: a human operator still removes the used tire, positions the new one and connects the air line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work inside a human service bay (E2). Shows the 2026 frontier of shop-floor vehicle service robotics is tire work with human steps still required; it does not substantiate any non-tire part replacement.

sources.system: NIO Power Swap Station 3.0/4.0
sources.title: NIO Power Swap Station 4.0 Now Operational - News | NIO
sources.claim: NIO Power Swap Station 4.0 performs a fully automatic exchange of a vehicle's bolted battery module in 144 seconds in a purpose-built station, deployed at thousands of sites - but on vehicles engineered with a robot-swappable interface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal and replacement of a large bolted vehicle module in a purpose-built station. Transfer fails here because interface, fastener pattern and connectors are co-designed for the machine on one vehicle family, whereas motorcycle tanks, mufflers and starters present varied, seized or hidden fasteners plus hose and harness work the station never performs.

tasks.label: Disassemble subassembly units and examine condition, movement, or alignment of parts, visually or using gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/independent motorcycle shop: engine pulled and mounted on a stand; mechanic strips the top end (valve cover, cam chain, cylinder head, cylinder, piston) of a used, oily, carboned engine, removes valves with a spring compressor, then measures bore diameter/taper with a bore gauge, piston and valve-stem diameters with a micrometer, ring end gap and valve-guide play with feeler gauges, and visually judges scoring, seat wear and discoloration.

Shop service bay: brake and wheel subassemblies taken apart - caliper unbolted and split, pistons and seals extracted, wheel pulled and bearings/seals checked for play and roughness by hand, rotor thickness measured with a micrometer and runout with a dial indicator, chain/sprocket and axle alignment checked; parts are corroded, greasy and vary by model.

Shop bench: carburetor bank or throttle-body/fuel subassembly disassembled - float bowls, floats, needle/seat, main and pilot jets, slides and diaphragms removed with small fasteners often varnished or seized, each part inspected visually and float height checked with a gauge.

Shop bench: front fork legs or rear shock disassembled - caps, springs, damper rods, bushings and seals removed, oil drained, tubes checked for straightness with V-blocks and a dial indicator, bushings and seal surfaces inspected for wear and pitting.

Shop bench: clutch and gearbox subassemblies torn down - primary/side cover pried off its gasket, pressure plate and springs released, friction and steel plates lifted out of oil, plate thickness measured with a micrometer, warpage checked with feeler gauge and surface plate, gear dogs, shift forks and bearings inspected for wear and free movement.

Field/mobile work: teardown and inspection of a subassembly away from the shop - customer's garage or driveway, race paddock, dealer lot, or a rental/fleet site - with portable tools on a tarp or tailgate, variable lighting and footing, and the bike parked as found.

sources.system: Non-destructive robotic disassembly platform (four-robot cell with vision-guided nutrunner)
sources.developer: University of Birmingham (Yongjing Wang et al.)
sources.title: Robotic Disassembly Platform for Disassembly of a Plug-In Hybrid Electric Vehicle Battery: A Case Study
sources.claim: A four-robot purpose-built cell autonomously performed non-destructive teardown of a used plug-in hybrid EV battery pack into modules, including 82 vision-guided unscrewing operations and nutrunner adapter changes; cable ties, harnesses and coolant-pad separation were simplified or excluded, and no gauge inspection of parts was performed.
sources.transferJustification: Closest demonstrated analogue to 'disassemble a subassembly unit': autonomous unbolting and extraction of parts from a used product in a fixtured cell. Transfer is only partial - one known product, threaded fasteners only, no gasket prying, press fits, spring-loaded parts, or gauge-based examination of part condition.

sources.system: Q-Span Gauging System (UR3e/UR5e-based workstation)
sources.title: Q-Span Systems | Automated Small Part Measurement | New Scale Robotics
sources.claim: Commercial benchtop robotic gauging workstations autonomously handle small parts from trays and take dimensional measurements with standard shop metrology (digital calipers, micrometers, bore gauges, linear probes), logging results; parts must already be separated and presented in trays or fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Substantiates the 'examine ... using gauges' half of the task with the same instruments a mechanic uses, but only for already-disassembled parts presented in a purpose-built cell; it performs no disassembly and no wear/condition judgment on worn assemblies.

sources.system: Robotic measurement cell (Mitutoyo CMM plus Engineering Data robot)
sources.title: Robotic measurement cells removes bottleneck in parts inspection process
sources.claim: A deployed robotic measurement cell loads fixtured parts onto a coordinate measuring machine and runs dimensional inspection programs unattended, cycling through stored pallets of parts in a manufacturer's quality department.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional inspection of parts. Shows measurement and alignment checking is automatable in a purpose-built cell on fixtured, pre-programmed parts, but the cell neither disassembles anything nor judges wear on used components.

sources.system: Vision-based robotic aircraft-engine disassembly (YOLO-SAM pipeline)
sources.title: Vision-based robotic disassembly of aircraft engines with YOLO-SAM: a novel method for task orientation estimation
sources.claim: Research system uses vision (YOLO plus SAM) to detect and orient toward removable, worn bolts on aircraft engines for robotic disassembly, independent of engine model; the demonstrated scope is bolt detection and removal, not full teardown or part inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown of a used engine. Nearest engine-specific work, but covers only fastener detection/removal in a lab cell; nothing about splitting gasketed joints, extracting press-fit parts, or gauge measurement of clearances.

sources.system: Recirculate robotic battery disassembly cell (KUKA KR10)
sources.developer: Centria University of Applied Sciences / Recirculate project
sources.title: Recirculate project pioneers robotic EV battery disassembly system
sources.claim: A purpose-built robotic cell built around a KUKA KR10 on a linear track autonomously detects and disassembles EV battery packs for second-life processing in an EU project pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of a used assembly. Confirms that where teardown is automated it is done in a cell purpose-built around one product family, not on the heterogeneous used assemblies a motorcycle mechanic strips.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly systems in remanufacturing (state of the art review)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: Industry review of remanufacturing automation states that robotic disassembly of used products is only beginning to emerge and that seized bolts, deformed parts and ... remain major obstacles, leaving teardown largely to skilled human technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Context on the same underlying activity (teardown plus condition assessment of used mechanical assemblies); cited only to characterise the state of the art, not to support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Repair or adjust motorcycle subassemblies, such as forks, transmissions, brakes, or drive chains, according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership or independent motorcycle shop service bay: drive chain and final-drive service on a customer street bike on a lift — loosen axle, set chain slack and wheel alignment to spec, clean/lube, or replace chain and sprockets, torque axle to spec, road-test feel.

Shop service bay: brake system repair on a used bike — remove wheel/caliper, replace pads and worn rotors, clean and rebuild seized caliper pistons, replace fluid and bleed hydraulic lines, adjust lever/pedal free play, verify no drag or spongy feel.

Shop service bay: front fork / suspension subassembly work — remove forks from triple clamps, disassemble legs, replace leaking seals and bushings, refill damping oil to measured level, reassemble, set preload/damping and sag to specification.

Shop bench work: engine-internal driveline repair — clutch pack replacement, primary drive, or gearbox teardown to replace worn shift forks/dogs and bearings on a dirty used unit, reassembled with new gaskets and torqued to spec, then run-tested for shifting quality.

Off-site work in an unstructured setting — mobile mechanic in a customer's driveway/garage, or trackside/trailside dirt-bike repair: adjust or bleed brakes, adjust chain, straighten or swap bent levers and adjust fork clickers, with only portable tools and no lift.

Powersports/rental-fleet shop: scooter, moped or ATV subassembly work — CVT/variator and belt service, drum brake shoe replacement and cable adjustment, on high-mileage, corroded units with seized or rounded fasteners.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced automation actually entering automotive service bays as of mid-2026 is a semi-automated tire changer that still requires a human operator for several steps; it does no subassembly repair.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest deployed automation in a vehicle service bay (an E2 human work facility). It covers only tire mounting on cars, with human steps each cycle, so it does not substantiate repair or adjustment of motorcycle forks, brakes, transmissions or chains.

sources.system: RoboTire tire-changing system
sources.title: AI-powered RoboTire can change 4 tires twice as fast as a human | Fox News
sources.claim: A vision-guided robotic cell installed in tire stores removed and reinstalled car wheels by unscrewing lug nuts; the task is limited to wheel/tire handling and the company later went bankrupt.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = wheel removal on cars, a preliminary step to brake work. It demonstrates only fastener removal on standardized lug patterns in a purpose-built bay; it does not demonstrate caliper rebuild, bleeding, fork or gearbox repair on used motorcycle assemblies.

sources.system: Experimental robotic disassembly cell for EV battery modules
sources.developer: University of Birmingham (Wang et al., Journal of Remanufacturing)
sources.title: An experimental robotic cell for the disassembly of electric vehicle battery modules
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic disassembly of used vehicle assemblies remains a research prototype cell run on mock-up modules, limited to unfastening/removal steps rather than diagnosis, repair and reassembly to specification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic disassembly of end-of-life vehicle assemblies in a fenced cell (E1). It shows the frontier is fastener removal on known mock-up geometries, not fault-specific repair of worn motorcycle subassemblies, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task even at E1.

sources.system: e-Bike motor assembly robot system
sources.title: The e-Bike Motor Assembly: Towards Advanced Robotic Manipulation for Flexible Manufacturing (arXiv)
sources.claim: Robotic assembly of a two-wheeler drive subassembly (e-bike motor) with new, presented components is still framed as a research demonstration of flexible manipulation, not a fielded capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = assembly of a two-wheeler drive subassembly in a structured industrial cell. It uses clean new parts staged for the robot and omits diagnosis, teardown of a worn unit, fluid work and torque-to-spec verification, so it does not carry over to repairing motorcycle subassemblies.

tasks.label: Reassemble frames and reinstall engines after repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Independent shop or dealership service bay: mid-size street/sport/cruiser motorcycle whose engine was pulled for a rebuild. Tech hoists the engine back into the frame, threads long through-bolts and spacers through frame lugs, torques mounts to spec, then reconnects wiring harness connectors, oil/coolant lines, exhaust, intake/throttle bodies, clutch and throttle cables, shift linkage and drive chain, refills fluids and verifies it runs.

Shop bay, dirt bike / scooter / small-displacement single or moped: lighter engine (30-80 lb) lifted back into frame by hand or small stand, mount bolts and skid plate refitted, carb/injector, CDI and stator connectors, kickstarter/shift lever, exhaust, chain and plastics/bodywork reinstalled, then run-tested.

Shop bay, chassis reassembly after suspension service or crash repair with no engine drop: swingarm and pivot shaft, shocks/linkage, fork legs and triple clamps, subframe, wheels and brake calipers, fasteners and plastic bodywork panels refitted, aligned, torqued and safety-checked.

Restoration or custom shop: vintage, heavily modified or one-off bike. Non-standard, fabricated or aftermarket parts, corroded or seized fasteners, no factory fitment; requires trial fitting, shimming, chasing threads and improvised routing of cables and wiring before the engine and chassis go back together.

Dealership bay, heavy touring bike or big-twin: 150-250 lb engine/transmission assembly maneuvered into a tight frame with a jack or hoist, precise alignment of mounts and isolators, then reconnection of extensive accessory wiring, ABS lines, exhaust and drive components.

Field or mobile service: race paddock or trailer, customer's home garage, or roadside. Engine or chassis reassembly performed on uneven ground with portable tools, ad-hoc supports, variable lighting and weather, and whatever parts are on hand.

sources.system: Auto & Multi-Fasten Chassis Marriage system
sources.date: 2026-06 (product page retrieved; product line in service for years)
sources.title: Auto & Multi-Fasten Chassis Marriage - Fori Automation
sources.claim: Commercially supplied chassis marriage lines automatically fasten a powertrain/chassis module to a vehicle body with automated torque tooling or robots in an automotive assembly line (a purpose-built, fenced cell).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining a powertrain to a vehicle chassis and torquing its mount bolts. It transfers only to the single bolt-up step, with brand-new, dimensionally identical parts arriving on dedicated per-model pallets; it does not cover threading used fasteners, reconnecting harness connectors, hoses, cables, exhaust and drive components that a repair reinstall requires, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.

sources.system: Learned connector-assembly policies (behavioral cloning study)
sources.title: Behavioral Cloning for Robotic Connector Assembly: An Empirical Study
sources.claim: Automotive wire-harness routing and connector insertion, a core part of reconnecting an engine after reinstallation, remains largely a manual operation in vehicle production despite decades of industrial automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting electrical connectors and handling harnesses on vehicles. Directly relevant because reinstalling a motorcycle engine requires plugging stator, ignition, sensor and injector connectors and routing deformable harnesses; the literature shows only isolated lab-scale insertion, not whole-vehicle reconnection.

sources.system: UC Berkeley furniture-assembly robot (as assessed by Epoch AI)
sources.developer: UC Berkeley / assessment by Epoch AI
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: Independent 2026 assessment of robot autonomy finds multi-step assembly with tools and varied parts (IKEA-furniture-level) is at an early research stage; the leading demonstration handles one plank type and a human does the screwing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous multi-step mechanical assembly of a fastened structure from varied parts. Motorcycle reassembly is far harder (heavier parts, dozens of fastener types, deformable harnesses/hoses, torque specs), so failure here is strong evidence the whole instance is not completable even in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Electric Atlas
sources.title: Beyond the Lab: Boston Dynamics' Electric Atlas Begins Autonomous Shift at Hyundai's Georgia Metaplant
sources.claim: A humanoid robot is running autonomous parts sequencing and heavy-lifting shifts inside an automotive plant, but the work is moving and staging parts, not installing or fastening them onto vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling of heavy automotive parts inside a vehicle plant. It shows current humanoids handle and sequence parts but stops short of bolting components into vehicles, so it cannot substantiate engine reinstallation or chassis reassembly.

sources.system: SmartBay autonomous tire-changing system
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced robot deployed in a vehicle service bay changes tires while leaving wheels on the car specifically to avoid the fastener work, and still needs a human to handle the tires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic vehicle service work performed in a repair shop bay (E2). It marks the current frontier of in-shop service robotics — one highly standardized operation with human assistance — far below the multi-part, multi-fastener reassembly required here.

sources.system: Motorcycle/E-scooter assembly line (vendor product)
sources.title: Motorcycle Assembly Line Design Plan and Manufacture — E-scooter Assembly Line
sources.claim: A motorcycle assembly-line vendor advertises that the powertrain is lowered into the frame by ... on a new-build line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing an engine into a motorcycle frame on a new-build line. The wording does not distinguish a robot from an operator-guided hoist and gives no evidence of autonomous bolting, so autonomy is unclear and it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Remove cylinder heads and grind valves to scrape off carbon and replace defective valves, pistons, cylinders, or rings, using hand and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership or independent shop, modern four-stroke street/sport bike: drain fluids, strip fairings/tank/exhaust, remove cam chain and cylinder head, scrape carbon from chambers and valve faces, lap or replace valves and seals, check seats and shim clearances, install new gaskets, reassemble to torque sequence and cam timing, run and leak-check.

Powersports shop, dirt bike/two-stroke or small four-stroke top-end: pull pipe and cylinder, remove circlips, wrist pin and piston, measure bore/plating and ring end gap, decarbonize head and exhaust port, fit new piston, rings and base/head gaskets, reassemble and test.

Older, vintage or neglected engine with unknown history: seized, rounded or corroded head fasteners needing heat, penetrant or extraction; head stuck to gasket; heavy carbon; valve grinding/lapping, guide and seat work possibly sent to a machine shop; parts sourcing and improvised fitment; done in an independent shop.

Race/performance shop rebuild between events: teardown, precision measurement of bore, taper and clearances, oversize or forged pistons after rebore, full valve job with new springs/valves, blueprinted reassembly to spec under time pressure.

Mobile/field service: trackside pit, customer's garage, farm or transport trailer - top-end repair with portable tools, bike on a stand or the ground, variable lighting, weather and no bench or fixturing.

sources.system: AUTOREMAN robotic disassembly testbed (University of Birmingham Autonomous Remanufacturing Laboratory)
sources.developer: University of Birmingham (D.T. Pham group), EPSRC AUTOREMAN programme
sources.title: Disassembly demonstration key to robotic remanufacturing
sources.claim: State of the art in robotic disassembly of engine-type assemblies is a laboratory demonstration of one elementary operation - extracting pins from holes - with researchers noting that disassembly automation is ad hoc and confounded by unknown component size, shape and condition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown of internal-combustion engine cores for remanufacturing. It bounds this task from above - head removal, decarbonizing and valve work are far beyond single pin extraction - so it supports no positive judgment.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly systems in remanufacturing (industry survey)
sources.developer: various integrators (survey by Robotics & Automation News)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: Industry review of remanufacturing automation (2026) reports robotic disassembly systems are only beginning to emerge and that seized bolts, deformed parts and ... defeat automation, leaving the work with skilled human technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown/rebuild of used mechanical assemblies. Establishes that the fastener-removal and used-part variability central to a top-end overhaul is not solved even in dedicated remanufacturing plants.

sources.system: Piston ringer assembly cell (6-axis robot + 6 rotary tables)
sources.developer: Patti Engineering (integrator) for heavy equipment manufacturer
sources.title: Case Studies: Piston Ringer Assembly: Rewriting the Code
sources.claim: A fully automated fenced cell with a 6-axis robot and rotary tables installs piston rings on new piston sets presented on pallets in a heavy-equipment engine plant - an E1 sub-step of assembly only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic piston-ring fitting on a new-engine line. Covers only ring installation on clean, identical new parts arriving on pallets; no teardown of a used engine, wear measurement, carbon removal or refitting to a worn cylinder, so it cannot substantiate the whole instance.

sources.system: Industrial cylinder head automated finishing cell (track-mounted dual robots, Cognex vision)
sources.developer: Midwest Engineered Systems (MWES) for an industrial engine manufacturer
sources.title: Industrial Cylinder Heads Assembly Automation | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: A fully automated dual-robot cell processes four models of new diesel cylinder heads (vision ID, heated wash, shot peen, plug-insertion inspection, cooling) on a production line at a 3-minute cycle with one supervising operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and finishing of cylinder heads in a purpose-built cell. It handles new machined heads of known geometry presented by conveyor; it performs no head removal from an engine, no valve grinding or lapping, and no work on carboned used parts.

sources.system: SmartBay tire-changing system (and predecessor RoboTire)
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay
sources.claim: Even the far simpler vehicle-service task of changing tires in a service bay is only semi-automated in 2026: the newest system requires a human to remove the used tire ... one, and the earlier autonomous wheel-changing company RoboTire went bankrupt.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work on customer vehicles in a repair shop (E2). If wheel/tire service - coarse, standardized, accessible - still needs a human in the loop, no cited shop-floor system covers engine teardown and valve work.

tasks.label: Install motorcycle accessories.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/independent shop service bay: simple external bolt-on hard parts on a customer's bike — windshield/windscreen, luggage rack, backrest or sissy bar, engine guard/highway bars, footpegs, mirrors, chrome/trim covers. Tech unpacks the kit, removes a few stock fasteners, positions the bracket (often holding a nyloc nut behind the mount), applies threadlocker, torques to spec and checks alignment/clearance.

Electrical accessories in the service bay: heated grips, auxiliary LED driving lights, GPS/USB power, alarm/security module, audio kit. Requires removing seat/tank/side panels, routing the loom along the frame away from heat and steering travel, splicing or connecting to the harness/fuse block, zip-tying, reassembly and function test.

Exhaust/intake/performance accessory: remove heat-cycled stock muffler or full system (springs, clamps, gaskets, heat shields), fit slip-on or full system with new gaskets, install high-flow air cleaner, load ECU tune, run engine and check for leaks and heat-shield rattles.

Handlebar, control, grip and seat accessories: replacement handlebars requiring rerouting or replacing cables, brake lines and switch wiring; custom grips fitted with adhesive or compressed air; levers, risers, floorboards; seat swap where a tongue must slide under a frame tab before the stud is bolted.

Complex/custom fitment jobs: bagger/fairing conversion kits, hard-bag conversions, ATV/UTV winch and plow mounts, aftermarket parts with poor instructions requiring test fitting, drilling, trimming, shimming or fabricating a bracket, plus judgment on clearance and safety.

Off-site/mobile install at a customer's garage or driveway, a rally, or a race paddock: a simple bolt-on accessory fitted with portable tools, bike on its sidestand or a portable stand, uneven ground and variable light.

sources.system: SICK TriSpector1030 3D vision + collaborative robot bolt-tightening station
sources.title: Comparison of 3D Sensors for Automating Bolt-Tightening Operations in the Automotive Industry (Sensors)
sources.claim: A vision-guided collaborative robot performing bolt tightening on vehicles moving through an automotive assembly line station was deployed in production, tightening fasteners located by 3D perception despite conveyor position variation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torquing threaded fasteners on a vehicle whose pose varies. Motorcycle accessory installation ends in the same act — driving and torquing M6–M10 fasteners at known bracket locations on a vehicle — so the fastening capability transfers to a fixtured bike in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Vision-guided robotic bolt-tightening station (van rear axle damper)
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Trade-press account of the same deployment: the human assembler still picks the part from a bin, installs it on the vehicle and hand-starts the bolts; the robot only performs the final tightening.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task; this source bounds it — even inside a car plant the part placement and bolt hand-start remain human, showing the limits of robotic part attachment outside fully purpose-built cells.

sources.system: RoboTire System (Discount Tire stores)
sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: A commercial robotic system installed in tire stores removed lug nuts, removed wheel/tire assemblies from customer vehicles and re-installed them, with the vehicle raised and the wheel held by purpose-built tooling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detaching and re-attaching a bolted component to a vehicle with torqued threaded fasteners in a purpose-built bay. Comparable object scale and fastener precision to bolting a rack, guard or windshield bracket to a fixtured motorcycle.

sources.system: RoboTire
sources.title: AI-powered RoboTire can change 4 tires twice as fast as a human | Fox News
sources.claim: RoboTire's machine vision located wheels and lugs and guided the arms to unscrew and remove nuts or bolts autonomously, handling varying wheel sizes and bolt patterns, with a human technician assisting other steps and supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task as above: vision-located fastener removal and installation on a vehicle. Establishes autonomy (not teleoperation) for the fastener-handling steps a bolt-on accessory install shares.

sources.system: Skill-based force-controlled connector installation system
sources.title: Automotive Wire Harness Connector Installation Using Skill-Based Robotic Programming (European Robotics Forum 2025)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art force-controlled robotic installation of automotive wire-harness connectors reached only 76.7% success on a car door in a laboratory validation.
sources.transferJustification: Bears directly on accessory wiring: mating a harness connector is the easiest sub-step of an electrical accessory install, and even that is only ~77% reliable in a lab, below employer-acceptable reliability.

sources.system: Robotic windshield insertion cells on automotive assembly lines
sources.title: Sensors Make Robots Smarter When Inserting Vehicle Windshields | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Six-axis robots pick windshields with suction cups from a fixed location and insert them into car bodies on the assembly line, a long-standing automated part-placement operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precisely placing a large part onto a vehicle presented in a known position — the placement half of bolting a windshield, fairing or luggage rack onto a fixtured motorcycle.

sources.system: FANUC M-10iA/M-20iA robotic screwdriving workcells
sources.title: Automated Screwdriving: What's New | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robotic screwdriving workcells with automatic screw feeders and torque/angle/depth monitoring are standard commercial automation; an integrator installed 30 FANUC robots across three screwdriving workcells in an automobile plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: feeding, driving and torque-verifying threaded fasteners on fixtured workpieces in a purpose-built cell — the fastening core of a bolt-on accessory install once the bike and hardware are presented.

sources.system: BMW Group Plant Berlin motorcycle production
sources.title: BMW Group: 4,000,000 motorcycles made in Berlin
sources.claim: At BMW's highly automated Berlin motorcycle plant, robots handle machining, welding and painting, but motorcycle joining/assembly is still described as resting on human work.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the negative judgments: even in a purpose-built motorcycle factory, attaching parts to a bike (cables, hoses, small hardware, many variants) is done by people, indicating no fielded system performs varied motorcycle part fitting.

tasks.label: Reassemble and test subassembly units.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership or independent motorcycle shop, engine on a bench or stand: reassemble the top end of a used engine — rings on pistons, pistons into bores, base/head gasket, cylinder, head with valves, seals and keepers, cam chain and timing, torque sequence to spec, valve clearance shims — then turn it over and verify by leak-down/compression test.

Shop bench work on lower-end subassemblies: crankcase halves with crank and bearings, transmission gear cluster and shift drum/forks, clutch basket and friction/steel plate stack, primary drive; shims and endplay checked, then rotated and shifted through the gears to verify action before installation.

Bench rebuild and test of fuel-system subassemblies on varied, often varnished/corroded used cores: carburetor jets, needle and seat, float and float height, slide/diaphragm, o-rings and gaskets (or throttle body/fuel pump units); bench-checked for float level, leaks and bank synchronization.

Bench rebuild of hydraulic subassemblies in the shop: brake caliper pistons with square-cut seals and dust boots, master cylinder kits, fork legs with seals, bushings, damper rods and measured oil level, or rear shock; then pressure/leak-tested and stroked to check action.

Wheel, final-drive and electrical subassemblies in the shop: press wheel bearings and seals into hubs, cush drive and sprocket carrier, mount and balance a tire, or rebuild a starter motor/charging component; spin-checked, torque-checked or bench-tested with a meter/test stand.

Off-site reassembly and test with limited tooling: mobile service van in a customer's driveway or a race paddock/trackside, reassembling a mechanical subassembly (clutch pack, brake caliper, chain/sprocket, suspension linkage) and test-running or stroking it to confirm function before the bike goes back out.

sources.system: Piston ringer assembly cell (Patti Engineering controls upgrade)
sources.title: Case Studies: Piston Ringer Assembly: Rewriting the Code
sources.claim: A fully automated industrial subsystem with a 6-axis robot and rotary tables installs piston rings onto piston sets as part of engine assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is factory engine assembly; ring installation on pistons is the same fiddly operation a mechanic performs when reassembling a motorcycle top end, on comparable parts and clearances, but with fixtured presentation.

tasks.label: Hammer out dents and bends in frames and weld tears and breaks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealer or independent shop: a steel bracket, tab or mount on the frame (footpeg mount, exhaust hanger, sidestand tab, luggage-rack lug) has broken off or torn loose. Mechanic strips/protects surrounding parts, grinds paint and old weld off, clamps the piece back in correct position, tacks, MIG/TIG welds the joint, dresses and paints it.

Shop: a crack or tear in a frame tube, gusset or dirt-bike/ATV subframe. Mechanic finds the crack extent (often stop-drills it), grinds it out to a V-groove through paint and rust, sometimes fabricates and fits a reinforcing gusset, then welds thin-wall tubing without burn-through or distortion, and rechecks alignment.

Shop: crash-damaged bike with a bent frame, subframe or swingarm. Mechanic measures against factory specs, mounts the frame in a jig/straightening bench, applies hydraulic ram pressure with heat, hammers/dollies out local bends and dents, and re-measures until alignment is within spec.

Shop: bent or dented ancillary steel parts straightened by hand — sidestands, footpegs, shift/brake levers, fender stays, handlebar mounts, engine guards, dented exhaust headers — clamped in a vise or on an anvil and hammered/pressed back to shape, checked by fit and eye.

Custom/restoration work: damaged or rusted section of a vintage or custom frame is cut out; mechanic measures, bends/notches replacement tubing or fabricates a bracket, fits and tacks it in a jig, welds it in, and blends the weld so the frame geometry stays true.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 autonomous welding cells
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 robotic welding cells autonomously scan, plan and weld steel parts and are in commercial use in North American fabrication shops; the AF-1 also picks and fits parts without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix arc welding of steel parts inside a robotic cell. It transfers to re-welding a broken steel bracket/tab onto a fixtured motorcycle frame: same material, similar fillet/butt joint sizes and weld quality demands, with the cell locating the joint itself rather than relying on pre-programmed paths.

sources.system: RAMLAB MaxQ Repair (MaxQ Cobot / Fanuc smart repair cells)
sources.title: Patch welding of large castings with MaxQ Repair - RAMLAB
sources.claim: RAMLAB's MaxQ Repair performs one-off repair welding of damaged/worn metal parts end to end: after an operator marks the area, the system scans it, generates an adaptive weld toolpath and deposits the patch, with interpass temperature and process monitoring, on a cobot or Fanuc welding station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repair welding of damaged, one-off steel parts (rails, rotors, dies, castings) whose defect geometry is never the same twice. It shows a robotic cell can scan an unknown damaged region and lay down an accepted repair weld, the core of 'weld tears and breaks' — though demonstrated on heavy sections, not thin-wall tube.

sources.system: Rio Tinto Tiwai Point anode yoke robotic repair cell (Autoa robot welding systems in the same sector)
sources.title: Robotic smelting: how automation is reshaping aluminium production - Mining Technology
sources.claim: Rio Tinto has an automated robotic repair-welding system in production at its Tiwai Point aluminium smelter, using through-arm welding robots plus a handling robot that loads and positions each worn anode yoke.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic repair welding of worn steel assemblies in a purpose-built cell where a handling robot fixtures each part. Comparable weld size and steel structure to re-welding frame brackets; establishes that repair welding is done autonomously in production, not just in demos.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic welding cell (3D camera + laser interferometer seam finding)
sources.developer: Fairmont Machinery / cell integrators (reported by The Fabricator)
sources.title: Uncovering the potential of autonomous robotic welding - The Fabricator
sources.claim: Autonomous welding cells now handle custom, high-product-mix work without dedicated weld fixtures: a 3D camera locates the tacked and clamped part and a laser interferometer finds the seam, adjusting the robot path before welding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: one-off/low-volume arc welding of clamped steel weldments. Supports the E1 counterfactual for bracket re-welding, where the frame and broken piece are held in a fixture and the robot must find the joint on a part it has not been programmed for.

aliases: Small Engine Repair Tech (Small Engine Repair Technician)
roles.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul small engines used to power lawn mowers, chain saws, recreational sporting equipment, and related equipment.

tasks.label: Record repairs made, time spent, and parts used.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Test and inspect engines to determine malfunctions, to locate missing and broken parts, and to verify repairs, using diagnostic instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench diagnosis of a customer's no-start walk-behind mower, snowblower or pressure washer: pull the plug, check spark with an inline tester, take a compression/leak-down reading, check fuel delivery, and identify the failed part (coil, sheared flywheel key, blocked carburetor, worn rings). Independent repair shop or dealer service bay, unit on a bench or lift.

Service-bay diagnosis of a riding mower / lawn tractor that cranks but won't run or has an electrical fault: multimeter checks of charging system, stator, regulator, safety interlock switches and solenoid, plus a run test with tachometer; on EFI/electronic models a scan tool is connected to read fault codes.

Bench diagnosis of a handheld two-stroke (chainsaw, trimmer, blower): spark and compression check, crankcase pressure/vacuum leak test with a pump kit, tachometer reading while setting carburetor limits, inspection for broken or missing components (crank seals, impulse line, cracked cylinder).

Post-repair verification: after a rebuild, carburetor, ignition or valve job, run the engine on a test stand or in the unit, verify RPM with a tachometer, confirm smooth idle and acceleration, check for oil/fuel leaks and abnormal noise, and load-test before returning to the customer. Shop.

Field/on-site testing of installed or non-transportable equipment: load-and-diagnostic test of a standby generator at a customer property, diagnosis of a commercial mower fleet unit at the customer's grounds, or an outboard/utility engine at a dock or job site, in whatever weather and access conditions exist.

sources.system: Polytec laser vibrometer / SonicTC QuickCheck engine cold-test systems
sources.title: End-of-line test for noise and vibration on engines - Polytec (Engine cold test)
sources.claim: Laser-vibrometer engine cold-test systems used in combustion-engine production lines automatically identify specific component and assembly faults (cam shaft deviations, valve clearance, bearing damage, foreign bodies) so targeted repair can be done — i.e., machine diagnosis of an engine's malfunction with instruments in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line engine fault identification in manufacturing. It uses the same physical quantities a mechanic reads with diagnostic instruments (vibration/noise, valve and timing faults, bearing/piston damage) on fixtured internal-combustion engines, so the fault-determination step of shop diagnosis carries over when the engine is presented in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Daifuku Europe cold engine test bench
sources.title: The rise of cold engine test technology | Automotive Powertrain Technology International
sources.claim: Daifuku Europe has installed cold engine test platforms at multiple vehicle OEMs; the benches verify the whole engine and its critical subsystems and the end-of-line system is fully automated with test profiles that enable engine fault diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory end-of-line engine verification. The cell motors and instruments an assembled engine and reports which subsystem is defective — the same determination a mechanic makes with compression, ignition and vacuum instruments — so it transfers to shop diagnosis when the engine is delivered fixtured to the machine.

sources.system: EOLexpertise engine hot test bench (no-load and load EOL hot test)
sources.title: Engine hot test, engine performance test | EOLexpertise
sources.claim: End-of-line engine hot-test benches start and run assembled engines automatically and check start ability, idle stabilisation, acceleration response, cylinder power balance, ignition system integrity, fuel system integrity and sealing (oil/water/air) integrity, verifying assembly deficiencies across the power range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-assembly hot test. It is the same act as a mechanic's post-repair run test — start the engine, confirm idle and acceleration, measure speed and power, check for leaks and abnormal noise — performed automatically on an engine fixtured in a test cell.

sources.system: EOLexpertise end-of-line test rigs with automatic loading (conveyors, portals, grip-arm robots)
sources.title: EOL test, automotive end of line test rig | EOLexpertise
sources.claim: Engine and driveline end-of-line test benches are loaded automatically by conveyors, portals and gripper robots rather than by hand, so the work is brought to and fixtured in the test machine without a human.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: material handling into test cells. It establishes that in a purpose-built setting the unit under test is presented and fixtured by machine, which is the E1 counterfactual condition for the diagnostic instances.

sources.system: ACS end-of-line automated lawn mower test stand
sources.title: End of Line Automation Lawn Mower Test Stand - ACS
sources.claim: An outdoor power equipment manufacturer's end-of-line functional test of lawn mowers was fully automated: a PLC-driven test stand tests three mower models in a range of configurations and automated transfer carts move each mower from the assembly line into an available test stand and back out after verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional verification of outdoor power equipment (electric mowers rather than engine-powered). Same product class, same purpose — machine-run functional test with automated presentation of the unit — supporting the E1 verification instance; combustion-specific measurements are covered by the engine hot/cold-test evidence.

sources.system: Cognex vision / deep-learning final assembly verification
sources.title: Final Assembly Verification - Automotive | Cognex
sources.claim: Deployed machine-vision assembly-verification systems on production lines automatically confirm that all required components are present and correctly positioned and return a pass/fail result, i.e. locating missing or wrong parts by inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated visual inspection for missing/incorrect components on fixtured assemblies. It covers the 'locate missing and broken parts' element of the task for units presented in a fixed pose under controlled lighting, as a purpose-built inspection station presents them.

sources.system: Simcenter Anovis end-of-line NVH test system
sources.title: Going from hot and cold testing of engines to a robust end-of-line testing system for electrified vehicles - Simcenter
sources.claim: End-of-line test software analyses engine sound and vibration signals to make automatic pass/fail decisions and reliably detect fault patterns in production testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fault detection in end-of-line engine testing. The mechanic's 'listen and judge' step and instrument-based fault determination are performed automatically on engines running in a purpose-built test cell.

sources.system: (no system found) shop-floor service robots / humanoid robots
sources.title: 38 Best Humanoid Robots in 2026 (Evidence-Ranked) | RoboZaps Blog
sources.claim: Searches for robots performing engine diagnosis inside repair shops or service bays return only human-assist material handling and cobots plus software diagnostic tools; no autonomous robotic system is shown testing or inspecting engines in a service facility, and humanoid work remains parts handling in controlled workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to record the absence of E2/E3 capability: no named robot performs instrument-based engine diagnosis in a repair shop or at a customer site.

tasks.label: Dismantle engines, using hand tools, and examine parts for defects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench teardown of a walk-behind mower engine (Briggs & Stratton / Honda / Kohler single-cylinder, ~140-190cc): drain fuel and oil, pull blade and adapter, remove blower housing, carburetor, muffler, flywheel with a puller, cylinder head, sump, piston/rod and valves; then examine head gasket, bore, rings, valve faces/seats, crank taper and keyway for scoring, wear, carbon, cracks, and out-of-spec clearances.

Shop teardown of handheld two-stroke equipment (chainsaw, string trimmer, backpack blower): split plastic housings and covers, remove clutch, flywheel, muffler, carburetor and intake boot, cylinder and piston, split crankcase; inspect piston skirt and cylinder plating for scoring, ring wear, bearing play, crank seals and cracked/melted plastics. Many models, tiny fasteners, mixed screw types.

Shop teardown of a larger unit — riding mower / zero-turn V-twin, generator, pressure washer, or snowblower engine — often partly stripped on the machine or after pulling the engine: remove shrouding, air/fuel/electrical accessories, heads, sump, camshaft, pistons; inspect valve train, bearings, camshaft lobes and compression-release for wear and damage. Heavy, awkward assemblies.

Teardown of a seized, corroded, water-damaged or previously botched unit: rusted, stripped, rounded or sheared fasteners, stuck flywheels and gaskets, gummed varnish, mismatched hardware; requires penetrating oil, heat, impact driver, extractors and improvised prying while judging which parts are damaged beyond reuse.

Field/mobile service at a customer site (farm, golf course, landscaping yard, jobsite, residence): partial dismantling of an engine in place on a machine using hand tools from a service van, on uneven ground or a trailer, in variable light and weather, with parts inspected on the spot to decide repair vs. shop haul-in.

sources.system: UR10e + RealSense D405 + mechatronic screwdriver e-waste unscrewing system
sources.developer: academic group (Journal of Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing paper)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robotic disassembly of used products is demonstrated only for the fastener-removal sub-step: a UR10e arm with a vision system and custom screwdriver autonomously unscrews accessible screws on electronic devices in a lab cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unscrewing during product disassembly. It is the closest robotic analogue to removing an engine's fasteners, but it covers only accessible screws on electronics in a fixtured cell — not press-fit flywheels, torqued head bolts, stuck gaskets, or examining removed parts for wear and cracks.

sources.system: Human-robot collaborative disassembly cell (2x KUKA LBR iiwa 14 R820)
sources.developer: University of Birmingham Autonomous Remanufacturing Laboratory
sources.title: An experimental human-robot collaborative disassembly cell
sources.claim: The nearest engine-adjacent robotic teardown demonstration — an automotive turbocharger in a dedicated remanufacturing lab cell — is human-robot collaborative, with a human retained for the complex, judgment-heavy steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remanufacturing teardown of a mechanical assembly with bolted and press-fit parts, i.e. the closest published analogue to engine dismantling. Even there the cell is collaborative and human-supervised, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of an engine teardown.

sources.system: Molg robotic microfactory
sources.title: ABB Robotics and US start-up Molg tackle data center e-waste with robotic microfactories
sources.claim: Autonomous full-product disassembly exists commercially only for purpose-designed electronics: Molg's robotic microfactory, built with ABB robots, autonomously disassembles laptops, servers and industrial electronics inside a dedicated cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous teardown of a whole product in a purpose-built cell. Transfer to small engines fails: servers use uniform accessible screws and slide-out modules with no corrosion, carbon, press fits or high-torque fasteners, and the microfactory sorts parts rather than judging wear, scoring or cracks.

sources.system: Daisy disassembly robot
sources.title: Apple expands global recycling programs
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line shows that deployed autonomous disassembly is achievable only for a small set of known product models with purpose-built tooling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-throughput autonomous product teardown in a purpose-built line. It does not transfer to engine dismantling: Daisy handles a fixed catalogue of undamaged consumer devices with bespoke per-model tooling and performs no defect examination of the recovered parts.

sources.system: robotic disassembly systems in remanufacturing (industry review)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: Industry review of remanufacturing automation reports that robotic disassembly is still emerging and that seized bolts, deformed parts and ... defeat current systems — exactly the conditions of used small-engine teardown.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about robotic disassembly of used mechanical products for remanufacture; identifies the same failure modes (seized fasteners, deformed parts, model variability) that dominate small-engine teardown.

sources.system: robotised EV battery disassembly systems (systematic review of 63 publications)
sources.title: Robotised disassembly of electric vehicle batteries: A systematic literature review
sources.claim: Even for a comparatively standardized used product (EV battery packs), expert consensus in a systematic review is that fully automated disassembly is not yet feasible.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of used products in dedicated facilities. If fully automated teardown is not yet feasible for standardized battery packs, it is not substantiated for heterogeneous, corroded, carbon-fouled small engines requiring defect judgement.

tasks.label: Repair and maintain gasoline engines used to power equipment such as portable saws, lawn mowers, generators, and compressors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench, seasonal service of a walk-behind mower or similar consumer unit: drain/refill oil, change spark plug and air filter, clean or replace fuel filter, scrape deck, remove/sharpen/balance and reinstall the blade, then start and run-test. Units arrive dirty, grass-caked, with varied fastener sizes and some corroded hardware; dozens of different makes/models come through a dealer or independent shop bay.

Fuel-system/carburetor repair on a handheld 2-stroke (chainsaw, trimmer, blower) or small 4-stroke left with stale fuel: remove shroud and air box, pull the carburetor, disassemble it, clean varnished jets/passages, replace diaphragms, gaskets, fuel lines and primer bulb, reassemble, set the mixture screws by ear/tach, and verify the engine idles and revs correctly.

Diagnostic job in the shop on a no-start or poor-running engine: interpret the customer's complaint, run compression and spark tests, check ignition coil/air gap and sheared flywheel key, inspect valves/valve lash and governor linkage, isolate the fault, then perform the indicated repair and confirm the fix on a test run.

Major repair or overhaul in the shop on a riding-mower, generator, or compressor engine: pull the engine or remove the head, grind/lap valves, replace rings, gaskets, crank seals, or a short block, measure clearances, torque fasteners to spec in sequence, reassemble accessories and wiring, and break the engine in on a test stand.

On-site field service call: repairing or maintaining a standby generator, air compressor, pressure washer, or commercial mower at a customer's home, farm, or job site — cramped or awkward access, no lift or bench, uncontrolled weather, dirt and clutter, using only what is on the service truck.

sources.system: UC Berkeley furniture-assembly robot (best-in-class per Epoch AI review)
sources.developer: UC Berkeley / survey by Epoch AI
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: Epoch AI's 2026 capability assessment rates autonomous multi-step mechanical assembly with hand tools and varied parts (IKEA furniture) as 'Early research stage': only fragments demonstrated, tool use and handling varied parts unproven even in the lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-step mechanical assembly with hand tools and heterogeneous fasteners. Small-engine repair requires that same skill set plus fault diagnosis, torque-to-spec, and handling worn/corroded used parts, so a task rated early-research bounds engine teardown and rebuild from above.

sources.system: Survey of leading manipulation systems (Figure, Physical Intelligence, Amazon Vulcan, etc.)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: Epoch AI's survey finds that manipulation tasks generally, and complex multi-step manipulation in particular, remain in the lab; deployed manipulation is confined to simple tasks in environments designed around the robot.
sources.transferJustification: General bound on the E1/E2 counterfactual: engine repair is a complex multi-step manipulation task on used goods, which this review places outside what deployed systems do even in environments built around the machine.

sources.system: Robotic agentic EV battery disassembly platform (robot arm with vision and nut-runner)
sources.title: Robotic Agentic Platform for Intelligent Electric Vehicle Disassembly
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robotic disassembly of a used product in a purpose-built lab cell covers only fastener removal, taking roughly 24-36 minutes for one cover's fasteners with 57-97% success depending on strategy; no reassembly or repair is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously unscrewing fasteners on a used, variable-condition assembly — the entry sub-step of any engine teardown. It shows the frontier stops at that sub-step, well short of diagnose-disassemble-replace-reassemble-test.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly systems in remanufacturing plants (industry survey)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: Trade coverage of remanufacturing automation reports robotic disassembly systems are only beginning to emerge and that seized bolts, deformed parts and ... still defeat automation; each returned unit differs in condition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: engine remanufacturing teardown in a purpose-built plant, the closest industrial analogue to shop engine repair. It shows that even inside an E1 facility the variability of used engines blocks autonomous teardown, let alone rebuild.

sources.system: RoboTire autonomous tire-changing system
sources.title: RoboTire installs system at Detroit Garage
sources.claim: The most advanced deployed robotic vehicle-service system in a retail shop bay performs a single standardized operation — removing lug nuts and swapping four wheels in about 25 minutes using a six-axis arm with vision and a torque wrench; it does no diagnosis, teardown, or engine work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated servicing of customer vehicles in a shop bay. It marks the ceiling of deployed shop-floor service robotics — one repetitive fastener operation on a scanned, known geometry — which does not transfer to diagnosing and rebuilding varied gasoline engines.

tasks.label: Adjust points, valves, carburetors, distributors, and spark plug gaps, using feeler gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench/service bay: setting valve lash on a used OHV four-stroke small engine (Briggs, Kohler, Honda GX, Kawasaki). Pull the valve cover, rotate the crank to TDC on compression, check intake/exhaust clearance with a feeler gauge, turn the rocker adjuster, hold and lock the nut, recheck, reinstall the cover.

Shop tune-up: checking and setting spark plug gap to the model's spec with a feeler/wire gauge on one or two plugs (new out of the box or cleaned), bending the ground electrode with a gapper, re-measuring; plug sizes range from mower plugs to small two-stroke saw/trimmer plugs.

Shop: adjusting a carburetor with the engine running — warm up the chainsaw, trimmer, blower or mower, set the idle speed screw and the low/high-speed mixture needles by ear and tachometer, verify clean acceleration with no bogging or four-stroking, iterate until it runs to spec.

Bench work during a carburetor rebuild: setting float height or diaphragm metering-lever height to spec with a gauge/straightedge, presetting the mixture screws a specified number of turns off the seat, pressure/leak-checking the carb before it goes back on the engine.

Older or magneto ignition work: setting breaker point gap with a feeler gauge on vintage equipment with the flywheel off, or setting flywheel-to-armature air gap with a shim/feeler gauge and torquing the coil screws while the magnet pulls the armature.

On-site field service at a customer's property, golf course, farm, or job site: adjusting carburetor mixture/idle or valve lash on equipment as found — mounted in the machine, outdoors, variable weather, lighting and access.

sources.system: Hirata valve clearance adjusting device (engine assembly line station)
sources.date: 2014-04 (patent granted; Hirata supplies cylinder-head/valvetrain assembly lines)
sources.title: Method and device for adjusting valve clearance - Hirata Corporation
sources.claim: Automated valve-clearance adjusting devices are standard equipment on engine assembly lines: the machine sets valve clearance on the fixtured cylinder head/engine after the valves are assembled, then re-measures and checks the result.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical operation as the shop task (measure valve clearance, turn the adjuster screw, lock it, re-verify) on the same class of workpiece (an internal-combustion engine cylinder head) at the same 0.001-0.002 in tolerance; only the fixturing and workpiece newness differ.

sources.system: Automated valve clearance adjustment machine (IFAC-reported)
sources.developer: IFAC paper authors (automotive engine plant machine); assignee not stated in abstract
sources.date: IFAC proceedings paper, archived on ScienceDirect 2017-07
sources.title: Development of Automated Adjustment Machine for Valve Clearance of Automobile Engine - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A fully automated machine adjusts intake and exhaust valve clearance on automobile engines using motor-driven screwdrivers with torque detection and electric micrometers, sequencing the whole adjustment and verifying clearance and fixing torque.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same operation as the mechanic's valve-lash adjustment, substituting micrometer measurement for the feeler gauge; the acceptance criterion (clearance within spec, adjuster locked) is identical.

sources.system: Automatic valve lash adjustment machine (US 6,973,905 / US2005/0098125)
sources.developer: US patent 6,973,905 assignee (engine assembly automation builder)
sources.title: Valve lash adjustment apparatus and method (USPTO 6,973,905)
sources.claim: An automatic valve lash adjustment ... operates as a stop station on a moving engine assembly line, using a displacement probe (LVDT) to sense lash and torque-controlled spindles to set the adjusting screw and its lock nut.
sources.transferJustification: Same task as the instance (set valve lash and tighten the lock nut without disturbing the setting) on a fixtured engine; the patent background states this machine replaces the manual feeler-gauge technique.

sources.system: Spark plug manufacturing apparatus (USPTO 8,371,889)
sources.title: Spark plug manufacturing method and spark plug manufacturing apparatus (USPTO 8,371,889)
sources.claim: Spark plug production apparatus bends the ground electrode by a measured pressing amount so that the spark discharge gap is formed to the specified dimension 	o a plug get machine-set gap.
sources.transferJustification: The mechanic's instance is this same operation on the same object — measure the gap and bend the ground electrode to a target dimension — the only difference being that the target comes from the engine spec rather than the plug part number.

sources.system: Apparatus for making a spark plug with a predetermined spark gap (USPTO 7,112,112)
sources.title: Method and apparatus for making a spark plug with a predetermined spark gap (USPTO 7,112,112)
sources.claim: Production apparatus measures finished spark plug electrode geometry by image processing and applies a computed bending adjustment to reach a predetermined spark gap, closing the loop between measurement and adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Same workpiece and tolerance class as gapping a plug in a shop; demonstrates closed-loop measure-then-bend control that substitutes for the feeler gauge and gapping tool.

sources.system: NGK factory gap setting
sources.title: Do I need to set the "gap" when installing a new set of plugs? - NGK Spark Plugs

sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that gap setting to a numeric target is a routine factory process; autonomy of the factory step is not established in this source, so it is used only as context and is not decisive.
