sources.transferJustification: Not the adjustment task itself; cited to show robots handling small valvetrain components to assembly tolerances in fixtured cells, supporting the E1 counterfactual where valvetrain work is presented on a pallet.

tasks.label: Repair or replace defective parts such as magnetos, water pumps, gears, pistons, and carburetors, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench: replacing a fuel-system or ignition component on a handheld or walk-behind unit (carburetor, ignition coil/magneto, fuel lines, primer bulb) — remove shroud/air cleaner, unhook governor linkage and springs, disconnect fuel line, swap gaskets, mount and adjust the new part, verify it starts and runs.

Shop bench: internal engine work on a 2-stroke or OHV small engine — replacing piston/rings/cylinder, crank seals, valves, or splitting cases; degreasing, measuring wear, seating rings with a compressor, press-fit bearings, sealant/gasket work, torque-to-spec reassembly.

Shop floor/lift: replacing bolt-on assemblies on larger equipment (riding mower, generator, pressure washer, snowblower, outboard) — water pump/impeller kits, gearbox gears, spindles, pumps, drives; awkward access under decks or in tight frames, heavy sub-assemblies, hose and belt routing.

Shop: repairs complicated by corrosion, seized or snapped fasteners, stripped threads, non-standard prior repairs, or unavailable parts — heat/penetrant, extractors, re-tapping, improvised fixes, and on-the-fly repair-versus-replace judgment.

Mobile/field service at the customer's site (homeowner's yard, farm, jobsite, dock): diagnosing and swapping a coil, carburetor, or pump on equipment in place, with a portable tool kit, uneven ground, variable weather and lighting, and no fixturing.

sources.system: AutoReman robotic disassembly research programme (Univ. of Birmingham et al.)
sources.title: Robotic disassembly and remanufacturing automation | IEEE Conference Publication
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of robotic disassembly for remanufacturing/repair states the domain is hard to automate because used products vary in condition and the manipulations demand dexterity; work remains at research stage rather than production repair.
sources.transferJustification: Removing a defective part from a used machine is the first half of this task; this source shows that even the disassembly half of used-product repair is unsolved outside narrow lab settings, so it cannot substantiate whole-task completion.

sources.system: DRL-based robotic screw-removal system (6-DoF arm with F/T sensor and spanner socket)
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing / ScienceDirect)
sources.title: Robotic disassembly of screws for end-of-life product remanufacturing enabled by deep reinforcement learning
sources.claim: Robotic removal of screws from used products is still an active research problem requiring force/torque search strategies and reinforcement learning to achieve reliable bit-to-screw engagement.
sources.transferJustification: Every carburetor, magneto, pump or gearcase replacement begins with removing fasteners of unknown condition; this shows single-fastener removal alone is still a lab-scale problem, far short of a whole engine-component swap.

sources.system: Six-axis cobot robotic fastening station with 3D sensor
sources.developer: INESC TEC (Institute for Systems and Computer Engineering, Technology and Science), Porto

sources.claim: Robotic bolt tightening on new automotive assemblies is achievable in a purpose-built cobot workstation with 3D vision and force sensing — but only for known new parts presented at known poses on an assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening components in manufacturing. It transfers only to the final torqueing step on a new, known part; it does not cover diagnosing part location, removing a corroded defective part, gaskets, linkages and fuel lines on a used engine.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: unbolting and re-bolting a component on a used machine in a service bay. It handles one standardized, fully exposed bolt pattern on a rigidly positioned wheel; small-engine part replacement involves buried, varied fasteners, hoses, springs and gaskets, so capability does not carry over.

sources.system: RAISE robot-assisted selective disassembly and sorting system for end-of-life phones
sources.title: RAISE: A Robot-Assisted SelectIve Disassembly and Sorting System for End-of-Life Phones
sources.claim: State-of-the-art high-throughput robotic disassembly of used products is limited to small, standardized consumer devices and is selective/destructive component recovery, not repair and reassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of used goods in a purpose-built cell. It shows the ceiling of current practice — flat, standardized, low-force devices taken apart for recovery — with no installation of replacement parts or return to working order, so it cannot substantiate engine repair.

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance such as cleaning and oiling parts, honing cylinders, and tuning ignition systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Seasonal/annual tune-up of a customer's walk-behind lawn mower at a dealer or independent small-engine shop service bay: drain and refill crankcase oil, clean or replace the air filter, remove and replace the spark plug (gap set, boot reseated), scrape caked grass from the deck, clean cooling fins and recoil housing, sharpen/balance or replace the blade, clean carburetor bowl and fuel filter, oil pivot points and cables, then start and run-test. Machines arrive dirty, of a dozen different makes and vintages, with seized or corroded fasteners.

Service of handheld two-stroke equipment (chainsaw, string trimmer, backpack blower, hedge trimmer) on a shop bench: clean/replace air filter, decarbon and clean the spark arrestor screen and muffler, clean cooling fins and flywheel, replace and gap the spark plug, check coil air gap, adjust carburetor H/L/idle screws to spec by ear/tach, clean and oil the bar and sharpen the chain, lubricate gearheads.

Multi-point seasonal service of a riding mower, zero-turn, or snowblower in the shop bay: oil and oil-filter change, fuel filter, air/pre-cleaner filter, two spark plugs, grease zerk fittings on spindles and front axle, inspect and oil belts/chains/cables, battery service, deck removal, cleaning and blade sharpening, tire pressures, then test run. Requires lifting/jacking the unit and working under it.

Bench machining operation during an engine rebuild in the shop's machine area: a disassembled cylinder or cylinder block is set up and honed/deglazed to specified bore size, roundness and crosshatch finish, gauged to spec, then washed clean of abrasive grit and oiled for reassembly.

On-site maintenance away from the shop: a mobile mechanic services a portable generator, pressure washer, pump, or a commercial mower at a customer's home, a landscape contractor's yard, or a jobsite — oil and filter change, plug replacement, filter cleaning, lubrication and adjustment, performed on uneven ground from a service van with no fixtures or lift.

Tune-up of a marine outboard or powersports engine at a dealership service bay: replace spark plugs, check/adjust ignition timing and coil output, change gear lube and engine oil, lubricate grease points and linkages, clean/replace fuel filter and water separator, fog cylinders, and run the engine on muffs or in a test tank.

sources.system: Sunnen honing systems (SV/HTA series, automated bore-sizing cells)

sources.transferJustification: Directly the listed sub-operation 'honing cylinders': the machine hones engine-type bores to size and finish and gauges the result, the same acceptance criterion a mechanic works to.

sources.claim: Engine rebuild shops now use CNC automated honing machines with programmable stroke/dwell and spindle-load size control to hone bores to production-line consistency.

sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'cleaning parts' element of the bench rebuild instance: the same degreasing of engine components a mechanic would otherwise do by hand before honing and reassembly.

sources.system: RoboTire robotic tire-changing system
sources.date: 2022-08 (Discount Tire, Fountain Hills AZ); 2023-05 (Detroit Garage, Livonia MI)
sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The only vehicle-service robot actually installed in customer-facing repair shops performs a single fixtured operation — removing and mounting four wheels — and does not perform multi-step maintenance such as filter, plug, oil and lubrication service.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed analogue to shop maintenance work (fastener removal/installation on a customer machine in a service bay); cited to show the demonstrated envelope is one repetitive fixtured operation, not the varied disassembly, cleaning, adjustment and reassembly of small-engine tune-ups.

tasks.label: Reassemble engines after repair or maintenance work is complete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Walk-behind mower engine on a shop bench after carburetor/valve service: refit carburetor with new gaskets onto studs, hook governor link and spring, reattach fuel line, air cleaner, blower housing, ignition coil with air-gap set, spark plug, recoil starter; all fasteners to spec, engine must start and run.

Handheld two-stroke (chainsaw, trimmer, blower) after piston/cylinder or crank-seal work: press seals and bearings into clamshell crankcase halves, torque case screws, fit piston/ring with circlips, cylinder and base gasket, clutch and drum, muffler, carburetor and fuel/impulse lines, starter housing and handles.

Full overhaul reassembly of a single-cylinder OHV engine (riding mower / commercial mower): fit rings to piston, install piston-rod assembly with ring compressor, torque rod cap, set camshaft timing marks, RTV the sump, install head gasket and torque head bolts in sequence, set valve lash, install flywheel with key to torque.

Generator, pressure washer, or snowblower engine reassembled in the shop after repair: refit engine covers, fuel tank and lines, carburetor and gaskets, control linkages, recoil or electric starter, muffler and shrouds, then reconnect the engine to the driven unit (pump, alternator, auger drive).

On-site reassembly at a customer property, golf course maintenance shed, marina dock, or job site: engine partly reassembled where it sits on the equipment, limited bench space and lighting, whatever fasteners and parts are on the service truck.

sources.system: KUKA Assembly & Test engine block assembly line at Scania Södertälje
sources.title: Engine block assembly line for Scania's trucks of tomorrow | KUKA Global
sources.claim: KUKA integrated a 21-station engine block assembly line at Scania where 15 robots and 13 fully automated stations perform bolting of connecting rod bearing caps, feeding/setting/bolting of up to 38 cylinder head ..., cylinder head cover and oil cooler bolting, bearing shell placement and inspection, and robot-based valve clearance adjustment with a twin screwdriver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is new-engine assembly rather than post-repair reassembly, but the physical operations are the same ones a small-engine mechanic performs on reassembly (bearing shells, rod caps, head gasket and head-bolt torque sequence, cover bolting, valve lash adjustment), on comparable metal engine components at comparable torque and clearance precision, in a fixtured line.

sources.system: Honda Manufacturing of Alabama automated engine assembly line (92 robots)
sources.title: Honda launches new automated engine assembly line in Alabama - Made in Alabama
sources.claim: Honda's Alabama engine assembly facility includes a robotic station that assembles pistons (rings onto pistons) at six seconds each and a fully automated piston installation ... into the block.
sources.transferJustification: Piston-ring fitting and piston insertion into the bore are the two hardest manipulation steps of an overhaul reassembly; this line does them on automotive pistons of comparable size and fit tolerance, with the work fixtured and presented, i.e. an E1 setting.

sources.system: AMS dual-robot precision screwdriving system with ASG X-PAQ torque/angle driver
sources.title: Precision Robotic Screwdriving for Automotive Assembly: A Tier 1 Case Study - AMS Automated Machine Systems
sources.claim: Commercial dual-robot screwdriving cells with vacuum screw pickup, fixtured nests and torque-and-angle validation on every fastener are delivered and run in automotive plants, replacing manual driving of fasteners.
sources.transferJustification: Most of a small-engine reassembly is driving screws and bolts to specified torque into aluminum and steel housings; torque-and-angle monitored robotic screwdriving in fixtured nests covers that step and also detects cross-threaded or missing fasteners the way a mechanic's torque wrench and feel would.

sources.system: FANUC Oshino lights-out robot assembly plant
sources.title: Lights-Out Manufacturing | AMT
sources.claim: FANUC runs lights-out assembly plants in which robots build robots, producing roughly 50 robots per 24-hour shift with production running unsupervised for ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task is complete mechanical product assembly (servo motors and robot arms: cast housings, bearings, seals, gears, many torqued fasteners) rather than engine reassembly, but it shows whole-assembly completion without step-by-step human intervention in a purpose-built fixtured plant, the E1 counterfactual for this task.

sources.system: Learning-Augmented Robotic Automation (learned task controllers + neural 3D safety monitor)
sources.developer: authors of arXiv:2604.22235 (industrial deployment on a motor line)
sources.title: [2604.22235] Learning-augmented robotic automation for real-world manufacturing
sources.claim: A learning-based robotic system was deployed on a live electric-motor production line to automate ..., a step previously done by hand, running continuously under manufacturing constraints.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is cable insertion on a motor line; it transfers to the deformable, fiddly parts of small-engine reassembly (fuel/impulse lines, wire leads, gaskets) at comparable scale and precision, in a fixtured production cell rather than a repair shop.

sources.system: STIHL Virginia Beach engine block assembly line with collaborative robots
sources.title: Assembly Plant of the Year: STIHL Stays a Cut Above the Competition | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: STIHL's US plant assembles chainsaw and handheld two-stroke products on high-mix lines and has deployed collaborative robots on an engine ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task is factory assembly of handheld two-stroke engine blocks, the same components (crankcase halves, bearings, seals, cylinder, fasteners) a mechanic refits on reassembly; it shows the parts are within robotic handling in a fixtured line, though the cobot stations work alongside human operators.

tasks.label: Replace motors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bay: replace the seized gasoline engine on a walk-behind push/self-propelled mower. Drain fuel and oil, tip the deck, remove blade and blade adapter, break loose four often-rusted deck bolts, disconnect throttle/control cable, kill-switch wire and fuel line, lift the old engine off, set the replacement on the deck studs, torque bolts, reinstall blade/adapter, route and adjust the governor/throttle cable, fill oil, and test run.

Shop bay: replace the engine on a riding mower, lawn tractor or zero-turn. Remove hood and shrouds, PTO/drive belts, muffler, fuel lines and wiring harness connectors, unbolt the engine from the frame, hoist a 70-100 lb engine out with a shop crane, transfer pulleys/PTO clutch and flywheel screen to the replacement, align and shim, reconnect harness, cables and fuel, refill fluids, and test under load.

Bench work on handheld and portable units: replace the powerhead/short block on a chainsaw or string trimmer, the engine on a pressure washer or portable generator, or the electric motor module on a battery/corded mower, blower or snow thrower. Small fasteners, fragile plastic housings, fuel/oil lines, wiring connectors, coupling alignment, then function test.

Dealership service bay: replace the engine or drive motor in other powered equipment the shop handles — snowmobile, ATV/UTV, go-kart, small outboard, golf cart or utility vehicle. Heavier assemblies, exhaust and cooling connections, wiring harness, mounts and alignment, then road/water test.

On-site field service from a truck at a customer's property (residential yard, farm shed, golf-course or municipal grounds yard): replace the engine or motor on a mower, generator, pump or sprayer where it sits — uneven ground, poor lighting, weather, no lift or fixture, tools limited to what is on the truck.

sources.system: BEAM-1 battery disassembly autonomous mobile manipulator robot
sources.title: Revolutionizing Battery Disassembly: The Design and Implementation of a Battery Disassembly Autonomous Mobile Manipulator Robot (BEAM-1)
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile manipulator (BEAM-1) autonomously perceives and removes many types of bolts from end-of-life EV battery packs at high success rate, but the demonstrated scope is the unfastening sub-step, not removal and reinstallation of a powertrain component with its cables, lines and wiring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bolt removal during disassembly of used equipment. It shows only the unfastening step on flat, accessible battery-pack bolts; it does not substantiate disconnecting fuel lines, throttle/governor cables and harnesses, lifting an engine off deck studs, mounting and torquing a replacement, refilling oil, and test-running, which the mechanic's task requires end to end.

sources.system: Robotic e-waste unscrewing cell (UR10e + Intel RealSense D405 + custom mechatronic screwdriver)
sources.developer: Academic research group, published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: A vision-guided UR10e cell autonomously unscrews fasteners of varied head types in a range of used electronic devices, again covering only fastener removal in a laboratory disassembly cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fastener removal on used, variable products. It bounds the state of the art at the sub-step level — small screws in light devices — and does not cover heavy engine handling, connection/reconnection of fluid and control lines, or post-install adjustment and test firing.

sources.system: DeMoBat robotic disassembly cell (KUKA KR QUANTEC robots)
sources.title: "DeMoBat": Battery disassembly for electric cars using KUKA robots
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IPA and KUKA demonstrated an industrial robotic cell for disassembling EV batteries and electric motors, i.e. tearing components down for recycling in a purpose-built research cell rather than replacing a motor in a serviceable machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial robotic disassembly of batteries and electric motors. Transfer fails because the goal is destructive/recycling teardown of one known product family in a fixtured cell, with no reinstallation of a replacement motor, no reconnection of controls and fuel systems, and no requirement that the machine work afterwards; autonomy of the full sequence is also not established.

sources.system: SmartBay robotic tire-change platform
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic component-replacement system shown in an automotive service bay changes tires/wheels; no comparable system performs engine or motor replacement, and the tire platform was only unveiled in May 2026 with a technician overseeing multiple bays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic replacement of a bolted component in a vehicle service bay. Wheels have standardized bolt circles and no fuel, oil, cable or electrical connections; engine/motor replacement on used outdoor power equipment involves corroded fasteners, cable routing and adjustment, fluid fill and a start-and-run acceptance test, none of which this system performs.

tasks.label: Obtain problem descriptions from customers, and prepare cost estimates for repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Show customers how to maintain equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At the shop service counter, a mechanic returning a repaired walk-behind mower to a homeowner explains and points out routine upkeep: oil level and change interval, cleaning/replacing the air filter, spark plug replacement, and blade sharpening schedule. Purpose is served when the customer understands the routine.

At drop-off or pickup, the mechanic explains fuel-related care to a customer whose equipment failed from stale/ethanol fuel: which fuel to buy, using stabilizer, running the carburetor dry, and end-of-season storage and battery care. Largely verbal advice with reference to the machine or a product on the shelf.

A chainsaw or trimmer customer at the dealership counter is walked through chain tensioning, bar-oil checks, filing/sharpening angles, and mixing two-stroke fuel, with the mechanic handling the saw and a file to illustrate the motions while narrating.

In the shop bay or lot, the mechanic briefs a commercial landscaping crew or fleet customer on daily pre-operation checks and greasing points for zero-turn mowers, deck leveling, and service intervals, sometimes with the machine running.
Remote follow-up: the mechanic explains maintenance steps, service intervals, or a warranty-required upkeep item to a customer by phone, text, email, or a short video sent to the customer.

tasks.label: Remove engines from equipment, and position and bolt engines to repair stands.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Walk-behind push/self-propelled mower in a dealer or independent small-engine shop bay: tip or invert the mower, break loose the blade bolt and pull the blade/adapter, disconnect kill wire and throttle cable, back out 3-4 deck bolts (often grass-caked, rusted, sometimes rounded), lift the 25-40 lb vertical-shaft engine off the deck, set it on a bench engine stand and bolt it down.

Riding mower, lawn tractor or zero-turn in a shop service bay: remove hood/grille, seat pan and shrouds, disconnect battery, fuel line, wiring harness, throttle/choke cables, remove drive belt and PTO clutch, unbolt the engine from the frame, hoist the 90-130 lb engine out with a shop crane and bolt it to a rolling repair stand.

Handheld two-stroke unit (chainsaw, string trimmer, blower, hedge trimmer) on the shop bench: remove clamshell housing/handle screws, detach gummed fuel and impulse lines, ignition and throttle linkages, separate the powerhead from housing and anti-vibration mounts, and clamp/bolt the small engine into a bench fixture or vise-mounted stand.

Generator, pressure washer, water pump, tiller, snow blower or utility engine in the shop: disconnect fuel, controls and electrical, uncouple the driven element (alternator rotor, tapered pump shaft, gearbox coupling) from the crankshaft, unbolt the engine from the frame, and lift the 40-90 lb engine onto a repair stand and bolt it.

On-site removal by a mobile service tech: equipment sitting on uneven ground at a customer's property, a golf-course maintenance shed, farm barn or rental yard; the engine must be pulled where it stands with hand tools and a portable hoist or two-person lift, then set onto a stand on the truck or shop floor.

sources.system: Recirculate robotic battery disassembly cell (Centria UAS, KUKA KR10 on linear track)
sources.developer: Centria University of Applied Sciences / Recirculate EU project
sources.title: Recirculate tests AI-driven robotic system for EV battery disassembly
sources.claim: A KUKA-based robotic cell autonomously detects, unscrews and removes components (e.g., ~50 lid screws) from used high-voltage EV battery packs in a purpose-built disassembly cell; it is a project pilot, not a production system, and covers a single product family with flat, accessible fastener patterns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unfastening and lifting a heavy sub-assembly off a used, model-varying machine. It is the closest deployed-style analogue to pulling an engine, but it operates only on battery packs with known lid geometry, does not handle corroded threaded fasteners under high torque on grass-caked equipment, does not disconnect throttle cables/fuel lines, and does not position and bolt the removed unit onto a repair stand.

sources.system: Daisy disassembly robot
sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line autonomously disassembles used iPhones in a purpose-built recycling facility, handling 23 models at 200 units per hour by removing fasteners and separating components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of used consumer products in a purpose-built line. Transfer to engine removal fails on object class and scale: Daisy handles sub-200 g devices with tiny screws and adhesive in a pre-mapped model database, not 25-130 lb engines held by high-torque, corroded bolts with cables, fuel lines and drive couplings, and it destroys/discards rather than preserving a serviceable assembly to be mounted on a stand.

sources.system: Atlas (electric)
sources.title: Atlas Goes Hands On
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid autonomously picks and places automotive engine covers between containers and a sequencing dolly in a factory-style cell, using ML vision; the demonstrated work is part handling, with no fastening, unfastening, or removal of parts from an assembled machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of automotive-scale parts in a structured facility. It substantiates only handling and placement of loose parts into fixtures, not the unbolting, cable/fuel-line disconnection, hoisting of a heavy engine, or torqueing it to a repair stand that this task requires.

sources.system: state-of-the-art robotic ECC disassembly (survey of systems)
sources.developer: University of Bologna (Carricato et al.), MDPI Robotics
sources.title: Robotic Disassembly of Electrical Cable Connectors: A Critical Review
sources.claim: A 2026 critical review of robotic disassembly finds that non-destructive removal of electrical cable ... — the class of step needed to free throttle cables, kill wires and harness plugs before an engine can come out — remains unsolved, with accessibility, motion planning and extraction at an early stage.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant sub-step: every engine removal instance requires disconnecting harness plugs, kill wires and control cables before the engine can be lifted; the review establishes that no fielded robotic system does this reliably even in purpose-built cells.

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing system for automated e-waste disassembly
sources.developer: academic research group (Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: A laboratory robotic unscrewing system for e-waste disassembly reports that reaching full reliability and industrial readiness remains future work, indicating autonomous fastener removal is not yet at production quality even on flat, presented workpieces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous removal of threaded fasteners from used products. It shows the enabling sub-step for engine removal is still below the reliability a shop would accept, and it was demonstrated only on small, light electronic devices, not on corroded engine mounting bolts.

tasks.label: Sell parts and equipment.

tasks.label: Grind, ream, rebore, and re-tap parts to obtain specified clearances, using grinders, lathes, taps, reamers, boring machines, and micrometers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop: reboring/honing a worn cylinder of a lawn-mower, generator or chainsaw engine to an oversize spec. Mechanic clamps the block/cylinder on a boring bar or hone, cuts, then checks the bore with a telescoping gauge and micrometer against the piston to obtain the specified piston-to-cylinder clearance.

Shop bench: thread repair on a small engine part — re-tapping a stripped spark-plug hole, blower-housing, muffler or head-bolt hole, or drilling out a broken stud and installing a thread insert, then verifying the thread with a bolt/plug gauge. Part is often still partly assembled and held in a vise.

Shop: cylinder-head and valve work — grinding/lapping valves and seats, reaming or replacing a worn valve guide to a specified stem clearance, and resurfacing a warped head or crankcase mating face; measured with micrometer, small-hole gauge and straightedge.

Shop lathe/grinder: turning or grinding a shaft to size (crankshaft journal, PTO or blade shaft), machining a bushing/spacer, or pressing in a bushing and reaming it to the specified running clearance, sized with a micrometer.

Shop bench, freehand/vise work: grinding or dressing a damaged surface to restore fit — cleaning up a scored flywheel taper or crankcase face, grinding down a seized or broken fastener, deburring a bore after boring — with a bench grinder or die grinder, judged by feel, fit-up and micrometer check.

Field/mobile service: hand-tapping or reaming a hole on an assembled machine at a customer site (mower deck, generator, snow blower) using a tap wrench, hand reamer and portable tools, with the machine as found on a driveway, lawn or in a service truck bay.

roles.title: Bicycle Repairers
roles.description: Repair and service bicycles.

tasks.label: Install and adjust speed and gear mechanisms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop repair stand, customer's cable-actuated derailleur bike (road/MTB/hybrid, mixed brands and wear states): diagnose poor shifting, check hanger alignment, set high/low limit screws, tension cable at pinch bolt, index gears with barrel adjuster while spinning cranks, verify crisp shifts across all cogs and both rings.

Shop repair stand, drivetrain replacement on a varied customer bike: install new rear (and sometimes front) derailleur and shifter, route new inner cable and housing through frame/bar tape, fit cassette and chain to correct length, then set limits and index the whole system to worker-quality shift feel.

Retail/big-box assembly area, new bike out of the carton (repetitive similar models): finish derailleur mounting, seat and tension shift cables, set limits, index shifting to factory spec, road/roller test before the bike goes on the sales floor.

Shop bench, commuter/fleet/rental bikes with internal gear hubs (Shimano Nexus/Alfine, Sturmey-Archer) or older friction/thumb-shift systems: install or reconnect the shifter cassette joint/indicator chain, align yellow index marks, adjust cable, verify all hub gears engage.

Shop bench, electronic shifting (Shimano Di2, SRAM AXS): bolt on the electronic derailleur, route wires or fit batteries, pair components, run firmware/micro-adjust trim through the app or buttons, and confirm shifting across the cassette.

Field service: race-day pit area, mobile repair van, or customer's driveway/curbside — adjust or install shifting components on a bike as found, kneeling or with a portable stand, under time pressure and variable light and weather.

sources.system: MERL autonomous gearbox assembly system (Ota et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Assembly: From Part Singulation to Precise Assembly
sources.claim: A research robotic cell autonomously assembles a gear box (meshing gears, shafts, precise insertions) from parts randomly placed on a plane, with 99.11% end-to-end success over 225 trials — the closest demonstrated capability to 'installing a gear mechanism', but performed on a bench-top gearbox kit in a fixtured lab cell, not on a bicycle drivetrain, and with no functional tuning loop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise assembly of a gearbox (gear meshing, shaft insertion, screw-scale tolerances) in a purpose-built cell. It shows robots can mate gear parts at bicycle-component precision, but it does not carry over to installing a derailleur on a full bicycle: no shift-cable routing/tensioning, no chain threading, and no iterative index-and-test tuning against shift quality.

sources.system: Bosch Research e-Bike motor assembly system
sources.title: Bosch Research | E-Bike Motor Assembly
sources.claim: Bosch Research demonstrates robot skills for assembling a Bosch Performance Line e-bike mid-drive motor (gear/shaft insertions, PCB and casing mounting) in an industrial research cell, with skills taught on site by human demonstration and then executed by the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of a bicycle drive-unit gear mechanism in a fixtured cell. Objects and precision are comparable to bicycle component fasteners, but the work is component manufacturing on a jig, not mounting and indexing a shifting system on an assembled bicycle; nothing in it addresses cable tensioning or shift-quality adjustment.

sources.system: Dual-arm cable shape-control system (Cao et al.)
sources.developer: academic research group, published in Advanced Intelligent Systems
sources.title: Shape Control of Elastic Deformable Linear Objects for Robotic Cable Assembly
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic handling of cables (deformable linear objects) — the closest analogue to routing and tensioning a bicycle shift cable — remains laboratory dual-arm shape control on simplified setups rather than a deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cable manipulation/routing. It is the capability a robot would need to thread and tension a shift inner cable through housing, but demonstrations are lab-scale shape control, not insertion of a cable through bicycle housing stops and clamping it to a set tension.

sources.system: Giant Manufacturing bicycle assembly line
sources.title: Video: Thread, Resin, & Robots: How Giant Builds Carbon Frames Differently - Pinkbike
sources.claim: At the world's largest and most automated bicycle factories, robots handle carbon lay-up, inspection and material movement, while bicycle final assembly (including drivetrain fitting and shifting setup) is done by human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Context, not a positive capability claim: the highest-volume purpose-built bicycle production environments in the world still perform drivetrain assembly and shifting setup manually, indicating no fielded machine performs this task even in an E1 setting.

tasks.label: Install and adjust brakes and brake pads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail bike shop service floor: worn rim-brake pads (V-brake, caliper, or cantilever) replaced on a used customer bike of unknown make and condition. Mechanic removes old pads, fits new ones with washers in correct orientation, sets pad height/toe-in against the rim, retensions and re-anchors the cable with a 5 mm hex, centers the arms with spring-tension screws, squeezes lever to seat, spins wheel to check rub, and adjusts barrel adjuster to final lever feel. Corroded fasteners, mixed brands, dirty parts.

Bike shop stand: hydraulic disc brake service on a modern mountain/road/e-bike. Wheel out, old pads and retaining pin/clip removed, pistons pushed back and cleaned, new pads plus spring installed, caliper loosened and re-centered over the rotor by eye/feel while torquing mount bolts, sometimes a lever/caliper bleed and rotor truing, then test ride or spin-up to confirm no rub and full lever power.

New-bike assembly / pre-delivery inspection in the shop back room or a distribution-center build area: boxed bike of a known model, brake levers and calipers mounted to bar and frame/fork, cable housing routed and cut or hydraulic hose connected, cable anchored and tensioned, caliper centered, bolts torqued to spec, brakes bedded in and lever throw set. Repetitive across batches of identical models.

Fleet/rental depot (bike share, campus, resort, police fleet): high-volume brake pad swaps and adjustments on a standardized bike model, warehouse workbench or stand row, bikes arrive dirty and with varying wear, drum/roller or disc brakes, output must pass a safety check-off before the bike returns to service.

Mobile/on-site repair: mobile-mechanic van at a customer's driveway, office park, race or event tent, or curbside bike-share unit. Bike on a portable stand or upside down, variable light, wind, rain and dust, limited parts on hand; brake pads installed and brakes adjusted on whatever bike shows up.

sources.system: Giant carbon frame and assembly plant automation
sources.title: Video: Thread, Resin, & Robots: How Giant Builds Carbon Frames Differently - Pinkbike
sources.claim: At the world's largest bicycle factory (Giant), robots and machines handle carbon frame layup, inspection and X-ray checks, while bicycle assembly itself remains overwhelmingly manual — no robotic fitting or adjusting of brakes is described.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (bicycle assembly, including brake fitting) at the most automated scale in the industry; establishes that brake installation/adjustment is not performed by machines even in a purpose-built factory.

sources.system: Laser-guided AGVs, AI visual inspection and robotic pallet systems at a new Chinese bicycle plant
sources.developer: Unnamed Chinese bicycle manufacturer (reported by Bicycling Australia)
sources.title: Inside China's newest high-tech bicycle manufacturing giant - Bicycling Australia
sources.claim: A newly opened high-tech bicycle plant in China automates material movement, warehousing and visual quality inspection; the automation described does not include robotic assembly or adjustment of brakes.
sources.transferJustification: Same industry and a purpose-built (E1-grade) setting; shows the frontier of deployed bicycle-plant robotics is logistics and inspection, not brake fitting or adjustment.

sources.system: Bosch e-Bike motor assembly robotic manipulation system
sources.title: [2304.10595] The e-Bike Motor Assembly: Towards Advanced Robotic Manipulation for Flexible Manufacturing
sources.claim: Robotic assembly of an e-bike component (motor) in a structured industrial cell is presented as a research challenge requiring on-site teaching, adaptive control and reaction to unexpected situations; it covers subassembly of rigid motor parts, not fitting or adjusting brakes on a bicycle.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published robotic manipulation work on bicycle-industry components; the demonstrated skills are fixtured insertion of rigid motor parts, which does not cover cable tensioning, pad alignment to a rim/rotor, or iterative feel-based brake adjustment.

sources.system: Motionworks Robotics Disc Brake Assembly Line
sources.title: Disc Brake Assembly Line — Motionworks Robotics
sources.claim: A commercially offered automated line assembles automotive disc brake modules (calipers, brackets, pistons, seals, pads) on fixtured stations; it manufactures brake units rather than installing and adjusting brakes on a vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and insertion of brake pads into calipers in a purpose-built cell. It does not transfer to the bicycle repairer task because the parts are dedicated automotive components at fixed poses, the caliper is never mounted to a vehicle, and no cable tensioning, pad-to-rim alignment, centering or lever-feel adjustment is performed.

sources.system: Automated Tire SmartBay (and predecessor RoboTire at Discount Tire)
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Vehicle-service robotics that does exist in human repair bays is limited to wheel/tire changing, and even the newest system automates only part of the job; an earlier tire-changing robot deployment failed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fastener work on vehicles inside a structured service facility (E2). It does not substantiate bicycle brake work: lug nuts are large, standardized and rigidly located, whereas brake installation requires manipulating flexible cable/hose, setting pad clearance by sight and feel, and iterative verification.

tasks.label: Install new tires and tubes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail bike shop workshop: customer brings in a commuter/hybrid bike with a flat or worn tyre. Mechanic clamps bike in a repair stand, releases brake, removes wheel, deflates and levers off the old tyre, removes the tube, inspects rim tape and tyre casing for the thorn/glass causing the puncture, fits a new tube and tyre without pinching, inflates to spec, refits wheel and checks brake/derailleur clearance.

Bike shop workshop, performance road/gravel/MTB bikes: fitting tight-bead tyres to hooked or hookless rims, including tubeless setups (rim tape, valve, sealant, bead seating with a charged inflator) or lightweight tubes on narrow rims, with torque- and pressure-sensitive handling of carbon rims and correct tyre rotation/label alignment.

Bike shop workshop, heavy/awkward bikes: e-bikes, cargo bikes and Dutch-style city bikes with hub motors, internal gear hubs, roller/drum brakes, chain cases and fenders, where the rear wheel must be disconnected and re-installed with cables/connectors before and after the tyre and tube are replaced.

Fleet/institutional maintenance shop or depot (bike-share, rental fleet, campus or police fleet, or new-bike assembly area at a shop): batch tyre and tube replacement on many near-identical standardized bikes/wheels, work benched and staged, with consistent parts and a fixed workflow.

Mobile/on-site repair: mobile bike-repair van, workplace or campus pop-up service, roadside or event support, and customer driveways; bike encountered as found, on uneven ground, variable light and weather, with tools carried to the bike rather than the bike brought to a bench.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics Tyre Mounting Console (TMC)
sources.date: 2025-10 (page last modified), product line commercial for years
sources.title: Tyre Mounting Console - TMC - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: State-of-the-art bicycle-factory tyre fitting equipment is an operator workstation: the human fits the tyre and tube while the machine provides centring, lubrication and automatic inflation. No autonomous mounting of tyre plus inner tube is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (installing bicycle tyres and tubes) but in a factory; shows the industry-leading equipment automates only sub-steps (centring, lubrication, inflation) while a human performs the tyre/tube fitting.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics MV manual tyre fitter
sources.title: MV - Tyre Mounting - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: Holland Mechanics' bicycle tyre mounting machines require a human operator to physically drive the mounting motion; the machine is a powered fixture, not an autonomous cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in a bicycle factory; establishes that even in the most structured (E1-like) setting, tyre and tube fitting is performed by a human operator.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics Disc Tyre Fitter (FD/DTM)
sources.title: Disc Tyre Fitter - FD - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: Even the high-throughput bicycle disc tyre fitter is described as a working station with safety handles for an attending operator, automating wheel centring and inflation rather than the bead/tube fitting itself.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (bicycle tyre fitting) in a purpose-built production line; shows the E1 counterfactual is still an operator-attended station, not autonomous completion.

sources.system: Bikebotix PNA tyre fitting machine
sources.title: PNA - Bikebotix
sources.claim: A second specialist supplier of bicycle wheel-building machinery likewise sells a tyre fitting machine as production equipment for an operator, with an integrated inflation system; no autonomous tyre-plus-tube assembly is described.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (bicycle tyre fitting) in a factory; corroborates that commercially available bicycle tyre-fitting automation is operator-driven, so autonomy cannot be established.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic tire changing exists for passenger cars in service bays: SmartBay dismounts and mounts car tires and balances wheels with a technician supervising several bays, but it works on tubeless automotive wheels, not bicycle wheels with inner tubes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive tire changing. Transfer to this task is NOT supported: bicycle work requires inserting a flexible inner tube without pinching it between bead and rim, levering thin high-pressure beads onto narrow (often carbon) rims, and removing/reinstalling a wheel from a bike frame past brakes and derailleurs - objects, forces and precision are unlike a car wheel on a lift.

sources.system: RoboTire
sources.title: RoboTire Installs First Tire Changing Robots at Discount Tire Store
sources.claim: Robotic wheel change systems are deployed in US tire retail stores, removing and reinstalling car wheels on vehicles, but they handle lug nuts and complete wheel assemblies rather than fitting tyres and tubes to rims.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive wheel removal/refitting in a shop (E2). Does not transfer: the robot never separates tyre from rim or handles an inner tube, and bicycle wheels are held by quick-releases/thru-axles with chain, brake and hub-motor interfaces.

sources.system: 3defacto Wheel Assembly Machines (WAM)
sources.title: Wheel Assembly Machines - 3defacto
sources.claim: Fully automated tire-to-rim assembly lines exist for large industrial/agricultural wheels, with operators loading tires and rims onto infeed conveyors and the system assembling and inflating them; these handle tubeless large-diameter wheels, not bicycle tyre-and-tube sets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated tire mounting onto rims in a purpose-built line. Transfer to bicycle tyre-and-tube installation is not supported: the line mounts large stiff tubeless tires with heavy machinery and has no inner-tube insertion, pinch-avoidance or thin-bead handling capability.

tasks.label: Assemble new bicycles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Independent bike shop service area: mechanic unboxes a new adult hybrid/road/MTB from the carton, removes packing material, installs fork/front wheel, stem and handlebar, seatpost/saddle, pedals and accessories, tensions and indexes derailleur cables, centers and adjusts rim/disc brakes, checks wheel true and hub/headset bearing preload, torques all fasteners to spec, inflates tires, then test rides and does a final safety check before the bike goes on the floor or to the customer.

Mass-retail / chain store back room or receiving area (Walmart, Target, Dick's, REI, or a contracted assembly service): high-volume assembly of entry-level adult and children's bikes that arrive ~85% assembled; install front wheel, bars, seat, pedals, training wheels, reflectors; adjust brakes and shifting; torque and complete a written safety checklist, often 5-15 bikes per shift under time pressure.

Shop assembly of a new e-bike or premium complete bike: heavy (20-30 kg) machine, battery/motor and wiring harness connections, display and firmware/diagnostic check, hydraulic disc brake alignment or bleed, torque-critical carbon components, plus normal cable, gear, wheel and tire setup and a road test.

Custom build in the shop from a frameset plus boxed components: face/chase bottom bracket, press headset, cut steerer, route internal cables/hoses, install drivetrain and cockpit, set up tubeless tires, fit the bike to the customer's measurements, and fine-tune shifting and braking.

On-site / mobile assembly: mobile bike-shop van or direct-to-consumer delivery-and-assemble service builds the new bike in the customer's garage, driveway or apartment lobby, or at an event/tour staging area, with variable lighting, floor surface, space and weather, tools carried in.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics Robotic Lacing Station (RLS) + tensioning/truing robots
sources.title: Removing the last manual step in wheelbuilding
sources.claim: Bicycle wheel building — spoke lacing, tensioning, truing — is automated in purpose-built factory machines; Holland Mechanics' Robotic Lacing Station laces wheels unattended and tensioning/truing robots are already in service on many bicycle factory floors. This is a sub-step of bicycle manufacturing, not assembly of a complete new bicycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory wheel building. It shows machine-level competence on one bicycle component in a fixtured cell, but a shop-floor new-bike build starts from pre-built wheels and requires cockpit installation, cable routing/indexing, brake setup and a test ride, none of which this machine performs.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics wheel building machines
sources.title: Holland Mechanics' virtually unmanned wheel construction machine meets demand for wider rims
sources.claim: Holland Mechanics' commercial wheel construction machines run virtually unmanned in bicycle factories, confirming that E1 automation in the bicycle industry is confined to wheel and rim production rather than complete-bicycle assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory wheel production. Cited as the state of the art in bicycle-industry automation; it substantiates only component production, not the multi-tool, adjustment-heavy build of a complete bicycle.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics Airline / Floorline / Skyline assembly conveyors and pre-assembly machines
sources.title: Assembly - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: The leading supplier of bicycle assembly equipment sells conveyor lines and single-purpose machines (chain cutter, brake sleeve cutter, head-cup press, bottom-bracket facing, fork cutter) that are fed and operated by human workers; complete-bicycle assembly on these lines is performed by operators, not robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory final assembly of new bicycles, the closest industrial analogue to the shop task. The equipment on offer presents the bike to human operators, showing that no commercially available system assembles a complete bicycle autonomously.

sources.system: Bosch adaptive assembly robot framework (e-Bike motor assembly case study)
sources.developer: Bosch Center for AI / Bosch Research
sources.title: The e-Bike Motor Assembly: Towards Advanced Robotic Manipulation for Flexible Manufacturing (arXiv:2304.10595)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art learning-based industrial manipulation has been demonstrated on an e-bike motor sub-assembly in a fixtured robot cell, with skills taught from demonstration and executed with force control; the demonstrated scope is a motor sub-assembly, not building a rideable bicycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precision, force-sensitive mechanical assembly of bicycle-related components in a purpose-built cell. It does not transfer to assembling a new bicycle, which adds deformable cables and hoses, brake and derailleur adjustment to feel, wheel/tire fitting on the frame, and a ride-quality safety check.

tasks.label: Estimate costs of repairing bicycles and write service tickets.
Install, repair, and replace equipment or accessories, such as handlebars, stands, lights, and seats.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail bike shop service bench: customer brings in a used bike of arbitrary make, model and age; mechanic clamps it in a repair stand and swaps a saddle/seatpost, replaces grips or wraps new bar tape, fits a new handlebar or stem, mounts battery lights, or replaces a bent kickstand. Fasteners may be worn, greased or seized; the finished part must be aligned, torqued and set to the rider's fit.

New-bike build-out at a shop or big-box/warehouse assembly area: bike comes out of the carton partly assembled, known model with kitted hardware; mechanic installs handlebar into stem faceplate, seatpost and saddle, pedals, reflectors/lights and kickstand, torques bolts to spec and checks alignment. Highly repetitive across identical units.

Custom or awkward accessory fitting on a customer bike: racks, fenders, child seats, baskets, dynamo or wired e-bike lighting, dropper posts, or a drop-bar swap requiring re-routing shift cables or hydraulic hoses, shimming or improvising mounts on frames without standard eyelets, then re-taping bars and testing.

Mobile/on-site service: mechanic works at a customer's home or workplace, at a race/community event, or at a curbside bike-share station, installing lights, seats, handlebar accessories or a kickstand with a portable stand and hand tools, in whatever space, lighting and weather is found.

Fleet or bike-share depot: high-volume maintenance of standardized shared or rental bikes returned dirty, wet and vandalized; technician strips damaged saddles, lights, baskets and grips and fits replacements, working through racks of bikes on a line of stands in a warehouse.

sources.system: ABB automotive final-assembly robot cells
sources.title: Final Assembly | ABB
sources.claim: ABB supplies deployed robotic cells for automotive final assembly that mount head and tail lamps, glass and wheels onto fixtured vehicle bodies, i.e. picking a rigid component, aligning it to a mating interface and fastening it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting lamps and wheels onto a fixtured vehicle in a robot cell. Transfer to fitting a light, kickstand, seatpost or handlebar on a fixtured bicycle frame is close in object class (rigid metal/plastic parts), in precision (millimetre alignment plus torqued fasteners), and in environment (parts kitted, workpiece held in a known pose).

sources.system: ABB Dynamic Assembly Pack for Final Trim and Assembly
sources.title: Dynamic Assembly Pack sensors enable ABB to automate trim assembly - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ABB's Dynamic Assembly Pack adds sensing that lets standard robots perform final trim and assembly operations - installing vehicle equipment - on car bodies in production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sensor-guided installation of vehicle equipment and trim in a production cell; the same class of guarded, fixtured, kitted-part cell is what an E1 bicycle accessory-fitting station would be.

sources.system: Cobot screwdriving cells (Universal Robots arms with Visumatic screwdriving tooling)
sources.title: Screwdriving With Cobots | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Collaborative-robot screwdriving cells are routinely deployed on assembly lines and cover the torque range used for bicycle accessory fasteners (roughly 5-6 Nm), with torque control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated driving of fasteners to a specified torque on presented components - the core motion of clamping a saddle rail, seat collar, stem faceplate or light bracket, whose specified torques (about 5-8 Nm) sit at the top of this cobot range.

sources.system: Cobot screwdriving system at an electronics manufacturer
sources.developer: Cobot/screwdriver integrator reported by ASSEMBLY magazine
sources.title: Cobot Automates Screwdriving at Electronics Company | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A deployed cobot screwdriving system performs precision fastening with screw-presence detection, torque control and position ... at 1-4 Nm on a production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torque-controlled fastening with verification on a fixtured workpiece; equivalent to the bolt-tightening and verification step of installing a bicycle saddle, stem faceplate or accessory bracket in a purpose-built station.

sources.system: Robot ANT (Automatic Nipple Truer) and related automatic hub filling/lacing and truing robots
sources.date: 2026-03 (product page; product line in factory use for years)
sources.title: Robot ANT - Truing - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: Holland Mechanics sells automatic bicycle wheel-building robots used in bicycle factories that lace hubs and true wheels to tension spec without a human performing the manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly and tensioning of bicycle components (spokes, nipples, hub, rim) inside a purpose-built machine. It shows bicycle parts of a known model can be assembled to spec by machine when fixtured and presented, which is the E1 counterfactual for new-bike accessory fitting.

sources.system: Robotized Hub Filler
sources.title: Bikebotix : bicycle assembly
sources.claim: Bikebotix (formerly Mach1 Machinery) supplies a robot-arm machine that inserts spokes into bicycle hubs as part of commercial bicycle wheel assembly machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot arm performing precise insertion of small bicycle parts into a fixtured bicycle component; supports fixtured, known-model bicycle part fitting at E1 but says nothing about arbitrary used bikes.

sources.system: Bosch e-Bike motor assembly robot system
sources.title: The e-Bike Motor Assembly: Towards Advanced Robotic Manipulation for Flexible Manufacturing (arXiv:2304.10595)
sources.claim: Bosch researchers built a robot system that autonomously performs e-bike motor assembly (grasping, insertion, force-controlled mating) as a flexible-manufacturing challenge in a laboratory robot cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: learned, force-controlled assembly of bicycle drive components in a fixtured cell; comparable part sizes and insertion tolerances to fitting a seatpost or stem, though demonstrated only on one known product in a lab cell.

sources.system: Shuz Tung complete bike assembling machines (HT-70 series)
sources.title: Shuz Tung Bicycle Production Lines | Best Bicycle Manufacture Equipment
sources.claim: Bicycle factory build-up machinery consists of single-purpose, operator-loaded stations (headset and bottom-bracket presses, crank and cup tightening machines, cable cutters) rather than robots that fit accessories to varied bikes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory fitting and tightening of bicycle components. Cited as context on what bicycle-industry automation actually covers; the machines are operator-loaded single-purpose stations, so they cannot by themselves support a positive judgment.

sources.system: SmartBay (Automated Tire); earlier RoboTire installations at Discount Tire
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The closest robotic vehicle-service systems working inside customer-facing shops handle only the highly standardized wheel/lug-nut interface, and even the newest system is not yet full end-to-end automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal and refitting of bolted vehicle parts inside a human service facility (E2). Included to show the limit of that transfer: it covers one standardized interface on a lifted car, not varied bicycle accessories, and is not yet fully autonomous.

tasks.label: Clean and lubricate bicycle parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full tune-up prep in a bike shop workshop: customer bike (road, MTB or e-bike, arbitrary dirt load) goes on a stand or wash bay; mechanic degreases and scrubs chain, cassette, chainrings and derailleur pulleys, washes and dries frame and wheels, then re-lubricates the chain and wipes off excess.

Quick drivetrain service in the shop: chain scrubber or rag-and-degreaser on the chain of a commuter, rental or fleet bike, dry it, apply chain lube link by link while backpedalling, wipe excess, oil derailleur/brake pivots.

Overhaul work at the bench: hub cones/cups and loose balls, bottom bracket, headset and pedal internals already disassembled; solvent-clean the greasy parts, dry them, then apply/repack fresh grease into races, threads and bearing surfaces.

New-bike assembly and pre-delivery in the shop: apply grease or anti-seize to seatpost, stem/pedal threads, bottom-bracket and headset interfaces and cable housings on a fixtured frame, and wipe the bike clean of shipping grime before delivery.

Mobile van, event or race-support work at the customer's home, workplace curbside, trailhead or race venue: clean and lube drivetrains outdoors with limited water and no fixed bay, in variable weather and layouts.

tasks.label: Align wheels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench truing of a customer's used wheel at a bike shop: mechanic removes the wheel, mounts it in a truing stand, and corrects lateral runout, radial hop and dish by turning nipples, evening spoke tension on a sound alloy or carbon rim.

Quick in-frame alignment: wheel left in the bicycle on a repair stand, trued against brake pads/frame as reference, plus seating and centering the wheel squarely in the dropouts/fork so it runs straight with even brake and chainstay clearance.

Crash- or pothole-damaged wheel in the shop: tire, tube, rim tape and sometimes cassette removed; broken or badly loosened spokes replaced and the rim judged salvageable or not, then re-tensioned and trued back into spec.

Final tensioning and truing of a freshly laced wheel during a shop wheel build or new-bike assembly prep: bring an untensioned, badly out-of-true wheel to final tension, roundness, lateral trueness and correct dish.

Mobile/on-site service: mobile repair van at a customer's driveway or office, race neutral support, or community repair event; wheel trued in a portable stand or in the frame under variable light, footing and weather with limited tooling.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics Robot SG truing robot
sources.title: Robot SG - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: Holland Mechanics' Robot SG is a commercial truing robot for bicycle spoked wheels (16"-29") that scans the incoming wheel with its Wheel ID system and executes the truing/nipple-turning cycle autonomously in a factory wheel-building line.
sources.transferJustification: Machine truing of a laced wheel is the same physical task as service wheel alignment: same objects (rim, spokes, nipples), same measured quantities (lateral runout, radial hop, dish/offset), at equal or tighter tolerance.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics Robot ANT
sources.title: Robot ANT - Truing - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: The Robot ANT (Automatic Nipple ...) is a six-arm truing robot handling 16"-32" wheels including fat-bike and eBike wheels, specified to ±0.1 mm accuracy with an integrated spoke tension analyser.
sources.transferJustification: Precision (±0.1 mm) exceeds the 0.2-0.5 mm lateral tolerance a shop mechanic works to, so the correction quality carries over to service truing of the same wheel types.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics wheel construction line (Inline Lacer, Robot SG, Robot-DTI)
sources.title: Holland Mechanics' virtually unmanned wheel construction machine meets demand for wider rims
sources.claim: In wheel-building plants using Holland Mechanics machines, human staff are needed only for lacing and tyre mounting; ... tensioning, stressing and truing stages run unattended, indicating the truing stage is machine-autonomous in production use.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics Proline truing/wheelbuilding robots
sources.title: The robot wheel building revolution | BikeRadar
sources.claim: Automated truing machines are in production use at major wheel brands, and after the move to automated outside truing the trade press reports machine-built wheel accuracy matching or exceeding skilled hand building.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that machine truing reaches worker-quality (indeed hand-builder-quality) output on the same wheels a bicycle repairer aligns.

sources.system: Bikebotix AFT4 / AFT4A truing robot
sources.title: AFT4 - Bikebotix
sources.claim: Bikebotix sells competing four-wrench truing robots (AFT4/AFT4A) that tighten by torque or turns, display measured side-to-side, up-and-down and offset values, and true up to 60 wheels per hour on 12"-32" classic, e-bike and carbon wheels.
sources.transferJustification: Second independent vendor confirming that measuring runout/offset and correcting it by nipple turning is a solved, productized machine operation on the same wheels repairers true.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics Roce / Roce Pro
sources.title: Precision wheelbuilding without the lock-in | Bike Europe
sources.claim: For workshops and small wheelbuilders, the new Holland Mechanics Roce machine measures runout but guides a human builder through the correction; automation of the correction itself remains tied to the company's factory truing robots.

tasks.label: Make adjustments to bicycles to improve customer fit and riding position.
Disassemble axles to repair, adjust, and replace defective parts, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail bike shop service area: cup-and-cone wheel hub overhaul on a customer's used bike. Mechanic removes the wheel, strips cassette/freehub, unscrews locknut and cone with cone wrenches, withdraws the axle, degreases, inspects cones and races for pitting, replaces loose 1/4" or 3/16" ball bearings and worn cones, repacks grease, reassembles and adjusts cone preload so there is no play but no binding, then reinstalls the wheel. Hub brands, axle types (nutted, quick-release, thru-axle) and corrosion levels vary bike to bike.

Bike shop: bottom-bracket/crank-axle service. Remove crank arms (often seized, using a crank puller or self-extracting bolt), unscrew cups or extract the cartridge spindle (reverse-threaded drive side), clean and grease frame threads, replace worn spindle/bearings, reinstall and torque to spec, verify chainline and spin.

Bike shop: damage or complex-internals cases — bent axle replacement after a crash, freehub body/pawl-and-spring service, coaster-brake or internally geared hub teardown. Requires pressing bearings, dealing with stripped or seized threads, sourcing an axle of correct length/thread, and reassembling internals in the right order.

Fleet maintenance depot (bike-share operator, campus/rental fleet, police or delivery fleet): repetitive axle and bearing service on a standardized fleet — same hub model repeatedly, cone adjustment, axle and bearing replacement in volume at a fixed workbench with a full tool set and parts bins.

Mobile/on-site repair: mobile-mechanic van at a customer's driveway, an event or race support tent, or an outdoor community repair stand. Bike clamped in a portable stand on uneven ground, variable light and weather, limited tools and parts; typical job is adjusting or replacing a loose/bent hub axle so the bike can be ridden away.

sources.system: Daisy (and Taz) recycling robots
sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy is an autonomous, purpose-built disassembly cell that takes apart iPhones (punching out screws, removing modules) at high rate; it is the most mature deployed example of robotic teardown of a fastened consumer product, but it only disassembles for material recovery — it does not diagnose worn parts, replace them, or reassemble a working product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic disassembly of a small fastened mechanical assembly in a purpose-built cell. It shows unfastening is automatable only for a closed set of known models presented in fixtures, and it stops at teardown; it does not substantiate defect diagnosis, part replacement, regreasing, reassembly, or bearing preload adjustment, which are the accepted output of bicycle axle repair.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly cell for permanent magnet electric motors
sources.developer: University research group (published in Royal Society Open Science)
sources.title: Robotic disassembly of permanent magnet electric motors
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic disassembly of a bearing-supported rotating machine (permanent-magnet electric motor) remains a research-lab activity: force-controlled extraction paths are planned to avoid damage, in an experimental cell, and the work covers teardown for remanufacturing rather than repair-and-reassembly of the unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous teardown of a shaft/bearing assembly with force control, the closest published analogue to pulling a hub axle. It is a single known product in a laboratory fixture and produces separated parts, not a repaired, preload-adjusted assembly, so it does not substantiate completing the bicycle axle instance even at E1.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics wheel-building machines (e.g. Robot SG, Robot OT truing robots)
sources.title: Bicycle Wheel - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: Automation that exists in the bicycle industry is purpose-built new-wheel production machinery (lacing, spoke threading, truing) inside factory lines; it builds wheels around supplied hubs and does not disassemble, diagnose, or overhaul hub axles and bearings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated bicycle wheel assembly in a purpose-built factory cell, the same object class (wheels/hubs). It shows the industry's automation envelope stops at building and truing new wheels; no machine in this line strips a hub axle, replaces cones/balls and sets bearing preload, so it cannot substantiate this task.

sources.system: RoboTire robotic tire-changing system
sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The nearest robotic system operating in a vehicle service facility performs wheel/tire changing (lug-nut removal, tire mounting) at a tire retail store; even this deployment does not touch axle or bearing service, which the trade press explicitly lists as separate work a service centre still inspects and performs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic unfastening and refitting of a vehicle wheel inside a human service shop (E2). Objects are far larger and standardized, the robot works on lug nuts only, and autonomy/human loading are unclear, so it cannot substantiate small-scale axle teardown, loose-ball bearing replacement, or cone preload adjustment on bicycles.
