tasks.label: Build wheels by cutting and threading new spokes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench build of a complete new wheel from all-new components: mechanic measures/calculates spoke length for the customer's hub and rim, cuts and rolls threads on spokes to that length with a shop spoke machine, laces the pattern, seats nipples, brings up tension, then trues, rounds, dishes and stress-relieves the wheel in a truing stand.

Batch building of several identical wheels in the shop for stock, house-brand wheelsets, rental/fleet or bike-share bikes, or e-bike builds: one spoke length cut and threaded in quantity, wheels laced, tensioned and trued to a repeatable standard.

Rebuild around a customer's existing wheel parts (rim swap onto a good hub, replacing a cracked rim on an e-bike motor hub, vintage restoration): de-tension and unlace the used wheel, clean/inspect the hub, then cut and thread new spokes to the new length and build, tension and true the wheel.

Repair of an assembled customer wheel with one or a few broken spokes, tire, rim tape, cassette and disc rotor still fitted: an odd spoke length is required, so the mechanic cuts and threads a spoke from a longer blank, threads it through the hub flange and existing crossings, then retensions and re-trues the wheel.

Specialty or heavy-duty wheel: tandem, cargo bike/trike, wheelchair or handcycle, recumbent, or moped-style wheel with a nonstandard hub, spoke count or rim, where lengths must be measured off the parts and spokes cut and threaded in-house before building.

Off-premises work: mobile repair van at a customer's home or office, or an event/race support tent, where a wheel must be rebuilt or spokes replaced on site with a portable spoke cutter/threader, on uneven ground and variable light.

sources.system: AMBA SpM II spoke making machine (with cutting and threading machine)
sources.title: Spoke making machines - AMBA - Aachener Maschinenbau
sources.claim: AMBA's SpM II spoke making machines take wire from the coil and automatically straighten, cut, roll threads and bend it into finished spokes at up to 300 spokes/minute with ±0.05 mm cutting tolerance, in a factory machine line.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the 'cutting and threading new spokes' element of the task, producing the same threaded spokes a shop mechanic cuts on a Phil Wood/Hozan machine, but under machine control in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: AMBA SpM II spoke making machine
sources.title: Spoke making machines - AMBA - Aachener Maschinenbau
sources.claim: AMBA states its current spoke machine generation cuts spokes to length with a servo-controlled feed to ±0.05 mm, i.e. length precision at or beyond what hand cutting achieves.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics Proline lacing and truing robots
sources.title: The robot wheel building revolution | BikeRadar
sources.claim: Holland Mechanics' computer-controlled wheel-building robots (lacing and outside-truing machines) build finished spoked wheels in bicycle factories for major wheel brands, with the company's managing director claiming accuracy that exceeds master hand building.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics wheel building lines (Lacer, Robot Quattro, Truing Robot, Hub Filling Station)
sources.title: Scalable solutions - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: Holland Mechanics sells scalable wheel-building lines in which a lacing/tightening machine feeds an automatic truing robot, optionally preceded by an automatic hub filling station, producing up to 650 finished wheels per eight-hour shift.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics CT-Twin Lacer
sources.title: Twin Lacer - CT - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: Holland Mechanics' CT Twin Lacer performs complete wheel lacing, with an automatic nipple feeder, in about 35-42 seconds per wheel.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics wheel building solutions
sources.title: Solutions - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: Holland Mechanics states its wheel-building machinery covers spoked wheels of any size, including fat-tire, e-bike, motor and wheelchair wheels.
sources.transferJustification: Extends the demonstrated bicycle-wheel building capability to the specialty wheel types (e-bike motor hubs, wheelchair, oversized) that make up the specialty-build instance.

sources.system: Holland Mechanics MOTO Inline Lacer / Moto Trueing Robot DM
sources.title: MOTO INLINE LACER - Holland Mechanics
sources.claim: Holland Mechanics also sells an automatic motorcycle inline lacer with automatic changeover for large-diameter spoked wheels, and an automatic motorcycle truing robot.
sources.transferJustification: Motorcycle wheel lacing is the same operation (spokes through hub flanges into a drilled rim, nipples started and tensioned) on heavier, larger spoked wheels, covering tandem/cargo/moped-style specialty builds.

sources.system: Phil Wood Spoke Cutting and Threading Machine
sources.title: Spoke Machine – Phil Wood and Company
sources.claim: The spoke cutting and threading equipment actually used at bike-shop benches is a hand-cranked, human-operated machine, not a machine-controlled system.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as context for the negative judgment that no autonomous system does this work in an ordinary human bike shop; it is a hand tool, not a robotic system.

tasks.label: Shape replacement parts, using bench grinders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dressing a cut-to-length part at the shop bench grinder: after cutting an axle, bolt, seatpost shim, steerer tube or brake stud, the mechanic removes the burr, chamfers the end and restores the thread lead. Small steel/alloy parts held freehand against the wheel, seconds to a minute each, judged by eye and by threading a nut on.

Fit-adapting a bracket or adapter to one particular bike: grinding metal off a fender stay, rack strut, disc-brake caliper adapter, derailleur hanger or dropout face until it clears the frame/tire and bolts up, with repeated hand test-fits on the customer's bike between grinding passes; the target shape exists only in the mechanic's judgment of the interference.

Salvaging damaged hardware removed from a bike: grinding down a rounded or snapped bolt, grinding a screwdriver slot into a seized fastener head, removing a rivet or peened head, dressing a damaged thread start or a burred dropout/brake-boss face on a detached component.

Reconditioning shop tools and jigs on the bench grinder: reshaping and sharpening cable-cutter jaws, screwdriver tips, chain-tool pins, cone-wrench faces and punches, or grinding a one-off special tool (drift, slotted socket, alignment pin) from bar stock.

Custom/high-end frame shop work: shaping dropouts, braze-on tabs, spacers and bushings from stock, and blending brazed or welded joints after a frame repair, to a defined profile and cosmetic standard on the shop's grinder/belt sander.

sources.system: Teqram EasyGrinder
sources.title: Teqram deploys automated grinding robot in 2 states with AMP - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Teqram's EasyGrinder, an AI/3D-vision robotic grinding and deburring cell, was installed and put into production at a US steel processor and fabricator, performing grinding of cut steel parts autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production grinding/deburring of cut metal parts. Bicycle-shop shaping is the same physical operation on comparable small steel/alloy workpieces (burr removal, chamfering, stock removal) at comparable precision; it shows force-controlled abrasive removal is deployed when the part is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Teqram EasyGrinder
sources.title: Autonomous solution from Teqram simplifies precision grinding - Cutting Tool Engineering
sources.claim: The EasyGrinder is reported to grind thermally cut steel workpieces without programming or preloaded geometry data, i.e. it copes with parts whose geometry it has not seen before.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix deburring/grinding of one-off cut parts. Bike-shop grinding is almost always a one-off part, so the relevant transfer is handling unseen geometry inside a cell rather than running a fixed program.

sources.system: Scan&Sand / GMR-AI
sources.title: Solutions - GrayMatter Robotics
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Sand autonomous robotic cells scan any mix of parts with onboard sensors, auto-generate the model and toolpath, and perform sanding, dimensional correction and surface finishing in high-mix production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive material removal and dimensional correction on varying, non-CAD parts inside a robotic cell. Transfers to shaping a replacement bike part when it is fixtured and presented, since object size, abrasive process and tolerance class are comparable.

sources.system: Robot-held-part grinding/polishing cell configuration
sources.title: Automated Grinding & Polishing | Surface Finishing Automation | AMD Machines
sources.claim: Commercial robotic grinding cells are routinely configured with the robot holding the workpiece and presenting it to a fixed, continuously running grinding station - the automation analogue of a worker holding a part against a bench grinder - and this configuration is preferred for small parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic surface finishing of small parts. It establishes that this task's specific motion pattern - part carried to a fixed abrasive wheel - is standard practice in purpose-built cells.

sources.system: E 50 RT robotic knife sharpening cell (Staubli TX2-90)
sources.title: Sharpening knives with a robot | Staubli
sources.claim: A fully automated Staubli TX2-90 robot cell loads knives from a magazine, measures them at a laser station and grinds/hones the cutting edges, processing hundreds of blades per shift.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sharpening/edge grinding of hand tools. Reconditioning cable-cutter jaws, screwdriver tips and punches on a bench grinder is the same operation - controlled edge geometry ground on hardened steel with in-process measurement - at similar size and precision.

sources.system: FANUC Integrated Force Sensing material removal
sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC's commercial material-removal packages combine industrial robots with integrated force sensing to hold constant tool-to-part contact force during robotic cutting, deburring, grinding, sanding and polishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled robotic deburring and cutting. Freehand bench grinding is fundamentally a contact-force-controlled abrasive process; this shows the contact control needed to avoid over-grinding small parts ships as an industrial product for cells.

sources.system: CLOOS welding robot + FerRobotics AAK/AOK grinding end-effectors
sources.title: Reproducible processes with automated robotic grinding - FerRobotics
sources.claim: At Kohl & Sohn, after CLOOS robots weld steel/stainless/aluminium assemblies a second robot performs automated rough and fine grinding of the welded joints with a force-compliant FerRobotics end-effector, to a consistent production quality standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic blending/dressing of welded joints on formed steel assemblies. Frame-shop blending of brazed or welded joints and dressing of tabs is the same abrasive joint-finishing operation at comparable scale and cosmetic standard.

sources.system: Marine welding/grinding robot (shipyard deployment)
sources.title: China deploys marine welding robot that handles 30-ton steel parts
sources.claim: A marine grinding robot using visual positioning and real-time force compensation has autonomously prepped and finished more than 500 steel sections on a shipbuilding shop floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grinding of fabricated steel parts at a fixed robotic workstation. Supports that vision-plus-force grinding of variable, non-nominal metal parts is in production use, but only where the work is brought to the machine.

tasks.label: Repair holes in tire tubes, using scrapers and patches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail bike shop workshop bench: customer's road/hybrid wheel comes in flat. Mechanic deflates and pulls the butyl tube, inflates it, finds the pinhole by sound/feel or a water bath, marks it, scuffs the area with the metal scraper/sandpaper, spreads a thin coat of vulcanizing cement, waits for it to go tacky, centers a small round patch, presses/rolls it, peels the backing, re-inflates and checks it holds.

Bike shop, awkward tube repairs: snakebite pinch flats with two holes, punctures near the valve stem or on a seam, multiple holes, or thick MTB/e-bike/fat-bike tubes. Mechanic must judge whether the tube is repairable at all, locate every hole, also find and extract the thorn/glass shard still embedded in the tire casing, then scuff and patch each site and verify.

Bike-share, rental or campus/institutional fleet maintenance shop: batches of standardized tubes of one or two sizes patched at a bench in volume, with a water tub for leak finding, a standing stock of patches and cement, and repaired tubes tagged and returned to stock.

Mobile bike mechanic on site at a customer's home, driveway, office bike room or curbside van: wheel handled on the ground or a portable stand, variable light and weather, tube patched with the kit carried in the van, then reinstalled and pressure-checked.

Event/neutral race support tent, group-ride roadside or shop-counter quick fix: fast repair under time pressure, often with a glueless self-adhesive patch or a hasty scuff-cement-patch, on unfamiliar tubes and wheels, sometimes with the rider waiting and helping hold the wheel.

sources.system: ROB4GREEN (EU AI/robotics tire-retreading project)
sources.developer: ROB4GREEN consortium (Horizon Europe / ROBIX cascade funding)
sources.title: AI and Smart Robotics for Tire Retreading: Boosting Circular Economy through Innovation – Rob4Green
sources.claim: In industrial tire retreading plants — a purpose-built, high-volume rubber-repair setting — the steps analogous to this task (inspecting the casing, skiving the injury, and repairing it with bonded patches) remain largely manual as of late 2025; the EU ROB4GREEN project's stated aim is to guide and support the human operator, not replace them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rubber puncture/injury repair by abrading the damaged area and bonding a rubber patch over it — the same operation sequence as inner-tube patching, on the same material class. It shows that even inside a purpose-built industrial cell with the workpiece fixtured on a spreader, the abrade-cement-patch sequence has not been automated; the transfer is therefore negative for this task.

sources.system: Kal Tire Cananea OTR retread plant skiving/grooving robot
sources.title: Kal Tire opens Mexico mining tire retreading and repair facility
sources.claim: A retread and repair plant uses an industrial robot for skiving and tread ... of mining tire casings — material removal on rubber — but the injury repair/patching itself is not reported as robotic, and the installation was described as a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive/cutting preparation of a rubber tire surface, comparable to scuffing a tube with a scraper. It covers only the surface-prep sub-step on a large, rigid-walled, machine-mounted casing; it does not locate pinholes in a limp inner tube, apply cement, or place and press a patch, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.system: SmartBay
sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial robotic tire-service system operates in an automotive service bay and performs wheel/tire changing, balancing and inspection with one technician supervising up to three bays; its scope is mounting/demounting and balancing, not puncture patching.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tire/wheel service in a structured shop bay. It demonstrates handling of wheels and tires under machine control, but its accepted output is a mounted, balanced wheel; no leak finding, scuffing, cementing or patch bonding is performed, so it does not carry over to repairing holes in tubes.

sources.system: Automated/robotic composite scarf-patch repair systems (e.g., STARC, robotic multi-tool for automated composite repair)
sources.title: Development of a Robotic and Automated Multi-Tool for Automated Composite Repair
sources.claim: Robotic patch repair of punctures/damage that has been automated in research and industry targets rigid composite aircraft structures (scarfing and pre-moulded patch bonding), not limp elastomer tubes, and the damage location is established beforehand by inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine surface preparation plus adhesive patch bonding over a defect. Transfer fails for this task: the substrate is rigid and dimensionally stable, damage is pre-located by NDI, and the systems are research demonstrators, whereas an inner tube is a floppy elastomer whose pinhole must first be found by inflation/immersion.

tasks.label: Diagnose and repair furnace or air conditioning systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/RV service bay: customer reports rooftop air conditioner not cooling. Tech climbs a ladder onto the RV roof, removes the shroud, checks capacitor, compressor and fan motor with a multimeter/clamp meter, checks thermostat and control board, then replaces a capacitor, fan motor, or the entire ~80 lb rooftop unit, reseals the roof gasket, and verifies cooling and amp draw.

Service bay: LP furnace 'no heat' complaint on a travel trailer. Tech reads board fault codes, checks 12V supply and thermostat, tests sail switch, limit switch and igniter, measures gas pressure with a manometer, clears blocked burner/orifice or exhaust, often pulls the furnace out through a cramped exterior access door, replaces board/blower/gas valve, reinstalls, leak-tests and verifies flame and airflow.

Mobile service call at a campground, RV park, storage lot or customer's driveway: uneven ground, weather, limited tools and power; tech diagnoses a furnace or A/C failure on site (roof access by ladder, cramped interior compartments), makes the repair or condemns the unit and orders parts.

Shop-based seasonal service/inspection with minor repair: clean or replace A/C filters and coils, check refrigerant-side performance indirectly (delta-T, amp draw), tighten roof mounting bolts, clean furnace burner tube and combustion-air passages of insect nests, check propane connections for leaks, lubricate/replace blower wheel.

Shop-based complex or intermittent diagnosis: chasing intermittent 12V/thermostat wiring faults, ducted-A/C airflow problems, control-board or compressor failures requiring manufacturer tech-line consultation and warranty documentation, then full unit replacement including roof cutout sealing or furnace duct reconnection.

tasks.label: Connect electrical systems to outside power sources, and activate switches to test the operation of appliances or light fixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-delivery inspection of a new travel trailer or motorhome in a dealership service bay: technician drags the 30A/50A shore cord out of its bay, plugs it into the shop pedestal (or adapts it), then walks the coach flipping every rocker switch and breaker — interior/exterior lights, roof A/C, microwave, converter/charger, water heater electric element, GFCI and all receptacles, range hood, fans, slide and awning switches — confirming each energizes and documenting faults on the PDI sheet.

Verification after replacing or repairing one specific 120V item (roof air conditioner, converter/power center, water heater element, receptacle, or a light fixture): connect the coach to shore power at the bay pedestal, switch on that one appliance or fixture, confirm it runs/illuminates and draws correctly, then disconnect.

Diagnostic troubleshooting of a customer complaint ("no power to half the ...", "A/C won't start on shore ...") on a used, owner-loaded coach in the service bay: connect shore power, cycle switches and breakers, reset GFCIs, meter voltage at the panel and at devices while operating switches to isolate the fault.

Seasonal service, de-winterization, or trade-in/intake inspection of a used unit in the shop or on the lot: connect to shore power and systematically activate all switches to test every appliance and light fixture, working around owner belongings and non-standard aftermarket wiring in a floorplan that differs from unit to unit.

Mobile RV service at a campground site, storage lot, or customer driveway: connect the coach to the campsite pedestal or a portable generator/adapter, then activate switches inside to test appliances and lights, on uneven ground, in weather, with no shop equipment and no control over the site.

tasks.label: Examine or test operation of parts or systems to ensure completeness of repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop service bay: after repairing an RV appliance (furnace, water heater, absorption refrigerator, roof A/C, cooktop), the tech runs it in place - lights the burner, confirms ignition sequence and flame, checks blower/compressor operation, measures temperature rise or cooling, verifies the fridge works on both LP and 120V - inside a customer coach of unfamiliar floorplan.

After any LP-gas-side repair (regulator, line, valve, appliance connection), the tech performs the required LP leak/pressure test: connects a manometer at a test port, pressurizes, watches for timed pressure drop, soaps/sniffs joints in cramped compartments, and verifies regulator delivery pressure. Done in a shop bay or on-site at a campground/driveway.

After plumbing repair (fresh-water fitting, pump, water heater bypass, drain/tank valve), the tech pressurizes the system or connects city water, runs every faucet/toilet/shower, cycles the pump, and crawls under sinks, into basement bays and behind panels looking and feeling for drips, then checks tanks drain and monitors read correctly.

After 12V/120V electrical work (converter/inverter, transfer switch, breaker or fuse panel, wiring, slide-out or jack motor, generator), the tech meters voltages at the panel and outlets, tests GFCI and polarity, exercises lights, slides, jacks and awnings through full travel, starts the generator and verifies output under load.

After chassis/running-gear work on a motorhome or towable (brakes, bearings, suspension, tires, hitch, drivetrain, trailer lighting), the tech re-inspects the components, checks torque and lamp function, then road-tests the unit on public roads for braking, tracking, noise and drivetrain behavior before release.

After roof, seam, window or sidewall resealing, the tech verifies the coach no longer leaks: hose/water spray test or low-pressure air test with soapy solution over all exterior seams, plus interior inspection with a moisture meter and by eye for water entry paths.

tasks.label: Repair plumbing or propane gas lines, using caulking compounds and plastic or copper pipe.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/RV service center bay: fresh-water supply leak in a travel trailer. Tech pulls interior panels, crawls into a cabinet or under the dinette/bed to trace a wet PEX or poly line, cuts out the damaged section, installs a coupling/crimp or push-fit, reseals the wall or floor penetration with caulk, pressure-tests the system and reinstalls trim. Customer belongings and cabinetry in the way; each floorplan routes lines differently.

Service bay: propane/LP gas line repair on a motorhome or trailer — replacing a chipped section of copper LP line or a cracked flexible hose/flare fitting at the regulator, furnace, water heater or range. Requires shutting down the system, flaring/threading fittings with pipe-joint compound, torquing flares in tight chases, then a manometer/soap leak test to RV industry standard before release.

Service bay, working under the coach or in basement compartments: drain/waste side repairs — cracked ABS drain line, broken low-point drain, leaking holding-tank flange or sewer outlet. Tech works on a creeper or lift, drops sections of corrugated underbelly, cements or clamps plastic pipe, and reseals fittings and the underbelly with caulk/sealant.

Mobile service call at a campground, storage lot or customer driveway: freeze-burst water lines or a leaking LP fitting found in the field. Uneven ground, weather, limited light and tools, no lift, unknown prior repairs; tech diagnoses, splices or replaces line, seals, and tests on site.

Custom van conversion / upfit shop: repairing or rerouting plumbing lines during a build or warranty rework — reworking a leaking galley supply run, replacing fittings on a fresh/grey tank, sealing hull penetrations — with the vehicle open and components still accessible on the bench or in the shell.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: sealing leaking gas-line joints. It shares the goal (stopping a gas leak with sealant) but is remotely operated, purpose-built for one pipe geometry, and cannot access, disassemble, or repair RV LP/water lines; being teleoperated it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Inspect recreational vehicles to diagnose problems and perform necessary adjustment, repair, or overhaul.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/RV service center bay: customer reports water stains and soft spots. Tech walks the roof, inspects seams, vents, skylights, windows and sealant, traces the leak (moisture meter, hose/pressure test), then re-seals, removes trim/molding, replaces rotted decking or delaminated wall panel, and reinstalls components. Unit is a 30-40 ft trailer or motorhome parked in a shop bay with lifts and ladders.

Electrical system diagnosis and repair in a shop bay: complaint of 'no 12V power' or dead outlets. Tech checks battery, converter/inverter, shore-power cord, breakers, fuses, and solar controller with a multimeter, traces harnesses behind cabinets and under the chassis in cramped spaces, then replaces the failed converter, breaker, wiring section, or connector and verifies operation.

LP gas and appliance work in a shop bay: furnace, absorption refrigerator, water heater, or cooktop not operating. Tech performs a manometer leak/pressure test on the LP system, pulls the appliance from its cabinet, cleans burners and orifices, checks the sail switch/thermocouple/control board, replaces the failed part, re-lights and verifies safe operation.

Chassis, running gear and mechanism service in a shop bay or outside lot: inspect and adjust brakes, repack/replace wheel bearings, check suspension, springs, axles and tires, adjust or repair slide-out room mechanisms (rack-and-pinion, hydraulic, cable), leveling jacks, awning motors, and hitch/coupler components on a lifted or blocked unit.

Mobile/on-site service call at a campground, storage lot, roadside, or customer's driveway: tech arrives in a service van, interviews the owner, diagnoses the complaint (A/C not cooling, generator won't start, slide stuck out, water leak) in situ with uneven ground, weather, pets and belongings present, and completes the repair with van-carried tools and parts.

Interior and structural repair in a shop bay: inspect and repair cabinetry, dinette/furniture hardware, flooring, plumbing fixtures and drains, ceiling panels, or a delaminated sidewall; includes removing damaged material, fabricating/fitting replacement pieces, and finishing to a customer-acceptable appearance.

tasks.label: Locate and repair frayed wiring, broken connections, or incorrect wiring, using ohmmeters, soldering irons, tape, or hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/RV service center bay: customer reports a dead or intermittent 12V DC circuit inside the coach (lights, water pump, slide controller). Tech pulls trim, drawers or a bed base, traces model-specific hidden harness runs behind wall/ceiling panels, uses a meter/ohmmeter to find a chafed wire or failed crimp, cuts out the bad section, splices/solders with heat-shrink or butt connectors, tapes and re-secures the loom, reassembles trim, retests.

Shop bay, exterior/chassis wiring: 7-way trailer umbilical, breakaway switch, brake and marker/clearance light circuits. Tech works on the ground, on a creeper or on a lift, checks continuity/ground through corroded pins, re-terminates the plug, replaces chafed under-frame wire, seals with heat-shrink and tape, secures with clamps, verifies each function with a tester.

Shop bay, 120V AC side: shore cord, converter/inverter, transfer switch, GFCI receptacles and breaker panel. Tech finds incorrect wiring (reversed polarity, open ground, loose lug, mis-wired outlet after an owner/DIY modification), de-energizes, re-strips and re-lands conductors under screw terminals, re-tests with meter and outlet tester.

Shop bay, heavy damage: rodent-chewed or water-damaged harness in a basement compartment, slide-out wire chase, roof run, or behind a refrigerator/furnace. Long confined-space reach-in work in a dirty, contaminated coach, often multiple splices per circuit, wire loom replacement, and re-routing to keep clearances.

Mobile service call: campground site, storage lot, customer driveway or roadside. Tech works from a van with hand tools and a multimeter, in variable weather and lighting, on an unfamiliar coach with the owner's belongings in place; diagnoses and repairs frayed wiring or a broken connection on site and verifies the circuit.

sources.system: Comau Racer-3-0.63 robotic soldering cell (with ETNEO soldering technology)
sources.title: Precision Robotic Soldering for Electronics Manufacturing - Comau
sources.claim: Comau has deployed a fully automated robotic soldering cell (Racer-3-0.63 with dispensing-soldering head and vision QC) in a high-volume electronics plant; it solders pre-programmed joints on fixtured parts inside a compact production cell, and does not locate or diagnose faults in installed wiring.
sources.transferJustification: Soldering is one tool named in the task. Transfer is limited: the cell works on parts fixtured and presented in a purpose-built cell with known joint coordinates, whereas the task requires finding an unknown fault in installed wiring and repairing it in place, so it substantiates only the soldering sub-step, not the whole instance.

sources.system: Cable Splicing Machine
sources.title: Con Edison and ULC Technologies test Cable Splicing Machine to improve worker safety, grid reliability - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced field cable-repair machine found, ULC/Con Edison's Cable Splicing Machine, is placed and loaded by human splicers and autonomously performs only cable end preparation on medium-voltage cable; humans still make the splice.

It falls short of this task because humans locate the fault, position the machine and clamp the cable, the machine only strips layers of a single large MV cable, and it performs no fault diagnosis, splicing, taping or verification.

sources.system: Dual-arm robotic wire harness assembly system (Tampere University)

sources.claim: Automated handling of vehicle wire harnesses remains a research problem even inside structured factory cells; published dual-arm systems address specific assembly steps and harness manufacturing is still largely manual.

sources.system: Robotic arm-assisted PCB diagnostic and measurement system (Dobot Magician + Arduino)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking resistance/continuity measurements with a robot, the diagnostic half of this task. Transfer is limited to fixtured boards with known probe locations in a benchtop cell; it performs no disassembly, no search of hidden harness routing, and no repair.

tasks.label: Confer with customers, read work orders, or examine vehicles needing repair to determine the nature and extent of damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Service-lane/write-up intake at an RV dealership: the customer describes symptoms of their motorhome or travel trailer (no hot water, slide-out won't retract, ceiling stain, 'something smells like propane'), the technician/advisor interviews them, walks around and through the coach, verifies the complaint, notes model/VIN and pre-existing damage, and produces the work order describing nature and extent of the problem.

Shop diagnostic examination of an electrical, appliance, or generator complaint: pull access panels and covers, meter 12V/120V circuits, test battery/converter/inverter, cycle the refrigerator, furnace, water heater, roof A/C or generator, read fault codes, and determine root cause and how far the failure extends (e.g., burnt harness, failed board, dead cooling unit).

Water-intrusion and structural damage examination in the shop: climb a ladder onto the RV roof, inspect sealant, seams and rooftop penetrations, take moisture-meter readings on sidewalls and ceiling, press/probe for soft spots and delamination, open interior panels or cabinetry to trace the leak and judge extent of rot.

Exterior/body damage assessment for an estimate or insurance claim on a unit parked in the shop or lot: document scrapes, punctures, hail dents, fiberglass cracks, torn awning, damaged skirt or underbelly across the exterior and underbody, and report the nature, location and extent of visible damage.

Mobile service call: technician drives to a campground site, storage yard, or customer's driveway, confers with the owner on site, and examines the RV in place (uneven ground, weather, hookups connected, limited access) to determine the problem and how extensive the damage is.

Pre-delivery or annual multipoint inspection on an incoming trade-in or new unit: systematically operate and check every system — LP pressure/manometer test, water system pressure test, appliances, slides, awning, brakes, bearings, tires, running gear — to determine defects and their extent before sale or repair authorization.

sources.claim: UVeye's automated drive-through scanners perform a full 360-degree ... (Class 6-8 trucks, buses) in seconds and automatically identify external and mechanical flaws, damage and foreign objects, generating an annotated digital report; over 1,000 systems are deployed at dealerships, fleets and auctions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated exterior/underbody damage detection on large road vehicles. It transfers to the RV exterior damage-documentation instance because the objects (truck/bus-sized vehicle bodies and underbodies), the required output (a report naming location and nature of damage), and the presentation (vehicle driven through a fixed scanning lane) are comparable to documenting body damage on a motorhome or trailer.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: vehicle condition documentation at a service drive. It bounds current capability: Spot inspects fixed, pre-taught assets on a repeatable route and reports anomalies; it does not interview customers, open RV compartments and appliances, or diagnose a reported fault on a varied consumer vehicle.

tasks.label: Repair leaks with caulking compound or replace pipes, using pipe wrenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Remedial roof reseal at a dealer/independent RV service center: tech climbs onto the coach roof in the bay or lot, water-tests or visually traces the leak, scrapes and cuts away cracked, weathered lap sealant around vents, skylights, AC shroud and front/rear seams, cleans the EPDM/TPO or fiberglass substrate with solvent, then lays self-leveling sealant beads and verifies no further intrusion.

Sealing a newly installed or reinstalled exterior component in the shop (roof vent, antenna base, ladder bracket, window, compartment door): flange surface is clean/new, tech beds it on butyl tape and runs a continuous non-sag sealant bead around the perimeter and over screw heads to make it watertight.

Sidewall, window, molding and slide-out perimeter recaulk on a used unit: cut out failed, chalky caulk with a knife/scraper along vertical and overhead seams, clean, mask, and tool a fresh bead of self-leveling or non-sag sealant, working around trim, decals and awning hardware in the service bay.

Interior fresh-water plumbing leak: tech empties cabinets, removes access panels or crawls into the wet bay, finds the leaking fitting or split PEX/copper/poly line, cuts out and replaces the section or fitting, tightens threaded connections with pipe wrenches and thread sealant, then pressure-tests the system.

Waste/drain plumbing under the coach: unit on a lift or tech on a creeper, drop or cut the underbelly, replace a cracked ABS drain pipe, P-trap, tank flange or termination valve, wrench up slip and threaded joints, seal with sealant, refill and leak-check.

sources.system: FANUC dispensing and seam sealing robots (e.g., M-20iA)
sources.title: Automotive Automation & Robotics Solutions | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC dispensing/seam-sealing robots autonomously apply sealant and adhesive beads to fixtured car bodies in automotive production cells, including vision-guided sealer application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive seam sealing. Same material class (elastomeric sealant beads) and bead-placement precision as RV exterior sealing around flanges and joints, but performed on clean, fixtured bodies presented in a fenced cell (E1), not on weathered surfaces needing sealant removal.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: sealing vehicle panel joints. Demonstrates closed-loop vision-checked bead application on vehicle sheet-metal seams in a fenced cell, the E1 analogue of running a perimeter sealant bead around a newly fitted RV roof vent or window flange.

sources.system: Boeing 'quadbot' automated drilling/fastening system

sources.transferJustification: Related task: sealing fastened joints on large vehicle skins. Comparable objects (thin skin panels, fastener rows) and comparable watertight/airtight bead quality, achieved with the workpiece fixtured in a purpose-built cell (E1).

sources.system: Flexible robot sealant dispensing cell (RGB-D + off-line programming)
sources.title: Flexible robot sealant dispensing cell using RGB-D sensor and off-line programming - ScienceDirect

sources.transferJustification: Related task: sealant dispensing on parts whose exact geometry/pose is unknown. Supports E1 bead application on unit-to-unit-varying RV flanges when the coach is fixtured in a cell; it does not address removing failed sealant or locating leaks.

sources.system: Sarcos Sapien 6M and Guardian DX
sources.title: Sarcos Successfully Demonstrates Robotics for Shipyard Maintenance, Inspection, and Repair - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Sarcos demonstrated dexterous robots performing shipyard maintenance, inspection and repair tool work, but the robots are teleoperated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hand-tool maintenance work on large vehicles/vessels. The closest analogue to wrenching and sealing in confined vehicle spaces is still human-in-the-loop teleoperation, supporting negative judgments for the plumbing and remedial-sealing instances.

tasks.label: Inspect, repair, or replace brake systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Travel trailer or fifth-wheel electric drum brake service in an RV dealership service bay: technician jacks the unit, pulls wheels and drums (often rust-seized), inspects linings, magnets, springs, backing plate and races, measures drum wear, replaces shoes/magnets or whole backing-plate assemblies, repacks and adjusts bearings, sets shoe clearance, reinstalls and road/controller tests.

Motorhome (Class A/C, Ford E/F-series or Freightliner chassis) hydraulic disc/drum brake service in a shop bay: inspect pads/rotors/calipers and hoses, measure rotor thickness and runout, replace pads and rotors, service or replace calipers, flush and bleed brake fluid, check ABS faults, test drive.

Electrical brake diagnosis on a trailer: test tow-vehicle brake controller output, measure magnet current draw per axle, check ground and connector corrosion, trace and repair chafed or broken axle wiring, test and replace breakaway switch and battery, verify with amp clamp and controller.

Mobile RV service call at a campground, storage lot, or customer driveway: uneven gravel or asphalt, no lift, technician works on jack stands under the unit to inspect and adjust brakes, replace a burned magnet or seized brake assembly, or diagnose a no-brakes complaint before travel.

Air brake system inspection/repair on a diesel-pusher motorhome in a heavy-vehicle bay: check air compressor and governor, drain tanks, inspect chambers, slack adjusters, S-cams and linings through the inspection port, measure pushrod stroke, perform leak-down and applied-pressure tests, replace lines, valves or chambers.

sources.system: RoboTire robotic tire changing system
sources.title: RoboTire Installs First Revolutionary Tire Changing System at Discount Tire | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: RoboTire deployed an autonomous robotic wheel-removal and tire-changing cell inside Discount Tire retail service bays; it locates lug patterns, removes lug nuts and wheels, and reinstalls them, but performs no brake inspection, repair, or replacement. Business later failed.

Cited to show the frontier: even this narrow, fixtured step is limited to passenger-car wheels, and no cited capability extends to disassembling, measuring, or replacing worn brake components.

sources.system: SmartBay (with BrakeWise brake insights)

It performs no brake repair or replacement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated tire service and vehicle inspection in a human service bay, the nearest commercial analogue. It substantiates no brake work: the brake element is data/insight generation, and the machine still depends on a human for manual handling steps.

sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic assembly of brake hardware in a purpose-built E1 cell. It is the strongest E1 candidate, but it covers only assembly of new, uniform components in fixtures; it does not demonstrate wear inspection, measurement, removal of seized/corroded parts, or brake adjustment on a used vehicle.

tasks.label: Connect water hoses to inlet pipes of plumbing systems, and test operation of toilets or sinks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-delivery inspection of a new travel trailer or motorhome in a dealership service bay: tech screws a city-water hose onto the coach's exterior inlet (or fills the fresh tank and runs the 12V pump), pressurizes the system, climbs into the coach, opens and closes each galley/lav faucet and the shower, flushes the toilet and checks that the bowl holds water, then inspects under sinks, behind access panels and at the water heater for drips before signing the PDI sheet.

Verification after a plumbing repair on a customer's used coach in the shop (new toilet seal, cracked PEX fitting, replaced pump or faucet): reconnect the water supply hose to the inlet, bring the system up to pressure, actuate the repaired fixture repeatedly, watch for seepage with a flashlight inside a cramped cabinet or under the coach, and redo the joint if it weeps.

Seasonal de-winterization / water-system service in the shop: connect hose to the city-water inlet, flush antifreeze through every line, run each faucet hot and cold until the water runs clear, flush the toilet several times, sanitize and drain, and confirm no leaks at fittings loosened by freezing.

Mobile service call at a campground, storage lot or customer driveway: hook the coach to the campsite spigot or a portable supply with regulator, then test toilet flush and bowl seal and sink/shower operation inside an owner-occupied coach cluttered with belongings, in variable weather and lighting.

Bench check of a replacement plumbing component before or after installation (12V demand pump, water-heater fitting, toilet water valve): connect a supply hose to the part's inlet on the shop bench, pressurize, cycle it, and confirm flow and leak-tightness.

tasks.label: Remove damaged exterior panels, and repair and replace structural frame members.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership/independent RV service bay: travel trailer with an impact- or hail-damaged (or delaminated) fiberglass sidewall panel. Tech removes awning rail, trim, windows and vents, cuts butyl/sealant, drills out rivets and screws, peels the bonded laminated panel off, inspects and repairs the framing behind it, then bonds/rivets in a replacement panel and reseals.

Water-intrusion repair in a shop bay: with the skin off, tech cuts out rotted wood (or corroded aluminum) studs, headers and blocking in a sidewall, scribes and fabricates replacement members from lumber/tube, glues, staples/screws and squares them into the wall, replaces damaged luan/foam, then re-skins.

Roof work on a lifted or ladder-accessed coach in the shop or yard: remove damaged aluminum/TPO roof skin sections and rotted or crushed rafters/roof bows after a tree-limb or low-clearance strike; sister or replace bows, re-deck, re-skin and reseal all penetrations.

Steel chassis/frame repair on a motorhome or fifth-wheel raised on jacks or a lift: cracked or bent frame rail, outrigger, or slide-out support member is cut/torched out, replacement steel or reinforcement plate is fabricated, clamped, fitted around brake lines, wiring and tanks, welded out and coated.

Collision repair in the body shop: remove a damaged molded front/rear fiberglass cap or a slide-out room exterior panel, repair the crushed framing and corner posts behind it, fit and align the replacement cap/panel to body lines, refasten and seal.

Mobile service call at a campground, storage lot, or customer driveway: cut out and remove a damaged section of exterior panel or skirt metal, sister or splice a broken frame/wall member for a road-worthy repair, patch and seal, working outdoors on uneven ground with limited tooling.

It substantiates only the fastener-removal sub-step on CAD-known airframes in a purpose-built robot cell; it does not cut sealant, detach and handle a bonded/damaged panel, or repair the structure behind it, which the RV instances require.

tasks.label: Reset hardware, using chisels, mallets, and screwdrivers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Entry door or baggage-compartment door hardware reset at a dealership/RV service bay: door sags or latch won't catch, so the tech removes the hinge or striker, chisels/pares the mortise deeper or plugs and re-drills stripped screw holes, taps the hardware home with a mallet, re-drives screws, and test-cycles the door until it seals and latches.

Interior cabinet, drawer, table and furniture hardware reset inside the coach: overhead cabinet hinges pulled loose in transit, catches and strike plates out of position, drawer slides and screen-door latches misaligned. Work is done kneeling in a cramped, unit-specific interior, often with the customer's belongings present, on thin lauan/particleboard substrate.

Exterior window, roof-vent, awning-arm, entry-step and trim hardware reset in the shop or on the lot: loosened or shifted brackets, latches and hold-downs re-seated with mallet taps, screws re-driven into fresh or plugged holes, sealant/butyl re-set behind the flange, on a curved fiberglass or aluminum sidewall.

Mobile service call at a campground, storage lot or customer driveway: tech works from a van, on uneven ground and in whatever weather, resetting a sagging entry door hinge, a slide-out fascia latch, a compartment lock or a step bracket with hand tools only.

New-unit PDI/prep bay at a dealership: going through a freshly delivered coach and resetting the hardware loosened or misaligned in transit — cabinet hinges, latches, strike plates, trim screws — many small resets across one unit before customer delivery.

sources.system: HRP-5P humanoid robot
sources.title: Development of a humanoid robot prototype, HRP-5P, capable of heavy labor
sources.claim: Research humanoid autonomously picked up a gypsum board and screwed it to a wall at a simulated residential construction ...; a laboratory prototype demonstration, not a fielded system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous screwdriver use against a building surface in a mocked-up human setting. It is the most advanced free-standing demonstration of tool-based fastening outside a fixtured cell, but it is a one-off prototype in a purpose-built mockup and far from worker-quality hardware fitting.

tasks.label: Open and close doors, windows, or drawers to test their operation, trimming edges to fit, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-delivery inspection or post-repair walkthrough of a whole coach in a dealership service bay: technician climbs through the unit and cycles the entry door, every exterior compartment door, all windows, and dozens of cabinet doors and drawers, listening/feeling for binding, then corrects minor rubs (adjust catch, ease a hinge, sand a rubbing edge) item by item.

Entry door or exterior baggage/compartment door on a unit in the bay binds, drags on the seal, or won't latch after damage repair, reseal, or frame flex; technician cycles the door, finds the interference point, shims or adjusts hinges and strike, planes/files/trims the door or frame edge, and re-tests until it opens and closes smoothly and seals.

Interior cabinetry: a cabinet door rubs its neighbor or a drawer front binds/sticks in a residential-style RV interior; technician removes the door or drawer, sands or trims the edge or face, adjusts Euro hinges or drawer slides, re-hangs, and cycles it to confirm smooth travel and even gaps on painted/laminated finished surfaces.

Window work: slider, awning-crank, or emergency-exit window is stiff, won't latch, or the interior trim ring/valance fouls the sash; technician operates the crank/latch, trims the trim ring, sash edge, or opening as needed, adjusts hardware, and re-tests operation and seal.

Mobile service call at a campground, storage lot, or customer driveway: technician diagnoses a single balky door, window, or drawer on site with hand tools, trims/sands the offending edge and adjusts hardware, working outdoors in whatever weather and access the site offers, often with customer belongings in the unit.

sources.system: RedViking Automated Aircraft Measure and Trim Cell
sources.title: Automated Aircraft Measure and Trim Cell - RedViking
sources.claim: A purpose-built automated cell uses laser radar metrology plus a robot to trim aircraft doors and hatches to dimensional tolerance, i.e. machine measurement of fit followed by robotic edge material removal on door-sized panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measure-and-trim of aircraft doors/hatches to fit. The core act of the RV task is judging where a door or panel interferes and removing material from its edge to achieve fit; the aerospace cell does exactly that on comparable door-sized workpieces at tighter tolerance, with the part brought to a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Dynabrade / FerRobotics Automated Cabinet Door Sanding Cell (ACF active force control)
sources.title: Dynabrade Automated Cabinet Door Sanding Cell - FerRobotics
sources.claim: A commercially offered robotic cell sands complete cabinet doors, including their edges and corners, held in a vacuum fixture that accommodates different door sizes, using active force control for consistent finish quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled robotic edge sanding of wood/MDF cabinet doors in a fixture. RV interior cabinet doors and drawer fronts are the same class of object and finish; easing or trimming a rubbing edge is the same contact-force material-removal operation the cell performs.

sources.system: Applus+ Reliable Analysis Door Slam test bench
sources.title: Test Bench Performs Door Reliability Analysis
sources.claim: A purpose-built test bench autonomously opens and closes (slams) vehicle doors through prescribed cycle types and conditions to evaluate door operation and durability, without a human operating the door.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated open/close cycling of a fixtured vehicle door to characterise its operation. This is the 'open and close doors to test their operation' half of the RV task, on a comparable door with comparable latch/hinge hardware, performed by machine on a fixtured unit.

sources.system: Skyline Instruments SL-T05 Drawer Slide Durability Cycle Testing Machine (ANSI/BIFMA X5.5 extendible element cycle test)
sources.developer: Skyline Instruments Co., Ltd / Dongguan Skyline Industrial
sources.title: Drawer Slides Durability Cycle Testing Machine SL-T05 - Skyline Instruments
sources.claim: Commercial automatic test machines cycle drawers and cabinet doors mounted on furniture, controlling travel and frequency and displaying the push-pull force required, i.e. machine measurement of how a drawer or door operates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cycling of drawers and hinged furniture doors with force readout. It supplies the objective 'test their operation' step for a fixtured drawer or cabinet door, the same hardware used in RV cabinetry.

sources.system: DoorBot bimanual mobile manipulator
sources.title: DoorBot: Closed-Loop Task Planning and Manipulation for Door Opening in the Wild with Haptic Feedback
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous door opening by mobile robots in unstructured, previously unseen settings reaches roughly 90% success on the opening act alone, with no fitting, trimming, or hardware adjustment involved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening unseen doors in the wild. It bounds what in-situ (E2/E3) robotic capability exists today: research-grade opening of doors at ~90% success, far short of a service technician's fit diagnosis, trimming, and re-verification inside a coach.

tasks.label: Explain proper operation of vehicle systems to customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Refinish wood surfaces on cabinets, doors, moldings, or floors, using power sanders, putty, spray equipment, brushes, paints, or varnishes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-coach spot repair/touch-up: tech works inside a customer's coach in the service bay, kneeling in a 7-8 ft wide aisle, repairing scratches, gouges and water stains on installed cabinet face frames, wall trim and moldings that cannot be removed — scuff-sand the area, fill with wood putty/stick, blend a color-matched stain, wipe/brush a topcoat so the repair disappears into the surrounding aged finish. Includes PDI touch-ups on new units. Layout, wood species and finish differ unit to unit; owner's belongings present.

Bench/booth refinishing of removed cabinet doors and drawer fronts: doors unscrewed, hardware bagged, then a batch of flat/raised-panel oak or maple fronts is stripped or scuff-sanded with orbital/power sanders, dings filled and sanded, then sprayed with stain, sealer and clear lacquer or varnish on a rack or in the shop's spray booth, cured, and re-hung.

Bench/booth finishing of replacement or removed trim: new molding, ceiling/wall trim strips, valances, slide-out fascia, tabletops or a replacement door are cut, sanded, stained to match the coach's original color (test panels/color sleuthing) and varnished off the vehicle before installation.

Full in-place interior cabinetry refinish/repaint on a renovation or water-damage job: mask off walls, counters, glass and upholstery inside the coach, sand all face frames, cabinet boxes and end panels in situ, prime and spray or brush paint/varnish in the confined interior with ventilation and overspray control.

Wood or laminate floor refinishing inside the coach: sand a damaged/discolored section of the coach floor with a small power sander around slide-outs, dinette legs and cabinet toe kicks, fill seams and gouges, and apply polyurethane/varnish in the confined interior.

sources.system: Vention Rapid Sanding Solution (RSS) with FANUC CRX-30iA cobot
sources.title: Vention Introduces Turnkey Robotic Sanding Solution for Cabinetmakers and Woodworkers – Wood Industry
sources.claim: Vention's Rapid Sanding Solution is a commercially sold turnkey robotic sanding work cell aimed at cabinetmakers and woodworkers, using laser panel measurement and preset sanding patterns to sand wood panels/doors after loading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production sanding of cabinet doors/panels. Same objects (wood cabinet doors and flat panels), same tool class (powered abrasives) and same surface-quality target as the sanding stage of RV cabinet refinishing, performed in a fixtured work cell.

sources.system: Scan&Sand
sources.title: GrayMatter Scan&Sand a Flexible Robotic Sanding Solution - The Robot Report
sources.claim: GrayMatter's Scan&Sand robotic sanding system adapts to varied part geometry and handles wood among other materials, i.e. high-mix parts rather than a single fixed part.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix robotic surface preparation. Establishes that scanning-based sanding cells cope with one-off wood parts of differing shape, which is the condition of RV refinish work where each door/trim piece differs.

sources.system: GrayMatter autonomous robotic cells (Scan&Sand / coating cells)
sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics – Member Spotlight - NCMS
sources.claim: GrayMatter deploys autonomous robotic cells performing surface preparation, coating and inspection in production facilities, i.e. sanding plus spray coating under one autonomous cell architecture.

sources.system: iGiotto spraying robot with 3D scanning on automated coating lines
sources.title: Automated coating line and solutions for spray systems | Cefla Finishing
sources.claim: Cefla's iGiotto anthropomorphic spraying robots coat wood doors, window frames and other 3D objects on automated lines, with a 3D scanner generating spray trajectories automatically for each product shape.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial spray finishing of wood doors and frames. Same materials (wood), same media (stains, sealers, topcoats) and same equipment class (spray guns) as the finishing stage of cabinet-door refinishing; scanning removes the need for a pre-programmed identical part.

sources.system: Putty Filling Roller Coater (coating feeder)
sources.title: Roller Coating Machine | Surface Finishing Equipment | Senr
sources.claim: Automatic putty-filling roller coaters are standard line machines that fill surface defects and pores on wood/MDF panels without manual filling, ahead of sanding and topcoating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine putty application on wood panels. Covers the 'putty' step of the refinish sequence for flat cabinet doors and panels presented to the line, the same filler-then-sand sequence the RV tech performs by hand.

sources.system: Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System
sources.title: 3M Finesse-It Robotic Paint Repair System Fixes Paint Defects on Assembly Lines - The Robot Report
sources.claim: 3M's Finesse-it robotic paint repair ... autonomously finds and repairs localized paint defects by sanding and polishing on automotive assembly lines, but only on uniform painted/clear-coated bodies inside a fixed plant cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated localized defect repair. Cited to bound the transfer — it does abrasive sand-and-polish on a fresh uniform clear coat in a fenced plant cell, and does not fill putty or blend color-matched stain into an aged wood finish, which is what in-coach touch-up requires.

sources.system: Okibo EG7+
sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7+ is an autonomous mobile robot ... sands and sprays drywall walls and ceilings on construction sites, i.e. in-situ surface finishing of large flat building surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ sanding and spray finishing in an unstructured setting. Cited to bound the transfer — it is a floor-standing machine working large open drywall planes with monochrome paint, not a manipulator that can enter a 7-ft-wide coach, mask an interior, and stain-match wood cabinetry.

tasks.label: Seal open sides of modular units to prepare them for shipment, using polyethylene sheets, nails, and hammers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End of line inside a manufactured/modular home plant: worker unrolls 6-mil polyethylene sheeting over the open 'marriage' side of a floor half sitting on its transport chassis, pulls it taut over a 13-14 ft tall by 40-70 ft long opening, trims it, and nails wood lath/battens through the poly into the studs and rim; works from ladders/rolling stands, overlapping seams.

Outdoor shipping yard at the plant: finished modules staged on carriers are sealed before dispatch - poly stretched over the open side plus roof edges, gable ends, and around protrusions, nailed with battens and taped; done in wind, sun, rain, on gravel, with ladders and a helper.

Service/production bay for an RV, park model, or van conversion: an open sidewall section, removed windows, or a cut-out opening is covered with poly sheeting cut to fit around trim, brackets and moldings, then fastened with furring strips and nails/staples so the unit can be moved or shipped.

Dealer lot, storage yard, or delivery site (no institutional control of the ground or weather): torn or blown-off poly on a stored or delivered unit is stripped and re-sealed before re-shipment or winter storage; access from ladders on uneven ground, adjacent units and vehicles nearby.

Irregular units in the plant: modules with porch cut-outs, dormers, hinged roof sections, cantilevered floors or partially open roofs; sheeting must be custom cut, folded around corners and 3D features, and nailed in multiple planes.

sources.system: Kawasaki BX250L robotic wall sheathing cell (SCADAware integration, Rehkemper prefab plant)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki Robotics
sources.claim: Four Kawasaki BX250L robots on Güdel rails autonomously place and nail OSB sheathing onto framed walls that are squared and clamped on a motorized table in a prefab housing plant, driving nails into studs per CAD data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nailing rigid sheathing to a framed element on a fixtured table. It transfers for the nailing half of this task (finding studs, driving fasteners at low precision), but the system handles only rigid panels, not the limp polyethylene sheet this task requires.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-380 multifunction bridge with batten positioner
sources.title: Everything done right from an early stage | HOMAG
sources.claim: A WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridge fitted with a batten positioner automatically positions and nails roof battens onto elements clamped on BUILDTEQ tables in a timber-element plant, fed from a batten magazine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying and nailing wooden battens onto a fixtured building element - the same fastening operation as nailing lath over poly sheeting. It does not, however, place or tension the sheeting itself.

sources.system: Randek AutoWall (S3000) wall production line
sources.title: Autowall - Systems for Prefabricated Houses | SCM Group
sources.claim: Randek's AutoWall line produces wall frames with sheathing and, optionally, a breather membrane on one side, with workflow described as fully automated via CAD/CAM; the membrane handling step is not separately documented as robot-applied.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a building wrap membrane to a framed element in a plant. Marketing copy does not establish that the membrane is placed and fastened without an operator, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Randek membrane cutting station (in timber-panel prefabrication factories)
sources.title: Assessment of Manufacturing Processes for Automated Timber-Based Panelised Prefabrication (Buildings, MDPI)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed survey of automated timber panel prefabrication finds that the commercial membrane (building wrap) station automates only feeding and cutting of the sheeting; a worker still feeds sheets into the machine and staples the membrane onto panels.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point: this is the same object class (flexible weatherproofing sheet applied over a framed element and fastened) and shows the placing/fastening of the sheet remains manual in commercial prefab plants.

sources.system: Pro-Tect / Gulf Coast Wrap modular shrink-wrap containment service
sources.developer: Pro-Tect Shrink Wrap Containments; Gulf Coast Wrap
sources.title: Protecting Modular Buildings with Shrink Wrap During Transport & Storage - Pro-Tect
sources.claim: Weatherproofing of modular building units for transport and storage is delivered as a manual contractor service - crews cut, place, heat-shrink and patch polyethylene film over roofs, walls and open sides of modules; no automated wrapping equipment is described.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed commercially at scale (sealing modular units with polyethylene for shipment); the state of practice is human crews, indicating no fielded robotic system performs it.
