Bench overhaul in the shop: a heavy-duty or floor closer is removed from the door and brought in, torn down (cover, retaining ring, pinion/spindle out), old packing removed and the spindle repacked with leather washers/seal kit, chamber refilled with hydraulic oil and bled, unit function-tested and reinstalled on site.

In-place repack of an obsolete or heritage closer/floor spring at an older mixed-use or apartment building where no seal kit is available: technician cuts or fits leather washers to size, packs the spindle, refills the oil chamber in situ, and tests, often with the unit partly inaccessible and leaking oil onto the floor.

tasks.label: Bore or cut holes in flooring as required for installation, using hand or power tools.

instances.label: Automatic sliding/swing door replaced or installed at the entrance of an operating commercial facility (retail store, hospital, office lobby). New build or large-facility fit-out, open bare slab: a run of anchor holes drilled from CAD/layout coordinates in open floor area for bollards, guide posts, high-speed door track bases or operator floor mounts, before finishes are installed.

Residential or small-business garage door work: drilling holes in a garage slab for vertical track anchors, bottom brackets, jamb anchors or protective posts; kneeling in a cluttered garage corner beside the track, slab painted/cracked/uneven, occasionally notching the slab or a wood floor for hardware clearance.

Boring holes through wood flooring/subfloor or raised access floor panels to route wiring/conduit for actuators, push plates, floor closers, loop wires or activation mats in a store, office or house; hole saws, spade bits or jigsaw, working around joists, ducts and hidden utilities, then sealing the penetration.

tasks.label: Clean door closer parts, using caustic soda, rotary brushes, or grinding wheels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop-bench rebuild of a hydraulic surface door closer: the disassembled aluminum body, piston, spindle/pinion, springs and valve screws are soaked in a hot caustic/alkaline degreasing solution, scrubbed and wire-wheeled to remove varnished hydraulic oil and grime, rinsed and dried, then inspected by the tech before reassembly. Repair shop with a parts sink/washer, bench wire wheel and grinder.

Heavily corroded or gummed concealed-overhead or floor-closer components (cast body, cover plate, arm/spindle assembly, fasteners) pulled from a commercial building and brought back to the shop or service van; rust, mastic, concrete dust and hardened grease removed with caustic soak plus rotary wire brushing, with judgment about how far to clean pitted surfaces.

On-site cleaning at the door of an occupied commercial building: brushing grease, dirt and old lubricant off the still-mounted closer body, arm, shoe, track and mounting plate, and clearing debris from a floor-closer cement case, working around pedestrians with hand brushes and rags, no shop equipment available.

Residential garage service call: cleaning caked grease, dust and debris from installed garage-door operator drive components — rail, chain/belt, sprocket, trolley, gear-and-sprocket kit — while working from a ladder in a cluttered private garage before re-lubrication.

Bench material-removal finishing of used closer/operator parts: dressing scored or pitted surfaces, deburring a nicked shaft, pinion or valve seat, and knocking corrosion off steel arms with a grinding wheel or rotary brush so the parts will seal and reassemble properly.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic brush/abrasive deburring and surface finishing of machined metal parts. tasks.label: Set in and secure floor treadles for door-activating mechanisms, and connect power packs and electrical panelboards to treadles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Replace a worn or failed floor treadle/pressure mat at an operating retail store or supermarket entrance: pry out the old unit from its recessed frame, clean and shim the pocket, set and secure the new treadle flush with the finished floor, land its leads in the header power pack/control box, adjust and test the door with customers passing through.

New installation at a commercial building under construction or fit-out (new store, office lobby, plant entrance): lay out the treadle position, saw-cut/recess the slab or set the frame before finish flooring, anchor it, run conduit and pull wire to the operator power pack and to the electrical panelboard, terminate, energize and commission - amid other trades, dust and unfinished floors.

Industrial/warehouse power-operated door: set a heavy-duty treadle or safety mat in a forklift traffic aisle, secure the frame to the slab, run wiring to the door power pack and to a panelboard or motor control panel, connect and verify interlock/safety operation in an operating plant.

Institutional building (hospital, school, airport, government office): install or swap a floor treadle at an automatic entrance in an occupied corridor, often after hours, secure it, connect the power pack and panelboard circuit, and verify ANSI/AAADM and ADA-compliant operation before returning the door to service.

Older or small commercial property (corner shop, converted building, parking-garage pedestrian door) with uneven, damaged or unknown flooring and legacy/undocumented wiring: fit the treadle to whatever pocket exists or build one up, chase or surface-raceway the wiring back to an old power pack and panelboard, and make it work.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wiring of control-panel mounting plates. tasks.label: Fabricate replacements for worn or broken parts, using welders, lathes, drill presses, or shaping or milling machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the door company's fabrication shop: a bracket, mounting plate, hinge strap or reinforcement for a rolling steel or hydraulic door has cracked. The tech measures the broken original with tape and calipers, marks out flat bar/angle stock, cuts it (bandsaw/torch/shear), drills mounting holes on the drill press, welds the assembly, grinds and primes it.

In the shop, on a lathe/mill: turning a replacement shaft, pin, bushing, roller stem, or drum/sprocket adapter for a door operator or counterbalance assembly to a measured fit; cutting a keyway or flats and drilling/tapping set-screw holes; one-off, often reverse-engineered from the worn part with no drawing.

In the shop: cutting and fabricating replacement linear stock to length - guide angle, track section, jamb angle, bottom bar, strut, or slat - squaring the ends, punching or drilling the hole pattern, welding splices or end caps, deburring.

On a field service call at a commercial building or loading dock: portable welder, grinder and cutting torch used at the opening to cut away a broken bracket, guide or weld joint on an installed door, then cut, fit and weld in a new piece in place, working overhead or on a lift, around traffic and weather.

At a residence or small commercial site: improvised fabrication out of the truck in a driveway or garage - cutting a strut, angle or shaft to length, drilling new holes in a track or bracket, filing/shaping a part to fit an obsolete garage door assembly with no replacement available.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended CNC turning/milling/drilling of one-off and small-lot metal parts. A replacement door shaft, pin or bushing is geometrically simpler and looser in tolerance than the aerospace parts produced in this cell, so performance transfers.

tasks.label: Cover treadles with carpeting or other floor covering materials, and test systems by operating treadles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket / retail store entrance vestibule: fit or replace the carpet or mat insert that covers the floor treadle (pressure mat) activating a sliding or swing door — measure and trim the covering to the aluminum trim frame, seat it so it does not bind the treadle, then walk on the treadle at several points to confirm the door opens, holds and closes correctly, while customers pass through.

Restaurant, grocery back-of-house or hotel kitchen swing door with a treadle plate: cover the plate with carpet, rubber or vinyl matting cut to fit, secure the edges against carts and wet mopping, and test by stepping repeatedly on the treadle from both traffic directions.

Hospital, nursing home, school or public building entrance/corridor treadle-activated door: install the floor covering over the treadle, then test activation, hold-open time and safe closing as part of a documented door-safety check, working around patient and staff traffic.

New door installation or store remodel: a newly set treadle in an unfinished or partially finished floor at a construction/renovation site — scribe and trim the carpet or floor covering around the treadle frame, glue or fasten it, and test the complete new system amid dust, debris and other trades.

Service call with no new covering: verify an existing carpeted treadle system by stepping on it at various points and speeds, diagnose intermittent or sticking activation caused by the covering or a worn switch, reseat/adjust the covering and re-test until the door operates reliably.

roles.description: Install, repair, and maintain mechanical regulating and controlling devices, such as electric meters, gas regulators, thermostats, safety and flow valves, and other mechanical governors.

tasks.label: Record maintenance information, including test results, material usage, and repairs made.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Disassemble and repair mechanical control devices or valves, such as regulators, thermostats, or hydrants, using power tools, hand tools, and cutting torches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gas distribution field work: technician repairs or rebuilds a service/district pressure regulator, meter-set valve, or relief valve at a customer premises or curbside meter set. Outdoors or in a basement/meter room, live gas, mixed-vintage hardware from many manufacturers, corroded threads and unions, hand and power tools, occasional torch work.

Municipal water utility: fire hydrant repair in the street or right-of-way - pull the bonnet or barrel, replace stem, O-rings, seat ring or main valve, sometimes cut seized bolts or a shear section with a torch, often in an excavation with mud, water and traffic control.

Building controls: repair or rebuild of thermostats, pneumatic controllers, actuators and small control valves in commercial or institutional buildings - mechanical rooms, ceiling plenums, rooftop units; disassemble the device in place or at a bench cart, replace diaphragms/springs/linkages, recalibrate.

Repair-shop bench overhaul in a valve shop or utility meter shop: disassemble a used gate, globe, ball, check or relief valve or a regulator of varied make and size, clean and inspect, lap or machine seats, replace packing, seats and soft goods, reassemble to torque spec and pressure-test to acceptance.

In-plant service of standardized, high-wear valve assemblies at a dedicated maintenance station in an industrial facility (e.g., steel-mill ladle slide gates, batch-identical units): open the assembly, strip worn sealing components, clean the seating faces, fit new wear parts, re-clamp and release for service.

tasks.label: Lubricate wearing surfaces of mechanical parts, using oils or other lubricants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench overhaul: technician rebuilding a gas regulator, control valve, relief valve, meter register or governor at a repair shop bench applies the specified grease/oil to stem threads, gear trains, bushings, O-rings and seat surfaces during reassembly, wiping off excess and avoiding contamination of seats and diaphragms.

In-plant field lubrication at an industrial facility (refinery, chemical plant, power station, water/wastewater plant): technician walks a route with a grease gun and oil can, lubricates valve stems, yoke nuts, gear operators, actuator linkages and governor pivots on installed valves, some at elevation on pipe racks or in tight spaces, then strokes the valve to distribute lubricant.

Customer-premises service call: technician servicing a gas meter set, house/commercial regulator, damper linkage or thermostat-driven control at a private home or small business lubricates the linkage, stem, pivots and threads in a cramped basement, crawlspace, closet or outside meter set with clutter and no fixed layout.

Outdoor distribution/pipeline work: greasing plug and ball valve stems, injecting sealant/lubricant into valve fittings at pipeline block valve sites, city gate stations, curb boxes and street valve vaults, in weather, mud, traffic, and with varying valve makes and buried or awkward access.

Installation/commissioning lubrication on a job site: after setting a new regulator, control valve or actuator on a construction or retrofit site, the installer lubricates stem threads, actuator gearboxes and packing follower surfaces before stroking and calibrating the device, amid unfinished, cluttered surroundings.

tasks.label: Calibrate instrumentation, such as meters, gauges, and regulators, for pressure, temperature, flow, and level.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility meter shop: technician proves/calibrates removed utility meters (diaphragm gas meters, positive-displacement water meters, electric meters) — mounts each on the shop test bench or prover, runs the accuracy points at prescribed flows/loads, adjusts or tags out-of-tolerance units, and records certified results.

Industrial plant or treatment facility (refinery, gas plant, power station, water/wastewater plant): technician calibrates installed process instrumentation — pressure/DP transmitters, RTD/thermocouple temperature loops, flow and level transmitters — by isolating the device, applying reference input with a hand pump/dry-block, comparing output, trimming via HART, and documenting as-found/as-left.

Customer premises (homes, apartment buildings, small businesses): technician checks and adjusts the meter set — in-place meter accuracy/leak check, service regulator delivery pressure and lock-up, resetting the adjustment screw and resealing — in tight, cluttered, varied spaces with occupants present.

Shop bench or accredited calibration lab: technician calibrates analog dial pressure gauges, digital gauges, thermometers/RTDs, and pressure/temperature switches against reference standards (deadweight tester, pressure controller, dry-well), adjusting or issuing pass/fail and calibration certificates.

Outdoor gas regulator/measurement station or metering skid: technician calibrates the station instrumentation — pressure transducers, chart recorders, EVC/flow computers, level and temperature elements — and sets pilot/regulator setpoints, working in a fenced station, vault, or skid in ambient weather.

tasks.label: Install, inspect and test electric meters, relays, and power sources to detect causes of malfunctions and inaccuracies, using hand tools and testing equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential / small-commercial self-contained (socket-type) electric meter exchange or new install at a customer premises: technician drives to the address, cuts the seal, pulls the old meter from the socket on the outside house wall or an apartment meter bank, inspects the socket jaws, seats the new smart meter, verifies voltage and that the meter registers/communicates, re-seals and documents. Weather, dogs, locked gates, obstructing vegetation and varied enclosure heights are normal conditions.

Utility meter shop / metering laboratory bench work: acceptance-sample and periodic accuracy testing and calibration of new or in-service self-contained meters on a test board (series of load points, registration, function and insulation checks), recording error percentages and passing, adjusting or condemning each meter. Batch volumes, standard meter types, indoor climate-controlled shop.

Field accuracy verification of a meter already installed after a high-bill complaint or routine field check: portable test set / phantom-load standard connected at the installed meter, load points run, error computed against the standard, and the meter judged accurate or pulled for replacement. Occurs at the customer's service location.

Field troubleshooting of a metering installation that is malfunctioning: no AMI reads, dead display, burnt or arcing socket jaws, loose or corroded service conductors, suspected tampering/bypass, mis-wired or reversed connections. Technician uses meters, clamp-ons and hand tools at an as-found service entrance, then repairs or replaces the affected part.

Transformer-rated (CT/PT) commercial or industrial metering install and commissioning: mount meter and test switch in a cabinet or switchboard room, wire CT/PT secondaries, verify ratios, polarity and phasing with test equipment, apply and verify load, correct errors found. Layout differs at every customer site.

Substation / control-house work: inspect and test protective relays, control-panel power supplies and station DC sources — open panels, isolate with test switches, connect a secondary injection relay test set, run pickup/timing tests, check battery and charger condition, and diagnose faults found. Utility-controlled premises with standard panel layouts.

instances.label: Gas utility service technician at a residential or small-commercial premises: after installing or repairing a meter set or answering a leak call, leak-tests the regulator, meter and piping joints with a combustible-gas detector and leak solution, then verifies delivery pressure and lock-up pressure with a manometer at the regulator test port. Cramped basements, crawl spaces, or outside wall sets; weather, clutter, and customers present.

Utility meter/regulator shop: technician bench-tests recovered or new diaphragm gas meters and service regulators for registration accuracy, internal/external leakage and set pressure using provers and test stands, then tags and records results. Indoor shop with fixed benches, standard fittings, utility-controlled access.

Valve repair shop (VR/NB stamp work): technician mounts a rebuilt pressure-relief or safety valve on a certified test stand, sets and verifies set/popping pressure, reseat pressure and seat tightness per API 527/ASME using nitrogen or water, adjusts the spring, and issues the test report. Indoor shop, standardized fixtures and media.

Industrial plant (refinery, chemical, power, large boiler room): in-situ testing and calibration of control valves, regulators and pressure/temperature switches — hooking a hand pump or documenting calibrator to the test port, verifying setpoint and deadband, stroking the valve, and leak-checking flanges and packing. Congested piping, elevated platforms, hot/live process, plant permit control.

Industrial plant routine or post-repair leak-check round: technician walks the unit checking previously repaired and in-service valves, flanges and packing for leakage with a gas detector, acoustic or IR instrument and logs findings against the asset list. Fixed plant layout, defined route, institution-controlled access.

Outdoor/field pressure-control assets: district regulator stations, farm taps, LP tank systems, water pressure-reducing valves and backflow preventers at varied sites — pressure-testing regulator and relief setpoints, running lock-up checks, and leak-surveying the station or assembly with portable precision gauges and detectors. Vaults, roadside enclosures, mixed weather, site-to-site variation.

tasks.label: Turn meters on or off to establish or close service.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential electric service turn-on/turn-off (move-in, move-out, non-payment disconnect and post-payment reconnect) at a single-family home or apartment: locate the socket-mounted meter on an exterior wall or in a meter bank, break/apply seals, pull the meter or operate the socket, install a blank or lock ring for a cut-off, verify the service is dead or live. Conditions vary: fenced yards, dogs, weather, occupants present.

Residential or small-commercial natural gas shut-off at the meter set: close the service valve at the outdoor (or basement) meter with a wrench, install a lock or plug, seal and tag the meter, record the index reading. Done for move-outs, non-payment, or safety.

Residential or small-commercial natural gas turn-on to establish service: open the meter valve, purge and pressure/leak-test the house piping, gain entry to the premises, check appliances, relight pilots and verify safe combustion before leaving service on. Requires an adult occupant present.

Water service on/off at a residential or small-commercial premise: operate the curb stop in a buried curb box with a valve key (often after clearing dirt/pavement debris) or the angle stop at the meter in a pit or basement; lock off for non-payment, restore on payment, and confirm flow.

Larger commercial, industrial or institutional customer (school, hospital, plant, office tower): close or establish service at a large gas meter set, CT-metered electric installation, or compound water meter in a mechanical room, meter vault or fenced yard - operate large valves or pull test-switch links/service disconnect, lock and tag, coordinate with facility staff.

tasks.label: Shut off service and notify repair crews when major repairs are required, such as the replacement of underground pipes or wiring.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gas service technician finds a leaking or damaged service line at a residence or small business and shuts off gas at the outdoor meter set: locates the meter (often behind shrubs, fences, in a side yard), applies a meter wrench to the quarter-turn service cock, closes it, locks/tags the valve, checks the meter has stopped, and calls dispatch to send a main/service replacement crew.

Water utility technician shuts off a service at the buried curb stop in the parkway or sidewalk: finds the curb box (sometimes paved over or silted in), clears the box, drops a long curb key onto the stop several feet down, closes it, verifies no flow at the customer's meter, and reports the failed service/main for excavation and replacement.

Shutoff inside customer premises: meter or main valve is in a basement, crawlspace, closet, or utility room of a home or small business; technician gains occupant access, works in cramped and cluttered space, closes a corroded or seized valve (or caps the line), verifies shutoff, and notifies the repair crew.

Isolation inside a controlled facility (industrial plant, hospital, campus, or institutional mechanical room): technician closes upstream isolation valves or de-energizes a control circuit on a failed regulator/control valve, applies lockout/tagout, verifies zero energy, and notifies the maintenance crew for pipe or wiring replacement.

Street or vault work: technician closes distribution main valves in roadway valve boxes or vaults (multi-turn gate valves, sometimes with a powered valve operator) to isolate a section of gas or water main for pipe replacement, under traffic control and with a valve card/turn-count record, then notifies the construction crew.

Electric service disconnect at a customer meter: technician cuts the seal, pulls the meter or opens the service disconnect/pole fuse, applies a lock and tag, confirms the premises are dead, and notifies the line crew that the underground service cable must be replaced.

tasks.label: Install regulators and related equipment such as gas meters, odorization units, and gas pressure telemetering equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service: install or change out a gas meter set at a single-family home or small apartment — mount the regulator on the service riser with pipe dope, hang the diaphragm meter on swivel nuts/meter bar, set shutoff and vent orientation per code, leak-test and purge, restore service and relight appliances. Work is on customer property (yard, alley, meter closet) with varying clearances, weather, pets and occupants.

Commercial/industrial customer meter set: install a larger regulator, filter, relief and a rotary/turbine meter with threaded or flanged 2-6 in piping on an outdoor pad, meter room or rooftop at a business, restaurant, school or plant; includes rigging heavier components, supports, pressure test and start-up.

Distribution/city-gate station work: install a new regulator run (regulator, monitor, relief, filter, valves) inside a fenced utility regulator station, vault or prefabricated skid enclosure; welded/flanged steel piping, torque-tightened bolting, set and verify pressure settings, pressure/leak test before cut-in.

Install gas pressure telemetering / remote monitoring equipment: mount RTU or pressure recorder enclosure, tap and install pressure transducers and gauge lines, run conduit and wiring, install antenna/solar panel, then configure and commission the unit and verify readings arrive at the SCADA/control center.

Install an odorization unit at a city gate or LNG/propane facility: set the injection pump/wick or bypass odorizer and odorant tank, connect tubing and controls, tie into the flow signal, charge with mercaptan under hazmat precautions, calibrate injection rate and verify odorant level in the gas stream.

sources.system: RND Automation Modular Assembly Platform (Epson T3/G3 SCARA and C8 six-axis robots, MagneMotion transfer)
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A commercially delivered multistation robotic assembly cell threads valve components together with anti-cross-thread compliance, applies O-rings and thread-locking adhesive, torque-tightens the joint with a driver, and then loads each finished valve into a leak-test fixture and unloads it after test.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly of pressure-tight threaded valve bodies. Installing a regulator/meter set is the same class of work — threaded pressure joints made up with sealant to a specified torque and then leak-verified — so performance carries over when the parts are fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: MAKEEN Energy Valve Leak Detector (VLD) with CIR-II infrared leak test head

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated leak verification of a threaded gas joint. The accepted output of a regulator/meter installation is a leak-free pressure-tight joint; this machine performs that verification autonomously on comparable threaded gas connections.

tasks.label: Cut seats to receive new orifices, tap inspection ports, and perform other repairs to salvage usable materials, using hand tools and machine tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility meter-and-regulator shop: a returned gas regulator or small control valve is stripped and inspected; the worn seat is re-cut/refaced (seat cutter, reamer, or bench lathe) so a new orifice/seat disc will seal, then checked for bubble-tight shut-off. Small brass/steel bodies, thousandths-of-an-inch seat finish.

Industrial valve repair shop: a worn gate/globe/check or control valve body is rigged, chucked or clamped, and the seating surface is re-machined (portable seat-machining head, lathe, or seat grinder) to accept a new seat ring or restore the contour; lapped and seat-leak/hydro tested.

Shop bench work: drilling and tapping inspection/test/gauge ports in valve, regulator or meter bodies, chasing damaged threads, and installing thread inserts (Heli-Coil) so a used housing can be put back in service.

Field/in-situ salvage repair at a regulator station, meter set, vault, or customer basement: re-tapping a stripped port, refacing or lapping a seat in place with hand and portable tools, in cramped or awkward positions with weather, dirt and live-gas precautions.

Ad-hoc salvage improvisation in the shop: measuring a damaged part, deciding what can be saved, then turning/cutting/grinding a bushing, spacer or shim from stock and hand-fitting it (file, bench grinder, hacksaw) so an obsolete or hard-to-source component can be reused.

tasks.label: Turn valves to allow measured amounts of air or gas to pass through meters at specified flow rates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility/meter-shop bench proving: technician mounts a residential or small-commercial diaphragm gas meter on a bell prover or shop transfer prover, connects hoses/index reader, then opens and throttles the prover valves to pass measured air through the meter at the specified check (~20%) and open (~100%) flow rates, records percent proof, adjusts or tags the meter.

Field accuracy test at a customer premises: technician isolates the meter set, connects a portable transfer prover (cart or van-mounted) to the in-service meter, purges, then operates the prover and meter-set valves to pass air/gas at two or more specified flow rates, reads proof, and restores service.

Commercial/industrial metering station or plant meter run: technician manipulates block, bypass and throttling valves on rotary/turbine/ultrasonic meter runs to establish specified flow rates through the meter for on-site proving, commissioning or capacity checks, coordinating with station load and pressure.

Shop bench testing of gas pressure regulators, relief/flow valves and governors: technician connects the device to a compressed-air bench, turns supply and throttling valves to pass air at specified rates through a flow indicator or meter, checks set point, capacity and lockup, and adjusts the device.

New or renewed meter-set turn-on at a residence or small business: after installing meter and regulator, technician slowly opens the service and outlet valves, passes a measured flow through the meter index (dial/flow test) to verify registration and check the customer's piping for leaks before restoring service.

sources.claim: The Dresser Model 6 Transfer Prover, a commercial gas-meter proving system used by US utilities in shops and the field, sets and holds the configured flow rate through the meter under test with an electrically actuated throttle valve and solenoid-operated butterfly valve under controller software; the operator selects test points and clicks Run Test and the prover executes the test sequence.

tasks.label: Report hazardous field situations and damaged or missing meters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Vary air pressure flowing into regulators and turn handles to assess functioning of valves and pistons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gas utility meter/regulator shop: technician clamps a rebuilt or new residential/commercial gas service regulator onto a shop test manifold, varies inlet air pressure through the range, opens and closes hand valves to load and unload it, and judges set point, droop, relief and lock-up against spec, recording pass/fail. Bench is a human-built shop station with hand-clamped connections and manometers.

Valve/actuator repair shop: rebuilt relief valves, pneumatically actuated control valves and cylinders are tested on shop benches — air/nitrogen pressure raised and lowered, actuator stroked, handwheels and hand levers turned to check piston travel, seat tightness, spring set and smoothness before the unit is certified and returned.

Industrial plant or refinery (in-service or during turnaround): instrument/valve technician varies the instrument-air signal to a pneumatic control valve or ESD valve positioner, strokes it partially or fully, and assesses actuator piston travel, friction, hysteresis, response time and lock-up; work occurs on the plant's process units under plant control.

Gas distribution district regulator station or farm tap: technician enters a fenced station enclosure or vault, turns bypass and isolation valve handles, applies and bleeds pressure to the worker and monitor regulators, and verifies set point, lock-up and relief with a manometer, outdoors in variable weather and confined space.

Customer premises meter set (house side, small commercial building, or crawl space/basement): technician turns the service valve and appliance handles, varies/blocks pressure to the second-stage regulator, and checks lock-up and delivery pressure with a manometer in a cluttered, non-standard, as-found setting.

Building pneumatic HVAC controls: technician in a mechanical room or above ceilings varies branch air pressure to pneumatic thermostats, valve and damper actuators with a calibrator or squeeze bulb, turns handles and observes piston/diaphragm stroke and seating to diagnose sticking actuators and out-of-calibration controllers.

sources.system: Senwell automatic safety relief valve (PRV/PSV) test bench
sources.title: Automatic Safety Relief Valve Test Bench for PRV Test | Senwell

sources.transferJustification: Same task content as the shop half of this task: pressure is varied into a fixtured valve and the valve's opening/reseating behaviour is judged against spec; the machine performs the pressure variation and the assessment.

sources.system: PLC-controlled safety valve test bench (Suncenter/gasboosterpump product line)

sources.transferJustification: Bench testing of spring-loaded and pilot valves by controlled pressure variation is the same operation the technician performs on regulators and safety/flow valves at a shop bench.

sources.system: Neometrix CNG Regulator Test Bench

sources.system: Spot with Spot Arm
sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Mobile plant robots with arms can turn valves and handles, but only semi-autonomously with an operator triggering each manipulation; autonomous arm use in missions is limited to door opening in beta.

tasks.label: Examine valves or mechanical control device parts for defects, dents, or loose attachments, and mark malfunctioning areas of defective units.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Valve repair shop bench teardown inspection: a used industrial valve (gate, globe, ball, or safety-relief) removed from service is disassembled; the technician examines body, seat, disc, stem, bonnet and fasteners for pitting, erosion, wire-drawing, dents, thread and gasket-face damage and loose/galled attachments, then marks the defective areas with a paint stick, scribe or tag so they can be lapped, machined or replaced. High mix of sizes, makes and service histories; parts are dirty, corroded and scaled.

Gas utility field call at a residential or small-commercial meter set: technician examines the meter, service regulator, relief vent, shutoff valves and swing-joint connections in place for dents, corrosion, cracked diaphragm covers, loose unions/bolts and leaks; red-tags or paint-marks the defective unit and writes it up for replacement. Outdoors or in a basement, weather and clutter as found, layout differs at each address.

Walk-down inspection inside an industrial or utility facility (refinery, chemical plant, power station, city gate/regulator station): instrument technician inspects installed control valves, actuators, positioners, regulators and relief valves for external damage, dents, corrosion, packing leaks and loose bolting/linkage, then hangs a deficiency tag or paint-marks the malfunctioning component and logs a work order. Fixed layout, controlled access, standard equipment.

Commercial building HVAC/BAS service: technician inspects pneumatic and electric control valves, damper actuators, linkages, thermostats and their mounting hardware in mechanical rooms, ceiling plenums and rooftop units for defects, dents, missing or loose attachments; marks or tags the defective device for replacement during the visit.

Shop or warehouse receiving / post-repair inspection: new, rebuilt or returned valves, regulators and meters are laid out on a bench or pallet and checked for shipping dents, damaged threads and flange faces, missing or loose fittings and nameplate/setting defects; rejects are marked and tagged before stocking, return-to-vendor or field issue.

tasks.label: Mount and install meters and other electric equipment such as time clocks, transformers, and circuit breakers, using electricians' hand tools.

instances.label: Residential/small-commercial electric meter set or exchange at a customer premises: cut the seal, remove the ring and old socket meter on an outdoor house wall, inspect socket jaws for burning, push in the new AMI meter, re-ring, seal, verify display/communication. Weather, dogs, shrubbery, varied socket heights and conditions.

Commercial/industrial metering install in a building electrical room or switchgear yard: anchor the meter enclosure/CT cabinet, install split-core or bar CTs on service conductors, land service-class conductors and CT/PT secondaries on a test switch, mount and program a CT-rated meter, verify phasing under load.

Install new circuit breakers in an existing panelboard, load center or MCC at a plant or institution: pull the dead front, snap or bolt the breaker to the bus or DIN rail, land and torque branch conductors, label, reinstall cover, test.

Populate and wire a control panel/enclosure backplate (in a shop or at the equipment): cut and fasten DIN rail and duct, snap on miniature breakers, control transformer, timers/time clocks, relays and terminal blocks, run and terminate control wiring, label and point-to-point test.

Mount and wire an auxiliary control device in the field — a lighting time clock/contactor cabinet, small control transformer or timer — onto a backplate or wall bracket in a mechanical/electrical room, connect conduit whips and terminate line and load conductors, then commission the schedule.

sources.system: Klippon Automated RailAssembler (with RailLaser / WMC software)
sources.title: Klippon® Automated RailAssembler – Rail mounting

tasks.label: Connect regulators to test stands, and turn screw adjustments until gauges indicate that inlet and outlet pressures meet specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gas utility meter/regulator shop: technician takes a rebuilt or new residential service regulator (Fisher/Sensus/Itron-type, 3/4"–1" threaded), screws it onto the bench test stand's union or quick-connect, applies rated inlet pressure, turns the spring adjustment screw until the outlet gauge reads spec (e.g., 7–11 in. w.c.), verifies lock-up and internal relief, then caps, seals and tags the unit.

Shop bench work on larger commercial/industrial or pilot-operated regulators (1"–2"+ threaded or flanged, heavy bodies, many models): technician rigs the unit onto the test stand with nipples/adapters and wrenches, pressurizes, adjusts pilot and main setpoint screws, checks droop and lock-up at rated inlet, documents results.

Repair shop bench testing of small precision regulators — cylinder/medical/welding gas regulators, instrument-air and propane appliance regulators — mixed brands and fitting types (CGA, compression, NPT), some oxygen-clean handling; connect to bench manifold, set delivery pressure to spec, check creep and seat leakage.

Batch setting at a manufacturer or regulator rebuild center: same model run repeatedly on a dedicated test stand with fixtures and preset instrumentation, high throughput, adjust to setpoint, record pass/fail and serial data.

Field setting/verification with a portable test stand or test manifold: district regulator station, vault, or customer meter set; technician connects gauges/test rig to the installed regulator outdoors in variable weather and access, adjusts the screw until inlet and outlet pressures meet the utility's spec, then locks and seals.

sources.system: SDC automated circuit board tuning machine (FANUC SR-20iA SCARA + Mecademic Meca500)
sources.title: Automated Circuit Board Tuning Machine for Medical Equipment
sources.claim: Purpose-built dual-robot cell that replaces a manual iterative 'turn a screw, read a measurement, adjust, repeat' tuning process: a Mecademic Meca500 turns the trim screw while instruments measure the device on an indexing table, with no manual intervention during the cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop trim of a device by turning an adjustment screw until an instrument reading meets specification. It is the same control loop as setting a regulator's outlet pressure with a spring screw, executed by a robot with in-fixture measurement feedback; only the measured quantity (RF response vs. pressure) differs.

sources.system: RND Automation Modular Assembly Platform hydraulic valve cell (Epson T3/G3 SCARA and C8 six-axis robots)
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robotic assembly-and-test cell for hydraulic pressure-control valves: an Epson SCARA threads the adjustment screw into the valve body with compliance to avoid cross-threading, springs are selected for the desired cracking pressure, and a robot loads finished units into a leak test fixture, producing a tested valve every 10 seconds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic threading of a pressure-adjustment screw into a pressure-regulating valve and robotic loading of the unit into a sealed pressure/leak test fixture — the same objects (small pressure regulating valves), the same threaded-fitting precision, and the same setpoint-by-spring-force physics as setting a regulator on a test stand.

sources.claim: Three-SCARA automated cell assembles pneumatic push-fit valve fittings and one robot performs a pressure decay (pressure-integrity) test on the completed part before sorting it into output trays; total cycle 7.8 seconds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic coupling of a small threaded/push-fit pneumatic component to a pressurized test circuit and execution of a gauge-based pressure test — the connect-and-pressure-verify half of connecting a regulator to a test stand, on comparable fittings and sealing tolerances.

sources.system: SCARA robot leak-test tending cell (industry example)

sources.claim: Robotic handling into leak/pressure test stations is routine production practice: a SCARA robot shuttles valves in and out of ... with three test fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine tending of a pressure/leak test stand with valves — establishes that loading valve-type workpieces into sealed test fixtures is a mature, autonomous capability in purpose-built cells.

tasks.label: Investigate instances of illegal tapping into service lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family residential premises visit on an AMI high-loss/tamper flag or a tip: technician works at an outdoor meter set/socket and service riser in a private yard (pets, occupants, weather, no fixturing), removes covers and seals, looks for jumper wires, hoses, unauthorized tees or a bypass around the meter, photographs findings and writes the theft case report.

Multi-family or small-commercial back-of-house investigation: cluttered basement meter room, alley meter bank or utility closet that differs building to building; technician traces which service feeds which unit, checks upstream piping/conductors for unauthorized connections behind covers and conduit, and documents evidence with the landlord or tenant present.

Buried or concealed service line: suspected tap upstream of the meter; technician locates the line (pipe locator/GPR), potholes or excavates in a yard, parkway or sidewalk, exposes the lateral in situ, confirms and photographs the illicit connection, and caps or flags it, working around other buried utilities and traffic.

Vacant, condemned or illicitly used property (self-reconnect after disconnection, suspected grow house) or a construction site with temporary service: field visit often with police or security escort; technician inspects the pedestal, meter socket or gas riser, documents a hard-wired bypass or unauthorized reconnect, and secures the service.

Distribution main / right-of-way investigation: suspected unauthorized tap into a gas or water main, or an unmetered hydrant/main connection serving a property; survey along the main in the street, vault or manhole entry, in-pipe or surface survey, cross-check against as-built records, and documentation for the utility's revenue-protection case.

sources.system: KITOV CORE / CORE+ robotic visual inspection system
sources.title: Systems - Kitov.ai - Smart AI based visual inspection
sources.claim: KITOV CORE/CORE+ are commercially sold robotic visual-inspection cells: a 6-axis arm plus rotating table autonomously plans and executes a full 2D/3D AI inspection of a fixtured part against a CAD or scanned reference, flagging defects and non-conforming features and issuing a report with imagery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly/defect verification of a fixtured workpiece against a reference model. Detecting an illegal tap on a meter set presented in a purpose-built cell is the same operation on comparable objects (metal fittings, conductors, valves) at the same visual scale, and yields the output the investigation needs: a flagged non-conforming connection with documentary imagery.

sources.system: KITOV.ai robotic 360-degree AI inspection (with CMM-Manager metrology)
sources.title: KITOV.ai Redefines Robotic Inspection with AI-Driven 360 Vision Metrology
sources.claim: KITOV's robotic AI inspection with 360-degree vision metrology is in deployment at aerospace, medical and precision manufacturers, i.e. it operates at production quality in industrial inspection cells rather than only in demos.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the KITOV CORE item: robot-guided AI inspection that detects, classifies and measures deviations from a reference configuration on a presented part, which is what identifying an added, unauthorized connection requires.

sources.system: Zivid robot-mounted industrial 3D cameras in automotive inspection cells (e.g. CMES robot-mounted solution)
sources.title: 3D Vision for Automotive: What Actually Matters in Camera Selection
sources.claim: Robot-mounted 3D vision inspection is routine in automotive production cells on large fixtured assemblies (car bodies), covering presence verification of fasteners, weld-seam geometry and panel fit, showing that reference-based robotic inspection scales beyond bench-size parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic presence/conformance inspection of a large fixtured assembly. A meter set or service riser presented in a cell is of comparable size and material mix, so demonstrated ability to verify what is and is not attached to an assembly carries over to spotting an unauthorized tee, hose or jumper.

sources.system: SOLO autonomous pipeline inspection robot

sources.claim: RedZone's SOLO is a commercially deployed sewer-inspection robot that, once launched by a crew at a manhole, autonomously traverses a live main capturing 360-degree video of the pipe and every connection; interpretation and coding of the footage is done afterwards off-site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-pipe survey of a municipal main that images every service connection, the method used to find unauthorized/illicit connections. Cited only to test the main-line instance; it does not cover locating the suspect site, gaining access, or reaching an investigative conclusion, which stay with the human crew.

tasks.label: Trace and tag meters or house lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family residential service call: technician follows the house line from the gas meter/service riser through basement, crawlspace or utility closet to appliances or the interior shutoff, confirms it is the correct customer's piping, and wires/affixes an identification or condition tag at the meter and on the line. Clutter, tight access, painted-over or shared piping, varies house to house.

Multi-unit building meter bank (basement or exterior wall bank of 4-24 gas or water meters): technician traces each riser/house line to the apartment it serves (valving off, appliance checks, following pipe runs through joist bays), then attaches numbered unit-ID tags to each meter and its house line. Cramped, poorly lit, non-standard layouts.

Commercial or institutional building / process plant: trace gas, steam, water or air lines from meters and regulators through mechanical rooms and pipe racks, then hang engraved or printed asset/valve tags on meters, regulators and isolation valves as part of a tagging or shutdown program. Premises controlled by the facility owner, standard equipment, escorted access.

Outdoor field work at a customer meter set, pad-mounted regulator station or curbside service: verify which service line and meter serve the address, then affix condition tags (red tag / out-of-service / tested-and-locked), seals or barcode tags to the meter and outlet piping, in weather, with vegetation, vehicles and pets present.

Utility meter shop / staging warehouse: incoming, refurbished or new meters are moved through test and inspection, then identified by serial/barcode and tagged, sealed or marked (test-date tag, certification seal, asset barcode) before being staged for field deployment.

sources.system: Spot (with gas-detection payload, Orbit mission software)
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot runs autonomous inspection missions in industrial gas facilities, navigating routes and collecting sensor/gauge readings, but the deployed capability is sensing and reading, not tracing pipe routing or affixing physical identification tags.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility inspection rounds in a gas plant. It substantiates autonomous navigation and instrument reading in an E2 industrial facility, but shows no capability to trace line routing or hang/wire a tag, so it does not carry over to completing 'trace and tag'.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic application of a printed identification label to a product on a line. Transfers to tagging a meter that a purpose-built line presents in a known position with its identity already resolved by barcode; same object scale and placement precision.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of identification labels to differing surfaces on a conveyed item. Comparable to affixing an ID tag to a meter body presented at a fixtured station; same payload class and placement tolerance.

tasks.label: Repair electric meters and components, such as transformers and relays, and replace metering devices, dial glasses, and faulty or incorrect wiring, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine field exchange of a self-contained (socket) watthour meter at a residence or small business: cut the seal, remove the locking ring with hand tools, pull the old meter from the socket jaws, plug in the replacement, refit ring and seal, confirm display/load. Outdoors on a house wall or in a meter enclosure, varying mounting heights, weather, pets, vegetation and customers present.

Field trouble/repair call at a customer premise: burned or corroded meter socket jaws, cracked dial glass/cover, damaged or incorrectly wired meter base found on inspection or after a no-power call. Technician de-energizes or bypasses, diagnoses, replaces jaws/cover/wiring with hand tools, re-terminates service conductors, reinstalls and re-seals.

Transformer-rated (CT/PT) metering at a commercial or industrial customer's electrical room: replace failed instrument transformers, test switches or meter sockets, and correct faulty or incorrect metering wiring (wrong phase, reversed CT polarity) found by testing; verify with a phasing/test set before re-sealing.

Utility substation or control-house metering work: repair or replace metering relays, transducers and instrument transformers, land and correct panel wiring per drawings, then functionally test the metering/relay circuit.

Meter shop bench work: meters returned from the field are tested on the test board, then diagnosed and repaired — registers, internal wiring, boards or mechanisms replaced — reassembled, re-calibrated/re-tested and sealed. Mixed meter makes and models, faults not known in advance.

Meter shop batch refurbishment of external parts on a single standard meter type: replace cracked dial glasses/covers and terminal covers on a run of returned meters staged on a bench, then re-test and re-seal for reissue.

tasks.label: Replace defective parts, such as bellows, range springs, and toggle switches, and reassemble units according to blueprints, using cam presses and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility meter/regulator shop: bench rebuild of standardized domestic and commercial gas pressure regulators returned from the field — split the spring case, replace diaphragm/bellows assembly, range spring, valve disc, orifice and O-rings, reassemble to the manufacturer's exploded drawing with correct torque, then set spring range and bench leak/lock-up test. Cores arrive dirty, oily, sometimes with corroded or seized fasteners.

Meter/instrument shop refurbishment of gas and water meters and metering instruments — replace index/register, gaskets, diaphragms, contacts and toggle/limit switches, press-fit bushings, pins and registers with a cam or arbor press, reassemble per blueprint and run a calibration/accuracy and leak test. High volume, a few standard models.

Valve repair shop or plant maintenance shop rebuild of industrial control valves and actuators of many makes and sizes — strip actuator, replace bellows seals, range/actuator springs, packing, seat rings, positioner and limit/toggle switches, reassemble to the drawing, torque bonnet bolting in sequence, stroke and bench-test. Heavy, dirty parts; each job differs.

Field replacement of defective parts on gas regulators, meter sets, relief and flow-control valves at customer premises, curbside sets, meter pits, and district regulator stations — isolate and purge, work in confined or awkward positions in weather, swap springs, pilots, diaphragms or switches, reassemble and leak-test before restoring service.

In-place repair of pneumatic and electronic controllers, thermostats and transmitters in building mechanical rooms and process areas — open the case on a wall or panel, replace bellows, range spring, toggle switch or relay, land wiring on terminals, reassemble the housing per the wiring/blueprint and recalibrate to setpoint.

sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY

Transfer: the objects (spring-loaded pressure valve bodies, range springs selected to a set pressure, O-rings, threaded parts), the precision (thread engagement, torque, leak-tightness) and the purpose-built fixtured environment match the 'reassemble units according to blueprints, using cam presses and hand tools' half of this task.

tasks.label: Measure tolerances of assembled and salvageable parts for conformance to standards or specifications, using gauges, micrometers, and calipers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility meter/regulator shop bench: after teardown and cleaning of a gas regulator, gas meter or water meter, the technician measures a handful of small components (valve stem and shaft diameters, orifice size, spring free length, seat/disc wear, diaphragm plate thickness) with dial calipers, micrometers and feeler gauges against shop standards, deciding reuse vs. scrap. Parts are used, sometimes pitted or scored; mix of models is high, volume per model low.

Industrial valve / pressure-relief valve repair shop: after disassembly, technician measures trim and body features — nozzle bore, seat contact width, disc and stem diameter/straightness, guide clearance, spring free height and squareness — using micrometers, bore gauges, calipers, surface plate and dial indicator, comparing to manufacturer and API/ASME specs to decide machining, salvage or replacement. Parts range from small trim pieces to heavy bodies.

Post-repair verification on the bench: after reassembly of a regulator, meter or valve, the technician measures the assembled unit's critical dimensions — stem travel/lift, spring compression height, set gap and clearances with feeler gauges and dial indicators — to confirm the build conforms before functional test and tagging.

Field work at a customer site, regulator station, plant or meter vault: technician measures a component in situ or a part removed on site (orifice size, spring, stem clearance, seat gap) with pocket calipers, small micrometers and feeler gauges under variable light, weather and access conditions to decide whether it meets spec or must be replaced.

Batch gauging of like parts in the shop: measuring a lot of refurbished or incoming replacement components (bushings, orifice plates, pins, gaskets, springs) of one model against go/no-go gauges, calipers and micrometers, recording results for the repair record — repetitive, uniform, higher volume work.

tasks.label: Clean internal compartments and moving parts, using rags and cleaning compounds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility meter/regulator shop bench work: technician has dismantled residential/commercial gas meters, service regulators or electric meter mechanisms; wipes and degreases housings, internal compartments, gear trains, index/register parts and linkages with rags, brushes and cleaning compound (solvent or aqueous) before reassembly, calibration and test.

Valve/instrument repair shop or plant maintenance shop: a control valve, relief valve or pressure regulator has been pulled and disassembled on a bench; body cavity, seat, plug, cage, stem, bushings and springs are wiped and scrubbed free of grease, hydrocarbon residue, scale and particulate with rags, brushes and cleaning compounds before inspection and reassembly.

Field service call at a residential or small commercial premises: technician opens a meter set, regulator, or gas control at an outdoor meter riser, in a basement or a meter closet, and wipes out dirt, spider webs, moisture, oil carryover and dust from the internal compartment and moving parts in place, with rags and spray cleaner, in whatever weather and clearance the site offers.

In-place cleaning at an industrial site, gate station, or pipeline regulator station: actuator housing, spring case, positioner interior, pilot, gearbox and linkage of a regulator or control valve are opened on the pipe and wiped free of oil, pipeline liquids, dust and rust with rags and solvent, often outdoors, at height or in congested piping.

Commercial building HVAC/controls service: technician cleans thermostats, damper actuators and linkages, control valve stems and packing areas, and the interior of control enclosures in mechanical rooms, rooftop units or above ceilings, wiping dust, grease and corrosion with rags and cleaning compounds.

tasks.label: Dismantle meters, and replace or adjust defective parts such as cases, shafts, gears, disks, and recording mechanisms, using soldering irons and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility/contractor meter shop: bench overhaul of a residential diaphragm gas meter returned from the field. Worker breaks the case seal, unbolts and separates the case (often painted, corroded, gas-soiled), inspects internals, diagnoses the fault, replaces valves, diaphragms, tangent/crank linkage or the index (recording) mechanism, reassembles with new gaskets, leak-tests and proves the meter for accuracy. Mixed makes, models and vintages arrive in the same batch.

Water utility meter shop: repair of returned positive-displacement or multi-jet water meters. Worker removes the register head retaining ring/seal, dismantles the measuring chamber, identifies worn discs, gears, shafts or a fogged/failed register, replaces the defective parts and gaskets, reassembles, then tests on a calibration bench for registration accuracy. Meters are dirty, scaled and sometimes frozen from field service.

Electric meter shop / test board: repair of watthour meters. Worker removes the cover and seal, cleans, replaces or adjusts registers, bearings/magnetic suspensions, contacts, terminal hardware or a failed electronic register board, resolders leads or terminals with a soldering iron, reassembles, reseals and retests the meter on the test board before return to stock.

On-site repair at a customer premises: gas, water or electric meter in a house basement, crawl space, curbside meter pit, alley set or business back room. Worker works in confined, variable, often wet or dark access, partially dismantles the meter or metering assembly on the spot to swap an index/register head, ERT/AMR module, or adjust a sticking recording mechanism with hand tools, then reseals and verifies operation.

Industrial/commercial metering equipment overhaul in a plant or specialty shop: large rotary, turbine or industrial flow meter, chart recorder, or meter-set instrumentation. Worker dismantles heavy housings, replaces shafts, gears, bearings, impellers and recording/charting mechanisms, adjusts linkages and calibrates against a prover; work may involve heavy lifting and disassembly of a piped-in unit.

tasks.label: Disconnect or remove defective or unauthorized meters, using hand tools.

instances.label: Residential electric meter: technician drives to a house, cuts the utility seal, removes the sealing ring with a nut driver/screwdriver, and pulls a defective (burned, stopped, or failed-test) socket meter from an outdoor meter base on the side of the dwelling, then installs a replacement or blank cover and re-seals. Conditions vary: overgrown shrubs, locked gates, dogs, weather, energized 240 V service.

Residential gas meter: technician shuts the service valve at an outdoor set or basement riser, uses pipe wrenches to break the union/swivel nuts on a defective diaphragm meter, removes it, caps or plugs the piping (or installs a spacer/replacement), and leak-checks. Tight meter sets, corroded fittings, cramped basements and crawl spaces.

Water meter: technician opens a curb/vault pit or works in a basement setter, shuts the inlet/outlet valves, unscrews couplings or unbolts flange bolts on a defective or unauthorized meter, removes it, and installs a spacer or new meter. Muddy or flooded pits, corroded nuts, confined space.

Unauthorized/tampered installation: revenue-protection removal of a meter that has been bypassed, jumpered, drilled, glued, or self-reconnected. Technician documents evidence, deals with damaged sockets, cut seals, non-standard hardware and sometimes a hostile occupant, removes the meter and locks or blanks the connection.

Commercial/industrial premises: removal of a defective meter from a multi-meter board in a building meter room, utility vault, or switchgear room — de-energize/tag, unscrew terminal or CT-metering wiring, unbolt and remove the meter, install replacement or blank. tasks.label: Attach air hoses to meter inlets, plug outlets, and observe gauges for pressure losses to test internal seams for leaks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility/contractor gas meter shop, high-volume leak test of reconditioned residential diaphragm meters (175-250 class): tech sets the meter on the test manifold/prover connection, air hose on the inlet, cap or plug the outlet, pressurize to a few psi/inches w.c., watch the gauge or manometer for pressure loss over the timed interval, mark pass/fail and record.

Same shop, meters just reassembled after repair (new diaphragms, valve seats, case gaskets, resealed case seams): pressure-test each unit, flag any that lose pressure and route them back to the repair bench, retest reworked units until they hold; output is an accepted leak-tight meter with a recorded test result.

Shop bay test of large commercial/industrial meters (rotary, turbine, large diaphragm, 2"-8" flanged), heavy units moved by hoist, requiring size-specific adapters/blind flanges on inlet and outlet, tested at rated pressure while the gauge is observed for decay.

Shop bench pressure/leak test of repaired gas regulators, relief valves and safety/flow valves: air hose to the inlet, outlet plugged, body and seat checked by watching gauge decay over a set interval before the unit is released to stock.

Field: after a residential meter change-out or new meter set, the tech attaches an air hose/test gauge at the meter set, plugs or caps the outlet and closes valves, pressurizes the set and house line, and watches the gauge for the required hold period; outdoor side yard, basement, or curb meter pit, with weather, dirt, pets and the customer present.

Field: commercial building meter room or fenced regulator/meter station; plugs and test gauges fitted to installed meter-set piping, air applied and gauges observed for loss before the set is gassed up.

tasks.label: Repair leaks in valve seats or bellows of automotive heater thermostats, using soft solder, flux, and acetylene torches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench repair in a shop: a standard, familiar model of automotive heater thermostat / heater control valve leaks at its known soldered seam (bellows-to-cap or bellows-to-body joint). Worker clamps it, cleans and fluxes the joint, re-flows soft solder with a small torch, then verifies in a hot-water or pressure leak test.

Bench repair of a leak at the valve-seat-to-body soldered joint on a standard model: clean the joint, flux, soft-solder with torch while keeping the seat sealing face clear of solder, reassemble and pressure-test the seal.

Leak is a pinhole or crack in the bellows convolutions themselves, not at a standard joint. Worker must pressurize and immerse the used, oxidized unit to find the exact bubble source, clean corrosion locally, then tin/solder very thin metal with the torch without collapsing the bellows or destroying its actuation travel; re-test for both seal and correct opening temperature.

Leak past a pitted or eroded valve seat: disassemble the valve body, clean/reface or build up the seat with solder, refit the poppet, adjust and pressure-test for a tight shutoff; judge whether the seat can be saved.

Job spans the vehicle: drain coolant, remove the thermostat or heater control valve from the engine bay in a service bay, take it to the bench for soldering repair, reinstall, refill and bleed the system, and check for leaks with the engine running.

Legacy, obsolete or heavily corroded unit (vintage or non-standard heater thermostat): no fixture exists, the construction is unfamiliar, the worker improvises clamping, decides repair-versus-scrap, and may fabricate or re-form a part before soldering and testing.

sources.transferJustification: Negative/limiting evidence: even where leak detection on soldered joints is fully automated, the corrective soldering repair is still handed to people, indicating no fielded system performs defect-located solder repair.

tasks.label: Splice and connect cables from meters or current transformers to pull boxes or switchboards, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New CT-metered service in a commercial/industrial building: technician pulls CT secondary leads from the current-transformer cabinet through existing conduit to the meter/test-switch enclosure, strips and ferrules #10-#12 conductors, splices where needed, lands them on the test switch and meter socket terminals in the switchboard section, and torques screws — done in the building's electrical room beside energized gear, in a layout that differs from site to site.

Field service/repair call: a failed CT or burned/corroded conductors in an outdoor pull box, meter pedestal, or handhole must be diagnosed, cut back, re-stripped, re-spliced (compression connector or split-bolt, taped/heat-shrunk) and reconnected to the meter; cramped, wet or dirty enclosure, mixed vintages of hardware, weather, work near live conductors.

Self-contained meter installation on a home or small commercial building: land heavy service-entrance conductors (2 AWG–4/0 Al/Cu) in the meter socket and adjacent pull box lugs, dress and torque the lugs, reconnect the load-side conductors; exterior wall or basement, varied socket types and cable conditions.

Utility meter-shop or prefab-bench work: building and rewiring metering panels and CT test-switch harnesses — cutting, stripping, ferruling and landing secondary wiring on test switches, terminal blocks and meter bases at a bench inside the shop, then continuity-testing the assembly.

Substation or large-customer metering station: terminate CT/PT secondary cables into junction boxes and route them to the metering/relay panel in the control house, land conductors on shorting terminal blocks and test switches, and verify polarity/continuity; fenced utility yard and control building.

sources.system: Averex robotic wiring centre
sources.title: Robotic wiring centre will save up to 15 hours per panel - Drives&Controls
sources.claim: The Kiesling (Rittal group) Averex robotic wiring centre automatically cuts, strips and ferrule-crimps wires, routes them through cable ducts and attaches them to terminal blocks, contactors and breakers on a fixtured switchgear mounting plate in a factory cell, with torque-controlled screwing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory wiring of switchgear/control panels. Same objects (insulated conductors, ferrules, terminal blocks, screw terminations inside a switchboard-type enclosure) and the same precision as landing meter/CT secondary leads on a test switch or switchboard terminal, with the panel presented fixtured to the machine.

sources.system: Averex robotic wiring system
sources.title: New acquisition for Rittal - Electrical Engineering Magazine
sources.claim: The Averex system checks the assembled mounting plate and then wires the components independently and automatically from EPLAN wiring data, changing wire colour and cross-section as required.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomy (not teleoperation) of the panel-wiring cell whose task — connecting conductors to terminals inside switchgear — is the factory analogue of connecting meter/CT cables to switchboard terminals.

sources.system: Averex portal robot
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems | SpringerLink
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed book chapter on automated control-cabinet wiring describes Averex as an existing fully automated portal-robot wiring solution covering cutting, crimping, connecting and routing wires inside the cabinet.
sources.transferJustification: Recent confirmation that automated in-cabinet wire connection is state of the art in purpose-built cells; the objects (cabinet-mounted terminals, ferruled conductors) match the meter/CT-to-switchboard terminations in this task.

sources.system: Komax CrX-44HD automatic crimping machine
sources.title: Automatic Crimping | Komax
sources.claim: Komax's CrX-44HD is a fully automatic crimping machine that processes large-gauge copper and aluminium conductors up to 95 mm² (000 ...), i.e. service-entrance sized cable, terminating them automatically in a machine cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated termination of heavy conductors. Meter-socket and pull-box work uses the same conductor sizes (2 AWG–4/0) and the same operation — cutting, stripping and crimping/lugging — performed here automatically with the cable presented to the machine.

sources.system: WIRES robotic switchgear cabling cell
sources.developer: University of Bologna / WIRES project consortium
sources.title: Robotic Wires Manipulation for Switchgear Cabling and Wiring Harness Manufacturing
sources.claim: The WIRES experiment demonstrated a robotic manipulator with a sensorised gripper that detects, grasps and connects wires for switchgear cabling, using multi-sensor perception and machine learning rather than teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotised cabling of switchgear in an industrial cell — same deformable insulated conductors and same terminal-connection operation as connecting meter/CT leads into a switchboard, with the switchgear fixtured.

sources.system: Cable Splicing Machine (v3)
sources.title: Con Edison and ULC Technologies Unveil Cable Splicing Machine – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Cable Splicing Machine, field-trialled with Con Edison, performs autonomous cable-end preparation (stripping cable layers, shorting, cutting) on medium-voltage feeder cables in underground vaults, but crews must lower it in, insert the cable and finish the splice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: utility cable splicing in the field. It shows automated cable-end preparation only when a human fixtures the cable into the machine; the splice itself is still made by human splicers, so it does not substantiate whole-instance field completion.
