tasks.label: Clean plant growth, scale, paint, soil, or rust from meter housings, using wire brushes, scrapers, buffers, sandblasters, or cleaning compounds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field service call at a residence or small commercial building: technician wire-brushes and scrapes flaking paint, rust and dirt off an outdoor gas meter case, regulator housing and set piping before repainting/recoating; live gas piping, shrubbery, uneven ground, weather, customer property.

Below-grade water meter pit/box at a curb or in a yard: technician lifts the lid, bails water, scrapes mud and silt, pulls grass/roots and plant growth off the meter housing and register lid, and wipes with cleaning compound so the housing can be read, tested or changed out.

Electric meter socket/enclosure at a home or business: technician brushes corrosion, dirt, insect nests and paint overspray from the meter housing, base and cover before reinstalling or resealing the meter.

Utility or contractor meter shop bench: meters removed from service arrive in carts/crates; technician degreases, wire-wheel buffs and/or sandblasts the meter bodies and cases to strip old paint, scale and rust before proving, testing and repainting.

Municipal pump/regulator station or process plant: technician chips and brushes scale, corrosion and old coating from control valve bodies, regulator and flow-meter housings using needle scalers, wire brushes and cleaning compounds, sometimes portable blasting, in place amid piping and equipment.

sources.system: Blastman B16XS robotic blast room
sources.title: BLAST CLEANING METALWORKING MACHINERY - Blastman Robotics Ltd
sources.claim: Blastman B16XS wall-type blasting robots run a fully automated pass-through blast chamber that strips paint, rust and scale from varied metal workpieces delivered by overhead conveyor, working in automatic mode from pre-created programs at a metalworking machinery factory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive blast cleaning of metal workpieces. Meter and valve housings are the same class of coated/rusted metal castings and fabrications; removing paint, rust and scale by blasting is the same operation the meter technician performs by hand.

sources.system: Guyson RB/RXS rotary-table robotic blast systems
sources.title: Rotary Table Robotic Blast System
sources.claim: Guyson supplies commercial robotic blast cells in which a six-axis robot manipulates blast nozzles inside an enclosed cabinet, with machine-tending robots loading and unloading parts and barcode part recognition selecting the cleaning program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated blast cleaning/surface preparation of production parts including automated part presentation; shows the shop cleaning cycle (load, clean, unload) runs without a human directing each step once parts are presented to the machine.

sources.system: Rosler RDT / RWK shot blast machines
sources.title: Forge & Foundry, Part 8 - Frequently Used Shot Blasting Machines for Sand Castings
sources.claim: Rosler shot-blasting machines are standard commercial equipment for cleaning exactly the workpiece class at issue - valve bodies, pump housings and fire hydrants - with parts placed on rotary tables or in chambers and blasted automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated blast cleaning of valve bodies and pump housings. Gas/water meter cases and regulator housings are the same kind of cast or fabricated fluid-device housing, cleaned of scale, soil and old paint by the same process.

sources.system: CleanTech Titan FX robotic laser cleaning workcell
sources.title: How Laser Cleaning Robotic Workcells Pick up the Pace on the Shopfloor
sources.claim: Laser Photonics CleanTech robotic laser workcells perform automated rust removal, paint stripping and surface conditioning on components inside an enclosed cell, a commercially sold alternative to hand wire-brushing and blasting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal of rust and coatings from metal components in a robot cell - the same output (bare, sound metal housing surface) the meter technician produces with brushes, scrapers or a sandblaster.

sources.system: FerRobotics ACF-K Active Contact Flange kits (brushing/sanding/paint stripping)
sources.title: ACF-K ACTIVE CONTACT FLANGE KIT (datasheet)
sources.claim: FerRobotics force-controlled robot end effectors are commercially sold for robotic brushing, cleaning and paint stripping with constant contact force on varied metal geometries - the powered wire-brush/buffer step of housing cleanup performed by a robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic brushing/paint stripping with active force control on metal parts; equivalent to the wire brush and buffer work called for on meter housings, provided the housing is presented to the robot.

sources.system: Gas meter repair and refurbishment line (human process reference)
sources.title: Gas Meter Repair and Calibration | Utilities and Industries
sources.claim: Context on the accepted human process: gas meter overhaul in a meter shop cleans the meter body and then blasts and sands it before painting, confirming that the cleaned workpiece is a removable housing routinely processed by blasting equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only to establish that meter housing cleaning is normally performed by blasting/sanding a removable meter body, the workpiece that robotic blast and laser cells handle.

tasks.label: Connect hoses from provers to meter inlets and outlets, and raise prover bells until prover gauges register zero.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility/contractor meter shop, high-volume routine proving of residential diaphragm gas meters: worker sets a meter on the bell-prover bench, attaches the prover's flexible hoses/quick-connect swivels to the meter inlet and outlet, opens the shutoffs, and raises the bell until the prover gauge/scale reads zero before running the check and open-flow proofs. Standard G1.6-G4 meter bodies, standard 1-inch/20-light connections, climate-controlled shop, dozens of meters per shift.

Same meter shop, larger commercial/industrial units (large diaphragm, rotary or turbine meters) proved on a large bell prover or a shop transfer prover: heavier meters set with a lift assist, larger threaded or flanged inlet/outlet hookups and hose adapters, longer settling and bell-zeroing before each proof run.

Mixed batches of field-returned meters of several makes, models and connection sizes arriving on the bench; the worker selects the right hose/adapter set for each, hooks it up, zeroes the bell, and re-does the hookup (re-seat swivel, replace gasket, re-tighten) when the prover's leak/differential check fails before the proof is accepted.

Awkward units: meters returned with corroded, cross-threaded, dented or nonstandard inlet/outlet connections, or fitted with unusual index/riser hardware, where the worker improvises an adapter stack or dresses the threads to get a leak-tight prover hookup and a valid zeroed bell.

Field proving at a customer site with a portable/transfer prover on a truck: worker isolates the meter set at a commercial or industrial service (outdoor meter set, vault, or basement), connects prover hoses to the meter's inlet and outlet test connections in place, and zeroes the prover before proving; weather, tight space, live gas piping.

sources.system: inotech gas meter test rigs (low-pressure), inotech Meter Calibration Systems GmbH
sources.developer: inotech Meter Calibration Systems GmbH (Bietigheim, Germany)
sources.title: Gas Meter Test Rigs (low-pressure) - inotech
sources.claim: Commercial low-pressure gas meter test rigs for diaphragm, rotary, turbine and ultrasonic meters are offered with automatic clamping equipment that itself provides the inlet and outlet connection sections to the meter under test - i.e. the machine makes the prover-to-meter inlet/outlet connection - and serial rigs with automatic tensioning run up to 24 test places.

sources.system: inotech serial gas meter test rigs
sources.title: Gas Meter Test Rigs (low-pressure) - inotech
sources.claim: The same vendor supplies serial gas-meter test rigs with automatic tensioning (clamping) for up to 24 test positions, i.e. multi-position purpose-built calibration benches where meter hookup is machine-actuated.

sources.system: Nagman gas meter calibration test bench (bell prover / sonic nozzle standard)
sources.title: Gas Meter Calibration System | Nagman Flow & Level
sources.claim: Commercial gas flow meter calibration benches built around a bell prover raise and lower the bell under machine control and switch the gas-output valve automatically, which is the automated equivalent of raising the prover bell to the zero mark before a proof.

sources.system: Gas Meter Test Bench (bell prover / sonic nozzle), distributed by Dutco Tennant
sources.title: Best and reliable gas Meter Test Bench l Dutco Tennant LLC
sources.claim: A distributor-listed domestic gas meter test bench with bell-prover standard likewise moves the bell automatically and switches the gas-output valve automatically, and is built in modules of 1x6 to 4x6 clamping points for the meters under test.

sources.system: EP GMC gas meter calibration test bench
sources.title: Calibration test bench for gas meters - EP
sources.claim: The GMC domestic gas meter calibration bench holds 1x6 to 4x6 clamping points, adapts and runs in up to twelve meters in parallel, and performs the leak tests on the hookups automatically - so verifying that the prover-to-meter connections are tight is a machine function on the bench.

sources.system: NI CompactRIO high-precision calibration and prover system (Cyth Systems integration)
sources.developer: Cyth Systems / National Instruments, for an industrial gas meter manufacturer
sources.title: Hardware-Timed Automation Accelerates Gas Meter Testing
sources.claim: A US industrial gas meter manufacturer automated its end-of-line piston-prover meter testing with an NI CompactRIO based system that controls valves and flow and validates meter accuracy to US weights-and-measures standards, showing machine-controlled prover operation accepted for production-grade meter accuracy work in the United States.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line prover testing of gas meters. Same objects (gas meters), same required metrological precision and same prover-sequence control (valves, flow, zeroing) as bell proving in a meter shop; it substantiates that the proving cycle itself runs under machine control.

sources.system: inotech Model AC automatic calibration test bench for cold water meters (DN50-DN300)
sources.title: Water Meter Test Rig - inotech
sources.claim: Industrial water-meter test rigs use a pneumatic closing system to clamp meters into the test rack, making the sealed inlet/outlet connections to the meters under test by machine actuation rather than by hand-threading each hose.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connecting a utility meter's inlet and outlet to a prover/test rig for an accuracy test. Comparable objects (DN50-DN300 utility meters), comparable leak-tight sealing precision, same purpose-built bench setting; supports that machine-actuated inlet/outlet hookup of meters is routine commercial practice.

sources.system: Can-Tronics BELL prover automatic gas meter proving system
sources.developer: Can-Tronics Gas Measurement and Control Inc. (Hamilton, Ontario)
sources.title: Bell Prover - Automatic Gas Meter Proving System
sources.claim: Bell provers with computer-controlled test stands are standard equipment for proving diaphragm and ultrasonic gas meters in North American meter shops, with the whole test sequence and data handling run by the prover's computer while the operator is guided step by step.

roles.description: Install or repair heating, central air conditioning, HVAC, or refrigeration systems, including oil burners, hot-air furnaces, and heating stoves.

tasks.label: Discuss heating or cooling system malfunctions with users to isolate problems or to verify that repairs corrected malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Test electrical circuits or components for continuity, using electrical test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential no-heat/no-cool service call: technician at a private house de-energizes the furnace or condensing unit, opens the control compartment in a cramped basement, attic, closet or side yard, and uses a multimeter/continuity tester on the limit switch, rollout switch, fuse, transformer secondary, contactor coil, run capacitor, igniter and compressor/blower motor windings to isolate the open component.

Light-commercial service on a packaged rooftop unit or air handler at an office, school or retail store: technician works on the roof or in a mechanical room owned by the building, pulls the control panel cover, and checks continuity of contactors, control-board fuses, safety switches, heat-strip elements and unit wiring between terminal strips.

New installation / commissioning check at a residential or light-commercial job site (often still under construction): before energizing, technician ohms out low-voltage thermostat wire runs, checks continuity/shorts of control harnesses between condenser, air handler and thermostat, and verifies ground continuity of the newly landed circuit.

Commercial refrigeration call at a supermarket, restaurant or convenience store: technician checks continuity of defrost heaters, door and drain-line heaters, defrost termination switches, solenoid valve coils and evaporator fan motor windings in a walk-in cooler or on a rack in the machine room.

Bench/truck testing of a removed component: technician places a suspect motor, compressor, gas valve, control board, pressure switch or capacitor on the shop bench and ohms it out (winding-to-winding, winding-to-ground, coil continuity) to confirm failure before ordering or installing a replacement.

sources.system: OMRON TM Series cobot PCB test cell (Absolute Robotics / Hanover Displays)
sources.title: Automated Circuit Board Testing with Cobots | Case Study
sources.claim: A deployed cobot cell (OMRON TM-series collaborative robots with NX controller, integrated by Absolute Robotics at Hanover Displays) automates the entire electrical test of circuit boards, including physically connecting test points, running the electrical checks and sorting pass/fail ..., running unsupervised.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line electrical test of electronic assemblies. The robot physically places/connects test probes on specified test points and returns a pass/fail electrical verdict — the same act an HVAC tech performs when ohmimg out a control board or component — with the workpiece fixtured and presented, i.e. an E1 cell.

sources.system: TAKAYA flying probe tester (APT series)
sources.date: 2026-07 (page retrieved; product line commercial for years)
sources.title: OPTION - PRODUCTS - TAKAYA Flying Probe Tester
sources.claim: Takaya flying-probe testers move probes under machine control to perform in-circuit electrical tests and run fully automatically when integrated inline with loader/unloader, i.e. unattended contact probing of specified test points.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtureless in-circuit test. The machine autonomously positions physical probes onto conductive test points and measures opens/shorts and resistance — the electrical measurement an HVAC technician makes with meter leads — in a purpose-built test station.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers (4060 family)
sources.title: Flying Probe Tester for electronic boards PCB | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA flying probers contact pins directly with moving probes to perform complete continuity tests without application-specific fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated continuity testing of boards/connectors. Explicitly the same measurement (continuity between conductive points) performed by a machine that positions its own probes, in a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.system: Marposs E.D.C. AMT320/W motor test systems
sources.title: End-Of-Line Testing Of Electric Motors | Marposs / Electrical Testing of E-Motors
sources.claim: Automatic in-line and end-of-line electrical test benches for electric motors check winding resistances and insulation condition on stators and complete motors in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated winding-resistance/insulation testing of motors. HVAC technicians ohm compressor and blower motor windings (winding-to-winding and winding-to-ground) for continuity; the automated station makes the same measurements on the same class of object when the motor is fixtured at the test bench.

sources.system: Flying probe / bed-of-nails harness test tables
sources.developer: various harness test equipment makers (as described by Cloom Tech)
sources.title: Wire Harness Testing Methods: Best Practices & Quality Guide
sources.claim: Automated wire-harness test practice uses flying-probe or bed-of-nails test tables to check continuity across thousands of test points in harness manufacturing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: harness continuity verification. The commissioning check an HVAC installer performs on thermostat/control wiring is a point-to-point continuity and short test of a cable set; automated harness testers perform exactly this when the harness is presented on the test fixture.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot substation inspection (Avangrid / United Illuminating)
sources.title: Utility to Utilize Mobile Robot, Artificial Intelligence for Substation Inspections | American Public Power Association
sources.claim: Field/facility inspection robots deployed on electrical infrastructure perform visual and thermal inspection only; no contact probing of terminals with test leads is part of the deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to show the limit of in-situ robotic electrical inspection in structured facilities: sensing at a distance, not opening panels and placing meter leads on terminals, so it does not substantiate E2 for this task.

tasks.label: Repair or replace defective equipment, components, or wiring.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential no-heat/no-cool service call at a private home: technician diagnoses with meters, then replaces a failed run capacitor, contactor, blower or condenser fan motor, igniter, inducer, gas valve or control board, or repairs rodent-chewed/burnt line- and low-voltage wiring. Work occurs in a furnace closet, attic, crawlspace, basement or on an outdoor condenser pad; access is cramped, layouts and equipment brands differ house to house, power must be locked out and the unit test-run afterward.

Light-commercial rooftop packaged unit or split system at a strip mall, restaurant or small office: technician climbs to the roof with parts, opens the unit, and replaces a scroll compressor, condenser fan motor, belt/bearing, contactor, transformer or VFD, or repairs chafed/burnt power wiring; includes refrigerant recovery, brazing, evacuation and recharge. Weather-exposed, ladder or hatch access, roof curbs and debris, layout differs site to site.

Supermarket or food-service commercial refrigeration: replace evaporator fan motors, defrost heaters, expansion valves, solenoid coils, rack compressors, or repair defective wiring and terminal blocks in walk-in coolers, reach-in cases and the store's refrigeration machine room, working around stocked product and customers during store hours.

Large-building mechanical room / central plant (hospital, campus, high-rise): replace pump motors and seals, chiller or AHU fan motors, valve actuators, VFDs, starters, contactors and burnt control wiring on chillers, boilers and air handlers; fixed plant layout, institution-controlled access, permits and lockout procedures, equipment often large and hard-piped.

Controls and electrical component work across residential and light-commercial sites: replace defective thermostats, zone dampers/motors, sensors, relays, transformers, limit switches and control boards, and re-terminate or re-run low-voltage control wiring inside unit control cabinets and at wall locations; requires reading wiring diagrams, tracing faults, and verifying operation.

sources.system: Quadruped inspection robots (Spot-class) integrated with Oxmaint CMMS
sources.title: HVAC Robots for Data Center Cooling Maintenance
sources.claim: Quadruped robots deployed for HVAC asset patrols in facilities perform thermal/vibration inspection and generate work orders; the actual repairs (coil cleaning, bearing replacement, refrigerant service) are still executed by human technicians during scheduled windows. This is the closest robotic presence to HVAC maintenance and it explicitly excludes component repair/replacement.
sources.transferJustification: Same equipment class (HVAC units in facilities). Cited as the state of the art for robots at HVAC assets: the robot inspects, a human performs the repair/replacement, so it does not substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

sources.system: Tianxun (2nd generation) data center operations robot
sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center
sources.claim: Alibaba's second-generation Tianxun data-center robot autonomously inspects, locates a faulty hard disk and replaces it without human intervention, operating in production data halls at five data centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous replacement of a defective component in a structured facility. Transfer to HVAC repair fails: a hard disk is a tool-free hot-swap module in a purpose-designed rack slot, whereas HVAC component replacement requires panel/fastener removal, terminal and harness work, refrigerant recovery/brazing, and post-repair functional verification on non-standard equipment.

sources.system: Automated unscrewing cell (UR10e + Intel RealSense D405 + custom mechatronic screwdriver)
sources.developer: Díaz et al., published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A UR10e-based cell with RealSense vision and a custom mechatronic screwdriver autonomously locates, identifies and removes screws from a wide range of electronic ... in a laboratory disassembly setup — i.e., only the fastener-removal sub-step of a repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fastener removal on varied devices, a sub-step of opening HVAC equipment. It substantiates only that sub-step; no diagnosis, component swap, re-wiring, reassembly or functional verification is demonstrated, so it cannot support whole-instance completion even at E1.

sources.system: Disassembly CPS robotic dismantling cell
sources.title: Appliance Manufacturer Uses Robots and AI to Disassemble Products | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Panasonic is programming six-axis robots in a purpose-built cell to dismantle end-of-life air conditioners, microwaves and washing machines using magnetic grippers and screwdrivers, driven by 3D CAD data and AI — destructive/terminal disassembly for material recovery, not repair or component replacement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown of air conditioners in a fixtured cell — the same object class as HVAC equipment. It does not transfer to repair: the goal is separation of materials, with no fault diagnosis, no installation of a replacement part, no re-termination of wiring, and no restored-function acceptance test.

sources.system: Dragon 15/20 induction brazing robot
sources.title: Induction Brazing Robot - Dragon 15 | UltraFlex Power Technologies
sources.claim: Robotic induction brazing of copper/brass tube joints is available as a fixtured factory workcell for HVAC-industry manufacturers, e.g. brazing compressor and heat-exchanger assemblies with a robot-held induction coil on an indexing turntable.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining refrigerant tubing, a sub-step when replacing a compressor or coil. Transfer is limited to that sub-step on new, identically fixtured parts in manufacturing; it does not cover fault diagnosis, refrigerant recovery, removal of a failed component, wiring, or evacuation/charge on as-found equipment.

sources.system: Digit / Apollo / Figure class humanoids
sources.title: Humanoid Robot Comparison Tracker (2026) – New Market Pitch
sources.claim: Commercially deployed humanoids remain limited to tote and simple part handling rather than general dexterous tool work; Digit's end effectors are specialized for plastic totes, and verified humanoid work is material handling, bin picking, inspection and simple assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize the general-purpose mobile manipulation frontier: the platforms most often proposed for field service work are not demonstrated performing diagnostic, fastener, wiring or brazing work on installed equipment, supporting the negative judgments.

tasks.label: Lay out and connect electrical wiring between controls and equipment, according to wiring diagrams, using electrician's hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential split-system or furnace changeout/installation: run and land 24 V thermostat/control wiring at the furnace or air-handler control board, land control and line-voltage conductors at the outdoor condensing unit and its disconnect, following the unit's wiring diagram; work in a basement, closet, attic or on an exterior pad in an occupied private home, with hand tools (strippers, nut drivers, wire nuts, spade terminals).

Residential or light-commercial service/repair call: replace a failed contactor, transformer, relay board, defrost control or thermostat and re-land the existing, often unlabeled and aged, field wiring per the diagram on the unit door; cramped as-found equipment compartments, dust/corrosion, live-circuit precautions.

Rooftop packaged unit (RTU) install or replacement on a commercial building: pull and terminate power at the disconnect, land control/BAS or thermostat wiring on the unit's low-voltage terminal block, wire economizer, sensors and safeties per the diagram; institution-controlled rooftop, weather exposure.

Supermarket/industrial refrigeration or chiller controls work in a mechanical room or equipment corridor: lay out and wire a control panel (contactors, relays, defrost timers, controllers, terminal blocks) and connect it to compressors, condensers, valves and sensors per schematic.

New-construction / rough-in: lay out and pull thermostat, zone-damper and equipment control wiring through framing, joists, chases and above ceilings between control locations and equipment per mechanical plans, before finishes; active construction site.
Shop prefabrication: technician assembles and wires a control panel or unit sub-assembly on a bench in the contractor's shop per a wiring diagram, before it is taken to the field.

sources.system: Averex robotic wiring centre

Stocking the service van / shop bin replenishment: estimate consumable levels (filters, fittings, wire nuts, brazing rod, refrigerant cylinders), place the order, pick it up at the supply-house warehouse counter, load the truck and put the stock away on van shelves.

instances.label: Retrofit replacement of a wall thermostat in an occupied single-family home: shut off power, pull the old unit, identify/label 4–8 low-voltage conductors of varied color coding coming through a drywall hole, drill and anchor the new subbase level on the wall, land wires on screw/push terminals, snap the faceplate, configure system type (conventional/heat pump, stages), set schedule, and verify heat/cool/fan calls at the equipment.

New-construction or full-system-replacement trim-out: thermostat/humidistat mounted at a rough-in wire in a framed or newly finished wall, conductors also landed at the furnace/air-handler control board or humidifier transformer, jumper/dip-switch configuration, then commissioning of the control with the new equipment.

Light-commercial or institutional building (office, retail, school, clinic): install or replace a programmable thermostat, zone sensor, or 7-day timer; wiring run in conduit or plenum to a rooftop unit or zone panel, device mounted on a wall or in a control enclosure, schedule and lockout limits programmed, operation verified.

Commercial refrigeration / food service: install or adjust a defrost timer, temperature control, or humidistat in the control panel of a walk-in cooler or display case at a supermarket or restaurant; line-voltage and low-voltage terminations inside an enclosure, defrost times and cut-in/cut-out setpoints set, cycle observed.

Adjust-only service call with no wiring: change setpoints and programmed schedules, recalibrate a thermostat offset or set the heat anticipator, turn a humidistat dial to match outdoor conditions, reset a timer's clock, and confirm the reading against a reference thermometer in an occupied home or small business.

tasks.label: Comply with all applicable standards, policies, or procedures, such as safety procedures or the maintenance of a clean work area.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service/maintenance call in an occupied home: tech lays drop cloths or shoe covers on finished floors, kills and verifies power at the disconnect before opening the furnace/air handler, wears gloves and eye protection when brazing or connecting gauges, contains filter, rust and coil debris, vacuums the mechanical closet/attic/basement, carries old parts and packaging out to the truck, and leaves the area as clean as or cleaner than found.

Residential or light-commercial equipment changeout/installation: protect floors and stair rails along the carry path, recover refrigerant per EPA 608 before opening the system, follow hot-work and ladder rules while brazing and cutting sheet metal, control the sheet-metal scrap, insulation, cardboard and old duct debris, haul the old unit and all waste off site, then sweep/vacuum and walk the customer through the finished, cleaned area.

Commercial/institutional building service (school, hospital, office tower): sign in under the facility's contractor safety program, apply lockout/tagout to the rooftop unit or chiller disconnect, use roof-access and fall-protection procedures, cone off or barricade work in occupied corridors, wear required PPE, then clean the mechanical room/roof curb area, bag and dispose of used filters, oily rags and refrigerant oil, replace ceiling tiles, and log the compliance paperwork.

Supermarket or food-service refrigeration service: work on cases and racks in occupied sales floor and back-of-house under store sanitation and food-safety rules, perform and record leak checks and refrigerant handling per EPA/state rules, keep aisles barricaded and clear for customers, wipe up oil, water and defrost debris, remove packaging and replaced components, and sanitize surfaces near food before leaving.

Shop, warehouse and service-vehicle housekeeping between jobs: keep the shop bay and van organized, store and label refrigerant recovery cylinders and hazardous waste per DOT/EPA rules, maintain and inspect PPE, gauges and ladders, sweep/clean the bay after fabrication, and stage materials for the next job.

tasks.label: Repair or service heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems to improve efficiency, such as by changing filters, cleaning ducts, and refilling non-toxic refrigerants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential efficiency tune-up / service call in an occupied home: access attic, closet, garage or basement air handler and the outdoor condenser, swap the return-air or media filter, rinse/chemically clean the condenser coil, clear the condensate drain, check airflow, measure superheat/subcooling and adjust charge, then explain findings to the homeowner. Layout, equipment brand, clearances and clutter differ at every house.

Refrigerant service on a residential or light-commercial split system after a leak repair or during a low-charge complaint: locate service valves, recover remaining charge, pull vacuum, weigh in the nameplate charge of R-410A/R-454B, verify subcooling and log the refrigerant per EPA 608. Done on site at a house or small business.

Preventive maintenance on a packaged rooftop unit at a retail store, restaurant or small office: ladder/hatch roof access, remove screwed access panels and hoods, replace the filter bank, chemically wash condenser and evaporator coils, flush the drain pan, check belts/bearings and verify charge, in outdoor weather on a roof controlled by the building owner.

Scheduled filter change-out program in a large institutional facility (hospital, university, office tower): work through mechanical rooms and ceiling fan-coil units on a route, pull dozens of loaded pleated/bag filters from racks, install and seal new ones to spec, and log each unit. Standard equipment, fixed layout, facility-controlled access.

Duct cleaning job, usually in a private home or small commercial suite: set up the negative-air machine, cut/open access ports, remove registers, run brushes and vacuum lines through trunk and branch ducts, clean the blower and coil face, reseal access panels and restore the space.

Refrigeration/HVAC efficiency service at a supermarket, convenience store or restaurant: clean condenser coils on rooftop racks and walk-in condensing units, change filters on make-up-air and RTU units, check and top off charge on cases, working around store operations and food-safety constraints.

tasks.label: Test pipes, lines, components, and connections for leaks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call, no-cooling complaint on a split system: tech hooks up a manifold/nitrogen or trace gas, then hunts a refrigerant leak with an electronic sniffer, bubble solution or UV dye across the evaporator coil in an attic or closet, the lineset through crawlspace/walls, and the outdoor condenser joints and Schrader ports. Occupied home, tight access, dust, wind outdoors.

New install or post-repair verification on a jobsite (house under construction or light-commercial tenant space): pressurize the freshly brazed lineset/coil with dry nitrogen to several hundred psi, hold a standing pressure test, bubble-test each brazed joint and flare, then pull vacuum and run a micron/vacuum-decay check before charging.

Commercial service call on a rooftop packaged unit, VRF branch piping, or a chiller in a mechanical room: remove access panels, isolate circuits, connect gauges/nitrogen, and probe compressor fittings, service valves, coil hairpins and flare/brazed connections with an electronic detector and bubbles; document findings for the building owner.

Scheduled leak inspection (e.g., EPA 608 / refrigerant management compliance) of a supermarket rack room, cold-storage engine room or large chiller plant: walk the exposed pressurized piping runs, headers and valve stations with an electronic/IR detector or acoustic imager, locate and log any leaking joints, no disassembly required.

Combustion-side / fuel and water piping leak test: after replacing a gas valve, furnace, or boiler section, pressure-test the gas piping and check unions, drip legs and manifold fittings with a combustible-gas detector, leak-detect solution and manometer drop test; or pressure-test hydronic/condensate piping. Home basement or small commercial boiler room.

tasks.label: Braze or solder parts to repair defective joints and leaks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call on a split system with a refrigerant leak: tech locates the leaking joint (service valve, filter-drier, line-set fitting, evaporator/condenser tube stub), recovers refrigerant, cuts out the defective section, cleans and fits a coupling or new component, flows nitrogen through the line, and torch-brazes 1-3 copper joints in situ in a closet, attic, crawlspace or beside the outdoor unit, with heat shields near siding/insulation; joint must hold a pressure/leak test.

New or replacement installation in a home or light-commercial building: brazing line-set connections at the condenser and coil, TXV or accessory joints, sometimes soldering copper hydronic/water piping at a boiler or air handler; joints made overhead, in tight mechanical closets or outdoors, with nitrogen purge and hot-work precautions.

Commercial rooftop unit or built-up system at an office/school/retail building: brazing repairs to leaking refrigerant piping, driers, or compressor stubs on a roof curb or in a mechanical room, working around ductwork and fixed equipment, in wind/heat, under a hot-work permit.

Supermarket or industrial refrigeration: brazing leak repairs on rack piping, headers, valves or display-case and walk-in evaporator coils in a machine room, sales floor, or cooler, often in cramped bundled piping runs and cold/wet conditions while the store operates.

Shop/bench work at the service company or a truck tailgate: brazing on a component that has been removed and brought to the bench (accumulator, drier, receiver, coil stub, valve body), or fabricating/repairing short copper pipe assemblies and adapters before installation.

tasks.label: Recommend, develop, or perform preventive or general maintenance procedures, such as cleaning, power-washing, or vacuuming equipment, oiling parts, or changing filters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential PM tune-up in a private home: tech carries tools into the house, pulls and replaces the 1" filter at the return grille or furnace cabinet, vacuums the blower compartment and burner area, hoses/chemically rinses the outdoor condenser coil, clears the condensate drain with a wet-vac, oils a blower motor where fitted, and tells the homeowner how often to change filters. Clutter, pets, attic/crawlspace or side-yard access, varied equipment brands and ages.

Rooftop packaged-unit (RTU) PM route at a retail store, restaurant or office building: several units on the roof, each with screwed/latched access panels; swap 4-8 filters per unit, inspect/replace belts, chemically wash condenser and evaporator coils with a pressure washer, clean blower wheel and drain pan, grease bearings, and log readings on a PM checklist. Institution-controlled premises, weather exposure, unit models differ.

Central plant / mechanical room PM in a hospital, school, campus or office tower: change large AHU filter banks (dozens of 24x24 panels or bags), grease fan and pump bearings, vacuum and clean coils, drain pans and UV sections, brush chiller condenser tubes, wipe down and power-wash equipment. Tight plant-room aisles, ladders/platforms, scheduled shutdown windows.

Supermarket / restaurant refrigeration PM: clean condenser coils on walk-in and rack systems (roof or back-of-house), clean evaporator coils and fan blades inside coolers/freezers, clean and sanitize ice machines, clear defrost drains, change filters on HVAC units. Cramped, wet, cold, food-safety constraints, work around store staff.

Industrial/process or data-center cooling PM: cooling tower basin and fill cleaning, large fin-tube coil and air-cooled heat exchanger washing, CRAC/CRAH filter changes, scheduled lubrication rounds under a formal PM program at a plant or data hall. Institution-controlled site, permits/lockout, mostly repeat equipment.

sources.claim: JNW's Cleaning Robot is a commercially supplied, PLC-controlled fully automatic water-jet cleaning system for air-cooled condensers and flat-bed coolers; once started it runs the whole cleaning cycle unattended, parks itself and shuts down, controlled from a panel at the cooler or the plant control room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated water-jet cleaning of finned heat-exchanger bundles. This is the same physical operation as the 'power-washing/cleaning equipment' element of HVAC PM - pressurized water on fin-tube coils, with fin-damage tolerances at least as tight as an HVAC condenser coil - performed on a purpose-installed traversing chassis, i.e. an environment built around the machine.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-pressure washing and cleaning of fixtured mechanical components inside a fenced cell. tasks.label: Adjust system controls to settings recommended by manufacturer to balance system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential startup/commissioning of a furnace, split AC or heat pump in a home basement, closet, attic or crawlspace: set control-board dip switches/jumpers and blower speed tap per the manufacturer's airflow table, adjust gas manifold pressure with a screwdriver while reading a manometer, verify temperature rise and refrigerant charge (superheat/subcooling), configure the thermostat, and re-check until readings match the installation manual.

Balancing the air distribution of an installed residential or small light-commercial system: measuring room-by-room airflow and temperature, then adjusting branch balancing dampers in joists/attics, register throws, zone-panel damper minimums and bypass settings until each room meets design, in an occupied, as-found house.

Startup/adjustment of a packaged rooftop unit or small commercial split system on a strip-mall or office building: setting fan speed (belt sheave or ECM/VFD parameter) to design CFM against measured static pressure, economizer changeover and minimum-position settings, staging and setpoint parameters on the unit controller, per the manufacturer's startup sheet, on a rooftop in weather.

Large commercial/institutional system: adjusting AHU and VAV terminal controller parameters (minimum/maximum flow setpoints, PID/loop settings, static-pressure reset), hydronic balancing valve positions and pump/VFD settings in mechanical rooms and above ceilings across a building, coordinating with a test-and-balance report to bring the whole system to manufacturer/design values.

Commercial refrigeration in a supermarket, restaurant or walk-in: adjusting TXV superheat stems, EPR/head-pressure valves, low/high pressure control cut-in/cut-out, defrost termination and case controller setpoints to the manufacturer's published values while reading pressures and temperatures on the running rack or condensing unit.

sources.system: Auto Toe Set (ATS) robotic system with Non-Contact Alignment (NCA)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated vehicle toe setting at end of line. It is the same class of work as adjusting HVAC controls to manufacturer settings — closed-loop measurement followed by fine adjustment of a threaded control (tie rod/jam nut vs. gas-valve regulator screw, TXV superheat stem, pressure-control setscrew) to a published specification, with comparable precision and with the workpiece fixtured and instrumented in a purpose-built cell, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

tasks.label: Perform mechanical overhauls and refrigerant reclaiming.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential or light-commercial changeout/removal: technician recovers the full refrigerant charge from an aging split-system condensing unit or heat pump sitting on a pad beside a house (or a window/PTAC/small package unit), hooking a recovery machine and hoses to the service ports, pulling the system down to the required vacuum, weighing and labeling the recovery cylinder, and turning the charge over for reclamation before the old unit is hauled away. Recovery only; no mechanical rebuild.

Shop or warehouse yard: technician recovers refrigerant from scrapped, warranty-returned, or decommissioned equipment (condensing units, reach-in coolers, PTACs) staged at the service shop, runs recovered charge through a recovery/recycling machine, manages and weighs cylinders to the 80% fill limit, and prepares drums for shipment to a certified reclaimer.

Field sealed-system repair at a home or on a commercial rooftop package unit: recover the charge, cut out and replace a failed hermetic/scroll compressor or leaking coil (torch brazing, nitrogen purge, new filter-drier and oil), pressure-test with nitrogen, evacuate to 500 microns, recharge by weight, and verify superheat/subcool. Access by ladder, weather and cramped cabinets are part of the job.

Supermarket or cold-storage machine room: mechanical overhaul of a semi-hermetic reciprocating or screw compressor on a refrigeration rack — pump down/isolate and recover the charge, pull heads, replace valve plates, gaskets, unloaders, bearings or the whole compressor, change oil and driers, then evacuate, recharge and bring the rack back on line while the store operates.

Building mechanical room / industrial plant: scheduled overhaul of a large chiller or ammonia/industrial compressor — pump the refrigerant out to a storage vessel or recovery unit, tear the compressor down (shaft seal, bearings, impeller/rotors, motor), inspect and replace worn parts to tolerance, reassemble and align to spec, leak-test, dehydrate under deep vacuum, recharge and run-test the machine.

sources.system: ATN Engineering (Andritz Group) degasser for domestic fridges and air-conditioning units
sources.title: Degasser for domestic fridges and air-conditioning units - ATN Engineering
sources.claim: ATN Engineering's degassing systems automatically pierce the compressor of end-of-life refrigerators and air-conditioning units and extract essentially the whole refrigerant charge and oil into storage tanks, with measured 99.5% gas and oil collection efficiency and volume tracking, in recycling plants running continuously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plant-based degassing/de-oiling of end-of-life fridges and AC units. It transfers to a technician's refrigerant reclaiming on units being replaced or scrapped: the same refrigerants and compressor oils are pulled from the same class of sealed systems, the accepted output is the same (charge captured for reclamation rather than vented, unit ready for disposal), and the machine performs the extraction cycle itself once the unit is presented.

sources.system: ATN Automatic Degassing System of Domestic Fridges
sources.title: ATN Automatic Degassing System Of Domestic Fridges
sources.claim: ATN builds fully automatic versions of the degassing station using a patented automatic drill-head that degasses and de-oils a refrigerator compressor in under a minute, at line capacities up to 200 units per hour including high-pressure gases from AC units.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above; this listing establishes that the extraction cycle (positioning, piercing, evacuation, separation and collection) runs fully automatically rather than being hand-operated, which is what a positive judgment at E1 requires.

sources.system: SEDA AFR (automatic refrigerant and compressor oil extraction device)
sources.title: Refrigerator Recycling Equipment by SEDA - Professional Car Recycling - SEDA
sources.claim: SEDA's AFR is a commercially sold automatic refrigerant and compressor-oil extraction device for refrigerator/AC disposal, achieving up to 98% emptying rate, sold as a stand-alone unit or built into automated refrigerator recycling systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated refrigerant/oil extraction from end-of-life appliances at recycling and vehicle-depollution sites. Transfers to the reclaiming half of this task for the same reasons as the ATN evidence — same refrigerants, same sealed-system compressors, same accepted output of captured refrigerant.

sources.system: robotic disassembly / remanufacturing cells (survey of the field)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: Survey of remanufacturing automation as of March 2026: robotic disassembly systems are only beginning to emerge, and used-product variability (seized bolts, deformed parts, inconsistent assembly) still blocks automating the teardown-inspect-rebuild sequence that an overhaul requires; cleaning and washing are the mature automated stages.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as context for negative judgments on the mechanical-overhaul instances: remanufacturing of used machines in purpose-built plants is the closest analogue to a compressor or chiller overhaul, and it is not yet performed end-to-end by autonomous machines.

sources.system: Rolls-Royce remote boreblending robot / snake robots
sources.developer: Rolls-Royce with University of Nottingham / Harvard
sources.title: Rolls-Royce Developing Robotics For Engine Maintenance
sources.claim: The most advanced in-situ machine-repair robots in heavy MRO — Rolls-Royce's boreblending robots for repairing compressor blades inside an assembled engine — are operated remotely by a skilled technician rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ mechanical repair of rotating machinery. It bears on the overhaul instances by showing that even the flagship machine-repair robots are remotely controlled, so they cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous compressor or chiller overhaul.

tasks.label: Install expansion and control valves, using acetylene torches and wrenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential split-system service call: replace a failed thermostatic expansion valve at the indoor evaporator coil in an attic, closet, crawlspace or basement — recover refrigerant, unbraze/cut out the old valve, braze in the new TXV with an oxy-acetylene torch under nitrogen purge and heat shielding, strap the sensing bulb and connect the external equalizer with wrenches, pressure test, evacuate and recharge. Cramped, varying access, homeowner property.

Light-commercial rooftop package unit or outdoor condensing unit: install or replace a TXV, liquid-line solenoid, or head-pressure/control valve on a cluttered rooftop or in an outdoor equipment yard — ladder or hoist access, wind, sun, weather, ad hoc positioning of torch and tanks, panels removed for access.

Supermarket, cold-storage or institutional refrigeration rack: install expansion valves, solenoid valves and EPR/control valves on rack piping in a machine room or on evaporators above display cases — premises controlled by the store/facility, fairly standard rack layouts, scheduled night or off-hours work, brazing plus wrench work on flare/threaded fittings.

New construction or major retrofit inside a building under construction: braze expansion valves, service valves and control valves into new line sets and coils, working from ladders or lifts amid other trades, dusty and changing site conditions, no fixed layout.

Shop or bench prefabrication at the contractor's fabrication facility: braze expansion/solenoid valves onto tubing subassemblies and valve packages at a bench, or wrench flanged/threaded control valves into hydronic piping spools, then pressure test before shipping to the jobsite.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: brazing copper joints of a refrigeration circuit in production. Same materials (copper tube, silver-phos filler), same joint type and precision as brazing an expansion valve into a liquid line, performed with the assembly fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.claim: The Novarc Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 welds pipe joints autonomously in pipe-fabrication shops, using real-time vision to adapt parameters to joint inconsistencies such as HiLo and varying root gaps, with the spool loaded onto a positioner by an operator.

tasks.label: Inspect and test systems to verify system compliance with plans and specifications or to detect and locate malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential no-cooling / no-heat diagnostic service call in an occupied private home: check thermostat and breaker, pull panels on the furnace/air handler in a closet, attic or basement, meter the capacitor/contactor/control board, attach manifold gauges to the condenser service ports, read superheat/subcooling and temperature split, inspect filter and coil, and identify the failed component. Clutter, pets, tight access, and a homeowner present.

Light-commercial diagnostic on a packaged rooftop unit or split system at a retail store, restaurant or small office: ladder/roof-hatch access, open access panels in wind and sun, clamp-meter the compressor and fan motors, check refrigerant pressures, economizer and control board, verify operation against the unit's rating plate, and locate the malfunction.

Commercial refrigeration troubleshooting at a supermarket, convenience store or restaurant: walk-in cooler or display case not holding temperature; check pressures and superheat at the rack or condensing unit, run an electronic leak search along evaporator and line sets, verify defrost timing, EPR/TXV and controller settings while cases stay merchandised and the store stays open.

Startup/commissioning verification of a newly installed system against plans and specifications, in a new-construction or replacement job: measure supply airflow at registers and total external static pressure, check duct leakage and venting/combustion per spec, verify charge by weigh-in and subcooling, confirm control wiring and safeties, and complete the startup/inspection documentation.

Scheduled rounds/condition inspection of central plant and air-side equipment in a large institutional or industrial facility (hospital, campus, plant): walk the chiller/boiler room and mechanical mezzanines, read gauges and panel displays against setpoints, thermal-check motors, bearings and electrical connections, listen and scan for refrigerant or air leaks, log readings, and flag abnormal conditions for follow-up.

tasks.label: Connect heating or air conditioning equipment to fuel, water, or refrigerant source to form complete circuit.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential split-system A/C or heat pump changeout in an occupied single-family home: route and connect the line set between outdoor condenser and indoor coil (braze or flare fittings, nitrogen purge), tie into service valves, pressure test, evacuate and charge. Work in tight closets, attics, crawl spaces, along exterior walls; layout unique to each house.

Residential gas furnace or boiler hookup: connect black-iron/CSST gas piping with drip leg and shutoff to the burner manifold, connect condensate and (for hydronic) supply/return water piping to the near-boiler circuit, then soap/pressure leak test. Basements and utility closets, existing piping in unknown condition.

Light-commercial rooftop unit or split system in an occupied commercial building: connect gas train to the roof gas main, run and braze refrigerant lines to a remote condenser or through a mechanical room, connect condensate/water. Building is managed and access controlled, but the roof/mech-room layout is site specific.

Commercial refrigeration: walk-in cooler/freezer or supermarket rack — braze suction and liquid lines from case or evaporator back through the store's back room and into the machine room, connect to the rack/condensing unit, pressure test, evacuate, charge. Store premises are institution controlled but full of stock and fixtures.

New-construction tract-house or multi-family rough-in and trim-out: repetitive line-set, gas and condensate connections on identical units before occupancy, on an active construction site with debris, other trades, and unfinished conditions.

tasks.label: Mount compressor, condenser, and other components in specified locations on frames, using hand tools and acetylene welding equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial split system installation at a private home: securing the outdoor condensing unit to a pad, bracket or roof frame, mounting the indoor coil/air handler on its stand or frame, and brazing line-set connections with an oxy-acetylene torch in a side yard, attic, crawlspace or closet whose layout differs house to house.

Commercial building mechanical/equipment room: mounting a compressor, condenser section, receiver and accessories in specified positions on a unit frame or rail base per shop drawings, bolting through vibration isolators and brazing/welding the interconnecting refrigerant piping, working around existing equipment in a controlled building.

Contractor or OEM fabrication shop: building up condensing units, parallel refrigeration racks or skid-mounted packages on a steel frame — hoisting compressors into place, bolting them down, mounting condenser coils, receivers and controls, and brazing copper headers on the bench.

Field compressor/condenser replacement in an existing packaged rooftop or condensing unit at a commercial site: cutting out the failed compressor, freeing corroded frame bolts, setting the replacement on the frame rails with isolators, and brazing suction/discharge lines in confined outdoor conditions on a legacy unit of unknown configuration.

Supermarket walk-in cooler or transport refrigeration work: mounting a condensing unit or compressor onto a rack frame in a store back room, or onto a truck/trailer chassis frame in a fleet shop, then brazing the refrigerant lines and fastening guards and controls.

Light commercial retrofit: rooftop packaged unit or split system at a store, restaurant or small office - curb adapter and duct transitions, dampers, economizer hood, flue/vent, gas piping and refrigerant piping on a cluttered as-found roof or in a mechanical room.

Large commercial/institutional building under construction (office, hospital, school, data center): installing overhead duct mains and branches on hangers, VAV boxes, fire/volume dampers, and hydronic or refrigerant piping to air handlers, working from lifts in a coordinated but changing site.

Commercial refrigeration in a supermarket, cold-storage or restaurant: installing expansion valves (TXV/EEV), EPR and discharge/suction line components, copper refrigerant piping and drier shells on display cases, walk-ins and parallel racks, brazing and leak-checking the joints inside a store or machine room controlled by the operator.

Shop/prefabrication work before delivery: assembling refrigerant or hydronic pipe and valve packages, coil/valve assemblies and equipment sub-assemblies on benches or jigs in the contractor's fabrication shop or a prefab facility, where parts are cut to size and held in position.

tasks.label: Install or repair self-contained ground source heat pumps or hybrid ground or air source heat pumps to minimize carbon-based energy consumption and reduce carbon emissions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New ground-source (geothermal) heat pump install in an existing single-family home: carry the packaged water-to-air unit into a basement/utility closet, set and level it, connect supply/return loop piping to a flow center, tie into existing plenum/ductwork with sheet-metal transitions, run condensate and low-voltage/line-voltage wiring to a panel, purge and pressurize the loop, charge/verify refrigerant, commission and program the thermostat, and document the job for rebates.

Service/repair call on an installed ground-source or water-source heat pump: diagnose a no-heat/no-cool complaint in a cramped mechanical room or crawlspace, test electrical and control circuits, replace a failed compressor, circulator pump, reversing valve, expansion valve, or control board (brazing, recovery/evacuation, recharge), clear a fouled coil or plugged loop, re-purge, and verify operation.

Hybrid/dual-fuel retrofit at a home: set an outdoor air-source heat pump condenser on a pad or wall bracket, install indoor coil or air handler above the existing gas furnace, route and braze a refrigerant line set through joists/walls, pull vacuum, wire the dual-fuel/outdoor-temperature control and thermostat, set changeover logic, and start up.

Commercial/institutional water-source or ground-source heat pump work: install or replace ceiling-hung or console WSHP units in a school, office, or apartment building mechanical space; hang the unit from threaded rod, connect hoses/valves to the building water loop, connect ducted branches, wire to the BAS/controls, balance and commission, on an occupied or under-construction site.

Outdoor ground-loop side of the job: header and heat-fuse HDPE loop piping in an open trench or vault, transition to the building entry, pressure-test, flush and purge the loop with a purge cart, add antifreeze, and backfill/seal the penetration, in weather and mud at a residential lot.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling hangers/anchor holes for mechanical piping and ductwork on jobsites. It is the closest field-deployed mechanical-trade robot, but it covers only one sub-step of an install; it cannot set a heat pump, make piping or refrigerant joints, wire controls, or commission a system, so it does not carry over to completing this task.

Residential/light-commercial install of a whole-house media air cleaner, high-MERV filter cabinet or HEPA bypass unit — fabricate/modify sheet-metal return transitions, hang and fasten the cabinet, seal joints, wire any controls or bypass blower, verify static pressure and airflow after installation.

Residential/light-commercial repair call on existing purification equipment: replace a burned-out UV lamp and its ballast/power supply, clean or replace electronic air cleaner collector cells and broken ionizing wires, diagnose a no-light or nuisance-arcing complaint in a tight mechanical closet, then retest.

Scheduled replacement of the filter media/element in an already-installed air-cleaning unit at a home or small office (media cartridge or pre-filter pad swapped on a set interval, correct orientation and seal, old media bagged and removed).

Commercial building work in a mechanical room or on a rooftop unit: pull and replace banks of pleated and bag final filters of several sizes in an air handler, and/or retrofit UV-C fixtures into the coil section — mount rails, wire fixtures to a disconnect, log pressure drop and verify operation.

Healthcare, laboratory or cleanroom HEPA work in a controlled facility: terminal HEPA/ULPA filter change-out or bag-in/bag-out housing filter exchange, gasket/gel seating, clamping to leak-tight condition, coordination with certification and documentation.

tasks.label: Supervise and instruct assistants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lead HVAC technician on a residential furnace/split-system install directs a helper through the day: assigning which duct runs, line sets, or condenser pad work to do next, checking in verbally, and adjusting assignments as the job unfolds in an occupied home.

Journeyman inspects an apprentice's completed work on a commercial rooftop unit or walk-in cooler (flare joints, wiring terminations, condensate routing), points out defects, and instructs the apprentice on how to correct them before the job is signed off.

Technician explains and demonstrates a technique to an apprentice at the job site — brazing with nitrogen purge, pulling a vacuum and reading a micron gauge, superheat/subcooling charging, or safe lockout/tagout — narrating the reasoning so the helper can repeat it unsupervised.

Retrofit or addition inside an existing, operating commercial facility: marking anchor points for a replacement rooftop curb or unit rails on an occupied roof, laying out new supports and equipment positions in a live mechanical room or above an existing ceiling, working around installed piping, ducts and running equipment.

New commercial construction / retrofit jobsite: hard-piping refrigerant, chilled-water or hydronic lines — measuring to layout drawings, sawing/cutting larger copper or steel pipe and bending or preparing ends for fittings amid an active, changing construction site.

tasks.label: Install dehumidifiers or related equipment for spaces that require cool, dry air to operate efficiently, such as computer rooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential whole-house dehumidifier install: set/hang a 70-130 pint ducted unit in a finished or unfinished basement or mechanical room of an occupied home, tie supply/return ducts into the existing air-handler plenum with sheet-metal collars and flex duct, run a gravity or pumped condensate line to a sump/laundry drain, pull a dedicated 120V circuit, mount and wire a humidistat, then start up and verify RH setpoint.

Crawlspace or encapsulated substructure dehumidifier: crawl through an 18-36 inch clearance, dirt- or vapor-barrier-floored crawlspace, hang the unit from floor joists with straps or set it on blocks, run ducting and a drain hose to a sump or condensate pump, fish and terminate power from the panel, seal vents, and commission the unit.

Small commercial server/telecom closet or small computer room in an office building: install a dedicated cooling/dehumidification unit (ceiling- or wall-mounted ductless head or small precision unit) plus condensate pump, core-drill/route the line set through wall or ceiling plenum above an occupied office, braze/flare and evacuate refrigerant lines, connect power and controls, and verify temperature/RH.

Data center or large computer room: rig and set a CRAC/CRAH or in-row cooling unit on a raised floor or slab, anchor it, connect chilled-water or refrigerant piping and humidifier/condensate lines, land power and BMS/controls wiring, cut floor tiles or ductwork, then commission the unit alongside live IT load with no downtime.

Large institutional/industrial dehumidification: crane-set a natatorium pool dehumidifier, ice-rink or warehouse desiccant unit, or DOAS rooftop unit at a school, hotel, or food plant; hang and connect ductwork, condensate and refrigerant/water piping, dampers, disconnects, and controls in a mechanical room or on a roof curb, then balance and commission.

tasks.label: Lift and align components into position, using hoist or block and tackle.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential replacement: furnace, air handler, or evaporator coil (100-250 lb) moved into a basement, attic, closet, or crawlspace of an occupied home using an appliance dolly, stair-climbing hoist, or block-and-tackle rigged to a joist; unit aligned to the existing plenum/return opening and set level on its stand or pad.

Commercial rooftop packaged unit (3-25 ton, 500-3,000 lb) set or replaced: unit flown by crane or hoisted with a gin pole, then guided down onto the roof curb, rotated and aligned so supply/return openings and the curb gasket line up, and bolted down; done outdoors on an occupied building's roof in whatever weather and layout is found.

Compressor, condenser fan motor, or blower assembly (150-800 lb) swapped inside a commercial mechanical room, walk-in cooler condensing unit, or rooftop cabinet using a chain fall or come-along rigged to unistrut/overhead steel; part lifted out of a tight space and the replacement aligned to mounting rails, vibration isolators, and suction/discharge stubs.

New construction or retrofit fit-out: air handlers, fan coils, VAV boxes, and large duct/coil sections hoisted to overhead hangers, housekeeping pads, or platforms with chain hoists, lifts, and rigging; held in position while threaded rod, trapeze hangers, or anchor bolts are attached, on an active construction site shared with other trades.

Industrial/large refrigeration machine room: ammonia or large chiller compressor, motor, or bundle lifted with the room's overhead crane, monorail hoist, or chain fall; landed on its base skid, aligned to the coupling/flange faces, shimmed and bolted in a plant machine room with fixed layout and standard rigging points.

Outdoor condensing unit, heat pump, or mini-split outdoor unit (80-400 lb) moved from a truck and set on a ground pad, roof stand, or wall brackets, sometimes hoisted over fences or up to a balcony with block and tackle, then aligned to line-set and pad anchors at a residence or small commercial site.

Service/replacement work inside an operating commercial or institutional building: core drill a 2–6 in. penetration through a concrete floor slab or masonry wall for refrigerant piping, condensate or a duct sleeve; rebar scanning, water control, dust containment, protection of occupied space below.

Roof work: cut an opening through an existing roof deck (plywood or metal deck) and roofing membrane for a rooftop-unit curb or duct drop, or make smaller roof penetrations for line sets and flue vents, then flash and seal; outdoors, variable roof build-up and weather.

roles.description: Repair, adjust, or install all types of electric or gas household appliances, such as refrigerators, washers, dryers, and ovens.

tasks.label: Bill customers for repair work, and collect payment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Observe and examine appliances during operation to detect specific malfunctions such as loose parts or leaking fluid.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Service call in a customer's home: technician starts a washer or dishwasher, watches a fill/wash/spin/drain cycle in a cramped kitchen or laundry closet, listens for knocking or rattling, feels the cabinet for vibration, watches the floor and under-cabinet area for water, and localizes the leak (door boot, pump, hose clamp) or loose part.

In-home refrigerator/freezer call: technician runs the unit, listens to compressor and evaporator fan for abnormal noise, checks for refrigerant loss and oil traces at joints, and looks for water from a defective ice maker line or clogged defrost drain, often pulling the unit out from the wall.

In-home gas or electric range, oven, or dryer call: technician fires burners or heating elements and observes flame pattern, ignition and cycling; checks gas connections for leaks; runs the dryer drum to hear a worn roller, loose belt or blower rattle.

Post-installation or post-repair operational check in the customer's home: run the newly installed or repaired appliance through a short cycle and observe for leaks at supply/drain connections, abnormal noise, or unstable/loose mounting before sign-off.

Bench diagnosis in an appliance repair shop or manufacturer service center: the appliance sits on a test bench with power, water and drain hookups; the tech runs service/test modes and full cycles, observes operation, and pinpoints the leaking or loose component.

Institutional/commercial setting (apartment-complex laundry room, laundromat, hotel or hospital laundry, campus kitchen): technician runs one of a fleet of similar machines through a cycle and observes for leaking water, unbalanced drum, or loose panels amid ambient noise from other running machines.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line leak inspection of finished refrigerators. It transfers to the repairer's 'detect leaking fluid' judgment on the same object class (household refrigerators), locating leaks at specific joints, and MIRAI copes with model-to-model variation in the appliance's rear layout, the main variability a service diagnosis faces.

sources.system: Cosmo Instruments LS-R902 differential-pressure leak tester
sources.title: Leak Testing Appliances | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Automated appliance leak testers are used on fully assembled home appliances to check natural gas, propane and water line connections for leaks, and on ice makers, water dispensers, washing machines and steam-clean dryers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production leak testing of assembled appliances. It substantiates machine detection of the exact fault class the repairer looks for (leaking water or gas at appliance connections) when the appliance is presented at a purpose-built test station.

sources.system: Simcenter Anovis end-of-line NVH test system

sources.claim: A commercial end-of-line test system automatically runs products on a test bench and identifies mechanical anomalies from sound and vibration signatures within seconds, using automatically adapted limits.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vibro-acoustic end-of-line fault detection on running machines. The repairer's 'observe during operation to detect loose parts' is the same judgment - abnormal noise/vibration from a running unit - made by machine on a fixtured product at a test bench.

sources.claim: Plug-and-play end-of-line acoustic test systems are applied to home appliances such as dishwashers and washing machines, analyzing microphone and accelerometer signals during operation to flag rattling parts, worn bearings and unbalanced rotating parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acoustic quality inspection of running dishwashers and washers at a production test station. Same appliances and same fault class (rattles, loose or unbalanced parts heard during operation) as the repairer's observation, with the appliance fixtured at a machine-built station.

sources.system: ML-based quality-control inspection on a washing machine production line

sources.claim: Machine-learning feature extraction was applied on a washing-machine production line to detect units with mechanical defects or incorrect assembly from measured signals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of mechanically defective or mis-assembled washing machines on a line. Same appliance type and same 'loose parts' detection judgment, made automatically at a fixtured station.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with acoustic imager and Orbit

sources.claim: Over 1,500 Spot quadrupeds run autonomous inspection missions in industrial facilities, using acoustic imagers to find air leaks and ultrasonic inspection of rotating equipment to flag early bearing failures, with missions planned and alerts triaged remotely in Orbit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous walking inspection of operating equipment for leaks and abnormal noise inside a human work facility. It shows E2-tier leak/noise sensing, but only on pre-registered industrial assets already running; Spot does not operate appliances, open panels, or localize a specific appliance fault.

sources.transferJustification: Cited to document the absence of autonomous in-home mobile manipulation and inspection, which is why the E3 (private home) instances are not supported at their own tier.

tasks.label: Refer to schematic drawings, product manuals, and troubleshooting guides to diagnose and repair problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-home service call on a refrigerator that is not cooling: technician pulls the unit out, reads the wiring diagram/tech sheet stored behind the kickplate and the manufacturer's service manual on a tablet, probes the compressor start relay, thermistors and control board with a multimeter, replaces the failed component, reassembles and verifies cooling.

In-home washer or dryer repair (no drain, no spin, no heat): technician looks up the model's troubleshooting flowchart and error codes, removes the cabinet/front panel, tests drain pump, door switch, thermal fuse or belt per the schematic, swaps the defective part, reassembles and runs a test cycle in a cluttered laundry closet or basement.

In-home range, oven, dishwasher or gas appliance repair: technician retrieves the service manual for the error code, checks igniter/valve/heating element or control board per the schematic (including gas-leak and continuity checks), replaces the part in a tight built-in cabinet space, and verifies safe operation.

Bench repair at an appliance service shop or manufacturer service depot: customer-dropped small appliance, microwave, vacuum or a removed control board is diagnosed on the bench against the schematic, components are tested and desoldered/replaced or modules swapped, and the unit is function-tested before return.

Service call at an institutional or commercial site (laundromat, apartment-complex laundry room, nursing-home or campus kitchen): standardized coin-op washers or commercial ranges, service manual and diagnostic mode consulted, component tested and replaced on site with the facility staff controlling access.

It shares the objects (washers, microwaves, A/Cs) and tool use, but covers only teardown for material recovery: no schematic-guided fault diagnosis, no electrical testing, no part replacement and reassembly to a working, accepted repair. It therefore does not substantiate completion of this task at any tier.
