tasks.label: Trace electrical circuits, following diagrams, and conduct tests with circuit testers and other equipment to locate shorts and grounds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a customer's home: washer or dryer that won't start or won't heat. Tech pulls the unit out, removes the rear/console panel, finds the wiring diagram tucked inside the cabinet, and ohms out the door switch, thermostats, thermal fuse and heating element, checking each leg for continuity and for a short to the chassis. Cramped access, dusty cabinet, live 120/240 V.

In a customer's home: refrigerator, dishwasher or range with an intermittent or no-cool/no-heat fault. Tech follows the ladder diagram to the control board, measures supply and output voltages at board terminals, checks compressor/motor windings and defrost or bake-element circuits for winding-to-ground shorts, and isolates the faulty leg of the harness.

Bench work in a repair shop or parts depot: a customer-dropped small appliance (microwave, dryer control console) or a returned control board is placed on the bench; tech traces the printed circuit and harness against the schematic with a meter to find a shorted trace, burned relay or grounded winding before ordering/quoting the repair.

Institutional/commercial site: coin laundry, apartment laundry room, nursing-home kitchen or hotel. Tech diagnoses a commercial washer, dryer or range in place — tracing the machine's control circuit against the diagram, checking contactors, timers and heating circuits with a meter for shorts and grounds, often on a 208/240 V three-wire supply, while the facility stays open.

No-power complaint in a home where the fault may be upstream of the appliance: tech checks the receptacle voltage and polarity, tests the cord and plug, verifies the ground path back to the panel, and checks the breaker/GFCI before condemning the appliance. The 'circuit' under test is the building's wiring, not a removable assembly.

sources.system: SPEA 4050 S2 Flying Probe Tester
sources.title: 4050 Automatic 4x Flying Probe Tester - Multi-Function - SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA's 4050 S2 flying probe tester is a commercial machine whose motorized probes automatically move to programmed test points on an assembled board and run in-circuit and 100% short-circuit tests, generating its test program automatically from CAD or from the board itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-circuit fault localization on electronic assemblies. The machine performs exactly the measurement act the repairer performs (probe defined circuit nodes, compare against the netlist/diagram, report shorts and opens) on the same class of hardware found inside modern appliances (control boards), in a fixtured purpose-built cell.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating shorts on populated circuit assemblies. Same measurement objective (find shorts/grounds against a known circuit map) with comparable precision on appliance-grade electronics, in a machine-built test environment.

tasks.label: Replace worn and defective parts such as switches, bearings, transmissions, belts, gears, circuit boards, or defective wiring.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-home service call on a washer or dryer: pull the machine from a tight laundry alcove, disconnect power/water/vent, remove the cabinet or front panel (varied screws, clips, spring-loaded hooks, sometimes corroded), and replace a mechanical part — drive belt, pump, motor coupler, drum rollers or tub bearings, lid/door switch — then reassemble, level and test-run the machine in the customer's home.

In-home refrigerator or freezer repair: pull the unit out, remove interior panels or rear access covers, and replace an electrical part — main control board, defrost thermostat/heater, evaporator or condenser fan motor, start relay, or a chafed/burnt wiring harness segment — reconnecting multi-pin connectors and routing wire, then verify cooling operation.

In-home range, oven, cooktop or dishwasher repair: work under a counter or behind a slide-in range, replace an oven igniter, gas valve, thermostat/switch, element, dishwasher circulation pump or wiring, including breaking and remaking a gas or water connection and leak/function testing before leaving.

Bench repair at a service shop or manufacturer depot: the appliance (or a removed module) arrives at the shop, is set on a bench or lift, diagnosed, and the defective switch, board, motor, gear or belt is replaced and the unit reassembled and tested before customer pickup; models vary widely, units arrive dirty and worn.

Route service at a commercial or institutional site — laundromat, apartment/dorm laundry room, hotel or small commercial kitchen — replacing belts, motors, coin/card mechanisms, switches, timers or control boards on a fleet of largely standardized machines in a facility controlled by the operator.

tasks.label: Disassemble appliances so that problems can be diagnosed and repairs can be made.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a customer's home laundry area or basement: pull a clothes washer or dryer away from the wall, remove the top panel/rear service panel, console screws and front panel clips of a specific brand/model to expose the pump, belt, motor, switches and wiring so the fault can be found and the part replaced; cramped, varied placement, hidden clips, mixed fasteners.

In a customer's kitchen: open up a refrigerator/freezer — remove the rear machine-compartment cover over the compressor/condenser, the toe/kick plate, and interior panels such as the evaporator cover, fan shroud or ice-maker assembly — to reach the failed component; requires reaching into a cabinet interior and working around shelves, food and cabinetry.

In a customer's kitchen: disassemble a gas or electric range/oven/cooktop — lift burner grates and caps, raise or remove the cooktop, pull the rear control panel and oven door, expose igniters, valves, bake elements and the control board — with a live gas line and enclosed installation between cabinets.

In a customer's kitchen: disassemble a built-in dishwasher, over-range microwave or disposal — remove toe/access panels, drop the unit from the counter or wall, split the door panel or sump housing — working low, overhead or in a tight cabinet cutout with plumbing and electrical attached.

Deep component-level teardown for a major repair: splitting a front-load washer's outer tub for bearings/spider, removing a dryer drum and bulkhead, or opening a refrigerator's sealed system area — many nested fasteners, springs, clamps, harness connectors and heavy sub-assemblies that must come apart non-destructively and go back together.

Institutional or shop setting: bench teardown of an appliance brought into a service shop, or opening coin-op washers/dryers and commercial units in an apartment-complex laundry room, laundromat or facility kitchen where a fixed layout and standard machines are maintained by the operator.

The physical operation an appliance repairer performs to gain diagnostic access — locating and backing out varied screws on a dirty appliance and lifting off a sheet-metal cover over a compressor/heat exchanger — is the same operation, on the same class of objects, at the same precision; it is performed here on a fixtured plant line (E1).

tasks.label: Respond to emergency calls for problems such as gas leaks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential gas-smell emergency: dispatched same-hour to a private house where the customer smells gas near a range, gas dryer, or water heater. Technician enters an unfamiliar kitchen/utility space, sniffs and sweeps with a combustible-gas detector and soap solution, pulls the appliance out from the wall, finds the leaking flex connector, union, or gas valve, shuts off the supply, replaces/re-seals the fitting, leak-tests, relights pilots, and either restores service or red-tags the appliance and advises the utility.

Residential electrical emergency: burning smell, sparking, smoke, or tripped breaker from a range, dryer, dishwasher, or microwave in an occupied home. Technician cuts power, disassembles the appliance in place (often in a cramped alcove), identifies the failed element, terminal block, wiring harness, or control board, replaces or disconnects it, tests, and makes the appliance safe.

Residential water emergency: burst washer inlet hose, leaking dishwasher, or fridge ice-maker line flooding a floor. Technician shuts the supply valve, moves the appliance over wet flooring, replaces hose/valve/pump/seal, runs a test cycle, checks for further leaks, and cleans up.

Multi-unit property emergency dispatched by a property manager or landlord after hours: gas or electrical odor reported in an apartment unit. Technician gets keyed access to an unfamiliar cluttered occupied unit, sometimes coordinating with the utility or fire department who have already shut the meter, isolates the offending appliance, repairs or replaces the fitting/component, and documents the call.

Emergency call at a commercial or institutional site with the same appliance classes: laundromat or care-facility laundry room with a leaking gas dryer, small commercial kitchen with a leaking range connector, or building laundry room. Site is maintained by an institution with fixed layout and standard equipment; technician isolates gas, locates the leak, repairs the fitting or valve, leak-tests, and returns equipment to service.

sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped, carrying a combustible-gas payload, autonomously runs inspection missions at a 40-acre midstream gas plant, detecting and reporting gas leaks — detection and reporting only, with no repair or fitting-level intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous gas-leak surveying in an industrial plant. It covers only the detection step of an emergency gas call; it does not include diagnosing an appliance, disassembling it, or replacing a leaking fitting, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous leak detection in oil-and-gas and process plants. Transfer fails for repair: no manipulation of appliance gas fittings, no disassembly, no leak-test-and-restore step is demonstrated.

tasks.label: Reassemble units after repairs are made, making adjustments and cleaning and lubricating parts as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-home service call on a washer or dryer: after replacing a drain pump, belt, heating element or door switch, the tech refits the component, reconnects wire-harness plugs and hoses, remounts the front/rear panel and control console with a dozen screws and clips, wipes lint/debris, lubricates the drum bearing or hinge, then runs a test cycle in a cramped laundry closet or basement.

In-home refrigerator/freezer reassembly after a fan-motor, defrost-heater or icemaker repair: reinstall evaporator cover and insulation, reconnect harness connectors, replace shelves, drawers and liner trim, rehang the door and seat the gasket, grease hinges, and check door alignment and seal before restarting the unit.

In-home range, oven, cooktop or dishwasher reassembly: refit control panel and knobs, reinstall igniters/elements and burner grates or spray arms, rehang a spring-hinged door, adjust latch/door alignment and leveling, clean spilled grease off refitted parts, and verify safe operation (gas/water leak check).

Bench reassembly in the shop of an appliance or module brought in (microwave, vacuum, small motor, control assembly, washer transmission): parts laid out on the bench, housings degreased, bearings cleaned and lubricated, casing screwed together, then bench-tested.

Reassembly of an old, heavily soiled or non-standard unit: corroded or stripped fasteners, brittle clips, missing hardware substituted, caked lint/grease requiring cleaning before parts will seat, and improvised adjustments (shimming, retensioning, re-routing wiring) judged on the spot in a home or apartment laundry room.

instances.label: Leak check on a gas range/cooktop connection in a customer's private home after installing or repairing the appliance: pull the range from the wall, open the shutoff, brush leak-detection solution or run an electronic combustible-gas detector over the flare fittings, flexible connector and manifold, tighten and retest any fitting that shows bubbles.

Leak check on a gas clothes dryer or gas water heater hookup in a home basement, garage or laundry closet: verify the flex connector, shutoff valve and union joints are tight and leak-free in a cramped, cluttered space, often with poor lighting and awkward access behind the appliance.

Determining gas pressure and flow on a household gas appliance: remove the pressure-tap plug on the appliance gas valve, attach a manometer hose, fire the burner, read inlet and manifold pressure, adjust the regulator, and/or clock the gas meter to confirm burner input rate; then reseal the tap and leak-test it.

'I smell gas' service call in an occupied home: survey the interior gas piping runs, appliance connections, meter/regulator and basement or crawlspace with a combustible-gas detector to find and pinpoint the leak source, ruling out appliances one by one.

Gas leak and pressure testing of appliances in a commercial/institutional facility controlled by an operator - restaurant kitchen range or fryer, apartment-building laundry room dryers, school cafeteria equipment: sniff the connections and hard piping for leaks and take manifold pressure readings on the equipment in place.

instances.label: In-home service call on an older residential gas range/cooktop: pull the range out, lift the cooktop or remove burner grates, relight and adjust the standing pilot(s) or ignition pilot, clean clogged burner ports, set air shutters until the flame is the specified blue cone, and soap-test the manifold and valve connections. In-home installation or reconnection of a gas range/cooktop: connect the flexible line, pressure/soap test the fittings and shutoff for leakage, light each burner and the oven, verify ignition and specified flame, convert orifices for LP if required.

In-home gas dryer or built-in wall oven: operate the appliance, confirm the burner ignites and burns with the specified flame, check the thermocouple/flame sensor cut-in, and leak-check the shutoff and appliance gas connection.

Customer reports a gas odor: technician inspects the stove's valves, taps, manifold and connections with combustible-gas detector and soap solution to find and localize leakage, then repairs or shuts off and tags the appliance.

Shop/bench work at the repair company's premises: a gas cooktop, range top or gas valve/burner assembly is hooked to a bench gas supply, lit, adjusted to the specified flame, and leak tested before being returned to the customer.

Service visit in an institution-controlled facility (apartment complex maintenance program, cafeteria or light-commercial kitchen): relight and adjust standing pilots on facility ranges, verify burner flames, and leak-check valves after a gas shutoff or seasonal restart.

Periodic cycle count / inventory audit of shop stock: walk the stockroom shelving, count and verify bin contents against the inventory record, flag items below reorder point, and place replenishment orders.

End-of-day van inventory check in the yard or a customer driveway: count what remains in the van's bins, strip packaging and used/defective parts out of the van, and restage the parts needed for tomorrow's calls inside the cramped, non-standard van interior.

Self-employed or small-shop repairer maintaining parts stock in a home garage or basement shop: unbox mail-order parts, shelve them on improvised racking, keep a running want list, and salvage reusable parts off scrapped machines.

tasks.label: Level refrigerators, adjust doors, and connect water lines to water pipes for ice makers and water dispensers, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New refrigerator delivered to a customer's private home: technician walks it into the kitchen alcove, adjusts the threaded leveling legs/rollers front-to-back and side-to-side so the unit is level and tilted slightly back, checks door gaps and alignment and adjusts hinges/handles, connects the 1/4 in. supply tubing to the under-sink or wall shutoff with a compression fitting, purges the line, checks for leaks and runs the ice maker.

Service call at a private home on an installed refrigerator: doors sag, gaskets don't seal, doors won't self-close or gaps are uneven. Technician re-levels the cabinet on the existing (often uneven, vinyl/tile/wood) floor, loosens and shims/adjusts hinge bolts and door stops with hand tools, and verifies seal and gap by eye and dollar-bill test.

Home ice maker/water dispenser supply work: no existing water line, so the technician taps the cold-water supply (saddle valve or tee at a stop valve), routes copper or braided tubing through cabinet backs, floor or crawlspace to the fridge, makes up compression/quick-connect fittings at both ends, flushes and leak-checks.

Install/adjust in an institution-controlled facility: apartment-complex unit turnover, office breakroom, hotel suite or dorm kitchenette with standardized appliance models and repeatable layouts; level the unit, align doors, connect the ice-maker line to the existing stub-out.

Built-in, counter-depth or panel-ready refrigerator in custom cabinetry in a home: precise leveling and shimming to the cabinet opening, mounting and aligning decorative door panels/handles so gaps and reveals match the cabinetry, then routing and connecting the water line in the tight cabinet chase.

tasks.label: Observe and test operation of appliances following installation, and make any initial installation adjustments that are necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private home kitchen, newly delivered refrigerator: after the unit is set in its alcove, the repairer levels the cabinet with a wrench/nut driver, verifies the water supply connection for the ice maker/dispenser, runs water through and checks the saddle valve and fittings for drips, confirms compressor start-up and cooling, checks that doors close and seal and adjusts hinge/door-alignment screws, and sets control temperatures before leaving.

Private home laundry area, newly installed washer and/or dryer: shipping bolts removed, machine leveled on an uneven floor, a short test cycle run to check fill, drain, agitation/tumble and spin for leaks at hose connections, excessive vibration or 'walking'; dryer heat, airflow and vent connection verified; leveling feet re-adjusted and door swing reversed if required.

Private home kitchen, gas range, cooktop or wall oven just connected: soap-solution or detector leak check of the gas connection, verify each surface burner and the oven igniter light properly, inspect flame color/size and adjust the low-flame setting or air shutter, run bake/broil and check temperature calibration, confirm the appliance is level and the anti-tip bracket engaged.

Private home, built-in dishwasher or under-counter appliance just installed: run a full or diagnostic cycle, watch fill, wash, drain and heated-dry, check under the sink and around the tub for leaks at supply and drain connections, adjust leveling legs and door-spring tension so the door aligns flush with cabinet fronts and latches, verify no rubbing on countertop or panels.

Institution-controlled facility (laundromat, apartment-building common laundry, hotel, nursing home or small commercial kitchen): newly installed commercial washers, dryers, ice machines or ranges are test-run, water/gas connections checked for leaks, coin/card or control settings verified, machines leveled and anchored, cycle times and temperatures adjusted before turnover to the operator.

It does not transfer to this task: the demonstrated skills are grasping and placing household objects, with no closed-loop diagnostic testing of an appliance's operation (leak, flame, vibration, temperature checks) and no wrench/screwdriver adjustment of leveling feet, hinges or gas shutters at worker reliability.

tasks.label: Set appliance thermostats, and check to ensure that they are functioning properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-home service call on a refrigerator/freezer: tech sets the cold-control dial or electronic temperature control to the specified setting, confirms the compressor starts and cycles, places/reads a thermometer in the fresh-food and freezer compartments, and confirms the cabinet pulls down to spec before leaving. Kitchen is cluttered; the unit is often boxed in by cabinetry.

In-home oven/range calibration: tech measures actual cavity temperature against the set point with a thermocouple or oven thermometer, then adjusts the hydraulic thermostat's calibration screw behind the pulled-off knob or enters an offset on the electronic control panel, re-runs a heat-up cycle, and verifies the corrected temperature.

In-home dryer (or washer) thermostat work after a heating complaint: tech pulls the rear/front access panel, checks cycling thermostat and hi-limit continuity/resistance with a multimeter, replaces or resets as needed, reassembles, then runs a heat cycle and verifies outlet air temperature and cut-out/cut-in behavior.

Bench work in the employer's appliance repair shop: a customer unit or a swapped-out control is on the bench after a thermostat/temperature-sensor replacement; tech sets the control, powers the unit on the test rig, and verifies switching temperatures and cycling before the unit is returned.

On-site work at an institutional/commercial customer (restaurant reach-in and prep-table refrigeration, apartment-building laundry room, school kitchen oven): tech sets the thermostat to the required food-safety or process temperature and verifies the unit holds it, documenting the readings for the facility.

sources.claim: MATT, a commercial test-automation robot, physically actuates appliance controls on a fixtured device under test, including rotating the main program knob of a washing machine and operating buttons, switches and knobs, replacing manual human input during test sequences.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic actuation of an appliance's temperature/program control on a fixtured bench. It covers the 'set the thermostat/control' half of this task with the same objects (household appliance dials and control panels) at the same precision, in a purpose-built test setup.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated actuation of appliance control knobs and switches. Same class of controls a repairer sets on a thermostat dial or control panel, performed unattended on a fixtured unit.

sources.claim: A commercial 10-station automated bench thermally cycles refrigerator thermostats under electrical load and automatically verifies their switching set points and contact behaviour, i.e. determines whether the thermostat is functioning to specification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine verification that a thermostat switches at its set temperature. This is the 'check to ensure it is functioning properly' half of the task, on the identical component, in a purpose-built fixtured bench.

sources.title: Figure Launches Humanoid Robot Upgrade Helix 02 for Full-Body Autonomy
sources.claim: A humanoid robot autonomously performed a multi-minute kitchen sequence including unloading, reloading and starting a dishwasher in a full-sized ...; the demonstration involves operating an appliance's start control but no thermostat calibration or temperature verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous appliance operation in a home-like kitchen. It is cited to show the frontier of unstructured-setting appliance interaction; it does not include dial calibration, instrumented temperature measurement, or pass/fail judgement, so it does not substantiate E3 here.

tasks.label: Install appliances such as refrigerators, washing machines, and stoves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Install a washer and/or dryer in a customer's home laundry closet, basement or second-floor laundry room: uncrate the unit, wheel or carry it (often down/up stairs, through tight doorways), remove shipping bolts, thread hot/cold inlet hoses onto the wall valves and the machine ports with rubber washers, route the drain hose into a standpipe or laundry tub, connect or vent the dryer, level the feet on an out-of-level floor, plug in, run a test cycle and check for leaks or vibration, and haul away the old unit.

Install/replace a refrigerator in a home kitchen: maneuver it through doorways (sometimes removing doors, handles or trim), position it in a cabinet cutout, connect the 1/4-inch water supply line for the icemaker/dispenser to an existing shutoff, level and adjust doors so they seal and align with cabinetry, plug in, and verify cooling and ice/water production before leaving.

Install a freestanding electric range or cooktop in a home: slide the unit into the cabinet opening, attach the 3- or 4-wire pigtail cord to the terminal block or hardwire it, secure the anti-tip bracket into the floor or wall, level the unit flush with the counter, and test elements, oven and controls.

Install a freestanding gas range in a home: shut off the gas, fit the flexible gas connector with adapters and thread sealant to the range and the shutoff valve, tighten the flare fittings with two wrenches, leak-test the joints (soap solution or gas detector), install the anti-tip bracket, plug in the 120 V cord, level the range, and light and test all burners and the oven.

Install a built-in appliance in a home: an under-counter dishwasher, an over-the-range microwave, a wall oven, or a built-in cooktop. Requires fitting the unit into an existing cabinet opening that may be out of square, drilling/anchoring mounting brackets (often overhead or into studs), connecting water supply and drain hose to the disposal, and making the electrical connection at a junction box or receptacle in a confined space, then testing.

Batch installation of identical appliances for a property manager or builder in a managed multi-unit building (apartment complex turnover, dorm or condo laundry rooms): repeated same-model washer/dryer, range and refrigerator hookups in units of standardized layout, with building staff controlling access, elevators and utility shutoffs.

sources.transferJustification: Related tasks: multi-step assembly with tools and cable/connector insertion in cramped spaces - the core skills of an on-site appliance install. The assessment establishes that these are not yet autonomous outside environments designed around the robot.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household manipulation in private homes, the setting of most appliance installs. Its teleoperated status shows no autonomous in-home mobile manipulator is available to do install work at E3.

tasks.label: Level washing machines and connect hoses to water pipes, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New washer delivered to a single-family house: technician walks it into a basement, garage or laundry room on a dolly, slides it into the alcove, threads hot and cold inlet hoses onto the wall shutoff valves (rubber washers, hand-tighten plus pliers/wrench), routes the drain hose into a standpipe or laundry tub, then turns the threaded leveling feet with a wrench while checking a spirit level on an often sloped or uneven concrete/wood floor, rocking the cabinet to verify no walk.

Apartment, condo or townhouse laundry closet or stacked unit: very tight enclosure, hookups (often a recessed washer box with valves) directly behind the machine, minimal clearance to reach hoses or feet; technician must connect hoses partly blind and level the machine while it is wedged in the closet.

Service call on an already installed washer: machine walks, vibrates or leaks. Technician pulls the machine out from the wall, shuts the valves, inspects/tightens or replaces the inlet hoses on the pipe spigots and machine inlets, checks the drain hose, then re-levels the cabinet with wrench and level and re-tests the spin cycle in the customer's home.

Multi-family common laundry room, laundromat, dormitory or nursing-home laundry: a row of machines on a curbed or drained floor with a bank of supply valves; technician installs or swaps several machines, connects inlet hoses to the shared supply pipes and drains, and levels each unit; premises controlled by the property or operator.

Retail store display floor or warehouse/test bay setup: hooking a washer to a demo or test water supply and drain, connecting hoses to prepared pipe stubs and leveling the unit on a flat, prepared floor in an institution-controlled facility.

sources.system: KUKA KR AGILUS screwdriving robot station (integrator Qbig)
sources.title: Automatic screwing of washing machine doors with a robot | KUKA Global
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic station using a KUKA KR AGILUS screwdriving robot performs torque-controlled threaded fastening on washing machines on a sub-assembly line at a major household-appliance manufacturer, i.e., threaded joints made autonomously on fixtured washer cabinets in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic threaded fastening on washing machines in a fixtured production cell. It transfers to the hose-coupling and leveling-foot half of this task because both are threaded joints on a washing machine made to a torque target with the workpiece held in a known position; it does not transfer to home settings, where the machine is unfixtured.

sources.system: Outrider TrailerConnect robotic arm

sources.claim: Outrider's TrailerConnect system mounts Yaskawa Motoman robot arms on autonomous yard trucks that locate and autonomously connect and disconnect pressurized air brake hoses and electrical lines to unmodified trailers in freight distribution yards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously mating a flexible pressurized hose end to a fluid coupling. It transfers to 'connect hoses to water pipes' in the sense of gripping a deformable hose and seating its coupling on a fitting under vision, but the couplings are quick-connect glad hands on a truck-mounted arm, not threaded fittings reached in a cramped domestic alcove.

sources.system: Fori Automation robotic wheel aligner / robotic toe set stations
sources.title: End of Line Testing Systems – Wheel Aligners, Headlamp Aimers, Robotic Toe Set & Automated Tooling Changeover
sources.claim: Automotive end-of-line stations use robotic wheel aligners with nut-runner gear heads that measure vehicle geometry and then turn threaded adjusters in a closed loop until the measured setting is within tolerance (toe set to +/- 0.03 degrees).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop geometric adjustment of a product by turning threaded adjusters against sensor feedback. Leveling a washer is the same loop (measure inclination, turn threaded feet, re-measure) and the same class of tool, but demonstrated only on vehicles held in a purpose-built end-of-line station.

sources.system: Robotiq Screwdriving Workcell / Screwdriving Solution
sources.title: Screwdriving Solution | Robotiq
sources.claim: Commercially sold robotic screwdriving workcells perform high-volume torque-controlled threaded fastening in industrial workcells, replacing manual fastening at scale (over a million screws per year at one deployment).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous threaded fastening with controlled torque in a fixtured workcell. It supports the E1 counterfactual for starting and torquing hose couplings and leveling feet when the workpiece and fasteners are presented in known positions; it says nothing about unfixtured, in-home work.

tasks.label: Clean and reinstall parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-home laundry appliance service: technician kneels in a basement, closet or stacked-unit alcove, removes the cabinet/front panel of an unfamiliar washer or dryer model, pulls the lint-caked blower housing, exhaust duct, drain-pump filter or drum baffles, brushes/vacuums out lint, hair and detergent sludge, refits the part with its gasket and fasteners, reassembles the cabinet and runs a test cycle.

In-home refrigeration service: technician pulls the unit from a tight surround, removes the kick plate, rear access panel, evaporator cover and fan shroud, cleans condenser coils, blocked defrost drain and fan blades of dust and grease, then reinstalls covers, shelves and drawers and verifies cooling.

In-home cooking or dishwashing appliance service: technician lifts grates and burner caps on a range, clears clogged burner ports and igniters, or removes a dishwasher filter, spray arm and sump cover, degreases baked-on soil and food debris, and refits the parts and panels in a customer kitchen with varied clearances and finishes.

Shop-bench repair: the appliance or a removed subassembly (drain pump, drive motor, gas valve, blower wheel, control housing) is on the bench in the company's repair shop, where the technician degreases/descales it in a parts washer or by hand, replaces seals, reinstalls it in the unit and function-tests before return to the customer.

Institutional/commercial-site service: technician services a standardized fleet in a laundromat, apartment-complex laundry room, hotel or commercial kitchen - opening coin-op washers and dryers, clearing lint chambers, pump filters and coin traps, cleaning ice-machine and dishmachine components, and reinstalling panels on premises controlled by the operator.

sources.system: Panasonic automatic dismantling system for air conditioner outdoor unit covers (with PETEC Kanto, Mitsubishi Materials)
sources.title: Panasonic Develops an Automatic Dismantling System for Covers of Air Conditioner Outdoor Units to Improve the Recycling Process of Home Appliances
sources.claim: Panasonic operates an AI-guided robotic dismantling line at a home-appliance recycling plant that autonomously locates screws on dirty or rusted used air-conditioner outdoor units and removes screws and covers; it is one-way teardown for recycling, with no cleaning or reinstallation of parts, and Panasonic calls it partial automation.
sources.transferJustification: Closest industrial analogue on the same objects (used household appliances, dirty and corroded fasteners) in a purpose-built cell. It substantiates autonomous fastener/cover removal only; it does not clean removed components or reinstall them into a working appliance, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task even at E1.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic disassembly of consumer electronics in a laboratory cell. sources.claim: Trade coverage of remanufacturing automation describes component cleaning as a comparatively mature automated stage (washing, blasting, chemical treatment) but presents robotic disassembly as only beginning to emerge, and names no deployed system that autonomously performs the disassemble-clean-reinstall chain on a used product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial remanufacturing of used cores, which shares the clean-and-refit motif. No specific named system is credited with autonomous removal, cleaning and reinstallation of a part, so this item documents the gap rather than substantiating completion.

sources.system: 1X NEO home humanoid

sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household manipulation in private homes, the setting of most instances of this task. Since even simple chores require teleoperation, tool-based disassembly, part cleaning and refitting in homes is not substantiated.

tasks.label: Clean, lubricate, and touch up minor defects on newly installed or repaired appliances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a customer's home, after repairing a washer/dryer or dishwasher in a cramped laundry closet or basement: wipe down the cabinet and control panel, vacuum lint and debris from around and under the machine, lubricate door hinges, latch and bearings, and touch up a chipped or scratched painted spot on the cabinet before leaving.

In a customer's kitchen after installing a new refrigerator, range or dishwasher: peel protective film and remove adhesive residue, clean fingerprints/shipping dust from stainless and glass, lubricate and adjust a door hinge or gasket, and touch up a shipping scuff with a paint pen, working around cabinets, flooring and household clutter.

Bench finishing in an appliance service shop: a repaired unit (microwave, vacuum, small appliance, or a removed motor/transmission assembly) sits on a bench; the repairer degreases it, re-lubricates motor bearings, gears and slides to spec, wipes it down and touches up minor paint/finish defects before returning it to the customer.

At an institutional site — apartment-complex laundry room, laundromat, hotel or dorm — after servicing standardized commercial washers/dryers: clean cabinets and lint paths, lubricate hinges and rollers, and touch up chipped enamel on machines lined up along a wall in a facility whose premises are controlled by the owner.

On a refurbisher's or retailer's detailing line in a warehouse: scratch-and-dent or returned appliances are cleaned inside and out, moving parts lubricated, and dents/scratches sanded, polished and touched up with paint before the unit is resold, with units staged in a row and handled by pallet jack or conveyor.

tasks.label: Conserve, recover, and recycle refrigerants used in cooling systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-home sealed-system repair of a household refrigerator/freezer: technician pulls the unit from its cabinet cavity in a kitchen, brazes on a process-tube adapter or clamps a piercing valve, hooks up manifold, recovery machine and DOT recovery cylinder, recovers the whole charge without venting, and after the repair evacuates to deep vacuum and recharges to nameplate weight.

Shop bench work: a wine cooler, undercounter ice maker, small freezer or window A/C brought into the repair shop; technician recovers the charge into a cylinder on the bench, makes the sealed-system repair, then evacuates and weighs in a new charge, logging the amounts.

Evacuating refrigerant from an appliance condemned during a service call, at the customer's home or at the truck, before haul-away: attach piercing valve to the process tube, pull the charge to the EPA-required level, cap/tag the unit for disposal.

Batch recovery at the employer's warehouse/depot or an appliance recycling drop-off: dozens of hauled-away refrigerators, freezers and room air conditioners de-gassed one after another before scrapping, using a recovery machine or degassing station and bulk recovery cylinders.

Refrigerant inventory and cylinder management in the shop or van: transferring recovered refrigerant into DOT-approved recovery cylinders without exceeding 80% fill, weighing and labeling, purging non-condensables or running refrigerant through a recycling machine, and staging cylinders for shipment to a certified reclaimer with records.

sources.title: Automatic degassing - ATN Engineering Stadskanaal
sources.claim: ATN Engineering (ANDRITZ Group) sells a fully automatic degassing unit for end-of-life refrigerator compressors: the compressor is automatically positioned, then drilled, degassed and drained of oil by a patented automatic drill-head, with recovered refrigerant routed to collection and gas treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Same operation as the task's recovery step — extracting refrigerant (and oil) from a household cooling appliance's sealed circuit — performed on end-of-life units rather than units being repaired.

sources.system: ATN automatic degassing system (patented automatic drill-head)
sources.title: Automatic degassing - ATN Engineering Stadskanaal
sources.claim: The same ATN automatic degassing equipment reports 99.5% gas and oil collection efficiency, machine-regulated collecting-tank pressure, gas/oil separation and qualification for flammable refrigerants, i.e. capture completeness comparable to a certified technician's recovery.
sources.transferJustification: Output-quality evidence for the same refrigerant-recovery operation on domestic refrigeration circuits.

sources.system: ATN degassing units within ANDRITZ refrigerator recycling plants
sources.title: Recycling plants for refrigerators | ANDRITZ
sources.claim: ATN degassing units are widely installed in refrigerator recycling plants worldwide (more than 200 units delivered), performing the cooling-circuit oil and refrigerant extraction stage.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment context for the degassing machinery cited above; same appliance refrigerant-recovery step at industrial scale.

sources.system: ANDRITZ encapsulated single-stage refrigerator recycling plant with matrix degassing
sources.title: ANDRITZ successfully starts up refrigerator recycling plant at EMP Recycling UAB, Lithuania
sources.claim: ANDRITZ commissioned a fully encapsulated refrigerator recycling plant at EMP Recycling UAB (Lithuania) that processes cooling appliances continuously and recovers the environmentally harmful gases they contain, including matrix degassing of the insulation foam.
sources.transferJustification: Same purpose as the task's recover-and-recycle step for scrapped cooling appliances, executed by continuously running plant machinery rather than a technician.

sources.system: ATN fridge turner handling system for refrigerator degassing
sources.title: New handling system for refrigerator degassing - ATN Engineering
sources.claim: In ATN's standard whole-refrigerator degassing line the machine positions the appliance ('fridge turner') but a human operator still connects the drill-head to the compressor, showing the coupling-to-sealed-system step is not automated in whole-appliance degassing.
sources.transferJustification: Directly bounds the automation: attaching recovery equipment to an appliance's sealed system remains a manual step even in purpose-built degassing lines.

sources.system: VTech MRC-HC Automatic Evacuation and Refrigerant Charging System
sources.title: Refrigerant Charging Equipment for Domestic Refrigeration - VTECH
sources.claim: Factory equipment for domestic refrigeration automates the vacuum, vacuum-decay leak test and weighed refrigerant charging cycle for newly built units; it is a charging/evacuation station, with no recovery of an existing charge from a used appliance described.
sources.transferJustification: Closest factory analogue to service-side recovery/recharge; cited to show the automated function covers charging new units, not recovering charge from a repairable appliance.

sources.system: EVST robotic refrigerant charging / dosing cell
sources.title: Robotic Refrigerant Charging with Vision Error-Proofing
sources.claim: A robot integrator markets vision-guided robotic refrigerant charging cells in which the robot seats a nozzle on a charge port and doses with closed-loop weighing, but the source is vendor how-to guidance with no named deployment and covers filling, not recovery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic refrigerant filling) examined for transfer to service recovery; judged insufficient because no named deployment is given and it does not cover recovering an existing charge into a cylinder.

tasks.label: Install gas pipes and water lines to connect appliances to existing gas lines or plumbing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gas range or gas dryer hookup in an occupied single-family home: shut off the existing gas cock, apply pipe dope/PTFE to adapter nipples, thread and torque a CSA-approved flexible connector between the appliance inlet and the wall stub, work behind/under the appliance in a cramped kitchen or laundry alcove, then bubble- or sniffer-test every joint and light the burners.

Refrigerator ice-maker/water-dispenser line in a home: tap or use an existing cold-water supply (under-sink stop or basement branch), route 1/4 in. copper or braided PEX tubing through cabinets/floor/behind the fridge, make compression connections at both ends, open the valve, purge and check for drips.

Washer hose hookup or dishwasher water supply plus drain connection in a home: thread braided fill hoses onto hot/cold hose bibbs behind a washer, or connect a 3/8 in. compression supply to the dishwasher inlet elbow and clamp the drain hose to a disposer/air gap while lying inside a cramped under-sink cabinet.

Appliance water/gas connection in an institution-controlled facility: apartment-building laundry room, dormitory or small commercial kitchen, with standardized stub-outs, valves and appliance positions, and building staff controlling access.

Extending supply: running a new short branch of black iron pipe or CSST from an existing gas line (basement, crawlspace or joist bay) to a new appliance location, including measuring, cutting/threading, hanging, multiple joints, and a code pressure test.

sources.system: KUKA LBR iiwa (dishwasher hose-connection application)
sources.title: Appliance Manufacturers Look to Robots to Boost Productivity | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A KUKA LBR iiwa collaborative robot autonomously makes a hose connection on a dishwasher in appliance assembly: it grips a hose presented by a feeder, uses joint force sensing to find the hose end, and pushes ... — the factory analogue of attaching an appliance water line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching a flexible water hose to an appliance port on a production line. Same objects (appliance fluid inlets, flexible hose), same insertion/seating precision, but with the workpiece fixtured and the hose presented by a feeder — an E1 presentation of the home hookup step.

sources.system: SDC hose assembly and test machine (FANUC SCARA, Cognex vision, CTS air leak test)
sources.title: Hose Assembly & Testing Machine for Appliance Manufacturing
sources.claim: A single fully automated machine assembles drain-hose connectors to appliance hoses (vision-verified, spin-welded) and then air-leak-tests each assembly at 15 PSI and sorts pass/fail, at 24 parts per minute, inside guarded automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining a fitting to an appliance fluid line and verifying leak-tightness. Same class of objects (appliance water/drain hoses and connectors) and the same accept criterion (no leak), performed autonomously in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Shibaura Machine SR-654-HSP SCARA fitting-assembly cell
sources.developer: TM Robotics / Shibaura Machine (UK fittings manufacturer)
sources.title: Automated valve fitting | TM Robotics | Case study
sources.claim: A three-SCARA robot cell with vision assembles multi-part pipe fittings (fitting body, lubricated nylon tube, air ring, swivel nut, swaging) and then performs a pressure-decay leak test on each finished part before sorting it into output trays, in 7.8 s per unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a pressure-tight tube-to-fitting joint and proving it leak-free. Comparable objects (compression/push-in plumbing fittings, small-diameter tubing) and precision, done autonomously with the work fixtured and fed — the E1 form of making a supply-line connection.

sources.system: UR5e cobot with Mech-Eye PRO S 3D vision / Mech-Viz (Arçelik Gebze plant)
sources.developer: Mech-Mind Robotics with Universal Robots / Arçelik
sources.title: Appliance Assembler Automates Leak Testing | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Appliance maker Arçelik runs a UR5e cobot with a sniffer probe, 3D vision and AI path planning that autonomously locates each low-pressure weld joint on air-conditioner compressors in a tangle of pipes and leak-tests it, alerting and routing faulty products for repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sniffer leak-testing of gas-carrying joints on an appliance, which is the acceptance step of a gas or water hookup. Same instrument and joint geometry, performed autonomously in a factory cell.

sources.system: PMC-Colinet CST05 coupling starter machine
sources.title: Coupling Applying Machines for Precision and Efficiency | PMC-Colinet
sources.claim: PLC-controlled coupling starter/applier machines make up threaded pipe connections automatically, with a total floating gripping head ... prevents cross-threading and controlled applying torque, on pipe from 1.9 in. to 5 in. OD.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making up a tapered threaded pipe joint to a specified torque without cross-threading — the mechanical core of connecting gas piping and adapter nipples, here performed by machine on fixtured pipe presented by the line.

sources.system: CENTAURO centaur-like mobile manipulator
sources.title: Flexible Disaster Response of Tomorrow -- Final Presentation and Evaluation of the CENTAURO System
sources.claim: In the CENTAURO disaster-response evaluation, connecting and disconnecting a fire hose to a ... — a hand-tool fluid connection closely analogous to an appliance hookup — was accomplished by an operator driving the robot through an exoskeleton, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making a sealed hose/fitting connection with a wrench in an as-found setting. It is cited as negative evidence: the state of the art outside fixtured cells remains teleoperated, so E2/E3 is not supported.

tasks.label: Take measurements to determine if appliances will fit in installation locations, performing minor carpentry work when necessary to ensure proper installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private home kitchen: measure the alcove/cutout for a replacement refrigerator, range or dishwasher — width, height, depth behind trim and baseboard, door-swing and handle clearance, plus doorway/hallway path — and determine whether the specified appliance will fit; no carpentry needed.

Private home: minor carpentry to make the appliance fit — shave/trim a cabinet stile or face frame, notch or cut back a countertop overhang or cabinet rear panel for water/gas line and plug, plane a door casing, shim and level the opening.

Private home laundry area, basement or closet: measure for a washer/dryer or stacked unit including door swing and vent path, then cut a dryer-vent or hose pass-through in wall/floor sheathing, trim closet door casing, or build a small wood platform/pedestal.

Multi-unit apartment or property-management unit turnover: standardized kitchen/laundry openings, institution controls access; measure the opening against the stock replacement appliance and do light trim work if the new model is slightly oversized.

Commercial/institutional premises (office break room, laundromat, assisted-living kitchenette): measure the millwork opening and utility clearances for a replacement appliance and make minor cabinet/trim modifications so it seats flush.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor Robotic Sub-Assembly / Robotic Framing
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic sub-assembly and framing system automatically manufactures wooden wall subcomponents, including framed rough openings, and robotically cuts and places studs and ... to precise lengths inside an offsite production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory framing of rough openings. Cutting studs and noggings to exact length and framing an opening to a required dimension are the same wood-cutting operations, on the same materials and to tighter tolerance, as building an appliance platform or framing/trimming an opening so an appliance seats.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300/M-500 multifunction bridge
sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges (brochure)
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ CNC multifunction bridges carry out all work on ... fully automatically, including formatting panels and routing out all openings (windows, doors, sockets, service pass-throughs).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic routing of openings in panel sheathing. Cutting a vent/hose or water-line pass-through and trimming panel material to size is the same class of minor carpentry cut on the same sheet materials, performed here on fixtured panels on a production line.

sources.system: Robotic timber joinery workflow (KUKA robot + Zivid 3D camera, eye-in-hand)
sources.developer: Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María (L.F. González-Böhme), published in Buildings (MDPI)
sources.title: Workpiece Coordinate System Measurement for a Robotic Timber Joinery Workflow
sources.claim: A robotic timber-joinery workflow uses a Zivid 3D camera on a KUKA industrial robot to measure the actual workpiece cross-section and coordinate frame, then dynamically updates toolpaths so cuts fit real, dimensionally variable timber.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measure-then-cut adaptive joinery. The instance's core loop — measure the as-found piece, compare with the required dimension, then trim to fit — is exactly this workflow, on wood, at millimetre precision, in a fixtured robot cell.

sources.system: Hexagon PRESTO robotic inspection cell / PRESTO System
sources.title: Hexagon revolutionises robotic quality inspection with highly flexible and scalable PRESTO System
sources.claim: Hexagon's PRESTO family are turnkey automated robotic inspection cells that take 3D dimensional measurements of parts loaded into the cell and check them against specification, deployed in automotive and aerospace plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional inspection. 'Take measurements to determine if it will fit' is a gauging decision — measure the presented enclosure and compare against a required envelope — which robotic inspection cells perform routinely to far tighter tolerance than appliance clearances.

sources.system: Hundegger ROBOT-Compact / ROBOT-Drive / ROBOT-Max joinery machines
sources.title: Main units ROB — Hundegger ROBOT-Compact
sources.claim: Hundegger's 6-axis robot joinery machines perform trimming, grooving, drilling, milling and slotting on timber fed automatically through the machine, with the manufacturer's measuring and feed management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated carpentry machining. Trimming and milling dimensional lumber and panel stock to a target size is the machine equivalent of shaving a cabinet stile or trimming a casing, performed with the workpiece fed and clamped by the machine.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Trimble X7 (and FARO Trek)
sources.title: Trimble goes laser scanning with Boston's robot dog
sources.claim: Trimble integrated its X7 3D laser ... quadruped for autonomous 3D data capture ... construction sites, giving robotic as-built dimensional capture in as-found building interiors along pre-taught routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic as-built survey. Cited here as the closest in-situ robotic measurement capability; it captures general site point clouds on taught routes and does not render an appliance-fit determination inside furnished cabinetry, nor perform any carpentry.

sources.system: Okibo EG7
sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic
sources.claim: The Okibo EG7 is a fully autonomous mobile construction robot that scans interiors in 3D and applies plaster, paint and drywall finish on interior construction sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-situ interior finishing. Shows what mobile robots do inside as-found buildings today — flat-surface finishing — and that no cited in-situ system performs dimensional fit assessment or cutting/trimming of cabinetry.

tasks.label: Measure, cut, and thread pipe, and connect it to feeder lines and equipment or appliances, using rules and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential gas appliance hookup: in a customer's home kitchen, the repairer shuts off the gas, measures the offset between the existing gas stub and the range/dryer inlet, cuts and threads a black-iron nipple (or fits a flexible connector with adapters), dopes the threads, wrenches the joint up in the tight space behind the appliance, and soap-tests for leaks.

Residential water-supply line: in a home kitchen/basement, the repairer measures, cuts copper or PEX tubing to length, adds a shutoff/saddle or compression fitting on the cold feeder line, routes the line through cabinets or floor joists, and connects it to a refrigerator ice maker or dishwasher inlet, then checks for drips under pressure.

Home laundry closet / basement washer-dryer or water-heater adjacent work: connecting supply lines and a gas or water stub to the appliance, occasionally cutting and threading a galvanized nipple or extending a short pipe run, working in a cramped closet or low-headroom basement.

Commercial or institutional premises (restaurant kitchen, hotel, apartment-building laundry room, laundromat): running and connecting code-compliant threaded black-iron gas pipe or water pipe from the building feeder line to a commercial range, dryer, or dishwasher, working around fixed equipment during facility hours.

Shop/van bench prefabrication: at the service company's shop, the repairer measures required lengths from job notes, cuts pipe in a vise, reams it, and threads the ends with a power threading machine to produce nipples/short sections for an upcoming appliance installation.

sources.system: Nabors RZR (with SmartROS) robotic rig-floor module
sources.title: Retrofit Kit Makes Robotic Drilling a Reality for Existing Rigs (JPT/SPE)
sources.claim: Nabors' RZR rig-floor robotics module autonomously makes up threaded pipe connections (screwing tubulars together to torque) on drilling rigs, with no crew member on the floor; deployed on land rigs drilling horizontal wells in the Permian ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making up a threaded pipe joint to controlled torque without human hands. It is the same physical operation as threading a nipple into a gas feeder line fitting (rigid steel tubular, tapered/threaded connection, torque-controlled make-up), performed on much larger and heavier pipe, in a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.system: Okuma LOC-650 Oil Country CNC lathe
sources.title: CNC Lathe | Oil Country | LOC-650 | Pipe Threading | Okuma
sources.claim: Commercial CNC oil-country pipe threading lathes cut and cut threads on pipe to programmed dimensions under machine control; such machines are standard equipment in pipe-processing shops and threading lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting pipe to a programmed length and cutting threads on its ends. This is the measure/cut/thread portion of the appliance task, done to tighter tolerance than NPT hand threading, but only where the pipe is chucked and presented by the machine's own fixturing.

sources.system: Synergy Automatics High-Speed Automatic Pipe Cutting & Threading Machine
sources.title: High-Speed Automatic Pipe Cutting & Threading Machine
sources.claim: High-speed automatic pipe cutting and threading machines with CNC motion control, laser-guided ... servo threading heads cut and thread pipe to programmed variable lengths and are built to integrate with robotic or conveyor feeding lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cut-to-length and thread-cutting of pipe stock. Same workpiece class (steel pipe) and same operations the repairer performs with a rule, cutter and threader, but requiring pipe to be clamped and fed by purpose-built handling.

sources.system: Automatic PTFE thread seal tape wrapping machine (models H91/H92; also 'Thred Taper')
sources.title: Automatic thread taping machine, thread tape wrapping machine, applicator
sources.claim: Automatic PTFE thread-seal tape application machines wrap sealing tape into the thread root of pipe threads and fittings in 2-3 seconds per part, used in industrial gas, LPG, water and fire-protection fitting production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying thread sealant before making a gas-tight joint — the sealing step of the repairer's connection, performed by machine on the same NPT-style threads (1/8" to 3").

sources.system: Durulsan Automatic Valve Screwing Machine (LPG cylinder line); MAKEEN valve changing machine
sources.title: Valve Screwing Machine Automatic - Durulsan Lpg
sources.claim: Automatic valve screwing machines on LPG cylinder lines screw and unscrew threaded cylinder valves into cylinder necks hydraulically at a set torque, as an in-line station on the production/filling conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: threading a tapered-thread gas component into a gas-carrying port to a controlled torque so the joint is gas-tight. Same fitting sizes and sealing requirement as connecting a threaded nipple to an appliance gas inlet, but with the workpiece conveyed and clamped in a fixed station.

sources.system: MAKEEN Energy Valve Leak Detector (VLD, CIR-II test head)
sources.title: Valve leak detector | MAKEEN Energy
sources.claim: Fully automatic in-line valve leak detectors test every filled LPG cylinder's threaded valve joint for leakage against a preset limit and reject non-conforming units, including sorting out over-torqued screw valves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying that a newly made threaded gas joint does not leak — the acceptance check that ends the repairer's connection task, done automatically on the same class of threaded gas joints in a conveyorized line.

sources.system: BLM GROUP ALL-IN-ONE tube processing (end-forming, bending, cutting; 4-RUNNER line)
sources.title: ALL-IN-ONE - How to integrate different tube processing technologies in Industry 4.0 perspective
sources.claim: Automated tube-processing lines cut tubing from coil or bar and form the tube ends (flaring, rolling, threading) to produce finished fluid lines such as water, gas and fuel lines under CNC control with automatic loading and unloading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting soft copper/steel tubing to measured length and forming its ends (flare/thread) for a fluid connection — the fabrication half of a refrigerator or dishwasher water-line hookup, performed on the same tubing sizes in a fixtured machine.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: The most advanced construction-site robots used by mechanical, electrical and plumbing contractors perform semi-autonomous ceiling drilling and layout marking only; no fielded jobsite robot cuts, threads and connects pipe to feeder lines or appliances.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the negative E2/E3 judgments: the leading MEP jobsite robot's scope is drilling holes from a BIM model, not pipe fabrication or joint make-up, so it does not substantiate completion of this task in human work settings.

tasks.label: Assemble new or reconditioned appliances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Used-appliance/repair shop bench: rebuild and reassemble a reconditioned washer or dryer after service — reinstall tub/drum, bearings, belt, pump and motor, reconnect wiring harness and flexible hoses with spring clamps, then refit cabinet, console and access panels. Mixed brands and model years, worn/rusted fasteners, some parts replaced with substitutes.

Shop floor: recondition a used refrigerator or range for resale — rehang doors on hinges, fit gaskets and door liners, install shelves, bins and crisper drawers, refit burner assemblies, grates, knobs and trim panels after repairs. Unit sits on a dolly, floor or work stand; model varies job to job.

Dealer warehouse/shop prep area: uncrate a new major appliance and finish its assembly before delivery — remove packing and shipping bolts, attach handles and doors, fit leveling feet or rollers, install shelves/bins, fit accessory kits (icemaker, pedestal, stacking kit), then power up and check operation.

Customer's home during delivery/installation: final assembly of a new appliance in the kitchen or laundry area — attach handles, mount a custom cabinet door panel, install a pedestal or stack kit, thread and adjust leveling legs, fit trim and supplied hardware, working around cabinetry, flooring and household clutter.

Shop bench: reassemble a reconditioned small appliance (microwave, vacuum, mixer, toaster oven) after parts replacement — refit housing halves, small fasteners, clips, control knobs and internal leads, verifying operation.

sources.system: KUKA KR AGILUS screwdriving station with KUKA.ConveyorTech (integrator Qbig)
sources.title: Automatic screwing of washing machine doors with a robot | KUKA Global
sources.claim: A deployed, fully automated robotic station on a washing-machine production line drives the screws that attach window doors to washing machines, tracking the moving conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory attachment of a door to an appliance body with threaded fasteners. It transfers to the repairer's new-appliance assembly instances (attaching doors, handles, panels with screws) because the objects, fastener sizes and alignment tolerances are the same; it only holds in a fixtured, conveyor-fed E1 cell.

sources.system: LGE Clarksville smart factory (six-axis robot fleet, LG CLOi CarryBot AGVs/AMRs)
sources.title: Inside LG's Smart Factory | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A US appliance assembly plant runs 130 fixed six-axis robots performing welding, painting, screwdriving, material handling ... on washer and dryer assembly lines, plus 200 mobile robots delivering parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-volume assembly of new washers and dryers. It substantiates that fastening and part-placement operations on new appliance bodies are robot-doable inside a purpose-built line; the same article notes manual screwdriving is still used, bounding the claim to fixtured, single-model stations.

sources.system: SDC Gas Burner Assembly Machine (FANUC SCARA + 6-axis robots, SDC Flex Feeders)
sources.title: High-Speed Gas Burner Assembly Machine – Robotic Automation | SDC Automation
sources.claim: A purpose-built assembly machine assembles gas burners for cooking appliances autonomously: fixtures on an indexing ring, vision-guided FANUC SCARA robots picking from flex feeders, press stations and inline inspection at 30 parts per minute.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly of an appliance sub-assembly (gas burners) from loose parts. It transfers to new-appliance assembly at E1 because parts are presented in fixtures/feeders and the robots perform the same pick, seat and fasten operations; it does not transfer to unfixtured or used-unit work.

sources.system: GE Appliances Decatur refrigerator assembly lines (robots, AGVs)
sources.title: 2019 Assembly Plant of the Year: Refrigerator Production Heats Up at GE Appliances | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: At an award-winning refrigerator plant, robots are used for tube bending and adhesive application while human operators perform the fitting work — installing gaskets, doors, door stops, shelf fronts, attaching components and connecting tubing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembly of new refrigerators in a purpose-built plant. Cited as a limit: the compliant-part fitting steps that dominate appliance rebuild work (gaskets, hoses, harnesses, liners) are still performed by people even in the most automated appliance factories.

sources.system: Panasonic automatic dismantling equipment (six-axis robots with AI vision)
sources.title: Appliance Manufacturer Uses Robots and AI to Disassemble Products | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robots applied to used household appliances are used for teardown, not rebuilding: six-axis robots with magnetic grippers and vision-guided screwdrivers strip covers and fasteners from returned air conditioners, microwaves and washing machines for recycling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of used, in-service appliances. It shows the demonstrated capability on second-hand units is destructive disassembly in a recycling cell; no cited system reassembles a reconditioned appliance to working order.

sources.system: Figure AI, Agility Digit, Tesla Optimus, Unitree (industrial pilots)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Industrial Manufacturing: What They Can (and Can't) Do in 2026
sources.claim: As of 2026 humanoid and mobile manipulators in industry are limited to a narrow set of tasks (material handling, limited machine tending, inspection routes), with many claimed deployments being teleoperation with data collection rather than autonomous work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose mobile manipulation in human work facilities. Cited as a limit on E2/E3: no free-standing robot performs multi-step appliance assembly on unfixtured units in a shop, warehouse or home.
