roles.description: Repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems. May also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans.

tasks.label: Repair or maintain the operating condition of industrial production or processing machinery or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled preventive maintenance route on production line equipment on the plant floor: open guards, grease bearings and slides, change oil/air/hydraulic filters, check and tension belts and chains, torque fasteners, top up fluids, wipe down and note wear items on a filler, conveyor, mixer or press. Machine locked out, mechanic works around adjacent running equipment.

Consumable/wear-item servicing on highly automated production equipment inside an existing fenced cell (e.g., robotic welding guns: spatter removal from nozzles, contact tip and torch-body replacement, anti-spatter application) on a fixed schedule, where servicing hardware can be installed at a fixed station in the cell.

Breakdown repair of mechanical power-transmission components on the plant floor: diagnose a failed bearing, gearbox, drive motor, coupling or sprocket; lock out, remove guards and fasteners (often seized/corroded), rig and hoist the component out, press/pull and fit the replacement, laser-align the coupling, reassemble and run-test, under time pressure with the line down.

Repair and adjustment of packaging/processing machine subsystems on the floor: replace leaking pneumatic cylinders, hoses, seals and valves, swap a failed proximity or photoeye sensor and re-teach it, replace worn change parts and timing belts, re-time and re-align guides and star wheels, then run product to confirm quality.

Shop bench overhaul of a component removed from service: strip a centrifugal pump, gearbox, hydraulic cylinder or control valve, clean and inspect parts, measure clearances, decide reuse vs replace, fit new seals/bearings/wear rings, reassemble to torque and clearance spec, and pressure- or spin-test before returning it to stores.

Repair of process equipment in refinery, chemical or outdoor plant areas: change a pump mechanical seal, repack or rebuild a valve, replace a compressor part or gasketed flange joint, working in a hot/weather-exposed unit under permits, at height or in congested piping, with hot-work and confined-space constraints.

sources.system: Fronius Robacta CTC / Robacta TX/i change stations
sources.title: Robotics Change Stations – Robacta | Fronius
sources.claim: Commercially available change stations let welding robots autonomously replace worn contact tips and complete torch bodies inside a fenced robotic welding cell, with no human intervention — i.e., autonomous replacement of production-equipment wear parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: consumable/wear-part replacement on production welding equipment. It is the same act a mechanic performs when maintaining the operating condition of that equipment, performed on the same hardware, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Power REAM robotic torch maintenance center; ABICOR BINZEL TCS Compact cleaning station
sources.title: Power REAM | Lincoln Electric
sources.claim: Automatic nozzle cleaning/reaming stations perform preventive maintenance on robotic MIG torches (spatter removal, wire cutting, anti-spatter application) as a programmed step in a robotic welding cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled cleaning of production-equipment consumables. Same objects (weld torch nozzle/tip), same maintenance purpose, executed inside the purpose-built cell without a technician.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (ST Engineering MRAS factory; BMW plant)
sources.title: Boston Dynamics' robot dog patrols 1.5 million-square-foot factory
sources.claim: Deployed plant maintenance robots (quadrupeds) perform autonomous inspection rounds — thermal, acoustic and gauge data collection — but do not perform repair manipulation on the machinery they inspect.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: condition monitoring on the plant floor. It shows what mobile robots do achieve autonomously in this exact setting (sensing only), and therefore bounds what is substantiated for repair work.

sources.system: Figure 02/03 (BMW Spartanburg), Apptronik Apollo (Mercedes-Benz), Agility Digit (GXO)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots on Manufacturing Floors in 2026
sources.claim: Humanoid robots documented in 2026 factory deployments are limited to material handling, parts transfer, bin ... — no documented maintenance or repair of production machinery.
sources.transferJustification: General-purpose manipulators are the only plausible route to floor-level machine repair; their documented task set in the same E2 setting contains no disassembly/repair work, bounding the positive evidence available.

sources.system: UR10e-based autonomous unscrewing cell for e-waste disassembly
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: Research robotic cells can autonomously remove fasteners from devices presented in a fixtured workspace, using vision and force-sensed screwdriving, but the demonstrated scope is the unscrewing sub-step of disassembly, not diagnosis, part replacement, reassembly and test.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastener removal during teardown, a sub-step of bench overhaul. Cited to show the frontier of fixtured-cell autonomy is a single sub-step on small devices, well short of a whole component rebuild.

sources.system: Tele-robotic EV battery disassembly platform
sources.title: Towards Reuse and Recycling of Lithium-ion Batteries: Tele-robotics for Disassembly of Electric Vehicle Batteries
sources.claim: Robotic disassembly of larger industrial assemblies (unbolting stacked modules with a socket wrench) is demonstrated under human teleoperation, with the operator responsible for aligning the tool.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unbolting a heavy fastened assembly, the core physical act in mechanical breakdown repair and overhaul. It is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

tasks.label: Repair or replace broken or malfunctioning components of machinery or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-place mechanical repair of a production machine on a manufacturing plant floor: after lockout/tagout, the mechanic diagnoses a failed drive component on a conveyor, mixer, packaging machine or press, breaks loose corroded/torqued fasteners in a cramped guarded space, pulls the worn bearing, belt, chain, sprocket, coupling or seal, installs the replacement, aligns and tensions it, re-torques, re-guards, and test-runs the machine.

Hydraulic or pneumatic component replacement on a press, injection molder or hydraulic power unit: isolate and bleed pressure, drain fluid, disconnect and cap lines, remove and replace a leaking cylinder, hose, valve manifold, accumulator or pump, refill and bleed the circuit, set pressures and verify no leaks under load.

Electrical/control component replacement on production equipment: replace a burned-out motor or gearmotor, a failed proximity/limit switch, encoder, solenoid, contactor or VFD; land and dress wiring at terminals, restore conduit and guarding, then calibrate/verify sensor position and confirm correct machine sequence.

Bench rebuild in the plant maintenance shop of a subassembly pulled from a machine (centrifugal pump, gearbox, spindle, actuator, control valve): disassemble on the bench with press and pullers, inspect and measure to find the worn or broken internals, replace bearings, seals, gears or springs, reassemble to torque and clearance spec, and bench test before reinstallation.

Field repair inside a refinery, chemical plant or pipeline pump station: under a hot-work/confined-space permit, replace a pump mechanical seal, a valve actuator, a strainer element or a section of piping/instrument tubing at grade or on an elevated platform, in weather, in congested piping, then re-torque flanges and leak-test on restart.

Routine wear-part / consumable component swap on production equipment: change worn welding contact tips and nozzles on a robotic weld cell, replace slitter blades, filter elements, wear plates or a plug-in module, then verify the machine runs to quality. Fast, repetitive, low-diagnosis work often done at a purpose-designed change station.

sources.system: Optomec CS-250 / Acme automated turbine blade repair work cell
sources.title: Industry's First Fully Automated Work Cell for the Additive Repair of Turbine Parts
sources.claim: Optomec and Acme built a commercially available automated work cell that repairs worn turbine compressor blades by grinding, laser cladding and post-clad finishing on fixtured pallets, with machines automatically adapting tool paths to part-to-part wear variation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated repair of a worn machinery component. It shows what purpose-built repair automation covers today — restoring material on one fixtured, geometrically known part — not diagnosing a fault, dismantling an assembly and swapping internals, which is what the mechanic's instances require.

sources.system: Robotic fastener extraction system (industrial robot work cell)
sources.developer: University research group (published in MDPI Applied Sciences)
sources.title: A System for Robotic Extraction of Fasteners
sources.claim: A robotic work cell with vision, force/torque sensing and custom tooling autonomously extracted fasteners with 78-89% first-pass success (100% on a second pass) and over 30 seconds per fastener.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unfastening, a sub-step of nearly every component replacement. It marks the state of the art for autonomous fastener work in a structured cell and shows it is slow and imperfect even on presented, undamaged fasteners.

sources.system: DeMoBat robot disassembly cell (KUKA robots)
sources.title: Robot cutting - Fraunhofer IPA
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IPA built a robot cell that automatically disassembles battery modules from EV battery systems, including robot-supported cutting of screw, plug and cable connections, demonstrating feasibility of industrial disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown of a bolted assembly in a purpose-built cell. It is the closest automated analogue to the disassembly half of a repair, but it is destructive/one-way disassembly of a standardised product, with no fault diagnosis, part replacement or reassembly to spec.

sources.system: RUSSELL 7 Model R AutoMotion Mill Relining Machine
sources.title: RME deploys world's first semi-automated mill relining system
sources.claim: The most automated component-replacement work in heavy industry — exchanging worn grinding-mill liners — is a semi-automated, operator-directed roboticised machine that lets crews reline from outside the mill, not an autonomous repair system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing worn components and installing replacements on large industrial machinery. Autonomy is not established (described as semi-automated with reline crews), so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Nasarc INTELLIREAM robotic torch maintenance center and Tip Exchange System
sources.title: Simplified automated consumables management and manual welds
sources.claim: Commercial robotic torch maintenance centers automatically remove and replace worn welding nozzles and contact tips on robotic weld guns inside production weld cells, without a human doing the change.

sources.system: Tianxun (2nd generation) data center robot
sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Enables Five Super Data Centers to Support Double 11
sources.claim: Alibaba Cloud's second-generation Tianxun robot operates in production data centers and autonomously inspects racks, locates a faulty hard disk and replaces it in about four minutes without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous replacement of a failed component of equipment inside a structured facility. Transfer is limited: the disks are tool-less hot-swap modules in standardised racks with robot-adapted access, unlike bolted, aligned, torqued industrial machine components.

sources.system: Taurob Inspector autonomous offshore robot
sources.title: Equinor Deploys a Robot That Can Find Its Way Around an Offshore Platform
sources.claim: Equinor deployed autonomous ATEX-certified Taurob robots offshore for inspection, but the oil and gas industry has no autonomous devices able to carry out the repairs the robots detect.

sources.system: Figure 02 humanoid at BMW Group Spartanburg
sources.title: Humanoid Robots Complete Trial Project at BMW Assembly Plant
sources.claim: In the most advanced humanoid deployment in an automotive plant, Figure 02 robots ran autonomously for months doing pick-and-place of sheet metal into a welding fixture — parts handling, not machine repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose humanoid manipulation inside a plant (E2). It bounds what mobile manipulators actually do on plant floors today — repetitive part handling at fixed stations — well short of dismantling and repairing machinery.

tasks.label: Clean, lubricate, or adjust parts, equipment, or machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine lubrication round through a manufacturing plant: mechanic walks a PM route with grease gun and oil cans, hits zerk fittings on conveyor bearings, motor/pump bearings and drive components, checks and tops off gearbox oil levels and refills bottle oilers, wipes purged grease, logs points completed. Points are at varied heights, some behind guards or under machines, on live or idled equipment.

Setting-type adjustments on production machinery: repositioning guides, stops, rails and gap/clearance settings for a size or product changeover, setting tensioner and spring set-points, repositioning proximity/limit switches to spec, then verifying by test run.

Condition-driven mechanical adjustment after inspection or wear: shimming and aligning a motor-gearbox coupling to laser-alignment tolerance, re-tracking a wandering conveyor belt by tweaking idlers, adjusting chain/V-belt tension by feel and gauge, setting brake/clutch clearance or a valve packing gland - diagnosing by feel, measurement and iterative trial.

Cleaning machinery of dry and oily soils: blowing out and vacuuming chips, swarf and dust from machine interiors, guards and control panels, degreasing frames and gearcases, cleaning coolant screens, filters and strainers, and washing/degreasing components removed during a PM or overhaul on the maintenance-shop bench.

Wet sanitation washdown of process equipment in a food, beverage or pharma plant: rinse, foam, scrub and sanitize the exterior and open surfaces of fillers, conveyors, mixers and tanks after production, working around drains, wet stainless surfaces and hoses.

Field service at an outdoor or rough site: greasing and cleaning a quarry crusher, screen plant, remote pump station or customer's yard machinery - uneven footing, weather, mud and dust, layout and fitting locations different at every site.

sources.system: Graco automatic grease/oil lubrication pumps and injector systems (in-plant)
sources.title: Automatic Oil & Grease Pumps for Machinery Lubrication
sources.claim: Graco in-plant automatic lubrication pumps automatically deliver metered grease/oil to machine bearing points at frequent intervals while equipment runs, replacing the manual greasing round in industrial plants.

sources.system: DOPAG automated grease-metering production cell (robot + spray/shot valves)
sources.title: Production cell for automated grease metering | DOPAG
sources.claim: A DOPAG production cell uses a robot to pick gearwheels from workpiece carriers and present them to spray and shot valves that meter grease onto the parts inside and out, then return them to the carrier.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of metered grease to gear/bearing surfaces in production. Same lubricant, same class of mechanical components and film precision as a mechanic greasing parts; demonstrates grease application under machine control in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: ICS robotic dry-ice cleaning cell for rubber/tire molds
sources.title: Rubber Industry | ICS dry ice
sources.claim: Molds are transferred automatically into a closed robotic dry-ice cell where a robot arm runs a programmed blasting sequence, cleaning the tooling operator-free with repeatable pressure, standoff and angle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning heavily fouled production tooling. Same soils (baked polymer, oils, release residue) and same metal equipment surfaces a mechanic degreases; shows robot-borne cleaning media applied to equipment to an accepted production standard.

sources.system: Fives RoboWash robotic industrial parts washer
sources.title: RoboWash Robotic Industrial Parts Washer
sources.claim: Fives RoboWash is a production industrial washer in which a sealed 6-axis robot manipulates parts such as engine blocks, ... through pre-wash, high-pressure wash and drying stages fully automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic washing/degreasing of heavy machined components. Matches a mechanic cleaning removed machine parts (housings, blocks, covers) on the bench: same oily/chip soils, same part sizes, cleanliness verified to production spec.

sources.system: halstrup-walcher PSE 3xx-14 positioning systems (automatic format/axis adjustment)
sources.developer: halstrup-walcher GmbH (deployed on Gerhard Schubert and Langguth machines)
sources.title: Labeling specialist Langguth relies on the right drive technology during changeovers
sources.claim: halstrup-walcher PSE positioning systems replace handwheels on packaging/labeling machinery, automatically driving each adjustment axis to the stored target position; on a Langguth labeling machine up to 37 adjustment points are repositioned for a format change that took an operator over 15 minutes manually.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the machine-adjustment work a mechanic does with handwheels, scales and wrenches (guides, stops, gaps) performed instead by integrated, absolutely-measured actuators to the same positional spec and verified by the control system.

sources.system: Rosie (CleanBotix)
sources.title: Rosie by CleanBotix | Robotic Sanitation for Food Plants
sources.claim: CleanBotix Rosie is an autonomous wheeled robot with a 6-DOF arm and spray system that performs open-plant rinse-foam-rinse-sanitize cleaning of food and beverage processing equipment, navigating the plant floor as found without special fittings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sanitation washdown of production machinery in a plant. Same objects (fillers, conveyors, tanks), same in-place cleaning of equipment surfaces to a measurable acceptance standard (ATP swabs).

sources.system: Rosie R6 (CleanBotix, MoveIt Pro autonomy stack)
sources.title: CleanBotix Builds Autonomous Food-Processing Robot with MoveIt Pro to Accelerate Market Launch
sources.claim: In customer pilot deployments the Rosie R6 cleaned at about 80% of human cleaning speed ..., running four to five hours of ....
sources.transferJustification: Same as the Rosie product evidence: quantifies worker-comparable quality and throughput for autonomous in-plant cleaning of processing equipment.

sources.system: Graco off-road / heavy equipment automatic lubrication systems (e.g., Electric Dyna-Star)
sources.date: 2026 (product page; widely fielded on mining/construction fleets)
sources.title: Off-Road Equipment Automatic Lubrication | Graco
sources.claim: Graco off-road automatic lubrication systems installed on excavators, loaders, haul trucks, dozers and drills deliver precise lubricant doses at intervals to all bearings, pivot ..., with controllers monitoring performance.

sources.system: StoneAge AutoBox 3L / ABX-2L with Sentinel Automation Technology
sources.title: StoneAge | Automated Equipment for High-pressure Industrial Cleaning
sources.claim: StoneAge AutoBox tractors provide hands-free automated cleaning of heat exchanger tube bundles and fin-fans; with Sentinel the system uses active sensing to position the lances and clean tubes end to end without an operator in the blast zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: internal cleaning of process equipment during maintenance. Same industrial fouling-removal work a mechanic does on strainers, tubes and coolers, executed by a machine mounted to the equipment and indexed automatically.

tasks.label: Disassemble machinery or equipment to remove parts and make repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ repair of a production machine on a manufacturing plant floor (packaging line, conveyor drive, press, CNC): lock out/tag out, strip guards, panels and covers, break loose torqued or corroded fasteners in cramped access, pull a failed drive, coupling, chain, cylinder or bearing, replace it, reassemble, align and run-test.

Bench overhaul in the plant maintenance shop: a pump, gearbox, electric motor or hydraulic unit is brought to the shop, torn down on a bench or press, parts cleaned, measured and inspected, bearings/seals/wear parts replaced, unit reassembled to torque and clearance spec and function-tested.

Field disassembly of rotating or pressure equipment at a refinery, chemical plant or pipeline station: outdoor/piping-congested location, hot or corroded bolting, gasketed flanges, hoists and slings, permit and confined-space conditions; pump/compressor/valve/exchanger opened, damaged internals removed and replaced, then buttoned up.

Heavy teardown during an outage in a mill or heavy plant: mill roll, crusher, large press or paper-machine section; rigging with overhead crane and jacks, torch heat and hydraulic pullers to free interference-fit parts, several mechanics working over hours or days, then rebuild and alignment.

Field service call at a customer or satellite site (small shop, bakery, warehouse, farm, remote pump house): unfamiliar or older equipment, no fixtures or documentation, variable access and lighting; the mechanic diagnoses, partially disassembles the machine on the spot, swaps the failed part and reassembles.

sources.system: Daisy
sources.date: 2018-04 (system still in operation as of 2026 reporting)
sources.title: Apple adds Earth Day donations to trade-in and recycling program - Apple Newsroom
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy is a deployed, purpose-built robotic disassembly line that takes apart iPhones at up to 200 units per hour for material recovery — the most industrially mature autonomous disassembly system, but limited to one product family, performing recycling teardown rather than repair or reassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated product teardown. It is the strongest existing case of machine-performed disassembly, so it bounds the frontier; it works only on a fixed catalogue of identical, fixtured consumer devices and never diagnoses, repairs, or reassembles, so it does not carry over to opening an industrial pump or gearbox and restoring it to service.

sources.system: ORNL automated battery disassembly line
sources.title: Automated disassembly line aims to make battery recycling safer, faster | ORNL
sources.claim: ORNL built an automated, purpose-built disassembly line in which robots unbolt and open EV battery pack housings after a robot loads the pack, removing human contact during teardown; it is a laboratory/prototype recycling line, not a repair operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic unbolting and cover removal on end-of-life equipment. It shows the reachable sub-step (fastener removal on a fixtured unit in a purpose-built cell) but stops at destructive teardown for recycling: no diagnosis, wear-part replacement, torqued reassembly, or functional test, which are required to complete this task's instances.

sources.system: BEAM-1
sources.developer: Shanghai Jiao Tong University et al. (Peng et al.)
sources.title: Revolutionizing Battery Disassembly: The Design and Implementation of a Battery Disassembly Autonomous Mobile Manipulator Robot (BEAM-1)
sources.claim: BEAM-1 is a research autonomous mobile manipulator that autonomously perceives and removes multiple bolt types on end-of-life EV battery packs with 98.78% success in real experiments — an autonomous fastener-removal sub-step only, in a laboratory setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bolt removal on aged equipment. It substantiates only unbolting on accessible external surfaces of one product type in the lab; it does not substantiate extracting press-fit internals, replacing wear parts, or reassembling a machine to spec, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

sources.system: robotic disassembly systems in remanufacturing (industry review)
sources.developer: Robotics & Automation News (trade press survey of the field)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: Trade-press review of automation in remanufacturing and repair reports that robotic disassembly systems are only beginning to emerge and that seized fasteners, deformed parts and unknown as-found condition remain major obstacles to automating teardown of used equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of used machinery for remanufacture, the closest industrial analogue to mechanic disassembly-and-repair. It documents that no fielded system handles the as-found variability that defines this task, supporting negative judgments even under an E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: robotic disassembly research systems (systematic review)
sources.developer: Ameur et al., Hassan II University / Arts et Métiers
sources.title: The future of robotic disassembly: a systematic review of techniques and applications in the age of AI | Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of robotic disassembly finds the field lacks disassembly documentation and standards, limiting robots' ability to generalise across product types — i.e. autonomous teardown remains product-specific and largely experimental.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly generally. The review establishes that demonstrated autonomy is confined to narrow, pre-characterised products, which is why nothing transfers to the diverse machinery a plant mechanic tears down and repairs.

tasks.label: Reassemble equipment after completion of inspections, testing, or repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-place reassembly of installed production machinery on the plant floor after a repair: remount a gearbox, motor or drive onto the machine frame, refit shafts, sprockets, chains and belts, align and shim the coupling, reconnect sensors and wiring, torque mounting bolts to spec, and function-check. Access is confined, parts are used, fasteners and sequences differ machine to machine.

Buttoning up equipment after a scheduled inspection or PM: reinstall access panels, sheet-metal guards, belt covers and doors, reattach lube lines, hoses, quick-disconnects and interlock/sensor cables, and torque fasteners on machinery that stays bolted in place in the plant.

Bench reassembly in the maintenance/rebuild shop of a removable standard unit that the plant rebuilds repeatedly across a fleet of identical items (centrifugal pump, gear reducer, electric motor, pneumatic/hydraulic cylinder, valve actuator): press in bearings, install seals and O-rings, stack the housing, torque bolts in sequence, spin or leak test.

Bench reassembly in the shop of a one-off, unfamiliar or complex removable assembly (custom machine subassembly, OEM head or gearcase seen once a year): fit and shim parts to measured clearances, route internal tubing and wiring, hand-start fasteners in blind holes, adjust and verify against a service manual.

Reassembly away from the home plant: putting machinery back together during installation, relocation or field service at a customer site, an outdoor process area, a refinery unit or a mobile job site, using rigging and hoists, with the layout and conditions taken as found.

sources.system: Custom automated assembly and test machine for a hydraulic pump control module
sources.developer: The Christopher Stephen Corp. (with FANUC America, Schmidt Technology, Ingersoll Rand, ATEQ)
sources.title: Automated System Assembles Electronic Control Modules | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A deployed custom automated assembly cell (FANUC six-axis robot, rotary indexing dial, Schmidt presses, Ingersoll Rand torque spindles, ATEQ leak tester) executes a 29-step mechanical assembly of a hydraulic-pump control module: press-fits, part placement into build fixtures, robot tool changes, torqued bolts, inspection and leak test, with parts presented in trays and feeders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: line assembly of a hydraulic-pump module. It is the same physical work as bench reassembly of a repaired unit when parts are presented fixtured in a purpose-built cell - press-fitting components into a housing, seating parts in a build fixture, driving fasteners to a torque spec, and leak/function testing the finished unit - on comparable metal parts at comparable precision.

sources.system: Mikron Automation multistation stepper-motor assembly line at Sonceboz SA
sources.title: Automated system assembles stepper motors for Tier 1 supplier | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A multistation automated assembly line builds small electric (stepper) motors at high volume in a factory, assembling housings, rotors and internal components without operators performing the assembly steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: volume assembly of small motors. Reassembling a rebuilt motor or gearmotor in a purpose-built cell involves the same stack-up of housing, shaft/rotor, bearings and end covers with fasteners, so line-assembly performance transfers when parts are fixtured and fed.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robotic screwdriving system (physics-informed compliance control)
sources.developer: Realization of Robotic Systems Lab, University of Southern California (Manyar, Patel, Gupta)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic screwdriving for high-mix manufacturing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A research mobile manipulator drives screws autonomously in high-mix, low-volume conditions, tolerating hole pose uncertainty of several millimetres and degrees, validated on ten distinct parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: threaded fastening under pose uncertainty, the dominant sub-step of buttoning up a repaired unit. It shows autonomous bolt driving is feasible with imperfect part presentation, but it is only the fastening step, not whole-unit reassembly.

sources.system: Assessment of autonomous robot capabilities across industrial, household and navigation tasks
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: An independent 2026 assessment of autonomous robot capabilities finds multi-step assembly unsolved outside narrow engineered setups: connecting cables inside a PC case and assembling flat-pack furniture are rated lab-limited or early-research, and demonstrated skills rarely transfer to new objects or ....
sources.transferJustification: Used only as negative context: it evaluates autonomous multi-step assembly and cable connection, the closest analogues to reassembling repaired machinery, and reports they are not solved outside environments designed around the robot.

tasks.label: Examine parts for defects, such as breakage or excessive wear.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corrective repair on a plant floor: after a breakdown, the mechanic pulls suspect components (bearings, couplings, gears, seals, shafts, sprockets, belts) out of a production machine and examines them by eye and hand — spalled races, chipped teeth, scoring, cracks, heat discoloration, roughness when turned — to decide which part failed and whether others are reusable. Dirty, hot, time-pressured, line down.

Bench inspection during a planned overhaul in the maintenance shop: a pump, gearbox or drive is torn down, parts cleaned, then journals, bores, gear teeth, keyways and seal surfaces are measured with micrometers, bore gauges and dial indicators against OEM wear limits; surfaces checked for pitting, fretting and cracks (sometimes dye penetrant).

Scheduled PM route on operating equipment: the mechanic walks the plant checking accessible machinery externally — looking for broken or missing components, leaks, belt or chain damage, listening for abnormal noise, shooting temperatures on bearings and motors — and documents condition findings for follow-up work orders.

Scheduled PM requiring access: guards, covers and inspection ports are opened on stopped equipment to examine internals — chain elongation and sprocket hook wear, gear tooth wear inside a gearbox, brake pads and liners, wear strips, conveyor idlers and rollers, screens — often reaching into confined, awkward spaces with a flashlight and hand tools.

Field service call at an uncontrolled site: portable or mobile industrial equipment, a construction or temporary installation, a small customer shop or a remote outdoor skid; the layout is as found, lighting and footing vary, and the mechanic examines removed or in-place parts for breakage and wear on the spot.

Checking new, rebuilt or stocked replacement parts before installation, in the storeroom or at the machine: verifying a received bearing, gear, motor, seal kit or hydraulic component is undamaged (dents, bent shafts, corrosion, shipping damage, defective manufacture) and matches spec.

sources.system: AutoInspect
sources.title: Digital inspection procedure for engine components industrialized
sources.claim: Lufthansa Technik's AutoInspect is a robot-based, sensor-driven procedure that performs digital crack inspection on service-run engine components in an MRO shop; the system is in productive use and being rolled out to further CFM56/CF34 combustor components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: MRO crack inspection of used engine parts. Same output as a mechanic examining a removed part for breakage — a machine-made defect call on a service-worn metal component held in a purpose-built cell, at precision at least equal to hand/eye inspection.

sources.system: ARTIS-5 Pipe Inspection System
sources.title: ARTIS-5 – Oilfield Equipment Marketing, Inc.
sources.claim: The ARTIS-5 EMI unit is a commercial purpose-built line that inspects used oilfield drill pipe, tubing and casing as it passes through, electronically detecting cracks, splits, corrosion and erosion wall loss, and large-area OD/rod wear.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: NDT grading of used tubulars. The defect classes are the mechanic's — breakage (cracks, splits) and excessive wear (wall loss) — judged automatically on worn steel parts conveyed to the inspection head in a purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Gleason GMSP closed-loop gear metrology cell
sources.title: Inspection (Gear Technology) — 'Lights Off - Production On!'
sources.claim: Gleason gear metrology systems with robot or cobot loading fully automate dimensional measurement of gears in a fixtured cell, producing tooth-geometry deviation results without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated gear metrology. Calling 'excessive wear' on a gear, spline or shaft is a dimensional comparison to spec; a robot-loaded metrology cell makes that comparison on the same class of parts to tighter tolerance than a mechanic's micrometer.

sources.system: ATOS ScanBox (ZEISS/GOM)
sources.title: GOM Scanbox | Capture 3D
sources.claim: The ATOS/ZEISS ScanBox is a commercial automated optical 3D measuring cell that digitizes fixtured parts and compares them to nominal geometry; with an automated part handler it digitizes parts unattended for many hours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: full-field dimensional inspection of parts in a robotic cell. Deviation-from-nominal on a presented part is the same measurement used to call excessive wear, dents or deformation on a used or newly received component.

sources.system: ANYmal
sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped has run autonomous nightly inspection rounds at Vigier Ciment's cement plant since early 2025, covering more than 450 checkpoints across three mills and ... and scanning equipment for structural defects, overheating ...; over 33,000 inspections completed.

sources.system: Spot with Spot CAM+IR and Enhanced Autonomy Payload
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A midstream gas plant deployed Spot for autonomous inspection rounds across a 40-acre facility, including anomaly detection, thermal inspection and gauge reading, with the robot navigating the site and recharging on its dock between routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: route-based external condition monitoring of plant machinery. The output — documented findings flagging damaged, leaking or overheating assets — is what the mechanic's external PM walkaround produces.

tasks.label: Record repairs and maintenance performed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Operate newly repaired machinery or equipment to verify the adequacy of repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-plant run-off after an in-situ repair: mechanic finishes replacing a gearbox, bearing, belt/chain, hydraulic cylinder or sensor on a conveyor, filler, press, extruder or packaging machine, then restarts it at the local panel, jogs and cycles it, runs product through, listens and feels for noise, vibration and leaks, checks output quality, and decides whether the repair holds or needs rework. Manufacturing plant floor, mixed machine models, one-off faults.

Shop bench verification of a rebuilt component: mechanic mounts a rebuilt pump, motor, gearbox or hydraulic power unit on a maintenance-shop test stand, connects drive, piping and instrumentation, runs it up through speed/pressure/load points, records flow, pressure, temperature and vibration, checks for leaks, and signs it off as fit to reinstall.

Refinery or chemical plant restart: after a mechanical-seal, bearing or coupling repair on a process pump, blower or compressor, the mechanic lines up valves, starts the unit with operations, watches seal leakage, bearing temperature and suction/discharge pressures, takes vibration readings with a handheld analyzer, and releases the machine to service.

Machine tool / precision equipment verification: after spindle, ballscrew, way or servo-drive repair on a CNC machine or similar, mechanic warms it up, jogs axes, runs a test program or trial cut, checks backlash, runout and geometry, measures the test part, and iterates adjustments until tolerances are met.

Field, remote or newly installed equipment run-in: repaired or relocated machinery at a pipeline pump station, mine or quarry, customer plant or partially built facility - start engine/hydraulics, load-test, check alignment, temperatures and leaks outdoors, with site layout and conditions taken as found.

sources.system: RedViking end-of-line transfer case test and assembly cell (Vsync test executive plus part-transfer robot)
sources.title: Test Cell Automation Soup to Nuts - RedViking
sources.claim: Deployed automotive end-of-line test cell in which an industrial robot loads an assembled transfer case into a test stand, automated tooling engages it mechanically and electrically, a test executive runs a dynamic test with accelerometers, and the robot then routes the unit to final assembly or rework based on the result - machine-controlled operation of a powered assembly plus an automatic adequacy verdict.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line functional test of a newly assembled gear unit. It transfers to post-repair verification of a rebuilt gearbox, pump or motor: the same class of powered rotating assembly is run under load, the same quantities (speed, torque, vibration via accelerometers) are judged against spec, and the output is an accept/rework verdict - exactly what the mechanic's bench run-up produces.

sources.system: AMD Machines automated functional test stations
sources.title: Automated Functional Test Stations | AMD Machines
sources.claim: Commercially supplied automated functional test stations run an assembled unit through its real operating range, compare every measured channel against limits, and automatically sort good, reject and rework parts, with servo or pneumatic actuators making the mechanical and electrical connections in a fixtured nest.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered functional test of an assembled unit. Transfers to running a repaired unit to verify the repair because the physical act is the same - energize the unit, drive it through its operating range, compare measured behaviour to spec, accept or reject - on comparable industrial components.

sources.system: Hainzl hydraulic test stands (service and repair test benches) with OCEAN automation platform
sources.title: Hydraulic Test Stands - hainzl.at

tasks.label: Observe and test the operation of machinery or equipment to diagnose malfunctions, using voltmeters or other testing devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unplanned breakdown on a plant production line: a packaging/conversion machine faults or stops. Mechanic runs and observes the machine, opens the control cabinet and junction boxes, and uses a multimeter/clamp meter to check supply voltage, contactor coils, sensor and drive signals, and motor windings until the failed component or wiring fault is isolated. Live circuits, cramped enclosures, pressure to restore production.

Scheduled condition-monitoring / PM route through the plant: mechanic walks a fixed route past motors, pumps, gearboxes, compressors and electrical panels while they run, observing operation, listening, shooting thermal images, using an ultrasonic leak/electrical-discharge detector, and reading local gauges; abnormal assets are flagged in a report for repair.

Mechanical / hydraulic / pneumatic fault diagnosis on installed equipment: mechanic cycles the machine, watches motion and timing, hooks pressure gauges or a flow meter into hydraulic/pneumatic circuits, checks bearing temperature and vibration by contact probe, and determines the worn or failed component (valve, cylinder, coupling, bearing).

Refinery, pipeline pump station or process-plant unit (mostly outdoor, institution-controlled): mechanic tours the unit checking running pumps, compressors, fans and heat exchangers with portable gas detector, thermal camera, vibration pen and gauge/instrument readings to find which asset is malfunctioning.

Maintenance shop bench diagnosis of a removed component (electric motor, gearbox, hydraulic pump, VFD): mechanic mounts it on a stand or bench, runs it, takes insulation-resistance (megger), current, pressure and vibration readings, and decides the fault and whether to repair or replace.

Field service call at a customer, remote or outdoor site (quarry crusher, mobile processing skid, mill under construction, agricultural processing plant): unfamiliar layout, weather and clutter, no site-standard access; mechanic observes the machine running and uses meters and gauges to diagnose the malfunction.

tasks.label: Cut and weld metal to repair broken metal parts, fabricate new parts, or assemble new equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-place repair on installed production machinery on the plant floor: a cracked machine frame, torn conveyor chute/hopper, broken bracket or guard. Mechanic diagnoses the break, arc-gouges/grinds out the crack, torch- or plasma-cuts away damaged metal, fits and tacks a patch plate cut from stock, then welds out-of-position in tight access next to the down machine, and grinds the weld flush.

Fabrication of a one-off replacement or custom part in the plant maintenance shop: measure and lay out, cut plate/bar/tube with band saw, oxyfuel or plasma torch, fit up on a bench or welding table, tack, weld (often mixed material thickness, no drawing or only a sketch), grind and clean for fit to the machine.

Restoration of worn or damaged components removed from machines and brought to the shop: build-up/hardfacing of shafts, auger flights, crusher/bucket wear surfaces, worn bores and keyways, cracked castings — welded on a bench or rotary positioner, then machined or ground back to size.

Cutting and welding during installation/assembly of new equipment: fabricating and welding mounting plates, support frames, platforms, pipe supports and chutes at the installation location inside the plant, frequently elevated on ladders/lifts or over existing machinery, fitting to as-built conditions.

Outdoor/remote field cut-and-weld work at pipeline, tank farm, mine, quarry or outdoor conveyor structures: engine-driven welder, weather and wind, cutting damaged sections with a torch and welding replacement steel or pipe in place, sometimes elevated or in confined access.

sources.title: America Is Short Hundreds of Thousands of Welders. I Just Watched a Robot Try to Fix That.
sources.claim: Path Robotics' Obsidian-driven welding cells scan the actual part, plan welds on the spot without offline programming, and adapt to imperfect fit-up — enabling autonomous welding of high-mix, one-off steel parts inside a fenced cell with positioners.

sources.claim: A turnkey automated work cell performs adaptive repair of damaged turbine parts end-to-end: robotic grinding of the damaged area, laser cladding to add weld metal, and robotic post-clad finishing, with automated pallet load/unload.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: adaptive weld repair of damaged metal components. Same repair sequence a mechanic performs (prep by grinding, deposit weld metal, finish), executed on parts fixtured on pallets in a cell, with vision-driven adaptation to the as-found damage.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: hardfacing/build-up of worn heavy equipment components — the same welding operation industrial mechanics perform to restore worn shafts, flights and wear surfaces, on comparable steels and part sizes.

sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound, not establish, in-situ capability: it shows deployed mobile welding automation is limited to long prepared grooves on large structures in shipyards, not cut-and-fit repair of installed machinery.

sources.claim: Union Pacific has deployed truck-mounted robotic welding for in-track repair of frogs: crews position the robotic arm and step back while the system executes the welds — an in-situ repair application confined to one standard component type.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ build-up repair welding of a worn steel component. Cited to show field repair automation exists only for a single fixed component class, without cutting, fitting or patching.

sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound E2: cobot welders sitting in ordinary human shops still require per-job operator teaching, so they do not show autonomous completion of one-off shop work outside a purpose-built station.

tasks.label: Enter codes and instructions to program computer-controlled machinery.

instances.label: Plant maintenance mechanic connects a laptop with vendor software (e.g., Studio 5000, TIA Portal) to a PLC on a packaging or process line, edits/repairs ladder logic or restores a backup program, and downloads it to the controller so the line runs correctly.

Mechanic re-enters setup parameters after replacing a component: VFD/servo drive parameter sets, temperature controller setpoints, encoder scaling, safety relay configuration, entered through drive keypads or configuration software.
Mechanic enters or edits G-code, tool/work offsets, and machine parameters at a CNC machine's MDI/control panel following a repair, alignment, or tooling change, then proves out the program.

Mechanic uses a robot teach pendant or pick-and-place controller to enter position registers, edit motion instructions, or reload a stored program after a servicing or crash recovery on an automated cell.
Mechanic edits HMI/SCADA screens, recipe tables, timers, counters and alarm setpoints on packaging or filling equipment to accommodate a product changeover or corrected process condition.

tasks.label: Demonstrate equipment functions and features to machine operators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After completing a repair or adjustment on a production machine (e.g., a packaging filler or CNC lathe) on the plant floor, the mechanic shows the assigned operator what was changed — running the machine through a cycle, indicating the affected controls, and explaining the symptoms to watch for and when to call maintenance.

Commissioning of newly installed or relocated equipment: the mechanic (often alongside an OEM technician) walks the operating crew through the HMI/control panel functions, safety interlocks and e-stops, startup/shutdown sequence, and changeover steps, answering questions until operators can run it.

Informal on-the-floor coaching during a shift: showing an operator the correct loading technique, how to clear a jam safely, where lubrication/inspection points are, or how to interpret a specific fault code on the display.

Structured group session — a toolbox talk, huddle-room or classroom briefing with several operators after a machine upgrade or new feature rollout — using the manual, drawings, screenshots or a demo unit to explain new functions and revised procedures.

tasks.label: Dismantle machines and remove parts for repair, using hand tools, chain falls, jacks, cranes, or hoists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ teardown on the plant floor: after lockout/tagout, the worker strips guards, covers and chain drives off a production machine (packaging line, extruder, press feeder, conveyor drive), uncouples shafts and piping, and unbolts and pulls a failed subassembly (gearbox, drive motor, pump) with a chain fall or portable gantry, working in the machine's confined access spaces amid grease and product residue.

Bench teardown in the plant's maintenance shop of a component already removed and set on a bench or stand — typically a model the shop sees repeatedly (standard NEMA motor, centrifugal pump, gear reducer, valve actuator): unbolt housings and end covers, separate the halves, remove the failed internal part, lay out and tag hardware for the repair.

Heavy-assembly removal requiring rigging: removing a roll, drum, die, large bearing housing or complete drive package weighing several hundred to several thousand kilograms, using overhead crane, chain falls, jacks and slings, with the worker rigging lift points, jacking to break the fit and guiding the part clear of tight framework.

Dismantling assemblies that are seized, corroded, galled or damaged: bolts snapped or rounded, press-fits rusted in place; requires penetrating oil, heat, impact wrenches, pullers, bolt extractors, cutting/grinding and on-the-spot judgment about which route damages the machine least.

Strip-down of a food, beverage or pharmaceutical processing machine (filler, mixer, slicer, capper) for repair of a product-contact component: removing clamps, wing nuts, seals, augers and change-parts in a washdown-clean area, handling fragile stainless parts and hygiene requirements.

Field work away from the plant floor: dismantling outdoor or remote equipment — a quarry conveyor drive, an irrigation or well pump, a rooftop air-handling unit, mobile equipment at a customer site — with only portable tools, a truck hoist and improvised rigging, in weather and on uneven ground.

sources.system: DeMoBat robotic disassembly demonstrator (KUKA KR QUANTEC + Fraunhofer pitasc force control)
sources.title: "DeMoBat": Battery disassembly for electric cars using KUKA robots | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IPA's DeMoBat project built a robot-based disassembly cell in which a 270 kg-payload KUKA KR QUANTEC, guided by vision that locates screws automatically rather than by taught positions, detaches screws and adhesive joints on EV battery packs and e-drive units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of EV battery packs and electric drive units for recycling. Transfer: same class of operations as machinery teardown (locating and removing threaded fasteners, opening housings, separating heavy bolted assemblies) on comparably sized, worn components, but performed on a fixtured workpiece inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: DeMoBat Demonstrator 4 (e-drive unit disassembly)
sources.title: "DeMoBat" - Industrial disassembly of battery modules and electric motors - Fraunhofer IPA
sources.claim: The DeMoBat project's fourth demonstrator covers industrial disassembly of electric drive units; Fraunhofer describes the demonstrators as only partially automated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of an electric drive unit (motor plus gearbox), the same object class a maintenance worker strips on a shop bench; Fraunhofer's own "(partially) automated" wording bounds how much of such a teardown is machine-performed.

sources.system: DeMoBat robotic disassembly toolset

sources.claim: DeMoBat produced eight fully implemented robotic tools for non-destructive robot disassembly of EV batteries down to cell level, in a fixed laboratory/industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: non-destructive robotic disassembly of a bolted, cabled, multi-hundred-kilogram assembly — comparable fastener types and part weights to a bench teardown of a pump or gear reducer, again with the workpiece fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Daisy disassembly robot
sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line disassembles many iPhone models into components at production rates in a dedicated recycling facility, removing screws and separating modules automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: complete automated teardown of a manufactured product into its parts. Transfer is limited: objects are tiny and fastener torques trivial compared with machinery, but it establishes that whole-product disassembly runs reliably when the product family is known and the line is purpose-built (E1).

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing cell (UR10e + Intel RealSense D405 + custom mechatronic screwdriver)
sources.developer: academic group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A UR10e-based robotic cell with an RGB-D camera and force-sensing screwdriver autonomously locates and removes screws in a range of electronic devices with 91-100% success by screw type.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fastener removal, the opening step of any machine teardown. Transfer covers only small screws on fixtured devices in a cell, not the bolted, torqued joints of production machinery.

sources.system: Industrial-grade robot vision screw removal system
sources.title: Industrial-Grade Robust Robot Vision for Screw Detection and Removal under Uneven Conditions
sources.claim: A vision system for screw detection and removal on degraded real units achieved high screw detection but only 78.3% end-to-end disassembly success across 120 units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal of fasteners under degradation (rust, dirt, damage), the condition that dominates seized-fastener maintenance work; the reported success rate is far below what an employer would accept from a maintenance worker.

sources.system: iDEAR robotic disassembly demonstrator
sources.title: Automated Electronics Disassembly - Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IFF's iDEAR project demonstrates a robot that locates screws on a computer housing, changes tools and lifts internal components out non-destructively, following step-by-step disassembly instructions generated by the system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: non-destructive robotic teardown of a housed device with tool changes; comparable in kind to bench teardown of a small component, but restricted to lightweight electronics on a fixtured table in a research cell.

sources.system: RUSSELL Mill Relining Machine with AutoMotion / THUNDERBOLT SKYWAY
sources.title: RME deploys world's first semi-automated mill relining system | Global Mining Review
sources.claim: RME deployed the first semi-automated mill relining system at a mine, removing worn grinding-mill liners and placing new ones with nobody inside the mill, but the machines are remotely operated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing multi-tonne worn parts from a large machine with powered manipulators and rigging — the closest deployed analogue to heavy-part removal in maintenance — but RME describes it as semi-automated remote operation, so it cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

sources.system: review of robotic disassembly systems (Disassembly 4.0)
sources.developer: Poschmann et al., Chemie Ingenieur Technik
sources.title: Disassembly 4.0: A Review on Using Robotics in Disassembly Tasks as a Way of Automation
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed review of robotic disassembly reports that attempts to automate disassembly of complex products such as cars ... had not been implemented at industrial scale.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the task class (robotic disassembly of mechanical components); establishes that general machine teardown remains manual even in structured industrial settings.

tasks.label: Reassemble machines after the completion of repair or maintenance work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant-floor, in-situ reassembly of a large production machine after a major repair (packaging line, press, extruder, mixer): refit gearbox/motor and couplings, align shafts, reinstall chains/belts/sprockets, hydraulic and pneumatic lines, wiring and sensors, then covers and guards; cramped access, lockout/tagout, machine stays in place, verified by test run.

Plant-floor, in-situ reassembly of a moderate sub-system after a routine part change: remount a motor/gear reducer on a conveyor drive or a pump on its baseplate, align the coupling, refit and tension the belt or chain, reconnect conduit/piping, reinstall the guard, and run-test.

Bench reassembly in the plant maintenance shop of a discrete unit removed from service (centrifugal pump, gear reducer, electric motor, valve actuator) after bearing/seal replacement: press in bearings, fit seals, O-rings and gaskets, stack rotor and housing, torque fasteners to spec, check runout, spin test.

Repetitive shop reassembly of a standardized unit that the plant rebuilds regularly in batches (same model of pump, motor, gear case or hydraulic cylinder): identical part set and sequence each time, kitted parts, torque and leak/function test before the unit goes back to the spares crib.

Field reassembly at an outdoor or off-site location: farm, quarry or mobile equipment, remote pump house, rooftop or yard machinery; reassembled where it sits, with weather, uneven footing, improvised access and only the tools on the service truck.

sources.system: Ford Van Dyke transmission plant robotic assembly stations (force-controlled clutch/gear installation robots, delta pin-insertion robots)
sources.developer: Ford Motor Co. (reported by ASSEMBLY Magazine)
sources.title: 2018 Assembly Plant of the Year: Ford Shifts Flexible Assembly Into High Gear
sources.claim: At Ford's Van Dyke transmission ..., force-monitoring and vision-guided robots perform press-fit assembly and install gears and clutches into transmission cases on a high-mix production line, adapting to part variation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production assembly of gear cases rather than reassembly after repair. Transfer holds for shop reassembly of a repaired gear reducer or pump: identical object classes (gears, clutches, bearings, housings, threaded fasteners), the same press-fit and torque precision, and parts presented in fixtures as a purpose-built cell would present them.

sources.system: Autonomous Robotic Assembly system (part singulation to precise assembly)
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Assembly: From Part Singulation to Precise Assembly (arXiv:2406.05331)
sources.claim: A robot autonomously assembled a functioning gear box from parts placed in arbitrary configurations on a workbench, performing singulation, in-hand regrasping, tactile peg insertion and compliant gear meshing, with 99.11% end-to-end success over 225 randomized trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: first-time assembly of a gear box in a lab workcell. Transfer to bench reassembly of a repaired reducer is partial but direct: same operation set (grasping loose parts, precise shaft/bore insertion, gear meshing under force feedback) on a fixtured bench, which is how the work would be presented in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Learning-Augmented Robotic Automation (LARA) workstation
sources.title: Learning-augmented robotic automation for real-world manufacturing (arXiv:2604.22235)
sources.claim: A learning-based robotic workstation was deployed on a live electric-motor production line to autonomously perform deformable cable insertion and soldering, running 5 hours 10 minutes continuously and producing 108 motors at a 99.4% quality pass rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a wiring step in motor production, not maintenance reassembly. It substantiates that a fixtured production cell can autonomously handle one flexible-cable connection step at production quality on a standardized unit, supporting repetitive standardized rebuild work; it does not cover varied one-off wiring.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic screwdriving system (physics-informed screw-tip dynamics model with failure-recovery)
sources.developer: University of Southern California (Manyar, Patel, Gupta), Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing
sources.title: Autonomous robotic screwdriving for high-mix manufacturing
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic screwdriving system for high-mix, low-volume manufacturing handled hole-pose uncertainty up to 4 mm / 3 degrees and was evaluated on three screw types across ten industrial parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: threaded fastening in assembly. Reassembly is dominated by torquing fasteners into somewhat variable hole locations; this shows autonomous fastening tolerant of part-to-part variation on a fixtured workcell, the fastening component of shop reassembly.

sources.system: Capability assessment of autonomous robots (IKEA furniture assembly, PC cable insertion, precise small-object insertion)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: An independent 2026 assessment of autonomous robot capabilities finds multi-step assembly with varied parts and tool use unproven: IKEA-style furniture assembly is rated early research stage, and cable insertion inside a case shows significant limits even in the lab.

sources.system: Spot with Spot Arm
sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: The most capable commercially deployed mobile manipulator for industrial facilities performs only constrained, operator-initiated manipulation such as turning valves and flipping levers; no autonomous in-situ machine reassembly is offered.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly/reassembly systems in remanufacturing (industry overview, no single named system)

tasks.label: Lubricate or apply adhesives or other materials to machines, machine parts, or other equipment according to specified procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled grease-gun PM route on fixed production machinery inside a plant: worker walks the line with a grease gun and lube cart, wipes and greases dozens of zerk fittings on motors, pillow blocks, conveyor take-ups, fans and gearboxes at floor level and on platforms, pumping the specified number of shots of the specified grease and checking for purge.

Checking and topping off lubricant levels in service: reading sight glasses/dipsticks on gearboxes, hydraulic power units and compressors, adding oil to level, filling air-line lubricators, way-oil tanks and refilling automatic-lubricator/grease reservoirs from pails or drums.

Full oil change on a gearbox, hydraulic unit or compressor: drain hot oil into a container, dispose of used oil, remove and replace the spin-on or cartridge filter with a properly seated gasket, refill with the specified oil to level and check for leaks.

Lubricating parts and sub-assemblies during repair or overhaul at the bench or on the machine: packing bearings with grease, coating gears, cams, ways and slides with the specified lubricant, oiling chains and applying lube before reassembly.

Applying adhesives and other materials during machine repair/reassembly: RTV gasket maker on housing flanges, thread-locking compound on fasteners, anti-seize on bolts and shafts, retaining compound on bearing fits, epoxy patches — often in situ on the machine in awkward positions.

Lubricating outdoor and mobile equipment at yards, quarries, construction or field sites: greasing pins, bushings and pivot points on loaders, cranes, excavators and outdoor conveyors, plus spray lube on chains and cables, in dust, mud and weather, wherever the machine happens to sit.

tasks.label: Install, replace, or change machine parts and attachments, according to production specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant floor, installed production machinery: replace worn or failed mechanical components in place — bearings on shafts, V-belts and chains, seals, couplings, sprockets, rollers, small motors — plus non-quick-change wear items (slitter/mixer blades, screens, filters, wear liners). Lockout/tagout, partial disassembly in cramped access, fit and align the new part to spec, reassemble and test-run.

Product changeover on a machine or line in a factory: install/swap tooling and format change parts per the production spec for the next run — press-brake or press tooling, molds or mold inserts, forming and sealing tools, robot grippers, size/change parts on a filler or wrapper — then verify the first-off part/pack.

Scheduled replacement of machine-tool-type consumable tooling per tool-life or production spec in a machining/drilling operation: cutting tools and inserts, drills, punches, bits — pull the worn tool from the machine, load the correct replacement, set offsets, resume the run.

Install a new supplied component or attachment kit onto prepared mounting points per engineering/production spec: gearmotor, gearbox, pump, feeder attachment, guard or sensor bracket. Position the part, fit fasteners and dowels, torque to spec, function-check.

Field/mobile equipment with a machine-integrated changer: change the worn attachment (e.g., drill bit, with joint make/break) on a modern automated blasthole or drilling rig at a pit or site, from the cab or control room, in outdoor terrain and weather.

Field/mobile equipment, general: replace a part on machinery outdoors at a site or yard — hydraulic cylinder, belt, bearing, wear part on ag equipment, mobile crusher, or an outdoor conveyor — variable ground, weather, no fixed layout, hand and power tools only.

tasks.label: Set up and operate machines, and adjust controls to regulate operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-repair run-in of a production machine on a plant floor (packaging machine, press, conveyor, mixer, filler): the maintenance worker powers it up, jogs it, runs product through, and adjusts speed, tension, pressure, timing and stops until output and machine behavior are to spec; judged by sound, feel and product quality with the line waiting.

Maintenance machine shop: set up and operate a lathe, mill, drill press or grinder to fabricate or refurbish a replacement part (select and mount tooling and workholding, set feeds/speeds and offsets, run the cut, adjust as it cuts, check the part to a print).

Plant utility/auxiliary equipment in a boiler room, compressor house or pump room: line up and start a boiler, air compressor, chiller or pump set, throttle valves and adjust setpoints, and regulate operation while watching pressures, temperatures and amperage until conditions are steady.

Commissioning a newly installed or relocated machine: level and align it, connect utilities and guarding, load the program/controls, then run trials and dial in the controls over a shift until first-article output is accepted.

Field/mobile machinery at a variable outdoor site (farm tractor and implement, construction equipment, quarry crusher, well-site pump): after service, set the machine up on site and run it under load, adjusting controls to regulate the operation in as-found conditions.

sources.transferJustification: Directly covers 'operate machines and adjust controls to regulate operations': the robot cell runs the machine unattended and changes machine offsets/parameters in response to measured output, plus tool-breakage recovery, the same regulate-to-spec loop the worker performs after a repair.

Comparable objects (pedals, levers, starter), comparable precision (drive-trace tolerance), performed unattended in a purpose-built cell — the E1 form of 'operate machines and adjust controls to regulate operations'.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: the post-repair run-in and acceptance run of a rebuilt machine. Same purpose (verify and bed in a repaired machine by running it and regulating its operating conditions), performed by fixtured, automatically controlled rigs in a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Collaborate with other workers to repair or move machines, machine parts, or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Two-worker component replacement on a production machine on the plant floor: lock out the machine, break loose corroded fasteners, rig a motor/gearbox/pump/roll with a chain hoist while a partner guides and pries, remove the old unit, set and shim the new one, align the coupling, torque bolts, and run a test cycle.

Acting as the second pair of hands for a millwright, mechanic, or electrician: holding a part in position while the other bolts it, prying/aligning, catching shims and hardware, passing tools in and out of a cramped machine frame, and continually adjusting to verbal direction inside a factory.

Rigging and relocating a whole machine or large sub-assembly (press, conveyor section, packaging machine) across the plant with a forklift, overhead crane, jacks and machine skates, with several workers spotting, then setting it down, leveling, anchoring, and reconnecting it.

Fetching and transporting palletized or skidded replacement components, heavy tooling, and removed parts between receiving/storeroom/maintenance shop and the machine's location inside the plant, coordinating with coworkers and other traffic on marked aisles.

Field or outdoor two-person job: repairing or moving equipment at an off-site or outdoor location (quarry conveyor, farm or yard equipment, wastewater plant, rooftop or outdoor skid) on uneven ground, in weather, with a layout that differs at every site.

Crew teardown and reassembly in a washdown food/beverage plant: several workers disassemble a filler or packaging machine for repair or changeover, replace worn parts, reassemble under sanitary rules, and hand it back to production operators for a test run on wet floors.

sources.claim: Seegrid autonomous mobile robots for palletized material handling are deployed at scale inside manufacturing, warehousing and logistics facilities, having logged tens of millions of autonomous production miles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intralogistics transport of palletized loads. It carries over to the 'move machine parts/equipment' portion of this task because the objects (heavy palletized components on standard pallets/skids), the plant-floor environment, and the placement precision required are the same as when a maintenance worker moves a skidded replacement component across the plant.

sources.claim: The Palion Lift autonomous lift truck picks up, transports and places palletized loads at heights up to six feet, operating in dynamic facilities alongside human coworkers with little or no facility change.

sources.system: Vecna ATG Autonomous Tugger

sources.claim: A commercially offered autonomous tugger hauls heavy loads and carts for line-side delivery and work-in-progress moves inside manufacturing plants at payloads near 10,000 lb.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy cart/load transport inside a plant. Maintenance crews move heavy parts and equipment on carts and skids over the same aisles at the same payload class, so the transport portion transfers directly.

sources.title: The Growing Intelligence of Autonomous Mobile Robots | ISA InTech
sources.claim: MiR autonomous mobile robots move production components between lines inside an appliance factory, replacing manual transport by workers.

sources.system: Figure 02 / Figure 03 humanoid at BMW Plant Spartanburg

tasks.label: Read work orders and specifications to determine machines and equipment requiring repair or maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Inspect or test damaged machine parts, and mark defective areas or advise supervisors of repair needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ inspection of a suspect or damaged component on a production machine during PM or after a fault call: the worker opens a guard/access panel, looks and feels for wear, cracks, scoring, shaft play, chain stretch, seal leaks, rotates parts by hand, then marks the bad area with a paint pen or red-tags the machine and writes the repair need up for the supervisor. Plant floor, machine locked out, cramped access.

Bench inspection in the maintenance shop of a part already removed from a machine (bearing, gear, sprocket, shaft, bushing, hydraulic cylinder, pump impeller): clean it, measure with micrometer/calipers/bore gauge against spec, look for cracks, spalling, wear ridges; mark the defective areas and recommend repair versus replacement to the supervisor.

Routine condition-check round of operating equipment on the plant floor while doing lube/PM work: walk a fixed route looking for leaks and belt/chain wear, listening for abnormal noise, reading gauges and sight glasses, checking bearing housings for heat with an IR gun; log findings and report items needing repair.

Instrumented predictive testing of plant rotating equipment: ultrasonic bearing and compressed-air leak survey, thermal imaging of motors/couplings/electrical panels, vibration readings at defined measurement points, compared against baselines; write up severity and advise the supervisor which machines need repair and when.

Inspecting damaged equipment at an off-site, outdoor or non-standard location: rooftop or yard-parked equipment, a remote conveyor drive or pump at a quarry/grain site, mobile machinery parked in a lot, or a customer site; unknown layout, weather, awkward access, no fixed route.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-service wheelset NDT.
