tasks.label: Start machines and observe mechanical operation to determine efficiency and to detect problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant floor: after lubrication, belt/bearing change or other PM on a production or process machine (packaging machine, conveyor drive, press, mixer), the worker clears guards, resets faults at the local panel, starts the machine, runs it through several cycles, and watches/listens for abnormal noise, vibration, heat, leaks and correct speed/output before releasing it to production.

Scheduled test run and condition check of installed rotating equipment in an industrial plant (pumps, blowers, compressors, fans, standby units): worker starts the unit at a local starter or panel, lets it come up to speed, checks gauges/amps, feels bearing housings, listens for cavitation or bearing noise, and logs condition or writes up a defect.

Institutional building or facility equipment (hospital, hotel, school, warehouse, laundry/kitchen/packaging equipment, chillers, boilers, air handlers, compressors in mechanical rooms): worker starts the unit after service, observes operation, reads panel gauges and stack/alarm indicators, and judges whether it runs correctly.

Maintenance shop bench/test-stand run of a rebuilt or newly assembled component or small machine (electric motor, gearbox, pump, hydraulic power unit, small conveyor drive): worker mounts it, starts it, runs it up through speeds/loads, and observes for leaks, noise, vibration, heat and correct performance.

Mobile or field machinery at a farm, construction/mining site, or customer premises, often outdoors and in varying weather and clutter: worker starts the engine/hydraulics, cycles the machine's functions, and listens and watches for problems; layout and machine model differ site to site.

sources.system: Flexxbotics FlexxCORE / Intelligent Recovery with FANUC RoboDrill machine-tending cells (Ruland Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robot-Driven Manufacturing Enables "Lights-Out" Production
sources.claim: In a lights-out machining deployment at Ruland Manufacturing, the Flexxbotics-connected robot cell autonomously restarts machine operation after non-safety work stops, then keeps monitoring subsequent operations to identify recurring problems and alerts an engineer — starting machine cycles and observing operation for faults inside a purpose-built robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic machine tending / lights-out machining. Transfer: the system commands and restarts the machine's running cycle and then monitors its operation to detect recurring abnormal behaviour and raise an alert — the same start-and-watch-for-trouble loop, on the same class of production machine, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: FANUC CRX-20iA/L mobile manipulator on OTTO AMR (mobile machine tending)
sources.title: Have You Considered Mobile Cobots for Machine Tending? | FANUC CRX
sources.claim: A FANUC mobile manipulator (CRX cobot on an OTTO AMR) servicing CNC machines autonomously presses the machine's physical cycle-start button and then checks the machine's stack light to confirm it is actually running before leaving the station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine tending. Moving equipment along constrained internal routes: through doorways and roll-up doors, onto freight elevators to another floor, down narrow aisles between running machines, around other trades' work, in a plant, hospital plant room, food plant or utility building.

Field/outdoor transport at a site taken as found: moving tools and parts across unpaved or cluttered ground at a quarry, well site, farm, customer site or temporary outdoor installation, over gravel, mud, curbs and in weather, to equipment with no fixed layout.

Housekeeping of the immediate work area: sweeping or shop-vaccing metal chips, swarf, dust, broken hardware and absorbent from floors and machine bases in tight spaces around and under equipment, wiping up spilled oil/coolant, and dumping the collected debris and used rags into the correct refuse containers.

tasks.label: Inventory and requisition machine parts, equipment, and other supplies so that stock can be maintained and replenished.

instances.label: Day-to-day point-of-use stock control inside the plant: while doing routine machinery maintenance the worker draws bearings, seals, V-belts, filters and fittings from the maintenance crib or satellite bins near the machines, records the withdrawal, sees items at or below min, and enters a requisition in the CMMS so the storeroom is replenished. Shelving and bins are labeled, the facility is institution-controlled.

Scheduled cycle count or annual physical inventory of the maintenance storeroom: walking barcoded shelving and pallet racking, counting boxed spares (bearings, motors, gearbox kits, filters) and packaged consumables plus some loose small hardware in open bins, reconciling counts against CMMS records, flagging discrepancies and producing a reorder list.

Receiving and put-away: a pallet or several cartons of ordered parts arrive at the shop dock; the worker checks items against the packing slip/PO, unpacks, labels, places each item into its assigned shelf bin or rack location (some heavy items onto racking), and updates stock records.

Consumables and bulk supplies check across shop and plant: lube oil drums and totes, grease cartridges, coolant, hydraulic fluid, filters, rags, gloves and PPE, welding gas cylinders held at scattered points including a yard or lube room; estimate remaining quantities/levels and order replenishment.

Sourcing a specific non-stock item: after a failure or during a rebuild the worker takes the worn component, reads the nameplate or measures dimensions (shaft size, bolt pattern, seal ID/OD), cross-references OEM/vendor catalogs, confirms fit, and submits a purchase requisition with the correct part number ... quantity.

Mobile/field variant: a technician covering multiple sites (customer plants, remote pump stations, farms, job trailers) inventories the parts, fluids and supplies carried in the service truck and stashed at remote sites, and requisitions restock; layout differs site to site and no institution keeps the space to a standard.

tasks.label: Remove hardened material from machines or machine parts, using abrasives, power and hand tools, jackhammers, sledgehammers, or other equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant maintenance shop: hardened process residue (cured rubber/resin, set adhesive, baked-on food or slurry) is removed from machine components that were pulled off the machine — molds, dies, screens, mixer blades, extruder screws, pump impellers — using wire wheels, abrasive pads/blast cabinet, scrapers and hand grinders until the part is clean enough to reinstall.

In-situ inside a fixed machine during a scheduled shutdown: worker reaches or climbs into a hopper, chute, mixer housing, dryer or conveyor casing and chips out hardened caked material with an air chisel, chipping hammer, scraper and sledge; confined, dark, deposits of unpredictable shape and hardness, must not damage liners or shell.

Process plant outage: hardened scale, coke and product deposits removed from heat-transfer internals — heat exchanger/cooler tube bundles, condenser tubes, jackets — using high-pressure water lancing, rotary nozzles or mechanical rodding on a cleaning pad or in place, until flow/heat duty is restored.

Heavy hardened-mass removal: solidified concrete in a mixer or pump, slag/skull and spent refractory in ladles, crucibles and furnace parts, packed ore on crusher chute liners — broken out with jackhammers, hydraulic breakers, flails and sledgehammers; hot, dusty, heavy debris handling.

Surface preparation before repair or reassembly: grinding rust, mill scale, weld spatter, hardened paint and baked gasket/sealant off machine frames, housings, shafts, flanges and mating faces with angle grinders, needle scalers and wire wheels — often overhead or in awkward positions on the plant floor, judged by feel and eye.

Field/mobile maintenance at a site the employer does not control — a customer's yard, a farm, a construction site, a remote pump or compressor station — clearing hardened buildup from equipment with portable grinders, chisels and breakers under whatever access, weather and lighting is found there.

tasks.label: Replace, empty, or replenish machine and equipment containers such as gas tanks or boxes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant floor, routine PM round: top up or refill fluid reservoirs on production machines — hydraulic tanks, gearbox/way-oil cups, centralized grease reservoirs, coolant sumps. Worker opens covers/fill caps, pumps or pours from drums, jugs and grease guns, checks sight glass/dipstick level, wipes spills, closes and logs.

Plant floor: empty or exchange machine collection containers — CNC chip/swarf bins, stamping scrap boxes, dust-collector drums, oil-skimmer and waste-oil catch containers. Worker pulls the full container from under the machine, wheels or forklifts it to a dumpster/waste area, dumps it, returns an empty one.

Plant and yard: refuel engine-driven equipment — diesel generators, air compressors, yard tractors, floor scrubbers — from a yard tank or fuel cans, and swap forklift LP propane cylinders (unlatch bracket, disconnect POL fitting, lift ~33 lb tank, connect and leak-check fresh tank).

Plant floor: replace pressurized gas cylinders and chemical containers feeding machines — welding shielding gas, CO2/N2 bottles, nitrogen for accumulators, chemical drums/totes with dip tubes. Includes closing valves, cracking regulators loose, chaining/securing cylinders, reconnecting and leak-checking.

Plant floor: replenish consumable containers on machines — resin/pellet hoppers, hot-melt adhesive tanks, ink/solvent reservoirs, salt or chemical containers on washers, desiccant boxes, lubricant misters — from bags, pails or totes, then restart the machine.

Field/outdoor service at an unstructured site: fuel and refill containers on machinery at a quarry face, farm, construction site, remote pump/compressor station or customer premises; uneven ground, weather, no fixed layout, varied machine makes and fill points.

Field or non-standard site (equipment yard, farm, construction site, customer premises, outdoor mobile equipment): mix a bucket or sprayer of degreaser/cleaner from concentrate, or mix a two-part epoxy/repair compound, using whatever containers are at hand, and check it with test strips or by eye before use.

tasks.label: Replace defective parts of machine, or adjust clearances and alignment of moving parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant-floor / maintenance-shop rotating equipment repair: replace worn bearings, seals, mechanical seals or a coupling on a process pump, fan, blower or motor. Break loose corroded fasteners, pull seized components with pullers or induction heat, clean and inspect fits, press or heat-fit the new bearing, renew seals, reassemble and torque to spec, verify by hand rotation and vibration check.

Precision shaft alignment of a driver-driven train (motor to pump or gearbox): check soft foot, take dial-indicator or laser readings of offset and angularity, calculate and cut/insert shims under feet, move the machine with jackbolts, retorque hold-down bolts, and re-shoot until within ~0.002 in tolerance; also set coupling gap and, where applicable, thermal growth targets.

Conveyor idler/carrying roller change-out in a mill, mine, plant or distribution center: identify the failed roller, lift or lock out the belt, drop the worn roller out of its brackets and seat a new standard roller, at repeated, standardized positions along the conveyor structure.

Other conveyor / production-line drivetrain component replacement: worn belts (including splicing or replacing V-belts), roller chain, sprockets, drive gearbox or motor, followed by belt tracking, take-up tension and chain tension adjustment to running specification.

Clearance adjustment and part swap on production machinery: set gib/way clearance on a machine tool, shear or slitter blade gap, gear backlash, clutch/brake air gap, knife or guide clearance on a packaging or converting machine, using feeler gauges, dial indicators and OEM specs, often after replacing the worn component.

Heavy wear-part replacement at a harsh or field site: mill liner plates inside a SAG/ball mill at a concentrator, crusher mantle/concave or wear liners, paper machine roll, or a wind-turbine drivetrain component; requires rigging/cranes, confined space or work at height, weather and dirt exposure.

tasks.label: Align machines or equipment, using hoists, jacks, hand tools, squares, rules, micrometers, lasers, or plumb bobs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Precision shaft alignment of an installed rotating-equipment train (electric motor to pump, fan, blower or gearbox) on an operating plant floor (paper mill, refinery, food plant, power house). Millwright mounts a laser alignment system or dial indicators, checks soft foot, loosens hold-down bolts, jacks and shifts the machine, adds/removes shim stock under feet, re-torques and re-verifies offset/angularity to spec. Confined access, hot, dirty, other trades nearby.

Setting and leveling a new or relocated machine on its foundation inside a plant or shop: rigging with chain hoists/crane and jacks, setting on sole plates and shims or leveling screws, establishing centerlines with piano wire, plumb bob or laser, leveling to ~0.001 in/ft with precision level, then anchor bolting and grouting.

Aligning power-transmission and material-handling components on plant lines: conveyor head/tail pulleys and idlers, chain sprockets, belt sheaves, drive shafts and couplings on packaging, processing or milling equipment, using straightedge, laser pulley alignment tool, squares, rules, shims and hand tools.

Internal alignment during machine rebuild or overhaul: setting bearing housings and bores, gear mesh/backlash and bearing preload with dial indicators, feeler gauges and micrometers, aligning press rams, gibs and slides, selecting shims to specified clearances — performed in the maintenance shop or on the machine in place.

Field alignment at an unstructured site: greenfield or expansion construction site, mine, quarry or outdoor bulk-handling terminal — aligning a crusher drive, conveyor drive unit, fan or pump skid on new foundations, with mobile crane rigging, weather, mud, temporary access and site-to-site variation.

Shop assembly and alignment of a machine, drive package or skid before shipment/installation: parts staged on stands and fixtures under an overhead crane, good lighting and access, alignment of motor-gearbox-driven-unit on a fabricated base, doweling and bolting to specified tolerances.
