It requires bringing mating rotating machine elements (splined shafts, meshing gears) into specified relative position within tolerances tighter than typical coupling-alignment specs and securing them — the same functional outcome as a millwright aligning a driver to a driven machine — but only with parts fixtured and presented in a fenced cell.

sources.system: FANUC lights-out robot assembly plant (Oshino)
sources.title: Industry Insights: Should Manufacturers Turn Off The Lights? (A3/Automate)
sources.claim: FANUC's Oshino, Japan facility runs lights-out: industrial robots assemble other industrial ... — mounting servomotors, reducers and housings and torquing fasteners — unattended in purpose-built cells, producing thousands of robots per month.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembly of machinery (robot arms). Assembling a robot requires aligning gearboxes, motors and housings concentrically on machined interfaces and torquing bolts to spec — the alignment-and-fasten outcome of the millwright task — demonstrated autonomously, but only in a fenced, fixtured cell.

sources.system: FANUC M-2000iA/2300
sources.title: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 Robot | 2.3t Heavy Payload Robot
sources.claim: Ultra-heavy-payload industrial robots handle 2.3 tonne loads and precisely lift and position whole cars or bulky castings onto machine fixtures, replacing cranes and lifters inside fenced cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy part handling and placement onto fixtures. It substantiates the hoist/jack element of the alignment task at E1 — machine-scale masses can be raised and set into a fixtured position by machine, though only where fixtures define the target position.

sources.system: ABB e-motor assembly modular cells
sources.title: Solutions for e-motor assembly | ABB
sources.claim: ABB supplies robots and modular cells for electric-motor final assembly, including magnetic rotor and stator assembly, i.e. concentric insertion of a rotor into a stator with controlled air gap in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: e-motor assembly. Rotor-into-stator insertion demands concentric alignment of rotating machine elements to small air-gap tolerances, comparable in precision to coupling and bearing-housing alignment, achieved by robots in fenced cells.

sources.system: Pyxis Technologies axle/transaxle assembly cells and shim gauges
sources.title: Pyxis Technologies Inc - Automated Assembly Machine Production Gauges
sources.claim: Automated production cells for axle/transaxle assembly include gauging stations that measure backlash and differential case/bearing preload and select shims, with fully automatic stations used where the process sequence is ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measurement-driven shim selection in powertrain assembly, the closest industrial analogue to a millwright's measure-and-shim loop; cited only as context because the degree of unattended operation of shim placement is not established.

sources.system: Boltron autonomous flange bolting robot
sources.title: TMT Boltron – Autonomous Flange Bolting Robot (product brochure)
sources.claim: An autonomous flange-bolting robot is offered for use in refineries, alumina refineries, chemical and other production plants, performing bolt/nut make-up on flanges 500-4000 mm in diameter in harsh plant conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-plant bolting. It marks the state of the art for autonomous robots working on installed plant equipment — torque make-up on a located flange — and shows no capability for metrology-driven machine alignment, shimming or jacking in situ, supporting the negative judgments at E2/E3.

tasks.label: Insert shims, adjust tension on nuts and bolts, or position parts, using hand tools and measuring instruments, to set specified clearances between moving and stationary parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Operating industrial plant (paper mill, refinery, food plant): align a motor to a pump, fan or gearbox — loosen hold-down bolts, jack the machine, slide precut shim packs under the feet, retorque in sequence, and iterate against dial-indicator or laser alignment readings until offset/angularity is within a few thousandths of an inch; hot, dirty, cramped access around piping and guards.

Maintenance shop or on-machine overhaul: set internal running clearances while assembling a gearbox, pump, blower or bearing housing — bearing preload/end float, gear backlash and tooth contact, coupling gap, wear-ring and seal clearance — measured with feeler gauges, micrometers and dial indicators and adjusted with shim packs, locknuts and bolt-torque sequences.

New installation or relocation in a plant-expansion/construction area: set a machine base or soleplates on a concrete foundation — level with precision level and jacking screws, insert shim packs at anchor-bolt locations to bring level and elevation to spec, torque anchor bolts before grouting; site taken as found, dust, temporary lighting and power.

Outdoor field heavy equipment (mine crusher or conveyor, quarry screen, hydro/wind drivetrain, marine deck machinery): shim pillow blocks or drive units and tension large fasteners with hydraulic torque wrenches to bring specified clearances between rotating and stationary parts; weather, uneven footing, machine as found.

Factory production machinery adjustment during changeover or scheduled downtime: set press die shut height/clearance, knife-to-anvil or roller gap on a converting or packaging line, conveyor guide and take-up positions — loosen jam nuts, turn adjusters or add shims, check with feeler gauges, relock fasteners to torque.

sources.system: Broetje-Automation Rotary Torque System
sources.title: Ramping Up Wind Turbine Production with Torque Systems – Broetje-Automation delivers automated equipment to Siemens Gamesa
sources.claim: Automated Torque Systems delivered to Siemens Gamesa's offshore nacelle plant perform multi-stage tightening of large bolted connections on heavy turbine assemblies fully automatically in a purpose-built station.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'adjust tension on nuts and bolts' element on heavy machinery: staged tightening of large fasteners to specified preload, with the component brought to the machine in a factory station.

sources.system: Risong Technology flexible intelligent door assembly and adjustment line (Changan Mazda)
sources.title: Flexible Intelligent Door Assembly Line of Changan Mazda Automobile Co., Ltd. (IFR case study)
sources.claim: A fully automatic door/hood/lid assembly-and-adjustment line measures gaps, positions the panels under 3D laser vision guidance (0.1 mm accuracy) and tightens the mounting bolts with monitored torque to achieve specified fit gaps.
sources.transferJustification: Same structure as the task: measure the clearance, position the part to the specified gap, and tighten fasteners to torque — performed autonomously in a fixtured line at tenth-of-a-millimetre precision.

sources.system: Single-step shimming robot assembly cell
sources.title: Single Step Shimming Solution for Automated Aircraft Assembly
sources.claim: A robot assembly cell scans joining surfaces, computes the 3D gap and fills it with shim material in one step before robotically positioning and joining a large aircraft structural part, replacing manual shimming.
sources.transferJustification: This is the shim-insertion element of the task: measurement-derived shim thickness placed between mating parts, then the part positioned and fastened to a specified gap, at sub-millimetre precision, in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Marposs shim determination and verification gauging line
sources.title: MARPOSS gauging line for gear inspection
sources.claim: Commercial automatic gauging stations integrated in transmission assembly lines determine the shims needed to position components and to set tapered-bearing preload and gear backlash to specification.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the measure-and-shim element: machine-side determination of shim thickness to set bearing preload and gear backlash — specified clearances between moving and stationary parts — inside automatic assembly lines.

sources.system: Fori Automation Fully Automatic Toe Set system
sources.title: Toe Tool Systems - Fori Automation
sources.claim: End-of-line wheel alignment stations automatically engage tie-rod adjusting nuts with powered heads and turn them until the measured geometry is within specification, then lock the fasteners.
sources.transferJustification: Closed-loop 'measure, turn the adjusting nut, re-measure, torque' to hit a geometric specification — the same control loop a millwright uses when adjusting nuts to set a specified clearance, in a purpose-built station.

sources.system: Vision- and force-guided robotic bolt-tightening cells
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines
sources.claim: Industrial robots perform bolt tightening on automotive assembly lines using 3D vision and force sensing to locate and engage fasteners under production conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that sensor-guided robotic fastener tightening to specification, rather than purely scripted motion, is routine in structured factory stations — the fastener-tensioning element of this task.

sources.system: Robot-guided adaptive bolt tensioning system (Reis robot with self-adaptive tensioning tool)
sources.title: An adaptive and automated bolt tensioning system for the pitch bearing assembly of wind turbines
sources.claim: A robot-guided, self-adaptive bolt tensioning tool with adaptive process control was used to assemble the pitch bearing bolts of a roughly 25 t Gamesa wind turbine rotor hub in a factory setting.
sources.transferJustification: Heavy-machinery bolt tensioning to a controlled preload on components of the scale millwrights handle, but with the work brought to a fixed robot station rather than the robot going to the machine.

sources.system: Aerones robotic wind turbine maintenance platform
sources.title: How Aerones Is Redefining Wind Turbine Maintenance with Robots and AI
sources.claim: The most advanced fielded robots working on installed heavy machinery (wind turbines) are remotely operated and confined to inspection, cleaning, coating and blade repair; they do not shim, align or tension fasteners.
sources.transferJustification: Negative context for in-situ E2/E3 work: fielded robots that go to installed heavy machinery are teleoperated and perform no clearance-setting, shimming or fastener tensioning.

tasks.label: Signal crane operator to lower basic assembly units to bedplate, and align unit to centerline.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Operating process plant (paper mill, food or chemical plant): a 1–10 ton pump, motor, blower or gearbox assembly is picked by the plant's overhead bridge crane; the millwright rigs it, gives hand/radio signals to the crane operator to walk and lower it past piping and existing equipment, guides it down over anchor bolts onto the bedplate, and pries/jacks it to the scribed centerlines before shimming.

New machine installation or line relocation inside a manufacturing facility: a machine base, press frame, machining center or conveyor drive unit is set onto a soleplate/bedplate located from layout blueprints; mobile or plant crane, load shared floor with other trades, unit landed and brought to layout centerlines with bars, jacks and a tape/laser.

Greenfield or outdoor erection (construction site, refinery, mine, wind or power project): compressor skid, crusher, turbine module or large fan assembly lifted by a crawler/hydraulic mobile crane onto a concrete foundation; signalperson works with taglines, wind, mud and changing site layout, then aligns the unit to foundation centerlines and anchor-bolt pattern.

Shop or fabrication-floor sub-assembly: motor, gearbox or bearing housing under ~2 tons set with a jib crane or chain hoist onto a fabricated bedplate/subbase at a bench or layout table; short, repeatable lift, alignment to scribed centerline marks before bolting.

Precision heavy element during a plant outage: turbine casing/rotor, large reducer or press crown lowered onto a bedplate or soleplate over guide pins with clearances of a few thousandths; multiple riggers, chainfalls and jacks, inch-by-inch signaling to the crane operator, alignment to centerline verified with wires, laser or indicators.

sources.system: Dürr (CPM) flex decking / marriage station
sources.title: NEXT.assembly: New body marriage trends with flex decking - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr/CPM flex decking marriage stations automatically join a car body to its heavy mechanical assembly carried on a pallet, using programmable grippers and machine vision to bring all parts into the correct position for bolting — an automated, fixtured version of lowering an assembly unit onto a base and aligning it before fastening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive 'marriage' (mating a heavy powertrain/chassis assembly to a body). Transfer: it is the same physical act as landing an assembly unit on a bedplate — a multi-hundred-kilogram unit is raised/lowered into contact with a receiving structure, brought to design centerline by vision-driven positioning, and bolted, all under machine control in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Flexible decking line, FCA/Stellantis Melfi plant
sources.date: article page dated 2025-07 (line in production since ~2015)
sources.title: Fiat Melfi: The billion-euro factory | Automotive Manufacturing Solutions
sources.claim: A production flexible decking line at the Fiat Melfi plant mates body and powertrain in 54 seconds with camera-measured positional accuracy and robot arms pulling suspension struts into position, showing the automated mate-and-align operation running in volume production.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (body/powertrain marriage); cited to establish that the automated mate-and-align operation is deployed in real production, not only demonstrated.

sources.system: Beckwood Automated Die Storage & Retrieval System (ASRS) / quick die change
sources.title: Quick Die Change Technology | Beckwood Press
sources.claim: Automated die storage and retrieval systems shuttle a heavy die out of storage into a press, position it on the bolster and hydraulically clamp it, completing the die change automatically — i.e., a heavy unit is brought to a machine bedplate, located and secured under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic die change. Transfer: the die is a multi-ton assembly unit lowered/transferred onto a press bolster (a bedplate) and located to the press centerline by keys and locators, then clamped — comparable mass, comparable location tolerance, machine-controlled throughout.

sources.system: Rolling (moving) bolster quick die change systems
sources.developer: various press builders (Macrodyne, Beckwood, Atlas, etc.)
sources.title: Quick Die Change (QDC) in Stamping: Die Carts, Rolling Bolsters and Hydraulic Clamps
sources.claim: In big presses and tandem press lines the die sets handled by rolling-bolster automatic die change weigh tens of tons, establishing that machine-controlled placement of heavy units onto a machine bedplate is routine at millwright-scale masses.
sources.transferJustification: Supporting context on payload scale for the die-change evidence; not decisive on its own because the degree of autonomy of the specific systems described is not stated.

sources.system: A320 fuselage structure assembly line (Hamburg)
sources.title: Airbus inaugurates new A320 structure assembly line in Hamburg
sources.claim: Airbus' A320 fuselage structure assembly line in Hamburg performs automated positioning of large fuselage sections using laser measurement together with 20 robots, in serial production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated positioning and joining of large aerostructures. Transfer: multi-tonne structures are moved into a datum position measured against a reference (the aerospace equivalent of a centerline) by machine-controlled positioners, matching or exceeding the precision a millwright achieves in aligning a unit to a bedplate centerline.

sources.system: Posture alignment and joining test system for large aircraft fuselages (NC localizers + laser tracker)
sources.developer: Zhejiang University / aerospace assembly research groups
sources.title: Posture alignment and joining test system for large aircraft fuselages
sources.claim: A posture alignment and joining system drives multiple three-coordinate numerically controlled localizers from laser-tracker measurements to align large aircraft fuselages, achieving position adjustment uncertainty below 0.16 mm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: six-degree-of-freedom alignment of a large heavy component to a measured datum. Transfer: this is precisely the 'align unit to centerline' step performed by metrology-fed automatic positioners, at tolerances tighter than millwright centerline alignment on a bedplate.

sources.system: FANUC M-2000iA/2300
sources.title: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 Robot - Ultra Heavy Payload Robot | FANUC America
sources.claim: The FANUC M-2000iA/2300 is a commercially available six-axis robot with a 2.3 tonne payload marketed as able to replace cranes, lifters and shuttles for heavy material handling inside industrial cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy part handling and placement in fenced cells. Transfer: shows that ton-class assembly units can be lifted and set down repeatably by machine control in a purpose-built cell, which is the lifting element of landing a unit on a bedplate.

tasks.label: Conduct preventative maintenance and repair, and lubricate machines and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine lubrication route inside a manufacturing/processing plant: millwright walks an assigned PM route greasing zerk fittings on motor and conveyor bearings, checking gearbox sight glasses and topping off oil, wiping fittings, replacing missing grease caps, and logging each point.

Scheduled PM service on one production machine or line during planned downtime: drain and refill gear oil, change filters and breathers, replace worn V-belts/chains and sprockets, re-tension and track belts, torque fasteners to spec, clean and adjust guards.

Corrective repair of a failed drive component in place: pull coupling guards, break loose seized fasteners, use pullers/heat to remove worn bearings, seals or couplings on a pump, fan or gearbox, install replacements, re-shim and align, then test-run.

PM condition-monitoring round in a plant: follow a fixed route past pumps, motors, mills and compressors taking thermal, acoustic/ultrasonic and gauge/sight-glass readings, note abnormal noise, heat or leaks, and log/flag anomalies for work orders.

PM and repair on heavy equipment at outdoor or remote sites: quarry crusher, mine or grain-elevator conveyor, wind turbine drivetrain or tower bolts, working at height, on rough terrain, in weather and confined spaces with rigging and portable tools.

sources.system: ANYmal (ANYbotics)
sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped runs fully autonomous nightly PM inspection rounds in a working cement plant, covering 450+ checkpoints across six levels and ..., detecting overheating bearings, cracks and leaks.
sources.transferJustification: Condition-monitoring rounds are the inspection half of preventative maintenance: same assets (pumps, mills, bearings), same route-based checks of temperature, noise and gauges that a millwright performs on a PM round.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit/Autowalk inspection payloads
sources.title: Boston Dynamics' robot dog patrols 1.5 million-square-foot factory
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot is deployed for autonomous routine equipment inspection rounds in a 1.5M sq ft aerospace manufacturing plant using thermal and acoustic imaging payloads.
sources.transferJustification: Same PM inspection-round content as a millwright's condition-monitoring route in a structured plant.

sources.system: Spot Arm
sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot's manipulation of plant hardware (valves, levers) remains semi-autonomous/operator-triggered; only door opening became available inside autonomous missions, so hands-on maintenance manipulation in plants is not autonomous.

sources.system: DOPAG production cell for automated grease metering (6-axis robot + lubriLine metering valves)
sources.title: Production cell for automated grease metering | DOPAG
sources.claim: A commercial purpose-built production cell uses a 6-axis robot with metered spray and shot valves to apply measured grease to specified interior and exterior surfaces of fixtured gear components.
sources.transferJustification: Transfer from assembly greasing to PM lubrication: identical act of applying a metered quantity of grease to designated lube points of a machine component held in a known, fixtured position, with flow-metered verification.

sources.system: Motoman robot grease-dispensing machine
sources.title: Automation Drives Grease-dispensing Machine
sources.claim: A commercial grease-dispensing machine uses a Motoman robot ... place a part and apply lubricating grease to five specified contact surfaces, with parts presented by a vibratory feeder.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as greasing designated lube points on machinery, performed on fixtured work presented to the robot in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Durr Somac automated filling stations
sources.title: Durr Filling Technology - The market leader
sources.claim: Durr Somac supplies fully automatic filling stations integrated into assembly lines that fill operating fluids such as engine oils and coolants and test the fill, on work presented in fixtured line positions.
sources.transferJustification: Transfer from assembly fluid filling to PM oil top-off: metered dispensing of oil into a machine's fill port at a fixtured, known position with level/quantity verification.

sources.system: Aerones robotic wind turbine maintenance platform
sources.title: These robots crawl all over wind turbines so humans don't have to
sources.claim: Aerones' robotic wind-turbine maintenance system (cleaning, coating, leading-edge repair) is winched up the tower and run by a crew of technicians operating it from the ground, i.e. remote human control rather than autonomous work.

sources.system: UR10e-based robotic unscrewing system for e-waste disassembly
sources.developer: academic research group (Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous disassembly is limited to isolated sub-steps such as vision- and force-guided unscrewing of fasteners in a laboratory cell; no cited system performs a whole machine teardown, part replacement and rebuild autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic analogue to millwright teardown work (fastener removal on worn assemblies); it shows only a single sub-step is automated, in a bench cell, not a complete repair.

tasks.label: Assemble and install equipment, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inside an operating manufacturing plant during a scheduled shutdown or line retrofit: uncrate and assemble a production machine (packaging, processing, press feed) from its subassemblies — frames, drives, gearboxes, guarding — set it on its baseplate/anchor bolts, torque fasteners to spec, level it and align the drive coupling, working amid existing equipment, overhead obstructions and other trades.

Assembling and installing conveyor and material-handling systems in a plant or distribution center: bolting conveyor sections, supports, drives, take-ups and guarding together to layout drawings, floor-mounting or hanging from structure, then aligning and tensioning belts/chains with hand and power tools.

Setting and assembling large rotating equipment (pumps, gearboxes, blowers, fans, small turbines) on foundations at a power plant, paper mill, mine or refinery: rigging the unit onto soleplates, shimming and leveling, torquing anchor and flange bolts with powered wrenches, installing couplings and performing precision shaft alignment.

Greenfield/new-build plant construction: field assembly of crated equipment modules (mills, crushers, screens, silo drives, bucket elevators) on an open construction site with crane support, weather, uneven ground and temporary access, bolting large sections together per erection drawings.

Field-service installation at varied customer sites (farms, quarries, small shops, remote facilities): fitting and tying new equipment into pre-existing structures and machines, fabricating and bolting supports on the spot, working in cramped, non-standard, uncontrolled conditions.

sources.system: KUKA robotic engine-block assembly line (Scania powertrain)
sources.title: Engine block assembly line for Scania's trucks of tomorrow | KUKA AG
sources.claim: A 105-m Scania engine-block assembly line built by KUKA uses 15 robots and 13 fully automated stations that bolt and join heavy machine components — bearing caps, up to 38 cylinder-head bolts, cylinder-head cover, oil-cooler module — with robot-mounted powered screwdrivers in a fenced, fixtured production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory assembly of machinery (a truck engine) rather than plant installation. Transfer holds for the E1 counterfactual: the objects are multi-hundred-kilogram cast machine housings joined with torque-controlled threaded fasteners driven by power tools, the same joining operations and torque/precision class a millwright performs, differing only in that fixtures and conveyors present the work.

sources.system: Dürr Flex Bolt automatic bolting system (Flex decking)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved; product in series production use)
sources.title: Flex Bolt, Automatic Bolting System - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's Flex Bolt is a commercial automatic bolting system used in vehicle final assembly: after the marriage station joins the mechanical modules (powertrain, axles) to the body, Flex Bolt stations bolt the underbody from below in a completely automatic process, verify tightening, and can repeat a screwing operation without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting and bolting heavy mechanical assemblies (engine/transmission/axle modules) onto a supporting structure in a purpose-built line. This is the same physical act as a millwright mounting equipment onto a base and torquing its fasteners; precision and torque verification are equivalent, with the workpiece brought fixtured to the machine.

sources.system: 3D-vision-guided robotic bolt-tightening cell (INESC TEC / automaker assembly line)
sources.developer: Institute for Systems and Computer Engineering, Technology and Science (INESC TEC)
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A vision-guided industrial robot now performs the bolt tightening of rear axle dampers on a van assembly line, using 3D vision and force sensors to locate the attachment structure despite conveyor tolerances and vehicle-weight-induced position variation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered fastening of a mechanical component to a larger structure. It shows robots meeting production torque/quality requirements on real, imperfectly positioned workpieces using 3D vision and force control — the tolerance-absorbing capability a fixtured cell would need for millwright-type bolting.

sources.system: KUKA flexFELLOW mobile assembly robot
sources.title: Automated assembly with KUKA assembly robots | KUKA Global
sources.claim: KUKA's flexFELLOW mobile robot unit performs the installation of pump wells ... a dishwasher production line, i.e., a robot fitting a pump assembly into a machine on a running production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing a pump sub-unit into equipment on a production line. Comparable to a millwright fitting and fastening a pump/drive component, at smaller scale, with the work presented by the line — the E1 presentation condition.

sources.system: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 heavy payload robot
sources.date: 2016-10-03 (product line, still commercially sold as of 2026)
sources.title: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 Robot | 2.3t Heavy Payload Robot
sources.claim: FANUC's M-2000iA ultra-heavy-payload industrial robots handle up to 2,300 kg and are used to lift and position entire cars or bulky castings onto machine fixtures, doing work otherwise done by cranes and lifters.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy rigging and placement. Millwright installation requires setting multi-hundred-kilogram to multi-ton machine components onto bases; this shows fixtured industrial robots handle that mass class and place it on fixtures, the E1 analogue of rigging a unit onto its soleplate.

sources.system: UBTech Walker S1 humanoid
sources.title: BYD's China factory employs Walker S1 humanoid robot for manual work
sources.claim: The most advanced mobile/humanoid robots reported inside real human work facilities (auto plants) perform only light, presented-part operations such as tightening screws on car doors, inspection and parts carrying, in pilot deployments — not assembly or installation of industrial machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to characterise the ceiling of in-facility (E2) robotic capability: light screwdriving on presented car parts in a pilot with unverified autonomy, far short of assembling and installing heavy plant machinery; it supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Assemble machines, and bolt, weld, rivet, or otherwise fasten them to foundation or other structures, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inside an operating manufacturing plant (food, paper, auto parts, packaging): setting a pump, motor, gearbox, press, conveyor drive or packaging module onto its base/foundation and fastening it down — drilling or using existing anchors, driving hold-down bolts to torque, occasionally tack/fillet welding a baseplate. Plant is in production nearby; power tools, impact wrenches, torque wrenches used.

Assembling a machine from shipped components or subassemblies in a shop, maintenance bay or staging area next to the install point: bolting frame sections together, mounting drives, bearings, guards and covers with hand and power tools, following assembly drawings, before or as the unit is set.

Field welding or riveting connections that tie equipment to structure: welding baseplates, angle supports, clips and brackets to embed plates, structural steel or platforms, often in awkward, overhead or confined positions inside an industrial facility, with fit-up varying from as-found conditions.

Greenfield or capital-project installation at an industrial construction site: erecting and bolting up large equipment (conveyor runs, crushers, turbines, silos, process lines) on new foundations, coordinating with cranes and other trades, partly outdoors and amid changing site conditions.

Harsh or remote field settings — mines and quarries, pulp mills, wind turbine nacelles/towers, marine and elevated or confined spaces: assembling and fastening heavy equipment with large-diameter bolts, hydraulic torque tools and field welding, with restricted access, dust/weather and no standardized layout.

sources.system: Dürr flex decking / flex bolt marriage and automatic bolting stations
sources.title: NEXT.assembly: New body marriage trends with flex decking - Dürr
sources.claim: Automotive final-assembly 'marriage'/flex-decking stations join a heavy powertrain/chassis module to the vehicle structure and drive the underbody bolts in a fully automatic, fixtured, fenced line station with vision-guided positioning and torque verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting a heavy machine assembly (powertrain/suspension module) to a supporting structure with power nutrunners to specified torque. Same fastening action, comparable mass and bolt sizes to a millwright hold-down, performed with the work fixtured and presented as a purpose-built cell would present it.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 cells with 'Obsidian' AI
sources.title: The Technology - Path Robotics
sources.claim: Commercially sold intelligent welding cells scan each part, plan the weld path with AI and weld without programming, tolerating imperfect fit-up and part-to-part variation, with parts held by positioners inside the cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: structural welding of steel weldments (up to ship hulls and utility poles) with variable fit-up — the same welding operation a millwright performs on baseplates and brackets, but with the workpiece brought into a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Electroimpact low-voltage electromagnetic riveting workcells (Airbus Broughton)
sources.title: Automating the Riveting Process | Assembly Magazine
sources.claim: Airbus wing-panel workcells use fixtures plus an automated machine that drills and installs rivets, lockbolts, collars and temporary bolts in the panel — automated structural fastening in a purpose-built cell, in production since the 1990s.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: riveting and bolting one structural member to another with powered tooling. Objects are metal structural assemblies and required precision exceeds millwright hold-down work; supports the fastening element of this task at E1 only, since it depends on dedicated fixtures.

sources.system: FANUC lights-out robot assembly factory, Oshino, Japan
sources.title: Lights-Out Automation: Fact or Fiction? | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A production factory assembles complete machines (industrial robots) with automation running unattended for extended periods, with people present only for maintenance rather than to assemble products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a machine from components on an automated line. Demonstrates machine assembly to accepted quality when parts arrive fixtured and presented, i.e. in a purpose-built robotic environment.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E. (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler - The Construction Index
sources.claim: A self-climbing installation robot works autonomously from a digital plan in elevator shafts on live construction sites, measuring positions, drilling into concrete and setting anchor bolts; deployed at 36 job sites with roughly 50,000 anchor bolts installed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting anchor bolts into concrete structure at surveyed positions on an as-found site. It covers only the anchor-setting sub-step for one fixed geometry (a vertical shaft) and does not place, assemble or bolt down machinery, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot
sources.claim: A semi-autonomous mobile drilling robot drills anchor holes on construction sites from BIM data, with an operator positioning it and holes within reach drilled automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling anchor holes in unstructured jobsite conditions. It performs only the hole-drilling sub-step and requires operator repositioning, so it does not substantiate assembling or fastening machinery in the field.

sources.system: Figure 02 / Figure 03 humanoid at BMW Plant Spartanburg
sources.title: BMW Group to deploy humanoid robots in production in Germany for the first time
sources.claim: A humanoid robot worked daily shifts in an automotive body shop for about ten months, picking sheet-metal parts and placing them into welding fixtures — the current state of practice for mobile robots inside a structured production facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general mobile manipulation inside a structured factory. Cited to show that deployed in-facility humanoids perform part loading into fixtures, not machine erection and hold-down fastening, supporting the negative E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Move machinery and equipment, using hoists, dollies, rollers, and trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-plant relocation of a large production machine (a press, CNC machining center, pump/motor/gearbox skid, conveyor section, 5–40 tons) inside a manufacturing plant: sling and shackle it to lifting lugs, lift with the overhead bridge crane or chain falls, jack it onto machinery skates/rollers, walk it across the plant floor around columns, pipe runs and other equipment, and set it down at the new location.

Receiving or shipping a machine: unloading a crated or skid-mounted machine from a flatbed truck at a plant dock or yard using a forklift with extended forks, boom truck or mobile crane, choking and rigging the load, then moving it on dollies or a forklift into the building to the staging area.

Routine movement of palletized or skid-mounted equipment, spare parts, tooling, gearboxes and components across a plant floor with a pallet jack, forklift or cart, from the receiving/staging area or maintenance shop to the job location, sharing aisles with plant personnel and traffic.

Moving equipment through cramped or awkward access: down narrow aisles, through doorways, into basements, pits, mezzanines or between existing machines, using come-alongs, chain falls anchored to structure, hydraulic jacks, pipe rollers, cribbing and hand dollies, with inches of clearance and no crane coverage.

Field moves outdoors at a construction site, mine, refinery, or new plant build: moving machinery over uneven or unpaved ground with rollers, cribbing, skidding gear, mobile cranes and trucks, in weather and among other trades.

sources.system: KUKA omniMove heavy-duty AGV at AMAG Ranshofen
sources.title: Mobile KUKA omniMove automates transportation tasks | KUKA Germany
sources.claim: Two KUKA omniMove heavy-duty AGVs autonomously transport carrier frames loaded with multi-tonne aluminum plates through an operating rolling-mill production shop, picking up from and delivering to predetermined stations with ±5 mm precision; the platform variant carries up to 68 tonnes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated intralogistics transport of very heavy, machine-sized loads. It transfers to 'move machinery and equipment' because the loads (8.5 t carriers, up to 68 t capacity) exceed typical machinery weights and require the same precise set-down, but only when the load sits on a standardized transport carrier with a coded pick point.

sources.system: Morgan Automation automated coil-yard crane system (Siemens controls)
sources.title: US steel mill installs fully automated cranes system - Hoist
sources.claim: A US steel mill in ... operates a fully automated, unmanned three-crane system with coil transfer cars that grabs 28-ton hot coils, places them on saddles or transfer cars in the correct yard quadrant, and later retrieves them for shipment, running without crane operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated overhead-crane handling of 28-ton coils. It transfers to hoisting and moving machinery because it is the same class of hoist-and-place work at comparable weight and placement precision, but relies on a dedicated grab, known pick points and mapped set-down positions in a purpose-built crane bay.

sources.system: Seegrid Palion AMR fleet (autonomous lift trucks and tow tractors)
sources.title: Seegrid AMRs Surpass 17 Million Autonomous Miles Driven in Customer Facilities | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Seegrid autonomous lift trucks and tow ... perform pick, transport and drop of palletized loads in manufacturing, warehousing and logistics facilities that are shared with human workers, with over 17 million autonomous ... logged at customer sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous powered-industrial-truck transport of palletized material in working plants. Transfers to the millwright's cart/pallet-jack/forklift moves of equipment and parts because it is the same equipment, same facility floors, and the same pick-transport-place cycle.

sources.system: Seegrid Palion Lift AMR
sources.title: Seegrid Lift Autonomous Mobile Robot - Material Handling 24/7
sources.claim: The Seegrid Palion Lift autonomous mobile robot autonomously picks and transports payloads weighing up to 3,500 pounds and places them at height in customer facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the payload envelope of deployed autonomous forklifts, bounding which equipment moves an AMR can substitute for; the pick/place cycle is the same one a millwright performs with a forklift or pallet jack.

sources.system: Automatic stacking cranes (ASCs) at Long Beach Container Terminal
sources.title: What Makes Our Terminals Technologically Advanced? | Long Beach Container Terminal
sources.claim: Long Beach Container Terminal runs a fenced automated container yard in which 69 electric automatic stacking cranes lift and stack multi-ton containers driverlessly, with automated horizontal transport vehicles moving containers between the yard and the quay.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless crane lifting and precise placement of 20-30 ton standardized loads, including transfer to and from trucks. Transfers to hoisting machinery only where the load has standardized lift points (twistlocks) and defined positions inside a machine-dedicated, human-excluded block.

tasks.label: Level bedplate and establish centerline, using straightedge, levels, and transit.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Setting a multi-ton pump/compressor/driver baseplate or soleplates on a concrete foundation inside an operating process plant (refinery, chemical plant, paper mill): plate lowered over anchor bolts, brought up on jackscrews/wedges, leveled across machined mounting pads with machinist precision levels and straightedge to roughly 0.0005-0.002 in/ft, centerline and elevation transferred from plant benchmarks with transit/optical or laser level and scribed/punched, held true while anchor bolts are torqued and grout is placed.

Installing a machine tool, press, injection molder or packaging machine on a manufacturing plant floor: machine set on leveling wedge mounts/pads, leveled with precision level and straightedge across bed/ways and along the machine's length, soft foot removed with shim packs, centerline established relative to plant column grid lines or to adjacent machines in a line, iterative re-check after bolt torque.

Greenfield/outdoor heavy equipment installation on a construction or mine site (turbine-generator soleplates, crusher, ball mill, long conveyor line): transit or laser level shots from survey benchmarks over tens of meters, multiple soleplates brought to a common elevation plane and to a common machine centerline, work amid rebar, anchor pockets, mud, wind and temperature swings, layout differs site to site.

Maintenance re-leveling / re-establishing centerline on installed machinery in a plant: checking level and elevation of an existing bedplate that has settled or been disturbed, finding and correcting soft foot with shims, re-shooting the original centerline benchmarks with transit, often in cramped, oily, partially obstructed spaces around live equipment.

Shop/OEM pre-assembly work: leveling a fabricated skid or bedplate on blocking in a fabrication or rebuild shop before components are mounted or the unit is shipped, checking flatness/twist with straightedge and precision level, laying out and scribing machine centerlines and mounting-pad reference lines on the plate.

sources.system: Dusty Robotics FieldPrinter / FieldPrint Platform
sources.title: FieldPrinter autonomous robot automates jobsite layout - Construction Briefing
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics' FieldPrinter autonomously prints building-model layout lines (including equipment pads and centerlines) on finished floors at roughly 1/16 in accuracy and is in production use on many jobsites; it performs 2D marking only and does not measure or physically adjust the level of any workpiece.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction floor layout marking. It covers only the marking half of 'establish centerline' on a flat finished slab; it cannot lift, shim, or level a bedplate, cannot transfer elevations to machined pads, and so cannot complete this task's instances.

sources.system: HP SitePrint
sources.title: HP SitePrint - Robotic Layout Solution | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially sold autonomous layout robot that prints CAD linework (including anchor-bolt patterns and machine footprints) on floors at about +/-2 mm, and can log floor level deviations; it only measures floor deviation and cannot physically level or shim a machine base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic construction layout. Marking lines and reading floor deviations does not carry over to leveling a multi-ton bedplate with jackscrews and shim packs, nor to establishing elevations on machined mounting surfaces.

sources.system: Servomotor-driven leveling elements for machine tool frame-to-floor alignment
sources.title: Servomotor-driven leveling elements for machine tool frame-to-floor alignment - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: The closest demonstrated automation of machine-base leveling installs servomotors on the 12 leveling elements of a large 5-axis machine tool so a technician can drive the alignment remotely; the human remains in the control loop, and no centerline layout is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act (leveling a machine base on its foundation), but it is technician-driven remote actuation rather than autonomous operation, so it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.system: AAAM automatic machine alignment with 'smart feet'
sources.developer: Kovosvit MAS / CTU in Prague RCMT
sources.title: AUTOMATIC MACHINE TOOL ALIGNMENT ON ITS FOUNDATION - MM Science Journal
sources.claim: A published method for automatic alignment of a machine tool on its foundation using motorized 'smart feet' exists, but the reported results are from a simulation/algorithm case study (state-space and FEM models, PLC algorithm), not a deployed autonomous system leveling a real bedplate.
sources.transferJustification: Same act (leveling a machine on its base), but the demonstration is a virtual machine model and control algorithm rather than a named system shown completing a real leveling job, so it cannot substantiate completion.

sources.system: Enerpac Synchronous Lifting System (EVO/EVOP series)
sources.title: Enerpac Synchronous Lifting Systems | WB Equipment Network
sources.claim: Commercial machine-controlled synchronous hydraulic lifting systems used for heavy machinery installation hold multi-point loads level to roughly 1 mm under closed-loop control, an order of magnitude coarser than millwright bedplate leveling tolerances, and they are operator-supervised and do not establish centerlines or place shims.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: synchronized lifting/positioning of heavy loads. Precision (~1 mm) is far coarser than the 0.0005-0.002 in/ft leveling tolerance for bedplates, and the system performs no measurement of level across machined pads and no centerline layout.

sources.system: Newport S-2000A pneumatic isolators with automatic re-leveling / Fabreeka PAL
sources.title: S-2000A Pneumatic Vibration Isolators with Automatic Re-Leveling | Newport
sources.claim: Automatic pneumatic leveling isolator systems level and hold heavy precision payloads under mechanical closed-loop control, but standard height-control valve repeatability is about 0.25 mm and the systems are permanent machine mounts, not a means of leveling and laying out a bedplate on a foundation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic height/level maintenance of a heavy payload. It maintains a preset height rather than surveying and setting a bedplate to a specified level and centerline, and its repeatability is coarser than millwright leveling tolerances.

tasks.label: Dismantle machines, using hammers, wrenches, crowbars, and other hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Maintenance-shop teardown of a standard rotating-equipment unit brought in for overhaul (electric motor, centrifugal pump, gearmotor, blower): unit set on a bench or stand, housing bolts backed out with wrenches/impact, covers pried and tapped off, bearings/impeller pulled with puller or press, parts marked and laid out for rebuild.

Plant-floor dismantling of a mid-size production machine or module for replacement or relocation (packaging module, machine tool, pump-motor skid, conveyor drive section): guards and couplings unbolted, wiring/piping/air lines disconnected, anchor bolts broken loose, machine match-marked and split into crane-liftable pieces beside an operating line.

Shutdown/outage teardown of large fixed heavy equipment in place (mill, crusher, press, kiln drive, turbine, long conveyor): heavily corroded and seized fasteners needing heat, torch, sledgehammers and crowbars; multi-ton subassemblies rigged out with chain falls and cranes; work at height, on scaffolds and in confined spaces.

Decommissioning or scrapping of obsolete machinery at a closed or partially demolished plant, or clearing a customer site: layout as found, no production support, dirt/debris, unknown machine history, parts cut or knocked apart for removal and scrap.

Field dismantling at outdoor or remote sites (quarry/mine plant, grain elevator, wind farm, construction site): weather, uneven ground, temporary access, equipment dismantled where it stands for repair or removal.

Awkward-access in-situ teardown inside or under a machine (drive internals in a pit, gearbox under a press frame, components inside a hopper or housing): tools swung in tight quarters, blind fastener removal, parts pried and hammered out by feel.

sources.system: Panasonic automated appliance disassembly cell (six-axis robots, AI machine vision)
sources.title: Appliance Manufacturer Uses Robots and AI to Disassemble Products | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Panasonic uses six-axis robots with magnetic grippers, screwdrivers and cutting end effectors to automatically dismantle air conditioners, microwave ovens and ... in a purpose-built disassembly line, with AI vision detecting screws even when dirty or rusted.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic dismantling of end-of-life appliances. Transfers to shop teardown of a small machine because the objects are bolted machine assemblies with motors and wiring, and the operations (unscrewing, cover removal, cable cutting, component extraction) are the same hand-tool operations a millwright performs, at comparable fastener sizes.

sources.system: AgiProbot automated disassembly station
sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (wbk Institute of Production Science)
sources.title: 6D Pose Estimation on Point Cloud Data through Prior Knowledge Integration: A Case Study in Autonomous Disassembly
sources.claim: In the AgiProbot demonstrator factory, end-of-life starter motors are clamped in a cell and disassembled by a multifunctional ... using vision-based 6D pose estimation of the bolts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remanufacturing disassembly of an electric motor. This is essentially the millwright's shop teardown of a motor — unbolting the housing and separating internal components while preserving them for reuse — performed autonomously with the workpiece clamped in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: DeMoBat battery/e-drive disassembly cell (KUKA KR QUANTEC + Fraunhofer pitasc)
sources.title: “DeMoBat”: Battery disassembly for electric cars using KUKA robots | KUKA Global
sources.claim: In the Fraunhofer IPA DeMoBat project a KUKA KR QUANTEC robot (270 kg payload) automatically unscrewed screws, opened sealing joints and disconnected cables on varied heavy EV battery packs, with vision systems detecting screws so each step did not have to be taught; Fraunhofer describes the demonstrators as (partially) automated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dismantling of several-hundred-kilogram bolted assemblies (EV battery packs, e-drive units) in a fixtured industrial cell; the fastener sizes, torques and cable-disconnection steps resemble the lighter end of millwright dismantling work.

sources.system: iDEAR automated electronics disassembly cell
sources.title: Automated Electronics Disassembly: First Milestones in the Research Project - Fraunhofer IFF
sources.claim: The Fraunhofer IFF iDEAR project automated complete disassembly subprocesses on electronic products, from picking the required tool through unscrewing to setting down the removed component, including removing a motherboard from a computer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of electrical/electronic products in a cell. Supports the multi-tool, multi-step character of dismantling (select tool, unfasten, remove part) autonomously, though on far smaller objects than industrial machinery.

sources.system: Robotic PM motor disassembly setup (Liang & Pham)
sources.title: Robotic disassembly of permanent magnet electric motors | Royal Society Open Science
sources.claim: University of Birmingham researchers demonstrated robotic extraction of the rotor from the stator of a permanent-magnet motor using a force-model-optimized disassembly path that reduced peak disassembly force and avoided damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: separating an interference/press-fit machine component. This is the force-controlled 'pull the rotor / press off the part' step of a millwright motor teardown, executed by a robot on a fixtured motor.

sources.system: Boltron flange bolting robot
sources.title: Boltron Flange Bolting Robot | Total Marine Technology Products
sources.claim: Boltron is a commercially offered site-based flange bolting machine used at refineries, power stations and production ... to tighten and loosen flange bolts; it is positioned and set up on the flange for each job and no evidence of autonomous end-to-end operation was found.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-situ analog found for loosening fasteners on plant equipment; cited only to characterize the state of in-plant technology. Autonomy is not established and it performs a single sub-step, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Bolt parts, such as side and deck plates, jaw plates, and journals, to basic assembly unit.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New machinery installation inside a manufacturing plant (paper mill, food plant, steel mill): millwright rigs side plates, bearing housings/journals and drive frames off a crane or forklift onto a base assembly set on its foundation, drifts holes into alignment, starts and torques large bolts to spec, checks squareness with the machine's baseplate.

Outage/repair rebuild on an in-place machine on the plant floor: worn deck plates, wear liners, side plates or journal/bearing assemblies unbolted and new ones bolted back onto the existing unit in a cramped, hot, dusty spot with limited crane access and partial disassembly of guards and chutes.

Field work at a quarry, mine, or recycling yard on portable/fixed crushing-screening plant: bolting jaw plates, cheek/side plates and screen deck panels (200-2,000 lb castings) into a crusher chamber or screen box, outdoors, on uneven ground, with wedges, shims, drift pins and high-torque impact/hydraulic wrenches.

Shop pre-assembly at a millwright/rigging contractor or plant maintenance shop: parts staged on stands or a bench under a jib or bridge crane, plates and journals bolted to a base unit per blueprint before the assembly is shipped or set in place; standard tooling, good access, controlled conditions.

Elevated or awkward-access bolting during conveyor and bulk-handling work: side plates, skirt boards, deck plates and pulley/journal bearing blocks bolted to conveyor frames, elevators and head sections from scissor lifts, scaffolds or ladders inside plant galleries and tunnels.

sources.system: Dürr NEXT.assembly flex decking / flex bolt
sources.title: NEXT.assembly: New body marriage trends with flex decking - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's flex decking/flex bolt system performs the marriage of chassis modules to a car body and then fully automatic bolting of the underbody at dedicated bolting stations in automotive final assembly plants, with vision systems verifying part position before bolting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting heavy sub-assemblies (engine/axle modules) to a base assembly unit (the body) on a fixtured pallet line. Objects are heavy multi-hundred-kg steel/aluminium assemblies, holes must be aligned before fastening, and bolts are torque-monitored — the same operation class as bolting side plates, deck plates and journals to a basic assembly unit, in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: FANUC M-2000iA/2300
sources.title: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 Robot - Ultra Heavy Payload Robot | FANUC America
sources.claim: Commercially available ultra-heavy-payload industrial robots lift and position 2.3-tonne parts and load bulky castings onto machine fixtures with ±0.18 mm repeatability, replacing cranes and lifters in fenced cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy-part handling and placement onto fixtures. The millwright instances require lifting heavy plates/journals (100-1,000 kg) and seating them on a base unit before bolting; this substantiates the heavy placement half of the task inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: 3D-vision-guided robotic bolt-tightening system (INESC TEC / automaker line)
sources.developer: Institute for Systems and Computer Engineering, Technology and Science (INESC TEC) with an automaker
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A vision-guided robot fitted with torque tooling tightens rear axle damper bolts on vans moving through an automotive assembly line station, using 3D perception to compensate for vehicle position variation from conveyor tolerances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torque-controlled bolt tightening on a structural chassis part whose position is not perfectly repeatable; shows sensing-based hole/bolt localisation and fastening at production quality on a fixtured line, the fastening half of the millwright task.

sources.system: Atlas Copco Tightening Cell Robotics (TCR)
sources.title: Tightening Cell Robotics - Atlas Copco USA
sources.claim: Turnkey robotic tightening cells combining robots, vision, feeding systems and torque tools are sold as standard automated fastening stations for assembly plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated multi-bolt fastening of assemblies presented in a fixtured cell, with feeding of fasteners and torque documentation — the fastening operation the millwright instances require, in a purpose-built environment.

sources.system: Boltron Flange Bolting Robot
sources.title: Boltron Flange Bolting Robot | Total Marine Technology Products
sources.claim: An automated flange bolting robot is magnetically mounted onto flanges at refineries and power stations and then runs programmed star-pattern, staged torquing with a 3,400 Nm torque gun; an operator mounts it and uses a live camera stream for bolt alignment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-facility (E2) bolting analog found: high-torque multi-bolt tightening on equipment in place. It does not place parts, is manually mounted and camera-supervised, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion at E2.

sources.system: RUSSELL 7 Model R AutoMotion Mill Relining Machine, THUNDERBOLT SKYWAY, RME BOLTBOSS
sources.title: RME deploys first-ever roboticized mill relining system - North American Mining Magazine
sources.claim: A semi-automated, roboticised mill relining system deployed at PT Freeport Indonesia grabs worn liners and places new liner plates against the mill shell with millimetre precision without crew inside the mill; liner/bolt securing is done from outside with the BOLTBOSS toolset.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field analog to bolting heavy wear plates (liners) into installed machinery. It is described as semi-automated with reline crews operating the machines and securing bolts, so it cannot support a positive judgment at the mine-site (E2/E3) tier.

tasks.label: Lay out mounting holes, using measuring instruments, and drill holes with power drill.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Operating plant or warehouse, flat concrete floor slab: millwright transfers baseplate/anchor-bolt pattern from the layout drawing to the slab with tape, square, chalk line or laser, punches centers, then drills 1/2"-1" dia holes 4-10" deep with a rotary hammer for wedge/adhesive anchors under a pump skid, conveyor legs, press or machine base; holes vacuumed, dust controlled, dozens per job.

Same plant, but the holes go into a raised concrete machine pedestal or inertia block, into the wall or floor of a machine pit, or into the vertical face of a curb/foundation: cramped access next to installed equipment, drilling downward on a 6-18" elevated pad or sideways/awkwardly in a pit.

Field installation at a new plant, mill, mine or building under construction: layout of anchor holes on fresh concrete pads or a partly finished slab from foundation drawings and benchmarks, often outdoors or in an unenclosed structure, with mud, debris, other trades and weather; drilling with rotary hammer, sometimes on sloped or uneven surfaces.

Shop bench or laydown area: laying out and drilling (and often tapping) mounting holes in loose steel parts - baseplates, sole plates, shims, motor mounting brackets, guard frames, adapter plates - using scale, square, dividers, center punch and a drill press or hand/mag drill, working from a sketch or drawing.

In-place steel: laying out and drilling/tapping mounting holes in an already-installed machine frame, mezzanine beam, conveyor stringer or platform member, frequently overhead or sideways, from a ladder or lift, with a magnetic-base drill; often match-drilling through the equipment's own base or bracket used as a template.

Existing facility, overhead concrete: layout and drilling of anchor holes in a concrete ceiling, deck or beam soffit for hoist beams, monorail, conveyor hangers or supports, worked from a scissor lift with a rotary hammer and dust shroud.

sources.system: DALE (DEWALT drilling rig on August Robotics Lionel AMR)
sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) with August Robotics
sources.title: 9 weeks to 9 days: How autonomous drilling is transforming data center construction - The Robot Report
sources.claim: DEWALT/August Robotics 'DALE' is an autonomous mobile concrete floor drilling robot that takes hole positions from a CAD/CSV file, localizes each hole to about 1/8 in., and drills them; 12 units in the field had drilled 108,000 holes at 99.97% placement accuracy by January 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content as the millwright instance: hole positions taken from a plan (replacing tape/laser layout) and drilled into a concrete slab to receive anchors for bolted-down equipment (server racks vs. machine baseplates); comparable hole sizes and mm-level placement tolerance.

sources.system: DALE (DEWALT / August Robotics)
sources.title: 9 weeks to 9 days: How autonomous drilling is transforming data center construction - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The same system is stated to work in occupied/finished buildings with concrete floors, not only greenfield sites, and to route around obstructions on the floor.

sources.system: DALE
sources.title: Robotic Downward Drilling for Data Centers and General Construction | August Robotics
sources.claim: Product documentation for DALE gives the working envelope: drilling 1/2 in. to 1-1/2 in. ... holes up to 14 in. deep in concrete, with rebar detection and cutting, automated dust extraction, and autonomous execution from an uploaded CAD/CSV point file.
sources.transferJustification: Hole diameters (up to 1-1/2 in.) and depths (14 in.) cover the anchor sizes millwrights drill for machine baseplates; rebar detection matches the reinforced foundations they work on.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E. (ABB IRB robot arm)
sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler | The Construction Index
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E. is a self-climbing robot that autonomously measures positions, drills holes and sets anchor bolts in concrete elevator shaft walls from a pre-uploaded digital plan; by mid-2026 it had been used on 36 job sites and installed roughly 50,000 anchor bolts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out and drilling anchor holes in concrete for bolted equipment brackets. Transfers to non-floor concrete anchor work only inside an elevator shaft, whose geometry the robot's winch/bracing system depends on.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Jaibot - Hilti Corporation (media release)
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot marks and drills overhead/ceiling and wall anchor holes from BIM data using a robotic total station, but an operator must drive it by remote control from one drilling position to the next; only the holes within reach are drilled ....
sources.transferJustification: Directly the overhead-drilling instance (layout from a digital plan plus rotary-hammer drilling of anchor holes), but navigation between positions is human-driven, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot (2024 update)
sources.title: Hilti unveils new robot-powered drilling capabilities - Design World
sources.claim: Hilti has continued to sell the Jaibot as a semi-autonomous machine, adding concrete wall and metal-deck ceiling drilling in 2024; no fully autonomous successor is described.

sources.system: Baubot MRS12 / MRS15 (KUKA arm on mobile base)
sources.title: Robot colleagues now coming to construction | SICK
sources.claim: Baubot's mobile construction robots that drill bracket-mounting holes in tunnels are explicitly operated with a worker present rather than autonomously.

sources.system: Peddinghaus Advantage-2 CNC beam drill line
sources.title: CNC Beam Drill Line | Advantage-2 | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: CNC beam drill lines take structural members from a digital drawing and automatically scribe layout marks, drill, tap and countersink mounting holes in them at production rates; these are standard equipment in steel fabrication shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out (scribing) and drilling/tapping mounting holes in steel members and plates from a drawing - the same objects (structural steel, sole plates, brackets) and tighter precision than a millwright's bench layout, with the workpiece clamped and fed by the machine.

sources.system: Wilder Systems Agile Manufacturing Robot / drilling end-effectors
sources.title: HaaS 100 (late September 2024) - Hardfin
sources.claim: Wilder Systems fields robotic drilling systems that use CAD-to-path planning and vision to locate features and drill precise holes in aircraft metal structures inside manufacturing and depot facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated location and drilling of holes in metal structures. Supports metal-drilling capability where the workpiece is presented in a known position, not free-form in-place drilling on arbitrary installed machinery.

tasks.label: Attach moving parts and subassemblies to basic assembly unit, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-plant machine installation or rebuild at a manufacturing plant (food, packaging, auto, paper): the bedplate/base unit is already set on the floor, and the millwright attaches the drive motor, gear reducer, sheaves/sprockets, shafts, couplings and guards to it with sockets, torque wrenches, impact guns and a chain hoist, working around adjacent equipment in a running or shut-down plant.

Shop or staging-area pre-assembly before field installation: bearing housings, shafts, couplings, gear reducers and conveyor drive packages are built up on stands or benches with overhead crane support; parts are new, repeated across units, access is good and the layout is fixed.

Heavy field erection at a greenfield or outdoor industrial site (mine, quarry, grain terminal, mill, power plant): multi-ton subassemblies such as crusher rotors, mill drive assemblies, large fan wheels or turbine components are landed by crane onto the base unit, drift-pinned, and secured with large hydraulic/pneumatic torque tools, often at height, on scaffold, in weather.

Shutdown or breakdown reassembly in confined, awkward in-situ positions - inside a machine frame, in a pit, overhead - with worn, dirty or rusted hardware; the millwright fits and shims parts, hand-starts fasteners in blind holes and torques them from a restricted-access position.

Kit-based modular equipment assembly at a customer facility (conveyor line in a distribution center, packaging line modules): standardized sections, drive units, take-ups and guards bolted together per drawings on a level, cleared floor with staged parts and repeat hardware.

sources.system: Duerr flex decking marriage station (NEXT.assembly)
sources.title: NEXT.assembly: New body marriage trends with flex decking - Duerr
sources.claim: Duerr's flex decking marriage station joins the car body with its mechanical subassemblies (shock absorbers, powertrain, battery) using programmable grippers and 3D vision that bring all parts into position ready for bolting on an automated final-assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive chassis 'marriage'. automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ at an operating industrial plant (paper mill, steel mill, food plant, power house): millwright heats a coupling hub, sprocket, sheave or gear (roughly 20-200 lb) with an oxy-acetylene rosebud or portable induction heater, checks with temp sticks, and slides it down an installed drive shaft against a shoulder before it grips; tight quarters, at machine height, during a short outage window.

Bench/floor work in the plant maintenance or rebuild shop: shrink-fitting bushings, sleeves, bearings and wear rings into housings or onto shafts of pumps, gearboxes and rolls; part held in a fixture, vise or on a hoist; heated with torch, induction heater or oven; fit checked with micrometers and dial indicator after cooling.

Repetitive shrink fits in a shop that rebuilds many like units (motor shop shrinking rotors, bearing races and sleeves onto standard motor shafts; roll shop shrinking sleeves and rings onto standard roll journals) - same part family many times, known interference values.

Heavy but standardized interference/shrink assemblies in a dedicated heavy shop: wheels, gear wheels and brake discs mounted onto axles (rail cars, crane trucks), using presses plus heat, with dimensional gauging of the finished assembly.

One-off multi-ton shrink fits requiring crane rigging: a kiln tire or shrunk-on ring/gear onto a large drum or pinion shaft, a large sleeve onto a roll journal, a liner into a crusher or pump housing; interference computed from field measurements, several rosebuds or heating blankets, heavy sling handling, part must land right the first time.

Off-site field work with no controlling institution (construction site, mine/quarry, dock, outdoor conveyor line): shrink-fitting bushings into pin bores of excavator booms and buckets, sheaves and pulley hubs onto shafts, sleeves onto pins, working on uneven ground in weather with portable gas heating gear.

tasks.label: Troubleshoot equipment, electrical components, hydraulics, or other mechanical systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Breakdown call on a plant floor: a production machine or line (packaging machine, press, mixer, conveyor drive) stops or misbehaves; the millwright isolates the cause across mechanical, hydraulic and electrical possibilities — pulls guards, jogs drives, listens, checks for play/binding, consults drawings, takes measurements — until the failed element is identified.

Hydraulic or pneumatic fault diagnosis on installed machinery (press, injection molder, hydraulic power unit, heavy mobile equipment): connect gauges/flow meters, actuate valves and cylinders, check pressures, relief settings, leakage, contamination and filters to isolate the faulty pump, valve, cylinder or line.

Rotating-equipment condition diagnosis rounds inside the plant: vibration readings, thermography, listening and gauge checks on pumps, fans, motors, gearboxes and conveyor idlers to detect and localize degrading bearings, misalignment, imbalance, hot spots or leaks and flag them for repair.

Post-installation / commissioning troubleshooting at an erection, construction, mine or remote outdoor site: a newly installed or relocated machine runs rough — the millwright checks alignment, runout, coupling condition, soft foot, backlash and fit-up with dial indicators and laser alignment tools amid a site taken as found.

Shop/bench diagnosis of a removed component (gearbox, pump, motor, hydraulic cylinder) brought to the maintenance shop: mount it, run or pressurize it, measure, and where needed tear it down to confirm which internal part failed.

Electrical/control component troubleshooting on installed machinery: continuity, voltage, resistance and insulation checks on motors, starters, VFDs, limit switches, proximity sensors and control wiring to determine whether the electrical side is the cause of a machine fault.

tasks.label: Dismantle machinery and equipment for shipment to installation site, performing installation and maintenance work as part of team.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production-machine relocation teardown on a manufacturing plant floor: lock out and disconnect power, air, hydraulic and coolant lines, match-mark and photograph, unbolt anchor and frame bolts, split the machine into shippable subassemblies, rig each with overhead crane or forklift, block/skid/bolt to pallets and load a truck, working with a crew of riggers.

Heavy process-equipment teardown inside a mill, power plant, refinery or paper mill: turbine casings, gearboxes, conveyor drives, fans, agitators; work on scaffolds and elevated platforms or in confined spaces, corroded and seized fasteners requiring heat/impact tools or torch cutting, tag and crate components for shipment to the installation site.

Field teardown at an outdoor or remote site (mine, quarry, wind farm, construction/decommissioning site): uneven ground, weather, mobile crane support, no fixed utilities, one-off equipment such as crushers, screens, gearboxes or towers dismantled for trucking to a new location.

Shop-bench teardown of removed subassemblies (gearbox, pump, blower, drive unit) for shipment: strip guards and couplings, unbolt housings, pull press-fitted bearings and sleeves, inspect, clean, tag and match-mark parts, box or crate them with preservation for transport.

Reassembly and installation at the receiving site as part of a team: set components on the foundation per layout drawings, shim and level, install and torque anchor bolts, align shafts/couplings with dial or laser tools, reconnect piping and drives, grout, and run maintenance checks before turnover.

tasks.label: Connect power unit to machines or steam piping to equipment, and test unit to evaluate its mechanical operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Operating manufacturing plant (auto, food, packaging, paper): millwright couples a newly set electric motor/gear drive to a machine - mounts and torques hold-down bolts, installs coupling halves, laser-aligns shafts to thousandths, hooks up lube/cooling lines, then bumps and test-runs the unit checking rotation, vibration and bearing temperature.

Fluid-power hookup in a plant: connect a hydraulic or pneumatic power unit to a press, injection molder or conveyor drive - route and make up flexible hoses and rigid tubing with JIC/flange fittings, fill and bleed the reservoir, then cycle the machine and verify pressures, response and freedom from leaks.

Steam/process piping tie-in during a mill or power-plant outage: fit, gasket and bolt (or weld) steam supply and condensate lines to equipment such as a dryer, heat exchanger or turbine-driven pump, often at elevation or in tight quarters; pressure-test, warm the line and check operation.

Greenfield or plant-expansion construction site: set and connect drive units to conveyors, mixers and packaging machines in an unfinished building with temporary power, mud/debris, shifting trades and no fixed layout, then test run each drive.

Heavy/large drive train in a mine, mill, refinery or power house: connect a multi-tonne motor/gearbox to a mill, crusher, large fan, compressor or turbine using large couplings, jacking bolts and shims, precision-align with dial/laser, then commission with a monitored test run and vibration analysis.
