sources.title: Utility Analytics Week 2024 Recap: Focus On Drone Inspection And AI Technology In Utilities
sources.claim: A US utility's distribution inspection program uses drones to automate collection of imagery of poles, insulators and transformers and vision-AI models to detect and prioritize asset defects, feeding a trouble-ticketing system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect detection on distribution assets from drone imagery. Same defective components the task names (transformers, cutouts, insulators), identified in the field; the drone performs the physical action and the AI makes the defect call.

sources.system: Phoenix Air Unmanned BVLOS powerline inspection operations for Xcel Energy
sources.title: BVLOS Waiver for Powerline Inspections Granted | UST
sources.claim: Drone service provider flew over 13,000 miles of powerline inspection for a US utility beyond visual line of sight without visual observers under FAA waiver, and holds a nationwide waiver for utility powerline inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine line inspection at production scale in unstructured rights-of-way; shows uncrewed aircraft carry this instance at scale, though in-flight autonomy is not established from the source.

tasks.label: Install watt-hour meters and connect service drops between power lines and consumers' facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential watt-hour meter set or change-out at an existing socket on a single-family home: drive to the address, deal with gates/dogs/vegetation, cut the utility seal, pull the old socket-type meter under load, check socket condition and voltage, plug in the new AMI meter, install ring and seal, confirm it energizes and communicates, log the exchange.

New overhead service drop to a house or small shop: install/verify the service bracket and insulator at the customer's weatherhead, run and sag triplex from the pole, dead-end it, splice the drop to the energized secondary at the pole with piercing or compression connectors, land conductors at the weatherhead/meter base, set the meter and energize.

Underground service lateral connection in a subdivision: pull or receive service conductors at a pad-mounted transformer or secondary handhole, strip and terminate on secondary bushings/spades, terminate the other end in the customer's meter base, install and seal the meter, verify phasing and voltage.

Commercial or multifamily metering: install a CT-rated meter or meter-bank socket in a building meter room or on a commercial building's exterior wall, land service and CT/PT secondary wiring on terminal blocks, program and seal the meter, coordinate with the customer's electrician and inspector.

Storm or emergency service restoration: re-attach service drops torn loose from houses, assess and repair damaged masts, weatherheads, brackets and meter bases (debris, wind, wet conditions, aged or non-standard customer equipment), re-splice the drop and re-set or replace the meter to restore the customer.

sources.system: Automated electricity-meter verification line, State Grid Hubei Marketing Service Center (Metering Center)
sources.developer: State Grid Hubei Electric Power (Marketing Service Center / Metering Center)
sources.title: 湖北这个地方，可年检电表300万只，全部由机器人操作……
sources.claim: State Grid Hubei's metering centre runs two single-phase meter verification lines with 2,400 meter positions and 3 million meters/year capacity in which robots perform all operations fully automatically: retrieval from the automated warehouse, mounting and verification, labelling and seal engraving, sorting and boxing, and return to store.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bench verification of watt-hour meters. The physical acts are those the E1 form of meter installation requires - gripping a meter, seating it in a metering position so terminals connect, sealing and labelling it - on identical objects (utility watt-hour meters) at production reliability.

sources.system: Jiangsu Electric Power Metering Center automated verification and intelligent warehouse system (挂表机器人 meter-hanging robot)
sources.developer: Jiangsu Electric Power Design Institute / Jiangsu Electric Power Company Metering Center
sources.title: 江苏院 “智”成行业之先 - 中国能源报
sources.claim: Jiangsu Electric Power's metering centre (in service June 2014) uses AGVs plus meter-hanging robots that grip a meter and hang it onto the verification stand for testing and then remove it, with appearance check, sorting, sealing and labelling downstream; rated capacity 8 million single-phase meters per year.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated meter verification. Hanging a watt-hour meter onto a verification stand is the same insertion and seating operation, on the same object, as plugging a meter into a socket, substantiating the fixtured (E1) form of meter installation.

sources.system: 第四代人工智能配网带电作业机器人 (4th-generation AI distribution live-working robot, dual-arm autonomous variant)
sources.developer: State Grid Tianjin Electric Power (Zhang Liming team) / State Grid Corporation of China
sources.title: 人工智能配网带电作业机器人升级至第四代 (国家能源局)
sources.claim: The 4th-generation AI distribution live-working robot (State Grid Tianjin) autonomously identifies and grasps the drop lead and performs stripping, threading and making the live connection on 10 kV distribution lines; it entered distribution service after its first job and had completed over 80 operations across urban, suburban and mountain settings, with a 200-unit/year production base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: live connection of a drop/tap lead to an energized 10 kV overhead conductor - the pole-side half of connecting a service drop, with comparable conductor sizes and the same strip-and-clamp connection, showing the connection step is machine-feasible when conductors are held in known positions.

sources.system: 配网带电作业机器人 (distribution live-working robot) operated by State Grid Xinning County Power Supply Company
sources.developer: State Grid Hunan Electric Power / State Grid Xinning County Power Supply Company
sources.title: 国网新宁：首次自主完成配网机器人带电作业
sources.claim: In June 2026 State Grid Xinning County (Hunan) performed 12 robotic live-line jobs on two 10 kV lines, including three drop-lead disconnections; delivered to the work point by an insulated bucket truck, the robot automatically scanned the scene and located conductors, judged conditions and planned its path, and gripped, released and separated the three-phase leads while ground staff monitored remotely and issued commands.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making and breaking drop-lead connections on energized distribution conductors. It shows autonomous conductor handling in the field but only at the pole tap point, not the house attachment, cable run, weatherhead landing or meter set that the whole instance requires.

sources.system: 间隔棒安装机器人 (conductor spacer installation robot)
sources.title: 这个机器人能爬上输电线路 5分钟全自动完成任务
sources.claim: State Grid Hubei's spacer-installation robot is lifted onto a 110 kV transmission conductor by drone and installs a conductor spacer fully automatically in about five minutes; the twin-bundle version has been rolled out on more than 20 projects in the province with over 540 spacers installed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic installation of clamped hardware onto overhead conductors. Clamping hardware to a conductor at a known position is the mechanical core of dead-ending and connecting a drop, supporting feasibility once the conductor is presented in a fixed position.

sources.system: 10 kV live-working robot prototype with four-dimensional safety framework (with review of field state of the art)
sources.title: Research on Live Working Robots for 10 KV Distribution Networks Adopting Four-Dimensional Safety Guarantee Framework
sources.claim: A July 2026 review of 10 kV distribution live-working robots reports that all three generations rely on ... and support only monitoring rather than full autonomous ..., with most research still at laboratory stage; the paper's own field-validated prototype is a human-in-the-loop teleoperation system.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (energized overhead line connection work); cited to show unsupervised worker-quality autonomy for field line connections is not established, supporting the negative E3 and E2 judgments.

sources.system: Komax Alpha 550 G2 automatic cut/strip/crimp machine
sources.title: Automatic Cut, Strip and Crimp Machine | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Komax's Alpha 550 G2 is a commercially sold, fully automatic machine that cuts, strips and crimps wire in a fixtured processing cell without operator intervention, for cross-sections of 0.13 to 6 square millimetres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing and terminating insulated conductors. It substantiates that stripping and crimping terminations to accepted quality is routine when conductors are fixtured and presented (E1), though at far smaller gauge than service conductors, so it is supporting rather than decisive.

tasks.label: Test conductors, according to electrical diagrams and specifications, to identify corresponding conductors and to prevent incorrect connections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Overhead distribution: before tying a new line section, transformer bank, or backfeed into an existing energized 12.47/25 kV circuit, the lineworker works from a bucket at the pole with hot-line phasing sticks/phasing tester and hot stick, comparing each energized primary conductor against the circuit map and phase designations, in roadside right-of-way conditions (traffic, weather, vegetation, varying pole framing).

Underground distribution: in a street manhole/vault, padmount transformer, or URD pedestal, identify which of several unlabeled cables is which — ringing out with tone/ID sets, applying cable identification/spiking gear, and phase-checking against feeder maps and prints before splicing, terminating, or elbow switching; confined, congested, often wet space.

Substation or indoor switchgear room: ring out and verify power and control cable terminations against schematics and wiring diagrams (continuity, point-to-point checks, CT/PT circuit and phase verification) before landing conductors on breakers, relay panels, or bus, inside the fenced utility-controlled facility.

Services and secondaries: at a meter base, service entrance, secondary pedestal, or customer switchboard, identify and verify service conductors — phase vs. neutral, phase rotation, correct pairing of secondary legs — with a meter/tester per the service diagram before connecting, on residential or commercial premises taken as found.

Transmission/subtransmission tie-in and rebuild: at a structure or dead-end in open right-of-way, test conductors to confirm de-energized status before grounding and verify phase identity/phasing of each conductor against line prints prior to reconnection, working at height from a bucket or on the structure in variable terrain and weather.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers (4080/4085 series)
sources.title: Flying Probe Tester for electronic boards PCB | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA flying probe testers are commercial machines that autonomously move probes into contact with conductors on a fixtured board and verify every net against the design (CAD/netlist) data, detecting opens, shorts and wrong connections without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated electrical verification of conductors against a design diagram. The machine physically contacts each conductor and confirms which conductor corresponds to which net, flagging miswires/shorts — the same test logic and accepted output as ringing out conductors against a print, performed on fixtured work in a purpose-built enclosure (E1). Conductors are far smaller than utility cable, so the transfer is only to a fixtured E1 presentation, not to field work.

sources.system: KLOTZ fully automated end-of-line (EOL) test benches for electric motors/power packs
sources.title: End-of-line testing for high-performance electric motors | KLOTZ
sources.claim: Fully automated end-of-line test benches make electrical contact with a workpiece's power terminals and run the electrical test program autonomously in a fixtured cell, with robotic loading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-made electrical contact to a workpiece's phase terminals followed by automated electrical testing. This substantiates the physical act of applying test leads/probes to power conductors and executing a test program autonomously when the work is fixtured and presented, i.e. the E1 counterfactual for conductor testing.

sources.system: Komax EasyWiring Board with integrated Cirris 8100 tester
sources.title: Up to 70 percent faster: EasyWiring Board now features integrated testing | Komax
sources.claim: Automated low-voltage continuity testing of complete wire harnesses to catch miswires is integrated into commercial harness production equipment, though connectors are mated by hand on the wiring board.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying that each conductor of an assembled harness matches the wiring diagram. Cited only as context that miswire detection is a routine automated test function; the physical mating is manual, so this item is treated as non-supporting.

sources.system: Ti transmission line inspection robot
sources.title: Robots Take on Tough Tasks in Transmission and Distribution | EPRI Journal
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous field robot on overhead transmission lines performs inspection only — it travels the shield wire taking photos and sensor readings — and does not apply test instruments to conductors.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of autonomous field robotics on power lines: it inspects but performs no conductor identification or phasing test, supporting negative judgments at E3/E2 for line work.

sources.system: Cable Splicing Machine / Automated Cable End Preparation Machine
sources.title: Con Edison and ULC Technologies Unveil Cable Splicing Machine for Improved Worker Safety, Efficiency and Grid Reliability
sources.claim: A field-trialed machine performs autonomous medium-voltage cable preparation inside Con Edison manholes, but the operations are cable stripping, shorting and cutting under operator monitoring — no conductor identification or phasing testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine work on MV distribution cable in a vault. It shows field machines can manipulate utility conductors when clamped onto a single known cable, but it does not identify conductors or verify them against diagrams, so it does not substantiate this task in the field.

sources.system: Live working robot for 10 kV distribution networks (tracked insulated spider aerial platform, dual 6-DOF arms)
sources.developer: Chinese research/utility consortium (published in Sensors, MDPI)
sources.title: Research on Live Working Robots for 10 KV Distribution Networks Adopting Four-Dimensional Safety Guarantee Framework
sources.claim: State-of-the-art 10 kV live-line distribution work robots operate under a teleoperation architecture with only local autonomous decision logic, performing wire stripping and drainage-wire connection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: energized distribution line work at the pole. Even this most advanced live-line manipulator is teleoperated and performs connection work, not diagram-based conductor identification or phasing tests, supporting negative E3 judgments.

sources.system: Breaker Racking Robot (AMR)
sources.title: Breaker Racking Robot – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: Substation robotics with Con Edison is limited to a semi-autonomous mobile robot for racking medium-voltage breakers indoors; no cited system performs schematic-driven conductor ring-out in substations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile robotic work inside a utility substation (E2). It substantiates only breaker racking, not the application of test instruments to conductors and comparison against schematics, so it supports the negative E2 judgment.

tasks.label: Place insulating or fireproofing materials over conductors and joints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Temporary protective cover-up before/during energized distribution work: from an insulated bucket at a roadside pole, the lineworker installs rubber line hose, insulator hoods, and blankets over energized primary conductors, jumpers and connection points; pole framing varies, traffic and weather are as found.

Insulating a completed joint aloft: after making a splice, tap or connector on an overhead conductor or service drop, the worker builds up insulating tape, slides on a cold-shrink/heat-shrink sleeve, or installs an insulating boot over the joint, working at height from a bucket or climbing.

Covering a run of bare conductor for clearance/tree-contact mitigation: installing spiral line guards, covering material, or applied insulating covering over a span of energized or de-energized overhead conductor along a roadside or rural right-of-way.

Installing permanent wildlife/animal guards and insulating covers over transformer and cutout bushings, arrester leads and pole-top jumpers on a distribution pole, fitting covers around cluttered, non-standard hardware.
Underground manhole or vault: wrapping fireproofing tape/mats and insulating tape over cables and completed splices on racks in a congested, wet, confined space whose layout is taken as found.

Utility-controlled facility work: applying fireproof tape or coating to cable runs in a substation cable trench/rack, or insulating prefabricated jumper and termination assemblies at ground level in a service center yard.

sources.system: 绝缘涂覆机器人 (live insulation-coating robot), State Grid Qingyang
sources.developer: State Grid Qingyang Power Supply Co. / coating-robot vendor
sources.title: 国网庆阳供电公司：绝缘涂覆机器人上岗 林木区裸导线穿上“绝缘铠甲”-新华网甘肃频道
sources.claim: A live-line insulation-coating robot was hung on an energized 110 kV conductor and then moved along it autonomously at 6 m/min, spraying a ~2.5 mm insulating coating over the bare conductor in a forested area — i.e., placing insulating material over a conductor in the open field.

sources.system: 无人机+涂覆机器人 (drone-deployed insulation coating robot)
sources.developer: State Grid Wuhan Power Supply Co.
sources.title: 人民网：“无人机+机器人”联合作业 武汉首次进行导线带电喷涂绝缘漆 - 武汉市人民政府门户网站
sources.claim: In operational work in Wuhan, a heavy-lift drone placed a coating robot onto an energized 10 kV bare conductor; the robot travelled the line applying a 24 kV-rated insulating layer and the drone automatically took it off the line at the end of the section, covering about 1 km per day.

sources.system: Insulation skin wrapping robot for overhead distribution line
sources.developer: Lu, Chen, Cai et al. (Chinese university/utility research group)
sources.title: Design and application of insulation skin wrapping robot for overhead distribution line
sources.claim: A line-riding insulation-skin wrapping robot for overhead distribution lines was validated in laboratory and on a live running distribution line, wrapping insulating material over bare overhead wire with automatic operation and machine-vision quality checking.

sources.system: LineFly / Mini LineFly
sources.title: Aerial Robot Modernizes Bird Flight Diverter Installation | T&D World
sources.claim: An aerial line-riding robot autonomously installs helically-wrapped devices onto overhead transmission conductors in the field; it debuted in the US installing bird flight diverters on a 115 kV line and has since installed ~15,000 helical diverters on a 75-mile 345 kV line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing helically-wrapped protective devices onto an overhead conductor. Same objects (overhead conductors at height), same placement motion (helical wrap seated over the conductor at specified points), same outdoor line environment, comparable placement precision — so it transfers to placing spiral/covering material over conductor spans.

sources.system: CAM Innovation FT Follower / automatic spiral wrap taping machines
sources.title: Where to Find Automatic Spiral Wrap Taping Machines – CAM Innovation
sources.claim: Commercial automatic spiral-wrap taping machines apply insulating tape over fixtured conductors and joints — wire harnesses, coils and busbars — under machine control with automatic speed/overlap regulation, in a production (purpose-built) setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: taping insulation over conductors and joints. The material (insulating tape), the object (heavy conductors/busbars and their joints) and the accepted output (a uniform insulating wrap) match the lineworker's taping of joints; only the presentation differs, which is exactly what the E1 counterfactual supplies.

sources.system: Raychem RBK X1 / RBK-series heat shrink machines
sources.title: HEAT SHRINK MACHINES FOR RAYCHEM HEAT SHRINK PRODUCTS FROM TE CONNECTIVITY
sources.claim: Commercial heat-shrink processing machines automatically verify wire/splice position, position the heat-shrink tubing over the joint with automated guide arms, and shrink it — placing insulating material over a joint in a fixtured machine station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: insulating a completed splice with a shrink sleeve. Same material class (heat/cold-shrink sleeving) and same accepted output (a sealed insulated joint) as field splice insulation, performed by machine when the joint is presented fixtured.

sources.system: 配网带电作业双臂人机共融机器人 (dual-arm live-working robot)
sources.developer: State Grid Shijiazhuang Power Supply Co.
sources.title: 带电作业来了机器人“同事”
sources.claim: State Grid Shijiazhuang's dual-arm live-working robot installed three insulating shields over exposed energized metal parts on a distribution pole in under 15 minutes, but it is a human-machine-fusion robot mimicking the operator's motions, driven by a technician holding a controller on the ground (teleoperated).
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (placing insulating covers over energized conductors/fittings), cited to show the only field system doing it is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Splice or solder cables together or to overhead transmission lines, customer service lines, or street light lines, using hand tools, epoxies, or specialized equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Making a tap/jumper (drainage lead) connection of a branch or lateral conductor onto an overhead primary distribution conductor at a roadside or rural pole, worked from an insulated bucket truck, often energized: strip/abrade the main conductor, position the lead, install and tighten a hot-line clamp or compression tap, apply inhibitor.

Splicing/connecting customer service lines and secondary conductors: joining triplex or insulated aluminum service conductors to transformer secondary leads or to existing services at the pole, transformer, or house weatherhead, using split-bolt or compression connectors and insulating tape/covers, on a private property or street frontage taken as found.

Making a full-tension splice or repair sleeve on an overhead line conductor (ACSR/AAC distribution feeder or large transmission conductor) during storm repair, reconductoring, or stringing — compression sleeve pressed with a hydraulic head, or an automatic/implosive splice, done on the conductor in the right-of-way or at the pole.

Splicing medium-voltage underground cable in a manhole, vault, trench, or pad-mount enclosure: preparing each cable end (jacket, shield, semicon, insulation layers to precise dimensions), crimping the connector, and installing a heat-shrink/cold-shrink or epoxy-taped joint in a confined, wet, congested space.

Splicing street light and traffic-signal circuit conductors: small insulated conductors in a pole base, handhole, or luminaire arm, using in-line crimps, insulated splice kits, or fuse-holder connections, at grade or from a bucket on a street.

Ground-level prefabrication and make-up of cable assemblies at the truck or utility service center yard: cutting, stripping, crimping/soldering lugs and connectors onto jumpers, grounds, and pigtails on a bench or tailboard before installation.

sources.system: Outdoor live-working robot (室外带电作业机器人), new generation
sources.developer: Yijiahe Technology (亿嘉和科技股份有限公司)
sources.title: 亿嘉和科技股份有限公司 2025 年半年度报告
sources.claim: Yijiahe's outdoor live-working robot for 10 kV distribution networks uses dual-arm coordination and autonomous control algorithms to achieve fully autonomous perception, decision and execution (with optional teleoperation assist), performing energized branch-line lead connection: stripping, threading, laying on the wire and tightening the clamp.
sources.transferJustification: Connecting a branch-line lead onto an energized overhead primary with a clamp is the same physical operation as this task's 'splice cables to overhead transmission lines / customer service lines': same conductors, same strip-and-connect sequence, same aerial pole environment.

sources.system: 配网带电作业机器人 (distribution live-working robot)
sources.developer: State Grid Bishan Power Supply Company (国网璧山供电公司)
sources.title: 国网璧山供电公司：“带电作业机器人”首次亮相电网运行更可靠
sources.claim: A distribution live-working robot completed an energized drainage-lead tap connection on a 10 kV line at pole No.2 of a lateral in Bishan District, Chongqing; the robot's arms autonomously strip, thread and lay the lead onto the conductor, with one ground operator and a supervisor instead of a four-person crew.

sources.system: 带电作业机器人 (RJ-series live-working robot)
sources.developer: 国网瑞嘉（天津）智能机器人有限公司 (State Grid NARI / Yijiahe JV)
sources.title: 中新天津生态城助国网瑞嘉带电作业机器人实现产业化
sources.claim: Guowang Ruijia's live-working robots had by November 2021 performed more than 10,000 real energized line operations across 18 provinces; the machine autonomously strips, threads and lays conductors while the worker stays on the ground with a tablet.

sources.system: Autonomous Live-Line Maintenance Robot (ALMR)
sources.developer: Feng & Zhang (China Electric Power Research / university collaboration)
sources.title: Autonomous Live-Line Maintenance Robot for a 10 kV Overhead Line — IEEE Access
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed IEEE Access paper describes an autonomous live-line maintenance robot for 10 kV overhead lines that performs the connection/disconnection of lead wires largely automatically, needing only small corrections from the operator.

sources.system: Autonomous live working robot with real-time detection and motion planning
sources.developer: State Grid Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd. (Jinan)
sources.title: Autonomous live working robot navigation with real-time detection and motion planning system on distribution line — High Voltage (IET)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed High Voltage paper by State Grid Intelligence Technology reports real-world experiments with a fully autonomous live-working robot performing line cutting and drain-wire connection on distribution lines, with real-time detection and motion planning.

sources.system: 自主配网带电作业机器人 (autonomous distribution live-working robot)
sources.developer: State Grid Xinning County Power Supply Co. (国网新宁县供电公司)
sources.title: “无人智操”保供电！新宁供电开启配网带电作业智能新模式
sources.claim: In June 2026 a county utility ran its first autonomous robotic live-line work on two 10 kV lines, completing 12 operations including three lead disconnections; a bucket truck delivers the robot to the work point and it then automatically scans the environment and locates the conductors while a ground operator monitors and issues commands remotely.

sources.system: Cable Splicing Machine (electric cable end preparation machine)
sources.title: Con Edison and ULC Technologies Unveil Cable Splicing Machine for Improved Worker Safety, Efficiency and Grid Reliability
sources.claim: The Con Edison / ULC Cable Splicing Machine automates only the end preparation of medium-voltage cable in underground vaults: splicers lower it in and insert the cable, then it autonomously performs three operations (layer-by-layer stripping, shorting, cutting) in 25-30 minutes per phase; the splice itself is still completed by the human splicers.

sources.system: Schunk L-Splice / Schunk Sonosystems ultrasonic wire splicing machines
sources.title: Schunk: Inside Ultrasonic Technology — Wiring Harness News
sources.claim: Commercial ultrasonic metal-welding splicers join two or more conductors, in copper or aluminium, over cross-sections from about 0.26 to 200-300 mm², and the large-section L-Splice machines are built for integration into fully automated production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wire-harness splicing. It is the same act — joining stranded conductors into an electrically and mechanically sound splice — at cross-sections spanning street-light and service-conductor sizes, performed by a machine with the work fixtured and presented, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual for this task.

sources.system: Komax Zeta 620 / Gamma 450 automatic wire processing machines
sources.title: Fully Automatic Stripping, Crimping — ASSEMBLY Magazine
sources.claim: Komax sells fully automatic wire-processing machines that cut, strip and terminate conductors without operator intervention; the Zeta 620 produces 360 finished cables per hour with ferrules on both ends, and the Gamma 450 crimps and seals both ends of wires from 0.13 to 4 mm².
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cable assembly. The cut/strip/terminate cycle on fixtured conductors is the same manipulation and precision required for making up jumpers, pigtails and street-light splices when the work is brought to the machine.

tasks.label: Trim trees that could be hazardous to the functioning of cables or wires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Storm/outage restoration: a limb or whole tree has come down onto an energized primary conductor or service drop along a street or in a back yard; the lineworker cuts the limb free with a chainsaw/pole saw from a bucket or from the ground, clears the wire, and drops debris clear of traffic, fences and parked cars, often at night, in wind and rain, with the line possibly still energized.

Routine encroachment trimming during distribution maintenance: from a bucket truck on a residential/commercial street, saw back limbs growing into or rubbing primary conductors and crossarms, keeping required clearance, lowering or dropping cut limbs clear of sidewalks, vehicles and pedestrians.

Clearing for construction work: before setting a pole, re-conductoring, or pulling new wire, cut branches and small trees along the route or around the pole/anchor location using a chainsaw from the ground or bucket, on roadside verge, field edge or alley.

Service-drop clearance at a customer premises: trim branches rubbing the secondary/service wire or weatherhead in a private yard, working around fences, sheds, gardens, ornamental plantings and pets, cutting small limbs by pole saw and cleaning up the cuttings.

Rural / off-road right-of-way: trim limbs overhanging a wooded transmission or rural distribution line, larger stems, rough or steep terrain, access by track machine or on foot, brush left or chipped on site.

sources.system: Mini Jarraff urban tree trimmer
sources.title: Mini Jarraff - Prinoth - Vegetation Management
sources.claim: The state-of-the-practice mechanized line-clearance trimmer for utility rights-of-way is a remote-controlled (teleoperated) boom saw machine, not an autonomous one.

sources.system: AirForestry heavy-lift harvesting drone
sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First | Wood Central
sources.claim: A heavy-lift drone completed a first-of-its-kind fully autonomous harvest sequence in a production forest: identifying a thinning tree, delimbing it, felling it and carrying the trunk to roadside, with no operator on site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous forest thinning/delimbing of standing trees. It is the closest autonomous woody-cutting capability, but it operates in an open production forest with no energized conductors, buildings, traffic or debris-drop constraints, was a single first-of-kind demonstration rather than a reliability-proven service, and does not perform selective clearance trimming around wires.

sources.system: Survey of autonomous orchard and vineyard pruning robots
sources.developer: Politecnico di Torino PIC4SeR (review of multiple systems)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic pruning in orchards and vineyards: A review - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic pruning of woody branches remains a research capability with success rates well below human standards and long cycle times, mostly in controlled orchard/vineyard settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cutting of branches on standing trees. It bounds current capability — small-diameter cuts on trellised, uniformly planted trees at sub-worker success rates — far short of chainsaw-scale limb removal beside energized conductors.

sources.system: Learned branch-pruning robot (sweet cherry orchard)
sources.title: Learning to Prune Branches in Modern Tree-Fruit Orchards
sources.claim: A state-of-the-art autonomous branch-pruning robot achieved only a 58% cutting success rate in field trials on cherry trees in a commercial orchard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cutting of tree branches in an outdoor field setting. Even in a planted, row-structured orchard the success rate is far below the reliability a utility would accept for trimming beside energized conductors.

tasks.label: Pull up cable by hand from large reels mounted on trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Overhead distribution build: crew parks a reel truck on a road shoulder or rural right-of-way; a lineman grabs the conductor/secondary end and hand-pulls slack off the large reel, walks it down the line, and hoists/hands it up to the bucket worker at the pole. Traffic, ditches, brush, weather.

Residential/commercial service drop: hand-pulling triplex/quadruplex service cable off a reel mounted on the line truck, dragging it across a yard, over fences and landscaping to the house weatherhead, then up to the pole.

Underground (URD) work: reel truck set over a handhole/manhole in a street or easement; workers hand-pull cable off the reel to create slack, feed the end into the duct with rollers/pull rope, and figure-eight or coil the payoff while a winch takes the pull.

Storm/emergency restoration: hand-pulling cable off truck reels at night or in mud, snow, or off-road terrain with damaged poles, debris, and improvised access; speed matters and the site is degraded and unpredictable.

Substation, generating station, or industrial plant yard: reel truck inside the fenced facility; workers hand-pull power or control cable off the reel and route it into cable trenches, ducts, and trays along a fixed, engineered layout with controlled access.

sources.system: Conductix-Wampfler Motor-Driven Reels (KHD/BNA series)
sources.title: Motor-Driven Reels | Conductix-Wampfler | United States of America
sources.claim: Motor-driven cable reels are commercial, machine-controlled systems that pay out and retrieve heavy power cable from large reels under tension control, feeding mobile machines in ports, mines and ... without a person hand-pulling the cable.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered payout/take-up of heavy power cable from a large reel. It performs the same physical act as hand-pulling cable off a truck reel (drawing heavy conductor off a fixtured drum along a guided path under controlled tension), but only where the reel and cable path are engineered around the machine.

sources.system: Reel Power Industrial ILHSS Series HD automatic coiling / take-up and payoff systems
sources.title: Wire and Cable Take-Up, Spooling & Coiling Machines
sources.claim: Commercial cable take-up, spooling and coiling systems provide automatic, tension-controlled pay-out and take-up of cable from and onto reels in cable production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: de-reeling cable to a required length under controlled tension in a purpose-built line. Comparable objects (large cable drums, heavy conductor) and comparable output (cable drawn off the reel and delivered downstream), achieved with the reel fixtured and the path fixed.

sources.system: WIREPRO PF-S100 cable drum payoff stand / automatic de-reeler
sources.title: PF-S100 Big cable spool unwinding machine automatic de-reeler
sources.claim: Automatic de-reeler / drum payoff stands unwind cable from large drums under adaptive speed and tension control to feed downstream processing machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pulling cable off a large drum. The machine replaces the human hand-pull of cable from a reel, but requires the drum fixtured on a stand and the cable end presented to a fixed downstream path.

tasks.label: Lay underground cable directly in trenches, or string it through conduit running through the trenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential/commercial subdivision underground distribution: crew pays medium-voltage URD primary cable off a reel trailer directly into an open trench along an easement, works the cable around bends and into position, sets bedding sand/warning tape, and leaves proper slack at transformer pads before backfill. Outdoor construction site with mud, traffic, and varying terrain.

Pulling cable through existing conduit/duct bank between manholes or from a handhole to a padmount transformer in a city street: set up reel and cable puller, rod or blow in a pull line, attach pulling grip/basket, lubricate, pull several hundred feet under monitored tension and bend-radius limits, then rack and coil slack in the vault.

Installing conduit in a freshly dug trench and stringing cable through it for a commercial service, street-light circuit, or secondary run: glue/couple conduit sections in the trench, mandrel and rod the run, pull secondary/service cable through, cap and seal ends. Open trench at a jobsite with other trades nearby.

Fault repair / cable replacement: locate and expose the failed section, pull the defective cable out of the duct or trench, and pull in replacement cable through deteriorated or partially blocked ducts alongside energized adjacent circuits, in an existing right-of-way with landscaping, driveways, or pavement.

Cable placement inside a controlled facility: laying feeder cable in covered cable trenches/troughs or pulling it through duct banks within a fenced substation yard, generating plant, or industrial campus, where layout is fixed, access is controlled, and standard raceway hardware is used.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is trench excavation, the step preceding this task. It does not transfer: the machine moves soil with a bucket and never handles, feeds, tensions, or places a cable or conduit, which is the substance of laying/stringing cable.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is trenchless conduit installation. It does not substantiate this task: it is a laboratory-stage prototype under operator control that places empty conduit, not cable laid or pulled to utility standards.

sources.system: Dual-arm wire harness assembly robot cell
sources.developer: academic/industrial research consortium (published review and system papers)
sources.title: A dual-arm robotic system for automated multi-branch wire harness assembly in automotive industry

It does not transfer: the objects are light signal wires in a fixtured cell, not multi-hundred-kilogram reels of medium-voltage cable pulled at high tension into ducts, and even this analogue is not in production use.

tasks.label: Cut trenches for laying underground cables, using trenchers and cable plows.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Service lateral on an existing residential property: cut a 50–200 ft trench from a pad-mount transformer or pedestal to the house, using a walk-behind/ride-on trencher or mini excavator. Established lawn, shrubs, fences and gates, driveway, irrigation lines, and existing gas/water/sewer/telecom crossings; depth to spec, hand-dig at crossings, sod/landscape restoration expected.

New residential subdivision or commercial development under construction: contractor-controlled, graded ground with roughed-in streets; trench primary and secondary runs between transformer pads, pedestals and building stubs, often a joint trench with telecom/gas. Ride-on trencher or excavator; routes staked by survey; other trades working on site.

Rural or suburban road right-of-way and easements: ride-on trencher or tractor-mounted vibratory cable plow running cable along the shoulder/ditch line for hundreds to thousands of feet. Live traffic adjacent, driveway and culvert crossings, uneven ditch banks, fences, and marked crossings of existing buried utilities.

Greenfield energy-project or open-field cross-country run: long, mostly straight trench or plow run through open field or a graded generation/collector site for underground cable; exclusive-use work area, few or no pre-existing buried utilities, spoil piled alongside for backfill after cable is laid.

Urban or paved setting: saw-cut and trench through asphalt/concrete street, parking lot, or sidewalk in a congested corridor with dense existing utilities; traffic control and lane closures, potholing/vacuum excavation near locates, confined work zone, pavement restoration required.

tasks.label: Cut and peel lead sheathing and insulation from defective or newly installed cables and conduits prior to splicing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Urban network manhole/vault: prepare the ends of 13–27 kV feeder cables (legacy paper-insulated lead-covered and modern polymeric) for a splice — score and peel the lead sheath or jacket, remove shield/semicon and insulation to dimension without nicking the conductor. Confined, damp, congested structure under a city street with adjacent energized cables.

Suburban underground residential distribution: prepare 15/25 kV jacketed concentric-neutral cable ends (jacket, neutral wires, semicon, insulation) at a padmount transformer, switchgear pedestal or hand-hole in the street/right-of-way, often kneeling at grade in variable weather.

Secondary and service conductors: strip insulation from triplex/quadruplex service cable, secondary mains, street-light and transformer leads at a pole, weatherhead or pedestal, working from a bucket or the ground before splicing/crimping.

Overhead primary: remove covering/insulation from covered conductor (tree wire, spacer cable) or clean and prepare conductor ends for a splice sleeve at pole top from an aerial bucket, exposed to weather, traffic and clearance constraints.
Substation or building cable vault: prepare medium/high-voltage cable ends for joints or terminations inside a utility-controlled facility with racked cables, lighting and standard clearances.
Service-center shop or lay-down yard: cut cable to length off the reel and strip/prefabricate the ends on a bench before the assembly is taken to the field for splicing.

sources.system: Cable Splicing Machine (CSM)
sources.developer: ULC Technologies (SPX Technologies) with Con Edison
sources.title: Con Edison and ULC Technologies test Cable Splicing Machine to improve worker safety, grid reliability - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Cable Splicing Machine was field-trialed with Con Edison in underground structures; splicers lowered it in and inserted the medium-voltage cable, after which the machine autonomously carried out three cable-preparation operations per phase in about 25–30 minutes.

sources.system: Cable Splicing Machine (CSM)
sources.title: Con Edison demonstrates new MV cable splicing technology | Enlit World
sources.claim: The machine clamps onto an uncut cable in the field and its tool plate carries tools that strip back each layer of the ... specified dimension with precision depth control, with the operator monitoring from outside the manhole.

sources.system: Cable Splicing Machine (CSM)
sources.title: Con Edison and ULC Technologies Unveil Cable Splicing Machine for Improved Worker Safety, Efficiency and Grid Reliability | Utility Dive
sources.claim: The system is described as an automated cable-end preparation system for medium-voltage feeder cables in underground vaults, i.e. exactly the pre-splice cutting and peeling step of this task.

sources.system: MegaStrip 9680 automatic cut & strip machine
sources.title: MegaStrip 9680 | Komax
sources.claim: Commercial automatic cut-and-strip machines cut power cable to length and strip multiconductor and shielded cables up ... outside diameter and 300 mm² (600 MCM) autonomously once the cable is fed into the machine.

It is the same physical act as the lineworker's pre-splice preparation — cutting cable to length and removing jacket, shield and insulation layers to specified dimensions without damaging the conductor — on power cables of comparable size (up to 600 MCM), performed to tighter tolerance than field work when the cable is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.claim: Live-working robots used on 10 kV overhead distribution lines — the pole-top equivalent of stripping conductor insulation before making a connection — still rely on remote master–slave control and do not support full autonomous operation, with most prototypes at laboratory verification stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: live-line insulation peeling and drainage-wire connection on pole-top conductors, the closest robotic analogue to stripping overhead conductor insulation before splicing. Cited to show the pole-top instances are not autonomously served, supporting a negative E3/E2 judgment there.

tasks.label: Clean, tin, and splice corresponding conductors by twisting ends together or by joining ends with metal clamps and soldering connections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pole-top tap/jumper connection on 4–35 kV overhead distribution primary, worked from an insulated bucket at a roadside or alley pole: clean/strip the conductor at the connection point, position the tap lead, install and tighten a hot-line or wedge/compression clamp joining lead to main conductor, energized or de-energized, in traffic and weather.

In-line or mid-span splice of an overhead distribution conductor (#6–4/0 ACSR/AAC/AAAC) during storm repair or new stringing: cut back and wire-brush/clean the conductor ends, apply inhibitor, install a full-tension compression or automatic splice, aloft on the line or at ground level on the reel setup in a rural/roadside right-of-way.

Underground medium-voltage cable splice in a manhole, vault, trench or pad-mount enclosure: strip jacket, shield and insulation, clean/abrade the conductor, join conductors with a compression connector or shear-bolt connector, then build up the joint; confined, often wet, dirty, legacy layouts that differ vault to vault.

Service and secondary connections at a customer's premises or at the pole: splice/connect service-drop triplex or underground service lateral conductors (#6–4/0 aluminum) with compression sleeves, split-bolts or insulation-piercing connectors, cleaning aluminum surfaces and applying oxide inhibitor, working from a ladder, bucket or the ground on private property.

Full-tension compression splice of a large transmission conductor (e.g., 795 kcmil ACSR/ACSS) during stringing or emergency repair: clean the aluminum strands and steel core, press the steel sleeve then the aluminum sleeve with a hydraulic press, in the right-of-way.

Bench work in a utility service center, shop trailer or substation control house: tinning and soldering conductor and lead ends, making up cable assemblies and pigtails, splicing control/instrument and secondary wiring at a fixed workbench under company control.

roles.description: Install and repair telecommunications cable, including fiber optics.

tasks.label: Splice cables, using hand tools, epoxy, or mechanical equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aerial outside-plant fiber splicing: technician works from a bucket truck or ladder at a pole, or in a splice trailer at the roadside, opening a splice closure on the strand, stripping the cable sheath, identifying color-coded buffer tubes and 12-288 fibers, fusion splicing them into trays, and resealing the closure in wind, heat, or rain.

Underground fiber splicing: work in a manhole, vault, handhole, or curbside pedestal - often confined, wet, and dirty - to splice a new segment, add a mid-span tap, or restore a dig-cut cable, with the splice case reassembled and sealed.

Copper cable splicing/repair: reconnecting pairs in an aerial or buried splice case with modular connectors or crimp/scotchlok connectors, then re-encapsulating with gel or epoxy and pressurizing/closing the case, typically on a legacy voice/DSL plant trouble call.

Splicing inside a carrier facility: central office, cable headend, hub, cell-site cabinet, or an MDU telecom room - fusion splicing pigtails onto trunk/riser cable, terminating into fiber panels or an FDH, on a clean bench or splice cart with utility power and lighting.

Customer-premises drop splicing: FTTH drop terminated at the NID or inside a home/apartment - fusion splicing a drop to a pre-terminated stub or installing a mechanical splice/field-installable connector in a cramped, variable, occupied space.

sources.system: Thorlabs Vytran All-in-One Fiber Preparation and Fusion Splicing Workstation (FFS series)

sources.claim: Commercial benchtop workstation that integrates fiber preparation, cleaving, fusion splicing, proof testing and recoating into one machine-controlled system, producing finished splices once fibers are loaded into its holders.

sources.system: Vytran Automated Glass Processors with Integrated Cleaver (VHD320C / GPX series)
sources.title: Thorlabs · Vytran® Automated Glass Processors with Integrated Cleaver

sources.system: ficonTEC automated strip, cleave & insert fiber assembly set-up (with Nyfors and Fraunhofer IOF)
sources.title: Automated Strip, Cleave & Insert - ficonTEC
sources.claim: Machine-vision-guided automated system strips and cleaves 12-fiber ribbon and inserts the bare fibers into ferrules with about 1 micron clearance, inside a fixtured photonics assembly machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated ribbon-fiber stripping, cleaving and connectorization. Same objects (125 µm coated fibers, ribbons), same micron-level precision and same fixtured machine environment as the preparation and joining steps of a fiber splice.

sources.date: commercial line, in production use through 2024-2026

tasks.label: Inspect or test lines or cables, recording and analyzing test results, to assess transmission characteristics and locate faults or malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outside-plant fiber fault location/verification at a field access point: after a cable cut or reported outage the technician opens a handhole, pedestal, street cabinet or aerial splice case, connects an OTDR/light source with a launch cord to individual fibers, shoots traces at 1310/1550 nm, interprets events, records the distance to the break or high-loss splice, and reports it to the repair crew. Weather, traffic, mud, and buried/aerial access conditions vary by site.

Fiber testing performed from a central office, headend, remote terminal hut, or colocation/data-center patch panel: connect to jumpers on the frame, run OTDR/optical power/loss measurements on point-to-point or PON feeder fibers, sectionalize a fault or verify a circuit before turn-up, and log results in the trouble ticket or records system.

FTTH/small-business service call: at the customer premises the technician reads ONT/ONU receive light levels, tests the drop fiber with an OTDR, VFL or power meter, inspects and cleans connector end-faces, determines whether the fault is in the drop, the NID/ONT, or upstream, and records the readings on the ticket. Home layouts, clutter, and access vary.

Metallic (copper pair or coax) outside-plant testing at a cross-connect box, pedestal, terminal or aerial tap: TDR/resistance-fault-locate, insulation resistance, capacitance length, tone-and-probe pair identification, or coax sweep/signal-leakage checks to find a wet section, short, open, or damaged sheath, with results recorded for the repair.

Metallic/coax testing at the customer end (NID, demarc, drop): loop measurements, noise/balance, DSL sync or RF signal-level readings taken at the network interface device to divide the trouble between inside wire and outside plant, results recorded on the ticket.

Acceptance/certification testing of newly installed cable on a build: bidirectional OTDR and insertion-loss certification of tens to hundreds of fibers (or continuity/pair testing of new copper) on a new route, campus, or building riser at a jobsite, producing a documented test report accepted by the customer or engineer.

tasks.label: Clean or maintain tools or test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field fiber job (aerial bucket, pedestal, handhole, splice van): repeatedly cleaning connector end faces on test jumpers, launch cords and pigtails and cleaning/inspecting the OTDR, OLTS and power-meter optical ports with wipes, cleaning pens, IPA and a scope, in dust, wind and cramped positions before and after each test.

Field splicing work: routine upkeep of the fusion splicer and cleaver — swabbing V-grooves, lenses/mirrors and electrode area with alcohol and lint-free swabs, blowing out dust and fiber scraps, emptying the scrap-fiber bin, running arc calibration — inside a splice van/trailer or at the work site.

Field splicing work: replacing worn consumables and adjusting the splicer/cleaver — unscrewing and fitting new electrodes, rotating or replacing the cleaver blade, changing rubber pads/clamps, swapping batteries, checking the unit still meets loss specs afterward.

End-of-job upkeep of hand tools at the truck or job site: washing/wiping mud, grease and gel off strippers, cable knives, cutters, crimpers and wrenches, drying them, light oiling, and returning them clean to the truck bins.

Shop/warehouse bench session on test sets: wiping down cases and cords, cleaning optical ports and reference jumpers, cleaning and inspecting electrical test leads, clips and adapter contacts, and functionally checking each set against a reference before it goes back on the truck.

Central office, hub, cell site cabinet or customer equipment room: cleaning patch-cord and panel connector end faces and the ports of test gear kept on site, dusting and wiping the test equipment and its carrying case, in a climate-controlled, institution-controlled space.

sources.system: Telescent Network Topology Manager (NTM) robotic patch panel

sources.claim: Telescent's Network Topology Manager is a rack-mounted robotic fiber cross-connect whose robot cleans each fiber connector end face automatically before making a connection, delivering repeatable low-loss connections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning single-fiber connector end faces to a tested low-loss standard. Same objects (1.25/2.5 mm ferrules), same micron-scale cleanliness requirement, and same verification-by-loss-measurement acceptance criterion as a technician cleaning jumpers and test-set ports.

sources.system: Telescent G4 NTM
sources.title: MOX Signs Agreement to Deploy Telescent's Fiber Automation Platform on its Next-Generation Long-Haul Route

sources.claim: NTT-AT's Offsoon optical connector end-face cleaning system mechanically controls solvent injection and wiping to clean SC/LC/MT/MPO end faces, and can be combined with a robot arm and ... end-face inspection machine to form an automatic cleaning-and-inspection line.

sources.system: Robosonic robotic ultrasonic cleaning cell (Fanuc CR-7i)

sources.title: TCS-FP torch cleaning station available from Abicor Binzel | Canadian Metalworking

tasks.label: Set up service for customers, installing, connecting, testing, or adjusting equipment, such as digital subscriber line modems.
Access specific areas to string lines, or install terminal boxes, auxiliary equipment, or appliances, using bucket trucks, climbing poles or ladders, or entering tunnels, trenches, or crawl spaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aerial work from a bucket truck on a street or rural roadside pole line: set up truck and traffic control, ride the bucket to the communications space, string/lash new fiber or coax across several spans, and mount aerial terminals or splice closures on the strand. Weather, traffic, vegetation, varying pole framing.

Poles or structures a truck cannot reach (rear-lot easements, backyards, slopes, alleys): climb with gaffs and belt or set an extension ladder, carry hardware aloft, attach brackets/terminal boxes and pull drop or distribution cable.

Underground vault/manhole entry in a street or parking lot: confined-space setup (gas test, ventilation, pumping water), descend, rack and pull cable through duct, place or reopen splice cases and auxiliary equipment in a wet, cramped, variably configured vault.

Street-level underground plant: working in or alongside an open trench or bore pit, feeding/pulling cable and innerduct into conduit, setting pedestals and handholes at a dug-up roadside or subdivision construction site.

Customer premises (home or small business): ladder to the eave, drill and mount the NID/terminal box, run drop cable, and enter crawl space, attic or basement to route cable to the inside jack; clutter, insulation, low headroom, pets, unknown layout.

Inside an institution-controlled building (central office, campus equipment room, hospital riser, data center): ladder or rolling-stair access to cable tray/ladder rack, run tie cables in a riser, terminate on blocks or patch panels in an equipment lineup.

sources.system: Averex robotic wiring centre
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (Springer)
sources.claim: Kiesling/Rittal's Averex portal robot performs fully automated wiring of fixtured control cabinets: cutting, crimping, connecting wires to terminals and routing them inside the enclosure, in a purpose-built machine cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiring and equipping electrical enclosures. Same class of objects as this task's end product (terminal boxes, terminal blocks, auxiliary devices, insulated conductors) at equal or finer precision, with the enclosure fixtured and presented to the machine — exactly the E1 counterfactual for 'install terminal boxes, auxiliary equipment' once access is supplied by the environment.

sources.system: Perforex MT 1101 / MT 2201 milling terminal
sources.title: 4055912 Perforex Milling Terminal MT 1101 S — Rittal
sources.claim: Rittal's Perforex Milling Terminal is a commercially sold four-axis CNC machine that automatically drills, threads and cuts openings in enclosures and mounting panels to accept components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing and mounting hardware in enclosures. The drilling and cut-out work a line installer performs to hang a terminal box or backboard hardware is done automatically when the workpiece is fixtured, supporting the mounting half of the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Telescent G5 Network Topology Manager / robotic patch panel
sources.title: Telescent Introduces Highest Density Optical Circuit Switches for 1.6T DR4 and DR8 Interconnects in GPU Clusters (Business Wire)
sources.claim: Telescent's G5 robotic patch panel is a commercially shipped system whose internal robot physically makes and breaks single-mode fiber connections under software control, routing large numbers of fiber cords inside a purpose-built enclosure without a technician present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically running and terminating fiber jumpers between ports. Same objects (single-mode fiber, latching connectors) and tighter loss/precision tolerance than field work, performed by a robot inside a purpose-built structure — evidence that stringing and connecting lines is achievable when route and terminations are presented to the machine (E1).

sources.system: Bombyx aerial fiber deployment robot

sources.transferJustification: Directly related: aerial placement of fiber along an existing overhead route. It substitutes for part of the bucket-truck stringing job, but wraps only on utility MV conductors, remains a prototype licensed for productization, and neither attaches pole hardware nor terminates, so it does not complete the aerial instance.

sources.system: Q-Bot underfloor insulation robot
sources.date: 2022 (award write-up); deployed in UK social housing
sources.title: RetroFIT for the Future: Q-Bot underfloor insulation — Torus
sources.claim: Q-Bot's crawl-space robots enter suspended-floor voids through a hatch or vent and apply insulation, but they are remotely operated by a technician over a tether rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing installation work inside a residential crawl space. It is the closest existing crawl-space work robot and is continuously teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment for entering crawl spaces to install telecom cable and terminal boxes.

tasks.label: Lay underground cable directly in trenches, or string it through conduits running through trenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: FTTH/coax distribution and drop cable placed directly in a plowed or trenched line through a residential neighborhood: public right-of-way and private yards, sod/driveways/landscaping, existing gas-water-electric utilities to avoid, cable paid off a reel into the trench at required depth, slack coiled at pedestals, backfill and restoration.

Urban duct work: pulling or jetting fiber/copper cable through existing conduit between manholes and handholes in a city street, under traffic control, with duct proving/rodding, lubricant, pulling grip and winch or blowing machine, intermediate figure-8 or mid-assist at each vault, sealing ducts and coiling slack.

Rural/highway backbone placement: long runs of conduit and/or direct-buried cable placed in trenches or plowed in along roadside right-of-way and field crossings, uneven terrain, reel changes, road/creek bores tied in, warning tape and locate wire installed.

Institutional grounds (university, hospital, airport, industrial plant, military base): conduit and cable placed in trenches across controlled premises between buildings/manholes, coordinated with facilities staff, known as-builts, marked existing utilities, restoration of lawn/pavement.

Repair/replacement: damaged buried cable located and exposed by careful hand/vacuum excavation, a replacement section laid in the open trench or re-pulled through the damaged conduit segment, slack and splice enclosure positioned in the trench or a new handhole, then backfilled.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is trench excavation, which precedes this task. Transfer does NOT carry: the cited autonomy covers bucket digging along a geofenced line, not handling a cable reel, feeding cable into the trench at depth, or pulling/jetting cable through conduit, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.system: Bombyx fiber-wrapping robot

sources.claim: Meta's Bombyx robot places fibre optic cable by wrapping it on medium-voltage power lines, and in its demonstrated state still requires a remote operator to get past obstacles — the closest fielded fibre-placing robot, and it is aerial rather than underground.

Transfer does not carry: the medium is an energized aerial conductor, not a trench or duct, and the demonstration relies on a remote operator, so it cannot support a positive judgment for underground cable placement.

tasks.label: Pull cable through ducts by hand or with winches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outside-plant underground pull: crew sets up at street manholes/handholes, rods or blows a pull line through a buried duct that may contain silt, water or existing cables, attaches swivel and pulling grip to a 1,000-3,000 ft fiber or copper cable, applies lubricant, feeds from a reel trailer and runs a truck-mounted capstan winch while monitoring tension; traffic control and confined-space entry apply.

Commercial building / campus conduit and riser pull: fish tape or rod through EMT, sleeves and 90-degree bends between telecom rooms, tie on and hand- or power-pull backbone fiber/copper up risers and through cable tray, protect bend radius, dress and label at each end.

Residential service drop: hand-pull a drop fiber/coax through a short driveway sleeve, buried conduit from pedestal to NID, or through a wall/crawlspace conduit at a private home, clearing obstructions and dealing with unknown, sometimes collapsed or blocked duct.

Central office, headend or data center pull: place cable through innerduct, floor sleeves and overhead racking inside a controlled telecom facility, working around live equipment with fire-stopping and tight bend-radius and dressing standards.

New-build microduct placement along a subdivision or right-of-way: set up jetting/pulling gear at a handhole, install duct seals and pushers, blow or winch fiber microcable into freshly placed microduct, coil and secure slack at each vault.

sources.system: Intelli-SuperJet cable jetting/floating machine
sources.title: Intelli-SuperJet™ < Plumett - Push the boundaries
sources.claim: Plumettaz Intelli-SuperJet is a commercial cable blowing/floating machine that drives telecom cable and multiducts into pre-installed ducts under embedded computer control, monitoring installation force and automatically stopping if preset maximum force or slippage is exceeded; the operator sets it up and starts it rather than driving each motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cable jetting/floating into pre-installed duct. It produces the same accepted output as a winch pull — a telecom cable placed through a duct run — on the same objects (fiber/copper cable, HDPE duct), with the machine, not the worker, supplying and regulating the installation force.

sources.system: OptiJet cable jetting machine
sources.title: Intelligent cable jetting, fiber blowing and floating machines | Plumett
sources.claim: Plumettaz markets the OptiJet micro-cable blowing machine as autonomous and intelligent; it automatically determines the maximum pulling/pushing force the cable can take and controls belt drive and speed to place fiber micro-cables in micro-ducts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine placement of micro-cable into pre-installed micro-duct. Same objects and end state as the worker's duct pull in new-build microduct work; the machine self-limits force to protect the cable, which is the quality criterion for a pull.

sources.system: HDPE conduit extrusion line with pull-line/cable pre-installation
sources.title: HDPE Conduit Material: Five Frequently Asked Questions
sources.claim: HDPE conduit manufacturers routinely insert pull tape or the cable itself into conduit on the factory extrusion line, with the line feeding the cable into the pipe continuously as the conduit is formed — machine-executed placement of cable inside duct in a purpose-built production setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory pre-installation of cable in conduit. It is the E1 form of the worker's task — duct and cable brought to the machine — and delivers the accepted output (cable free inside duct, ready for service) at production quality and volume.

sources.system: SIMpull Cable-in-Conduit (CIC) production

sources.claim: Southwire's SIMpull Cable-in-Conduit is a shipping product in which the cable is factory-installed inside lubricated HDPE conduit so that the cable sits free in the duct and can later be pulled out and replaced; this factory line output substitutes for a field duct pull in DOT, utility, airport and data-center work.

sources.system: SAM (Sewer Access Module) / FiberCop sewer fiber robots
sources.title: CableRunner North America launches pilot project to build San Francisco's first city-owned fiber-in-the-sewer infrastructure
sources.claim: Robots used to place telecom fiber inside existing underground pipes — CityNet's SAM sewer access module and CableRunner's FiberCop — are lowered into manholes by two-person crews and driven through the pipe with cameras; autonomy is not established and human crews perform the man-accessible portions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing fiber conduit inside existing underground pipe. Cited to show the only field robots working inside live duct/pipe networks are crew-deployed and remote-driven, so they cannot support an autonomous field (E2/E3) judgment for duct pulling.

sources.system: MicroBORE trenchless drilling robot

sources.claim: Openreach's 2025 field robotics trial for last-drop fiber is a trenchless boring machine that cuts a channel from the main duct to the premises; it is an operator-run machine, and no autonomous system is reported performing the cable pull itself.

tasks.label: Pull up cable by hand from large reels mounted on trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aerial placement along a roadside right-of-way: technician at a line truck hand-pulls fiber or coax off a large reel mounted on the truck, feeding hundreds of feet of cable up to the messenger strand for lashing across pole spans; traffic, weather, driveways, trees and uneven shoulders vary span to span.

Underground duct placement on a city street: reel truck parked at the feed manhole; the tech hand-pulls cable off the reel and manually feeds it into the duct while a winch pulls from the far manhole, figure-eighting slack on the pavement and watching for kinks and minimum bend radius.

Service drop to a residence or small business: tech pulls drop cable off a reel on the service truck and pays it out across a yard, driveway or alley to the pole or NID, judging slack and avoiding fences, shrubs, pets and parked cars.

Greenfield/rural build: large heavy reel on a truck or reel trailer; crew hand-pulls cable off the reel to lay it out along a plow/trench route or to figure-eight a long pull, over rough ground, ditches and driveways.

Institutional or campus site (hospital campus, airport, business park, central office/data center): reel truck at a dock or MPOE inside controlled premises; tech hand-pulls cable off the reel and feeds it into a riser, cable vault or conduit sleeve along a fixed, maintained route.

sources.system: KABELMAT coil winder and binding line (drum unwinder + length measuring + cutter + coiler)
sources.title: Coil winder and binding line • Cable winding made easy — KABELMAT Wickteltechnik
sources.claim: KABELMAT sells a fully automatic coiling and winding line in which a powered drum unwinder pays cable off a large cable drum, measures length, cuts and coils it without a person pulling cable off the drum; it runs as a fixtured factory line.

Small business or commercial premises (bar, clinic waiting room, hotel, office): wall-mount or service displays, run cable above a drop ceiling or through conduit, install a distribution amplifier/headend or MDU tap, connect and balance multiple TVs, test and hand off during business hours.

tasks.label: Place insulation over conductors, or seal splices with moisture-proof covering.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fiber fusion-splice protection: after each fusion in an aerial closure, pedestal or vault, the technician slides the heat-shrink protection sleeve over the bare fused fiber, runs the splicer's heat oven, and seats the protected splice in the tray — dozens to hundreds of fibers per closure, working from a bucket at a pole, a splice van at the roadside, or kneeling at a handhole.

Sealing a splice closure: fitting gel/grommet seal blocks around cable sheaths, seating end-plate gaskets, latching or torquing a dome or in-line closure, and pressure/leak checking it, on aerial strand, in a ground pedestal, or in a below-grade handhole exposed to weather, dirt and standing water.

Copper cable splice: insulating individual pair connections with sleeves, IDC modules or tape, then re-sealing the splice with encapsulant/gel or a re-enterable moisture-proof wrap inside a manhole or pedestal, often damp, cramped and poorly lit.

Drop/service connection weatherproofing at a customer premises: sealing the drop terminal, NID or outdoor connector with boots, mastic/sealing tape and silicone around the sheath entry, on the exterior wall of a private home or small business.

Indoor splice work in a central office, headend, equipment hut or MDU cable room: applying splice protection sleeves and closing/sealing splice trays and enclosures in a clean, climate-controlled, institution-controlled facility.

tasks.label: String cables between structures and lines from poles, towers, or trenches, and pull lines to proper tension.

instances.label: Aerial outside-plant placing along an existing joint-use pole line on a suburban/rural road: crew rigs blocks on poles, pays fiber or coax off a reel from a bucket truck, pulls the span through blocks, sets sag/tension against a chart, dead-ends at each pole and lashes cable to the messenger strand, working around traffic, trees, and existing power/telecom attachments.

Underground placing: pulling a fiber or copper cable several hundred to a couple thousand feet through duct/conduit between manholes or handholes in a city street or roadside, using pull rope/winch, lubricant and tension monitoring, feeding from a reel trailer, figure-eighting slack and coiling at the far vault, under traffic control.

Service drop / lateral: stringing a drop or small self-supporting cable from a pole or pedestal to a house or small business, crossing a yard or driveway, attaching a drop clamp/hook to the structure, tensioning to clear ground and vehicle traffic, and securing to the building.

Inside-plant / facility cable runs: pulling cable between structures inside a controlled facility — central office or data center risers, cable trays and ladder racks, campus building-to-building runs, or coax/fiber runs up a cell tower inside a fenced compound — with slack, bend radius and support spacing to standard.

Direct-buried / trench placing in rural or roadside right-of-way: laying cable from a reel into an open trench or feeding it behind a plow/boring rig, pulling it through the run to remove slack and set proper tension before backfill.

tasks.label: Fill and tamp holes, using cement, earth, and tamping devices.

instances.label: Backfilling and tamping a pole hole after a new telecom/joint-use pole is set from a digger derrick on a rural or suburban roadside right-of-way: spoil (and sometimes crushed stone) returned in lifts into the annulus around the pole butt and tamped with a bar or pneumatic/hydraulic pole tamper while the pole is held plumb; uneven ground, energized lines overhead, passing traffic.

Backfilling and compacting an open trench or plowed slit for buried fiber/coax drop or distribution cable in a residential yard or roadside easement: sand/soil bedded over conduit, spoil returned by shovel or mini-excavator, compacted with a plate compactor, topsoil and sod replaced; landscaping, driveways, sprinkler lines and other buried utilities in the way.

Restoring a cut in pavement, sidewalk or driveway over a bore pit, handhole or cable-fault dig on a public street: gravel base placed and compacted in lifts, then concrete poured, screeded and finished flush (or hot/cold asphalt patch placed and tamped), under traffic control with pedestrians nearby.

Filling and tamping small hand-dug potholes/keyholes in congested urban strips — locate/potholing test holes, anchor holes, pedestal or handhole sets — where fill must be replaced and tamped by hand in tight quarters immediately adjacent to live gas, water and power facilities.

Backfilling and compacting conduit trench segments on institutionally controlled premises — a university or hospital campus, industrial plant, data-center yard or telecom facility compound — with controlled access, a maintained layout, marked utilities and room for machine compaction equipment.
