sources.transferJustification: A short design-data-driven trench with a leveled floor is the same output as a short cable trench; establishes that small, discrete trenches (not just long production runs) can be dug autonomously in a prepared setting.

sources.system: Gravis Rack / Gravis autonomous earthmoving system
sources.title: Gravis Robotics raises $23M to scale autonomous earthmoving tech - Tech.eu
sources.claim: Gravis Robotics' retrofit autonomy for excavators handles trenching and earthworks and was deployed by Taylor Woodrow on an active construction project at Manchester Airport, described as the UK's first ... autonomous excavation on a live site.
sources.transferJustification: Trenching is named among the tasks the system performs; the deployment shows autonomous excavation working on institution-controlled premises with mapped constraints, the E2 case for conduit trenching on campuses.

sources.system: Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES)
sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs, Buried Utility Lines | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System uses ground-penetrating radar, a robotic arm with interchangeable tools, road-surface coring and soft vacuum excavation to expose buried gas mains beneath roadways and reinstate them; trialled with SGN in the UK.
sources.transferJustification: Keyhole excavation to daylight a buried gas main is the same act as potholing to expose a buried telecom conduit: soft-dig around a fragile known asset at similar depth and precision; prototype status limits it to a purpose-built/controlled setting.

tasks.label: Install equipment such as amplifiers or repeaters to maintain the strength of communications transmissions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aerial HFC/coax plant: replace or add a strand-mounted line amplifier or optical node from a bucket truck at a pole in a residential street — unbolt/bolt the housing to the messenger strand, mate and torque coax connectors and power inserters, seat the amplifier module and lid, set pads/equalizers and sweep-verify levels, working over live traffic in variable weather.

Headend, hub, central office or in-line amplifier hut: rack-mount an optical amplifier (EDFA), regenerator or repeater shelf — mount rails/chassis with screws in an existing 19-inch rack, land DC/AC power, clean, route and plug fiber jumpers, label, then turn up and verify gain/output power.

Customer premises or in-building: install a drop amplifier, bi-directional amplifier or cellular/DAS repeater at a home, MDU or small business — mount the unit on a backboard or wall, terminate and connect coax/fiber, power it, and verify signal levels in a space the technician takes as found.

Underground/at-grade plant: install an amplifier, power supply or repeater in a pedestal, handhole vault or street cabinet — kneeling in the right-of-way or entering a wet, cramped vault, pulling slack cable, bolting the unit in the enclosure, mating connectors and testing.

Cell site, rooftop or tower: install a tower-mounted amplifier, remote radio/booster or repeater at height — hoist the unit, bolt it to the mount, connect jumpers/fiber and grounding, weatherproof the connections, and verify performance outdoors.

sources.system: SoftBank robot-friendly server rack with lifter robot / CTU container robots
sources.title: Inside Look: How SoftBank Corp. is Creating "Robot-friendly" Environments at Data Centers
sources.claim: SoftBank developed a purpose-built 'robot-friendly' cable-less server rack in which a lifter robot autonomously places rack equipment into a specified slot, with power, optical network and cooling connections made blind-mate on insertion; testing at its Tomakomai AI data center.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing a rack-mounted unit into telecom/IT racks. Installing a rack-mount amplifier/repeater is the same class of work — insert a chassis into a rack position and make power and optical connections — and the article states standard racks' dense cabling defeats robots, so this only works in a purpose-built rack.

sources.system: Telescent G4 NTM robotic fiber cross-connect
sources.title: MOX Networks to Deploy Telescent's Fiber Automation Platform
sources.claim: Telescent's G4 Network Topology Manager is a commercially deployed robotic fiber cross-connect: inside its purpose-built enclosure a robot autonomously grabs, routes and plugs single-mode fiber connectors to requested ports in carrier facilities, with built-in power-meter/OTDR verification and NEBS Level 3 certification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making and verifying fiber optic connections in a carrier facility, the connector-mating and optical-verification portion of installing an optical amplifier or repeater. Same objects (LC/SC single-mode jumpers), same micron-level cleanliness and insertion-loss standards, but only inside a purpose-built robotic patch panel.

sources.system: Robotiq SD-100 screwdriving system on Universal Robots cobots
sources.title: Screwdriving With Cobots
sources.claim: Commercially available cobot screwdriving cells (Robotiq SD-100 screwdriver plus SF-300 feeder on Universal Robots arms) perform automated fastening in fixtured assembly cells at manufacturers including Continental, Faurecia, Hella, ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatable torqued fastening of enclosures and modules in a fixtured cell — the mounting/lid/bracket portion of installing an amplifier housing when the work is presented to the machine, with comparable fasteners and torque tolerances.

sources.system: Ericsson USA 5G Smart Factory automated production line
sources.title: Feature: Ericsson smart factory is where AI meets US-made 5G
sources.claim: Ericsson's USA 5G Smart Factory in Lewisville, Texas runs a highly automated 24/7 line building Massive MIMO radio-antenna units (RF amplifier hardware), using long pick-and-place lines, automated inspection and mobile robots on the floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated build and electrical verification of RF amplifier/radio units in a purpose-built line. It shows the amplifier hardware itself can be assembled and tested to carrier quality by machines when the work is fixtured and presented, i.e. the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Tianxun data center O&M robot (2nd generation)
sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center
sources.claim: Alibaba's second-generation Tianxun data center robot is reported to replace faulty hard disks in racks without human intervention, but its scope is hot-swap module exchange, not mounting chassis or making cable/fiber connections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hardware replacement inside racks in a structured facility. It is cited to show the limit of in-facility robotic hardware work: hot-swap trays with no fasteners, no power/fiber cabling and no turn-up testing, so it does not cover a whole amplifier installation.

sources.system: Bombyx aerial fiber deployment robot
sources.title: Meta Bombyx & SLAM | Slamcore case study
sources.claim: Meta's Bombyx aerial robot travels along medium-voltage power lines wrapping fiber optic cable and passing obstacles; reports differ on how much remote operator guidance it needs, and it performs cable laying only, not installation of amplifiers or other line equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work on aerial telecom plant. Cited to show that the only field robots operating on aerial lines deploy cable; none mounts amplifiers, mates and torques coax/fiber connectors, or sets and sweep-verifies levels at a pole.

tasks.label: Use a variety of construction equipment to complete installations, such as digger derricks, trenchers, or cable plows.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Setting or replacing a distribution/telecom pole or anchor with a truck-mounted digger derrick along a roadside right-of-way: position and outrigger the truck in a coned-off lane, auger a 6-8 ft hole through unknown soil/rock, unload and upend a 35-45 ft pole from the trailer, plumb it, backfill and tamp, all under overhead clearance constraints near energized conductors and passing traffic.

Trenching/excavating a conduit route in a developed suburban or urban right-of-way with a chain trencher or mini-excavator: parkway strips, shoulders and driveway aprons, working to locate marks around existing gas/water/power/telecom, hand-exposing crossings, staying inside a traffic-controlled work zone with pedestrians and property owners present.

Burying a residential fiber/coax service drop with a vibratory cable plow or walk-behind plow across a customer's yard from the pedestal to the house: navigating fences, sprinkler lines, landscaping, gates and pets, keeping depth over irregular terrain, feeding the drop cable and restoring the slit.

Long open-ground trenching or plowing for a conduit/fiber route on rural or greenfield ground: cleared right-of-way, farm field, or a new subdivision before build-out, with long straight runs to a surveyed alignment, few surface obstacles and no public traffic in the work area.

Directional boring a crossing under a driveway, sidewalk or road with a compact HDD rig: setting up entry/exit pits, steering the bore head to depth on grade while a locator walks the surface tracking the head, then reaming and pulling back the conduit — done in a street or yard with buried utility conflicts.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem (autonomous trenching excavator)
sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit kit turns standard mid-size excavators into fully autonomous trenching machines that dig to a geofenced plan on jobsites, commercially licensed to contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: excavating utility trenches for buried cable. Telecom underground installation uses the same machine class and the same accepted output (a trench on line and grade for conduit/cable), so trenching performance carries over where ground conditions are comparable.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem trenching robot
sources.title: Building the Future of Construction / Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built's autonomous trenching robots have excavated over ... in the US and Australia, with digging accuracy of 0.1 ft and rates up to 180 ft/hour.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above: production trenching for buried electrical/communication cable, at accuracy (0.1 ft) comparable to what telecom conduit trenches require.

sources.system: Built Robotics retrofitted excavators (trenching, piling, pre-drilling)
sources.title: Autonomous construction bots are building the solar infrastructure behind Meta's massive Hyperion data center
sources.claim: Built Robotics' retrofitted machines are working at active utility-scale solar and data-center construction sites, doing pile driving, trenching and pre-drilling, with more than 40 deployments completed.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the environment of the decisive system: open, contractor-controlled greenfield energy construction sites, not public streets or private yards.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 robotic pile driver
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers from Built Robotics for Solar Projects | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomously surveys, distributes, drives and inspects steel H-piles on utility-scale solar sites; contractors including Blattner use it, with a first large-scale fleet deal in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving foundation piles (survey, pick pile from a rack, place, drive to plumb/elevation) — the closest existing analogue to digger-derrick pole setting. Transfer is limited: piles are ~12-14 ft steel beams on graded solar sites, not 40 ft poles augered, upended, backfilled and tamped in a roadside right-of-way near energized lines.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem safety system
sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous machines rely on an eight-layer safety system with taped physical barriers and a GPS geofence that keeps people out of the autonomous work zone.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the operating envelope: an exclusion-zone work area cleared of people, which an active public street right-of-way with traffic and pedestrians does not provide.

sources.system: Bedrock Robotics Operator retrofit kit
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics begins supervised autonomous excavation on live construction sites as it moves toward commercialization
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics' excavator autonomy on live US construction sites is still supervised, with humans able to take over remotely; fully operator-less deployment was still a 2026 target as of February 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mass excavation and truck loading. Cited only to show that the frontier for excavator autonomy on as-found sites remains supervised mass earthmoving, not congested-corridor utility work.

tasks.label: Dig holes for power poles, using power augers or shovels, set poles in place with cranes, and hoist poles upright, using winches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rural/suburban roadside pole set in a public right-of-way: crew sets up a digger-derrick truck on a sloped shoulder, augers a 6-8 ft hole in mixed soil, picks a 40-ft wood pole off the trailer, lowers it into the hole, plumbs it and tamps backfill, working around live traffic, overhead energized primary and located buried facilities.

Urban/residential street pole replacement in a congested corridor: parked cars, driveways, sidewalks and tight setbacks; buried utilities force vacuum excavation or hand digging with shovels/bars near the hole; old pole is removed, new pole hoisted upright with the derrick winch and set, backfilled and compacted under traffic control.

Rear-lot easement or backyard pole where truck access is blocked: hole dug by hand with shovel, spoon and hand auger; the pole is carried/skidded in and hoisted upright with pike poles, a gin pole or a winch line run from the street; fences, trees, soft ground and property to protect.

Cross-country line construction over fields, pastures or hillsides: staked pole locations, track-mounted digger derrick or drill, rocky or wet ground needing rock augers or oversize holes, several poles set per day with poles distributed along the right-of-way by a pole trailer.

Pole set on institution-controlled premises - industrial plant, university campus, port/airport service area or the utility's own yard: graded ground, known layout, access controlled, poles staged nearby; hole augered and pole set, plumbed and backfilled with a derrick or crane.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 / RPS 25 autonomous piling system
sources.title: Advancing Utility-Scale Solar Construction with Robotic Automation for Precision Pile Driving (SICK Sensor Connection)
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomously selects a steel H-pile from inventory carried on the machine and drives it vertically into native ground with a vibratory hammer, paired with an RPS 25 stabilizer that holds each pile to tracker plumb/z-height tolerances, on utility-scale solar construction fields.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving foundation piles. Transfer is partial - the same core acts as pole setting (select a long structural member from a rack, position it at a surveyed point, hoist it upright and install it vertically to plumb tolerance) with tighter tolerances than a utility pole needs, but it omits augering a 6-8 ft hole and backfilling, so it substantiates only the fixtured, purpose-built (E1) version of the instance, not roadside pole setting.

sources.system: Built Robotics autonomous pile-driving excavators (RPD 35 / RPS 25)
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers From Built Robotics for Solar Projects - Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Blattner (Quanta Services) is deploying dozens of Built Robotics' autonomous pile-driving excavators on US solar projects; the machines carry piles onboard and install them unaided around the clock, with two machines working in tandem (one positions the pile, one drives it).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: solar foundation pile installation. Establishes that autonomous hoisting and vertical setting of long steel members in native ground is a commercially deployed, limited-intervention capability; it does not cover hole augering, backfilling or 40-ft wood poles in a roadway.

sources.system: Epiroc Pit Viper autonomous surface blasthole drill rigs
sources.title: Epiroc's ground-breaking drill rig Pit Viper celebrates 25 years including a decade with autonomous operations
sources.claim: Epiroc Pit Viper surface drill rigs have drilled more than ... of vertical blastholes autonomously over a decade at dozens of open-pit mines, running unmanned and with automatic bit changing, with improved hole depth and spatial accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: augering/drilling vertical holes to a specified position and depth in natural ground with a heavy machine, including automated tool handling - the hole-making half of this task. Hole depth and ground conditions are comparable in kind to a pole hole; the rig places no member, so it supports the fixtured (E1) case only.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem autonomous excavator
sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US - Construction Dive
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem converts standard excavators into machines that dig trenches, excavate foundations and grade pads fully autonomously between pre-determined GPS points on construction sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation to spec at surveyed coordinates. Supports the digging half of the instance with comparable machinery and soils, but it produces trenches/pads rather than a plumb pole hole and does not set or hoist a pole.

tasks.label: Participate in the construction or removal of telecommunication towers or associated support structures.

emergingTasks.label: Locate and mark cables that are buried underground.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Camera and Photographic Equipment Repairers
roles.description: Repair and adjust cameras and photographic equipment, including commercial video and motion picture camera equipment.

tasks.label: Adjust cameras, photographic mechanisms, or equipment such as range and view finders, shutters, light meters, or lens systems, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vintage/mechanical film camera on a repair shop bench: bring focal-plane or leaf shutter timing back to spec (curtain tension, slit width, slow-speed escapement), align rangefinder vertical/horizontal coincidence, calibrate a selenium/CdS meter. Model-specific internals, worn and gummy parts, iterative test-measure-tweak with jeweler's screwdrivers, spanners and tension keys.

Modern digital body at an authorized service center: after a shutter unit, mount or main-board replacement, adjust sensor plane/tilt shims, lens-mount flange depth and AF calibration; requires teardown past flex cables and shields, hand-tool adjustment of shim stacks and eccentric screws, reassembly, and verification against a chart or collimator.

Interchangeable still lens on the bench where the adjustment feature is reachable without internal teardown: infinity/back-focus shimming at the bayonet, focus-scale or adjustment-collar setting, verified on a collimator/projector to a stated MTF or focus tolerance.

Interchangeable lens needing internal teardown: re-seat or re-center a decentered element group, adjust helicoid stops, aperture blade linkage, zoom cam and floating-element timing inside the barrel, then reassemble and re-verify.

Cinema/broadcast camera and zoom at a rental house or service facility: flange-depth (back-focus) shimming of a PL/EF mount, zoom back-focus tracking adjustment, viewfinder/eyepiece and witness-mark calibration on large, varied bodies and lenses under fast turnaround between rentals.

On-location adjustment at a customer site (film set, studio, stadium, school, news truck): back-focus and mount adjustments, viewfinder alignment, quick shutter or meter tweaks performed with a pocket tool kit on whatever surface is available, under time pressure and uncontrolled lighting.

sources.system: Averna Active Alignment platform
sources.title: Active Alignment Camera Modules & Optical Devices | Averna
sources.claim: Commercial automated active-alignment cells assemble camera modules by dynamically adjusting lens position in 6 DOF against real-time image feedback to micron accuracy, with machine vision, robotics and in-line optical verification inside a production cleanroom station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory optical alignment rather than bench repair. It transfers only to the sub-case of setting a mounted lens assembly's focus/tilt to an optical spec (comparable objects, tighter precision), not to teardown of used, model-varied equipment.

sources.system: TRIOPTICS ProCam active alignment station
sources.title: Active alignment & assembly of camera modules | TRIOPTICS
sources.claim: TRIOPTICS ProCam active alignment stations measure the module optically and align lens to sensor, and with an integrated dispenser and UV cure operate as a fully automated camera-module fabrication/alignment station in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production alignment of new optics, not repair adjustment of a used camera. Comparable objects (lens/sensor assemblies) and tighter precision, but the workpiece is a known new product presented in a nest, not an arbitrary serviced device.

sources.system: TRIOPTICS OptiCentric 100 / ATS 100 with robot loading
sources.title: ROBOT-BASED: Automated centering of lens systems
sources.claim: Robot-loaded centering and alignment-turning stations center mounted lens systems to micron level in series production, with the robot handling loading of the centration tester and the adjusting lathe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: series-production lens centering. Objects (mounted lens assemblies) and precision are comparable or tighter and the measure-then-adjust-to-spec loop is the same, but the machine aligns/machines rather than servicing an assembled used lens with hand tools.

sources.system: Teledyne Adimec SPS3000 sensor positioning system
sources.title: Active Sensor Alignment - Adimec
sources.claim: Machine-controlled active sensor alignment stations position and fix an image sensor relative to the lens in camera production, replacing manual alignment for high-performance camera assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sensor-to-lens alignment during manufacture of a known camera model in a fixtured station; it covers the metrology-driven alignment step of a camera but not opening, shimming and reassembling a serviced camera body.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic screwdriving system (Manyar, Patel, Gupta)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic screwdriving for high-mix manufacturing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A research robotic system performs autonomous screwdriving in high-mix, low-volume manufacturing, with a physics-informed model of screw-tip motion and automatic detection of and recovery from failure modes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving fasteners, one hand-tool motion used in camera adjustment. It is a fixtured laboratory cell handling three screw types; it does not demonstrate diagnosing or adjusting an optomechanical mechanism to a measured spec.

sources.system: Automated e-waste disassembly (unscrewing) robotic system
sources.developer: academic research group (Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A robotic cell autonomously locates and removes screws from electronic devices for disassembly using a UR10e arm, depth camera and custom screwdriver, demonstrated as a laboratory e-waste unscrewing station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening electronic devices. Demonstrates only screw removal for recycling in a lab cell, with no reassembly, no adjustment to an optical or timing spec, and no worker-quality damage constraint.

sources.system: Daisy disassembly robot
sources.title: Apple's iPhone recycling robot shifts gears - Resource Recycling
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line disassembles iPhones at industrial rate in a purpose-built cell, but works by punching components out of identified known models for recycling rather than performing serviceable teardown and reassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of small consumer optical/electronic devices in a purpose-built cell. It bounds the state of the art: destructive, model-specific, one-way disassembly, so it cannot substantiate repair-quality adjustment and reassembly.

tasks.label: Disassemble equipment to gain access to defect, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench teardown of a consumer/prosumer digital camera body (DSLR, mirrorless, compact) in a repair shop: peel adhesive grip/leatherette, remove 20-40 recessed JIS/Phillips micro-screws of several lengths, release plastic clips with a spudger, unlatch and pull several ZIF/FPC ribbon connectors, lift shielding and the rear LCD/top plate to expose the shutter, sensor or main board defect, keeping every part reusable for reassembly.

Bench teardown of an interchangeable lens (AF zoom or prime): remove bayonet mount screws, shims and contact-block flex, use spanner wrench on staked retaining rings, split helicoid/cam barrel and free the AF motor, aperture unit or fungus-affected element group without disturbing optical centering or losing shim stacks.

Bench teardown of professional video/cinema gear (broadcast camcorder, digital cinema camera, EVF, studio monitor, lens control unit) at a service center: many panel and chassis screws, coax/board-to-board and ribbon connectors, ESD precautions, modular boards removed in sequence to reach the faulty board or connector.

Bench teardown of a vintage or mechanical film camera / classic lens: corroded, staked or lacquer-locked screws, adhesive-set retaining rings and leatherette, non-standard fasteners, no service documentation, improvised tools and judgment about how far to go without breaking brittle parts.

Bench teardown of coarser accessory and support equipment (studio strobe or flash head, battery grip, tripod/fluid head, LED panel, camera cage/rig): standard machine screws in a rigid housing, few or no fine flex circuits, cover and side panels removed to expose the failed switch, tube, motor or wiring.

On-site partial disassembly during field service at a customer location (event venue, location shoot, stadium camera position, client studio): technician opens a camera, lens or rig on a table or floor amid cables and crew to reach a jammed mechanism or loose connector, working around whatever the site provides.

sources.system: iDEAR intelligent disassembly demonstrator
sources.developer: Fraunhofer Institute for Factory Operation and Automation IFF
sources.title: Automated Electronics Disassembly - Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft research news
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IFF's iDEAR project demonstrator autonomously performs nondestructive disassembly steps on desktop computers in a robotic cell: locating and removing housing screws with tool changes, opening the housing and lifting the motherboard out, guided by 3D metrology and AI; the developers note glued parts and rusty or stripped screws hinder nondestructive disassembly, and the subprocess demonstrators are not yet integrated into one system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening electronic device housings with hand-tool operations (unscrewing, levering, lifting parts out) in a fixtured cell. It transfers to coarse photographic accessories with standard machine screws in rigid housings, but the demonstrated objects are PC-scale sheet-metal enclosures, not camera-scale M1.4 micro-screws, adhesive grips or ribbon connectors.

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing system (UR10e + mechatronic screwdriver)
sources.developer: Vicomtech / Tecnun-University of Navarra (Diaz et al., Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing 95:103032)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: A UR10e arm with a wrist RealSense camera and a custom mechatronic screwdriver autonomously detects four screw-head types, aligns by force sensing and unscrews fasteners on a recycled hoverboard, with 91-100% success per screw type; the tested fasteners are Allen M8/M4 and Phillips M3 class, mounted on an optical bench in the lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided removal of threaded fasteners from an end-of-life electronic assembly, the first step of any repair teardown. Transfers to coarse equipment with M3-M8 machine screws presented in a fixture; it covers only the unscrewing sub-step, not connector, adhesive or optical work.

sources.system: survey of robotic electrical-cable-connector disassembly systems
sources.developer: University of Bologna (Carricato et al.), journal Robotics
sources.title: Robotic Disassembly of Electrical Cable Connectors: A Critical Review
sources.claim: A 2026 critical review of robotic disassembly of electrical cable connectors concludes that non-destructive connector removal is still unsolved, with accessibility, motion planning and extraction at an early stage of maturity and industrial application judged still far off.
sources.transferJustification: Camera and lens teardown requires unlatching and withdrawing FPC/ZIF ribbon connectors without tearing them; this review is the state of the art on exactly that operation and shows it is not solved even in fixtured industrial cells.

sources.system: Daisy disassembly robot
sources.title: Apple expands global recycling programs - Apple Newsroom
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line disassembles iPhones in a purpose-built recycling facility, handling 15 (later 23) models at 200 units per hour and separating modules rather than shredding, but the process is a one-way recovery line for materials, not a repair teardown that preserves every part for reassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-throughput disassembly of small, dense consumer electronics in a purpose-built line, the closest deployed analogue to camera teardown. It is model-specific and recovery-oriented, so it does not substantiate repair-grade, reassemblable access to a defect.

sources.system: ReconCycle reconfigurable robotic work cell
sources.developer: Jozef Stefan Institute / ReconCycle consortium with Electrocycling GmbH
sources.title: Robots supercharge e-waste recycling in EU with SoftHand, modular parts
sources.claim: The EU ReconCycle project built a self-reconfigurable robotic work cell, developed with e-waste recycler Electrocycling GmbH, that autonomously disassembles small electronic devices such as heat cost allocators and smoke detectors (prying the housing open, removing the PCB and battery) using modular tools and a SoftHand gripper.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-device opening of a small screwed/clipped electronic housing in a fixtured cell to reach internal components. Comparable to opening a coarse photographic accessory housing; the devices are far simpler than a camera body and the process is tuned per device type.

sources.system: RAISE robot-assisted selective disassembly and sorting system
sources.title: RAISE: A Robot-Assisted SelectIve Disassembly and Sorting System for End-of-Life Phones
sources.claim: The RAISE automated end-of-life phone disassembly system processes over 120 phones per hour at 98.9% success, but achieves this with an adaptive cutting subsystem that cuts phones open to extract selected high-value components rather than reversibly unfastening them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of dense, camera-sized consumer electronics. It shows that where automation works at this scale it relies on destructive cutting, which would not yield a camera that can be repaired and reassembled.

tasks.label: Test equipment performance, focus of lens system, diaphragm alignment, lens mounts, or film transport, using precision gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-repair bench test of a digital camera body (DSLR/mirrorless/camcorder) in a repair shop: mount a reference lens or collimator, shoot resolution/focus charts, verify sensor-plane alignment (image plane tilt), autofocus calibration and image quality, and issue a pass/fail against factory spec.

Optical test of a lens after cleaning/reassembly on a shop bench: check infinity focus, resolution/MTF across the field and element centration on a collimator or lens projector, then re-check after fine adjustment of element spacing.

Diaphragm and shutter check: verify aperture-blade alignment and correct opening at each f-stop, and measure shutter/leaf-shutter timing across speeds with a shutter tester and precision gauges, on a mix of mechanical and electronic cameras and lenses.

Lens mount and flange focal distance check: measure flange-to-sensor/film-plane distance and mount flange flatness/parallelism with depth micrometer, dial indicator or collimator, add or remove shims, and re-measure to tolerance.

Film transport test on a mechanical still or motion-picture camera: thread a film/test loop, run the transport, check frame spacing, sprocket and gate registration, take-up tension and transport-to-shutter timing, on legacy models with no standard fixture.

Testing cine/broadcast camera-and-lens packages at a rental house or broadcast facility: back-focus/flange-depth verification with charts and collimator, mount seating check and overall performance verification before the package goes out.

sources.system: TRIOPTICS ImageMaster Cine (Flex)

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sensor cleaning of a digital DSLR/mirrorless body at the shop bench: lens off, shutter/mirror locked open, blower and brush first, then a wet swab with solvent drawn across the sensor filter with controlled pressure; verify with test frames at f/16 and repeat until spot-free. Customer-owned bodies of many makes; no disassembly.

External clean-and-check of bodies, lenses and filters in the shop: blow and brush dust from seams and mirror box, wipe grips and housings, clean front and rear elements and filters with lens fluid and tissue to a smear-free finish, clean eyepiece, LCD and electrical contacts; final detailing before returning gear to the customer.

Lens teardown for internal cleaning at the bench: disassemble a used, often decades-old lens of an unfamiliar model, clean haze, fungus and oil from internal elements and aperture blades, strip old grease from the focus helicoid and re-grease with the correct viscosity, reassemble and check focus/collimation.

Clean-lubricate-adjust of a camera body: disassemble a mechanical film camera or DSLR, degrease and re-oil shutter, mirror-box and film-transport pivots with micro-quantities of watch-grade oil/grease, clean internal debris and old lubricant migration, reassemble and test shutter timing.

Cine/broadcast prep-bay cleaning between rentals: clean the front and rear elements of large PL zoom and prime lenses, filters and matte boxes, wipe down camera bodies, viewfinders and accessories, blow dust from ports and mounts; heavy items, fast turnaround, institution-controlled prep room.

Cleaning gear on location during a shoot: dust, sand, sea spray or rain on bodies and front elements at an outdoor or improvised set, cleaned in place between takes with blower, brush and lens tissue.

tasks.label: Calibrate and verify accuracy of light meters, shutter diaphragm operation, or lens carriers, using timing instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Authorized/advanced service-center bench: after repair of a digital ILC (DSLR/mirrorless) body or interchangeable lens, technician verifies and adjusts sensor-to-mount alignment and flange focal distance, autofocus, and aperture/diaphragm actuation, using collimators, resolution charts, timing/exposure instruments and manufacturer service software. Many different models pass across the same bench.

Independent repair shop: film SLR or rangefinder focal-plane shutter after cleaning/lube. Camera is set on the bench with an electronic shutter tester at the film plane; each marked speed is fired and measured (exposure time, curtain travel, evenness), then the escapement, spring tension, magnet timing or electronic trim inside the partly disassembled body is adjusted and retested until in tolerance.

Leaf (between-the-lens) shutter in a medium/large-format or vintage lens: after clean-and-lube the assembly is mounted in a shutter tester, each speed fired and timed, the retard train/cams adjusted, and diaphragm blade travel verified to open to the marked apertures. Mechanisms differ by maker and vintage.

Light-meter calibration: an in-camera meter or a handheld exposure meter is checked against a calibrated light source/lightbox across the EV range; the technician adjusts a trimmer or resistor, replaces a cell, or enters correction constants, then verifies tracking at several light levels and speeds.

Cine/broadcast equipment at a rental house or specialist shop: set and verify flange focal depth/back focus with a collimator, check iris (diaphragm) motor drive and T-stop tracking, and verify shutter angle/frame-rate timing on a motion-picture or professional video camera; work is sometimes done at the client's facility or on set.

Other photographic equipment (enlarger, projector, process camera, copy stand) in a lab, darkroom or school facility: verify and align the lens carrier/negative stage parallelism, check lamp output and timer accuracy with timing instruments, and shim or adjust the carrier.

tasks.label: Examine cameras, equipment, processed film, or laboratory reports to diagnose malfunction, using work aids and specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench intake triage of a consumer digital camera body (mirrorless/DSLR/compact) brought in by a customer: verify the reported complaint, power up, cycle shutter and AF, shoot test frames, read error codes/service menus, check card slot, ports, battery and screen, and inspect for impact or liquid damage; produce a diagnosis and repair estimate. Repair-shop bench, intact device, no disassembly beyond covers.

Deeper fault localization on a camera body where external testing is inconclusive: partial disassembly, probing boards and flex connectors, exercising shutter/mirror/IBIS mechanisms by hand, judging corrosion, intermittent faults and mechanical wear (including mechanical film cameras) to identify the failed component. Repair-shop bench with hand tools, scope, meters.

Diagnosing an interchangeable lens for image-quality complaints: soft or uneven images, back/front focus, decentering, tilt, AF hunting or non-focusing. Technician mounts the lens on a test body or optical bench, shoots targets or measures resolution/centration against the maker's specification.

Diagnosing lenses and accessories dominated by mechanical and cosmetic condition: gritty or seized zoom/focus helicoids, sticky or oily aperture blades, loose mount, damaged filter threads, internal fungus/haze/separation, plus flash units and battery grips; judgment by feel, listening, and inspection under a lamp/loupe.

Diagnosing professional gear at a service center, rental house, broadcast facility or on the customer's premises: cinema/broadcast cameras, lens control and video systems, studio strobes and lab/minilab equipment. Connect to diagnostic software and signal test gear, read firmware logs, check sensor blocks, cabling, cooling and mounts on low-volume, model-specific equipment.

Evaluating imaging output rather than the mechanism: examining processed test film, test prints, customer sample files or test-chart captures, plus laboratory/test reports, against published specifications to determine the fault (light leak, shutter timing error, banding, flare, color/exposure error, dead pixels, dust on sensor).

instances.label: Shutter-speed / exposure-timing verification at the shop bench: technician sets a film SLR or digital body on an electronic shutter tester (photodiode head or LED timing panel), fires the shutter at each marked speed, reads measured exposure times and compares deviation against the manufacturer's tolerance before and after adjustment.

Dimensional measurement of small mechanical parts and assemblies during a repair: shims, gears, springs, screws, mount rings and body register/flange depth, measured with dial calipers, micrometers, depth gauges and dial indicators at a repair bench, verifying against service-manual dimensions.

Optical verification of a lens or body: back-focus / flange focal distance with a collimator or depth gauge, focus and resolution accuracy against a test chart, AF calibration check on a bench test rig in the shop, comparing measured values to specification.

Light-meter / exposure-meter accuracy check: a camera's built-in meter or a handheld exposure meter is read against a calibrated uniform light source or reference meter over a range of levels in a controlled lighting corner of the shop, and the error recorded.

Electrical parameter measurement on camera or flash circuitry: multimeter and oscilloscope readings at test points on a partly disassembled body or flash unit (supply voltages, sync timing, capacitor and sensor outputs), verified against service specifications.

On-site verification of professional video/cinema/broadcast gear at a customer's location, studio floor or rental-house shelf: back-focus check with a Siemens-star chart, waveform/level and timing checks, confirming settings against spec after a field repair, in a setting taken as found.

tasks.label: Fabricate or modify defective electronic, electrical, or mechanical components, using bench lathe, milling machine, shaper, grinder, or precision hand tools, according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench in a camera repair shop: turn or mill a small precision metal replacement part (bushing, shaft, threaded retaining ring, gear blank, custom screw) from bar stock on a bench lathe/mill, to dimensions from a drawing or measured off the broken original with micrometers; tolerances of a few thousandths of an inch; deburr and polish.

Bench under a loupe or stereo microscope: modify a tiny mechanism part by hand - stoning/filing a shutter or wind lever, re-bending a distorted spring or contact finger, lapping a shim to thickness, trimming a claw, plus freehand micro-soldering of hair-thin wires or a broken flex-cable trace - fitted by feel with repeated trial in the mechanism.

Shop bench/drill press/surface grinder: straightforward stock removal on a fixturable metal part to a stated dimension - shorten a shaft or screw and re-chamfer, open or relocate a hole, drill and tap a thread, grind a flat or pad to spec thickness, deburr.

Electronics bench: modify or repair a small circuit board per schematic/spec - remove a failed surface-mount or through-hole component and solder in a replacement, add a jumper or wire mod, replace a connector - on a board removed from the camera and held in a board holder.

Machine area of a pro/cinema service shop: fabricate a custom bracket, adapter plate, lens-support foot or mounting block from aluminum plate on a mill, drill press and grinder to a sketch or dimensioned drawing; moderate tolerances, larger workpiece, tapped holes, finished edges.

Repair shop: fabricate a nonmetal replacement - 3D-print or machine a plastic gear, cover, spacer or battery-door part from a model; cut gaskets, shims and light-seal foam to pattern; bond and finish the piece to fit the housing.

tasks.label: Install electrical assemblies and wiring in aircraft camera housings and memory cards or film in cameras, following blueprints and using hand tools and soldering equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repair-shop bench work on a consumer or professional camera body: soldering replacement wires, flex-cable pigtails or a small electrical subassembly (flash board, battery contacts, shutter/aperture motor leads) into an opened camera per the service manual's wiring schematic, using a fine-tip iron and hand tools, then reseating connectors.

Installing a memory card and battery into a repaired or newly assembled digital camera: opening the card/battery door, seating the card, powering up, formatting and shooting test frames to verify the repair before the camera is returned.

Loading film for a functional test after repair: threading 35mm cassette leader onto the take-up spool of an SLR, loading 120 roll film in a back, or loading a motion-picture magazine in a changing bag/darkroom, then checking transport, counter and rewind.

Shop/clean-bench build-up of an aerial (aircraft) camera housing: mounting internal electrical assemblies (control boards, heaters, shutter drives, connectors) and routing, lacing and soldering the internal wiring harness per blueprint/wiring diagram, then continuity/insulation checking. One-off or very small batch, unique references.

Installing/integrating the camera housing and its wiring on the aircraft itself in a hangar: mounting the housing at the camera port, routing and clamping cable runs through the airframe, mating connectors to aircraft power/data, and functional checkout in a cramped, non-fixtured airframe interior.

tasks.label: Lay out reference points and dimensions on parts or metal stock to be machined, using precision measuring instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repair-shop bench: repairer lays out a small aluminum or brass bar/plate blank for a discontinued camera part from a dimensioned sketch — applies layout dye, uses surface plate, height gauge, dial caliper, combination square, scriber and center punch to mark edges, centerlines and hole centers to roughly ±0.05–0.25 mm before milling/drilling.

Reverse-engineering layout: the only reference is a broken/worn original part (gear blank, shaft, latch, shutter lever). Repairer measures the original with micrometer/caliper/optical comparator, works out hole centers and profile, then scribes and punches the transferred dimensions onto fresh stock at the bench.

Layout marked directly on an existing camera or lens component to be modified — e.g., hole centers on a curved lens-barrel or mount flange, a slot on a cine camera baseplate — where the surface is irregular, finished, and adjacent to delicate optics/mechanisms that must not be scratched or distorted.

Straightforward layout on larger flat stock for motion-picture/studio support hardware (mounting plates, brackets, rod blocks, adapter rings), often a repeat job from an existing drawing or template, marked out at the shop bench or on a small mill table.

Off-site work at a rental house, studio or location: repairer marks drill/reference points on a camera mount, rig plate or bracket using a rule, square and scriber on whatever surface is available before taking it back for machining, or drilling on the spot.

sources.system: KEYENCE MD-X Series 3-Axis Hybrid Laser Marker
sources.title: Built-In Vision. Autofocus Anywhere. Data-Driven Analytics. | 3-Axis Hybrid Laser Marker MD-X Series | KEYENCE America
sources.claim: Keyence MD-X 3-axis hybrid laser marker carries a camera in the marking head that automatically finds the part's shape and corrects X, Y and theta offsets so marks land in the specified position on fixtured metal parts — the machine equivalent of scribing reference geometry from a drawing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated part marking. It transfers because the physical act required here is placing accurate reference points/lines on a metal workpiece from a digital dimension set, on the same size class of metal parts, with positioning accuracy at or better than hand scribing.

sources.system: KEYENCE MD-X / MD-F 3-axis laser markers

sources.transferJustification: Related task: marking curved/stepped metal surfaces. Relevant because instance 2 requires reference marks on a curved barrel or flange rather than flat stock, and the 3-axis focus control handles exactly that geometry.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: structural-steel layout marking. It is the same task — laying out reference points and dimensions on metal stock prior to cutting/drilling — performed automatically on fixtured stock, differing only in workpiece scale.

tasks.label: Test or calibrate components or equipment, following manufacturers' manuals and troubleshooting techniques, using hand tools, power tools, or measuring devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinical engineering shop bench: scheduled performance verification and calibration of portable electronic clinical devices (patient monitors, ECG carts, defibrillators, electrosurgical units, pulse oximeters). Tech connects patient simulators/analyzers and an electrical safety analyzer, follows the OEM service manual, cycles device controls, compares displayed values to reference readings, adjusts via service menu or trim pots, and documents in the CMMS.

Fluid- and gas-handling portable devices in the shop or at the bedside: infusion, syringe and feeding pumps, ventilators, suction regulators. Tech loads a test administration set or breathing circuit, connects an infusion-device or gas-flow analyzer, runs flow-accuracy, occlusion and alarm tests at several rate/mode settings, calibrates flow/pressure/O2 sensors, runs electrical safety, and documents.

Bench troubleshooting of a failed device to component level: with the service manual and schematics, measure supply rails, signals and component values on boards and modules using DMM, oscilloscope and bench power supply, isolate the faulty part, then retest and verify to spec after repair.

In-place testing/calibration of installed or large equipment in clinical space: fixed and portable imaging (X-ray, CT, ultrasound), sterilizers, surgical lights/booms/tables, dialysis water systems, exam-room fixed devices. Work is done around staff and patients, with phantoms, dosimeters, meters and hand tools, often on a ladder, inside cabinets, or under the device.

Off-site field service: outpatient clinics, physician and dental offices, ambulances and patients' homes. Test/calibrate home medical equipment (oxygen concentrators, home ventilators, CPAP, beds, wheelchairs) or office devices with portable analyzers and hand tools in whatever space is available, with clutter, no fixturing and variable lighting/power.

sources.system: Trescal DMM calibration robot (with Thinkbot Solutions / Linestar Automation)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: periodic calibration of a handheld electronic measuring instrument. It uses the same action set as bench test/calibration of portable electromedical devices — mate leads/cables into ports, actuate switches and buttons, read the device display, compare to a traceable reference, record results — at metrology-grade precision.

sources.system: Trescal DMM calibration robot
sources.title: Automated calibration of non-automated devices – BMTA
sources.claim: The same robot had two years of production use in Trescal's Dallas branch with calibration quality matching trained technicians; it runs unattended outside shift hours and passed UKAS assessment for accredited ISO 17025 calibration in the UK.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-quality output and accredited acceptance for autonomous robotic calibration of handheld instruments, which is the quality bar this task requires.

sources.claim: ZwickRoell roboTest R is a commercial robotic testing cell that runs the whole functional test sequence on drug-delivery medical devices (autoinjectors, insulin pens, syringes) — handling the specimen, measuring delivered dose, actuation and glide force — with 21 CFR Part 11 test documentation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: standards-based functional testing of fluid-delivery medical devices (dose accuracy, actuation force) in a fixtured cell — the same measurement class as flow-accuracy and occlusion testing of an infusion pump against an analyzer.

sources.system: TQC Series 20 drawer leak-test fixture with MALT test instrument
sources.title: Medical Device Leak Test Drawer Fixture - Case Study - TQC
sources.claim: TQC supplies automated leak/pressure test fixtures for medical devices in which the device is clamped in a drawer fixture, fluid connections are made and sealed by the fixture, and a multi-step pressure/vacuum test sequence runs and grades the part automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pressure/flow testing of medical devices where the machine, not a person, makes the sealed fluid connection — covering the tubing-hookup step of pump and ventilator performance testing when the work is presented fixtured.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers; TAKAYA APT-1400F/1600FD
sources.title: SPEA for MEC: Flying Probe Tester to avoid failure escapes from production process
sources.claim: SPEA and Takaya automatic flying-probe testers autonomously probe assembled electronic boards, execute in-circuit and functional measurements, and diagnose the failing component; they are standard equipment across electronics manufacturers including medical.

sources.system: ATAM FlexFlow cobot test system

sources.claim: Nextgen's ATAM FlexFlow cobot with a vision system was deployed at an OEM to physically operate a product's touchscreen user interface and verify displayed behaviour as an automated test sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a device's own controls and menus and reading its screen to verify function — the interaction layer of testing modern touchscreen medical devices (monitors, pumps, ventilators) in service mode.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit inspection software

sources.claim: The most capable mobile robots deployed loose in human work facilities perform autonomous inspection rounds collecting camera, thermal, acoustic and analog-gauge-reading data; they do not connect test instruments to equipment or make calibration adjustments.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E2 case: autonomous robots working in structured human facilities today only observe equipment; none hook up analyzers, actuate device controls and calibrate to spec in situ.

tasks.label: Perform preventive maintenance or service, such as cleaning, lubricating, or adjusting equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench PM in the hospital clinical engineering shop on portable patient-care devices (infusion pumps, vital-signs monitors, defibrillators, suction units): visual inspection for wear/damage, exterior and internal cleaning, battery and consumable replacement, lubricating latches/hinges, performance verification and electrical safety testing against manufacturer spec, adjustment, PM sticker and CMMS documentation. Many different makes/models pass the bench each week.

In-unit PM on the floors: pole-mounted pumps and monitors, patient beds, stretchers, wheelchairs, exam tables in occupied patient rooms, corridors and storage alcoves. Lubricating casters, bed actuators and side-rail mechanisms, adjusting brakes, latches and bed scales, wiping down and functional checks while working around patients, staff and cluttered rooms.

PM on large fixed imaging/therapy systems in the imaging suite (CT, R/F and portable X-ray, ultrasound, linear accelerator): cleaning air filters and detector covers, lubricating gantry bearings and table rails, checking collimator/mechanical alignment, replacing wear parts, running and adjusting calibration routines, generating QA records. Work performed inside the shielded room during a scheduled downtime window.

PM on OR, sterile-processing and anesthesia equipment: surgical tables and lights, steam sterilizers, washer-disinfectors, endoscope reprocessors, anesthesia machines and ventilators. Gasket, filter and soda-lime canister replacement, lubrication of table hydraulics and door mechanisms, leak and flow testing, pressure/valve adjustment, under sterile-area access rules and tight scheduling.

Field PM at outside customer sites controlled by an institution: clinics, nursing homes, dental and physician offices, laboratories. Servicing dental chairs and compressors, autoclaves, centrifuges, exam lights, lab analyzers, oxygen concentrators; cleaning filters, lubricating moving parts, adjusting and verifying performance in a small equipment room or treatment room.

Home medical equipment PM in patients' residences: hospital beds, patient lifts, power wheelchairs, oxygen concentrators, CPAP units. Working in cluttered, unpredictable rooms with pets and furniture; cleaning/replacing filters, lubricating mechanisms, adjusting brakes and controls, verifying flow and function, and documenting the service.

sources.system: Daisy (Apple disassembly robot)
sources.title: How Apple Robots are Closing the Waste Recycling Loop | Technology Magazine
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy is a purpose-built, autonomous disassembly line that fixtures a specific phone model, freezes and removes the battery and drives out screws at roughly 200 units/hour - device teardown in a dedicated machine cell, not service-and-return maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown of a handheld electronic device in a purpose-built cell, the closest deployed analogue to opening a device for service. It covers only fastener removal on one product family, with no cleaning, lubrication, wear judgment, reassembly, calibration or functional verification, so it does not substantiate completing a whole preventive-maintenance service.

sources.system: Motoman robot grease-dispensing machine
sources.title: Automation Drives Grease-dispensing Machine | Machinery Lubrication
sources.claim: Industrial robots routinely apply lubricating grease to defined points on fixtured workpieces inside purpose-built cells, showing the lubrication sub-step of PM is automatable when the part is presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: programmed lubrication of a fixtured part in a fenced cell. It covers one sub-step of PM on a single known geometry and provides no inspection, cleaning, adjustment or pass/fail verification, so it cannot stand in for a whole medical-device PM.

sources.system: SCARA functional-test cell (cell-phone manufacturer)
sources.developer: unnamed manufacturer / integrator, reported by ASSEMBLY magazine
sources.title: Quality in Assembly: Robots Can Help With Test, Inspection Applications | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: In electronics manufacturing, SCARA robots load fixtured finished units into functional testers and shuttle assemblies in and out of test stations; automated test handling exists only for a single known product in a dedicated cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling for functional/performance testing of a device. Transfer is limited: the robot tends a tester for one fixtured model and performs no cleaning, lubrication, part replacement or corrective adjustment, which are integral to the PM instances rated here.

sources.system: Spot (autonomous inspection missions)
sources.title: Using robots to perform preventive maintenance | Plant Services
sources.claim: The deployed state of the art for robots in maintenance work is autonomous inspection rounds - Spot walks routes and collects gauge, thermal and acoustic data - with the servicing actions still performed by human technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous preventive-maintenance rounds in industrial facilities. It establishes what is actually fielded (data-gathering inspection) and shows no cited system performs the manipulation-heavy clean/lubricate/adjust service work, supporting the negative judgments.

sources.system: hospital mobile service robots / cobots (fleet class)
sources.developer: various, reported in healthcare CMMS industry guidance
sources.title: Collaborative Robots (Cobots) in Healthcare: Maintenance Best Practices | Oxmaint
sources.claim: Hospital-deployed mobile robots in 2026 perform delivery, transport and disinfection roles; biomedical technicians remain the ones performing the scheduled inspections and servicing of equipment, including of the robots themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile work inside hospitals. It shows navigation of the E2 setting is solved, but the fielded roles are transport and disinfection while the same sources describe human biomedical technicians performing scheduled PM, so nothing substantiates robotic completion of this task.

tasks.label: Inspect, test, or troubleshoot malfunctioning medical or related equipment, following manufacturers' specifications and using test and analysis instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Biomed shop bench: a common portable clinical device of a known model (volumetric infusion pump, defibrillator, patient monitor, electrosurgical unit) arrives on a work order; the tech connects it to the matching analyzer/simulator (flow analyzer, defib analyzer, patient simulator, electrical-safety analyzer), runs the manufacturer's performance and safety test sequence, and confirms/localizes the reported fault against published specifications.

Biomed shop bench: fault isolation that requires opening the device  or internake  or internals — remove covers, inspect boards, cables, connectors, sensors, pump mechanisms and batteries, probe test points with a DMM/scope, interpret error logs, and decide which module or component is defective. Device models and internal layouts vary widely.

On the nursing unit or ED: staff report a device in service is misbehaving (intermittent alarms, occlusion errors, bad waveform). The tech goes to the bedside, inspects the device and its accessories/disposables in place, rules out user setup and environmental causes, does a quick functional check with portable test gear, and repairs on the spot or removes it from service.

Imaging suite: CT, MRI, general radiography, or ultrasound system faults. Tech works at the OEM service console, reads error logs, runs built-in service diagnostics and calibrations, measures kV/mA/dose or coil/transducer performance with test tools, and physically inspects the gantry, tube, detectors, cabling or probes.

Field service call at an outpatient clinic, physician or dental office, long-term care facility, or a patient's home: dental chair/x-ray, exam-room equipment, oxygen concentrator, hospital bed, wheelchair or CPAP. Site layout, access, power and lighting vary; the tech carries test instruments and diagnoses the unit where it sits.

Operating room, procedural suite, sterile processing or clinical lab: anesthesia machine, surgical table/lights, electrosurgical generator, endoscope/tower, steam sterilizer, or lab analyzer troubleshooting in place, around case schedules, infection-control rules and installed plumbing/gas connections.

sources.system: LF Technologies automated test bench for medical ventilation equipment
sources.title: Test bench for medical ventilation equipment | LF Technologies

tasks.label: Disassemble malfunctioning equipment and remove, repair, or replace defective parts, such as motors, clutches, or transformers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital nursing unit / ICU / ED: technician responds to a failed patient-care device in place (bed with a dead motor or brake, IV pole, suction regulator, telemetry unit, exam-light or stretcher hydraulics). Opens covers with hand tools around cables, patients and staff, removes and swaps the defective motor, switch, gear or cable, reassembles and checks function.

Hospital biomedical engineering shop bench: mixed population of devices arriving from clinical areas (infusion pumps, ventilators, defibrillators, surgical drills, vital-sign monitors, warming units). Technician disassembles a used, sometimes fluid-soiled unit of an unfamiliar model using service manual, removes defective board/motor/transformer/pump head, installs replacement, reassembles with cables and seals, then performs safety and performance verification.

Field service on large fixed equipment in imaging suites, ORs, labs and SPD: replacing an X-ray tube or table drive motor in CT/fluoro, a gantry or collimator drive, steam sterilizer valves/heating elements, surgical table hydraulics, dialysis machine pumps, centrifuge motors. Heavy components, confined access panels, lockout/tagout, work performed in the installed location.

Third-party or OEM depot/service center: high volume of one standardized model (e.g., a single infusion pump family, telemetry transmitters, dental handpieces). Technician repeats a known teardown sequence on a fixtured unit, swaps a defined module (pumping mechanism, motor assembly, battery, main board), reassembles and runs a standard functional/calibration test.

Service at non-institutional sites: patient homes and small clinics — home hospital beds, power wheelchairs and scooters, oxygen concentrators, CPAP units, dental or veterinary office chairs and compressors; also mobile imaging trailers and ambulances. Cluttered, uncontrolled sites, no bench, equipment repaired where it sits.

tasks.label: Examine medical equipment or facility's structural environment and check for proper use of equipment to protect patients and staff from electrical or mechanical hazards and to ensure compliance with safety regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled safety/electrical-safety inspection of portable medical devices (infusion pumps, patient monitors, defibrillators, suction units, electric beds) in a hospital: visual/physical check of cords, plugs, strain reliefs, casters, applied parts; protective-earth resistance and leakage-current measurement with a safety analyzer; functional/alarm verification; pass-fail decision, inspection label and CMMS documentation. Performed in the clinical engineering shop or at the point of use on the unit.

Incoming inspection of newly delivered equipment and post-repair safety verification in the clinical engineering shop before the device is released to service: full electrical safety test, mechanical/physical safety check, performance verification against manufacturer specs, entry into the equipment inventory and compliance record.

Walk-through rounds through patient care units (ICU rooms, med-surg rooms, ED bays, clean equipment rooms) checking that equipment is being used properly and safely in situ: daisy-chained power strips and extension cords, damaged cords/plugs, equipment on the wrong (non-emergency) receptacles, blocked or overloaded outlets, unsecured cylinders, poorly positioned poles/monitors; flagging deficiencies, coaching staff, logging findings.

Inspection of installed/fixed systems and the facility's structural environment supporting medical equipment: OR and procedure-room line isolation monitors, isolated-power and emergency-power receptacles, medical gas outlets, ceiling booms and surgical lights, imaging suites, sterilizers and dialysis water systems; mechanical hazard checks (brakes, latches, mounts, interlocks) and NFPA 99 / Joint Commission compliance documentation.

Off-site inspections at clinics, ambulatory surgery centers, physician offices, long-term care, or patients' homes (home ventilators, oxygen concentrators, home hospital beds): unfamiliar layouts and non-standard wiring, examining both the device and the site's electrical/mechanical environment, then advising the customer and recording compliance findings.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated end-of-line electrical safety/functional testing of an electronic unit. It transfers to a biomedical technician's bench safety inspection because the object (a mains-powered electronics unit of a few kilograms), the operation (place the unit in a fixture, run an instrumented electrical test sequence, log a pass/fail record) and the required precision are comparable; only the test standard differs (IEC 62353/NFPA 99 rather than avionics test specs).

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated mechanical safety/performance testing of medical devices against published safety standards. It transfers to the mechanical-hazard portion of a technician's safety inspection (forces, travel, alarm/timing behaviour, pass-fail against a standard) on the same class of medical devices, with robotic handling supplying the fixturing the E1 counterfactual assumes.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility inspection rounds. Cited to bound, not support, the in-situ rounds instances: the demonstrated capability is non-contact sensing of fixed industrial assets on fixed routes, which does not reach receptacle/grounding tests, mechanical checks or judgments about how clinicians are using medical equipment.

tasks.label: Install medical equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/clinic rollout of portable clinical devices (infusion pumps, vital-sign monitors, defibrillators, feeding pumps): uncrate, attach pole/cart mounts, batteries and accessories, run incoming inspection and electrical-safety test, configure settings/drug library and network, asset-tag and place in the care unit.

Fixed-mount device installs in exam/patient rooms and corridors: wall diagnostic stations, monitor and articulating-arm brackets, wall-mounted pumps/otoscope units — locate studs, drill and set anchors, bolt the bracket, hang the device, route and terminate power/data cable to nearby outlets and jacks, verify operation.

Large imaging system installation in an imaging suite (CT, MRI, R/F room, C-arm, mammo): rig and uncrate heavy components, mechanically assemble and align gantry/table/tube stand, pull and terminate high-voltage, console and network cabling, then calibrate and run phantom/acceptance testing with the physicist.

OR, procedural and laboratory installs: ceiling booms and surgical lights, endoscopy towers, anesthesia machines with medical-gas hookups, steam sterilizers and lab analyzers requiring water/drain/electrical connections, leveling, and post-install validation in an institution-controlled but crowded, service-scheduled space.

Home or long-term-care setup of durable medical equipment by an HME technician: deliver and assemble hospital bed, patient lift, oxygen concentrator, home ventilator or CPAP in the patient's residence, connect and test, adjust to the room and instruct the caregiver.

tasks.label: Test, evaluate, and classify excess or in-use medical equipment and determine serviceability, condition, and disposition, in accordance with regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench evaluation in the hospital clinical-engineering shop: a portable in-use device (volumetric infusion pump, vital-signs monitor, suction unit, feeding pump) arrives from a unit; tech visually inspects for damage/missing parts, opens covers if needed, runs electrical-safety (leakage/ground) and performance tests with an analyzer, classifies it serviceable / repairable / condemn, tags it and records the disposition in the CMMS per AAMI/Joint Commission requirements.

Scheduled in-place testing and classification of devices in clinical areas (patient rooms, ED bays, OR, clinics): tech locates each device on the PM list amid occupied rooms and clutter, performs safety/performance checks with a portable analyzer at the bedside or on a cart, and decides whether the unit stays in service, gets a repair tag, or is removed from service.

Batch evaluation of excess/retired portable equipment staged in a storage room or warehouse (dozens of older pumps, monitors, AEDs, thermometers, pulse oximeters): power-up and functional checks, condition grading, decision to return to inventory, harvest for parts, donate/surplus, or scrap, with disposition paperwork completed per institutional and federal property regulations.

Evaluation of large or installed equipment in situ for serviceability and disposition: imaging systems, sterilizers, dialysis machines, surgical tables, hospital beds. Tech accesses panels, runs built-in diagnostics and error logs, assesses mechanical wear and parts availability, and recommends repair, decommission, or trade-in.

Off-site/field evaluation: equipment at physician offices, long-term-care sites, or durable medical equipment returned from patient homes (wheelchairs, oxygen concentrators, CPAP, home beds). Tech inspects in whatever space is available, tests function, and classifies items for refurbishment, reuse, or condemnation.

tasks.label: Plan and carry out work assignments, using blueprints, schematic drawings, technical manuals, wiring diagrams, or liquid or air flow sheets, following prescribed regulations, directives, or other instructions as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled preventive maintenance/performance verification on general biomedical devices (infusion pumps, patient monitors, defibrillators, suction/vital-signs units) in the hospital clinical engineering shop or at the bedside: follow the manufacturer's PM procedure and service manual, inspect cords/enclosure, run electrical-safety and performance tests, calibrate, apply the PM sticker, and document in the CMMS per Joint Commission/regulatory requirements.

Corrective bench repair of a failed device in the biomed shop: read the service manual, schematic or wiring diagram, diagnose the fault (power supply, sensor, pump mechanism, board), open the housing with mixed fasteners, swap the board/module or component, reassemble, recalibrate, verify to spec, and write the service record.

Field service on large or plumbed systems in clinical suites — CT/X-ray/ultrasound, sterilizers, dialysis machines, anesthesia units, surgical tables — using wiring diagrams and liquid/air flow sheets: plan the downtime with the department, isolate power/water/gas, replace a module or valve, purge/leak-test, calibrate, and document per prescribed regulations.

Incoming inspection, installation and configuration of newly purchased equipment in a clinical area: unpack, assemble/mount per installation drawings, connect to power, gas or network, run acceptance tests per the manual and regulatory checklist, enter the asset into inventory and label it.

Service performed away from the controlled facility: home medical equipment (hospital beds, oxygen concentrators, home dialysis, ventilators) in patients' homes, small clinics or physician offices, and equipment in ambulances or temporary/field locations, working around clutter, pets, unknown layouts and non-standard power.

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing system for automated disassembly of electronic waste (collaborative arm with force-sensing screwdriver)

sources.claim: State of the art in robotic disassembly of electronic products is a laboratory cell that autonomously locates and removes screws with force sensing, validated on a recycled hoverboard — i.e. a single sub-step (unscrewing), not fault diagnosis, module replacement, calibration or documentation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of consumer electronics. It shares fastener removal with medical-device repair, but covers only one sub-step on a known product in a fixtured lab cell, so it cannot substantiate completion of a whole diagnose-repair-verify-document assignment.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic rework cell for through-hole and surface-mount component removal/replacement
sources.developer: Academic/industrial PCBA rework research (Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing / Elsevier)
sources.date: 1997 (foundational; commercial semi-automatic rework stations continue in this line)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated PCB rework. It shows component-level replacement is automatable when the board is fixtured and the defect is already identified, but not the diagnosis, device teardown, calibration and regulatory documentation that make up a medical-equipment repair assignment.
