roles.title: Watch and Clock Repairers
roles.description: Repair, clean, and adjust mechanisms of timing instruments, such as watches and clocks. Includes watchmakers, watch technicians, and mechanical timepiece repairers.

tasks.label: Clean, rinse, and dry timepiece parts, using solutions and ultrasonic or mechanical watch-cleaning machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Independent repair shop, full service of a mechanical wristwatch: after teardown, the watchmaker sorts ~100 movement parts (plates, bridges, wheels, click springs, sub-millimetre screws) into the compartments of cleaning-machine baskets, runs an automatic clean/rinse/dry cycle (Elma or L&R), unloads, inspects each part under a loupe or microscope for residue, re-runs or hand-touches up as needed, and lays parts out for reassembly; the case, bracelet and crystal go through an aqueous ultrasonic bath, are rinsed and blown dry.

Brand or regional service centre: batches of standardized calibers, dedicated solvent watch-cleaning machines and aqueous lines, standard baskets/trays per movement family, documented cycle recipes, throughput targets and post-clean cleanliness inspection before lubrication and assembly.

Clock work in the shop: brass plates, wheels, arbors, springs and pendulum hardware from mantel, wall or longcase movements, degreased in an ultrasonic tank with ammoniated or aqueous clock cleaner, rinsed in one or two rinses, then dried with hot air, compressed air or a drying cabinet before pegging pivot holes and inspection.

Delicate movement components handled apart from the main basket: balance complete with hairspring, pallet fork with shellac-set stones, mainspring and barrel - dipped in small jars of one-dip/benzine with tweezers or run on a gentle high-frequency cycle, then air-dried and inspected for distortion or residue.

Dials, hands and cosmetic surfaces: the repairer judges whether a painted, lacquered, enamel or patinated dial can be cleaned at all, then works by hand with Rodico, a soft brush, distilled water or one-dip, blotting dry; hands are dipped and dried individually. Irreversible cosmetic damage is the risk that governs the work.

On-site cleaning of a turret/tower clock or a large public or estate clock left in place: the repairer brushes and wipes the frame, wheels and bearings with solvent-soaked rags and brushes in an unheated tower, loft or a customer's hallway, dries with rags and a blower, with layout, access and lighting differing at every site.

Transfer: identical process chain (wash, ultrasonic clean, rinse, dry) on metal parts, executed by a robot moving carriers between tanks - the same sequence a watch/clock repairer performs on movement plates, wheels, cases and clock brass once parts are presented in carriers.

tasks.label: Adjust timing regulators, using truing calipers, watch-rate recorders, and tweezers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench regulation of a serviced modern mechanical wristwatch of a common caliber (ETA/Sellita/Seiko/Rolex family) at an independent shop or brand service-centre bench: movement or cased watch placed on a watch-rate recorder (timing machine), rate, amplitude and beat error read in several positions, the index regulator nudged a few tens of microns with tweezers or a screwdriver, re-measured and iterated over hours or days until within a few seconds per day.

Beat-error and balance/hairspring correction done as part of regulating: rotating the collet or shifting the hairspring stud, truing a distorted hairspring or a bent/out-of-round balance wheel held in truing calipers, re-poising a balance after reassembly, all under a microscope with tweezers on parts a few hundredths of a millimetre thick.

Regulating vintage or antique wristwatches and pocket watches, or watches with unusual regulating organs (swan-neck micrometer regulators, free-sprung balances with inertia weights/Microstella-type nuts, worn or non-standard index assemblies) at the bench, where parts are worn, one-off and fragile.

Bench regulation of a clock in the shop: adjusting the pendulum rating nut, the regulator (fast/slow) lever, or the index of a platform escapement in a carriage/mantel clock, verifying with a clock rate recorder or microphone timer over hours to days until the clock keeps time.

On-site regulation of a tall-case, wall or tower clock at the customer's home, church or office: levelling the case, setting the clock in beat (bending the crutch or shifting the suspension), adjusting the pendulum bob, and returning after days to fine-tune the rate.

It produces the same accepted output as adjusting a timing regulator (a movement whose measured rate is within spec) on the same class of object (a mechanical watch oscillator) at equal or finer precision, performed entirely by machine in a purpose-built line; only the actuation differs (laser rather than moving an index arm).

tasks.label: Reassemble timepieces, replacing glass faces and batteries, before returning them to customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail jewelry-store or mall service bench: quartz wristwatch back is off, watchmaker fits the correct silver-oxide cell into the movement, seats the retaining clip/spring, checks and greases the caseback gasket, presses or screws the back closed, sets the time, pressure-tests, wipes the case and hands it back over the counter.

Watch service center or independent shop: casing up a just-serviced mechanical/automatic wristwatch — refit dial and hands to the movement, install movement and stem/crown in the case, seat crystal and gaskets, close the caseback to torque, water-resistance test, check amplitude/rate on a timegrapher before return.

Shop bench: replacing a scratched or cracked crystal on a common modern watch of a known reference — new OEM press-fit crystal and I-gasket seated in a crystal press, movement refitted, back closed, seal tested, then packaged for counter pickup or mail return.

Shop bench: reassembling a vintage or unusual watch — aftermarket crystal measured and sized to a worn or dented case, non-original gaskets and hands, corroded case threads, one-off fit problems solved by hand before the piece is returned.

Clock repairer's shop: reassembling a repaired mantel, wall, cuckoo or kitchen clock — movement refitted into wooden or metal case, dial and hands refitted, glass panes/door glass replaced and glazed, pendulum and chime rods hung, clock put in beat and test-run for days before return.

Customer's home or delivery site: reassembling and setting up a longcase/grandfather clock after repair — case leveled against the wall, movement and seatboard reinstalled, dial, hood glass and side glass refitted, weights, cables/chains and pendulum hung, chimes synchronized and beat set on-site.

tasks.label: Disassemble timepieces and inspect them for defective, worn, misaligned, or rusty parts, using loupes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full teardown of a mechanical wristwatch (ETA/Sellita/Rolex-type caliber) at a bench in an independent repair shop or authorized service center: remove bracelet, open case back, extract movement, pull hands, lift dial and calendar work, strip the automatic module, let down the mainspring, remove bridges, wheels, balance and barrel, then inspect every pivot, jewel, tooth and spring under loupe/microscope for wear, rust, magnetism and misalignment before quoting parts.

Quartz watch or module job at a shop bench or mall/jeweler service counter: open a snap, screw-down or screw-back case, lift out the movement, remove battery, hands and dial where needed, separate coil, circuit and gear train, and inspect for battery leakage corrosion, stripped plastic wheels, broken stem/setting lever and bent contacts.

Mechanical clock movement (mantel, wall, cuckoo, 400-day anniversary, chiming) brought into the shop: remove movement from case, safely let down mainsprings or remove weight drives, separate plates, extract the strike/chime train, and inspect pivots, bushing holes, wheel teeth, click springs and levers under a loupe for wear, ovalized holes and rust.

Vintage, heirloom or water/impact-damaged timepiece of unknown or obsolete caliber at the bench: seized or rusted screws, previous botched repairs, non-standard fasteners and broken parts require improvised extraction and careful, model-specific judgment about which components are serviceable versus scrap.

On-site dismantling of a tall-case (grandfather) clock, large wall regulator or tower/church clock in a customer's home, historic building or public building: remove hood, weights, pendulum and dial, unbolt and lift out the movement in situ amid furniture, ladders and uncontrolled lighting, and make a first inspection of pivots, bushings and rust before transport.

sources.system: Horosys Smart Micro Factory with Mecademic Meca500
sources.title: Smart Micro Factory Revolutionizing Watchmaking with Meca500 Robot
sources.claim: Horosys' Smart Micro Factory uses Mecademic Meca500 six-axis robots in a desktop cell to assemble, rivet and press-fit jewels and other watch components at 0.005 mm precision — the closest commercial robotic handling of watch-scale parts, but it assembles known new parts fed in fixtures, and does no teardown or wear diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic micro-ASSEMBLY of watch components. It shows watch-scale parts can be manipulated by machine in a purpose-built cell, but the cited cell works on new, identical, tray-fed parts; it does not disassemble a used movement or judge wear, so transfer to this task is not established.

sources.system: Sistem51 automated movement production line
sources.title: Swatch Sistem51 automatic watches | Swatch USA
sources.claim: Swatch's Sistem51 is the only mechanical watch movement whose production is fully automated, and it was made possible by redesigning the movement (51 parts, a single central screw, laser-welded modules) specifically for machines; conventional movements are still assembled and serviced by hand.

tasks.label: Oil moving parts of timepieces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service lubrication of a current/recent standard mechanical wristwatch caliber (e.g., ETA 2824, Sellita SW200, Seiko, Rolex 3135) at a bench in a repair shop or brand service center: 30-60 lube points including jewel holes, Incabloc cap jewels, pallet stones, escape wheel teeth, keyless works grease and barrel/braking grease, applied with calibrated oilers under a microscope, interleaved with reassembly.

Lubrication of a vintage, antique or unusual wristwatch/pocket-watch caliber (long-tail calibers, worn pivots and reused parts, no standard lube chart): the repairer inspects wear and decides which points get which viscosity and how much, at the bench under a microscope.

Oiling a standard, currently produced clock movement (Hermle, Kieninger, cuckoo, modern chiming movement) on the shop bench: calibrated oil drops into the pivot oil sinks on both plates, escapement pallets, levers and mainspring/barrel grease, with the movement out of its case.

Oiling an antique or one-off clock movement (19th-century longcase, mantel, tower-clock movement on the bench) with worn or rebushed pivot holes, non-standard layout and hand-made parts, requiring judgment about points, quantity and lubricant type.

Partial or touch-up lubrication in the shop without full teardown: oiling accessible pivots, oil sinks, motion work or strike levers of a movement still assembled in its case or partly dismantled, reaching past case parts, dial and hands.

On-site lubrication at the customer's premises: longcase/grandfather clock in a private home, or a tower/public clock in a church or civic building, oiled in place on ladders or platforms with a hand oiler and grease gun, in dust, poor light and confined access.

tasks.label: Estimate repair costs and timepiece values.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail counter intake of a common consumer watch (quartz battery replacement, crystal chip, band/pin work): the repairer looks the piece over with a loupe, identifies the needed work, and quotes a price from a shop price list before writing the ticket.

Mechanical wristwatch brought in for service: the watchmaker opens the caseback at the bench, inspects the movement, dial and case for wear, broken parts, rust or prior bad repairs, checks it on a timing machine, prices parts and labor, and gives the customer an overhaul estimate.

Mail-in or corporate/warranty service center workflow: the technician performs an intake diagnostic on a shipped watch and issues a written/digital estimate to the customer or brand for approval, often within a set turnaround, including parts availability and non-repairable determinations.

Clock work: estimating repair of a grandfather, mantel or wall clock, sometimes on an in-home service call, judging movement condition, case and dial restoration needs, cable/weight/chime issues, plus travel and setup charges.

Valuation of a vintage, antique or high-value timepiece for a buyer, seller, insurer or estate: grading originality and condition, checking references and comparable sale prices, and stating a market or replacement value (with or without an accompanying repair estimate).

tasks.label: Repair or replace broken, damaged, or worn parts on timepieces, using lathes, drill presses, and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench overhaul of a mechanical wristwatch in a repair shop or brand service center: after disassembly and cleaning, the watchmaker identifies worn/broken components (mainspring, balance staff, cracked jewels, click spring, worn pivots, stripped keyless works) on a caliber that may be decades old, presses out and rivets/press-fits replacements under a microscope with tweezers, staking set and jeweling tool, then reassembles and proves timekeeping.

Quartz/electronic watch repair at a retail or mail-in bench: open the case (snap-back or screw-back of unknown make), replace exhausted battery, corroded coil, broken stem/crown, damaged circuit or a complete replacement movement, transfer dial and hands, re-case and reseal.

External/case-side part replacement on a customer's wristwatch: fit a new crystal, gasket, crown tube, pusher, broken bracelet link, spring bar or clasp, refit bent or loose hands, using press, case tools and hand tools; then pressure-test.

Mechanical clock movement repair at the bench: bush worn pivot holes with a bushing machine or drill press, re-pivot or turn a replacement arbor/pinion on a watchmaker's lathe, replace mainspring, suspension spring or broken wheel teeth on an old, non-standard movement, then reassemble and set in beat.

On-site repair of a large or fixed clock (longcase clock in a private home, church/tower clock, street clock): diagnose and replace broken or worn parts such as pulleys, cables, suspension springs, worn bushings or hands, working in the customer's uncontrolled space with portable hand tools.

tasks.label: Test timepiece accuracy and performance, using meters and other electronic instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mechanical wristwatch (customer repair or post-service check) at the bench: watchmaker sets the watch on the timing machine's microphone holder, runs rate/amplitude/beat-error measurement in 5-6 positions (dial up/down, crown down, etc.), often repeated at full wind and 24 hours later, records results and decides pass/adjust.

Quartz watch electrical test at the bench: case opened, movement in a holder, probes applied to battery contacts/coil to read battery voltage, current consumption, coil resistance, pulse and rate deviation on a quartz analyzer; results interpreted to diagnose the movement or confirm the repair.

Water-resistance/case integrity test after reassembly: cased watch placed in a dry-air or vacuum/pressure tester, the electronic instrument runs a pressure/vacuum cycle and measures case deformation, giving pass/fail; failures re-tested after gasket work.

Clock work in the shop: mantel, wall or grandfather movement mounted on a test stand or in its case, a clamp/acoustic pickup attached, and the electronic timer run over hours or days to measure rate and beat, with results used to adjust the pendulum or balance.

On-site testing after delivery/installation: technician visits a customer's home, church tower or office, attaches a microphone/timing sensor to an installed longcase or tower clock in place, measures beat and rate under as-found conditions and adjusts.

tasks.label: Perform regular adjustment and maintenance on timepieces, watch cases, and watch bands.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Jeweler/retail service bench: routine battery replacement on customer quartz watches — identify and open a snap-back, screw-back or screw-down case back with the right tool, swap the cell without shorting or bending contacts, inspect and re-grease or replace the case gasket, reseal the case and run a pressure/water-resistance test, then reset time/date. Wide model variety, some corroded or fragile.

Bench work on watch bands: sizing a metal bracelet by removing or adding links (friction pins, screws, or pin-and-collar), replacing spring bars, swapping leather/rubber straps, adjusting clasp micro-adjustment and re-tightening loose clasp/end links on customer watches of many designs.

Bench: routine rate adjustment of a mechanical watch — put the watch on a timing machine in several positions, interpret rate/amplitude/beat error, demagnetize if needed, nudge the regulator index and hairspring stud for beat, re-measure over 24 hours and confirm the watch keeps to spec; also check crown, hand-setting and winding function.

Shop back room: cosmetic maintenance of watch case and bracelet — ultrasonic/steam cleaning, then refinishing scratched surfaces with emery, satin and polishing wheels while preserving case lines and brushed/polished demarcations; light crystal polishing. Customer pieces in steel, gold or titanium.

Bench: scheduled full service of a mechanical movement — case it out, strip the movement completely, inspect and replace worn parts, machine-clean and dry components, re-oil jewels and pallets with correct lubricants and grease the mainspring/keyless works, reassemble, then adjust and case up. Varied calibers, many decades old.

On-site clock maintenance in a private home, church or public building: grandfather, wall or tower clock — level the case, oil pivots and bushings in place, adjust pendulum/beat, check weights, cables and chimes, and regulate the rate. Access is cramped, layouts differ site to site.

On-site battery and electronics service at customer premises: battery-driven grandfather clock movements, church/tower or post clock controllers, museum and office installations — reached by ladder or in a cluttered room, layout unknown before arrival.

tasks.label: Demagnetize mechanisms, using demagnetizing machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Independent watch/clock repair shop bench: watchmaker notices a fast rate on the timegrapher or a magnetized hairspring, picks the customer's cased wristwatch or a bare movement off a cluttered bench, holds it on/over a Bergeon-type bench demagnetizer, presses the button, draws it slowly away while the field is on, then re-tests on the timing machine and repeats if needed.

Manufacturer-authorized or mail-in service center: routine demagnetization of movements and cased watches as a standard step in the service workflow (after intake diagnosis, after cleaning/assembly), watches arriving in trays with job tickets, verified on a timing machine and logged.

Jewelry store / mall watch counter: quick over-the-counter demagnetization of a customer's watch while they wait; varied watches of unknown make, some fragile or vintage, handled at a small service bench behind the counter.

Watch technician on a manufacture or refurbishment line: batches of movements, hairsprings and steel components demagnetized after machining, cleaning or magnetic-exposure testing, at a dedicated demagnetizing station feeding the next operation, with residual-field/rate checks.

On-site clock work: servicing a longcase, wall or tower clock in a customer's home, church or public building; the repairer applies a portable demagnetizer to the movement, mainspring or hairspring in situ in cramped, variable conditions and confirms the clock's rate settles.

tasks.label: Fabricate parts for watches and clocks, using small lathes and other machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Watch bench in a repair shop or service center: the watchmaker turns a small hardened-steel component from scratch on a watchmaker's lathe for an obsolete caliber — balance staff, winding stem, arbor or screw — with pivots roughly 0.08–0.15 mm diameter and tolerances of a few microns, then hardens, tempers and burnishes the pivots to a running fit.

Clock repair shop: the repairer turns a one-off brass or steel clock part from bar stock on a bench lathe — an oversized bushing for a worn plate hole, a winding arbor, a pillar, a collet or a pinion blank — to roughly 0.01–0.02 mm, sized to one particular movement.

Repair by modification of an existing damaged component: re-pivoting (drilling out a broken clock pivot from a hardened arbor and turning/fitting a new pivot plug), truing a worn arbor, or shortening and re-threading a stock winding stem; the worn original is itself the workpiece and its as-found geometry must be measured and matched.

Cutting gear teeth: making a replacement wheel, pinion, ratchet or count wheel on a wheel-cutting engine, dividing head or small mill — blank turned first, then teeth cut to a module and count copied from the broken original.

Flat and sheet parts made at the bench with occasional machine use: click springs, levers, clock hands, small cocks or brackets, sawn or pierced from sheet, filed to profile, drilled, hardened/tempered and blued.

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance, such as inspecting drives, motors, or belts, checking fluid levels, replacing filters, or doing other preventive maintenance actions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled HVAC preventive maintenance in a commercial/institutional building (office, school, hospital, hotel): lock out the air handler or rooftop unit, open access panels, pull and dispose of 4–12 dirty pleated filters, install correctly oriented new ones, check fan belt wear/tension and sheave alignment, grease motor bearings, check the drain pan, close up, restart and log the PM in the CMMS.

Route-based condition-monitoring round in an industrial plant, boiler room, or large facility: walk a fixed route past pumps, motors, drives, compressors and panels; read analog gauges and displays, take thermal readings of motors/bearings, listen for abnormal noise or air leaks, look at belts and sight glasses, record readings and flag anomalies for follow-up work orders.

Hands-on PM on production or facility machinery (conveyors, fans, gearboxes, packaging machines): shut down and lock out, remove belt guards, check belt condition and tension by hand/gauge, re-tension or replace, grease fittings, check gearbox oil, tighten fasteners, re-guard and test-run.

Fluid service on vehicles, mobile equipment, generators, compressors or hydraulic units: check dipstick/sight-glass levels, top off engine oil, coolant, hydraulic and fuel, verify to spec, wipe up spills, record levels and consumption.

Apartment/residential PM rounds for a property manager: enter occupied units of varying layout and clutter, change furnace/AC filters, check water heater and TPR valve, test smoke detectors, clear dryer vents, check under-sink plumbing and appliances.

Light-equipment PM in retail, food service or warehouse facilities: clean refrigeration condenser coils, check small motors and belts on ovens/mixers/conveyors, lubricate dock levelers and door operators, replace grease and water filters, log each item.

tasks.label: Inspect, operate, or test machinery or equipment to diagnose machine malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Reactive fault diagnosis on downed production machinery in a manufacturing plant (packaging line, conveyor, mixer): worker jogs the machine, watches the cycle, listens, checks limit switches and sensors, opens the control cabinet and probes with a multimeter, isolates the failed component while production waits.

Commercial/institutional building HVAC and mechanical equipment not performing (rooftop unit, chiller, boiler, circulating pump): run the unit, measure amp draw, temperature split and refrigerant pressures, check belts, filters, contactors, float switches and controls, on a roof or in a mechanical room.

Routine preventive inspection round through an industrial or institutional plant: walk a fixed route past pumps, motors, compressors, gearboxes and panels; read gauges, look for leaks and overheated bearings, listen for abnormal noise and vibration, log readings and flag deteriorating equipment.

Scheduled functional testing of equipment: exercise standby generators and fire pumps under load, cycle valves and dampers, test safety interlocks and emergency stops, run a machine through a test cycle to confirm correct operation and expose intermittent faults.

Equipment in occupied human-service spaces (hotel, school, hospital, restaurant, retail): commercial dishwasher, laundry washer-extractor, ice machine, automatic door operator, walk-in cooler; operate the unit, reproduce the fault, open panels and inspect internals while staff and occupants work around the technician.

Tenant or residential unit and scattered small sites: water heater with no hot water, unit HVAC, range or refrigerator, disposal, sump pump; enter an occupied, cluttered dwelling, test the appliance, verify power/gas/water supply, and determine the cause.

tasks.label: Adjust functional parts of devices or control instruments, using hand tools, levels, plumb bobs, or straightedges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Door and closure hardware in an occupied institutional/commercial building (school, office, hospital): adjust a door closer's sweep and latch-speed valves and spring tension, reposition hinges/strike plates, shim a sagging frame, checking plumb and square with a level and straightedge until the door swings, latches and self-closes correctly.

HVAC and building control devices: adjust thermostat/aquastat/pressure-switch setpoints and differentials, damper and actuator linkages, float and pilot valves, plus belt tension and sheave alignment (straightedge) on air handlers in mechanical rooms and rooftop units; verify the device controls to spec afterward.

Plant or facility machinery on the production floor between runs: adjust conveyor belt tracking screws and guide rails, chain tension and clutch settings, reposition limit switches and photo-eyes, and align a motor-pump coupling using straightedge/dial indicator and shims.

Installing, leveling and squaring new equipment or fixtures inside the facility: bring a machine base, appliance, rack or cabinet to level using leveling feet and shims read against a spirit/laser level, plumb a post or frame with a plumb bob, square components with a straightedge, then lock the adjusters.

Occupied apartment or house service call (residential maintenance variant): align cabinet doors and drawers with three-way hinge screws, adjust toilet fill-valve float and flapper chain, patio/closet door rollers and tracks, window hardware, garage-door opener limits and force settings, amid clutter, furniture, pets and non-standard hardware.

Exterior/site work in weather: adjust a vehicle gate operator's limit cams, chain tension and force settings, gate hinges and latches, parking barrier arm balance, or plumb an exterior post/handrail with level and plumb bob on uneven ground.

It is the same act as the rated task - loosening a lock nut, turning a threaded adjuster with a powered hand-tool head, and re-torquing until a measuring instrument reads within spec - on comparable steel hardware at comparable precision, and it demonstrates measurement-driven adjustment rather than blind fastening.

tasks.label: Repair machines, equipment, or structures, using tools such as hammers, hoists, saws, drills, wrenches, or equipment such as precision measuring instruments or electrical or electronic testing devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ repair of production or process machinery on a plant/warehouse floor: worker responds to a breakdown (conveyor, packaging machine, pump, compressor, motor drive), diagnoses the fault with meters and observation, locks out power, removes guards and fasteners, replaces the failed bearing/belt/chain/sensor/motor, aligns and adjusts, then runs and verifies the machine. Machine is in place, access is cramped, surfaces are oily.

Repair of building mechanical/electrical systems in a commercial or institutional building: rooftop HVAC unit, air handler, boiler, circulating pump, lighting circuit or panel, plumbing fixture, kitchen or laundry equipment. Worker troubleshoots with a multimeter/manometer, opens access panels, replaces a contactor, capacitor, belt, valve, or motor, and tests operation. Mechanical rooms, ceilings, rooftops.

Structural and carpentry repairs in an institutional/commercial building: sticking or damaged doors and closers, damaged drywall and trim, loose railings and stair treads, damaged flooring or ceiling tile, broken hardware. Worker measures, cuts with saw, drills, fastens, patches and finishes to match, working around occupants and furniture.

Repairs inside occupied private residences (apartment/property maintenance calls) and outdoor site features: garbage disposal, toilet, faucet, cabinet, appliance, window, fence, gate, exterior stair, lot lighting. Cluttered, non-standard, unpredictable layouts and equipment; pets, weather, and tenants present.

Shop bench work restoring a worn or damaged metal part removed from equipment: a worn shaft journal, seal surface, blade, wear plate or cracked bracket is measured, built up by welding/cladding, then ground/machined back to dimension and checked with precision instruments.

Shop bench rebuild of a removed assembly: pump, gearmotor, gearbox or valve is disassembled on the bench, parts cleaned and inspected for wear, bearings/seals/gaskets replaced, unit reassembled with correct torque and clearances, then bench-tested before reinstallation.

tasks.label: Diagnose mechanical problems and determine how to correct them, checking blueprints, repair manuals, or parts catalogs, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Reactive breakdown diagnosis of production/process machinery on a plant floor (conveyor stalls, motor won't start, hydraulic press erratic): worker responds to a down machine, reads controller fault codes, opens guards and control panels, manipulates and tests components (belts, couplings, sensors, contactors), consults schematics and repair manuals, and determines the faulty part and the fix.

Routine condition-monitoring rounds in an industrial plant or utility: walk fixed equipment routes while machines run, sense hot bearings/motors, abnormal noise or vibration, compressed-air or steam leaks, read gauges, and identify developing mechanical faults plus the corrective action (replace bearing, realign pump, repair leaking fitting) for the maintenance schedule.

Commercial/institutional building mechanical systems: rooftop packaged AC unit, boiler, chiller, air handler or circulation pump not performing; worker climbs to the unit or enters the mechanical room, opens access panels, checks belts, motors, filters, refrigerant pressures with gauges, electrical controls and safeties, consults wiring diagrams and manuals, and determines the corrective action and parts needed.

Occupied residential unit (apartment, campus housing, rental house) work order: no hot water, refrigerator or dishwasher failing, garbage disposal jammed, window/split AC not cooling, plumbing leak under a sink; worker enters a cluttered private dwelling with occupants and pets present, moves belongings, inspects and tests the appliance/fixture, and determines the repair.

Occupied institutional interiors (school, hospital, hotel, retail, office): binding door closer or lockset, leaking flush valve, commercial kitchen or laundry equipment malfunctioning, exercise or lab equipment fault; worker diagnoses on the spot amid furnishings and people, consulting parts catalogs to identify replacement components.

Outdoor grounds and building envelope: automatic gate or overhead-door operator failing, mowers and small engines, loading-dock leveler, irrigation pump, tracing a roof or wall leak through attics/crawlspaces; work occurs in weather, on ladders and roofs and in tight unlit spaces with site-to-site variation.

tasks.label: Design new equipment to aid in the repair or maintenance of machines, mechanical equipment, or building structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant maintenance shop: after an obsolete part fails, the worker measures the machine with tape and calipers, then works out and sketches a dimensioned design for a custom bracket, shim, or mounting adapter that will let a substitute part fit. Output is a marked-up sketch/spec handed to the welder or machinist for fabrication.

Designing a jig, fixture, puller, or alignment aid for a recurring repair (e.g., a fixture to hold and position a motor or gearbox during change-out). The worker conceives the device, selects stock material and dimensions, and documents it as a sketch or simple CAD drawing plus a bill of materials.

Designing a machine guard, safety cover, interlock mount, or small access platform/railing modification to meet a safety finding in a facility; requires checking clearances and applicable standards and producing a drawing for approval before anything is built.

Institutional building setting (school, hospital, hotel): designing a purpose-built cart, rack, hoist point, or storage/handling device for tools, filters, or parts, sized to fit doorways, elevators, and mechanical rooms; output is a sketch and parts list.

Designing a modification to building or HVAC hardware — a weatherproof enclosure, duct transition, condensate/drainage rework, or pipe support arrangement — including layout sketch, materials list, and rough cost estimate submitted to a supervisor or facilities engineer for approval.

tasks.label: Assemble, install, or repair wiring, electrical or electronic components, pipe systems, plumbing, machinery, or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plumbing repair in a commercial/institutional building (school, hospital, office, plant restroom or mechanical room): locate a leak or failure, shut off and drain the line, disassemble in place under a sink, in a chase or at a fixture, replace the failed valve, cartridge, flush valve, trap or pipe section, reassemble and test for leaks.

Install new or replacement piping/plumbing and connect equipment in a facility: measure, cut, thread/solder/press/weld pipe or tube, fabricate spools and hangers, hang and route the run, land connections on pumps or equipment, pressure-test.

Electrical/electronic work on facility equipment and building systems: pull and terminate wiring in conduit and junction boxes, wire or rewire control panels, and troubleshoot and replace failed contactors, relays, drives, sensors, motors, light fixtures and receptacles, then test.

Repair machinery in place on the plant floor or in a mechanical room: lock out, remove guards, replace bearings, belts, chains, seals, couplings, pumps or gearboxes, realign and rebalance, torque fasteners, and test-run the machine.

Bench work in the maintenance shop with the work brought to the worker: rebuild or repair removed components (pump, motor, gearbox, valve), fabricate and weld brackets or pipe spools, and assemble new equipment subassemblies before installation.

Repairs inside occupied private residences/apartment units (apartment maintenance technicians): leaking faucets, toilets, garbage disposals, outlets, switches and fixtures, appliance and HVAC component swaps, in cluttered occupied rooms with varied fixtures and unknown existing installations.

Lubrication route on a manufacturing or warehouse floor during scheduled downtime: oil or grease conveyor chains, sprockets, trolley bearings, gearboxes, motor bearings and bearing blocks on production and material-handling machinery; check oil levels and wipe fittings before greasing.

Cleaning production machinery in a processing plant (food/beverage or similar): removing product residue, dust, carbonized buildup and grime from machine frames, guards, rollers, conveyors and drive components during a shutdown or sanitation window, using hoses, foam/chemicals, brushes or blast media.

Bench work in the maintenance shop during a repair: degrease and clean disassembled shafts, bearing races, sprockets and gear sets with solvent, brushes or blasting; remove old hardened grease; re-pack bearings with fresh grease and coat gear teeth before reassembly.

Rounds through an institutional building lubricating hardware and small equipment: door hinges, closers, panic hardware and locks, overhead/roll-up door tracks, chains and rollers, dock levelers, cart and exercise-equipment bearings; wipe dirt off before applying oil or grease.

Property/apartment maintenance inside occupied residential units and garages: lubricate garage door rollers, springs and opener chain, blower motor and fan bearings on residential HVAC, appliance and dryer parts; clean lint, dust and old grease from those parts amid tenants' furnishings.

tasks.label: Align and balance new equipment after installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Precision shaft alignment of a newly installed rotating machine set (pump/motor, motor/gearbox, air compressor) on a baseplate in an industrial plant or building mechanical room: mount dial indicators or a laser alignment head on the shafts, check soft foot, compute vertical/horizontal corrections, loosen hold-down bolts, insert or remove stainless shims under motor feet, jack the motor sideways, re-torque, and iterate to within a few thousandths of an inch, then document.

Sheave alignment and belt tensioning on newly installed belt-driven equipment (air-handler fan, blower, belt-drive compressor) in a mechanical room or rooftop of an institutional building: set sheaves on shafts, align with straightedge or laser, install and seat belts, adjust the motor slide base, set tension with a tension gauge, lock set screws and jam nuts, recheck after run-in.

Vibration check and dynamic balancing of a newly installed rotating assembly (AHU fan wheel, blower rotor, pump impeller) in a plant or mechanical room: attach accelerometer and phase reference, run the machine, read amplitude and phase, attach trial weights, then clip/weld/bolt correction weights to the wheel until vibration meets the ISO/spec limit.

Setting, leveling, squaring and anchoring new stationary equipment on a plant or facility floor (machine tool, conveyor section, packaging machine, commercial laundry machine, generator skid): use a precision level and laser, adjust leveling feet and shim packs, square to reference lines, drill and set floor anchors, torque hardware, and verify level/flatness to the manufacturer's tolerance.

Field alignment and leveling of newly installed rotating equipment in unstructured settings taken as found: a small commercial or residential building, crawlspace, well house, rooftop under construction, or a renovation site — cramped access, no fixed layout, varied makes and mounting arrangements (e.g., a new pump/motor set, an RTU fan and motor assembly).

Aligning and adjusting one-off, non-standard mechanisms after installation in unstructured settings: overhead door track and opener alignment, gate operator, conveyor take-up and tracking on a job-built frame — each installation different, adjustment by feel and trial, no standard fixture or reference.

sources.system: Fori Automation robotic wheel aligner / robotic toe set system
sources.title: End of Line Testing Systems – Wheel Aligners, Headlamp Aimers, Robotic Toe Set & Automated Tooling Changeover
sources.claim: Fori Automation built and integrated robotic wheel-alignment stations in which four robots with toe-set gear heads autonomously loosen, rotate and re-tighten tie rods and cam bolts under continuous optical alignment measurement, driving the geometry to within ±0.03 degrees of nominal in a fenced end-of-line cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line vehicle alignment. It is the same measure–adjust–lock loop as machine alignment after installation: metrology measures residual misalignment, a robot with a nut runner loosens a locking fastener, turns a threaded adjuster, and re-torques, iterating until within a tight angular tolerance on a fixtured assembly — comparable object size, fastener torques and precision to shimming/jack-bolting a motor to a pump.

tasks.label: Maintain or repair specialized equipment or machinery located in cafeterias, laundries, hospitals, stores, offices, or factories.

instances.label: Commercial kitchen/cafeteria: a dish machine, combi oven, steam kettle, fryer or walk-in cooler fails during or between service. Worker replaces drive belts, bearings, seals, water/steam valves, drain valves, door interlocks or motors; lint and heat, machine bolted to floor, work done in place with wrenches, pullers and meters.

Hospital or other institution: service of specialized support equipment — sterilizer/autoclave, dietary and cart-wash equipment, pneumatic tube station, patient lifts, lab/vacuum-pressure equipment — performed in an occupied, infection-controlled facility with tight scheduling and lockout/tagout.

Retail store or office building: repair of specialized fixtures and equipment — refrigerated display cases and their compressors/fans/defrost controls, trash compactors and balers, automatic entrance doors, checkout conveyors, dock levelers, rooftop HVAC units — layouts differ store to store, work done during business hours around customers.

Factory floor breakdown repair on production machinery: conveyor, packaging machine, press, pump or mixer stops. Worker diagnoses the fault, then replaces a bearing, belt, chain, seal, gearbox, sensor, cylinder or motor in place on the line, realigns and re-commissions the machine under production pressure.

Scheduled preventive maintenance and wear-part/consumable replacement inside fenced automated production cells: changing spot-weld electrode caps, dressing electrodes, cleaning and re-tipping MIG torch consumables, swapping worn tool inserts — repetitive, standardized service on a known machine at a known location.

tasks.label: Dismantle machines, equipment, or devices to access and remove defective parts, using hoists, cranes, hand tools, or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant-floor teardown of production/process machinery in place: lock out the machine, remove guards, covers and drive components, unbolt and rig a failed gearbox, motor, bearing housing or roll with an overhead hoist or chain fall, and extract it. Fasteners are often seized or corroded, access is cramped, and the surrounding line is live.

Building mechanical equipment teardown in institutional/commercial facilities: rooftop HVAC units, air handlers, boilers, chilled-water pumps, compressors, exhaust fans. Remove access panels and sheet-metal covers, disconnect couplings/piping/wiring, unbolt and pull a blower motor, fan wheel, heat exchanger or valve actuator, working off ladders, in mechanical rooms or on roofs, in weather.

Bench teardown in the maintenance shop of a one-off component brought in from the field (centrifugal pump, gearmotor, valve actuator, conveyor drive, power tool, cart or lift assembly) of varied make, model, age and condition: press off bearings, pull couplings and impellers, split housings, remove the defective part non-destructively so the unit can be rebuilt.

Repetitive shop teardown of a standardized device or subassembly the facility handles again and again (same model of appliance, electronic unit, battery pack, small motor or pump in a fleet), where the fastener pattern and disassembly sequence are known in advance and the part to be removed is the same each time.

In-place disassembly of small fixed devices and fixtures inside occupied institutional space: door closers and overhead door operators, laundry and vending machines, light fixtures and ballasts, plumbing fixtures, drinking fountains. Work is done on a ladder or on the floor among staff and the public, using hand and cordless power tools.

Field/residential property work: dismantling a tenant's clothes dryer, dishwasher, range, water heater, garage-door opener or split-system condenser inside an apartment, house or unconditioned crawlspace/garage, with unpredictable layout, clutter, pets and occupants present.

tasks.label: Plan and lay out repair work, using diagrams, drawings, blueprints, maintenance manuals, or schematic diagrams.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Machine/controls fault: worker receives a work order for a stopped packaging or conveyor line, pulls the ladder/schematic diagram and OEM manual, traces the control circuit, and determines the diagnostic and repair sequence, parts, tools and lockout steps before touching the machine.

HVAC or plumbing component replacement: worker studies the manufacturer service manual and building mechanical drawings (piping/duct runs, valve and isolation points) to decide isolation sequence, replacement procedure, required fittings and materials, and schedules the outage window.

Building/structural repair (door, partition, flooring, stair, roof leak): worker reviews building blueprints or as-builts, takes field dimensions, and works out the approach — materials list, cut dimensions, and sequence — sketching the arrangement for the job.

New equipment installation or realignment: worker reads OEM installation drawings and foundation/anchor details plus utility drawings to plan mounting positions, clearances, rigging, and hookup sequence, coordinating with other trades.

Routine/preventive work order planning: worker reviews the PM checklist, equipment manual and parts catalog in the CMMS to determine tasks, spare parts, permits and time estimate for the shift's list of repairs.

tasks.label: Install equipment to improve the energy or operational efficiency of residential or commercial buildings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lighting and lighting-controls retrofit in an occupied commercial or institutional building: from a ladder or lift, remove fluorescent troffers/high-bays, install LED fixtures or retrofit kits, cut and cap ballast leads, make line-voltage connections with wire nuts, mount occupancy sensors and timers, restore lenses and ceiling tiles; ceilings 9-25 ft, furniture and occupants present.

Mechanical/electrical room of a commercial or institutional building: mount and connect energy-saving equipment such as a VFD, premium-efficiency motor or pump, building-automation sensors/controllers, or programmable thermostats; drill anchors into masonry, run conduit and low-voltage cable, terminate conductors at screw terminals, power up and commission.

Occupied apartment or single-family rental: replace an old thermostat with a programmable/smart thermostat and add occupancy or daylight sensors - remove old base, identify unlabeled existing conductors, mount base level on drywall/plaster, terminate wires, configure and verify heating and cooling operation.

Occupied apartment or single-family rental: install non-wired efficiency fittings - low-flow faucet aerators and showerheads, water-heater blanket/timer, foam pipe-insulation sleeves, adhesive weatherstripping and door sweeps on entry doors, window film - working around tenant furnishings.

Weatherization of envelope and distribution systems: add attic or crawlspace insulation, air-seal penetrations with caulk and spray foam, insulate or seal duct joints and hot-water piping in unconditioned attics, basements and crawlspaces; crawling in tight, dusty, as-found spaces with joists, wiring and obstructions.

Replace an end-of-life unit with a high-efficiency model in a utility closet or mechanical room: water heater, circulating pump/motor, exhaust or make-up air fan, window/through-wall AC; hoist and set the unit, connect water/gas/vent and electrical, purge, test and verify operation.

sources.system: Q-Bot underfloor insulation robot
sources.developer: Q-Bot Ltd (deployed with Torus housing group)
sources.title: Torus - RetroFIT for the Future: Q-Bot underfloor insulation
sources.claim: Q-Bot's insulation robot is deployed in occupied UK housing to spray foam insulation under suspended timber floors, but it is remotely operated rather than autonomous, showing that in-building energy-retrofit installation robots still depend on a human operator.

sources.system: Robotiq Screwdriving Workcell (UR cobot + Robotiq screwdriver/grippers) at Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories
sources.title: Screwdriving Automation and Cobot Components for Electrical Equipment Manufacturers | Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories

sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening small components onto a fixtured workpiece with torque-controlled screwdriving. Transfers to fastening small efficiency fittings (aerators, sweeps, sleeves) when the workpiece is fixtured and presented, comparable object size and precision.

sources.system: GLPPR robotic batt-insulation installation method (6-DOF arm + custom end effector)

sources.claim: A 6-DOF robot arm with a custom end effector autonomously installed batt thermal insulation into fixtured light-frame wood wall panels with a 92.5% success rate across mineral wool and fiberglass and various frame sizes.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical operation as the weatherization instance (placing and pressing thermal insulation into a framed cavity), performed on a fixtured prefabricated panel in a robotic cell rather than in an as-found attic.

sources.transferJustification: Same task family (installing energy-efficiency envelope equipment on existing buildings); cited as evidence that no demonstrated in-situ system exists, not as evidence of capability.

sources.transferJustification: Same task family (installing insulation/air-sealing in existing buildings); prize-stage descriptions with unestablished autonomy in real buildings, so used only as context.

tasks.label: Set up and operate machine tools to repair or fabricate machine parts, jigs, fixtures, or tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant/campus maintenance shop: turn a one-off round replacement part (bushing, shaft, pin, spacer, sleeve) from bar stock on an engine lathe. Dimensions taken with calipers/micrometer from the broken original or a sketch; typical fits held to a few thousandths; chuck/collet workholding, occasional between-centers setup.

Maintenance shop: mill/drill a fabricated item from plate or bar — mounting bracket, guard plate, adapter, or a jig/fixture to hold a part for a repair job. Layout from a sketch, vise or clamp workholding on a knee mill or drill press, drilling and tapping holes, milling slots or steps.

Bench and secondary machine work supporting a repair: cut stock to length on the horizontal bandsaw, deburr and grind edges, dress/sharpen tooling on the pedestal grinder, chamfer and thread with die or tap, finish surfaces. Many small pieces, mixed sizes, short cycles.

Re-machine an existing worn or damaged component to restore fit: skim a scored shaft journal, face a leaking flange or seal surface, bore a worn housing oversize for a new bushing, chase damaged threads. The workpiece is an as-found used part with unknown wear, no drawing, and irregular clamping surfaces.

Larger maintenance shop with a CNC mill or CNC lathe: program (conversational or CAM), set tool offsets and work offsets, prove out, and run a small batch of spare parts (e.g., 6 wear plates or 20 bushings) for plant stock.

In-place field machining on installed equipment that cannot be moved: portable line boring a worn bearing bore in a machine frame, portable flange facing on a pump or piping, drilling/keyway cutting on an assembled machine on the plant floor — machine brought to the work, alignment set on site.

sources.system: FANUC RoboDrill + FANUC robotic arm automation cells (integrated by Methods Machine Tools) at Ultradent
sources.title: Small-Batch Medical Shop Embraces Automation to Capture Market Share, Triples Throughput
sources.claim: FANUC RoboDrill machining cells with a robot arm and raw-stock storage produce precision machined parts (including accurately threaded blind holes) while running unattended 16 hours a day and lights-out on weekends at a US manufacturer.
sources.transferJustification: Same operations as the task's milling/drilling/tapping instances (metal parts, thousandths-level tolerances), performed in a purpose-built robot cell.

sources.system: Robotic mill-turn cell with integrated Mitutoyo CMM at Acutec Precision Aerospace
sources.title: Integrated Metrology Solution Powers Lights-Out Aerospace Production | Modern Machine Shop
sources.claim: A robotic mill-turn cell paired with a shopfloor CMM runs unattended aerospace production at Acutec Precision Aerospace while holding micron-level quality, covering both turning and milling operations.

sources.system: Hadrian automated precision-machining factories (Opus software, CNC fleet, robotics)
sources.title: Report: Hadrian Business Breakdown & Founding Story | Contrary Research
sources.claim: Hadrian's software-driven precision machining factories run their CNC fleet unattended overnight and are organized so that one-off parts are produced with the same standardized setup as batches, i.e. high-mix single-piece machining under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Shows one-off (quantity-of-one) precision machining, the dominant mode in maintenance shops, being executed unattended in a purpose-built machining environment.

sources.system: Renishaw SPRINT on-machine scanning probe / OSP60 with adaptive machining software
sources.title: Adaptive machining (Renishaw resource centre)
sources.claim: Renishaw SPRINT/OSP60 on-machine scanning enables adaptive machining in which the actual (as-found, variable) part is scanned on the machine and a tailored cutter toolpath is automatically generated and loaded ... CNC control — the standard industrial method for machining repaired/worn components such as turbine blades.
sources.transferJustification: Transfers to re-machining worn parts: the system measures the actual worn geometry on the machine and adapts the cut, which is exactly what restoring a journal, flange face or bore requires.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics GMR-AI smart workcells
sources.title: GrayMatter raises $45M Series B to ease robot programming for manufacturers - The Robot Report
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' GMR-AI workcells self-program for high-mix, high-variability parts and autonomously perform sanding, polishing, grinding, coating and ...; the technology is commercially deployed with industrial customers including shipbuilder HII.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the grinding/deburring/finishing bench-work portion of the task on high-mix one-off parts, without part-specific programming.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / autonomous welding cells (Obsidian AI)
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' welding cells autonomously scan and weld one-off steel parts without part programming and are deployed in fabrication ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task (one-off metal fabrication of brackets/fixtures): shows machine perception replacing per-part programming for as-presented, non-repeating steel workpieces in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: CloudNC CAM Assist / CAM Assist 2.0
sources.title: CAM Assist now used by over 1,000 machine shops globally to accelerate CNC programming with AI
sources.claim: AI CAM automation that generates CNC toolpaths from a part model is in routine commercial use in over 1,000 machine shops, supplying the programming layer that lets a machining cell run a new one-off part.
sources.transferJustification: Software, not a robotic system: cited only as the programming layer that accompanies the physically embodied CNC/robot cells above; it is not decisive for any judgment on its own.

tasks.label: Perform general cleaning of buildings or properties.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine floor care of the open areas of a large commercial or institutional building the worker maintains (warehouse/plant aisles, store sales floor, school or hospital corridors, lobby): dust-mop, vacuum or run a scrubber over broad obstacle-light floor, dump and refill tanks. Done off-hours or alongside occupants.

Restroom / locker-room servicing round in a facility with no dedicated custodial staff on shift: scrub toilets, urinals, sinks, mirrors and partitions, mop the floor, empty the waste bins into a cart, restock paper and soap, report anything broken.

Cleanup at the site of a repair the worker has just finished: sweep or vacuum drywall/metal dust, pick up cut-offs, packaging, fasteners and old parts, mop a coolant or water spill, wipe down the equipment and surrounding surfaces, and haul the debris to the dumpster. Occurs in mechanical rooms, shops, tenant spaces and occupied corridors, with layout and mess different every time.

Sweeping the paved surfaces of the property: parking lot, parking garage deck, loading dock apron, plaza or large paved walkway, with a push broom, blower or ride-on sweeper; grit, leaves, cups and dust, around parked cars.

Other exterior cleaning of the grounds: policing litter out of lawns, beds and shrubs, blowing/sweeping entry walks and breezeways, emptying exterior trash cans and ashtrays, hosing or pressure-washing entrances, stairs and the dumpster pad.

Deep or turnover cleaning of a vacant residential unit or a heavily soiled space (make-ready of an apartment, cleanup after a leak or a tenant move-out): scrub kitchen and bath fixtures and appliances, wipe cabinets, baseboards, blinds and windows, clean floors, remove leftover debris.

sources.system: Tennant T7AMR with BrainOS (Brain Corp)
sources.title: Walmart expands use of robotic floor scrubbers | Chain Store Age
sources.claim: BrainOS-powered Tennant T7AMR autonomous floor scrubbers clean the open sales floors of hundreds of Walmart stores, with expansion to 1,500 more locations; they navigate and clean autonomously among shoppers.

sources.title: Interview with ENWAY – FineEngineering Magazine
sources.claim: Enway's Blitz One autonomous industrial sweeper is a serial product in use sweeping warehouses, parking lots and production ....

sources.title: Skyline Robotics deploys Ozmo window cleaning robot in New York City - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Skyline Robotics' Ozmo robot cleans the glass facade of a 45-story New York office tower, cleaning autonomously while a human operator supervises from the rooftop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior building surface cleaning. Shows automated facade washing on a managed high-rise, but it is a suspended-platform glass system and does not perform grounds-level cleaning rounds.

tasks.label: Train or manage maintenance personnel or subcontractors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Fabricate or repair counters, benches, partitions, or other wooden structures, such as sheds or outbuildings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop fabrication of a freestanding wooden item for the facility: the maintenance worker builds a workbench, plywood shelving unit, storage cart, sawhorses, picnic table or a plain plywood partition panel in the maintenance shop from dimensional lumber and sheet goods using table/miter saw, drill and fasteners; the accepted output is the finished item delivered to the requester.

In-place repair or replacement of built-in casework in an occupied institutional building (school, office, hospital or plant break room): a damaged laminate counter, reception counter top, cabinet door or face frame is assessed on site, the damaged section cut out, a replacement piece scribed to out-of-square walls and existing plumbing, fastened, then caulked/refinished while occupants and other trades work around.

Repair or replacement of partitions in a facility: broken restroom stall panel, wooden office/shop divider, locker-room bench back, or a temporary dust partition. The worker removes the damaged panel and hardware on site, cuts a new panel to fit existing posts/anchors, and installs it in the occupied building.

Outdoor structures on the grounds: repair rotted shed siding, door or floor, rebuild an outdoor bench or picnic table, replace a fence or gate section, or erect a small outbuilding. Uneven ground, weather, rot, hidden or rusted fasteners, and no fixed layout.

Residential/tenant-unit carpentry for an apartment or property-management employer: replace a kitchen countertop, rehang or replace cabinet doors and drawer fronts, rebuild closet shelving or a vanity, inside an occupied, cluttered home with out-of-square walls and unknown existing construction.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor robotic wall production line (KUKA robots)
sources.title: Autowall, Robotic wall production line for production of exterior walls. | KUKA Sweden
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic system is deployed in a timber house factory (Kodumaja, Estonia), where robots fabricate timber wall elements - framing, fastening and multi-layer sheathing - in an automated production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory fabrication of timber wall elements. It uses the same materials and operations as shop-fabricating a wooden bench frame, partition or shed wall (cutting lumber, positioning members, nailing/screwing sheet goods to a frame) at equal or tighter precision, inside a purpose-built line.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300/M-340/M-380/M-500 multifunction bridge

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fabrication of timber-frame wall/floor/roof elements and nested panels. Same operations and tolerances a maintenance carpenter uses for a bench, counter substrate or partition (sawing, drilling, nailing sheet goods to lumber), performed inside a purpose-built machine line.

sources.system: Adaptive robotic wood-frame construction cell
sources.title: Adaptive robotic construction of wood frames | Construction Robotics (Springer) / Autodesk Research
sources.claim: An Autodesk Research robotic cell autonomously assembled wood light-frame walls from real framing lumber, using deep-learning stud pose estimation plus refinement, achieving precision better than construction industry guidelines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of stud-framed wooden structures from variable lumber. A shop-built bench, partition frame or shed wall is the same class of object, material variability and fastening precision; the demonstration is in a fixtured robotic cell.

sources.system: Robotic cabinet face-frame assembly cell
sources.title: Automation Profiles: Cabinet Assembly Moves Into 21st Century | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A commercial two-robot cell built by JR Automation with Stiles Machinery automatically assembles wooden cabinet face frames of varying sizes and materials at a cabinet manufacturer, handling parts that vary in size, density and orientation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of cabinet/counter casework components. Same wooden workpieces and joinery precision as fabricating counters or benches, with parts presented to a fenced robotic cell.

sources.system: Woodot mobile robotic defect-repair platform
sources.title: Woodot: An AI-Driven Mobile Robotic System for Sustainable Defect Repair in Custom Glulam Beams
sources.claim: Woodot, an autonomous mobile manipulator, locates, mills and plugs knot defects in custom glulam beams on a timber shop floor; it is a research prototype whose perception model scores F1 0.69 and which achieves flush plug placement in 87% ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic repair of defects in wood members. Cited as the closest demonstrated wood-repair automation; it covers only milling and plugging knots on beams staged in a production shop, not diagnosing and rebuilding damaged built-in casework in a building.

sources.system: Alpine / House of Design robotic floor truss system
sources.developer: House of Design Robotics with Alpine, an ITW Company
sources.title: Alpine and House of Design Launch Floor Truss Robotics - Structural Building Components Association
sources.claim: Alpine (ITW) and House of Design deployed ABB robot systems that build floor trusses in component manufacturing plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fabrication of nailed wooden structural assemblies in a factory cell; comparable lumber handling and fastening to shop fabrication of benches, partition frames or shed components.

tasks.label: Paint or repair roofs, windows, doors, floors, woodwork, plaster, drywall, or other parts of building structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Patch and repair localized interior drywall or plaster damage in an occupied institutional building (school, hospital, office, hotel): cut out a damaged section or holes, install backing/patch, tape and mud, sand, prime and blend touch-up paint, working around furniture, occupants and existing finishes.

Repaint a cleared room, corridor, stairwell, or vacated apartment unit in a managed building: mask/protect floors, trim and fixtures, cut in edges, roll or spray walls and ceilings, remove masking and clean up.

Door and window repair in an occupied facility: rehang or plane a sagging/binding door, replace hinges, closers, thresholds and locksets, re-glaze a broken pane or replace a sash/screen, refit weatherstripping.

Floor, stair and ceiling repair: replace damaged VCT/carpet tiles or suspended ceiling tiles, cut and fit pieces around fixtures, patch subfloor, re-secure loose treads, nosings, transition strips and handrails in occupied corridors and rooms.

Woodwork and light structural carpentry repair: replace or refit baseboard and trim, repair cabinets, shelving, partitions, doors' jambs and framing, fasten and finish new wood in place inside a facility.

Roof and exterior envelope repair: trace and patch a leak on a flat or shingled roof, replace shingles and flashing, reseal penetrations, caulk exterior joints, repair siding/soffit and touch up exterior paint, working at height and outdoors.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EG7+
sources.title: Okibo launches EG7+ autonomous robot for painting and finishing
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7+ is a fully autonomous, AI-guided robot that performs sanding, painting and level 4/5 drywall finishing on interior construction sites, launched commercially in the U.S. and used on major American construction projects.
sources.transferJustification: Interior surface painting/finishing of walls and ceilings is the same physical operation as a maintenance repaint of a room or corridor: same coatings, same vertical surfaces, same building interiors.

sources.system: Legend Robot interior spraying robot
sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic — Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Trade press reports Legend Robot's machine spray-paints interior walls and ceilings fully autonomously, covering about 95% of surfaces, fitting through standard doorways, completing a four-room apartment in 60-90 minutes, deployed in Singapore high-rise apartment buildings with one operator supervising two robots.

sources.system: Legend Robot Putty & Latex Paint Spraying Robot
sources.title: Legend Construction Robot for Toa Payoh N4C30, Singapore
sources.claim: Legend Robot's putty and latex paint spraying robot automated wall finishing for nearly 1,000 units across ... in a retrofit of existing Singapore public housing (HDB) flats.
sources.transferJustification: Retrofit wall finishing (putty plus paint) of existing occupied-building dwelling units is the closest analogue to a maintenance repaint of rooms and units.

sources.system: Canvas 1200CX
sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic — Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robot is semi-autonomous and works alongside human crews, spraying joint compound over panel seams and machine-sanding to a level 5 finish on commercial construction sites; a human operator drives the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Drywall finishing of new panels is the nearest robotic analogue to drywall/plaster repair, but it applies compound over full wall surfaces rather than cutting out and patching localized damage.

sources.system: PaintJet Bravo
sources.title: PaintJet puts robots to work in construction and maintenance as labor shortage drags on — CNBC
sources.claim: PaintJet's Bravo exterior painting system mounts on a lift and scans the wall, but ground operators run both the lift and the spray end effectors by remote control on commercial/industrial repaint jobs.
sources.transferJustification: Exterior repainting of existing buildings is a maintenance painting task, but the demonstrated system is remote-operated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Rufus
sources.title: Beacon Announces Partnership with Renovate Robotics — Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus is an automated roofing ... that attaches to the roof and installs asphalt shingles on residential ...; as of mid-2025 it was in pilot with contractors, not doing leak diagnosis or flashing repair.
sources.transferJustification: Full asphalt-shingle re-roofing is adjacent to roof repair, but it is bulk installation on a stripped roof plane rather than locating and patching a leak, flashing or soffit on an existing roof.

sources.system: Robo-Buddy Floor / Robo-Buddy
sources.title: Shimizu Deploys Robot for Installing Raised Floor Named "Robo-Buddy Floor"
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy Floor is a twin-armed robot deployed on Japanese high-rise construction sites that autonomously installs raised access floor pedestals and panels to within 1 mm; a related Robo-Buddy variant installs ceiling boards.
sources.transferJustification: Raised-floor and ceiling-board installation is the closest robotic analogue to floor/ceiling tile work, but it is repetitive new installation on an empty grid, not removal of damaged material, adhesive cleanup and custom cutting around fixtures in an occupied space.

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance on boilers, such as replacing burners or hoses, installing replacement parts, or reinforcing structural weaknesses to ensure optimal boiler efficiency.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Annual/seasonal burner service on a gas- or oil-fired hot water or steam boiler in a commercial or institutional building mechanical room: lock out gas and power, pull the burner or blast tube, replace electrodes/igniter, nozzle, flame sensor and gaskets, reassemble, re-fire and verify safe operation. Cramped, hot, pipe-dense room; soot-covered used fasteners.

Replacing failed ancillary components on a boiler in an apartment or institutional basement boiler room: circulator pump, relief valve, sight glass, low-water cutoff, flexible hoses/connectors and gaskets. Requires isolating and draining, breaking threaded/flanged unions, wiring, refilling and purging, and leak checking on old, varied equipment in a cluttered space.

Scheduled shutdown maintenance on a firetube or small watertube boiler in a small industrial or manufacturing plant boiler room: swap the burner assembly, fuel hoses, manway and handhole gaskets, install replacement parts from a plant spares kit; hoist available, standardized plant layout, heavier components.

Reinforcing structural weaknesses / weld and refractory repair: grinding and welding a cracked support bracket, stay, or casing patch on a boiler or its frame, or patching refractory and insulation, followed by inspection and sealing.

Boiler service at scattered residential or very small light-commercial sites handled by a property maintenance worker: residential-scale boiler in a private home basement or crawlspace, clutter and improvised access, unknown equipment vintage; replace circulator, hoses, igniter or controls and re-commission.

sources.system: AI-Enabled Robot for Automated NDE and Repair of Power Plant Boilers (Colorado School of Mines / Michigan State, DOE project)
sources.title: AI-Enabled Robots for Automated Nondestructive Evaluation and Repair of Power Plant Boilers. Final Report (Technical Report) | OSTI.GOV
sources.claim: DOE-funded final report on boiler maintenance robotics states that existing power-plant boiler robotics (drones, crawlers) have no live repair capability and ... AI autonomy; the project to add repair tooling and autonomy was research-stage.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about robotic maintenance/repair of boilers; establishes that fielded boiler robots inspect but do not perform repair work autonomously.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 autonomous welding cells
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 robotic welding cells scan parts, plan weld paths without programming, and weld steel autonomously; they are installed and running in fabrication shops in the US and Canada.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous arc welding of steel weldments in a fixtured cell; welding a reinforcement plate, gusset or crack repair on a boiler component presented in a cell involves comparable steel thicknesses, seam-finding and weld quality.

sources.system: Optomec / Acme Manufacturing automated adaptive repair work cell

sources.claim: Optomec and Acme built a fully automated work cell that repairs worn/damaged metal turbine parts end to end: tip grinding, adaptive laser cladding to add material, and post-clad finishing, with automated pallet load/unload.

sources.system: Boltron autonomous flange bolting robot
sources.title: TMT Boltron (Autonomous Flange Bolting Robot datasheet)
sources.claim: TMT's Boltron is marketed as an autonomous flange-bolting robot for refineries, alumina refineries, chemical plants and power stations, handling bolt/nut make-up and torque on large bolted flanges; a refinery contract was announced in 2026.

sources.system: Spot with Spot Arm (Autowalk autonomous missions)
sources.title: The Next Step in Safe, Autonomous Robotic Inspection
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial plants and, as of the 2025 release, can autonomously open doors with its arm during Autowalk missions; its fielded manipulation remains inspection-support, not equipment repair.

sources.system: RoboHarsh ladle sliding-gate maintenance robot (RFCS project)

tasks.label: Provide groundskeeping services, such as landscaping or snow removal.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine mowing of the property's open turf areas (apartment complex commons, school/office/industrial grounds): a recurring weekly-in-season job on a maintained, institution-owned lawn with known layout, trees, light poles and occasional pedestrians; output is an evenly cut lawn to the property's standard.

Detail finishing work: string-trimming and edging around building foundations, fences, signs, poles, walk and curb edges, plus blowing clippings off walks and drives afterwards. Tight, obstacle-dense, requires hand-tool precision to avoid scalping turf or damaging siding/bark.

Bed and shrub care and small landscape work: pulling weeds, spreading mulch or topsoil, pruning hedges and shrubs, planting annuals/shrubs, replacing broken sprinkler heads, repairing eroded or bare turf spots on the grounds.

Winter storm response on the property's paved areas: clearing snow from sidewalks, entry walks, drives and the parking lot by plow, snowblower or shovel, and keeping pavement passable/de-iced through and after the storm, often overnight or before opening.

Seasonal leaf and storm-debris cleanup: blowing/raking heavy wet leaves off lawns, beds and walks, gathering and hauling them to disposal, dragging downed limbs after wind or ice storms, clearing rough perimeter and wooded-edge areas.

Routine sweeping and litter/grit clearing of paved drives, parking lots, loading areas and walkways at the facility — a repeated pass over open pavement to remove sand, litter and debris to the property's appearance standard.
