tasks.label: Operate cutting torches or welding equipment to cut or join metal parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Maintenance shop bench work: worker cuts steel stock to size with an oxy-fuel torch, plasma cutter, or chop saw, fits up and MIG/stick welds a bracket, guard, machine base, or shop-made replacement part; work is clamped on a welding table in the facility's shop, indoor, good access.

In-situ repair welding on installed machinery or building structure: cracked machine frame, broken conveyor bracket, worn chute, torn hopper patch, pipe support or handrail re-weld. Worker diagnoses the break, grinds/gouges and cleans the area, clamps or tacks parts in position, and welds in awkward, overhead, or confined positions under a hot-work permit inside a plant or building.

Torch cutting for removal/demolition in place: burning off seized bolts and rusted fasteners, cutting out obsolete pipe, ductwork, tank, or structural steel so equipment can be removed; done in mechanical rooms, on platforms, or at height, with fire watch and surrounding equipment to protect.

Outdoor grounds and exterior metal repairs: welding a broken gate hinge or fence rail, repairing a dumpster, trailer, dock plate, ladder, or exterior handrail, or cutting/welding supports for rooftop equipment; portable welder/torch taken to the item, varied terrain, weather, and site-to-site layout.

tasks.label: Inspect used parts to determine changes in dimensional requirements, using rules, calipers, micrometers, or other measuring instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant/facility maintenance shop bench: worker measures a component just removed from a machine (shaft journal, bushing, bearing race, wrist pin, sprocket) with caliper and micrometer, wipes off grease first, compares readings against the manufacturer's spec or a new spare, and decides reuse vs. replace.

At the point of repair (plant floor, mechanical room, rooftop unit): a worn part is pulled off and measured on the spot with a handheld caliper, rule or tape to establish the correct replacement size (sheave groove, seal/gasket, coupling insert, bolt, belt), in poor light and cramped access.

In-place wear checks on installed, assembled equipment without disassembly: brake lining thickness, chain elongation, belt/sheave wear gauge, feeler-gauge clearances, dial-indicator shaft runout and end-play, taken during a PM round on the plant floor.

Maintenance machine shop: precision measurement of a worn part to plan a repair - multiple micrometer and bore-gauge readings for taper and out-of-round, deciding undersize regrind/sleeving, or reverse-engineering dimensions of a broken part so a replacement can be fabricated.

Large or fixed assets measured in place: pump casing/wear-ring clearance, worn crane rail or conveyor components, tank or pipe wall thinning checked with an ultrasonic thickness gauge, often in confined space or outdoors on the site.

Building fabric and fixtures in occupied buildings or residential units: measuring a worn stair tread, sagging door and frame, worn floor or handrail with a rule/tape to quantify the deviation and size a replacement.

tasks.label: Assemble boilers at installation sites, using tools such as levels, plumb bobs, hammers, torches, or other hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential or light-commercial boiler replacement in a home basement, closet or small shop: wrestle the packaged/wall-hung unit into a tight space, set and level it (or hang it on a bracket, checked plumb), assemble flue/vent sections, sweat or press near-boiler copper piping and the gas train with a torch, mount trim, circulators and controls, fill and leak-check.

Institutional or commercial boiler room (school, hospital, apartment house, factory) retrofit: rig a packaged firetube or condensing boiler onto a housekeeping pad, level and plumb it with level, shims and plumb bob, anchor it, bolt on burner and breeching/stack sections, fit jacket panels and insulation, land header piping and trim.

Field-assembled sectional cast-iron boiler in an existing mechanical room: carry sections through doorways and down stairs, stack them with push nipples, rope and sealant, draw them up evenly with tie rods to torque, hammer/align sections true, hydrostatically test for leaks, then fit burner, jacket and controls.

Boiler assembly in a mechanical room under new construction or gut renovation: unfinished floor, temporary lighting and power, other trades working around, materials staged wherever they fit, layout unique to the site; set and assemble the boiler and its vent and piping connections with hand tools and torch.

Assembling boiler auxiliaries and subassemblies on site in a plant or building boiler room: mounting and aligning a burner, economizer or expansion tank, bolting up breeching/flue sections, assembling feedwater and safety trim on an existing boiler, checking level/plumb and gasketed joints.

tasks.label: Position, attach, or blow insulating materials to prevent energy losses from buildings, pipes, or other structures or objects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Insulating installed piping in a facility's mechanical room, boiler room, tunnel or above ceilings: measuring and cutting split preformed fiberglass or elastomeric foam sleeves, fitting them over hot-water, chilled-water or steam lines, sealing seams/jacket laps with tape or mastic, mitering fittings and valves, working overhead and cramped around hangers, conduit and other services.

Blowing loose-fill (cellulose/fiberglass) insulation into an attic or ceiling cavity of a building the worker maintains — dragging the hose through a hatch, working on joists in a low, hot, unlit attic, filling to depth around ducts, wiring, cans and baffles after a roof or electrical repair.

Positioning and attaching batt or rigid board insulation in walls, ceilings, crawlspaces and mechanical closets during repair or renovation: cutting batts to fit studs/joists, friction-fitting and stapling facing, cutting and adhering foam board, sealing edges with canned foam.

roles.title: Wind Turbine Service Technicians
aliases: Wind Turbine Blade Composite Technician (Wind Turbine Blade Composite Tech)
roles.description: Inspect, diagnose, adjust, or repair wind turbines. Perform maintenance on wind turbine equipment including resolving electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic malfunctions.

tasks.label: Troubleshoot or repair mechanical, hydraulic, or electrical malfunctions related to variable pitch systems, variable speed control systems, converter systems, or related components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Onshore utility-scale turbine trips on a pitch fault. Technician climbs ~100 m, locks the rotor, enters the confined rotor hub, reads fault codes, checks pitch motor, encoder/limit switches, backup battery/ultracap cabinet, slip ring and wiring with a multimeter, and replaces the failed electro-mechanical component, then resets and verifies pitch travel.

Hydraulic pitch/brake system malfunction: pressure loss, leaking hose or fitting, contaminated valve block, failed accumulator or pump. Technician traces the leak in the oily, cramped hub/nacelle, depressurizes, replaces hose/seal/valve or recharges the accumulator, cleans up oil, bleeds and pressure-tests the circuit.

Converter/power-electronics fault (rotor- or line-side). Technician isolates and LOTOs the cabinet at the tower base or in the nacelle, uses fault logs, meter and thermal camera to find a failed IGBT stack, fuse, capacitor, gate-driver board, contactor or cooling fan, swaps the module (busbar bolts, coolant couplings, fibre-optic and control connectors), and recommissions.

Variable-speed control system fault: turbine controller/PLC cards, I/O modules, comms/fibre faults, anemometer, speed or vibration sensors, chafed harness or corroded terminals. Technician diagnoses across the top box and ground controller, replaces cards/sensors, re-terminates wiring, checks parameters and returns the unit to service.

Same pitch/converter/control troubleshooting and repair on an offshore turbine, reached by CTV transfer or helicopter, with a weather window, heavier components, salt corrosion and confined internal transit — including hub entry for pitch work.

sources.system: Wind O&M robotics sector survey (Zeitview crawlers/drones, Aerones, BladeBUG, TNO prototypes)
sources.developer: Power Technology (GlobalData) / Zeitview, Aerones, BladeBUG, TNO
sources.title: Robots versus humans: will wind turbine management reach complete automation?
sources.claim: Trade-press survey of wind O&M robotics as of late 2025: deployed robots do inspection and some blade-exterior repair; robots generally cannot yet carry out turbine repairs, and nuanced root-cause repair still relies on humans.

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance on wind turbine equipment, underground transmission systems, wind fields substations, or fiber optic sensing and control systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled periodic service (6-month/annual) inside a turbine: climb or lift to nacelle and hub, remove covers, inspect and lubricate drivetrain/yaw/pitch bearings, sample and change gear oil and filters, check hydraulic pressures and brake pads, verify bolt torque on hub/nacelle/tower flanges, clean and check electrical terminations, and log results. Confined space, per-model layout, one to two techs, weather-dependent access.

Routine external blade/tower condition inspection campaign at an operating wind farm: turbine stopped and locked, all three blades imaged and assessed for cracks, erosion and lightning damage; findings reported into the O&M system.

Routine blade surface maintenance from outside the turbine: washing/cleaning blades, leading-edge erosion repair and protective coating, protective tape replacement, lightning-protection-system continuity testing, drainage-hole cleaning; performed at height on a parked turbine.

Routine walkdown/thermographic inspection round of the wind field collector substation and switchyard: infrared scan of transformer, breakers and bus connections, gauge/level/alarm readings, look for oil leaks and damage, record readings.

Hands-on servicing of substation and underground collector system equipment: cleaning insulators and cabinets, torquing bus and cable-termination connections, transformer oil sampling and desiccant/filter changes, breaker and relay function tests, pad-mount transformer and underground junction/vault inspections and cable testing along buried collector runs.

Routine maintenance of fiber-optic sensing, SCADA and control systems: inspecting and cleaning fiber connectors and patch panels, checking media converters/switches and controller cabinets in the tower base and substation, verifying sensor and communication signals, replacing cards/modules and re-terminating damaged fiber.

tasks.label: Diagnose problems involving wind turbine generators or control systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Onshore turbine tripped on a fault code: technician drives to site, interrogates the turbine controller/HMI and alarm log at the tower base, then opens the control and converter cabinets and works through the schematics - checking fuses, breakers, contactors, relays and I/O modules, measuring voltages/continuity/resistance with a multimeter, tracing harnesses - to isolate the faulty board, sensor or wire, then resets and verifies return to service.

Generator-related alarm (winding or bearing over-temperature, high vibration, insulation/earth fault, slip-ring or brush problem) on a 1.5-3 MW onshore turbine: technician climbs 80-100 m into the nacelle, opens generator covers and terminal boxes, inspects brushes/slip rings, cooling fans, filters and couplings, takes IR/insulation-resistance and winding-resistance readings, listens and feels for bearing noise, and decides whether the generator, its bearings, the cooling circuit, a sensor or the cabling is at fault.

Control-subsystem fault outside the main cabinet: pitch system in the rotor hub (pitch motor, drive, encoder, limit switches, backup capacitor/battery bank, slip ring) or yaw/converter subsystem in the nacelle. Technician locks the rotor, enters the confined hub or crawls around the nacelle, connects a service laptop, commands test movements, measures signals and supply voltages, and localises the faulty drive, encoder or wiring.

Diagnostic condition survey rather than a hard trip: technician performs a thermographic scan of the generator, converter, switchgear and terminal connections plus a listening/vibration check on the drivetrain, to localise a developing hot joint, loose connection or bearing problem flagged by SCADA/CMS trends, and reports which component is degrading.

Offshore turbine: technician transfers by CTV in a limited weather window, climbs the tower, and performs the same generator/converter/control-system fault diagnosis in the nacelle under time pressure, motion, salt-laden air and restricted spares, deciding on the spot whether the fault is a board, a sensor, cabling or the machine itself.

sources.claim: Toshiba's T15/T35 in-situ generator inspection robots crawl the air gap of power-plant generators and run visual, wedge-tightness (acoustic hammer analysis), EL-CID core-imperfection and UT diagnostics; the robot is inserted and driven by a docking bay station fitted to the rotor retaining ring, and all movement, inspection and diagnostic evaluation is automated. Offered as a commercial inspection service (ultra-thin robot deployed in nuclear plants; multi-functional robot in service from fiscal 2023).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnosing faults inside a large electrical generator (core insulation damage, loose stator wedges, arcing/heating marks, blocked rotor ventilation). These are the same fault classes and comparable precision to the wind technician's generator diagnosis, but the transfer requires the machine to be opened and a docking station fitted to it - the work presented to the robot - which is why it supports E1 rather than in-nacelle work.

tasks.label: Test electrical components of wind systems with devices, such as voltage testers, multimeters, oscilloscopes, infrared testers, or fiber optic equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Troubleshooting a fault code in the nacelle top-box or down-tower control cabinet: technician climbs the tower, opens the cabinet, uses a voltage tester and multimeter to check control voltages, contactor/relay coil continuity, fuse integrity, sensor circuits and terminal-block wiring on partly energized circuits in a cramped, vibrating enclosure, and identifies the faulty component.

Diagnostics on power-electronics and generator circuits: oscilloscope capture of IGBT gate/converter waveforms, clamp-meter current checks, insulation-resistance (megger) and winding-resistance tests on the generator, slip-ring/brush measurements, performed on de-energized and LOTO'd equipment in the nacelle or converter cabinet at the tower base.

Scheduled infrared thermographic survey of electrical connections: scanning busbars, breaker and contactor terminals, cable lugs, the pad-mount/tower transformer and switchgear with a thermal imager while the turbine runs under load, logging hot spots against baselines.

Lightning protection system testing: micro-ohm/continuity resistance measurement from each blade receptor through down conductors, hub and nacelle bonding to the tower, plus earth-electrode resistance measurement at the tower base, done outdoors at height or at ground level in field weather.

Fiber optic and SCADA communication testing: connecting an OTDR or light source/power meter to fiber runs between nacelle, tower base and collector substation, inspecting and cleaning connectors, verifying loss budgets and locating breaks in the turbine communication ring.

Ground-level medium-voltage and commissioning tests: phase-rotation and voltage checks, cable and hi-pot/insulation tests, and functional verification at the turbine base switchgear, pad-mount transformer or collector-circuit interface during commissioning or post-outage re-energization.

tasks.label: Start or restart wind turbine generator systems to ensure proper operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine restart from the tower base after on-site work or a local fault: technician, standing at the base controller cabinet inside the tower, acknowledges/resets the fault on the controller HMI, turns the mode selector from service/local back to remote/auto, presses start, then watches the rotor pitch in, spin up and connect to the grid, confirming power output on the display before leaving.

Restart that requires up-tower actions first: reset the nacelle service switch and any pressed E-stops, disengage the rotor lock pin / release the mechanical brake, close and latch control cabinets, remove lockout devices and tags, verify nobody and no tools remain up-tower, then descend 80-100 m by ladder or service lift and start the turbine from the base controller, verifying it runs.

Restart after a fault that tripped protective devices: open switchgear/converter cabinets, reset tripped breakers, thermal overloads or protection relays, confirm hydraulic pressure, oil level and pitch/yaw readiness, then reset the controller and restart, staying to watch whether the fault recurs on the first production cycle.

Sequential restarts of many turbines after a site-wide event (grid outage, storm ride-through, icing shutdown, curtailment lift): technician drives farm gravel roads in cold/wind/snow, enters each tower, performs a local reset and start, and confirms production before moving to the next turbine.

First start at commissioning or after a major overhaul (gearbox, generator, converter, blade change), including offshore units reached by crew-transfer vessel: run the controller start-up and functional test sequence (yaw, pitch, brake, lubrication, converter, grid connection), verify parameters and protection settings, coordinate with the control centre/grid operator, and sign the turbine back into operation.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: starting an industrial machine from its operator control panel and confirming it runs. Same objects (industrial pushbuttons/selectors on a fixed panel), same precision and forces, and the same acceptance criterion (machine comes up and runs), which is what a turbine restart at a fixtured base controller requires.

tasks.label: Climb wind turbine towers to inspect, maintain, or repair equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled periodic service on an onshore utility-scale turbine: technician ascends 80–100 m inside the tower (ladder with climb assist or service lift) carrying tools and consumables, then performs the service checklist in the nacelle — torque/tension checks on structural bolts, greasing bearings and yaw/pitch drives, gearbox oil sampling and filter changes, brake pad and hose checks, cable and slip-ring inspection, cleaning, and function tests before returning the unit to service.

Unscheduled fault call on an onshore turbine: technician climbs to nacelle/hub to troubleshoot an electrical, hydraulic or mechanical fault (pitch motor or battery, yaw drive, sensor, contactor, hydraulic hose, converter fan), diagnoses with meters and OEM software in cramped nacelle space, removes and replaces the failed component, and resets/restarts the turbine, often in cold, hot or windy conditions.

External blade condition inspection: getting close-up eyes on all three blade surfaces (leading-edge erosion, gelcoat cracks, lightning-strike damage, receptor continuity) and producing a documented, severity-graded report — traditionally by climbing to the nacelle and descending each blade on ropes.

External blade surface repair: technician climbs to the nacelle and works on ropes down the blade to sand, fill, fair and coat leading-edge erosion, apply LEP tape/coating, patch minor laminate damage, or repair lightning receptors, with photo documentation of each stage.

Offshore turbine access and up-tower work: transfer from a CTV/SOV to the boat landing, climb the external access ladder to the platform, ascend the tower by ladder or service lift, then perform inspection, servicing or repair in the nacelle/tower within a weather-limited work window.

Tower-internal structural and safety inspection performed during the climb: checking and marking flange bolt torque at each tower section, inspecting ladder, fall-arrest rail, climb assist and service lift, platforms, power/communication cabling, lighting and downtower cabinets, and documenting findings.

tasks.label: Maintain tool and spare parts inventories required for repair, installation, or replacement services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift restocking of the service truck/van at the wind farm O&M building: tech reads the day's work orders, picks hand tools, torque tooling, hydraulic hose, filters, grease cartridges, fasteners, rags, consumables and PPE from storeroom shelves and bins, checks them off, and loads them (including heavy items) into the truck bed/van racks in the yard.

Periodic cycle count / physical inventory audit of the site storeroom: walking racks and bins, scanning barcodes or counting small parts (bearings, brushes, relays, bolts, filters), identifying shortages and discrepancies, and reconciling counts against the CMMS/inventory system so reorder points trigger.

Receiving inbound deliveries at the O&M building: unloading palletized and cased freight (oil drums, filter cases, crated pitch motors, cable spools) from a delivery truck with a forklift, verifying items against the packing list, putting stock away in racks and bins, and updating inventory records.

Tool crib upkeep: issuing/returning shared tools, checking torque wrenches and hydraulic tensioners for calibration due dates, inspecting slings, harnesses and power tools for damage, tagging out and sending defective/out-of-calibration tools for service, and replenishing consumable tooling.

Stocking and retrieving spares up-tower: carrying tool bags, spare parts and consumables into the tower, up the ladder or service lift 80-100 m to the nacelle, stocking down-tower/nacelle storage, and bringing used parts, oil containers and scrap back down for return or disposal.

tasks.label: Test structures, controls, or mechanical, hydraulic, or electrical systems, according to test plans or in coordination with engineers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled semiannual/annual service visit at an operating onshore wind farm: technician climbs the tower and runs the OEM functional test procedure on controls and safety systems — emergency-stop and safety-chain checks, brake and overspeed tests, yaw and pitch function tests, sensor/limit-switch verification — actuating controls in the nacelle, hub and down-tower cabinet with a service laptop, and logging pass/fail results.

Electrical system testing and diagnostics per test procedure or engineer instruction: insulation-resistance (megger) and continuity tests on generator windings, converter and tower cables, voltage/current and phase measurements in switchgear and converter cabinets, lightning-protection continuity checks, and thermographic scans of terminations, with results reported to engineering.

Hydraulic and mechanical testing: pressurizing and cycling pitch/brake hydraulic circuits, accumulator pre-charge and leak-down tests, pressure-switch setpoint verification, bolt torque/tension verification on flanges and bearings, vibration measurements and oil sampling on gearbox/main bearing — performed in the confined nacelle or hub of an erected turbine.

Commissioning or end-of-warranty test campaign on a newly erected or transferred turbine, executed with OEM/owner engineers: power-up sequence, grid connection and protection function tests, sensor calibration, controller parameter verification, run-up and power performance checks, with documented test records the owner accepts.

Structural condition testing per an inspection plan: full external blade survey (leading edge erosion, cracks, lightning damage), tower and nacelle exterior condition, damage classification and reporting to blade engineers for repair planning — at an onshore or offshore wind farm, weather permitting.

sources.system: DyNaLab (Dynamic Nacelle Testing Laboratory), CertBench project
sources.title: How accurately can system test benches simulate the conditions of field tests?
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IWES's DyNaLab dynamic nacelle test bench holds a complete multi-MW nacelle (including main and converter control systems) fixtured on a dynamometer with a hardware-in-the-loop rotor model and a 36 kV grid simulator, and machine-generated grid-fault sequences are applied to test the turbine's electrical and control behaviour for certification.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content as the worker's control/electrical function testing (grid-fault response, protection and controller behaviour per a test plan), performed on the same hardware, but with the nacelle fixtured in a purpose-built rig instead of erected on a tower.

sources.system: Sany 35 MW wind turbine test bench
sources.title: Test Bench for 35 MW Wind Turbines Goes Into Operation in China
sources.claim: A full-scale wind turbine test bench capable of testing turbines up to 35 MW, simulating full-lifecycle operating loads on the assembled drivetrain, entered operation at Sany Renewable Energy's wind power testing centre.
sources.transferJustification: Machine-applied load and function testing of complete turbine drivetrains is the same mechanical testing the technician performs on an erected turbine, with the work brought to a purpose-built rig.

sources.system: Marposs / e.d.c. electrical test systems for e-motors and stators
sources.title: Electrical tests: Partial Discharge Measurements for Insulation Quality | Marposs
sources.claim: Marposs supplies in-line and end-of-line electrical test stations for electric machines that run insulation-resistance, dielectric-strength (hi-pot), surge and partial-discharge tests automatically on the production line and judge the result.
sources.transferJustification: The worker's electrical test set (insulation resistance, continuity, hi-pot on generator windings and cables) is the identical measurement suite; here it is executed automatically on fixtured machines in a production cell.

tasks.label: Train end-users, distributors, installers, or other technicians in wind commissioning, testing, or other technical procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Site-office or trailer classroom session at a wind farm: a lead technician briefs new hires and contractors on commissioning checklists, torque specs, lockout/tagout, and OEM service bulletins using slides, manuals, and Q&A. Output is trained personnel who can sign off on procedures; no workpiece is handled.

Hands-on walkthrough inside a nacelle or down-tower cabinet on an operating turbine: an experienced tech demonstrates a procedure (bolt torque/tension sequence, converter or pitch-system test, sensor calibration) to one or two junior techs, explaining each step, then observes and corrects their attempt. Purpose is instruction, not completing the repair.

OEM or third-party training-center course for customers, owner-operator staff, distributors, or installers, using mock drivetrains, cutaway gearboxes, and simulator/SCADA benches; instructor delivers curriculum, assesses trainees, and issues competency sign-offs.

Remote coaching and virtual instruction: phone, video call, or shared-screen sessions walking installers or site techs through fault-code diagnosis, SCADA/HMI navigation, commissioning software steps, and documentation of test results.

Safety, climb, and rescue instruction (GWO-style refreshers, tower evacuation and rescue drills, arc-flash/electrical safety) delivered at a training tower or on-site, including verbal briefing, demonstration of technique, and evaluation of trainee performance.

tasks.label: Collect turbine data for testing or research and analysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine condition-data round on turbine ground-level and tower-base equipment at an operating wind farm: walk/drive the site, capture visual and thermal images of pad-mount transformers, converter/switchgear cabinets, and the down-tower controller, log gauge readings and audible anomalies, and upload to the fleet analysis system.

Up-tower data collection during a scheduled service visit: climb/lift to the nacelle and hub, take vibration and temperature readings on the main bearing, gearbox and generator, thermal-scan nacelle electrical cabinets and connections, borescope gearbox internals through inspection ports, and photograph/record findings for engineering analysis.

Blade and external structure condition data on operating turbines: high-resolution imagery (and sometimes thermography) of all four blade faces, tower exterior and nacelle skin, collected from the ground or by drone at an onshore or offshore wind farm, then delivered to the blade-engineering analysis platform.

Turbine controller/SCADA data retrieval and electrical diagnostic measurement at the turbine: open the controller cabinet, connect a service laptop or diagnostic instrument, download fault logs and high-frequency records, run functional tests (e.g., insulation resistance, power quality, pitch/yaw parameter capture), and export data for analysis.

Fluid and debris sampling for laboratory analysis: draw gearbox oil, hydraulic fluid or grease samples through sample valves/ports up-tower into labelled bottles, collect filter debris, avoid contamination, and ship to the oil-analysis lab.

Test/research instrumentation work on prototype or test turbines: surface-prep and bond strain gauges and accelerometers, mount met/anemometry or nacelle lidar instruments, route and terminate cabling to data loggers, calibrate, then retrieve loggers and data for the research campaign.

tasks.label: Inspect or repair fiberglass turbine blades.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled external blade condition inspection at an operating onshore wind farm: capture full-surface imagery of all three fiberglass blades of an erected turbine (historically by ground optics, uptower/rope access, now commonly drone), identify and size erosion, cracks, gelcoat damage, and produce a damage report with severity categories for the asset owner.

Leading-edge erosion / surface repair on an erected onshore turbine blade: technician descends by rope access or suspended platform, removes old tape/coating, sands and cleans the eroded leading edge, applies filler and leading-edge protection coating, sands smooth, and documents the repair.

Structural laminate repair at height on an erected blade: grind out a crack, hole, delamination or lightning-strike tip damage to a scarfed area, lay up multiple fiberglass plies with resin, vacuum bag and heat cure, then fill, sand and paint to restore the aerodynamic surface, working from ropes or a platform in variable wind.

Internal blade inspection: technician climbs the tower, enters the hub and the blade root cavity (or deploys a tethered crawler from the root), inspects bond lines, shear web, spar cap and lightning down-conductor for cracks/debonds, and reports findings; occasional small internal patching or receptor/conductor fixes.

Offshore turbine blade inspection or surface repair: access by crew transfer vessel to an offshore wind farm, blade imagery capture and damage assessment (drone or rope access), with weather-window constraints and vessel/platform logistics.

Blade inspection or repair with the blade on the ground: incoming/pre-installation inspection of blades in the laydown yard, or a blade removed and repaired in a service workshop — grinding, laminating, filling, sanding, painting a fiberglass shell that is supported on stands.

tasks.label: Assist in assembly of individual wind generators or construction of wind farms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tower erection support at an onshore wind farm under construction: rigging tower sections and holding tag lines while a crawler crane lifts, guiding and aligning the flanges, then installing and hydraulically tensioning/torquing several hundred large flange bolts inside the tower at height, in wind, dust and cold, with torque documentation.

Making up the major bolted joints of the drivetrain/rotor during erection: blade-root studs into the hub, hub/main-shaft and yaw-flange connections, using hydraulic torque and tensioning tools on hundreds of high-tensile studs to specified preload, partly on the ground in the laydown area and partly up-tower.

Tower internal fit-out and electrical work during construction: pulling and securing power and control cables down the tower, fitting cable clamps, ladders, platforms and the service lift, landing and torquing MV cable lugs and busbars in the down-tower switchgear/converter cabinets, connecting sensors and grounding.

Materials and logistics support at the site laydown yard: unloading trucks, uncrating and staging hardware kits, bolts, consumables and tools, moving pallets with a telehandler, keeping the staging area organized and feeding the erection crew.

Mechanical completion / punch-list work before commissioning: verifying and paint-marking bolt torque, greasing bearings, topping up gearbox and hydraulic fluids, wiping and chasing small leaks, fitting missing hardware and covers, cleaning the nacelle and tower base.

Assembly assistance inside a manufacturer's plant or a service shop: helping build turbine subassemblies (blade bearings bolted to hubs, generator rotor magnets and stator bolting, drivetrain modules) or assembling small wind generators on a plant floor with fixtures and overhead cranes.

tasks.label: Fill machines with products, ingredients, money, and other supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Route stop at an office/factory/school breakroom bank of machines: unlock the snack and drink machines, load bagged chips, candy bars, pastries into spiral trays per planogram, load cans/bottles into stacks, rotate dated stock, refill the coin changer with coins, pull bills from the validator, close and lock.

Beverage-only merchandiser/glass-front cooler machine at a high-volume cashless account (cafeteria, hospital, transit hub): cases of bottles and cans are delivered to the site and loaded into the machine's ordered rows/stacks, facings straightened, dates rotated.

Hot-beverage/coffee machine service in an office breakroom or convenience-store kiosk: refill canisters with ground coffee/beans, powdered creamer, sugar, cocoa; reload cup stacks, lids, stir sticks, syrup bags; top up water/filter supplies.

Arcade/family entertainment center: fill crane-claw cabinets with plush prizes, capsule machines with capsules, redemption prize cases with merchandise, load ticket/receipt paper rolls, and fill token/change dispensers with tokens, coins and bills.

Casino floor or bank/retail money machine: perform currency fills - load note cassettes/recyclers in slot machines, bill changers or ATMs, top up coin hoppers, load TITO ticket paper - under strict count and security procedure.

Machines at uncontrolled sites: gas-station forecourt, laundromat, apartment laundry room, roadside or park kiosk, construction trailer - restock product and coins with weather exposure, cramped or cluttered access, and no institutional housekeeping.

sources.system: TX SCARA (Telexistence, with NVIDIA-based 'GORDON' AI)
sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated shelves with bottled and ... in convenience stores, deployed commercially at 300 FamilyMart stores, with remote human takeover only for rare error cases.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restocking a refrigerated beverage display case. Transfer to filling a beverage vending machine is close - identical objects (cans/PET bottles from cases), same act of placing product into ordered rows/columns in a chilled cabinet, in a comparable institution-controlled retail facility.

sources.system: TX Ghost
sources.title: Telexistence Wins the Prime Minister's Award at the Japan Startup Awards 2025
sources.claim: Telexistence's successor robot TX Ghost is reported to have automated the majority of beverage ... work in convenience stores, with service expansion to 7-Eleven pilot stores in Tokyo in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as TX SCARA: filling a chilled beverage cabinet with cans and bottles, which is the physical content of restocking a drink vending machine at a fixed account.

sources.system: Vulcan
sources.title: Amazon's Vulcan robot uses force sensing to stow items
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously stows and picks a wide variety of consumer items into and out of tightly packed fabric pod compartments roughly a foot square in fulfillment centers, handling about 75% of stored item types at human-comparable speed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stowing packaged retail goods into small, crowded compartments. Loading snack bags, candy and small packages into vending trays/spiral pockets involves the same objects, similar insertion precision and force sensitivity, in a purpose-built cell where the storage unit is presented to the robot.

sources.system: Vulcan
sources.title: Amazon Unveils Vulcan, Its First Robot With a True Sense of Touch
sources.claim: Vulcan is operating in Amazon fulfillment centers in ..., having processed more than 500,000 items.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes real deployment (not a demo) of robotic insertion of varied packaged goods into small compartments in a purpose-built facility, the E1 counterfactual for loading vending trays.

sources.system: PKR Delta / PKR-Dual robotic case packer
sources.title: Robotic Packaging Machines | Robotic Systems by Paxiom
sources.claim: Commercial delta-robot case packing cells autonomously pick flexible snack packages - stand-up pouches, lay-flat bags, cups - and load them into cases and trays at high speed on production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading bagged snack products into compartmented trays. Same objects (chip/candy bags) and same placement precision as loading vending spiral trays when the tray is fixtured and product is presented, i.e. the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Automatic auger filler (bottle/jar/tin)
sources.title: Auger Fillers Dry Powder Filling Machine Manufacturer | VTOPS
sources.claim: Automatic auger filling machines fill dry powders and granulates into rigid containers such as bottles, cans and jars conveyed through the filling station, without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dosing coffee, creamer, sugar and cocoa powders into rigid containers. A vending machine's ingredient canister, when removed and presented on a conveyor as a purpose-built line would present it, is the same filling operation with the same materials.

sources.system: NotaTray Loading module for BPS M banknote processing systems
sources.title: Automation Solutions for Cash Management | G+D
sources.claim: G+D's cash-center automation includes a module that uses a robotic gripper to load banknotes into banknote processing systems, buffering up to 40,000 notes for continuous unattended operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled loading of currency into a machine's note containers in a cash center. Filling a bill validator/recycler cassette or coin hopper at E1 - cassette fixtured, money presented in bulk - is the same class of automated cash handling.

sources.system: RightPick / RightPick2
sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick systems autonomously pick mixed-SKU items, including poly-bagged goods, from totes and place them into designated cubbies/compartments in commercial fulfillment operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking varied retail merchandise, including poly-bagged soft goods, into open compartments. Filling claw-machine bins, capsule hoppers and prize cases with plush/poly-bagged prizes uses the same objects and far looser placement tolerance, when the cabinet is presented to the cell.

tasks.label: Inspect machines and meters to determine causes of malfunctions and fix minor problems such as jammed bills or stuck products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Route service call on a bank of snack/beverage vending machines in an office, school or hospital break room: technician responds to a no-vend/stuck-product report, unlocks and swings open the cabinet, watches a test vend, finds the product hung on a misaligned coil or against the glass, frees it, adjusts the coil/spacer, closes and re-tests.

Cash-handling fault on a vending, laundry, car-wash or kiosk machine (laundromat, gas station, apartment laundry room): technician opens the machine, pulls the bill validator head or coin mech, extracts a crumpled/jammed note or bent coin from the transport path, cleans sensor lenses and belts, reseats the stacker, then runs the validator test and verifies acceptance of several bills and coins.

Casino floor slot/video gaming machine fault: technician opens the main door with a key, reads the error/tilt code on the display or meters, diagnoses a jammed TITO ticket printer, stuck bill acceptor or hopper, clears the jam, reloads ticket stock, resets the machine and confirms meters and audit before returning it to play.

Amusement/arcade machine at a family entertainment center or bowling alley: crane claw not gripping, redemption ticket dispenser jammed, pinball ball trapped behind a ramp, coin door switch not registering; technician inspects the mechanism inside a game-specific cabinet, clears the obstruction, adjusts a switch or belt, and tests play.

Outdoor/public-space machines: parking meters and pay stations, coin-op air/vacuum units on a gas-station forecourt, exterior ice or newspaper vendors; technician works curbside in weather, deals with corrosion, debris, vandalism and coin jams, tests the meter, and clears or swaps the affected module.

Bench work in the operator's shop or warehouse: machines pulled from the field or being prepped for placement are inspected on the shop floor, powered up, run through diagnostics and test vends, minor faults (jammed mechanisms, sticky motors, dirty acceptors) found and corrected before redeployment.

sources.system: Spot (with Autowalk / Orbit inspection payloads)
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities — thermal imaging, gauge reading, anomaly and gas-leak detection — i.e. sensing equipment condition, but not opening machines or clearing faults.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available analogue to the 'inspect machines and meters' half of the task: Spot reads meters/gauges and flags anomalies in a facility, but the demonstrated scope is sensing only, with no cabinet opening, internal diagnosis, or jam clearing on vending/amusement machines.

sources.system: Spot Arm
sources.title: The Next Step in Safe, Autonomous Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot's manipulation is limited to constrained actions such as opening doors, turning valves and pulling levers; autonomous manipulation in missions was only extended to door opening as of late 2025, and other arm manipulation remains operator-directed/semi-autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Bounds the state of the art for autonomous mobile manipulation during inspection: opening a door is far below extracting a crumpled bill from a validator transport, freeing a product hung on a coil, or reseating a coin mech.

sources.system: Spot Arm
sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot Arm's advertised manipulation set is semi-autonomous constrained motions (valves, levers, doors, drawers) driven from a tablet interface, not autonomous fine repair of machine internals.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that even the leading fielded inspection robot's manipulation is operator-initiated and constrained, so it cannot substantiate autonomous diagnosis-and-repair of a vending, gaming or amusement machine.

sources.system: Robotic container-dispensing vending machine (patented control system)
sources.title: Vending machine container labeling and dispensing method (US 9,721,418)
sources.claim: Purpose-built robotic vending/dispensing machines are engineered to avoid jams and, when a pick fails repeatedly, hand off to a remote human agent because manual recovery is required — automation does not clear its own jams.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point for the 'stuck product' fault mode: even inside a machine designed around robotics, jam recovery is escalated to a human, indicating no cited robotic system clears such jams autonomously.

tasks.label: Test machines to determine proper functioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Snack/beverage vending machine at a customer account (office break room, school, hospital lobby): after installing, restocking or repairing, the tech runs a test cycle — inserts coins/bill, taps a card, presses selections, confirms product drops and change/refund returns, checks display messages, listens to the compressor and verifies cabinet temperature — then decides whether the machine is fit to leave in service.

Bench test in the operator's shop/warehouse: a refurbished machine, a rebuilt coin mech, bill validator, cashless reader or control board is powered up on a test stand, exercised with test coins/notes/cards and keypad commands, and passed or failed before being sent back to route.

Casino slot machine / VLT / route gaming device: after a board swap, printer, button-deck or bill-validator repair on the gaming floor, the tech inserts a test bill or ticket, cycles the game, verifies credits, meters, ticket printing and door/tilt clearing, and confirms the machine is ready for play.

Electronic amusement equipment at bars, arcades or family entertainment centers — arcade video cabinets, touchscreen countertop games, jukeboxes, ticket-redemption terminals: test coin/bill/card acceptance, boot-up, monitor and audio, control response, ticket or credit dispense.

Electromechanical amusement equipment: pinball machine, claw crane, air hockey, coin-op pool table — the tech plays or cycles the mechanism to verify flippers/solenoids, ball or prize release, scoring, playfield switches and coin drop behave correctly.

Unattended outdoor/roadside coin-op equipment: car wash bay pay station, air/vacuum machine, laundromat card/coin station, parking pay station — test payment acceptance and vend/activation output in weather, dirt and public-access conditions.

sources.system: ABB YuMi (IRB 14000) with Abrantix ATM Test Environment
sources.developer: Abrantix AG with ABB Robotics (for Diebold Nixdorf ATMs)
sources.title: ABB's YuMi® robot automates ATM testing for more reliable banking
sources.claim: A dual-arm ABB YuMi cobot running Abrantix test-environment software performs functional testing of ATMs — a cash- and card-handling self-service machine — by inserting cards, entering PINs on the keypad and withdrawing and depositing notes, running unattended overnight test cycles in the Abrantix/Diebold Nixdorf test lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: functional testing of an ATM. An ATM is the same class of coin/note/card-accepting, product(cash)-dispensing self-service machine a vending or gaming tech tests: the test consists of feeding payment media, pressing keypad/touch controls, and verifying the machine's dispense and on-screen response — the same objects, forces and millimetre-level precision as a vend or credit test.

sources.system: Abrantix EFTPOS Terminal Testing Robot (Robot T1/T4)
sources.title: EFT/POS Terminal Testing Robot | Abrantix
sources.claim: Abrantix sells a commercial three-axis payment-terminal test robot that presses keypad buttons and touchscreens, inserts and ejects cards, and uses camera OCR to validate terminal screens and printed receipts, running test suites unattended 24/7 on fixtured terminals in a QA cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-to-end functional test of unattended payment terminals (the same card readers, keypads and receipt printers built into vending, parking, car-wash and gaming machines). Verifying an accepted transaction and a printed receipt by camera is the same accept/verify judgment as a test vend or ticket-print check.

sources.system: Abrantix Robot T4
sources.title: Abrantix introduces robotic testing for payment terminals | Kiosk Marketplace
sources.claim: Trade press confirms the Abrantix payment-terminal test robot is a shipping commercial product able to test up to four terminals at once, sold into the kiosk/self-service market.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: confirms commercial maturity of robotic functional testing of unattended payment devices of the kind fitted to vending, parking and amusement machines.

sources.system: MATT (Standard/Extended/Adapt) device testing robot
sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Testing Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: MATT is a commercially sold test-automation robot that physically operates a device under test — pressing hardware buttons, switches and knobs and touching screens — and verifies proper functioning of display, touch, audio-speaker and UI state with AI computer vision against reference screens; it is used in repair/commissioning workflows, e.g. at Zebra's Repair Service Division, and runs continuous test cycles for over 72 hours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-repair functional verification of fixtured electronic equipment (Zebra scanners, HMIs, consoles). A vending/amusement/gaming machine test after service is the same act — drive the machine's buttons or touchscreen, watch the display and audio response, and issue a pass/fail — on comparable controls at comparable precision, in a bench cell.

tasks.label: Replace malfunctioning parts, such as worn magnetic heads on automatic teller machine (ATM) card readers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field repair of a vending machine at a customer site (office breakroom, school, hospital, plant, convenience store): technician unlocks and opens the cabinet door, unplugs a harness, unbolts and swaps a plug-in module such as a bill validator, coin mech, card/contactless reader, vend motor or control board, then tests a vend. Mixed makes and models, machine crowded with product, work done in a public-facing space.

Field repair of a vending or office-coffee machine requiring deeper in-cabinet work: replacing a refrigeration deck or compressor, delivery/elevator mechanism parts, door gasket or glass, water valve, tubing, or a chafed wiring harness. Confined access, heavy parts, hand tools, occasional plumbing/brazing, machine returned to service on site.

Field repair of an amusement or gaming machine on the floor of a casino, arcade, bowling alley or tavern: swapping a ticket/receipt printer, bill validator, button deck, monitor, reel or stepper motor, logic board, pinball coil or jukebox amplifier, with the machine in its cabinet among patrons and other machines.

Field service of an ATM or self-service kiosk at a bank branch, credit union or retail store: replacing a worn magnetic head or the whole card-reader module, a receipt printer, dispenser module or keypad, opening the fascia/chassis, unplugging ribbon and harness connectors, seating and aligning the new part, then running a test transaction.

Bench work in the operator's shop or repair depot: removed subassemblies (coin mechs, bill validators, card readers, hoppers, amplifier and logic boards) are disassembled on a workbench, worn parts such as heads, belts, rollers, gears, relays or board-level components are replaced, and the unit is reassembled and function-tested before going back on a route.

Repair of machines at unstructured or outdoor sites: sidewalk and gas-station vending, air/vacuum machines, car-wash bays, laundromats, carnival midway games and amusement park kiosks — weather, dirt, vandalism damage, no controlled premises, ad hoc access and power.

sources.system: Molg robotic microfactory (with ABB robots)
sources.title: ABB Robotics and US start-up Molg tackle data center e-waste with robotic microfactories
sources.claim: Molg's robotic microfactory autonomously assembles and disassembles complex electronic products (laptops, servers, industrial electronics) inside a purpose-built robotic cell, recovering components intact rather than shredding them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: non-destructive teardown/rebuild of electronic assemblies. It shares the manipulation of this task's bench work — removing fasteners and covers, extracting a module or component from a fixtured device and re-fitting parts — at similar scale and precision, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Molg robots at AWS reverse logistics facility
sources.title: Amazon's AWS hardware reuse is measured — Resource Recycling / E-Scrap News
sources.claim: AWS deployed Molg's AI-powered robots at its reverse-logistics facility in 2025, where they disassemble server equipment into components for ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: component-level teardown of used electronic hardware. Shows the microfactory cell working on real, worn field-returned units in production, which is the disassembly half of replacing a worn part on a fixtured bench unit.

sources.system: Tianxun (second generation) data center O&M robot
sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center — Data Center Dynamics
sources.claim: Alibaba Cloud's second-generation Tianxun robot autonomously locates and replaces faulty hard disks in operating data centers, with the inspection-locate-replace cycle done without human intervention; the system is in operation at five data centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replacing a failed part in a machine inside a human work facility. It shows autonomous swap of a rack-mounted, tool-free hot-swap module only; it does not involve unlocking cabinets, hand-tool fasteners, harness connectors or fine alignment as this task's parts do.

sources.system: PCBA robotic rework cell (University of Salford)
sources.developer: University of Salford (Aeronautical and Mechanical Engineering Dept.)
sources.title: Automated removal and replacement of through-hole components in robotic rework (IEEE)
sources.claim: A fully automated, autonomous robotic rework cell was developed that removes a defective through-hole/surface-mount component from a printed circuit board and installs a replacement, using vision guidance, board cleaning, solder paste dispensing, component placement and laser soldering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: board-level defective-part removal and replacement. Same core act as this task's bench work (extract a worn component from a fixtured assembly, fit and solder a new one) at equal or finer precision, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing system for e-waste disassembly
sources.developer: academic team, published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing — ScienceDirect
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic system using a UR10e arm, RealSense depth camera and a custom mechatronic screwdriver locates, identifies and removes screws to disassemble electronic devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fastener removal on used electronic devices — the opening step needed before a worn part (e.g. a card-reader magnetic head) can be swapped on a fixtured bench unit.

sources.system: Recirculate robotic battery disassembly cell
sources.developer: Centria University of Applied Sciences (EU Recirculate project)
sources.title: Recirculate tests AI-driven robotic system for EV battery disassembly — electrive.com
sources.claim: A purpose-built robotic cell built around a KUKA KR10 on a linear track autonomously detects, unscrews and removes components, including connectors and wiring, from high-voltage EV battery packs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous removal of bolted, cabled components from a large used assembly in a purpose-built cell — the closest published analogue to pulling a harness-connected module out of a machine, though demonstrated only on one pack family and only for removal, not refitting.

tasks.label: Clean and oil machine parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Route service of snack/beverage vending machines on customer premises (office break room, school, hospital, factory canteen): open the cabinet, wipe out spills and product debris, clean the coin mechanism coin paths and bill-validator belts/sensors with cloth and brush, clear the delivery chute, brush/vacuum condenser coils, and apply light oil or grease to vend-motor gears, door hinges, latches and slides.

Arcade and amusement equipment at a family entertainment center, bar, or bowling center: deep-clean pinball playfields and ball tracks, clean coin doors, crane cable guides, ticket-dispenser and card-reader paths, then lubricate flipper bushings, crane gantry rails, pool-table ball returns, and jukebox mechanisms with the specified oil or grease.

Bench refurbishment in the operator's shop or warehouse: a machine or removed subassembly (coin mech, bill acceptor, hopper, vend motor gearbox, dryer blower) is disassembled at a bench, parts are degreased/washed in a solvent or parts washer, dried, then re-oiled and greased before reassembly.

Casino slot machine / electronic gaming device service on the floor or in the casino's tech shop: clean bill-validator transport paths, coin hoppers, ticket printer path and button deck of dust, coin residue and lint, and lubricate sliding drawer rails, latches, and printer/hopper mechanisms per the manufacturer's PM schedule while adhering to gaming-regulator procedures.

Semi-public and weather-exposed coin equipment: laundromat washer/dryer coin slides and drives, car-wash and air/water vending, ice merchandisers, storefront kiddie rides. Heavy grime, corrosion, lint, sand and moisture; equipment sits as found in an entryway, parking lot, or sidewalk with cramped access and no controlled conditions.

sources.system: Blackstone-NEY / Cleaning Technologies Group 'Robosonic' robotic ultrasonic cleaning cell (Fanuc CR-7i)
sources.title: Ultrasonic Robotic Parts Cleaning Cell Provides Precision Cleaning and Maximum Efficiency
sources.claim: A commercially offered robotic parts-cleaning cell uses a Fanuc CR-7i collaborative robot to move small parts (up to 15 lb) through spray wash, ultrasonic immersion wash, rinse and dry stages inside a purpose-built four-tank enclosure, optionally with force sensing and integrated vision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precision industrial parts cleaning. It transfers to 'clean machine parts' because the objects are the same class and scale as vending/amusement machine subassemblies (small metal and plastic mechanisms under 15 lb) and the soils (oil, dust, residue) are comparable; only the E1 counterfactual presentation (parts fixtured and fed to the cell) differs from bench work.

sources.system: Better Engineering RTO-2000 parts washer in a robotic work cell
sources.title: Parts Washer for Robotic Work Cell – Case Study 22090
sources.claim: An aerospace manufacturer runs a two-chamber jet parts washer integrated into an existing robotic work cell, where one robot loads and unloads ... washer as well as machining centers, running a four-stage wash/rinse/fresh-rinse/dry cycle on production components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated degreasing/washing of machined parts. It substantiates the cleaning half of this task at E1 because the robot itself presents and retrieves the workpieces and the cell reaches an inspected production-quality cleanliness standard, i.e. an accepted output rather than a demo.

sources.system: Stäubli TX90 HE / TX200 HE washing-cleaning robots
sources.title: Robotic solutions for washing-cleaning parts | Stäubli United States
sources.claim: Stäubli TX90 HE washing robots were integrated into automated washing lines for Hyundai engine ... in South Korea, handling high-pressure waterjet cleaning of engine components in continuous production; other integrators use Stäubli HE robots for deburring and cleaning vehicle ... in wet spray areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic washing/cleaning of greasy mechanical assemblies. Transfers because engine components carry heavier oil/grease and swarf soils than vending or amusement mechanisms, and the robot manipulates either the workpiece or the cleaning tool, which is the same manipulation pattern as wiping/spraying a machine part.

sources.system: DOPAG automated lubricant (grease) dispensing system on an industrial robot
sources.title: Automated grease dispensing system for automotive industry | DOPAG
sources.claim: At a European automotive company an industrial robot fitted with two needle dispensing valves applies two different greases to several defined points, including hard-to-reach areas, on automotive components in production, with shot quantity controlled and documented.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic lubricant application in assembly. It substantiates the 'oil' half of this task at E1: applying metered oil/grease to specified points on a fixtured mechanism is the same act a servicer performs on vend-motor gears, rails and hinges, at equal or finer precision.

sources.system: FANUC Paint Mate robotic parts washing system (Prime Test Automation); FANUC M-20iB/25 robotic finishing cell (AV&R)
sources.developer: FANUC America with integrators Prime Test Automation and AV&R
sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC lists a production parts-washing system in which a Paint Mate robot washes and repositions parts inside a sealed stainless-steel enclosure, alongside robotic polishing, blending and deburring cells for surface finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic washing and robotic surface finishing/polishing. Transfers to cleaning flat and shaped surfaces such as playfields, coin doors and cabinet panels, since the robot both manipulates the part and guides a tool over its surface to a specified finish.

tasks.label: Adjust and repair coin, vending, or amusement machines and meters and replace defective mechanical and electrical parts, using hand tools, soldering irons, and diagrams.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field service call on a snack/beverage vending machine in an office, school, hospital or plant break room: open the cabinet, use the fault code and wiring diagram to find the problem, replace or adjust a vend motor, coin mechanism, bill validator, relay, gum-and-nut spiral, or refrigeration fan, reassemble, test-vend, and clean up around the customer's staff.

Amusement machine repair on location in a bar, bowling center, arcade or restaurant: jukebox, crane/redemption game, dart board, pool table or pinball — replace worn mechanical linkages, switches, coin door parts and lamps, solder broken harness/connector joints, adjust playfield mechanisms, and verify play, often in tight, cluttered spaces during business hours.

Bench/shop repair at the operator's warehouse: rebuild coin mechanisms and hoppers pulled from route machines, repair removed control or game boards with a soldering iron and schematics (replace capacitors, connectors, relays, ICs), refurbish and bench-test the assembly before it goes back out.

Casino or route gaming floor: repair a slot/VLT machine — swap a bill validator or ticket printer, reseat or replace a harness, button deck, reel motor or power supply, adjust the door and mechanism, then verify with test modes under gaming-compliance rules while patrons are present.

Outdoor/street equipment: parking meters on a public sidewalk, laundromat washers/dryers, car-wash and air-vacuum coin boxes — replace a meter mechanism, coin canister, battery or damaged card reader, repair vandalism damage, adjust the coin path, in weather and with pedestrians and traffic nearby.

sources.system: Panasonic robotic appliance disassembly cell (Disassembly CPS)
sources.title: Panasonic Turns To AI Robots To Pull Apart Old Appliances – channelnews
sources.claim: Panasonic is programming six-axis robots in a workcell to disassemble end-of-life appliances (air conditioners, microwaves, washing machines) using screwdrivers, grippers and cutting end-effectors — the closest robotic work to opening up and stripping parts from a consumer machine, but it is destructive disassembly for recycling, with no diagnosis, part replacement, reassembly or functional test.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of appliances. It shares tool use (screwdrivers) and cabinet-opening motions with vending/amusement machine repair, but it is one-way teardown of known models in a fixtured cell; it does not substantiate fault-directed part replacement, adjustment, reassembly and test.

sources.system: Ersa HR 600 P / HR 600 XL hybrid rework system
sources.title: Ersa Rework System HR 600 P
sources.claim: Commercial hybrid rework systems (Ersa HR 600 P/XL) automatically desolder a defective SMD/BGA, remove residual solder and place and resolder a replacement on a board clamped in the machine — an automated version of one sub-step of bench board repair, performed only after a human identifies the defective component, loads and clamps the board and selects the process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated SMT board rework. It covers the desolder/replace/resolder step on a fixtured PCB, but not diagnosis with diagrams, mechanical adjustment, disassembly/reassembly of the machine, or functional verification, so it cannot complete a whole repair instance.

sources.system: Tesla Optimus (and comparable factory humanoids)
sources.title: Will Humanoid Robots Replace Hand Soldering?
sources.claim: As of mid-2026, humanoid robots deployed in factories are limited to material handling, and trade coverage of soldering states that neither humanoids nor specialized machines are close to replacing technicians doing diagnostic, adaptive hand soldering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hand soldering and adaptive tool use. Repairing vending/amusement machines requires the same diagnostic, adaptive manipulation and soldering; the source indicates current robots cannot perform it at technician quality.
