instances.label: Vending route stop at an institutional account (office break room, school cafeteria, hospital, factory lunchroom): unlock each snack/beverage machine with a route key during business hours, pull the bill validator stacker and coin box, insert empties, read DEX/meter data, bag the cash, and leave or file a collection/commission slip; several machines per stop, people walking through.

Route stop at a small retail business (convenience store, gas station, laundromat, apartment laundry room): open machines or changers, remove bills and quarters, verify counts against meters, and hand the owner a printed or written invoice/commission statement for the location's share.

Amusement route stop in a bar, tavern, restaurant, or bowling center: open the coin door of a jukebox, pool table, dart or crane machine, bag coins and bills, count the take on the spot with the location owner, split revenue (often 50/50) in cash, and write the invoice/settlement receipt.

Casino slot floor drop and count: under camera surveillance, remove bill-validator cassettes/drop boxes from electronic gaming machines into a secure cart, transport them to the count room, unlock and empty each box, count and sort the notes/tickets, and reconcile totals against machine meters with the required paperwork.

Outdoor and unattended equipment: curbside parking meters/pay stations, car wash bays, air and vacuum machines, standalone changers; weather exposure, coin canisters heavy with quarters, collection on public sidewalks or open lots with pedestrians and vehicles present.

Back-office/commissary settlement: bring route bags into the money room, count and sort coin and currency, reconcile collections against machine meter and telemetry data, prepare invoices and commission statements, and settle accounts with location concessionaires.

sources.system: ICB ASAP (Intelligent Cash Box with Automated Secure Asset Processing)
sources.title: JCM looking to capitalize on robotic automation in the count room — CDC Gaming
sources.claim: JCM Global's ICB ASAP is a network of four industrial robots in an enclosed automation cell that scans a locked cash box placed on an inbound conveyor, reads its data, unlocks and opens it, removes the bank notes/tickets with a robotic hand, verifies the box is empty, then locks and returns it — performing the cash-extraction and audit-record steps of a collection with the box presented to the machine.

sources.system: ICB ASAP
sources.title: ICB ASAP Product Sheet (JCM Global)
sources.claim: JCM's product documentation states the cell operates with a single operator who only loads locked cash boxes onto the inbound conveyor; the robots orient, unlock and open the box, read and record the cash box data and asset number, remove the contents to a shuttle/tray, verify the box is empty, lock it and return it, with trays going to a count-sort machine.

sources.system: ICB ASAP
sources.title: MotorCity Casino Hotel celebrates ICB ASAP milestone — InterGame
sources.claim: The ICB ASAP cell has been in production use at MotorCity Casino Hotel in Detroit since October 2023, processing well over 180,000 cash boxes per year at up to 240 boxes/hour, establishing reliability and throughput at worker-acceptable quality inside a purpose-built enclosed cell.

sources.system: JetSort 6000 coin sorter/counter
sources.title: JetSort 6000 | CPI
sources.claim: High-speed commercial coin sorters/counters count and sort mixed coin at up to 10,000 coins per ... and export totals to attached printers/computers, covering the coin-counting and totalling portion of a route collection once coin is fed into the hopper.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk coin processing. Route collections are mixed US coin identical to what these machines process, and the machine produces the counted totals the servicer records on the collection report.

sources.system: Physical Intelligence robot (Robot Olympics key/lock task)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: Robotic key insertion and turning — the enabling skill for opening a machine's locked coin door on site — exists only as short lab demonstrations with no transfer to new locks, about 5x slower than a human and around 52% average task reliability, so no cited system can unlock and service machines at their installed locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unlocking with a key. Cited to bound on-site (E2/E3) capability, since opening a machine's locked cash door is the first step of every collection instance and remains at demo maturity.

sources.system: Seed Pro / Seed Delivery vending management system
sources.title: Seed Pro | Vending Management System | Cantaloupe
sources.claim: Vending management systems automatically generate collection, commission and invoicing paperwork from machine telemetry/DEX data, covering the non-physical invoice-preparation and account-settlement portion of the task.
sources.transferJustification: Software, not a robotic system; cited only for the non-physical invoicing/settlement sub-step, never as the basis of a physical-capability judgment.

tasks.label: Make service calls to maintain and repair machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Break-room vending service call at an office, school, hospital or plant: tech drives the route van to the account, unlocks the snack/beverage machine, diagnoses a reported fault (product hang-up, coil motor failure, bill validator or coin mech rejecting money, door switch, refrigeration not cooling), swaps the failed module or part from van stock, reassembles, test-vends with cash/card, cleans and restocks, and logs the call.

Scheduled preventive-maintenance / route maintenance stop across several accounts: inspect multiple machines, clean coin mechanisms and bill acceptors, vacuum condenser coils and change filters, adjust vend motors and delivery doors, update prices and card readers/firmware, check refrigeration temperatures, tighten and lubricate, and note parts to order.

Casino gaming-floor service call: respond to a slot machine tilt/error, unlock the main door with logged keys, clear a ticket printer or bill validator jam, replace a printer, button deck, reel motor or power supply, verify game and meters, clear the error under surveillance, and complete regulatory paperwork with a patron often waiting.

Amusement/arcade and redemption game repair at a family entertainment center, bowling alley, movie theater or bar: troubleshoot a ticket dispenser, ball/target sensor, monitor, pinball solenoid, joystick harness, jukebox or claw machine; board-level swap or mechanical adjustment, often on a busy floor during operating hours.

Coin-op service call in an uncontrolled or semi-public location: apartment-building laundry room, campground, car-wash bay air/vacuum machine, kiddie ride or gumball/crane machine at a storefront; cramped or outdoor conditions, vandalism or water damage, no on-site staff, variable access and lighting.

Installation or major on-site repair requiring machine handling: uncrate and place a new machine or swap out a failed one at a gym, hotel or convenience store, move it through doorways with a hand truck, level it, connect power/water/network, program planogram and payment device, then test.

sources.system: Tianxun (2nd generation) data center robot
sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD
sources.claim: Alibaba's second-generation Tianxun data-center robot autonomously inspects racks, locates a failed hard disk and replaces it in about four minutes; claimed in operation at five Alibaba data centers. This is the closest deployed analog to an autonomous 'maintenance service call' (fault localization plus modular part replacement) I could find, and it is confined to one standardized hot-swap component in racks designed for robotic access.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous replacement of a failed component in a machine at a customer facility. It does not transfer to this task: Tianxun handles a single standardized hot-swap sled in racks engineered for robotic servicing, with fault location supplied by server telemetry, whereas a vending/amusement service call requires unlocking and opening varied cabinets, electrical/mechanical diagnosis of unreported faults, harness and refrigeration work, and functional test-vending.

sources.system: TX SCARA
sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA is deployed in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores restocking refrigerated shelves with bottles ..., running mostly autonomously with remote human takeover for the small fraction of failures. It shows deployed autonomous manipulation of standardized retail items inside a human-run facility, but performs no diagnosis or repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restocking beverages in a chilled display, which resembles the product-filling portion of a vending maintenance stop. It does not substantiate this task, because TX SCARA is a fixed rail-mounted arm installed in one cooler and never opens, diagnoses, disassembles, or repairs the machine it serves.

sources.system: Digit
sources.title: Humanoid Robotics In 2026: The Race From Pilot To Platform - KraneShares
sources.claim: The most capable mobile humanoids in commercial operation as of 2026 are doing tote and material handling in warehouses, not diagnostic repair of machines; Digit is deployed in fulfillment center operations moving totes between AMRs and conveyors.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize the frontier of deployed mobile manipulation in human work facilities: repetitive tote transfer, not tool use, fastener removal, fault diagnosis or component-level repair. It therefore does not support completion of any service-call instance at any tier.

tasks.label: Adjust machine pressure gauges and thermostats.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refrigerated snack/beverage vending machine on route in an institutional break room, school or hospital cafeteria: customer reports warm or frozen product; tech unlocks the T-handle, probes product/cabinet temperature, then turns the mechanical thermostat dial or resets the electronic controller setpoint inside the crowded cabinet and verifies pull-down before leaving.

Office-coffee-service hot beverage vending machine in a small office kitchen: adjust brew-water thermostat or boiler pressostat to spec, read the boiler pressure gauge, and set the inlet water pressure regulator; work done with the front door swung open in a narrow space with counters and people nearby.

Post-mix / bulk cold beverage equipment at a vending or amusement location (convenience store, bar or arcade back room): set CO2 regulator and carbonator/water pressure by turning regulator knobs while watching the analog gauges, and adjust the ice-bank or cold-plate thermostat.

Machine sited in an uncontrolled location - laundromat, apartment laundry room, gas-station forecourt, outdoor kiosk or mom-and-pop storefront: cramped against walls, cluttered, ambient temperature extremes; tech adjusts the cold-vend or freezer thermostat and re-checks temperature on a follow-up visit.

Operator's shop or warehouse: machine on the bench during refurbishment or pre-deployment prep; technician sets the thermostat/controller setpoint to spec and checks refrigeration system pressures with a manifold gauge set, adjusting controls and charge before the machine ships to a location.

sources.system: MATT (Adapta Robotics)
sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: MATT is a commercial device-testing robot that works on a device fixtured on its bench and autonomously actuates hardware buttons, switches and control knobs on appliances including air conditioners and HVAC systems, with camera-based verification of device state.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated HMI testing of fixtured appliances (air conditioners, HVAC, kitchen appliances). It transfers because the physical act is the same as this task's core act - driving a thermostat control knob or keypad on an appliance to a commanded setting and confirming the resulting indication - at the same object scale and precision, on a bench with adjustable device fixtures.

sources.system: ANYmal
sources.title: Automate industrial inspection - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities and reads analog manometers, gauges and displays and determines lever/valve status, but its deployed function is reading and reporting, not adjusting controls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous gauge reading on industrial rounds. It covers only the reading half of this task (checking a pressure gauge or temperature indication) in a human work facility; no adjustment of thermostats or regulators is claimed, so it does not substantiate E2 completion.

sources.system: Spot with Spot Arm
sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets the Spot Arm as able to turn valves, flip levers and open doors in human-centric facilities, but only semi-autonomously and for objects with constrained movement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ manipulation of plant controls by a mobile robot. Even this coarse valve/lever actuation is described as semi-autonomous, and nothing covers opening a locked vending cabinet, finding a model-specific thermostat and setting it, so it cannot support completion at E2.

sources.system: Atlas humanoid autonomous valve-turning skill
sources.developer: research team on the Boston Dynamics Atlas platform (IEEE Humanoids publication)
sources.title: Autonomous valve turning with an Atlas humanoid robot | IEEE Conference Publication | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: An Atlas humanoid autonomously identified and turned an industrial valve after a single supervisory command, at turning speeds comparable to human performance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous turning of a rotary industrial control. A CO2/water pressure regulator knob or a thermostat dial is the same class of rotary control at lower torque and comparable precision; in a fixtured cell the perception and reach problem is far easier than for the free-standing valve demonstrated here.

sources.system: Learning-based analog gauge reading pipeline on a mobile inspection robot
sources.title: Under pressure: learning-based analog gauge reading in the wild (arXiv 2404.08785)
sources.claim: A learning-based analog gauge reading system was deployed on a mobile robotic inspection ... platform and read gauges at multiple locations and heights inside industrial plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine reading of analog pressure gauges. It substantiates the feedback element of 'adjust pressure gauges' - closing the loop on a dial reading - but provides no manipulation, so on its own it supports only the sensing half.

sources.system: PD400UR automatic screwdriving cell (UR5e cobot + Nitto Seiko driver)
sources.developer: Nitto Seiko America with Universal Robots (UR+ certified cell)
sources.title: Screwdriving | ASSEMBLY Magazine digital edition, February 2022
sources.claim: Commercially available fixtured robotic cells drive screws to controlled torque with a cobot and a precision electric driver, showing that small threaded adjusters can be turned to a controlled state autonomously in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torque/angle-controlled screwdriving on a fixtured workpiece. Thermostat and pressostat calibration screws are the same small fasteners at the same scale; in an instrumented cell the robot can turn them incrementally while a sensor reports the resulting setpoint.

sources.system: iTeide automatic refrigerant charging machine
sources.title: iTeide Automatic Refrigerant Charging Machine | Airserco
sources.claim: Purpose-built production-line stations automatically evacuate and charge refrigeration systems to a precise charge without a human working manifold gauges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated setting of refrigeration-circuit charge/pressure on a production line. It transfers to the bench-refurbishment instance's pressure work, where the technician's manifold-gauge check and charge adjustment is the same operation performed on a machine presented to a fixed station.

tasks.label: Disassemble and assemble machines, according to specifications and using hand and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-site repair of a food/beverage vending machine at a customer location (office break room, school cafeteria, hospital lobby, factory canteen): tech opens the door, unscrews and removes covers/shelf rails, pulls and swaps a failed component (vend motor, delivery bin, coin mech, bill validator, control board), then reassembles and tests, working in a narrow aisle beside a live machine with people passing.

Bench teardown and rebuild in the operator's shop/warehouse: machines pulled from routes are stripped down (door assembly, harnesses, refrigeration deck, boards), cleaned, worn parts replaced, and reassembled to factory specification with hand and power tools, then tested before redeployment.

Slot/gaming machine servicing on a casino floor or in the casino tech shop: unlock and open the cabinet, unscrew and remove button decks, printers, bill validators, monitors or logic-area boards under regulatory seal procedures, reassemble and re-seal, often while adjacent machines are in play.

Amusement machine service at arcades, family entertainment centers, bowling centers, bars and laundromats: disassemble a game cabinet, crane machine, jukebox or pinball to replace joysticks, monitors, ticket dispensers, coin doors or playfield parts; heterogeneous, often older, machines in tight or cluttered corners.

New machine installation or relocation at a customer site: uncrate the machine, bolt on base/legs, attach marquee/topper and side panels, mount and connect monitors, payment devices and harnesses per the installation specification, level and test; or reverse the process for removal.

Service at private or unattended locations: pinball/arcade machine in a private home game room or basement, or a vending/kiosk unit at an outdoor car wash, campground or curbside site, disassembled and reassembled in place with whatever access and lighting exist.

sources.system: Panasonic automated appliance disassembly workcells (six-axis robots, AI machine vision)
sources.title: Appliance Manufacturer Uses Robots and AI to Disassemble Products | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Panasonic has built robotic workcells at its Osaka R&D facility in which six-axis robots take apart used household appliances (air conditioners, microwave ovens, washing machines): magnetic grippers lift covers, screwdrivers remove fasteners located by AI machine vision even when dirty or rusty, and other end effectors cut wires and remove components; robots are also shown removing and installing washing-machine heat pumps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: teardown/part removal of used consumer appliances. A washing machine or room air conditioner is comparable to a vending or amusement cabinet in scale, sheet-metal construction, fastener types, wire harnesses and refrigeration hardware, and the cell copes with the used-unit conditions (dirt, rust) that make service disassembly harder than factory assembly.

sources.system: Molg robotic microfactory (with ABB robots)
sources.title: ABB Robotics and US start-up Molg tackle data center e-waste with robotic microfactories
sources.claim: Molg's robotic microfactory, developed with ABB Robotics, is described by ABB as able to autonomously assemble and disassemble complex ... in a purpose-built cell for data-center equipment recovery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastener-level disassembly and reassembly of electronic equipment. Servers and industrial electronics resemble the electronics packages inside slot machines, jukeboxes and game cabinets (screwed chassis, slide-in modules, connectorized boards), and the cell performs both directions of the task, not just teardown.

sources.system: Daisy disassembly robot line
sources.title: How Apple Robots are Closing the Waste Recycling Loop | Technology Magazine
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line in Austin, Texas has operated since 2018 as a purpose-built automated disassembly system that takes apart 23 iPhone models at 200 units per hour, punching out screws and separating components rather than shredding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated multi-model teardown of used products with fastener removal. It shows a purpose-built line can sustain production-rate, model-varying disassembly of used units, though at far smaller object scale than a vending machine.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic screwdriving system (Manyar, Patel, Gupta)
sources.developer: University of Southern California (Center for Advanced Manufacturing)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic screwdriving for high-mix manufacturing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A USC-developed autonomous robotic screwdriving system performs vision- and force-guided screwdriving for high-mix, low-volume manufacturing, using a physics-informed model of screw-tip motion to drive fasteners robustly under part and pose uncertainty.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered fastening of varied parts in a fixtured cell. 'Assemble machines according to specifications using hand and power tools' is dominated by driving and torquing fasteners on panels and modules; the high-mix result addresses the model-to-model variation typical of vending and amusement equipment.

sources.system: iDEAR robotic disassembly demonstrator
sources.developer: Fraunhofer Institute for Factory Operation and Automation IFF (Magdeburg)
sources.title: Intelligent Disassembly of Electronics for Remanufacturing and Recycling (iDEAR Project) - Fraunhofer IFF
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IFF's iDEAR project has demonstrated non-destructive robotic disassembly of computers in which the system identifies the device's geometry, materials and fasteners and executes AI-generated robot disassembly actions, including removing motherboards from housings, with subprocess demonstrators being integrated into one cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: non-destructive, AI-planned teardown of used electronic equipment without model-specific programming — the same perception-and-unfastening problem faced when opening an unfamiliar vending or game machine, but demonstrated only in a laboratory cell.

sources.system: RoboTire robotic tire-changing system
sources.title: From Manual to Robots: RoboTire's Impact on the Tire Shop Floor | Tire Review
sources.claim: RoboTire's robotic tire-changing system, installed in US tire shops, scans the vehicle, uses cameras to locate the wheel and lug nuts, removes the nuts and wheel with powered tools and torques replacement wheels to manufacturer specification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided removal and reinstallation of fasteners on used customer equipment with powered tools, torqued to spec and accepted by paying customers. It is done in a dedicated bay where the work is presented to the machine, i.e. a purpose-built station, not free-roaming field service.

sources.system: Skill-based robotic connector installation system
sources.developer: academic/industry research (Springer chapter, automotive wire harness installation)
sources.title: Automotive Wire Harness Connector Installation Using Skill-Based Robotic Programming
sources.claim: Robotic installation of automotive wire-harness connectors using force-controlled search and insertion, validated on a car door, reached only about 76.7% success, indicating that autonomous connector mating during reassembly remains below production reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reconnecting harness connectors during reassembly, a required step when rebuilding a vending or amusement machine. Cited as a limitation on reassembly reliability outside tightly fixtured, model-specific cells.

tasks.label: Contact other repair personnel or make arrangements for the removal of machines in cases where major repairs are required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Transport machines to installation sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Route/operator company delivers a full-size snack or beverage vending machine (600–900 lb) from its warehouse to a customer break room in an office, plant, or school: strap on a liftgate truck, drive public roads, lower to the lot, walk it on an appliance dolly over asphalt, a curb cut, door thresholds, sometimes an elevator, and set it in the designated spot.

Delivery of smaller coin/amusement equipment — arcade cabinets, jukeboxes, pool tables, ATMs, claw machines, countertop games — to bars, restaurants, laundromats and small retail; tight doorways, steps or basement stairs, uneven older floors, customer premises never seen before.

Casino or large-venue internal move: slot machines/route games taken from the property's receiving dock or storage on pallets and slot dollies, through back-of-house corridors and onto the carpeted gaming floor, set at their bank position among patrons and existing machines.

Movement inside the operator's own warehouse/shop: pulling refurbished or new machines from storage racks or floor staging on skids, moving them to the loading bay, and loading them into the delivery truck or trailer for the day's installs.

Transport to outdoor or semi-public installation sites — fairgrounds, stadium concourse, campground, gas-station forecourt, construction-trailer break area — over gravel, grass, ramps and grades, often with no dock and weather exposure.

sources.system: Seegrid Palion Lift RS1 autonomous lift truck (AMR)
sources.title: Seegrid Resource Center — Seegrid Lift RS1
sources.claim: Seegrid's Lift RS1 autonomous lift truck moves palletized loads up to 3,500 lb autonomously between pick and drop locations in manufacturing, warehousing and logistics facilities — the weight class of a full-size vending or amusement machine on a skid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous palletized material transport. A vending/amusement machine ships and is stored on a skid in the same weight and footprint class, so point-to-point transport of that load along a defined route is the same physical operation.

sources.system: Seegrid Palion AMR fleet (tow tractors and lift trucks)
sources.title: Seegrid Sets the Standard with Industry-Leading Forklift AMR Payload Versatility
sources.claim: Seegrid AMRs operate as a fleet inside busy human-occupied warehouses and plants, with more than 18 million autonomous production miles logged at customer sites, moving goods from receiving to storage to shipping docks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility transport of heavy palletized goods among people. It substantiates that the warehouse leg of moving machines (storage to loading bay) is done autonomously at production reliability in a structured human work facility.

sources.system: FoxBot Mk3 autonomous forklift
sources.title: ProMat 2025: Fox Robotics releases FoxBot Mk3 with new capabilities
sources.claim: Fox Robotics' FoxBot autonomous forklift picks, moves and loads or ... pallets into and out of over-the-road trailers at distribution-center docks, automating the truck loading step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous dock loading of palletized freight. Loading skidded machines into the delivery trailer at the operator's warehouse is the same pallet-in-trailer operation with comparable weights and clearances.

sources.system: Aethon TUG T3 / T3XL autonomous mobile robot
sources.title: Aethon — TUG product line
sources.claim: Aethon TUG robots autonomously tow wheeled carts of up to 1,000 lb through hospital corridors, calling and riding elevators, in daily deployed service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous towing of heavy wheeled loads through a human-occupied building. It shows the corridor/elevator leg is feasible, but the robot only tows carts humans load and unload, so it does not cover getting a machine onto/off the transport device or setting it in place.

sources.system: Aurora Driver (SAE L4 trucking system)
sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Aurora runs driverless Class-8 trucks hauling paid freight on Texas public highways, automating the over-the-road leg only; loading and unloading remain human work at the terminals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless long-haul freight on public roads. It covers only the highway sub-step of transporting a machine to a site; the system performs no loading, curbside unloading, or in-building placement, so it cannot complete a delivery instance.

tasks.label: Refer to manuals and wiring diagrams to gather information needed to repair machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Install machines, making the necessary water and electrical connections in compliance with codes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Route technician delivers a standard snack or bottled-beverage machine to an office/factory/school break room: unloads it from a lift-gate truck, dollies it over thresholds and through doors or an elevator, positions it against the wall with required clearance, levels the adjustable feet, plugs it into an existing 120V receptacle, sets up the coin/bill/card system, loads product and test-vends.

Installs a machine that needs plumbing: office coffee brewer, bottle-less water cooler, or ice/water dispenser. Locates a cold-water line under a sink or in a wall, installs a shutoff/compression tee, runs and secures poly tubing, mounts and primes an inline filter, connects to the machine, purges air, checks for leaks, and plugs in (GFCI where required).

Installs amusement equipment in a bar, restaurant, family entertainment center or laundromat: pool table, jukebox, dartboard, crane or arcade cabinet. Moves it through tight doorways and around furniture, assembles and levels it, plugs into available outlets, connects the cellular/network module, and configures pricing and diagnostics.

Installs slot/video gaming machines on a casino or route-location floor: sets each cabinet on a slot base or bank, secures/bolts it, dresses and connects power cords, SAS/network data cabling and bill validator, mounts signage/toppers, and completes regulator-witnessed power-up, communication verification and configuration.

Install requiring new utility work at an unfinished, outdoor or non-standard site (loading dock, gas-station lot, marina, campground, new-construction space): runs conduit and a dedicated branch circuit or hardwires the machine into a junction box, taps and runs a new water supply with backflow protection, anchors the machine or outdoor enclosure to a slab/wall, and passes inspection.

sources.system: NIO Power Swap Station (Gen 3 / 4.0)
sources.title: NIO Power Swap Station 4.0 Now Operational
sources.claim: NIO Power Swap Stations autonomously remove and install a heavy battery module into a vehicle in a purpose-built bay, mating high-voltage electrical and coolant connections, bolting it down and verifying the install; more than 1,000 highway stations and 100 million cumulative swaps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated installation of a heavy machine module into a fixtured bay with electrical/fluid connections and functional verification. It shows a purpose-built station positioning a heavy unit precisely, making its power connection and confirming operation without a human — the E1 analogue of setting a machine and hooking it up.

sources.system: Rocsys Platform / M1 hands-free charging robot
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic arms autonomously detect an arriving vehicle, open the charge port, insert the electrical connector, charge and disconnect, with a stated 99.9% plug-in success rate; deployed with port terminal operators such as APM Terminals and in robotaxi depots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mating of a power connector to a socket using vision and force compliance. The electrical-connection step of a machine install (inserting a cord/connector into a receptacle) is the same class of insertion at comparable tolerances, in a bay laid out for the robot.

sources.system: ATI QC-300 Robotic Tool Changer with utility modules
sources.date: documentation current 2025-2026; product line long deployed
sources.title: QC-300 Robotic Tool Changer (ATI datasheet)
sources.claim: ATI robotic tool changers are coupled and uncoupled under robot program control and pass utilities across the coupled joint, with pass-through modules for electrical power/signal, water and air.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-made simultaneous water/fluid and electrical connections. It substantiates that, where interfaces are engineered as quick-connect couplings in a purpose-built cell, a robot can repeatedly make leak-tight fluid and live electrical connections without human help.

sources.system: Dürr filling technology / robot filling stations and G4 Blue filling adapter
sources.title: Dürr Filling Technology – The market leader
sources.claim: Dürr supplies fully automatic filling and testing stations in which robot-guided filling adapters couple to a vehicle's fluid ports on the assembly line, seal under pressure, fill and decouple.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic robot connection of a pressurized fluid line to a machine presented by a conveyor, including leak-tight sealing and verification — the plumbing-connection step of an install, performed in a fenced production cell.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E. (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Schindler expands elevator installation robot fleet as demand for construction automation grows
sources.claim: Schindler's R.I.S.E. robot works autonomously inside elevator shafts on live construction sites, scanning concrete, drilling holes and setting anchor bolts to a digital plan, but it performs only drilling and anchoring — no machine placement or water/electrical connections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic equipment installation at an as-found building site. It marks the field ceiling — an autonomous anchor-drilling machine confined to a shaft — showing no fielded system moves equipment into a room and makes code-compliant water and electrical connections.

roles.title: Commercial Divers
aliases: NDT UW Welder (Non Destructive Testing Under Water Welder)
roles.description: Work below surface of water, using surface-supplied air or scuba equipment to inspect, repair, remove, or install equipment and structures. May use a variety of power and hand tools, such as drills, sledgehammers, torches, and welding equipment. May conduct tests or experiments, rig explosives, or photograph structures or marine life.

tasks.label: Check and maintain diving equipment, such as helmets, masks, air tanks, harnesses, or gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-dive and immediate post-dive check of the working rig at a dive station on a vessel, barge, or dock: inspect the helmet/band mask (seals, neck dam, visor, non-return valve, comms), function-test the demand valve and free-flow, check the bailout bottle pressure and whip, inspect the harness and umbilical along its length, confirm panel and pneumo gauge readings, and report ready-to-dive to the supervisor, in weather and on a moving deck.

Post-dive care in the dive locker or at the on-deck rinse station: flush and rinse helmets, masks, demand valves, hoses and harnesses in fresh water, disinfect the oral-nasal and mask interior between divers, dry the gear and stow it on racks or in transport boxes.

Scheduled or corrective overhaul in the dive shop: strip a helmet, band mask, demand valve or scuba regulator, clean and inspect used parts for wear/corrosion, replace O-rings, seats, diaphragms and springs from a service kit, lubricate, reassemble to torque, then adjust cracking pressure and leak-check.

Scheduled bench checks and instrument verification per the maintenance schedule: flow, leak, breathing-resistance and pressure tests on helmets, demand valves and bailout regulators with a magnehelic/flow tester, verification of depth gauges, pneumofathometers and analyzers against a standard, and entry of results in the equipment log.

Cylinder work in the dive locker or gas shed: check bailout and scuba cylinder pressures and hydro/VIP dates, inspect cylinder exteriors and valve O-rings, refill from the compressor or cascade, analyze and tag the gas, and set aside cylinders due for requalification.

Inland or remote job-site work out of a truck or small boat (bridge pier, dam, lock, water tank, riverbank): setting up and checking the spread on uneven ground or a tailgate, swapping a leaking whip or damaged harness strap, rinsing contaminated-water gear in a tote, checking gauges and bailout before entry, in mud, cold or rain.

instances.label: Offshore oil/gas or offshore-wind surface-supplied dive: diver dressed in a helmet and umbilical on a dive support vessel or platform, tended by helpers, descends via stage, wet bell or closed bell through open sea (waves, current, 20-150 m) to a subsea structure worksite.

Inland/marine-construction dive: diver descends from a barge, workboat or ladder into a river, lake, canal, lock, dam forebay or harbor to reach bridge piers, sheet pile, intake screens or pipelines; near-zero visibility, current, debris, silt bottom, layout differs site to site.

Ship-husbandry dive at a port berth or shipyard: diver descends off a pier, float or skiff alongside a moored vessel to reach the hull, running gear or sea chests for cleaning, inspection or repair; tended by helpers on the pier.

Enclosed industrial water system: diver descends through a hatch, manway or off a deck platform into a potable water tank/reservoir, power-plant intake or condenser bay, wastewater basin, or aquarium/process tank at a controlled facility, with tenders at the opening.

Scuba entry from a small boat in open coastal water for scientific sampling, aquaculture net/mooring work, salvage or survey; diver rolls or steps in with a buddy/tender and descends a line to the site in variable sea state and visibility.

instances.label: Underwater inspection of waterfront structures at a port, marina, shipyard or naval base: timber/concrete/steel piles, quay walls, bulkheads, fender systems and sheet pile. Diver documents corrosion, section loss, marine growth and damage with video/stills and takes thickness or caliper measurements; visibility is often poor, with tidal current and fouling.

Underwater inspection of bridge substructures, dam faces, spillways, trash racks and river/lake intake structures: scour measurement at footings, concrete/steel condition documentation with CCTV and stills, often in near-zero visibility, river current and silt, at sites reached from a boat or bank.

In-water survey of a vessel afloat at a berth or anchorage: hull plating, coating and fouling condition, sea chests and gratings, propeller, shaft, rudder and anodes, recorded on CCTV/stills for the owner or class surveyor (UWILD-type report), sometimes with UT thickness readings.

Interior inspection of sewers, force mains, outfalls and large-diameter conduits for a municipal utility using closed-circuit television: traverse the submerged/surcharged line, record defects, joint separation, deposits and infiltration, and deliver a coded condition report.

Inspection of treatment plant and power plant water systems: raw-water intake structures and screens, wet wells, clarifiers, and potable water storage tanks. Confined, contaminated, zero-visibility water; camera survey plus thickness/coating checks and debris documentation under utility supervision.

Offshore/subsea inspection of pipelines, risers, power and telecom cables, platform or wind-foundation members, anchor chains, mooring hardware and buoyage systems: general visual inspection, anode/CP checks, photo and video documentation from a vessel in open water with current and depth.

tasks.label: Inspect the condition of underwater steel or wood structures.

instances.label: NBIS Level I/II underwater bridge inspection: diver descends on piers, abutments, steel H/pipe piles and timber trestle piles in a river or tidal channel with near-zero visibility, current, debris and partial silt burial; sweeps and probes each member tactilely, removes growth at spot locations, measures section loss/scour and reports condition ratings.

Port/waterfront facility inspection: wharf, ferry terminal and bulkhead structures under a marine terminal — steel sheet-pile walls, steel pipe/H bearing piles, tie-rods, fender systems and some timber piles; diver scrapes marine growth at prescribed elevations, takes ultrasonic thickness readings, photographs and documents corrosion, holes and damage.

Ship husbandry / in-water hull inspection at a shipyard berth or port anchorage: survey of hull plating, coatings, welds, sea chests, rudder, propeller and shafting; fouling rating, damage documentation, occasional plate thickness readings, for owner or class in-water survey.

Routine general visual/structural survey of offshore steel assets in open sea: swim-along inspection of jacket members, wind turbine monopiles/transition pieces, subsea structures and risers to record marine growth, scour, debris, anode depletion and obvious damage.

Close-up detailed structural inspection offshore: cleaning a jacket node or splash-zone member to bare metal and performing contact NDT (ultrasonic thickness, MPI/ACFM on welds) and cathodic-protection contact readings in swell and current.

Hydro/utility facility inspection: dam intakes, gates and guides, trash racks, penstocks and flooded tunnels, lock walls, and potable-water tanks — inspecting steel gates, liners and embedded metalwork in confined, often zero-visibility water controlled by the plant operator.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-service inspection of a submerged steel pressure boundary. It is the same physical act as inspecting submerged steel structural members — ultrasonic thickness/flaw detection plus visual examination of steel underwater — performed to accepted code quality with the workpiece in a known, fixtured position, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual for pile, bulkhead and gate inspection.

instances.label: Offshore energy work: diver deploys and operates helmet/handheld video, stills and scanning sonar to inspect subsea structures — jacket members, risers, pipelines, mooring chains, wellheads — in open sea with current, depth and variable visibility; output is a recorded, referenced inspection product for the asset owner.

Ship husbandry: diver videos hull plating, propeller, rudder, bow thruster tunnels, sea chests and anodes alongside a berth or at an anchorage in a commercial port, often in turbid harbor water, producing recorded footage/report accepted for class UWILD, damage or fouling assessment.

Inland civil works: diver runs video camera and hand-held imaging sonar over bridge piers, footings, dam faces, lock walls, seawalls and intake structures in rivers/lakes with near-zero visibility, current and debris; deliverable is a documented condition inspection (defects, undermining, exposed rebar/timber loss).

Sonar/search work: operating scanning or side-scan sonar plus video to search for and map objects, wreck or debris fields, scour holes and channel bottom, for salvage, public-safety recovery or pre-/post-construction survey; open water, harbors and rivers.

Environmental/scientific survey: diver films marine life and habitat — reef, kelp, eelgrass, fish counts, invasive species, mitigation monitoring — with video/stills and transects in nearshore natural water.

Institution-controlled water facilities: video/sonar inspection inside potable water tanks and tunnels, power-plant intakes and screens, and aquaculture net pens, where an operator controls access, the layout is standard, and water conditions are managed.

tasks.label: Repair ships, bridge foundations, or other structures below the water line, using caulk, bolts, and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vessel afloat at a commercial berth: diver locates damage below the waterline (cracked, holed or heavily corroded shell plate), cleans marine growth off the area, fits and secures a steel patch or doubler plate over it and seals the edges so the compartment stays dry until drydocking. Zero-to-poor visibility, tidal current, curved hull surface.

Ship husbandry repairs to fittings and running gear afloat: bolting on replacement sacrificial anodes, fitting sea-chest blanks with rubber gaskets and bolts, renewing rope guards and shaft seals, freeing and re-torquing rudder/propeller fasteners, caulking around through-hull fittings. Diver works from a stage or free-swims with hand and hydraulic tools, tools tended from the surface.

Inland bridge pier, abutment or pile repair in a river or tidal channel: chipping out unsound concrete, placing forms or grout bags, injecting epoxy into cracks, wrapping and bolting fiberglass or steel pile jackets, bolting repair sleeves on timber or steel piles. Near-zero visibility, current, debris, silt, variable geometry site to site.

Dam, navigation lock, spillway or water/wastewater intake structure owned by a utility or USACE: replacing gate rubber seals, bolting trash-rack or screen panels back in place, caulking joints and sealing leaks with wedges, oakum and underwater sealant, re-bolting guide rails inside a lock chamber or wet well. Facility-controlled site, but silted, fouled and often blacked-out water.

Submerged steel waterfront or offshore structure: repairing corroded sheet-pile quay walls, steel bearing piles, jacket members or caisson plating by cleaning the steel and fastening/sealing a patch plate or clamp over the defect, plus bolted flange and clamp work on submerged pipework and outfalls. Open harbor or offshore water, surge and current.

sources.system: MARIOW underwater welding robot (DFKI modular underwater manipulator + UW-FCAW process)
sources.developer: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI) Robotics Innovation Center with TH Köln, Fraunhofer IGD, AMT GmbH, Unterwasserkrause–Mutzeck
sources.title: AI Goes Subsea: Autonomous Welding Robot Debut — Marine Technology News
sources.claim: The MARIOW underwater welding robot (DFKI-led consortium) autonomously detected weld joints with a stereo camera, planned the weld path with AI and executed continuous flux-cored arc welds (lap, fillet and build-up welds) on steel in a saltwater test basin, i.e., a repair-class operation on submerged steel with the workpiece presented in a fixtured laboratory setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: underwater welding rather than caulk/bolt work. Transfer is limited to defect closure on submerged steel plate — same objects (fouled/corroded steel structures, patch plates), same medium and comparable mm-level placement precision — where a welded patch is an output an owner accepts in place of a bolted, caulked patch. It does not transfer to fastener handling, gasket fitting or concrete work.

sources.system: MARIOW
sources.title: MARIOW - Projects - Robotics Innovation Center - DFKI GmbH
sources.claim: DFKI's own project page characterises the MARIOW robot as performing semi-autonomous underwater welding, with AI seam recognition and planning; the project ran to September 2025 and a follow-on project only begins evaluating the technology in the ports of Bremen from April 2026, confirming that field (non-tank) use is not yet established.
sources.transferJustification: Same related-task transfer as the MARIOW news item: underwater structural steel repair, demonstrated only in a purpose-built test basin.

sources.system: Review of intervention-AUVs (incl. Saab Sabertooth, Nauticus Aquanaut)
sources.developer: Frontiers in Robotics and AI (review authors)
sources.title: Inspection and maintenance of industrial infrastructure with autonomous underwater robots — Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of autonomous underwater inspection and maintenance concludes that submerged maintenance tasks (cleaning, welding of defects, valve turning, hot-stabbing) are still done by divers and remotely operated vehicles, and that autonomous underwater manipulation is not at high technology readiness.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the underwater intervention/maintenance capability class this task requires; cited as context for negative judgments, not to support any positive judgment.

sources.system: ODIN CLAM robotic cofferdam
sources.title: CLAM™ – Innovative Robotic Cofferdam Solution for Diverless Hull Repair — EM&I
sources.claim: The leading commercial 'diverless' below-waterline hull repair service installs a robotic cofferdam with ROV assistance so that the steel replacement is then carried out in the dry by technicians inside the hull; the robotic element is piloted, and the repair itself is not performed by an autonomous machine underwater.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (repair of ship structures below the waterline) performed on FPSO hulls; shows the commercial state of the art is ROV-assisted with human repair, so it cannot support a positive autonomous judgment.

sources.system: Armach Hull Service Robot / EverClean (Greensea IQ)
sources.title: Armach Robotics launches new hull cleaning service — Marine Log
sources.claim: Autonomous crawling robots operate unattended on ships' hulls in water at commercial berths, but their demonstrated work is grooming/cleaning of microfouling — no repair, fastening, sealing or hand-tool work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-water hull husbandry. It establishes autonomous robot operation on hulls in port (E2/E3 water), but cleaning involves no fastener handling, patch fit-up or sealant application, so it does not substantiate completion of a repair instance.

sources.system: Girona 500 I-AUV (TRITON project)
sources.developer: University of the Balearic Islands / University of Girona / Jaume I University
sources.title: I-AUV Docking and Panel Intervention at Sea — Sensors (MDPI)
sources.claim: An intervention AUV autonomously docked into a purpose-adapted subsea panel and performed manipulation tasks (turning a valve, plugging/unplugging a connector) in a water tank and at sea — autonomous underwater tool actuation, but only against machine-designed interfaces and not a structural repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous underwater manipulation of a fixed interface. It shows the E1-style pattern (work presented in a known, machine-adapted position) but covers only single-DOF actuation, not patching, bolting up plates, gasket fitting or caulking, so transfer to this repair task is partial.

tasks.label: Cut and weld steel, using underwater welding equipment, jigs, and supports.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inland/coastal marine construction: diver wet-welds and oxy-arc cuts steel sheet piles, H-piles, bracing, repair sleeves and brackets on bridge piers, wharves and bulkheads; near-zero visibility, tidal current, silt, work located by feel against as-found corroded steel.

Ship husbandry alongside a berth or at anchorage: cutting away damaged/fouled plate, welding doubler plates, cofferdam clips, studs and patches on a floating hull; curved fouled surfaces, surge, restricted access, class-surveyor-accepted repair quality.

Offshore oil & gas / offshore wind structural work: wet welding anode brackets and clamps, burning off damaged members, conductor/riser and jacket-member severance; surface-supplied or saturation diving, current, depth, marine growth.

Salvage, wreck removal and demolition: exothermic/oxy-arc cutting of wreck plating, collapsed structures and debris into liftable pieces; unpredictable geometry, entanglement hazards, zero visibility, unstable workpieces.

Inland utility/industrial facility work: hydro dam gate slots, trash racks, intake screens, water/wastewater plant tanks and power-plant intake structures; cutting corroded steel and welding brackets/guides inside an owner-controlled facility with dewatering, permits and known drawings.

sources.system: MARIOW underwater welding robot (DFKI modular underwater manipulator + UW-FCAW)
sources.developer: DFKI Robotics Innovation Center with TH Köln, Fraunhofer IGD, AMT GmbH, Unterwasserkrause – Mutzeck
sources.title: Autonomous Underwater Welding: Project Consortium Presents AI-Supported Welding Robot for Maritime Maintenance
sources.claim: MARIOW consortium (DFKI-led) built an underwater welding robot that autonomously detects the weld joint with stereo vision, plans the weld path, and executes underwater flux-cored arc welds; final demonstration was in DFKI's underwater test basin ... (fillet and build-up welds in a 20 m³ tank).

sources.system: MARIOW underwater welding robot
sources.title: Consortium Presents AI-Supported Underwater Welding Robot for Maritime Maintenance
sources.claim: Trade-press coverage of the same MARIOW demonstration confirms it is a research-stage system tested in a tank; weld-seam quality improvement and application in an actual harbor basin (salt water, current, waves, pressure) remain future work.

sources.system: PRSI Remote Welding System (remote welding habitat, POCO, remote welding tool)

sources.title: Remote welding habitat provides underwater welding solution
sources.claim: Statoil/Equinor's PRSI remote welding system joins subsea pipeline steel with a welding robot inside a dry gas-filled habitat whose claws fixture and align the pipe ends; the tool learns the weld path, then runs a pre-programmed welding sequence with weld acceptance judged by process monitoring. Qualified by trials at 400 m and 1,000 m and held operational in the PRSI Pool.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: welding steel underwater using jigs and supports (habitat pipe claws), except the arc burns in a dry hyperbaric atmosphere rather than wet.

sources.system: PRSI Pool remote controlled robotic hyperbaric welding
sources.title: Prepared for the Unplanned – Subsea Pipeline Tie-Ins and Repairs by Remote Controlled Robotic Welding (OTC 2025)
sources.claim: The same family of diverless robotic hyperbaric welding technology remains in use for subsea pipeline tie-ins and repairs, performed by machine inside a subsea-installed dry habitat rather than by divers.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (underwater joining of steel with jigs/supports); cited for maturity and recency, autonomy of the operator-controlled spread not established.

sources.system: CNC plasma water-table cutting systems (e.g., Hypertherm/ESAB-class machines on water tables)
sources.developer: Multiple machine-tool suppliers (article by Steve Zlotnicki)
sources.title: Putting heavy-duty cutting on the table
sources.claim: CNC thermal cutting machines routinely sever steel plate with the torch and arc fully submerged on water tables, the plate held on burning bars, with cut paths executed automatically by the machine controller.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled severing of structural steel with a submerged plasma arc — same process physics and material as diver oxy-arc/plasma cutting, with the workpiece fixtured and presented as a purpose-built cell would present it (E1 counterfactual).

sources.system: Oceaneering AWJC cutting suite (Internal Cutting Tool, Internal Multi-String Cutting Tool)
sources.title: Cutting | Oceaneering
sources.claim: Commercial subsea steel severance today (abrasive waterjet internal and external cutting of piles, conductors, caissons and jacket members) is delivered by ROV- or diver-deployed tooling positioned and run by human operators, not by autonomous robots working the site as found.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cutting steel underwater); cited to show that field-site cutting is teleoperated/diver-supported, supporting the negative judgment at E2/E3.

tasks.label: Carry out non-destructive testing, such as tests for cracks on the legs of oil rigs at sea.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Offshore oil/gas platform jacket: diver on surface-supplied air cleans marine growth off a node/brace weld on a leg, then runs crack detection (MPI or ACFM/eddy current) plus UT wall-thickness shots on legs, braces and risers from the splash zone down. Waves, current, variable visibility, topside NDT technician reading data live.

Inland/harbor civil infrastructure: bridge piers, steel H-piles and sheet pile bulkheads, dam and lock gates. Diver takes UT thickness readings on steel members and checks welds/gate frames for cracks in near-zero visibility, silt and tidal current, working largely by feel from a boat or barge.

In-water hull survey of a ship or barge at a berth or anchorage (UWILD/class or damage survey): grid of UT thickness readings on plating, weld seams and crack checks around rudder, sea chests and repair areas, with a class surveyor topside witnessing on video.

Facility water-filled structures: potable water tanks and reservoirs, clarifiers, power-plant intake bays, penstocks and industrial tanks. Diver enters clean or turbid water inside a plant-controlled site and takes UT thickness/NDT readings on steel shell, floor and welds while the structure stays in service.

Offshore wind and subsea assets: monopile/jacket welds and grouted connections, mooring chain and riser NDT, flooded member detection. Diver (or diver-tended tooling) cleans and scans welds at depth offshore, colder and deeper, with a support vessel and limited weather windows.

sources.system: ANDWIS eddy-current weld inspection robot
sources.developer: OceanTech Innovation with SINTEF, ConocoPhillips, DNV
sources.title: New robotic solution enables automated non-destructive weld testing in the splash zone
sources.claim: OceanTech/SINTEF ANDWIS underwater robot clamps onto a tubular welded brace and, in closed-loop mode, autonomously positions and scans an eddy-current (ACFM) probe along jacket welds to detect fatigue cracks; validated in SINTEF's underwater test lab.

sources.system: OceanTech eddy current weld inspection robot (Ekofisk C)
sources.title: A game-changer in weld inspection: Our partnership with ConocoPhillips on a new crack detection robot
sources.claim: The eddy-current weld inspection robot actually fielded offshore on ConocoPhillips' Ekofisk C jacket (20 welded joints in 28 days, replacing divers) is a remotely controlled robot deployed and positioned by a vertical access tool and manipulator arm.

sources.system: Square Robot SR-3 (and SR-1)
sources.date: 2026 (product page); platform in commercial inspection service for several years
sources.title: SR-3 Autonomous Tank Inspection Robot | Square Robot
sources.claim: Square Robot's SR-3 is a ... that swims inside in-service aboveground storage tanks and performs phased-array ultrasonic thickness inspection of floor and shell to API 653 standards, with no confined-space entry and the tank kept online.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-liquid ultrasonic thickness/NDT survey of submerged steel, which divers perform in water tanks, clarifiers and plant intake structures. Same measurement (contact PAUT/UT on steel through liquid), same code-based acceptance output (API 653), same institution-controlled facility.

sources.claim: Trade press confirms the Square Robot SR-1 carries a phased-array UT array that scans tank bottoms for thickness with an onboard autonomy engine, its data checked in real time by remote operators (supervisory, not step-by-step control).
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the SR-3 item: robotic in-liquid ultrasonic thickness measurement of steel inside a plant facility, the measurement divers make on tanks and submerged steel structures.

sources.system: Robotized ultrasonic cobot inspection system (immersion cell)
sources.title: Testia pioneers the future of NDT with the handover of a state-of-the-art robotized ultrasonic cobot inspection system
sources.claim: Commercially delivered robotized ultrasonic NDT cell: a cobot scans parts immersed in a water tank fitted with a lift and turntable, running standard UT instruments on fixtured workpieces presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated immersion ultrasonic inspection of a fixtured metal workpiece. Same measurement physics and accepted output (underwater UT thickness/flaw detection) as the diver's NDT, with the work brought to the machine as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: iFROG monopile inspection robot
sources.developer: InnoTecUK with ORE Catapult, TWI, Brunel University London
sources.title: Amphibious iFROG robot leaps ahead in ability to inspect and maintain offshore assets
sources.claim: iFROG amphibious crawler climbed a monopile and performed corrosion mapping, cleaning and weld-line NDT in ORE Catapult's dry and wet docks; its navigation is only semi-automated with an operator in the loop.

sources.system: EverClean Inspection Robot
sources.title: Greensea IQ to Showcase EverClean Inspection Robot at Ocean Business 2025
sources.claim: Greensea IQ sells an EverClean Inspection Robot that crawls ship hulls and submerged infrastructure carrying ultrasonic thickness sensors and cameras; the material describes operator-driven data collection like a traditional inspection ROV and does not establish autonomous survey execution.

sources.system: TSC Subsea ROV-deployed NDT (ACFM, FMD, grout inspection)
sources.title: Offshore Wind Subsea NDT Inspection Services - TSC Subsea
sources.claim: Current commercial subsea NDT of offshore wind and oil-and-gas structures (weld inspection, grout integrity, flooded member detection) is delivered with remotely operated robotics, i.e. piloted ROV-deployed NDT tooling.

tasks.label: Take test samples or photographs to assess the condition of vessels or structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-water hull survey of a commercial vessel alongside a berth or at anchorage in a port: diver swims the hull, propeller, rudder, sea chests and weld seams with a video/stills camera, documenting coating breakdown, fouling and damage for an owner or class surveyor (UWILD/IWS). Harbor water, moderate current, variable visibility, ship not moving.

Condition inspection of waterfront structures at a port, terminal or marina: photographing/videoing submerged concrete, steel and timber piles, sheet-pile bulkheads, quay walls, fender systems and seawalls, with measurements of section loss and marine growth. Institution-controlled premises, but silty water, debris and tidal current.

Underwater bridge substructure inspection in a river, tidal creek or lake for a state DOT/engineering firm: photographs and video of piers, footings, scour holes and riprap, often in low-to-zero visibility, current, and with logs/debris present; work staged from a boat at a site taken as found.

Taking physical test samples and contact NDT readings to assess condition: timber pile core borings, concrete cores, coating/corrosion-product or marine-growth samples, cathodic-protection contact readings and ultrasonic thickness shots requiring surface cleaning and probe coupling on piles, hulls or platform members.

Inspection of offshore energy structures (platform jackets, risers, caissons, subsea equipment, wind-turbine monopiles and scour protection) for an operator: photographic/video general visual inspection, marine-growth and anode-condition documentation, within an operator-controlled field with exclusion zone.

Inspection inside water/wastewater and hydro facilities: potable water storage tanks and reservoirs, intake structures, trash racks, dam faces, gates and penstocks; photo/video documentation of coating, cracking, debris and deterioration, in confined, utility-controlled, often low-visibility water.

sources.system: Sentinus (Blue Atlas Robotics)
sources.title: Underwater Inspection Solutions - Blue Atlas Robotics
sources.claim: Blue Atlas Robotics' Sentinus underwater inspection robot performs full-coverage close visual surveys of ship hulls and submerged structures with computer-vision self-steering, producing imagery, point clouds and 3D models; an operator supervises on site but does not fly the robot.

sources.system: Sentinus (Blue Atlas Robotics)
sources.title: Port Inspections - Blue Atlas Robotics
sources.claim: The same self-steering Sentinus robots are offered and used for port infrastructure and harbour wall inspection, delivering 3D digital twins of quay walls, piles and other submerged port assets.

sources.system: EverClean (Greensea IQ)

sources.claim: Greensea IQ operates an autonomous hull-crawling robotic service on commercial vessels in US ports (including the Port of New York ...), navigating hull-relative and covering the full hull under supervised autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous proactive hull grooming. It requires the same capability as photographic hull assessment - autonomous hull-relative navigation, full-coverage traversal of a vessel hull at a berth and continuous camera-based sensing - and Greensea markets an inspection variant on the identical platform.

sources.system: EverClean Inspection Robot (Greensea IQ)
sources.title: Greensea IQ to Showcase EverClean Inspection Robot at Ocean Business 2025
sources.claim: Greensea IQ sells a dedicated, standalone inspection robot for underwater hull and infrastructure inspection built on the same navigation/autonomy platform as its EverClean cleaning robot.

sources.system: ROV-based in-water/UWILD survey (DNV-accepted)
sources.developer: DNV (class society) with ROV service providers
sources.title: DNV GL's remote in-water ship surveys using ROV mark a world first
sources.claim: Classification societies accept robot-collected imagery in place of diver-collected imagery for in-water bottom surveys of ships and mobile offshore units, establishing that a robot's photographic record is an acceptable deliverable; these ROV surveys are, however, piloted.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (photographic assessment of a vessel's underwater condition); cited only to show the robot-produced photographic deliverable is accepted by the customer, not to establish autonomy.

sources.system: Tethys ONE
sources.title: UUVs - New frontiers (Uncrewed Systems Technology)
sources.claim: Tethys Robotics' Tethys ONE has been used to inspect hydroelectric plant facilities, holding station autonomously to view turbines and tunnels ... and autonomously scanning dam walls to produce geo-referenced 3D acoustic and photogrammetric models; the vehicle was validated in Swiss lakes and rivers with 10-20 cm visibility.

sources.system: Hydrone-R
sources.title: Saipem's underwater drone Hydrone-R performs autonomous mission in the Arctic coral area in Norway
sources.claim: Saipem's resident Hydrone-R underwater drone performs autonomous inspection and survey missions on Equinor's Njord field, without tether or surface vessel support, under a ten-year service contract; it has accumulated over 500 days of subsea residency and hundreds of missions.

sources.system: Hydrus micro-AUV
sources.title: 3D Shipwreck Model Built with AUV Imagery - Ocean Science & Technology
sources.claim: Advanced Navigation's Hydrus micro-AUV autonomously flew lawn-mower survey patterns in open ocean off Western Australia and captured 4K imagery of a 64 m shipwreck that was turned into a 3D photogrammetric model - autonomous photographic documentation of a structure in an uncontrolled natural water body, though in clear, obstacle-free water.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous photogrammetric survey of a submerged steel structure (wreck). It shows AUV-based photographic documentation outside a controlled facility, but in clear, open water rather than close-in turbid infrastructure inspection.

tasks.label: Supervise or train other divers, including hobby divers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acting as dive supervisor on a commercial surface-supplied job (harbor pier repair, inland river/bridge work, offshore barge): brief the crew and run the job safety analysis, control the dive from the dive station, monitor depth/time/gas/comms, direct tenders on umbilical handling, correct the working diver's technique by voice, log the dive, and manage standby-diver and emergency response in low-visibility, current-swept water.

Hands-on topside/deck training of tenders and entry-level divers at the company yard, dock, or vessel deck: teaching and physically demonstrating hat and harness rigging, umbilical make-up and tending, gas panel operation, tool and rigging handling, then correcting the trainee's hands on the actual equipment until it is done correctly.

Teaching hobby (recreational) divers in a swimming pool or confined-water session at a dive shop or aquatic facility: demonstrating mask clearing, regulator recovery, buoyancy and air-sharing underwater, physically steadying or repositioning students, adjusting their weighting and gear in the water, and intervening when a student bolts or panics.

Supervising open-water training or certification dives with hobby divers at a quarry, lake, or ocean site from shore or a small boat: leading the group in variable visibility and current, keeping the student ratio in sight, signalling and correcting underwater, assisting entanglement or buoyancy problems, and performing tows/rescues to the surface and boat.

Classroom and poolside/tank instruction at a commercial diving school or dive shop: delivering briefings and lectures on decompression tables, gas management and emergency procedures, evaluating and signing off student skill performance from the surface of a training tank, and grading logbooks and certification paperwork.

sources.system: CADDY BUDDY AUV + autonomous surface vehicle
sources.developer: UNIZG-FER LABUST (coordinator) with CNR, IST, Jacobs University, Univ. Vienna, Newcastle Univ., DAN Europe
sources.title: CADDY - Labust - FER
sources.claim: The EU CADDY project built an autonomous underwater 'buddy' vehicle plus surface vehicle that observes and assists a single working diver; it is the closest robotic analogue to in-water diver supervision, but it was a research project (2014-2016) that monitors and guides one diver rather than supervising a dive operation or training divers to certification standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-water monitoring of and assistance to a human diver. It is the nearest capability to supervising divers in the water, so its limits (a research-stage buddy that tracks one diver and cannot brief, instruct, correct technique, or run a dive station) bound what robots can do on this task.

sources.system: OceanOneK
sources.title: OceanOneK connects human's sight and touch to the deep sea | Stanford Report
sources.claim: OceanOneK, the most dexterous humanoid diving robot demonstrated in open water to ~1,000 m, is piloted by a human operator on a control ship through haptic and stereoscopic feedback rather than acting autonomously, so it cannot substitute for a diving supervisor or instructor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid underwater manipulation at dive sites. Any robot demonstrating or physically correcting diver skills in water would need at least this level of underwater dexterity; because the frontier system is continuously teleoperated, it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for in-water instruction.

sources.system: Deep Trekker DTG/Revolution ROVs used in commercial diving
sources.title: Commercial Diving Underwater ROVs | Deep Trekker
sources.claim: Commercially sold underwater ROVs used on commercial diving jobs provide topside video of the diver's progress, but they are flown by a human pilot on a handheld controller and only supply imagery — the human supervisor still runs the dive.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote observation of a working diver, the closest deployed commercial technology to dive supervision. It is piloted, delivers only a video feed, and makes no supervisory decisions, so it does not substantiate robotic completion of supervision.

tasks.label: Perform activities related to underwater search and rescue, salvage, recovery, or cleanup operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Public-safety/recovery dive on an inland lake, pond or river to locate and bring up a drowning victim or human remains: near-zero visibility, silt bottom, current, entanglement hazards; body must be recovered intact, bagged and handed to investigators/coroner with chain-of-custody care.

Law-enforcement or client search and recovery of discrete evidence or property from inland waters (handgun, phone, safe, outboard motor, stolen goods): diver runs a search pattern largely by feel in murky water, locates the item, secures it and surfaces it undamaged.

Salvage or refloating of a sunken/capsized vessel, sunken vehicle, barge cargo or heavy equipment in a harbor, river or coastal water: surveying the wreck, patching and sealing openings, rigging slings, chains and lift bags, hooking crane lines, dewatering and controlling the lift.

Recovery of dropped or lost objects and gear at a port berth, marina, shipyard or industrial waterfront (hand tools, pumps, fenders, small machinery, anchors, dropped cargo) in institution-controlled water with poor visibility; item located on the basin floor and brought to the surface.

Debris and sediment cleanup inside a municipal or industrial water facility: clearing trash and rags from intake structures, trash racks, wet wells and dam gates, and vacuuming sludge/sediment and debris from clarifiers and potable water storage tanks while the facility stays in service.

Environmental debris cleanup of a harbor basin, marina or waterfront: removing tires, bicycles, shopping carts, derelict fishing gear, bottles and general trash from the bottom and transferring it to a surface vessel or dock for disposal.

sources.system: SeaClear 2.0 (Smart Grapple UUV + Mini Tortuga survey UUV + uncrewed surface vessel)
sources.developer: EU consortium led by TU Delft, with TU Munich, Subsea Tech, Hamburg Port Authority

sources.system: Smart Grapple (SeaClear 2.0 collection UUV)
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / SeaClear 2.0 consortium
sources.title: This unmanned underwater robot can remove ocean trash | CNN
sources.claim: The TUM Smart Grapple diving robot has been demonstrated retrieving a wide range of real seabed litter at the Port of Marseille and the Port of Hamburg, replacing work normally done by divers.

sources.system: Smart Grapple (SeaClear 2.0)
sources.title: TUM develops autonomous underwater robot to collect marine litter
sources.claim: The autonomous gripper on the TUM diving robot can grasp and lift objects up to roughly 1 cubic metre and 250 kg, with force sensing to avoid damaging what it grips — the payload envelope needed for retrieving dropped gear and bulky debris.

sources.system: Commercial robotic pool cleaners (e.g., Fluidra/Zodiac, Hayward, MOVA Rover X10)
sources.title: What are the pool robot cleaner options for commercial pools? | Fluidra
sources.claim: Robotic pool cleaners are commercially deployed autonomous machines that scrub, vacuum and collect debris and sediment from the floor and walls of purpose-built water basins without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vacuuming settled sediment and loose debris off the floor of a water-filled basin. This is the core of diver sediment cleanout of potable-water tanks and clarifiers; objects (silt, leaves, small trash), submerged concrete/steel basin geometry, and precision requirements are comparable when the basin is purpose-built and free of obstructions.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: continuous removal of waterborne trash and debris from an intake screen, which divers otherwise clear by hand. Same debris types and same facility, with the work brought to a fixed machine rather than the machine sent to the work.

sources.system: Public-safety ROV (Pierce County Sheriff's Office)

sources.claim: Public-safety underwater search, victim location and evidence recovery in US inland and coastal waters is done with piloted remotely operated vehicles, not autonomous robots.

sources.system: Deep Trekker DT640 VAC utility crawler
sources.title: VAC Tank Cleaning Robot Package | Deep Trekker
sources.claim: Cleaning sediment out of municipal potable water tanks without divers is done today with operator-driven crawler vehicles run from a handheld controller, i.e. teleoperation rather than autonomy.

sources.system: SUPSALV recovery operation, contractor-operated unmanned system (Phoenix International)
sources.title: U.S. Navy Recovers F/A-18F and MH-60R Lost in South China Sea | The Aviationist
