tasks.label: Recover objects by placing rigging around sunken objects, hooking rigging to crane lines, and operating winches, derricks, or cranes to raise objects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inland waters (river, lake, canal, reservoir): diver descends in near-zero visibility with current and silt to a sunken vehicle, outboard/machinery, small barge or dropped equipment; passes wire slings/chokers under or around the object by feel, shackles them to the crane whip, and signals a crawler or barge crane to raise it.

Port berth, marina or shipyard basin (access-controlled premises, dredged bottom): recover items dropped from a quay or vessel - container, forklift, propeller, anchor/chain, toolbox, pallet of gear - rig them to a quay or mobile crane hook, and tend the lift to the surface.

Marine construction / offshore worksite: recover dropped subsea equipment, pipe joints, concrete mattresses, mooring hardware or a lost tool near a platform, jackup or lay barge; rig strops or a recovery hook to the deck crane wire in current and variable visibility, then raise on the crane or an air winch.

Controlled inland facility (hydro dam intake, navigation lock, water/wastewater plant, power-plant intake, dry dock): retrieve a dropped stoplog part, pump, gate component, grating or tool from a confined, murky basin and rig it to the facility gantry/monorail crane or a portable winch.

Emergency or casualty salvage and search-recovery: sunken boat, aircraft, vehicle or hazardous debris at an unsurveyed open-water site after an incident; diver locates the object, clears entanglement, rigs slings or lifting bridles under unknown load conditions and works with a crane barge to raise it.

sources.system: Girona 500 I-AUV (RAUVI project)
sources.developer: University of Girona / Jaume-I University / University of the Balearic Islands
sources.title: Reconfigurable AUV for intervention missions: a case study on underwater object recovery
sources.claim: The Girona 500 intervention-AUV (RAUVI project) autonomously searched for and recovered a flight-data-recorder mockup lying at an unknown position on the floor of a purpose-built water tank, using its arm to attach a hook to the object.
sources.transferJustification: This is the underwater half of the task performed autonomously - locating a sunken object and attaching a hook (rigging) to it so it can be raised - but with a light mockup carrying a designed grasp/hook point in a clear purpose-built tank, i.e. an E1-style presentation.

sources.system: Girona 500 I-AUV (RAUVI / TRIDENT)
sources.developer: University of Girona / Jaume-I University / University of the Balearic Islands
sources.title: I-AUV Docking and Intervention in a Subsea Panel (IROS 2014)
sources.claim: The same line of work demonstrated autonomous 'hooking' of a target object in a water tank and then repeated the experiment in a harbour with a 4-DoF arm and later a 7-DoF arm with a three-fingered hand.
sources.transferJustification: Hooking a sunken object with a manipulator is the rigging-attachment step of this task; the demonstrated objects are small, light mockups rather than multi-tonne loads needing slings and chokers.

sources.system: Girona 500 I-AUV with 7-DoF arm (TRIDENT)
sources.developer: TRIDENT EU consortium (Jaume-I University, University of Girona, GraalTech, University of Bologna)
sources.title: Trident submarine robot successfully tested at sea
sources.claim: In the TRIDENT project's final trials in the Port of Soller (Mallorca), an intervention AUV independently found and retrieved an object from an unknown seabed.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous search-and-recovery of a sunken object in a harbour; the object is a small black-box mockup grasped by hand rather than rigged to a crane line, so it covers only the lightest end of the task.

sources.system: SeaClear 2.0 (USV + collection UUV with grapple)
sources.developer: SeaClear 2.0 consortium (TU Delft, TU Munich, Fraunhofer CML, Hamburg Port Authority, others)

sources.claim: The SeaClear 2.0 multi-robot system was shown in a first public live demonstration at the Hamburg Port Authority's Harburg facility, where it autonomously detected, grabbed and lifted a ... tyre from the port seabed.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous retrieval of objects from a port seabed in low visibility is the closest real-facility analogue, but the objects are litter (tyres, bicycles, pipes) taken with a grapple into a basket, not loads rigged with slings and shackled to a crane line.

sources.system: SeaClear 2.0
sources.title: SeaClear 2.0: Cleaning Our Oceans bottom with Uncrewed Autonomous Systems - Ocean Business
sources.claim: SeaClear 2.0 is specified to work to 300 m depth and to lift objects of up to 250 kg, autonomously detecting, classifying and collecting litter.
sources.transferJustification: Bounds the payload of demonstrated autonomous underwater object recovery (about a quarter tonne with a grapple), well below the slung, multi-tonne crane lifts that dominate this task.

sources.system: TMEIC crane automation (and Konecranes automated mill cranes)
sources.date: 2025-08 (page); technology in commercial service for years
sources.title: Crane Automation - TMEIC
sources.claim: Industrial crane automation is sold and operated in fully automatic, unmanned mode for repetitive lifting cycles in steel plants and container terminals, with vision and auto-positioning subsystems.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'operating winches, derricks, or cranes to raise objects' half of the task: once a load is rigged, unmanned automated hoisting to a known set-down point is commercially routine in purpose-built cells and terminals.

sources.system: Hydrone-R
sources.title: Saipem's Hydrone-R drone sets 167-day subsea operation record
sources.claim: Saipem's Hydrone-R resident underwater intervention drone completed 167 days of continuous subsea residency at Equinor's Njord field, running autonomous missions but remotely operated interventions.
sources.transferJustification: Documents that in the most advanced offshore deployment of resident subsea robots, manipulation/intervention work is still piloted remotely, so it cannot substantiate autonomous rigging and lifting offshore.

sources.system: Resident AUV light-intervention programmes (industry-wide)
sources.title: ROV & AUV Technology 2026: Autonomous Subsea Robotics Transforming Offshore Inspection
sources.claim: Trade guidance as of 2026 describes light intervention such as retrieving a small component from ... as a capability the offshore industry is still working toward.
sources.transferJustification: State-of-the-art statement establishing that even light autonomous object retrieval offshore is not yet operational, let alone autonomous heavy rigging and crane recovery.

tasks.label: Install, inspect, clean, or repair piping or valves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Offshore/inshore external inspection survey of submerged pipelines, flowlines and risers (visual, sonar/laser, coating and span condition) along a route on the seabed, oil & gas or subsea utility crossings; report delivered to the asset owner.

Offshore subsea intervention on production piping: operating/servicing subsea valves on trees, manifolds and ROV override panels, removing marine growth from risers and flanges, fitting repair clamps at depth with current and variable visibility.

Municipal/industrial water and wastewater facility: dive into intake bays, wet wells, clarifiers and potable tanks to inspect and clean submerged piping, suction bells and gate valves, vacuum silt and clear debris, change gaskets and set plugs/blanks, usually in near-zero visibility by feel.

Marine construction: install new outfall/intake pipe strings and valves in a harbor, river or lake — rig and land spools, align and bolt/torque flanges or couplings, seal joints, backfill; site conditions (current, silt, tide) taken as found.

Ship husbandry at berth: inspect, clean and repair sea chests, strainers, sea valves and overboard discharge piping; remove fouling and gratings, blank off penetrations, replace fasteners while the vessel is alongside.

Power plant (fossil, hydro, nuclear) submerged water systems: inspect, clean, plug or make minor repairs on circulating-water piping, condenser inlets, screen wells, penstock entrances and their valves/gates, under lockout inside plant premises.

sources.system: Freedom AUV
sources.title: Oceaneering Conducts Freedom™ AUV Pipeline Inspection Pilot for TotalEnergies
sources.claim: Oceaneering's Freedom AUV autonomously completed a pipeline inspection industrial ... for TotalEnergies, tracking and inspecting subsea pipelines with laser and multibeam sonar without a pilot in the loop.

sources.system: Freedom AUV
sources.title: Freedom AUV completes North Sea pipeline trials for TotalEnergies | Offshore
sources.claim: The Freedom AUV inspected more than 120 km ... in a North Sea program for TotalEnergies, in addition to 60 km of near-shore pipelines in an earlier demonstration.

sources.system: Hydrone-R
sources.title: Saipem Completes Arctic Underwater Drone Mission
sources.claim: Saipem's resident Hydrone-R underwater intervention drone lives on the seabed at Equinor's Njord field under a 10-year contract and has run fully autonomous, untethered survey/inspection missions without surface support; interventions are still remotely operated.

sources.system: Girona 500 I-AUV (TRITON project)
sources.title: I-AUV Docking and Panel Intervention at Sea (Sensors 16(10):1673)
sources.claim: The Girona 500 intervention-AUV autonomously docked into a purpose-adapted subsea valve panel with a funnel docking guide and performed valve turning and connector plugging, tested in a water tank and at sea.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element as a diver's subsea valve work (operating a valve and making/breaking a connection), but only on a panel purpose-adapted for the machine with a docking funnel.

sources.system: AutoBox ABX-2L / ABX-3L automated flex lancing system
sources.title: StoneAge AutoBox 2L Automated Flex Lancing/Exchanger Tube Cleaning
sources.claim: StoneAge AutoBox systems clean the inside of heat-exchanger and condenser tube bundles hands-free: the operator rigs the frame on the fixtured bundle, starts it and stands outside the blast zone while the machine indexes and lances the tubes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: internal cleaning of piping/tubes. Same objects (steel tubes and piping), same accepted output (fouling and deposits removed), performed with the workpiece fixtured and presented to the machine, i.e. an E1 presentation of the diver's pipe-cleaning work.

sources.system: Spool Welding Robot (SWR)
sources.title: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot | SWR™ | Pipe Welding Robot
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot welds fixtured pipe spools root-to-cap hands-free in a fabrication shop, using laser seam tracking and the NovEye vision system, with the operator only setting up the joint.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining pipe sections to install a piping run. Same objects (steel pipe joints) and the same accepted output (a pressure-tight, x-ray-quality joint), with the pipe fixtured and presented to the machine as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: Robo-Spider automated riser-flange-bolt torque system
sources.title: Robo-Spider Automated Riser-Flange-Bolt Torque System | SLB
sources.claim: SLB's Robo-Spider is a fully automated hydraulic torque system that clamps to a marine drilling riser flange and torques the whole bolt circle without hands on the bolts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making up a flanged pipe joint to torque spec, the fastening step of installing piping and valves; the flange is held in a known fixed position by the machine, i.e. an E1 presentation.

sources.system: SOLO autonomous pipeline inspection robot
sources.title: SOLO® Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone Robotics' SOLO is an unmanned, autonomous sewer pipeline inspection robot deployed commercially by municipalities: it is dropped through a manhole, traverses the pipeline on its own sensors, handles obstructions and returns to the launch point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: condition inspection of utility piping that divers otherwise enter or dive to inspect; same object (large-diameter utility pipe) and same output (a coded condition report), but from inside the pipe and without any cleaning, valve or repair work.

sources.system: Hull Service Robot (HSR) / EverClean
sources.title: Armach Robotics launches new hull cleaning service - Marine Log
sources.claim: Armach Robotics' EverClean service uses autonomous crawling robots that navigate a ship's hull in the water at berth and remove microfouling, delivering a hull condition survey each visit; it addresses open hull plating rather than sea chests, valves or piping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-water cleaning of submerged steel at a berth; shows autonomous underwater cleaning of open surfaces but not of sea chests, strainers, valves or piping recesses.

tasks.label: Set or guide placement of pilings or sandbags to provide support for structures, such as docks, bridges, cofferdams, or platforms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New heavy marine construction (pier, wharf, bridge bent): 18-36 in steel pipe or concrete piles swung by a barge crane; diver descends 15-40 ft in 1-3 ft visibility, guides the pile into a submerged template or to layout marks, checks plumb, tip elevation and seating on the bottom, and signals the crane/hammer crew.

Sand/grout bag placement: diver hand-carries and stacks 50-100 lb sand or grout bags to restore scour protection at a bridge pier or dock footing, seal the toe of a cofferdam or a dam leak, or bed and support a submerged structure; near-zero visibility, current, bags fed down from the surface one at a time.

Cofferdam / sheet-pile work: diver guides sheet piles or H-piles into interlocks and template guides at the mudline, clears obstructions, positions and pins bracing frames for a bridge pier cofferdam in a river with current.

Small marina / commercial dock new piling: timber, composite or small-diameter pipe piles jetted or driven in 5-20 ft of water from a small barge; diver steadies and positions the pile, checks plumb and embedment, in open water beside the new dock line.

Repair / replacement piling around existing structures: pile set under an existing dock deck, alongside a fender system or into a socket adjacent to an in-service bridge pier; diver works in confined space among existing members, debris and marine growth to align the pile.

Offshore / heavy marine platform work: guiding jacket or mooring piles into pile sleeves or a seabed template, checking pile stab-in and grout connections for a platform or offshore foundation, in deeper water from a derrick barge or installation vessel.

sources.system: GIKEN GYRO PILER F401-G1200 with iNAVILINK autonomous operation / Implant NAVI
sources.developer: GIKEN LTD. / GIKEN SEKO CO., LTD.
sources.title: Next-generation Press-in Piling Using Digital Transformation. On-site Verification of Autonomous Operation and Remote Support | GIKEN LTD.
sources.claim: GIKEN's iNAVILINK autonomous-operation system drove 13 of 19 steel tubular foundation piles (1,000 mm dia., 10.5 m) for a storm-surge seawall at Usa Port, Kochi, placing them to planned location and depth under ..., with all piles meeting national tolerance standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled setting of steel foundation piles for a coastal seawall. The accepted output is identical to the diver-guided case (pile at planned position, depth and inclination within tolerance) and the objects are the same class of marine foundation piles; the pile is held and aligned in the machine's chuck, i.e. presented fixtured as a purpose-built (E1) setting would present it.

sources.system: RPD 35 Robotic Pile Driver
sources.title: Robotic solar pile driver three times faster than humans – pv magazine USA
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is a commercially offered autonomous pile-driving robot that surveys, distributes, drives and inspects foundation piles at utility-scale solar sites with a two-person crew, meeting placement/slope tolerances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous setting of driven piles that support a structure. It shows a machine can pick, position, plumb and drive piles to tolerance without a human guiding the pile; transfer is limited to cases where the pile is presented to the machine's mast/guide, since the RPD 35 is a land machine and cannot work submerged.

sources.system: Pile gripper on DP monopile installation vessel (Dogger Bank A foundation installation)
sources.developer: Seaway 7 / OHT (vessel operators); gripper suppliers incl. Huisman, MacGregor
sources.title: Dogger Bank achieves milestone with first monopile installation
sources.claim: Offshore monopile foundations at Dogger Bank are installed by transferring the pile to a vessel-mounted pile gripper that holds and guides it while it ... lowered and hammered into the seabed; no diver guides the pile.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (guiding placement of a piling that supports a structure), performed by machine rather than diver; cited to establish that the purpose-built gripper frame is the environment in which offshore pile guidance is actually done, not to establish autonomy.

sources.system: Motion Compensated Pile Gripper (MCPG)
sources.title: Motion Compensated Pile Grippers - Huisman
sources.claim: Huisman's motion-compensated pile gripper is a purpose-built frame on the installation vessel that holds the monopile, prevents oscillation during lowering and driving and keeps it vertical by automatically compensating vessel heave, roll, pitch and yaw.
sources.transferJustification: Same function as the diver's 'guide placement of a piling': holding the pile in position and plumb while it is driven. Cited for the purpose-built fixturing environment; closed-loop motion compensation is automatic but overall operation is operator-supervised, so autonomy is recorded as unclear.

sources.system: Waterproof SILENT PILER
sources.title: Development of Waterproof SILENT PILER™ | GIKEN LTD.
sources.claim: GIKEN's waterproof SILENT PILER installed steel sheet-pile cut-off walls in the Oe River from August 2025, but the company states that a genuinely underwater press-in machine working on ocean or river bottoms, combining remote and autonomous operation, remains a future development goal.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant limiting evidence: the leading automated piling developer treats submerged, as-found-bottom piling as not yet achieved, supporting the judgment that no cited system performs the diver's underwater guidance in an unstructured (E3) submerged setting.

sources.system: Buoyancy-enabled autonomous underwater construction system (BlueROV-class platform with 1-DoF manipulator)
sources.title: Buoyancy enabled autonomous underwater construction with cement blocks (arXiv:2305.05552)
sources.claim: A research free-floating autonomous underwater construction robot assembled structures of up to 12 cement blocks (100 kg) using active ballasting and a one-degree-of-freedom manipulator, with error-correcting block geometry - the state of the art for autonomous underwater placement of support material.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous underwater placement of heavy support elements (analogous to sandbag/grout-bag placement). Cited to show the capability exists only at research scale with purpose-made, self-aligning rigid blocks in controlled water, far below the reliability and throughput of a diver bagging a scour hole.

tasks.label: Install pilings or footings for piers or bridges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bridge/pier pile driving support: diver descends to the riverbed or harbor bottom in turbid, current-swept water to guide a driven pipe or H-pile into a subsea template, check alignment/plumb and seating, clear obstructions at the pile point, and signal the crane/hammer operator on the barge.

Underwater rigging and load handling: attaching and releasing slings, chokers, shackles and tag lines on piles, pile templates, forms and precast footing units; landing and unhooking crane loads at the bottom in near-zero visibility.

Bottom preparation for piles/footings: water-jetting piles down, airlifting or dredging silt, removing debris and boulders, leveling and cleaning the bearing surface (bedrock or prepared gravel pad) for a footing or pile cap seat.

Underwater burning and welding on installed piles: cutting piles to grade with exothermic torch, welding splices, driving shoes, brackets, cross-bracing and pile-cap connection plates on marine piles.

Footing formwork and concrete: setting and sealing forms/pile jackets against washout, placing rebar and dowels, positioning tremie pipe or grout bags, and placing underwater concrete or grout for a footing or pile encasement.

As-built verification and documentation of the installed pile or footing: measuring embedment, plumb and position, checking template fit and seal, and recording video/sonar documentation for the engineer.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 autonomous piling system
sources.title: Built Robotics develops autonomous solar piling robot
sources.claim: RPD 35 is a commercially offered, fully autonomous piling machine that performs the whole piling workflow - survey, pile distribution/handling, driving into the ground, and post-drive inspection - to sub-inch position tolerances on outdoor construction sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving foundation piles. Same object class (steel piles) and same accepted output (pile driven to design depth, position and plumb tolerance), including machine handling of the pile into the leads, which is what the diver's guiding serves. Performed dry on land, so it substantiates only a purpose-built, fixtured presentation of the work.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 autonomous piling system
sources.title: Built Robotics develops autonomous pile driving system
sources.claim: The RPD 35 handles and places piles itself from an onboard cartridge system with only a two-person supervising crew, i.e. no human rigger slings, positions or guides each pile.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized pile handling and placement. The pile-cartridge feed and automated positioning replace the sling/choker rigging and manual guidance a diver provides, at comparable object weight and placement precision, but only where piles are presented to the machine in a magazine.

sources.system: Exosystem autonomous excavator kit
sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem converts standard excavators into fully autonomous machines that excavate and trench to design grade without an operator in the ... sold commercially and has been deployed on large jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: excavating and grading to a design elevation. Same physical function as clearing silt/debris and preparing a level bearing seat for a footing, with comparable material and tolerance, but demonstrated only in dry, machine-accessible ground.

sources.system: AGT Robotics BeamMaster WELD robotic welding line
sources.title: Robotic welding for structural steel fabrication
sources.claim: Robotic welding lines for heavy structural steel are commercially installed in fabrication shops: a fitted beam is sent to the cell and the robot completes the required code-quality welds automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: welding structural steel members (stiffeners, brackets, splices). Same joint types, steel thickness range and weld-acceptance criteria as pile splices, brackets and bracing, but only with the workpiece fixtured and presented in a dry cell.

sources.system: Elematic Automatic shuttering station E9 (shuttering robot)
sources.title: Robot for automatic shuttering in precast wall production
sources.claim: Shuttering robots are standard commercial equipment in precast concrete plants, autonomously demolding, placing and aligning formwork and accessories on fixtured casting beds where concrete is machine-placed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting, sealing and stripping formwork with embedded accessories for a cast concrete element. Same objects (form profiles, inserts, embeds) and same accepted output (a formed, cast concrete member), but only on fixtured casting beds in a plant.

sources.system: Hydrone-R underwater intervention drone
sources.title: Saipem’s underwater drone Hydrone-R performs autonomous mission in the Arctic coral area in Norway
sources.claim: Saipem's resident Hydrone-R underwater intervention drone has completed autonomous survey/inspection missions at the Njord field with no tether and no surface vessel support.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous underwater survey and inspection of subsea assets. Supports the documentation/verification portion of pile installation; it is survey-only and does not bear on installing, rigging, welding or concreting underwater.

sources.system: EverClean autonomous hull cleaning/inspection robot
sources.title: EverClean Autonomous Hull Cleaning Service Expands to Port of New York
sources.claim: Greensea IQ's EverClean robot performs autonomous underwater inspection and cleaning of large submerged steel structures in working commercial ports, including an expansion of the service to the Port of New ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous contact inspection of large submerged steel structures in turbid harbor water at an institutionally controlled berth. Supports machine capability for in-water documentation of an installed pile; it involves no tool work, rigging or construction.

sources.system: MARIOW underwater welding robot
sources.developer: DFKI-led consortium (German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence)
sources.title: AI Goes Subsea: Autonomous Welding Robot Debut
sources.claim: Autonomous underwater welding remains at research-project stage: the DFKI-led MARIOW project has only recently produced a robotic system able to perform underwater welding tasks 'largely autonomously'.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (underwater welding on marine steel structures), cited as limiting evidence: a project demonstration rather than a deployed system, so it cannot support in-water (E2/E3) positive judgments.

tasks.label: Salvage wrecked ships or their cargo, using pneumatic power velocity and hydraulic tools and explosive charges, when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refloating a sunken small vessel (tug, barge, fishing boat, workboat) in a harbor, marina or river berth at 10-60 ft: diver surveys the hull in low-to-zero visibility, jets tunnels and reeves slings/chains, patches hull openings, fits pneumatic lift bags and dewatering pumps, and tends the crane lift.

Sectional wreck removal at an as-found wreck site: cutting hull and structure apart underwater with hydraulic/pneumatic saws, grinders and exothermic cutting torches, clearing entangled cable and debris, then rigging each cut section to a crane for lifting, amid silt, current and sharp steel.

Recovering cargo and contents from a wreck: penetrating flooded holds and machinery spaces, freeing and slinging containers, drums, machinery, vehicles or valuables and rigging them into baskets or to lift lines; may include hot-tapping and pumping off residual fuel/oil.

Deep or offshore salvage from a dive bell/saturation spread or surface-supplied at depth, alongside teleoperated work-class ROVs: attaching lift wires, chain slings and pad-eyes to a large sunken vessel or heavy debris in current, swell and poor visibility.

Placing explosive charges on wreckage: cutting charges on frames, plating or piling, or breaking up an obstruction blocking a navigation channel; shaping and taping charges to structure, running det cord and firing leads, and clearing the site before detonation.

Recovering discrete items and debris off the bottom near a wreck (a machinery part, a drum, an outboard, a small container, lost gear): locating the item in poor visibility, attaching a hook, strop or lift bag, and sending it to the surface.

sources.system: MARIOW underwater welding robot (DFKI modular subsea manipulator)
sources.developer: DFKI Robotics Innovation Center with TH Koeln, Fraunhofer IGD, AMT GmbH
sources.title: AI Goes Subsea: Autonomous Welding Robot Debut
sources.claim: MARIOW research robot performed AI-guided, largely autonomous underwater flux-cored arc welding on submerged steel: cameras detect the joint, the system plans the path and welds, demonstrated in DFKI's underwater test ...; transition to real harbor conditions is still future work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered thermal tool work on submerged steel, the nearest robotic analogue to a diver burning or cutting wreck steel. It shows autonomous tool control has only just reached a fixtured workpiece in a purpose-built basin, with no rigging, lifting or debris handling, so it does not carry over to a whole salvage job.

sources.system: Hybrid-controlled BlueROV2 object-recovery system (CIRTESU tank)
sources.developer: Universitat Jaume I (Pedro J. Sanz et al.)
sources.title: Underwater Object Recovery Using a Hybrid-Controlled ROV with Deep Learning-Based Perception
sources.claim: A BlueROV2 with a small manipulator, deep-learning pose estimation and autonomous approach/grasp behaviours recovered a known object (a black-box mockup) in a 12x8x5 m robotics test tank, with the operator issuing only high-level commands.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous location, grasping and recovery of a discrete submerged object, which is the same act as recovering a small cargo item or piece of gear off the bottom, at comparable object size, in a purpose-built tank.

sources.system: Girona 500 I-AUV (TRIDENT project)
sources.developer: Universitat Jaume I / Universitat de Girona, EU FP7 consortium
sources.title: Trident submarine robot successfully tested at sea
sources.claim: The TRIDENT project's Girona 500 intervention AUV autonomously searched for, hooked and recovered a mockup black box on the seabed at Port of Soller, an end-of-project research trial with a lightweight purpose-made target.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous search and recovery of a single object from the bottom, the light end of recovering wreck cargo; the target was a lightweight mockup with a grasp fitting, so it does not transfer to heavy, entangled cargo or to powered tool work.

sources.system: Aquanaut (Mark 2) with Olympic Arm
sources.title: Nauticus Robotics Announces Results for Year-End 2024
sources.claim: Nauticus's untethered Aquanaut works offshore under supervisory autonomy, but as of its 2024 year-end report the company stated that fitting autonomous manipulators was still ahead of it, indicating autonomous subsea manipulation was not yet a fielded capability.
sources.transferJustification: Frontier check rather than transfer: the most advanced commercial autonomous subsea vehicle had not yet fielded autonomous manipulation, so no autonomous system can perform diver-grade salvage rigging or tool work.

sources.system: Hydrone-R resident vehicle / AUV light-intervention class
sources.title: ROV & AUV Technology 2026: Autonomous Subsea Robotics Transforming Offshore Inspection
sources.claim: A 2026 industry review of subsea robotics states that even light intervention - valve turning, flying-lead connection, retrieving a small component - from ... autonomous vehicle remains the frontier; resident vehicles such as Saipem's Hydrone-R do light intervention under supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Frontier check: if valve turning and small-part retrieval are still the frontier for autonomous subsea manipulation, then cutting, patching, rigging and charge placement on a wreck are well beyond current autonomy.

sources.system: CURV-21
sources.title: Underwater Robots and Key Technologies for Operation Control
sources.claim: Real deep-water naval salvage is executed with pilot-flown tethered vehicles: the CURV-21 work ROV with two 7-DoF manipulators recovered an F-35 from the South China Sea in March 2023 under continuous human control from the surface.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (wreck and cargo salvage) performed robotically, but under continuous teleoperation, so it cannot support a positive judgment; it establishes that fielded salvage robotics is pilot-driven.

sources.system: Work ROV used on Samantha J tug recovery
sources.title: ROV Recovery of Sunken Tug Samantha J
sources.claim: Commercial salvage ROV work on a sunken tug was flown by a surface crew: pilots lowered a clump weight at the wreck coordinates, inspected the wreck and navigated around tow ropes and debris before rigging the recovery.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in a commercial setting: robotic participation in vessel salvage is continuously piloted, confirming there is no autonomous field capability for this work.

tasks.label: Remove obstructions from strainers or marine railway or launching ways, using pneumatic or power hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ship afloat at a berth or anchorage: diver goes down on the hull to clear a fouled sea chest / seawater intake strainer — heavy marine growth, shells, plastic sheeting, rope and yard debris jammed in the grating. Works with hydraulic/pneumatic impact wrench to free grating bolts, scrapers and grinders on the bars, then refits the grating. Harbor water, 1-3 m visibility, tide and passing traffic.

Power plant or large pumping plant intake structure: diver clears logs, plastic, silt and shell buildup from submerged trash racks, intake strainers and screen sections that surface raking gear cannot reach, using airlift, pry bars and hydraulic/pneumatic tools; near-zero visibility, intake flow, confined bays, unit locked out.

Shipyard marine railway / launching ways: before a haul-out, diver works down the submerged inclined track and cradle rails clearing silt, gravel, timbers, lost hardware and marine growth off rails and rollers with airlift/dredge and pneumatic chipping or impact tools, checking track condition by feel in murky basin water.

Emergency call-out: a net, mooring line, tarp or timber is sucked hard onto a live sea suction or pump intake and cooling is lost; diver is dispatched, often at night, to locate the object by feel and cut/pry it clear with a hydraulic saw, grinder or chisel against suction and current, then confirm flow restored.

Municipal or small industrial pump station or marina: diver enters a wet well, forebay or lock chamber to clear rags, debris and grit from small intake screens, foot valves and strainer baskets using a pneumatic tool, hand tools and a suction hose; confined, dark, contaminated water.

sources.system: Brackett Bosker Bandit Automatic Trash Rake
sources.title: Brackett Bosker® Bandit Automatic Trash Rake | Ovivo
sources.claim: Ovivo's Brackett Bosker Bandit is an automatic trash rake installed at raw-water intakes (land drainage, nuclear, hydro, cooling water) whose grab teeth penetrate the bar screen and recover debris on a pre-programmed cycle, discharging it on deck without a diver.
sources.transferJustification: Same output as the diver instance (clearing obstructions from an intake strainer/rack), performed by a purpose-installed machine whose grab penetrates the bar screen and recovers the debris for deck disposal.

sources.system: Duperon Self-Cleaning Trashrack (SCT) / FlexRake
sources.title: Duperon® Self-Cleaning Trashrack (SCT)
sources.claim: Duperon's Self-Cleaning Trashrack is an automated front-cleaning screen used in stormwater, power and flood-control pump stations that lifts large debris (aquatic vegetation, tree stumps, engine blocks) off the rack continuously without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same output as the diver instance for intake screens and pump-station bar screens: obstructing debris is removed from the strainer and brought clear, by a machine in an installation built around it.

sources.system: StoneAge AutoBox 3L with Sentinel Automation Technology
sources.title: StoneAge | Automated Equipment for High-pressure Industrial Cleaning
sources.claim: StoneAge's Sentinel automation with the AutoBox tractor automatically positions high-pressure water lances and cleans hard deposits out of fixtured heat-exchanger tube bundles inside a purpose-built cleaning enclosure, including in poor visibility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing hard fouling and blockages from a fixtured perforated metal component with high-pressure powered tooling. Comparable objects (steel grating/strainer vs tube sheet), comparable precision, and exactly the E1 presentation (workpiece fixtured in a cleaning box).

sources.system: Active Contact Flange (ACF) Kit
sources.title: Active Contact Flange Kit - FerRobotics
sources.claim: FerRobotics' Active Contact Flange kits give industrial robots and cobots force-controlled powered tools that automate previously manual grinding, brushing, stripping and cleaning of fixtured metal workpieces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered abrasive material removal from fixtured steel parts. It transfers to knocking hard marine growth, scale and jammed material off a strainer plate or grating presented in a fixture, which is the diver's tool action.

sources.system: AMP Cortex
sources.title: AMP's Horowitz on Bringing AI to the Recycling World
sources.claim: AMP's Cortex robots autonomously identify and pick heterogeneous, irregular waste items (cartons, cans, cardboard, plastics) off moving conveyor lines in materials recovery facilities at high rate and accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: perceiving and grasping novel, irregular debris presented on a machine-built line. It covers the loose-debris (rag, plastic, wood) part of clearing a strainer once the strainer is presented to the machine at E1.

sources.system: Hibbard Inshore ROV dredging spread (Seabotix/Mohican/Navajo class ROVs)
sources.title: ROV Controlled Unmanned Dredging Adjacent to Active Intakes
sources.claim: Hibbard Inshore performs intake sediment and debris removal at pumping plants and hydro intakes with remotely operated vehicles instead of dive teams; the work is ROV-piloted from the surface, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-water analogue to the diver instances (clearing debris/sediment from intakes). Cited to establish that such in-water obstruction removal runs under continuous remote pilot control, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: EverClean / EverClean IQ hull robot
sources.title: Greensea IQ Unveils Its Most Advanced EverClean Service Robot
sources.claim: Greensea IQ's EverClean hull robots work in commercial ports and can groom hull areas autonomously, and the inspection variant images niche areas such as sea chests; the service is proactive biofilm grooming and inspection, not obstruction removal with power tools.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of autonomous in-water work on ship hulls: soft-brush grooming of flat plate and imaging of sea chests, with no powered clearing of jammed gratings — which is why in-water (E2/E3) completion of this task is not supported.

tasks.label: Drill holes in rock and rig explosives for underwater demolitions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Channel/harbor deepening: diver works the bottom in support of a drill barge over a rock ledge — locating and clearing silted-in blast holes, lowering and seating cartridge/emulsion charges and primers in the holes, stemming, and tying det cord downlines into the surface trunkline. Turbid tidal water, near-zero visibility by touch, current, rock bottom littered with boulders and dredge debris.

Small-scale rock removal at a berth, pier footing, or plant intake where a drill barge cannot reach: diver drills a pattern of blast holes in bedrock with a hand-held pneumatic/hydraulic sinker drill (e.g., Stanley SK58), blows out cuttings, loads and stems cartridge charges, and rigs the initiation network, working off the bottom in low visibility with tight standoff to existing structures.

Demolition of an underwater structure — old concrete bridge pier, cofferdam remnant, seawall, or wreck section: diver drills holes into concrete/rock with underwater drill, places cartridge or shaped charges, tapes/rigs the charge array, runs det cord and detonators to the surface, and verifies placement before firing.

Rock excavation for a pipeline/cable trench crossing a river, lake, or nearshore route: diver drills patterned holes in shallow riverbed rock, loads and stems charges, and connects the delay network, in silty freshwater with current, shifting bottom, and variable rock quality site to site.

Work inside an institution-controlled engineered water structure — hydro dam intake, lock chamber, powerhouse forebay, or dewatered-adjacent cofferdam — where the concrete geometry is surveyed and the utility controls access: diver drills holes in a rock plug/concrete face and rigs charges for a controlled shot.

sources.system: Pit Viper (autonomous surface blasthole drill rig)
sources.title: Epiroc's ground-breaking drill rig Pit Viper celebrates 25 years including a decade with autonomous operations
sources.claim: Epiroc's Pit Viper surface blasthole drill rigs drill rock autonomously and have been used autonomously at open-pit mines worldwide for about a decade — the closest deployed autonomy to 'drill holes in rock', but on dry open-pit benches and covering only drilling, not explosives loading or rigging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous blasthole drilling in rock. It covers only the drilling half of this task, is performed dry on a prepared open-pit bench by a large tracked rig, and includes no charge loading or det-cord rigging; it does not transfer to a diver-held drill on a submerged, silted rock bottom.

sources.system: Avatel (mechanized development charging system)
sources.title: Epiroc and Orica unveil prototype system for first stages of underground automation
sources.claim: The state of the art in mechanized explosives charging, Avatel, is only semi-autonomous: a single operator performs the entire charging cycle from ... machine's cabin, i.e. under continuous human control, and it works dry underground faces, not submerged rock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading and priming explosives into drilled blastholes. Even in a dry, institution-controlled underground heading the charging cycle remains operator-driven from a cabin, so it cannot substantiate autonomous charge rigging underwater.

sources.system: Drill-and-blast automation (OEM autonomous drill rigs and Avatel charging)
sources.developer: Industry review — Mine magazine (NRi Digital), covering Epiroc/Orica/Sandvik systems
sources.title: What's new in automated drilling and blasting? - Mine, Issue 139
sources.claim: Industry review of drill-and-blast automation as of 2024 finds autonomous drilling widely adopted while automation of the blasting/charging step remains at an early stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized drill-and-blast. Establishes that even on land, in the most automation-intensive setting, the explosives-rigging half of the task is not autonomous.

sources.system: ROVDrill seabed drilling and coring system
sources.developer: Helix Energy Solutions / Forum Energy Technologies
sources.title: ROVDrill GEOTECHNICAL SURVEYING ROV SYSTEM (Helix)
sources.claim: Subsea drilling into the seabed is done by remotely operated seabed drill modules launched from a vessel and run by surface operators — teleoperated coring/sampling, not autonomous blasthole drilling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling into rock on the seabed. Demonstrates that underwater rock drilling machines are surface-piloted ROV tools for geotechnical coring; they are teleoperated and do not load or rig explosives.

sources.system: UXO neutralisation ROV (Dstl-adapted remotely operated vehicle)
sources.developer: UK Defence Science and Technology Laboratory (Dstl) and industry partners
sources.title: Underwater robot could improve pipeline and cable security (Royal Navy)
sources.claim: The most advanced fielded underwater explosive-charge placement robot is a remotely operated vehicle that operators drive to place charges on unexploded ordnance; charge placement is remote-controlled, and no drilling of blast holes is involved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing explosive charges underwater. It is continuously operator-driven and places a single charge on an exposed object; it neither drills rock nor rigs a stemmed borehole initiation network.

sources.system: Underwater remote mining crawler (Ekati flooded open pit)
sources.developer: Burgundy Diamond Mines with IHC Mining
sources.title: Underwater Remote Mining - Burgundy Diamond Mines Ltd
sources.claim: Underwater rock excavation by machine at a flooded open pit is performed by a remotely operated crawler that cuts rock mechanically and explicitly avoids the use of explosives.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine removal of submerged rock. Shows the fielded underwater approach is a surface-piloted cutter that substitutes for, rather than performs, drill-and-blast work.

tasks.label: Remove rubbish or pollution from the sea.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Seabed debris cleanup inside a port, marina or commercial waterfront basin: diver descends under berths, piers and moorings and recovers bottles, cans, tyres, cable, scrap metal and small dumped items into lift baskets/bags, working in port-controlled water with limited visibility and traffic control by the harbourmaster.

Boat-based cleanup dive in open nearshore coastal water off a beach, island or anchorage: scattered small litter (bottles, cans, plastic, small tyres) on sand and rock bottom in generally good visibility, collected and lifted to the support boat.

Entanglement- and hazard-heavy environmental jobs in open coastal water: cutting derelict fishing nets, pots and lines free of wrecks, reefs, pilings and moorings, and pollution-response diving at spill sites (locating and plugging fuel leaks on sunken vessels, recovering drums and oiled debris) in contaminated, low-visibility, current-swept water.

Clearing rubbish fouling a vessel's running gear at berth or anchorage: cutting and pulling ropes, nets, plastic sheet and shopping-trolley-type debris off propellers, shafts, rope guards, thrusters and sea-chest gratings without damaging blades, seals or coatings.

Debris clearance at industrial water intakes: diving on trash racks, bar screens, pump bays and intake tunnels at power plants, dams and municipal intakes to remove logs, weed, plastic, tyres and other rubbish blocking the submerged screens, usually in zero visibility with residual flow.

Bulky junk removal from inland and nearshore public waters (lakes, rivers, canals, public boat ramps, storm-damaged shorelines): locating and rigging bicycles, shopping carts, tyres, appliances, small sunken craft and construction debris for lift, in murky freshwater with current and snag hazards.

sources.system: SeaClear2.0 (SeaCat USV + detection/collection ROVs + crane gripper, Subsea Tech / TU Delft)
sources.developer: SeaClear2.0 consortium (TU Delft, Subsea Tech, TUM, Fraunhofer and partners)
sources.title: Robot clean-up crews tackle litter on Europe's seabed | Horizon Magazine
sources.claim: SeaClear2.0's uncrewed multi-robot system autonomously scanned and cleaned an area of a Marseille marina seabed, recovering tyres, fences, car seats and ...; project staff note humans still supervise the system.

sources.system: SeaClear2.0
sources.title: The future of ocean cleanup: robots on the seabed | European Commission Research and Innovation
sources.claim: At the Port of Hamburg live showcase in May 2025 the SeaClear2.0 system detected, grabbed, lifted and transported a large tyre from the port bottom to shore automatically; the system is being tested in clear (Dubrovnik, Larnaca) and low-visibility (Venice, Hamburg) waters.

sources.system: SeaClear (multi-robot seabed litter collection system)
sources.developer: SeaClear H2020 consortium (TU Delft, TUM, Subsea Tech, Fraunhofer, DUNEA, HCMR)
sources.title: Cleaning up our oceans with smart robots | CORDIS
sources.claim: The SeaClear project demonstrated a multi-robot system that autonomously searches for, identifies and collects litter from the seabed, presented as an alternative to expensive and dangerous diver-based removal.

sources.system: SeaClear collection ROV (Tortuga) with suction-gripper and collection basket
sources.developer: SeaClear consortium / TU Delft, TUM, Subsea Tech
sources.title: The SeaClear system: An intelligent multi-robot solution for autonomous cleanup of marine debris on the seabed - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed description of SeaClear field trials in open coastal water at the Lokrum test site near Dubrovnik: the collection ROV grasped a bottle on the seafloor ... in-gripper camera identification and deposited it into a collection basket.

sources.system: SeaClear prototype (2022 Hamburg trial)
sources.title: Building the first robots to clean up ocean floor litter (Tech Xplore / CORDIS)
sources.claim: Early SeaClear prototype trials in the Port of Hamburg showed very low visibility (often centimetres) and heavy ship traffic prevented camera-based litter detection, and that the integrated prototype did not yet run fully autonomously.

sources.system: Brackett Bosker Automatic Trash Rake / Brackett Green Cable Hauled Raking Machine
sources.title: Brackett Bosker Automatic Trash Rake | Ovivo
sources.claim: Commercially supplied automatic trash rake machines provide fully automated, 24-hour removal of debris from cooling-water and other water intake screens, raking, conveying and discharging the rubbish into a skip without divers or manual raking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: divers clear rubbish (logs, weed, plastic, tyres) fouling submerged intake trash racks and bar screens. The raking machine removes the same debris from the same racks in a purpose-built intake structure built around the machine, delivering the same accepted output (clear screens) continuously and unattended.

tasks.label: Perform offshore oil or gas exploration or extraction duties, such as conducting underwater surveys or repairing and maintaining drilling rigs or platforms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-water survey/general visual inspection at a producing offshore field: swim/fly the pipeline, flowline, riser base, wellhead/manifold and surrounding seabed; record video/stills, note spans, exposures, scour, debris and anode/CP condition; deliver an integrity data package.

Inspection support around a drilling unit or wellsite: visual checks of BOP, wellhead, riser, guide funnels and subsea equipment; dropped-object searches; watching/monitoring equipment landings and commissioning operations, often on short notice in poor weather.

Routine (Level I) structural inspection of a fixed platform jacket: swim the legs, braces, risers, caissons, conductors and anodes; video/photograph condition, damage, missing members and marine-growth extent; no cleaning or contact NDT. Shallow, turbid, current- and surge-affected water.

Detailed (Level II/III) inspection: remove marine growth to bare metal at nodes/welds with hydro-jet and hand tools, then close visual inspection, ultrasonic wall thickness, MPI/ACFM or flooded-member detection, and contact CP stab readings, reporting to inspection-engineer quality in low visibility.

Light subsea intervention: operating pipeline/production valves and panel interfaces, making hydraulic hot-stab connections, fitting or changing out small components and instruments, connecting hoses and tooling at a wellhead or PLEM.

Heavy repair, construction and removal work: installing repair clamps/sleeves and anode retrofits, torquing flange bolts, guiding and connecting spools/jumpers, rigging heavy lifts and lift bags, jetting/grouting, oxy-arc burning and cropping of piles/members during repair or decommissioning, and wet welding of patches or doublers.

sources.system: Hydrone-R Underwater Intervention Drone
sources.developer: Saipem (for Equinor, Njord field, Norwegian Sea)
sources.title: Saipem's Underwater Drone Carries Out Autonomous Survey at Njord Field
sources.claim: Saipem's Hydrone-R resident underwater intervention drone performs autonomous inspection and survey missions on subsea assets at Equinor's operating Njord field under a 10-year commercial service contract, staying resident on the seabed for months.

sources.system: Freedom AUV
sources.title: Oceaneering Conducts Freedom AUV Pipeline Inspection Pilot for TotalEnergies
sources.claim: Oceaneering's Freedom AUV autonomously inspected over 120 km of subsea pipelines for TotalEnergies, detecting and tracking the pipeline and gathering the required inspection data in a single pass.

sources.system: Aquanaut Mark 2
sources.title: US autonomous underwater robot starts commercial ops in Gulf of Mexico
sources.claim: Nauticus Robotics' Aquanaut Mark 2 completed untethered autonomous qualification work on subsea assets at a decommissioned field offshore Louisiana and entered commercial operations in the Gulf of Mexico.

sources.system: FiGS CP Inspection system on AUVs
sources.title: FiGS & AUVs: Revolutionizing subsea inspection
sources.claim: AUV-mounted FiGS field-gradient sensors are used commercially to survey cathodic-protection performance of subsea pipelines and structures without contact, replacing diver/ROV anode stab readings for survey-level CP assessment.

sources.system: state-of-the-art review of inspection AUVs/I-AUVs
sources.developer: ROSEN Creation Center / University of Bielefeld
sources.title: Inspection and maintenance of industrial infrastructure with autonomous underwater robots
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of autonomous underwater inspection/maintenance: AUVs are already used for general visual inspection, but detailed and close visual inspection require cleaning of the structure, ... remains very difficult for autonomous vehicles.

sources.system: Girona 500 intervention AUV
sources.developer: University of Girona (reported in Frontiers review)
sources.title: Inspection and maintenance of industrial infrastructure with autonomous underwater robots
sources.claim: An intervention AUV autonomously docked on a purpose-built mockup subsea control panel, visually detected a marked valve and turned it with an onboard manipulator, and performed hot-stab receptacle detection using markers.

sources.system: MARIOW underwater welding robot
sources.developer: DFKI Robotics Innovation Center, Fraunhofer IGD, TH Köln consortium
sources.title: AI Goes Subsea: Autonomous Welding Robot Debut
sources.claim: The MARIOW system performed AI-based weld-joint detection, automated path planning and ... underwater flux-cored arc welding in a purpose-built underwater test basin; transition to real harbour conditions with salt water, waves and currents is still future work.

sources.system: Bravo Marine mini ROV cleaning system
sources.title: Mini robots clean platforms underwater — Chevron
sources.claim: Marine-growth removal from offshore platform structures is done today by piloted mini ROVs with scraper arms and high-pressure nozzles, tested by Chevron in Thailand; the vehicle is remotely operated rather than autonomous.

sources.system: Armach hull service robot / EverClean service
sources.title: Armach Robotics Launchs of EverClean
sources.claim: Armach's EverClean hull service robots autonomously navigate a ship's submerged steel hull in port, removing fouling and georeferencing hull-condition data to its location on the structure, delivered as a commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-water hull inspection/grooming of ships at a berth. Transfer to Level I platform structural GVI is partial but direct: both require autonomous close-proximity navigation over a large submerged steel structure with camera-based, position-referenced condition recording; it does not cover contact NDT or heavy growth removal.

sources.system: intervention AUVs generally (incl. Saab Sabertooth, Nauticus Aquanaut)
sources.developer: ROSEN Creation Center / University of Bielefeld (review)

roles.title: Locksmiths and Safe Repairers
roles.description: Repair and open locks, make keys, change locks and safe combinations, and install and repair safes.

tasks.label: Cut new or duplicate keys, using impressions or code key machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop/hardware-store counter duplication: a customer hands over a standard residential or commercial pin-tumbler key (Kwikset/Schlage/Yale, sometimes worn); the worker identifies the keyway, pulls the matching blank from the board, cuts it on a duplicator, deburrs it, and hands back a key that must turn the customer's lock.

Origination by code in the shop: cutting one or several keys to a specified bitting from a code machine or code software (rekey jobs, master-key systems, replacement keys for file cabinets/padlocks, keys cut to a keyway/bitting derived from a lock code), then checking them against the cylinder or pinning kit.

Automotive keys: cutting edge-cut or high-security laser/sidewinder blades either duplicated from a customer's working key or cut by code obtained from the VIN/key code, using an electronic key machine with the correct jaw, in the shop or in the van (programming handled separately).

Mobile service call: cutting keys on the van's machine at a residence or business during a rekey, lock change, or lockout — carrying blanks and machine to an as-found site, cutting several keys to the new bitting, and trying each key in the installed cylinders.

Originating a key by impressioning on an installed lock with no key and no code: inserting a blank into the cylinder, torquing and rocking it, reading marks under light, filing the marks, and repeating until the key turns the lock — done on-site at a door or vehicle.

sources.system: KeyMe key duplication kiosk
sources.title: KeyMe Locksmiths, Leading Key Duplication Kiosk Service, Begins 2026 With New National Retail Collaborations
sources.claim: KeyMe self-service key-duplication kiosks use multiple cameras and machine-learning analysis of the inserted key, then cut a duplicate on the spot; they are deployed unattended in thousands of US retail stores (Walmart, Kroger, 7-Eleven, Meijer, WinCo, military exchanges).

sources.system: KeyMe key duplication kiosk
sources.title: What Types of Keys You Can and Can't Copy at a KeyMe Kiosk
sources.claim: KeyMe kiosks duplicate standard house, office, mailbox and cabinet keys and select automotive keys; restricted or highly encrypted keys are refused and routed to a locksmith, i.e. the machine screens the work it can accept.

sources.system: KeyMe key duplication kiosk
sources.title: What types of keys are available to cut at the KeyMe kiosk?
sources.claim: KeyMe kiosks hold blank stock internally and dispense the finished cut key immediately for common brass keys, and cover a very large automotive key database (support cited for over 38,000 make/model/years), with less common blanks shipped instead.

sources.system: minuteKEY self-service key duplication kiosk
sources.title: Minutekey self-service key duplication kiosk taps USAT for cashless payments
sources.claim: minuteKEY (Hillman) self-service key duplicating kiosks use internal robotics to select a blank and cut a duplicate unattended, and have operated for years in Lowe's and Walmart stores nationwide, replacing employee key cutting.

sources.system: Ilco (Silca) Futura Pro / Futura Pro One electronic key cutting machine
sources.title: Ilco Futura Pro One
sources.claim: The Ilco/Silca Futura Pro and Futura Pro One are CNC electronic key machines that originate (cut by code), decode and copy laser, dimple, cruciform and edge-cut keys once the key is held in the machine's quick-change jaw; the compact version is sold for mobile/van service.

sources.system: Xhorse Dolphin XP-005 / XP-005L automatic key cutting machine
sources.title: How to use Xhorse Dolphin XP005 Key Cutting Machine?
sources.claim: The Xhorse Dolphin XP-005 is a portable, battery-powered automatic key cutting machine used by mobile locksmiths: the operator clamps the blank and enters a key code or selects the vehicle, the bitting is generated automatically, and the machine mills the key; it also decodes an original key and cuts a copy.

sources.system: Automatic originating/code key machines (class description)
sources.title: Key Cutting Machines | An Ultimate Guide From A Locksmith Professional
sources.claim: Trade guidance for locksmiths describes automatic originating (code) key machines as computer-driven: the operator's work is in the software telling the machine what to cut, with the machine performing the cutting.

tasks.label: Insert new or repaired tumblers into locks to change combinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop or van bench: locksmith rekeys standard residential pin-tumbler cylinders (Kwikset/Schlage knob and deadbolt plugs) to a new key, keying several alike — pulls the plug with a follower, dumps old bottom pins, seats new pins from a pinning kit per the new bitting, reassembles, tests with old and new keys.

On-site residential service call after a move-in, tenant change or lost key: cylinders are pulled from the front/back doors at the house, repinned on a porch step or tailgate, reinstalled and tested; mixed brands, worn or dirty cylinders, weather and pets present.

Commercial/institutional master key work: repinning mortise, rim and small-format interchangeable-core cylinders to a master keying schedule (master wafers/pins in specified chambers), performed at the shop bench or in a building's maintenance area, verified against change key, master key and grand master.

Mechanical safe/vault combination lock at a business (jeweler, pharmacy, retail back office): technician opens the lock's back cover and changes the combination by repositioning or replacing wheel-pack tumblers/flies (or fitting a new wheel pack), then tests the new combination repeatedly before closing the door.

Wafer-tumbler locks: fitting new wafers and springs into an automotive door/ignition cylinder, or a desk/cabinet/file lock, to match a newly cut key — work done on the shop bench or curbside next to the customer's vehicle.

tasks.label: Move picklocks in cylinders to open door locks without keys.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Emergency residential lockout: locksmith arrives at a house or apartment, kneels at an exterior entry door and picks a keyed knob lock or deadbolt (Kwikset/Schlage-class pin tumbler, sometimes spool pins, weathered or worn), working at whatever door height/orientation exists, in variable light and weather, expected to open non-destructively within minutes while the customer waits.

Commercial/institutional lockout: office suite, retail store, school or medical building; picks a mortise or rim cylinder, lever-set or interchangeable core, often higher-grade with security pins and tight keyways, during business hours with staff present; may need several doors opened after a key loss.

On-site auxiliary lock picked at a customer's home or office: desk lock, filing cabinet, cabinet cam lock, mailbox, or padlock on a gate/shed; small wafer or pin-tumbler cylinders, often in cramped or awkward positions, lock still mounted in the furniture or hasp.

Automotive/roadside lockout: at the curb or in a parking lot, picking a vehicle door wafer lock with a Lishi-type pick/decoder (or picking a glovebox/trunk lock), in traffic and weather, with damage to paint and trim unacceptable.

Shop bench work: customer brings a lock to the counter and it is clamped in a vise and picked open — mixed population including removed door cylinders, commercial cores, security-pinned and higher-security locks, tubular and wafer cabinet locks.

Shop bench work, easy subset: a low-security pin-tumbler padlock (e.g., common hardware-store padlock) brought in without a key, held in a vise and opened by raking/tensioning at the bench with no time pressure.

It shows a deployed robot in this trade, but it turns an exposed external dial through a coarse mechanical search; it performs no pick-in-keyway tactile manipulation of pin stacks, so it does not transfer to picking door cylinders and is not used to support any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Cut new or duplicate keys, using key cutting machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Counter duplication in a locksmith shop or hardware/big-box key counter: customer hands over a standard edge-cut residential/commercial key (Kwikset KW1, Schlage SC1/SC4, mailbox, padlock). Worker identifies the keyway, pulls the matching blank from a peg board, clamps original and blank in a duplicator, cuts, deburrs on the wire wheel, and hands it over; often 2-4 copies.

Cutting keys by code at the shop bench on a computerized code machine: new keys for cylinders just rekeyed or pinned, master-key system keys, or a replacement cut from a manufacturer code / bitting list when no original exists. Often a batch of several keys, sometimes stamped or engraved, then tested in the cylinder.

On-site cutting from the mobile service van at a customer's house, small business, or parking lot: after decoding or impressioning a lock during a rekey or lockout call, the locksmith cuts the key on a van-mounted duplicator/code machine (12V or inverter power, sometimes in cold, rain, or poor light) and tests it in the lock while the customer waits.

Automotive key blades: cutting a laser/sidewinder or edge-cut transponder blank from the customer's original key, from the VIN-derived code, or from a decoded door lock, on a laser/electronic key machine at the shop or in the van, before or alongside transponder/fob programming.

Unusual or restricted keys: dimple, cruciform, tubular, safe-deposit and cabinet keys, or patented high-security keyways (Medeco angled cuts, Mul-T-Lock, Abloy) requiring authorization paperwork, special jaws/adapters or a dedicated machine, and sometimes hand finishing.

tasks.label: Open safe locks by drilling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential lockout: technician goes to a customer's home where a gun safe or small fire/burglary safe has a lost combination or a dead/failed electronic lock. He identifies the make/model, sets a magnetic-base drill rig on the door or side, drills a small hole at the charted drill point, inspects the lock with a borescope, manipulates or punches the lock to retract the boltwork, opens the door, then plugs the hole and repairs/replaces the lock. Safe is often wedged in a closet, basement, or bolted to a floor at an awkward angle.

Small-business on-site opening: retail back office, restaurant, pharmacy, or jeweler's shop with a B-rate or TL-rated safe, drop safe, or depository whose combination is lost, whose keypad failed, or whose door linkage jammed. Model may be unidentified or a legacy unit; technician must choose the drill point, cut through hardplate with carbide/diamond bits without tripping glass or thermal relockers, scope, manipulate, and open, working in cramped space during business hours.

Bank / institutional job: branch vault door, TL-30 composite safe, ATM safe, or a batch of safe deposit boxes to be drilled under bank staff supervision with audit/witness requirements. High-security barriers (hardplate, ball bearings, glass relockers), strict requirement to preserve and recertify the container, and precise drill-point work from proprietary charts.

Shop job: safe delivered to or dropped at the locksmith's shop (estate, auction, repossession, or moved unit). Technician works on it at a bench with rigs, jigs, full tooling and reference charts, drills at leisure, opens, then restores and repairs the lock and hole.

Difficult field job: fire- or burglary-damaged safe, safe in a storage unit, jobsite trailer, boat, or vehicle, or a unit lying on its back or with a distorted door. Drill point must be improvised from scratch, multiple holes may be needed, and access, lighting, and power are as found.

sources.system: SparkFun Safe Cracker (safe-cracking robot)
sources.title: Building a Safe Cracking Robot - SparkFun Learn
sources.claim: The SparkFun Safe Cracker is an autonomous ~$200 robot that magnetically attaches to a low-security combination fire safe, dials and measures the wheel pack, and opened a safe live at DEF CON 25; it is non-destructive (no drilling) and is explicitly limited to very low security combination fire safes.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic system to safe opening, but it addresses a different method (autodialing/manipulation, not drilling) and the page states it is designed only for very low security combination fire safes; it cannot locate drill points, cut hardplate, defeat relockers, or scope and manipulate a lock through a hole, so it does not substantiate this task at any tier.

sources.system: ADUbot (FANUC CRX-25iA cobot drilling unit)
sources.title: FANUC PARTNERS WITH ELECTROIMPACT & LUEBBERING TO AUTOMATE AIRFRAME DRILLING
sources.claim: The ADUbot pairs a FANUC CRX-25iA cobot with Electroimpact/Luebbering drilling units to automate high-tolerance hole drilling in aircraft structures, replacing hand-held drill-jig work in an aerospace assembly cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic drilling of precise holes in fixtured metal structures. It shows a robot can execute a pre-planned hole, but not the substance of safe drilling: identifying an unknown container, selecting a drill point from charts, penetrating hardplate/ball bearings without tripping relockers, then borescope inspection and manipulation of the lock to retract boltwork. No cited demonstration covers those steps.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot

sources.claim: The Hilti Jaibot is a ... deployed on construction sites that drills anchor holes in concrete and, more recently, corrugated metal deck, executing hole positions from digitally planned BIM data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous mobile drilling in an unstructured (E3) jobsite. It substantiates only pre-planned hole drilling into building substrate; it has no capability to diagnose a safe lock, choose a drill point, cut hardplate, or manipulate a lock mechanism through the hole, so it does not substantiate this task.

tasks.label: Set up and maintain master key systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Design/expansion of the system: survey a client facility door by door (door number, existing hardware, keyway, who must be admitted), build the keying matrix and bitting list in master-keying software, produce pinning charts and key-stamping lists, and keep key-issuance records current. Locksmith shop office plus walk-through of the client's building.

Shop bench pinning: pin up a batch of 20-60 cylinders, plugs and SFIC cores to the keying chart - bottom pins, master wafers, top pins, springs, caps/sealing - for mixed hardware (Schlage/Corbin mortise, rim, KIK, Best cores); bench-test every cylinder with its change key, submaster and grand master before labeling.

Key production for the system: cut change keys, submasters and masters to the specified code/bitting on shop code machines, gauge and verify depths and spacing, then stamp or mark each key with its key symbol and 'DO NOT DUPLICATE', tag and bag by door. Locksmith shop.

On-site changeover for a new or rekeyed system in an occupied building (office suite, school wing, apartment complex, retail chain): remove existing cylinders/knob and mortise hardware from dozens of assorted doors, install newly pinned cylinders or swap interchangeable cores, deal with worn or misaligned hardware, function-test every key in every door, hand over keys and get sign-off.

Maintenance service call on an existing system: key lost or employee terminated - travel to the site, pull the affected cylinders at the doors (or swap cores), re-pin to a new change key while preserving master operation, cut and mark replacements, verify masters and submasters still operate, update the bitting chart and key records.

tasks.label: Install door hardware, such as locks and closers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: install or replace a keyed entry knob/lever and a deadbolt on a homeowner's exterior door. Door is already hung; locksmith may bore a new 2-1/8" hole with a jig, chisel latch and strike mortises, shim/align to an out-of-square frame, mount and test.

Commercial/institutional building: replace or install a cylindrical or mortise lockset, lever trim or cylinder in a hollow-metal or solid-core door at an office, school, retail store or apartment common door, working around occupants and matching existing prep.

Install a surface-mounted overhead door closer on a commercial door: tape template, drill and tap the hollow-metal door/frame, mount closer body and arm, set arm preload, then adjust sweep, latch speed and backcheck and verify ADA closing force.

Install exit device/panic hardware or electrified hardware at a commercial site: mount rim or mortise exit device, install electric strike or maglock in the frame, run wiring through frame/raceway, mount reader or keypad, and verify fire/egress operation.

New construction or multi-unit turnover: install locksets, deadbolts and strikes on many newly hung doors at an active jobsite or apartment building, working from a hardware schedule amid dust, debris and other trades.

sources.claim: BETH Sondermaschinen's automated door production line machines door leaves (handle/key milling, lock case milling) and then performs lock assembly with a robot feeding locks from magazines and automated bolting, at 3.3 doors/minute, in a customer's plant.

tasks.label: Keep records of company locks and keys.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Disassemble mechanical or electrical locking devices, and repair or replace worn tumblers, springs, and other parts, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop or van bench work on pin-tumbler cylinders (key-in-knob, deadbolt, rim and mortise cylinders): pull the cam/retainer, push the plug with a follower, dump worn pins and springs, re-pin to a customer key or master-key chart, reassemble, lubricate and test. Small brass pins ~2 mm and light springs; mixed brands, some dirty or corroded.

On-site repair of commercial/institutional door hardware in an office, school or hospital: disassemble a mortise lock body, cylindrical lever lockset or exit-device chassis at the door, diagnose the failed part (broken latch or retractor spring, worn hub, bent spindle), replace it from van stock, reassemble and test against frame and strike.

Residential service call at a private home: take apart a worn or sticking knobset/deadbolt on the customer's door - remove screws, separate the chassis, replace worn springs, tailpiece, latch or retaining clips - on a varied, sometimes swollen or misaligned door, kneeling in an entryway with the homeowner present.

Repair of electrified/electronic locking devices at a commercial site: electric strike, electrified mortise lock, motor-driven or solenoid keypad/smart lock. Disassemble the housing, test and replace a burnt solenoid, worn motor, broken spring, clutch or gear/board, reassemble, re-wire and verify with the access-control system.

Automotive lock work at the vehicle or van bench: remove and rebuild a worn door or ignition wafer/sidebar cylinder - disassemble the cylinder, replace worn wafers and springs, key it to the customer's key or code, reassemble and refit.

Safe/vault lock service at a business or in the shop: disassemble a Group 2 mechanical combination lock (wheel pack, spline keys, drive cam, lever spring) or an electronic safe lock (solenoid, motor, board), replace worn parts, reassemble, reset the combination and verify.

An operator loads each cylinder.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory pinning of lock cylinders rather than repair of a worn one. Same objects (plug, pins, springs, cut key) and precision as bench re-pinning, in a fixtured purpose-built station, so the parts-replacement step of cylinder repair transfers at E1.
