sources.developer: University of Birmingham Autonomous Remanufacturing Laboratory
sources.title: An experimental human-robot collaborative disassembly cell - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed remanufacturing work reports that disassembly of used products remains overwhelmingly manual, with robotic disassembly at the experimental collaborative-cell stage - no fielded system performs diagnose-replace-reassemble repair of used mechanical assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as context for the negative judgments on repair of varied used hardware; establishes that robotic teardown-and-rebuild of used devices is not fielded.

sources.system: Physical Intelligence robot (Robot Olympics key/tool-use event), assessed by Epoch AI
sources.developer: Physical Intelligence; assessment by Epoch AI
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 - Epoch AI
sources.claim: As of early 2026, general-purpose robots' fine manipulation at locks is at lab stage: the best key-in-lock demonstration is about 5x slower than a human, trained on the specific locks, with no transfer to other locks or ... roughly 52% reliability across the task suite.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting and turning a key at a door. It bounds current in-situ dexterity at locks: if key turning is a frontier lab skill, on-site disassembly and spring replacement inside lock hardware is well beyond fielded capability.

tasks.label: Repair and adjust safes, vault doors, and vault components, using hand tools, lathes, drill presses, and welding and acetylene cutting apparatus.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Service call at a bank or credit union: diagnose and repair a vault door — worn/binding boltwork, sagging hinges, failed time lock or combination lock, misaligned day gate. Tech works in the vault vestibule with hand tools, drill rig, portable grinder, sometimes welding a hardplate patch after a lockout drill, then re-aligns, lubricates, re-times and cycle-tests the door.

Commercial site (jewelry store, pharmacy, restaurant, gun shop, cash-handling office): repair a TL-rated safe or depository — dead electronic/mechanical lock, broken relocker, sheared handle spindle, jammed bolt. Diagnose, drill and scope the container, replace the lock body, weld/plug the drill hole, dress the paint, adjust boltwork and verify operation.

Shop bench work: safe, vault component or lock body brought into the locksmith's shop. Disassemble, measure worn parts, turn a replacement spindle/bolt or bushing on the lathe, drill and tap on the drill press, weld/braze cracked parts, then hand-fit, adjust tolerances and cycle-test until the mechanism runs correctly.

Routine on-site adjustment/servicing at commercial or institutional premises: clean and lubricate a combination lock and boltwork, adjust dial ring and drive cam, tighten hinges, replace worn handle or dial, correct door drag, change the combination and verify with the customer.

Residential call: repair a home safe or gun safe in a closet, basement or garage — cramped, poorly lit, safe bolted to floor or wall, unknown make/model, customer's belongings around it. Diagnose the fault, drill or dismantle as needed, replace lock or repair boltwork, patch and finish, and leave the safe operating.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 Robotic Welding Cells
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 intelligent welding cells autonomously scan fixtured steel parts, plan weld paths without programming, and are deployed in fabrication ... in the US and Canada — the closest commercial capability to the welding sub-step of safe/vault repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production welding of steel weldments. It transfers only to the welding sub-step (e.g., welding a patch over a drilled hole) on fixtured, pre-fitted parts inside a fenced cell; it does not cover diagnosing a safe fault, drilling/scoping a lock, machining and hand-fitting replacement parts, or re-adjusting and testing boltwork, which is the bulk of this task.

sources.system: Path Robotics Rove (Obsidian AI)
sources.title: Path Robotics unveils mobile robotic welding system combining AI and quadruped mobility
sources.claim: Path Robotics announced 'Rove', a quadruped-mounted mobile welding system to bring adaptive welding to large workpieces in the field (shipbuilding, heavy construction) rather than fixturing them in a cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field welding of large fabricated assemblies. Even if mature, it addresses only laying weld beads on accessible seams; it provides no diagnosis, disassembly, machining, fitting or mechanical adjustment of a safe lock or vault boltwork.

sources.system: Autonomous e-waste unscrewing robot (UR10e + mechatronic screwdriver)
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A research system using a UR10e arm, RealSense D405 vision and a custom mechatronic screwdriver autonomously locates and removes screws from electronic waste — an autonomous disassembly sub-step demonstrated on a lab bench.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous disassembly of unknown consumer devices. It shows fastener removal on lightweight, accessible devices in a bench setup; it does not transfer to hardplate drilling, heavy boltwork, machining of replacement parts, or the fitting and adjustment that define safe and vault repair.

sources.system: SparkFun safe-cracking robot; ITL-2000 autodialer
sources.title: Building a Safe Cracking Robot - SparkFun Learn
sources.claim: Purpose-built safe-cracking robots (e.g., the SparkFun autodialer and commercial autodialers such as the ITL-2000) autonomously turn a safe dial to find an unknown combination and open the container — automation of opening, not of repair or adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening a locked safe (a different O*NET task). These devices only rotate a dial through combinations on one clamped-on container; they perform no diagnosis, no disassembly, no machining, welding or mechanical adjustment, so they cannot substantiate repair of safes, vault doors or vault components.

tasks.label: Install alarm and electronic access systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied commercial/institutional building (office suite, school, clinic): install electronic access control on a set of existing doors — mortise/drill door and frame, mount card reader and electric strike or maglock, fish and terminate low-voltage cable to the controller, mount power supply and panel, program credentials, test fail-safe/fail-secure operation and door position switches while staff work around the job.

Occupied private home: install a burglar alarm system — mount control panel and keypad, place door/window contacts, motion detectors, glass-break sensors and siren in varied rooms, route wiring or wireless-enroll devices, connect power and communicator, walk-test and instruct the homeowner.

Retrofit electronic/smart locks on doors at a small business or across apartment units: remove existing hardware, adjust or re-machine door prep, mount the electronic lockset and strike, fit batteries or wire a hardwired unit, enroll fobs/codes in management software, verify latching and code-compliant egress on doors of varying age, sag and material.

New construction or tenant fit-out: rough-in access control and alarm — mount back boxes and conduit stubs, drill and pull low-voltage cable through studs, joists and above ceiling grid on an active construction site, then return after finishes to trim out devices, terminate at the head-end panel and commission the system.

Locksmith shop bench prep: assemble and pre-wire an access control head-end enclosure — mount the controller board, power supply, relays and terminal blocks on the backplate, cut, label and land the interconnecting wires per the job drawing, and bench-test before the enclosure goes to site.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot - Hilti Corporation
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a semi-autonomous jobsite robot deployed on construction projects that marks and drills overhead holes for MEP/electrical and ceiling anchors from a BIM model; it automates only the hole-drilling sub-step, with an operator setting it up and humans installing anchors and devices.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed in-building installation robot: it drills anchor holes ... electrical/MEP work, one sub-step of mounting alarm/access hardware. It does not mount devices, pull or terminate low-voltage cable, or commission systems, so it cannot complete the whole task.

sources.system: Averex robotic wiring centre (Kiesling / Rittal)
sources.title: CDA Magazine - How automation became a reality
sources.claim: The Kiesling/Rittal Averex robotic wiring centre is a commercial portal-robot cell that automatically makes the wire connections between devices on a control-cabinet mounting plate fixtured inside a purpose-built panel-production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wiring of an electrical control cabinet. Objects (DIN-rail components, terminal blocks, stranded low-voltage wire), precision, and fixtured-backplate presentation match bench pre-wiring of an alarm/access-control head-end enclosure.

sources.system: Averex portal robot (Kiesling/Rittal automated cabinet wiring)
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (Springer)
sources.claim: An independent 2025 account of the same system confirms a full automated wiring cycle inside the machine: cutting, crimping, connecting both wire ends to terminals and routing the wire inside the cabinet.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: fixtured-cabinet wiring corresponds to shop pre-wiring of an access-control panel backplate; it does not transfer to in-building device mounting, cable pulling through structure, or system commissioning.

sources.system: CNC door machining centres (industry survey)
sources.title: How Automation Is Transforming Door Manufacturing - ELMENS
sources.claim: In door manufacturing, CNC machining centres automate lock-pocket routing, hinge mortising and core boring on fixtured doors, but hardware installation itself remains manual and has resisted automation at scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory door prep and lock hardware fitting. It shows that even with the door fixtured in a purpose-built line, mounting lock/reader hardware is not an automated capability, bounding the E1 counterfactual for electronic lock installation.

tasks.label: Install safes, vault doors, and deposit boxes according to blueprints, using equipment such as power drills, taps, dies, truck cranes, and dollies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential home/gun safe installation: technician delivers a 300–1,000 lb safe to a private house, moves it on a dolly or stair-climber through doorways and down stairs or into a closet/garage, positions it per the customer's wishes, then drills through the safe base into a wood subfloor or concrete slab and sets anchor bolts, shimming to level. Layout, floor type, obstacles and access differ at every house.

Small commercial safe install at a business (retail back office, restaurant, dispensary, jewelry store): deposit/TL-15 or under-counter safe wheeled in on a dolly, set in a cash room or under a counter, anchor holes drilled in the concrete slab, safe bolted down, door swing and lock/relocker operation verified after mounting. Premises are controlled by the business but the room layout is as-found.

Bank/credit union safe deposit box work: install or replace modular deposit-box nests inside an existing vault per the architect's layout drawing — set nests plumb and level on the vault floor, bolt nests to each other and to floor/wall, align fronts, and verify every box door, guard lock and nose operates.

Vault door / modular vault installation on a new-build or remodel per blueprints: rough opening prepared by others, door and frame delivered by truck crane or pallet jack, frame set plumb, square and level in the opening, anchored and grouted, door hung on hinges, then hinges, boltwork and time lock adjusted until the door swings and locks correctly. Active construction site with other trades, debris and no finished floor.

Heavy safe rigging and anchoring in an existing commercial building: 2,000+ lb TL-30 safe moved from the truck with a crane, gantry or stair-climbing rigging, through tight doorways or a freight elevator to a basement or upper floor, then leveled and anchored to the floor; sometimes floor loading checked and steel plate or blocking added.

sources.system: DEWALT / August Robotics autonomous floor-drilling robot (Lionel-based)
sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) and August Robotics
sources.title: 9 weeks to 9 days: How autonomous drilling is transforming data center construction — The Robot Report
sources.claim: DEWALT and August Robotics field an autonomous mobile drilling robot (Lionel platform + DEWALT rig) that reads hole locations from building CAD plans and drills anchor holes in concrete floors of buildings under construction; 12 robots in the field had drilled 108,000 holes with 99.97% ... by January 2026, with commercial launch in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling anchor holes in a concrete floor from the drawings is the anchoring sub-step of bolting down a safe. It transfers only partially — the robot drills but does not set anchors, move or position the safe — so it substantiates blueprint-driven concrete drilling capability, not completion of a whole safe installation in a building.

sources.system: KUKA KR 1000 titan / KR TITAN ultra
sources.title: KR 1000 titan | KUKA Global
sources.claim: KUKA's KR 1000 titan is a commercially deployed six-axis industrial robot that handles loads up to 1,300 kg — engine blocks, steel beams, precast concrete parts — precisely within fenced industrial cells; the KR TITAN ultra line (2026) extends this to 1,500 kg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise placement of multi-hundred-kilogram steel and concrete workpieces in a fixtured cell. Comparable object mass and rigidity to a safe body or vault door leaf, so a purpose-built cell could bring a safe into position for anchoring.

sources.system: Flexible Intelligent Door Assembly Line (Risong Technology)
sources.title: Flexible Intelligent Door Assembly Line of Changan Mazda Automobile Co., Ltd. — IFR case study
sources.claim: Changan Mazda's flexible intelligent door assembly line performs fully automated hanging and adjustment of car doors, hoods, lids and bumpers on the vehicle body, with 3D laser vision (0.1 mm), gap measurement, automatic bolt tightening and torque monitoring, replacing about 80 manual workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hanging a door on a frame to a tight gap tolerance and torquing its mounting bolts, verified by vision. This is the same operation class as setting a vault door or deposit-box nest plumb in a fixtured frame and bolting it, when the work is presented in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Robotic bolt-tightening stations (3D vision + force sensing) on automotive assembly lines
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robots on automotive assembly lines now perform bolt tightening on assemblies using 3D vision and force sensors, locating fasteners and controlling torque under production conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving and torquing structural bolts on a located assembly, the fastening step of anchoring a safe or bolting deposit-box nests together, with the same fastener sizes and torque verification requirements.

sources.system: Robotic deflashing, drilling and tapping cell (FANUC M10iA)
sources.title: Robotic Deflashing, Drilling, Tapping Cell Case Study — Pioneer Industrial Systems
sources.claim: A fielded FANUC M10iA robotic cell performs secondary machining operations including drilling and tapping on parts held in a locating fixture, running its cycle unattended behind a light curtain with laser-sensor verification of the finished part.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic drilling and tapping of fixtured workpieces, the drill/tap/die operations named in this task, performed in a fenced cell where the work is presented in a known position.

tasks.label: Unlock cars and other vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail parking lot or street-side lockout: customer has locked keys (or a smart fob) inside a late-model sedan/SUV. Locksmith verifies ownership, wedges the door frame with an air bladder, inserts a long-reach tool through the gap, and presses the interior unlock button or lifts the handle without marring paint, bending the frame, or damaging side-curtain airbags; make/model unknown until arrival; traffic, weather and bystanders present.

Residential driveway, apartment lot or rural roadside lockout, often at night or in rain/snow: mixed fleet including older vehicles with exposed lock linkage (slim jim) or door cylinders that must be picked and decoded with a keyway-specific Lishi tool; tight parking, uneven ground, poor lighting, anxious customer.

Lost-all-keys job wherever the vehicle sits: no key exists, so the locksmith opens the vehicle (wedge/long-reach or picking the door cylinder), decodes the lock or pulls the key code from the VIN, cuts a mechanical or laser key in the van, and programs the transponder/immobilizer through the OBD port so the vehicle can be driven away.

Emergency entry with a child, pet or running engine inside, in a public lot or street; police or fire on scene; entry must be made within minutes using rapid non-destructive entry or, failing that, controlled breakage of a chosen window.

Commercial account work on controlled premises: dealership, rental/auction lot, tow yard, impound or municipal fleet garage where a batch of vehicles must be opened and/or keys originated; access controlled by the operator, vehicles parked in rows on paved lots or inside a shop, each still a different make/model/condition.

Non-car vehicles: heavy trucks and tractor units, RVs and trailers, motorcycles, boats, and farm/construction equipment locked out at a truck stop, campground, marina or job site; larger and more varied hardware (cam locks, compartment locks, ignition switches), sometimes requiring on-site key origination.

sources.system: KeyMe key duplication kiosks / KeyMe Locksmiths lockout service
sources.title: AI Info | Key Me
sources.claim: The closest commercially deployed automated 'locksmith' hardware is the KeyMe robotic key-copy kiosk; for actual vehicle and home lockouts KeyMe dispatches a human technician, indicating vehicle opening is not performed by any fielded robotic system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = key duplication. The kiosk robot cuts keys from an existing key inside a machine enclosure; it never approaches or opens a vehicle, and the same company still sends human technicians for lockouts, so the capability does not transfer to unlocking a locked vehicle.

sources.system: Keys NOW! automated key duplication machine
sources.title: Car Keys Express Launches First-of-its-Kind Comprehensive Automated Retail Key Cutting Machine
sources.claim: Fully automated car-key cutting machines exist (Keys NOW!), but they duplicate a key the customer already has, inside a retail cabinet; they perform no vehicle entry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = originating/duplicating a car key. It requires an existing key as the pattern and does no lock decoding, entry, or immobilizer programming at the vehicle, so it cannot complete an 'unlock the vehicle' instance.

sources.system: ABB IRB 5350 door opener robot
sources.date: product page retrieved 2026-07 (product in service for years)
sources.title: IRB 5350 | ABB
sources.claim: Industrial robots do open vehicle doors, but only unlocked doors on a known body style fixtured on a paint-line conveyor inside a fenced booth, executing a taught door-swing motion rather than defeating a lock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = opening a car door in an assembly plant. Transfer fails: the door is unlocked, the body is one known model held on a conveyor in a fixed pose, and the robot replays a programmed trajectory; it cannot bypass or pick a lock on an unknown locked vehicle.

sources.system: Sparks and Code pin-sensing lockpicking robot
sources.title: A Lockpicking Robot That Can Sense The Pins | Hackaday
sources.claim: Autonomous lock manipulation remains a hobby/prototype pursuit on standard pin-tumbler cylinders; no reliable autonomous picking robot exists, let alone one for automotive wafer or laser-track door cylinders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous lock picking. It is a bench prototype on a pin-tumbler cylinder, not a vehicle lock, and coverage describes it as not yet reliably working, so it cannot substantiate worker-quality vehicle opening at any tier.

tasks.label: Remove interior and exterior finishes on safes and vaults, and spray on new finishes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full exterior refinish of a modern steel safe (gun safe, office/commercial safe) picked up and brought into the safe shop: remove dial, handle and hinge hardware, strip old paint and rust by sanding/media blasting, fill dents, prime and spray topcoat in the shop's booth, cure, reassemble hardware.

Antique/decorative safe restoration in the shop: strip multiple layers of old paint and varnish from cast-iron scrollwork and raised lettering, mask nickel/brass trim, spray gloss and flat base coats, then hand pinstriping, gold-leaf lettering and decorative panel artwork to match the original finish.

On-site spot refinish/touch-up at a commercial customer (bank branch, jewelry store, office): after a move, install, or drill-and-repair, mask the surrounding floor and the safe's hardware, scuff-sand and feather the damaged area, and blend a color-matched spray touch-up on the safe or vault door face.

Bank vault door and frame refinish on site: heavy steel door leaf with stainless cladding and boltwork installed in a masonry opening; sand off surface rust, mask lobby and door furniture, and respray/recoat door and jamb in place with portable spray equipment, working around branch hours.

Interior refinishing in the shop: tear out old glued felt/carpet liner, shelving and door pads, strip old paint and rust from the inside of the box and door back, spray interior finish into the deep cavity, then cut and fit new liner panels and reinstall shelving.

On-site touch-up at a private residence: home gun safe or in-home vault door in a basement, closet or garage; scuff-sand scratches from delivery or a lock repair, mask nearby household surfaces, and spray a color-matched touch-up with aerosol or small HVLP gun in a cluttered, unventilated space.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics Scan&Sand (dual-arm autonomous sanding cell)
sources.title: The World's First Dual-Arm Autonomous Robotic Sanding Cell
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Sand autonomous robotic sanding cell was deployed in production at BetterWay Products; the cell's AI generates its own robot programs for high-mix, high-variability parts rather than being hand-programmed per part.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive surface preparation of one-off, varying workpieces. Removing an old finish from a safe body is the same operation (powered abrasive removal of coating from a rigid painted/steel surface) on comparable-size parts, and the scan-based self-programming is what a one-off refinish job requires.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics GMR-AI robotic finishing cells
sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics opens physical AI innovation center - The Robot Report
sources.claim: GrayMatter's AI-driven finishing cells — covering sanding, grinding, buffing, polishing, blasting ... — are in production use at manufacturers, including fire-apparatus maker Pierce Manufacturing, and scan and program themselves and adapt to part variation without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix industrial surface finishing (strip/prep then coat) of large painted steel and composite assemblies. Fire-truck bodies and similar weldments are larger and more complex than a safe body, and the coatings and abrasives are the same industrial materials.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics robotic cells (Scan&Sand / Scan&Blast / Scan&Spray)
sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics Unveils 100,000-Square-Foot AI Robotics Innovation Center in Carson
sources.claim: At GrayMatter's Carson facility more than 25 robotic cells run real customer parts, with the robots autonomously sanding, spraying, blasting and inspecting parts of diverse materials and geometries — i.e., both coating removal and coating application are performed autonomously in purpose-built cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abrasive coating removal plus spray coating of varied parts in one workflow — the same two-step strip-and-respray sequence this task requires, on metal parts of comparable scale and with comparable finish-quality requirements.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics Scan&Blast / Scan&Spray
sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics – Member Spotlight - NCMS
sources.claim: GrayMatter's Scan&Blast product performs robotic abrasive blasting specifically for coating removal and surface ... large industrial assets, and Scan&Spray applies coatings with controlled standoff, speed and perpendicularity over complex geometries; the company deploys these as autonomous cells in production environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal of existing coatings from in-service steel assets and re-coating them. Removing old paint from a safe or vault door is the same abrasive coating-removal operation on smaller, simpler steel geometry.

sources.system: Blastman B20CS / B20CX blast cleaning robots
sources.title: BLASTMAN BLAST CLEANING AND PAINTING FACILITY - Blastman Robotics Ltd
sources.claim: Purpose-built blast chambers with gantry blasting robots are used commercially to clean rust and old paint off large steel objects such as railcars before repainting in an adjoining paint chamber.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stripping old paint and rust from large steel bodies in a purpose-built chamber before repainting — the same removal step this task requires, though Blastman's automatic mode replays operator-recorded motions, so autonomy is treated as unestablished.

sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System (with FANUC robots)
sources.title: General Motors and 3M Partner on New Robotic Paint System (digital edition)
sources.claim: The 3M Finesse-it robotic paint ..., installed on GM's Spring Hill production line, uses AI software and machine vision to locate topcoat defects and sand and polish them out automatically on a moving line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated localized repair of a painted metal finish — locating a defect, then abrading and refinishing just that area. This is the closest demonstrated analogue to spot touch-up refinishing of a safe's painted panel, in a fixed production cell.

sources.system: Hirebotics Cobot Painter (FANUC CRX-10iA/L Paint)
sources.title: Hirebotics Cobot Painter Brings No-Code Spray Painting to Metal Fabricators | Products Finishing
sources.claim: A commercially available explosion-proof painting cobot targeted at high-mix, low-volume metal fabricators applies liquid paint and powder coating without dedicated automated paint lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spray application of liquid coatings to one-off fabricated steel parts in a small shop booth — the coating step of this task; cited only as context because paths are taught by hand rather than generated autonomously.

emergingTasks.label: Read blueprints and project specification manuals to recommend appropriate hardware and electronic locking devices.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Manufactured Building and Mobile Home Installers
roles.description: Move or install mobile homes or prefabricated buildings.

tasks.label: Move and set up mobile homes or prefabricated buildings on owners' lots or at mobile home parks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Deliver and set a new single-section (single-wide) home on a rented space in a mobile home park: hitch a toter to the frame, haul it over public roads under oversize permits, back it between neighboring homes and utility risers, remove hitch/axles/wheels, block it on concrete piers with wedge shims, level the frame, install ground anchors and straps, set steps and skirting. Outdoor, weather-exposed, dirt or gravel pad, 2-3 person crew.

Set a new multi-section (double-wide) home on a private rural lot: pull each half onto the pad with a toter and winch/dollies over unimproved ground, position the halves within an inch over the pier layout, jack and align the sections, close and bolt the marriage line (floor lag bolts, ridge beam, roof), level across ~40 pier points from underneath in 18-36 in. clearance, then anchor and connect utilities. Mud, slope, trees, no fixed layout.

Relocate an existing used home from one lot/park to another: strip skirting and steps, cut or release anchor straps, jack the home, reinstall axles, wheels and hitch, tow it off the site and over the road, then re-block, re-level (often with a sagged frame or settled piers) and re-anchor at the new site. Older home, unknown condition, constant on-the-fly adaptation.

Set a commercial modular/prefab building — classroom, sales office, medical unit — on an institutional site (school campus, hospital or office grounds): craning or rolling modules off transport onto a pre-built pier or slab foundation, aligning and bolting sections, sealing the joint, installing ramps and stairs. The premises are institution-controlled with fixed roads and a prepared pad, but it is still an open outdoor work area.

Set a multi-section home on a permanent foundation or basement on a difficult private lot: crane or roller-set the sections onto poured foundation walls, in tight urban, sloped or snowy conditions, with welded/bolted frame connections and permanent-foundation-certification levelling and bracing. Highly site-specific, coordinated with a crane operator and inspector.

sources.system: Aurora Driver (driverless Class 8 truck)
sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Autonomous Class-8 trucks run driverless commercial freight on Texas highways, showing autonomy for on-highway hauling of conventional trailers only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: over-the-road freight hauling. It covers only the highway fragment of 'move' — a standard-width van trailer in mapped lanes — not a 14-16 ft wide, 60-80 ft house under escort permits, not backing it onto a dirt pad, and none of the blocking, levelling or anchoring work.

sources.system: RPD 35 Robotic Pile Driver
sources.date: 2025 (product page; first units deployed from Q4 2023)
sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: A commercially deployed autonomous machine drives foundation piles outdoors on utility-scale solar sites, combining survey, distribution, driving and inspection without an operator in the loop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing foundation elements on an outdoor site. It shows autonomy for repetitive georeferenced heavy work on a graded solar field, but the objects are identical steel piles driven from above on open ground; it cannot stack and shim pier blocks under a home's chassis, mate two house sections, or level a structure.

sources.system: Hadrian X
sources.title: 1st Hadrian X bricklaying robot arrives in U.S. — The Robot Report
sources.claim: An autonomous outdoor bricklaying robot lays blocks for house walls on residential building sites — the closest demonstrated case of autonomous heavy construction manipulation on a house lot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site placement of heavy building units on a residential lot. It handles one uniform block type delivered through its own boom onto a prepared slab; it does not transport a house, work under a chassis, join structural sections, or install tie-down anchors, so it does not carry over to setting a manufactured home.

sources.system: Enerpac SPMT600 with Intelli-Drive remote controller
sources.title: Enerpac unveils SPMT600 — Heavy Lift & Project Forwarding International
sources.claim: The heavy-transport equipment actually used to move and position building-size loads on site (self-propelled modular transporters) is human remote-controlled, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving and setting down building-size modules. This is the state of the art for the 'move and position' step of a house set, and it is continuous human remote control, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Seal open sides of modular units to prepare them for shipment, using polyethylene sheets, nails, and hammers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End of the production line inside a modular/HUD-code plant: crew covers the large open 'marriage' side of a finished module (a flat rectangular opening roughly 12-14 ft wide by 8-12 ft tall, or a full 60 ft long face) with rolled polyethylene sheeting, pulling it taut and fastening it with nails/cap staples and furring strips, trimming excess. Indoor, level floor, standard module widths, module indexed at a finish station.

Factory yard / loading area: modules already lifted onto transport carriers are sealed or re-sealed before dispatch. Same large flat open faces, but work is outdoors on uneven gravel, at height from ladders or scissor lifts, in wind and cold that make the poly billow; carrier position varies.

Detail sealing of irregular open sides: gable/ridge ends, recessed porches, cantilevered floor or roof overhangs, protruding trusses, hinged roof sections, open ends with stub walls, plumbing and duct stub-outs. Requires custom cutting, tucking, overlapping courses, taping seams and lapping over the roof edge so water sheds.

Destination staging lot or set site: re-sealing or patching polyethylene torn in transit or by wind on modules parked on the site before the set, working around soft ground, blocking, cribbing, tow hitches and straps, with the crew judging where the sheeting failed and patching it.

Small units inside the plant: park models, single-section units, or commercial modular offices whose open ends or window/door openings are covered with poly and lath before shipment; small, flat, standardized openings at working height.

sources.system: Randek AutoWall / S3000 Auto Wall System

sources.claim: Randek's AutoWall (marketed by SCM Group) is a commercial prefab-house production line that produces wall frames with sheathing and, optionally, a breather membrane applied on one side, with the workflow automated from CAD/CAM and automatic transport and alignment of elements between stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a polyethylene-type weather membrane over a timber frame and fastening it in a factory line. Same material class (rolled poly sheeting), same fastening class (staples/nails into wood), same coarse precision, and a purpose-built machine setting; it differs in that the frame is flat and horizontal rather than the vertical open face of a 3D module.

sources.title: From Lumber to Bundle: The Prefabrication of a Bensonwood Panel
sources.claim: At Bensonwood's US prefab plant, a WEINMANN multifunction bridge automatically nails OSB sheathing to wall panels at all connection points, driven by CAD machine files, after automatically framing and nailing plates to studs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously fastening sheet material to a wood frame with nails from a CAD model. The sealing task also fastens sheet material to the module's wood framing with nails; the fastening precision required for poly and lath is lower than for structural sheathing.

tasks.label: Repair leaks in plumbing or gas lines, using caulking compounds and plastic or copper pipe.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Water supply line leak under a set manufactured home on a private lot or in a park: installer crawls into an 18-30 in. crawl space over dirt/vapor barrier and skirting, works overhead among joists, insulation and heat duct, finds the wet spot on PEX/CPVC/copper, cuts out the damaged section, installs a coupling or crimp/push fittings, re-insulates and re-pressurizes to verify no leak.

Leak at marriage-line crossover connections during set-up of a multi-section home: water crossover and drain crossover joined under the floor at the mate line; a pressure/fill test shows weeping at a fitting, so the installer re-makes the joint (re-glue, re-clamp, new fitting) and seals penetrations with caulk, working prone under the home at the site.

Interior fixture-area leak: under-sink supply riser, angle stop or P-trap; toilet flange/closet connection; tub-shower drain reached through a floor access cutout. Tight cabinet or closet spaces in a furnished, occupied home; parts vary; finish must be reassembled and the area caulked and dried.

Gas line leak on the home's fuel piping: manometer/soap-bubble test after set, locate a leaking flare or black-iron fitting, damaged CSST, or crossover connection under the floor; disassemble, re-dope/replace the fitting or a pipe section, re-test to code and re-light appliances. Safety-critical, at the home site.

Leak repaired on a unit staged indoors in a factory finish line or a dealer's set-up/service bay: the water test at final QC shows a leaking joint, the home is on jacks or blocked with good access, lighting and standard tooling, and repair crew fixes the joint before shipping/handover.

sources.system: CISBOT (Cast Iron Joint Sealing Robot)
sources.developer: ULC Technologies / ULC Robotics (with National Grid, Cadent, SGN)
sources.title: ULC Technologies' CISBOT Seals 50,000 Joints in Live Gas Mains - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: CISBOT is a commercially deployed robot that seals leaking joints from inside live cast-iron gas mains, but it is a remotely controlled machine operating inside buried utility mains, not a system that repairs residential water or fuel piping under a home.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing robotic gas-leak repair. It does not transfer: it works only inside large-diameter buried mains on a single standard joint type, is operator-controlled from a surface control van, and cannot access, cut, or join small-diameter PEX/CPVC/copper/black-iron piping in a crawl space.

sources.system: CISBOT
sources.title: CISBOT - Cadent Gas Ltd
sources.claim: Cadent's own description confirms CISBOT is remotely controlled rather than autonomous, sealing joints from inside the main with a sealant.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to establish autonomy status of the leading pipe-leak-repair robot: it is remotely controlled, so under the rules it cannot support a positive judgment for any instance.

sources.system: Pipebots (and companion 'No Dig Leak Repair' project)
sources.title: Tiny robots could help fix leaky water pipes | News | The University of Sheffield
sources.claim: Pipebots are 40 mm research micro-robots for inspecting buried water mains; autonomous repair of leaks remains a development goal, and they operate inside utility mains, not on accessible household piping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-pipe leak location/repair in water mains). Does not transfer: the demonstrated capability is inspection/leak finding inside buried mains, repair is prospective, and nothing addresses cutting and rejoining exposed supply or DWV piping under a manufactured home.

sources.system: ANYmal with acoustic imaging / gas leak detection payload
sources.title: Autonomous Gas Leak Detection - ANYbotics
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous legged inspection robots handle gas leak detection in industrial plants, but only detect and report leaks; they perform no repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (finding gas leaks). Transfer fails at the repair step: the robot carries sensors, not tools, and cannot disassemble, replace, or seal a leaking fitting.

sources.system: UltraFlex Dragon 15 brazing robot cell
sources.title: Robotic Induction Brazing of Copper to Brass - UltraFlex
sources.claim: Robotic joining of copper piping exists only as programmed brazing of fixtured, identical parts in a manufacturing cell; the robot positions a coil on a pre-known joint and does not locate defects, cut, or fit pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (joining copper tube) used to test the E1 counterfactual. It substantiates only a pre-programmed braze on a fixtured, known joint - not locating a leak, cutting out a damaged section, fitting a replacement, sealing, and re-testing, which is what the instance requires.

tasks.label: Connect water hoses to inlet pipes of plumbing systems, and test operation of plumbing fixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-section (single-wide) home set on a private suburban/rural lot: installer routes and connects a flexible water supply line from the site riser/shutoff valve to the home's inlet stub, working in a dirt or gravel crawl space of roughly 24-36 inches clearance under the home, seals threaded fittings with tape/dope, then goes inside to open every faucet hot and cold, flush the toilet, run tub/shower, purge air, and inspect under sinks, at the water heater and under the home for leaks.

Multi-section (double-wide/triple-wide) home on a private lot: in addition to the site supply connection, the installer joins the hot and cold crossover water lines between the halves under the home, supports and insulates them, pressurizes the system, and then tests every fixture in both halves, correcting drips and loose fittings found during the walk-through.

Home set on a pad in a manufactured-home community: pad graded and water riser placed to the park's standard, installer connects the supply and crossover lines under the home and then runs the full interior fixture test, often with the park manager or a state installation inspector present.

Commercial/institutional modular building (classroom, office trailer, medical unit) set at a customer construction site: installer connects the building's water inlet to the contractor's stub-out, pressure-tests the system for code inspection, then tests restroom lavatories, water closets, janitor sink and any kitchen fixtures.

Display-home hookup at a dealer sales center: temporary water hose run to a home's inlet on a gravel display lot, water turned on and each fixture run and checked for leaks so the model can be shown; later drained/winterized.

Warranty/service callback on a previously set home: installer must locate a leaking, loose, or freeze-damaged supply or crossover connection under the home, re-make or replace it in place, and then retest the fixtures to confirm the system is tight.

sources.system: RND Automation hydraulic valve assembly cell (Epson T3/G3 SCARA and C8 six-axis robots, MagneMotion transfer)
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A production assembly cell built by RND Automation with Epson SCARA and six-axis robots autonomously threads fluid-system fittings (screws, hex bodies) into valve bodies with anti-cross-thread compliance and torque control, then loads each unit into an automated leak test fixture and sorts it - i.e. a machine makes threaded fluid connections and verifies they do not leak, in a purpose-built fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic make-up of threaded fluid fittings followed by automated leak verification. Transfer: the installer's core physical act is threading a water line onto an inlet fitting without cross-threading, to a seal-tight torque, and then confirming no leak - the same objects (metal fluid fittings, O-rings/sealant), similar precision, done here autonomously when the work is fixtured and presented, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: innomatec automated leak and function test benches (LTC-802 / LTC-902 based) for valves and fittings
sources.title: Leak and Function Test Benches for Valves & Fittings | innomatec
sources.claim: innomatec supplies automated/robotic leak and function test benches specifically for plumbing valves and fittings (faucets, mixer valves), in which parts are fed and fixtured by robotic handling or servo tooling, connected to test heads, pressurized, and leak- plus function-tested on one machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated connection to a plumbing part's inlet ports plus combined leak and functional testing. Transfer: 'test operation of plumbing fixtures' is, when the work is presented to a machine, exactly pressurizing the water side, actuating the valve, and verifying flow and tightness - which these benches do commercially on faucets and mixer valves.

sources.system: ROBOFUEL autonomous refuelling system
sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: SCOTT Automation's ROBOFUEL autonomous refuelling system, built around ABB/KUKA robots at a purpose-built refuelling station, autonomously mates a fuel nozzle to a haul truck's fill receiver and transfers fluid; an installation in the Pilbara reached site acceptance in late 2019 ... in production use with autonomous truck fleets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously connecting a fluid hose/nozzle to an inlet on a large object and transferring liquid without spill. Transfer: same class of act as connecting a water hose to a home's inlet pipe, but only achieved where the receiving adapter is standardised and the vehicle presents itself to a fixed, purpose-built station - supporting E1, not the as-found underside of a home.

sources.system: AutoFuel autonomous truck refuelling robot
sources.title: Autonomous Truck Refuelling with Universal Field Robots
sources.claim: Universal Field Robots' AutoFuel robot is described as positioning itself and connecting a fuel nozzle to a truck without an operator, using vision and sensors to locate the receiver and a gripper to remove the fuel cap, at a fixed refuelling point beside the haul road.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hose/nozzle-to-inlet coupling on a large object. Transfer: shows machine-controlled fluid-line coupling is achievable when the inlet is a standardised adapter presented at a fixed station, i.e. an E1-style purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Rocsys Steward / S2 autonomous connection device
sources.title: Rocsys launches integrated platform to enable hands-free charging for autonomous mobility - Charged EVs
sources.claim: Rocsys' autonomous connection device detects a vehicle's arrival, opens the port, plugs in, transfers energy and unplugs without a human, deployed hands-free in port and logistics fleet yards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous coupling of a service line to a port outside a fenced cell, in an institution-run yard (E2). Included to show the limit: even at E2 the coupling only works with purpose-designed ports and a robot-owned bay, and it involves no threaded plumbing fittings or fixture testing.

sources.system: GPK-32 Wireless Inspection Robot
sources.title: Home Inspector Crawlspace Inspection Robot | SuperDroid Robots
sources.claim: Robots used today under manufactured homes are small teleoperated camera crawlers for inspection only; they carry no manipulator and make no plumbing connections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic access to the crawl space under a manufactured home. It establishes that under-home robotic presence today is remote-controlled inspection without manipulation, so no cited system can make and test water connections at the E2/E3 job site.

tasks.label: Install, repair, and replace units, fixtures, appliances, and other items and systems in mobile and modular homes, prefabricated buildings, or travel trailers, using hand tools or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After the sections are set on a pad at a mobile home park or rural private lot, the installer works in the 2-4 ft crawl space under the home (dirt/gravel, variable light, weather) to connect the utility crossovers: mate the HVAC crossover duct, join water supply lines with fittings and clamps, connect drain/sewer lines to the riser, hook up the gas line, and join the electrical crossover; then pressure-test and check for leaks.

Inside the newly set home at the site, install units and appliances shipped loose or removed for transport: set and connect the water heater, furnace/AC coil, range and dryer (gas or electric hookups), install toilets, faucets, shower doors, ceiling fans and light fixtures; secure, level, seal, and verify operation.

Finish work at the marriage line and closures on site: hang pre-hung interior and exterior doors, install steps, trim and molding, close marriage-line drywall/ceiling panels, cut and fit skirting vents and access panels - with hand and power tools, custom cutting, shimming and scribing to non-standard gaps.

Warranty or service call at an occupied manufactured home: diagnose and replace a failed fixture, appliance or system component (leaking faucet, water heater, furnace blower, sagging door, damaged countertop) while working around residents, furniture and pets in a narrow hallway or small bathroom.

Pre-delivery / finish-out work in a controlled facility: a dealer lot prep bay or manufactured-home / travel-trailer plant finish area, installing appliances, rooftop A/C units, awnings, plumbing fixtures and light fixtures in a unit staged on the premises; standard tools and controlled access, but cramped interiors and model-to-model variation.

sources.system: AUAR robotic micro-factory
sources.title: Automated Architecture uses robotic micro-factories to build homes | Building Design + Construction
sources.claim: In robotic offsite-housing micro-factories, robots assemble wood-frame floor, wall and roof panels, while human trades install the mechanical, electrical ... - i.e., fixture/appliance/MEP installation remains manual even in highly automated prefab factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic factory production of modular/prefab housing. It bounds the state of the art for the rated task: robots there handle structural panels, while installation of fixtures, appliances and MEP systems is explicitly left to human trades.

sources.system: Kawasaki MX420L robots on the Sekisui Heim unit assembly line
sources.title: Case Study "Robotic House Construction-Sekisui Heim's Pursuit in Combating a Housing Industry Labor Shortage" | Kawasaki Robotics
sources.claim: In one of the world's most automated modular housing plants, industrial robots perform steel-frame assembly and welding of housing units; interior fixture and appliance fitting is not robot work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: purpose-built factory assembly of finished housing units. Even in this fixtured E1 line the robots weld and assemble frames rather than install fixtures, appliances or plumbing, indicating no E1-capable system exists for the rated task.

sources.system: Canvas 1200CX drywall finishing robot
sources.title: Canvas | Drywall Finishing Robot
sources.claim: The most capable commercial interior-finishing construction robot performs drywall compound spraying and sanding on large commercial jobsites; it does not install fixtures, appliances, doors or trim, or make utility connections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior finish trade work inside buildings. It is the closest deployed robotic capability to the rated task's interior finish component, but is limited to coating and sanding flat surfaces, so it cannot complete door, trim, fixture or appliance installation instances.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Construction robots marketed for MEP and interior-finishing installation automate only BIM-driven hole marking and drilling; the actual installation of hangers, pipe, fixtures and equipment is done by tradespeople.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: MEP and interior installation support on jobsites. It shows the deployed robotic contribution to fixture and system installation is limited to drilling anchor holes, not placing, fastening or connecting the units themselves.

sources.system: Maximo solar installation robot
sources.title: Transforming solar farms: AI, robotics, and industry partnerships at AES - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous field installation of units with power tools is demonstrated only for large, uniform, repetitive modules on standardized racking in open purpose-organized construction fields, not for household fixtures, appliances or utility hookups.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement and mechanical fastening of units at a construction site. Transfer to this task fails: identical flat modules on standardized racking in open ground involve no confined crawl spaces, plumbing/gas/electrical connections, or model-to-model variation.

sources.system: 1X NEO
sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Consumer humanoids intended for household work depend on human teleoperators for anything beyond simple pick-and-place; no humanoid has been shown completing a household task end to end autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose manipulation inside homes. The general-purpose robots that might otherwise service or replace fixtures in an occupied home are teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Inspect, examine, and test the operation of parts or systems to evaluate operating condition and to determine if repairs are needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-set utility check at a home site: after hookup, the installer pressurizes/tests water lines and drains for leaks under sinks and in the belly, air-tests the gas line, checks electrical crossover connections and the panel, energizes lights/outlets, fires the furnace and checks air handler/AC operation, and notes what must be repaired before final inspection.

Under-home structural check on a private lot or in a park: crawling in an 18-36 inch crawl space over dirt/vapor barrier to verify piers are plumb and shimmed, footings bear, anchors/straps are tight, the chassis is level (water level/laser), crossover ducts are connected and undamaged, and the bottom board is sealed; determine re-leveling or repair needs.

Interior walkthrough after the set: check that the marriage line closed properly, doors and windows open/close and latch, drywall/ceiling seams and floors show no transport cracks or separations, cabinets and trim align, and appliances/fixtures function; list punch-out repairs.

Pre-move inspection of an existing/used home before relocation, at the owner's lot: check the frame, axles, tires, hitch and running gear, roof and siding condition, and structural soundness to determine repairs needed before the home can be transported.

Exterior/roof damage inspection at the site: walk around and inspect the roof cap, shingles/metal, ridge over the marriage line, siding, and skirting for transport, hail, or wind damage after delivery or a storm, and determine which areas need repair.

sources.system: SuperDroid GPK-32 / crawlspace inspection robots
sources.title: Using Robots for Home Inspections | AHIT
sources.claim: Crawl-space/under-home inspection robots marketed to home inspectors are remote-controlled camera vehicles driven by the inspector, not autonomous evaluators.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the related task of under-home inspection in residential crawl spaces; it shows the only fielded under-home robots require continuous human driving and provide imagery only, so they cannot substitute for the installer's judgment.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit/Scout inspection payloads
sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous, scheduled inspection rounds in industrial plants, capturing thermal, acoustic leak and analog-gauge data and flagging abnormal readings for maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous condition monitoring of installed equipment. Transfer to manufactured-home system testing is limited: Spot only observes fixed assets on taught routes in plants, does not operate faucets, valves, breakers or thermostats, and cannot enter an 18-inch crawl space.

sources.system: ANYmal / ANYmal X
sources.title: ANYmal - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: ANYmal runs routine autonomous inspection rounds in industrial plants, collecting visual, thermal, gas and acoustic data and detecting anomalies such as leaks and corrosion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned inspection of plant equipment to determine maintenance needs. It substantiates only sensor-based observation of fixed industrial assets in institution-controlled plants, not functional testing of residential plumbing, gas, electrical or HVAC systems.

sources.system: Eagleview Assess (Skydio House Scan / 3D Scan autonomy)
sources.title: Roof inspection drone tech with EagleView | Skydio
sources.claim: Autonomous drone scanning of residential roofs/exteriors is a commercial service: the drone plans and flies the capture itself after the operator outlines the area, and AI assesses the imagery for damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: residential roof/exterior damage inspection on properties taken as found, the same objects (shingles, roof facets, siding) and the same output (a damage determination) as the installer's exterior transport-damage check.

sources.system: Eagleview Assess
sources.title: Eagleview Assess Expands Drone Roof Inspection Solution
sources.claim: Eagleview's drone product produces AI anomaly/damage reports for roofs and larger buildings, with vendor-reported improvements in damage-detection precision and fewer false positives.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior damage assessment of residential structures; the flagged-anomaly report is the same deliverable as the installer's determination that roof/siding areas need repair.

sources.system: HVAC inspection/leak-detection robots (review of the field)
sources.title: Robotics for HVAC applications: A critical review and future perspectives
sources.claim: A 2025 review of robotics for HVAC applications reports that real-world performance of HVAC inspection/maintenance robots remains limited and that they are largely not integrated with building systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic inspection/testing of HVAC and piping systems in buildings; the review indicates no fielded system performs functional testing of a dwelling's mechanical systems at worker quality.

tasks.label: Remove damaged exterior panels, repair and replace structural frame members, and seal leaks, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field repair at a set manufactured home on a private lot or in a mobile-home community: cut out and remove crushed, torn or rotted exterior siding/panel sections (metal, vinyl or hardboard) damaged in transport or by weather, pull trim and fasteners, cut a replacement panel to fit, fasten it, and caulk edges. Work is done from ladders on uneven ground around AC units, utility lines, shrubs and skirting, in whatever weather is present.

Locating and sealing leaks on an occupied home in the field: tracing water stains to a source, stripping failed sealant, re-taping/re-caulking roof seams and the roof cap, vents, window and door perimeters, and re-sealing the marriage line, plus brushing or rolling elastomeric coating over patched areas.

Repairing or replacing structural frame members: sistering or replacing damaged floor joists, rim joists or outriggers, repairing wall studs or chassis crossmembers, often working prone in the crawl space under the home behind skirting and belly wrap, or through an opened floor/wall section, with pry bars, saws, jacks and hand tools.

Close-up work during setup of a multi-section home at the customer's site: installing or repairing closure/end-wall panels at the marriage line, fitting gaskets and butyl tape to seal the seam between sections, and patching shipping damage to siding and trim before final inspection.

Rework inside a controlled facility: a dealer's service bay or a manufactured-housing plant's repair/finish station, where a damaged unit is parked in a fixed bay with standard equipment, lighting and lifts, and crews replace damaged siding panels, repair framing and re-seal joints before delivery.

sources.system: Rufus
sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus is a cable/winch-driven roofing robot that places and nails new asphalt shingles on residential roofs; it is a new-installation machine supervised by a technician and does not diagnose or repair leaks, strip damaged panels, or repair framing.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field system working on residential roofs/exterior cladding; cited to show the frontier of exterior-envelope robotics is placing new standard shingles on a prepared deck, not removing damaged panels, replacing framing, or finding and sealing leaks.

sources.system: Jaibot
sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially deployed, semi-autonomous jobsite robot that drills overhead holes from a BIM plan after a human lays out the site; it performs one pre-planned drilling operation and no removal, fitting, fastening or sealing work.
sources.transferJustification: Represents the state of the art for autonomous hand-tool-type work on real construction sites (E3); shows such systems are limited to a single pre-planned operation on known geometry, not damage assessment and repair with hand tools.

sources.date: 2021-2025 (jobsite deployments; Suffolk and Bay Area contractors)
sources.title: How a Drywall Robot Is Reshaping Interior Construction | Built (Bluebeam)

sources.transferJustification: Surface-finishing/seam work on building interiors is the nearest deployed analog to sealing seams; cited to show the deployed capability covers uniform new surfaces, not diagnosing leaks or stripping and re-sealing weathered joints on an existing home.

sources.system: Automated Roof/Floor Truss Systems
sources.developer: House of Design Robotics (for Builders FirstSource)
sources.title: BUILDERS FIRSTSOURCE PLACES LARGE AUTOMATED TRUSS SYSTEM ORDER WITH HOUSE OF DESIGN
sources.claim: House of Design supplies commercially installed robotic roof- and floor-truss lines in component plants, where robots lift, preplate and assemble new trusses from lumber fed and jigged by the line; the work is fabrication of new members from uniform stock, not removal or replacement of damaged members in an existing structure.

sources.system: ALC wall panel installation mobile robot
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Journal of Building Engineering)
sources.title: A scheme of installing ALC wall panels based on autonomous mobile robot - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Autonomous installation of building wall panels by a mobile robot with gripper and SLAM navigation remains a research demonstration, not a fielded capability, and covers placing new panels rather than removing damaged ones.

tasks.label: Open and close doors, windows, and drawers to test their operation, trimming edges to fit, using jackplanes or drawknives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Newly set single- or multi-section home on a customer's lot: after blocking, leveling and marriage-line closure, the installer opens and closes each interior passage/bedroom door, finds one binding or rubbing the jamb, marks the high edge, pulls the pins, planes the stile with a jackplane/block plane, rehangs and re-tests swing and latch. Dusty, uneven floor, home slightly out of square.

Exterior entry door or marriage-wall door of a set home on site: after leveling the unit the door is out of square, drags at the threshold or will not latch; installer tests operation, shims/adjusts the jamb, trims the door edge and strike side to restore even reveal and weatherstrip contact, then re-tests closing and locking.

Windows in the set home on site: installer opens and closes every sliding/single-hung sash and screen, finds sashes binding where the wall racked during transport, frees them by adjusting the frame and trimming sash stops, jamb liners or interior trim edges, then re-tests operation and locking.

Kitchen and bath casework in the set home on site: installer opens and closes cabinet doors and drawers, finds drawers rubbing or doors out of alignment after the road trip and floor leveling, trims/planes edges of drawer fronts, doors or filler pieces, adjusts hinges and glides, and re-tests each one.

Manufactured-home plant finish line or dealer's service/display lot: the completed unit sits inside a controlled facility or on a graded lot; a finisher cycles every door, window and drawer as part of the punch list, trimming edges with a plane where units bind, before delivery or customer walk-through.

tasks.label: Locate and repair frayed wiring, broken connections, or incorrect wiring, using ohmmeters, soldering irons, tape, and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Set home in a mobile home park or on a private lot: occupant reports dead outlets or a tripping circuit after the set. Installer pulls cover plates and devices, traces the circuit with an ohmmeter/tester across receptacles, switches and junction boxes, finds a loose or broken connection, remakes the splice (wire nut or solder), tapes and re-secures it, verifies, and reinstalls devices and plates. Furnished, occupied interior; no two homes laid out alike.

Under-home belly / crawl space repair: wiring chafed or torn during transport, or gnawed by rodents. Installer crawls under the home over dirt, gravel or vapor barrier with 18-36 inches of headroom, cuts out the damaged run, splices in a new segment in an accessible box, tapes and staples it up, and checks continuity. Cramped, dark, damp, insects, variable ground and weather.

Multi-section home at set-up on the lot: connecting and correcting the crossover/marriage-line wiring where the halves join — pulling the crossover harness through the floor or attic, landing conductors, correcting reversed or mislanded wires, testing continuity end to end, and taping/securing. Work done at the raw site, partly in the attic cavity and partly under the floor.

Dealer lot or set-up yard pre-delivery inspection: technician finds incorrect wiring in a home on blocks (reversed polarity, open ground, a miswired 240 V range or dryer receptacle, a mislanded breaker), diagnoses with ohmmeter/tester, re-terminates the conductors correctly, and retests. Institution-controlled yard, similar model homes, but each home's interior is entered as built.

Warranty or post-relocation service call on an older occupied home: chased fault after a storm, a leak or a move — frayed conductor at a light fixture, damaged range cord, burnt receptacle, or a break in a branch circuit. Repair amid furniture, clutter, pets and sometimes standing water or wet insulation.

In-plant rework at the manufactured-housing factory: QC or the final electrical test flags a nicked conductor, an open connection, or a circuit wired to the wrong breaker in a floor section still on the line or in a rework bay. Worker opens the wall/ceiling access, locates the fault with an ohmmeter, repairs or re-lands the conductor, tapes, and re-tests before shipment.

tasks.label: Reset hardware, using chisels, mallets, and screwdrivers.

instances.label: Interior passage, closet and bifold doors inside a single- or double-wide just set on the customer's lot: transport racking has loosened hinges and thrown latches out of alignment. Worker chisels hinge mortises deeper or shims them, taps hinge leaves with a mallet, re-drives or relocates strike-plate and hinge screws until each door swings and latches. Dusty, partly finished interior, portable light, layout differs home to home.

Exterior entry, back and storm/screen doors on the set home: deadbolt and latch will not catch after the frame racked; worker chisels the jamb strike mortise, resets strike and keeper plates, re-mortises or shims hinges, resets threshold and closer hardware. Work from steps or blocks at the door opening, outdoors, in whatever weather and ground conditions the lot presents.

Cabinet, drawer and trim hardware in the kitchen and baths of the set home: cabinet hinges and cup-hinge plates loosened or pulled out, drawer glides and catches shifted, pulls, closet-rod brackets, towel bars and medicine-cabinet hardware re-seated; stripped holes plugged and hardware re-screwed, occasionally chiseling a shallow gain flush.

Window and miscellaneous hardware on the set home: sash locks, crank operators, keepers, screen and storm window hardware, and access-panel/skirting latches re-seated after transport, including light chisel work to seat a keeper flush and re-driving screws into shifted or stripped holes.

Hardware reset while the home is staged at a retailer's set-up yard or a manufacturer's finish/repair bay before or just after delivery: homes on blocks in rows on controlled premises with shop power, tools and parts at hand; same chisel/mallet/screwdriver refit of door, cabinet and window hardware from the punch list.

instances.label: Single-section (single-wide) manufactured home just set on a private lot: installer lands the feeder conductors from the home's main distribution panel into the exterior meter base or service pedestal (strip large SER/aluminum conductors, torque lugs, bond neutral/ground, drive/attach ground rod), works partly outdoors and partly in the crawl space under the home, then energizes and walks the house flipping switches to verify lights, receptacles, range, water heater and furnace operate before inspection.

Home placed on a rented space in a manufactured-home community: hook the home's feeder to the existing park power pedestal (hardwire or cord/plug connection) in a tight space between adjacent homes, then energize and test lights, receptacles and appliances throughout.

Prefabricated/modular commercial or institutional building (classroom, office module, medical unit) landed on a jobsite: mate inter-module electrical connections, connect building feeders to the site service or temporary power, then energize and verify lighting, receptacles, exit/emergency fixtures and HVAC operation.

Punch-list or callback visit: a circuit is dead, a fixture or appliance does not operate, or a breaker trips after the initial hookup; the installer diagnoses the fault (loose crossover connector, mis-landed conductor, damaged fixture), repairs it, and re-tests to pass the electrical inspection.

roles.description: Set up or repair rigging for construction projects, manufacturing plants, logging yards, ships and shipyards, or for the entertainment industry.

tasks.label: Test rigging to ensure safety and reliability.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Construction/industrial jobsite, pre-lift verification: rigger checks the made-up rigging on the actual load (slings, shackles, hooks, spreader), takes tension, makes a trial lift a few inches, watches for sling slippage, hardware seating, load balance/center-of-gravity, then re-checks before the pick proceeds. Outdoors, load and layout differ every pick.

Entertainment load-in (arena, theater, touring show): testing the installed rig in situ - dead-hang/tension checks on rigging points and bridles, running chain motors up and down under load, verifying brakes, load-cell readings on points, checking truss connections and safety cables before the rig is flown out.

Manufacturing plant or shipyard: removable lifting gear (chain hoists, lifting beams, spreader bars, C-hooks, other below-the-hook devices) taken out of service and proof/re-certification load tested on an in-house vertical test stand or with calibrated load cells, results recorded and the device tagged.

Manufacturing plant or shipyard: in-situ rated load test of installed lifting systems - overhead/gantry cranes, jibs, monorails, davits - hanging calibrated test weights or water bags, running the equipment through hoist/travel/limit/brake functions while monitoring deflection, then documenting the test.

Rigging shop / sling fabrication and test facility: proof-load testing of new and repaired wire rope slings, chain slings, synthetic slings, shackles and end fittings on a horizontal or vertical test bed - specimen gripped in the bed, load pulled to twice working load limit, held, elongation/distortion checked, certificate issued and gear tagged.

Outdoor/marine/logging in-situ rigging tests: ship's cargo gear and davit annual tests with water bags, tensioning and testing of yarder guylines, skyline and chokers in a logging setting, or guy/anchor testing at a tower or wind site - variable terrain, weather, and one-off configurations.

Construction or renovation site: rigging an HVAC unit, generator, transformer, boiler section or elevator machine down a stair shaft, through a floor hatch or a knocked-out wall opening into a basement/mechanical room, using gin poles, gallows frames, chainfalls and temporary beams; site as found, partial structure, changing obstructions.

Power plant, refinery or paper mill outage/turnaround: moving pumps, turbine internals, motors, valves or heat-exchanger bundles through equipment-room doors, grating openings and hatches in congested piping, with chainfalls, trolley beams and jacking gear inside a confined space with permits.

Shipyard / vessel: lowering or extracting machinery (pumps, generators, shafting, engine components) through deck hatches, scuttles and engine-room casings on a vessel in dry dock or at a pier, using chainfalls, padeyes, gallows frames and tag lines in tight below-deck spaces.

Entertainment venue: moving heavy show equipment (motors, road cases of automation gear, scenic units, chain hoists, turntable sections) through narrow loading doors, backstage passages and up to the grid in a theater or arena, using chainfalls, deck winches and rolling gear on a load-in schedule.

tasks.label: Tilt, dip, and turn suspended loads to maneuver over, under, or around obstacles, using multi-point suspension techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Construction site steel/precast erection: rigger hangs a beam, girder or precast panel from a two- or four-leg sling set or spreader bar under a mobile/tower crane, then tilts and rotates it (differential sling lengths, come-alongs, tag lines) to thread it past existing steel, shoring, scaffolding and power lines into a bolted connection. Outdoors, wind, congested and changing site, multiple trades present.

Operating manufacturing plant / refinery / power plant machinery move: rigger uses overhead bridge crane, chain falls and equalizing hardware to lift a motor, pump, press die or chiller with a multi-point sling arrangement, tilting and dipping it to clear pipe racks, conduit, mezzanines and doorways while plant staff work nearby; load pick points and centre of gravity vary piece to piece.

Entertainment venue: rigger flies scenery, truss or a set piece on a 3- or 4-point hoist bridle in a theater or arena, raking/tilting it by running points at different speeds to clear the proscenium, electrics bars, other scenic units and performers, during load-in and repeatedly through a show run.

Shipyard / marine: rigger turns, upends or dips a hull block, rudder, propeller shaft or large ship equipment using spreader beams, multi-leg slings and often two cranes in tandem, maneuvering it around staging, dock walls and adjacent blocks in the building dock or fabrication shop.

Retrofit rigging inside an occupied existing building: gantry, beam clamps and chain hoists used to tip, dip and swing an elevator machine, transformer, boiler section or AHU through door openings, stairwells and hatches with only inches of clearance; layout as found, no two jobs alike.

sources.system: Konecranes automated steel mill cranes

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated crane transport and placement of coils/slabs. Transfer: same class of machine (suspended load on hoist ropes) moving multi-tonne loads along collision-free paths and setting them into tight storage positions, i.e. the maneuvering half of this task in a purpose-built automated bay.
