tasks.label: Select gear, such as cables, pulleys, and winches, according to load weights and sizes, facilities, and work schedules.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Construction site crane pick: rigger/lift planner determines the weight, center of gravity and dimensions of a structural steel member, precast panel or rooftop HVAC unit, then specifies the sling type and rated capacity (wire rope, synthetic round slings, chain), shackles, spreader/lifting beam and tag lines, accounting for sling angle, access, and where the pick falls in the day's crane schedule.

Industrial machinery moving inside a manufacturing plant: millwright-rigger determines what chain hoists, come-alongs, jacks, machine skates, wire rope and softeners are needed to move a press or CNC machine, checking overhead monorail/beam capacities, floor loading, doorway and aisle clearances, and the plant's shutdown window.

Entertainment rigging: arena/theatre rigger selects chain motors, truss, steel wire rope bridles, shackles, span sets and deck chain for a show hang, based on point loads from the production's rigging plot, the venue's published beam capacities and rigging grid, and the load-in/out schedule.

Shipyard/marine work: rigger selects wire rope pendants, blocks, winches, shackles and spreader beams for lifting a ship module, propeller shaft or engine component, considering drydock and gantry crane capacities, hook height, tidal/vessel constraints and shift scheduling.

Logging yard/cable yarding: rigger determines choker sizes and lengths, blocks, guy lines, straps and mainline/haulback cable sizes for the day's yarding corridor, based on log sizes and species, terrain and deflection, and the yarding plan.

Routine repeat lift: rigger picks the standard gear package for a familiar recurring job (e.g., loading a known machine onto a lowboy), confirming rated capacities and current inspection tags, and confirming the gear is not committed to another crew that shift.

tasks.label: Dismantle and store rigging equipment after use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Construction site, after a crane pick: rigger disconnects synthetic/wire-rope slings, shackles, spreader or lifting beam and tag lines from the set load (often working off a ladder, lift or the erected steel), untwists and coils slings, inspects them per OSHA/ASME for cuts and broken wires, tags out damaged gear, and loads everything into a gang box, conex or the crane truck. Uneven ground, mud, weather, other trades moving through.

Arena/theatre entertainment load-out: after the show, riggers up in the roof steel or on catwalks/in lifts unhook chain hoists, motors, steel bridles, span sets and shackles from beams, lower them to the deck, break down truss sections, coil hoist chain and motor/control cable, pack hardware into road cases and hoist carts, and load the trucks under overnight time pressure.

Manufacturing plant machinery move: after the machine is set and grouted, rigger removes chain falls, come-alongs, hydraulic gantry/jacks, rollers, skates, dollies, cribbing and slings from around the equipment, cleans and coils the gear, and returns it to the rigging loft or tool crib with in/out records; indoor plant floor with production equipment and personnel around.

Shipyard/marine: after a hull section, engine or outfitting lift, riggers strip wire rope pendants, blocks, snatch blocks, chain falls, turnbuckles and staging rigging from the ship or dock structure, spool or coil the wire, and stow it in the rigging shop; confined decks, ladders, weather, salt exposure.

Film/TV or theatre studio: after a shoot or run, rigger derigs points from the permanent studio grid or pipe grid, removes clamps, safeties, spansets, chain and pick-up cables, coils cable, and stores gear on carts and shelves in the studio's rigging store; controlled indoor stage.

Logging yard/skyline setting: after yarding is complete, rigging crew unhooks chokers and butt rigging, pulls blocks, straps and guylines off stumps and the spar/tower, spools mainline/haulback onto the yarder drums, and stores blocks, shackles and straps on the machine or crummy; steep, brush-covered terrain taken as found.

sources.system: Elebia automatic lifting hooks (evo series, auto shackles, quick-release hooks)
sources.developer: Elebia Autohooks S.L.U. (distributed by Holloway Houston, Mazzella)
sources.title: Elebia Automatic Lifting Hooks | Holloway Houston
sources.claim: Elebia automatic crane hooks are the closest commercial automation to detaching rigging after a lift, but attachment and release are performed by a human with a remote control; the devices only open the hook and do not coil, inspect or stow slings and hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: releasing slings from a load/hook at the end of a lift, the first step of derigging. It does not transfer to the whole task because it is remote-button operated (not autonomous) and performs no dismantling, coiling, inspection or storage of the gear.

sources.system: Digit (with Agility Arc)
sources.title: GXO deploys humanoid robots in Spanx warehouse | DC Velocity
sources.claim: The most mature autonomous humanoid material handling deployment moves rigid, standardized totes between fixed stations inside a structured warehouse; nothing comparable handles heavy slings, chain hoists or truss at height.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling and put-away of objects in a structured human work facility (E2). It does not transfer: the objects are light rigid totes on flat floor, not deformable multi-hundred-pound slings, chain and hardware removed from overhead structure.

sources.system: SGTM (Sliding and Grasping for Tangle Manipulation) on an ABB YuMi bilateral robot
sources.title: Autonomously Untangling Long Cables (arXiv:2207.07813)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous manipulation of rope-like objects is limited to thin, light cables on a laboratory workcell with partial success rates, far below the reliability needed to coil, bundle and stow rigging slings and hoist chain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of deformable linear objects (cable untangling/slack management), the core skill in coiling and stowing slings, hoist chain and control cable. Performance does not carry over: lab bench, 3 m thin cable, ~50-67% success.

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing cell (UR10e arm, RealSense D405, custom mechatronic screwdriver)
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic disassembly in a purpose-built cell has been demonstrated only for small threaded fasteners on fixtured consumer devices, not for rigging hardware such as shackle pins, hoist bridles or truss pins with slings attached.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous disassembly of a fixtured assembly in an E1 cell. It does not transfer: objects are small electronics screws on a bench, whereas rigging teardown involves heavy hardware, deformable slings and chain, and subsequent inspection and stowage.

tasks.label: Attach loads to rigging to provide support or prepare them for moving, using hand and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor construction jobsite crane pick: rigger selects and attaches wire-rope/synthetic slings, shackles, spreader bars and tag lines to structural steel members, precast panels, rooftop HVAC units, pipe spools or modular assemblies, judging center of gravity and sling angles, tightening shackle pins with hand and power tools; each load differs, ground and weather vary, other trades work nearby.

Millwright/machinery rigging inside a manufacturing plant, refinery or power house: attaching eyebolts, chain slings, shackles, come-alongs and chain hoists to motors, pumps, presses, transformers or vessels for an overhead-crane or gantry move in congested aisles; loads are one-off, lifting points must be located or fabricated, and clearances are tight.

Repetitive hookup of standardized loads in a controlled shop, mill or terminal yard: coils, slabs, plate, bar bundles, bulk material or intermodal containers engaged with a matched lifting device (C-hook, magnet, tongs, grab, spreader) or with pre-rigged slings, many cycles per shift on a fixed layout with known load geometry.

Entertainment/stage rigging: at height in an arena, theatre or convention hall, attaching bridles, steel slings, shackles, beam clamps and chain motors to overhead building steel, then attaching truss, line-array speakers, scenery and lighting to the hoists; overhead structures and rigging plots differ venue to venue, work is done on ladders, lifts or from the grid under time pressure.

Shipyard/marine rigging: attaching shackles, chain and wire slings, lifting beams and turnbuckles to hull blocks, panels, deck houses and shipboard machinery for a gantry or crawler crane lift in a graving dock, platen area or quayside; loads are large one-off weldments with lifting lugs, worked outdoors amid staging and scaffolding.

Logging/wood yard rigging: hooking logs and log bundles for movement — setting chokers or attaching grapples/tongs to stems at a landing, and hooking or grappling bundles off trucks and rail cars in a mill log yard; loads are irregular natural objects, ground is rough, and weather is uncontrolled.

tasks.label: Manipulate rigging lines, hoists, and pulling gear to move or support materials, such as heavy equipment, ships, or theatrical sets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mill or plant repetitive heavy transfers: a rigger uses an overhead bridge crane with a dedicated lifting attachment (C-hook, magnet, vacuum lifter, coil tongs) to hoist standardized loads — steel coils, paper rolls, slabs, dies — from a fixed pick station and stack or land them at a marked position inside the building.

One-off machinery move inside a manufacturing plant or powerhouse: rigging a unique 5-50 ton machine (press, transformer, pump, chiller) with slings, spreader bars, chainfalls, come-alongs, hydraulic jacks, skates and gantry; hauling and tensioning lines by hand to inch the load through tight clearances, past piping and occupied workstations, onto anchor bolts.

Active construction site lift: hooking to a mobile or tower crane, hauling taglines, running chain motors and pulling gear to guide structural steel, precast, rooftop HVAC units or generators through wind, mud, congested laydown and other trades, then dogging the load down onto bolts or curbs.

Entertainment rigging: in a theatre, arena or studio, hanging and operating chain hoists and winches to fly trusses, LED walls, drops and set pieces — pulling bridles and dead-hangs to high steel at load-in, then running line sets/hoists to trim and cueing set moves during rehearsal and performance.

Shipyard or marine rigging: hoisting hull blocks, engines, propellers, stores and gangways with cranes, chainfalls and winches; handling mooring, pulling and tending lines dockside and aboard; loads are heavy, irregular, and placed in confined ship spaces.
Logging yard cable rigging: setting and hauling skyline, mainline, haulback and choker rigging on steep, uneven terrain to yard logs from the cut to the landing with a yarder and carriage.

tasks.label: Align, level, and anchor machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Manufacturing plant floor: rigger sets a multi-ton production machine (CNC machining center, press, extruder, conveyor line section) onto its concrete pad, walks it into layout position with skates/jacks, levels it with wedges/shims and a precision level to a few thousandths per foot, then drills concrete anchor holes and sets/torques anchor bolts (sometimes grouts).

Active construction site or new mechanical room/rooftop: rigger lands packaged equipment (rooftop AHU, chiller, generator, transformer, pump skid) on a housekeeping pad, curb, or vibration isolators; aligns to piping/duct connections and layout marks, shims to level, and anchors with wedge/epoxy anchors or welds to embeds. Site is congested, weather-exposed, and layout varies.

Process/power plant maintenance shutdown: rigger sets a pump, motor, gearbox, or fan on an existing baseplate/soleplate, levels the baseplate, performs coupling/shaft alignment with dial indicators or a laser kit, inserts shims under feet, and torques hold-down bolts to spec.

Entertainment venue: rigger installs and anchors stage machinery — chain hoists, winches, motorized truss, orchestra lift or turntable components — aligning bolt patterns to structural steel or grid beams at height and torquing structural fasteners.

Shipyard or aboard a vessel: rigger lands machinery in an engine room or on deck through hatches/confined access, aligns it to the shaftline or existing foundation, sets chocks/shims to line-up tolerances, and bolts it to the foundation.

Remote outdoor site (logging landing, quarry, temporary yard): rigger levels and anchors mobile/portable machinery — yarder, portable spar, chipper, crusher, winch — on uneven, unprepared ground using cribbing, jacks, guylines and ground anchors/deadmen.

sources.system: Dürr Flex Bolt / Flex decking marriage station
sources.title: Flex Bolt, Automatic Bolting System - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's Flex Bolt Cartesian axis system performs fully automatic bolting of the car ... after the body and its mechanical parts (powertrain, suspension, subframes) are joined in an automatic marriage/decking station — i.e., a heavy mechanical assembly is aligned to a structure and structurally fastened by machine in a purpose-built line cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive 'marriage' (decking) of a powertrain/chassis module to a body. It involves the same elements as aligning and anchoring machinery — a several-hundred-kilogram mechanical assembly brought into precise bolt-hole alignment with a receiving structure and fastened with torque-controlled structural bolts — and it is done in a purpose-built (E1) cell, so it substantiates E1 completion, not higher tiers.

sources.system: IPT AGV decking system (RedViking); Fori chassis marriage AGV
sources.title: Automotive Assembly Decking AGV - RedViking
sources.claim: Automated guided vehicles with integrated lifts position and raise heavy chassis/powertrain modules and automatically synchronize with overhead body conveyors on automotive marriage lines, performing the precise lift-and-mate positioning step by machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and mating a heavy chassis module to a car body. It covers the align-and-level element of the rigger task — bringing a heavy load up to a receiving structure in controlled, synchronized, millimetric motion — but only inside a purpose-built decking loop, supporting E1.

sources.system: MIRAI AI-vision robots with automatic torque wrench
sources.developer: Micropsi Industries (with a leading US automotive OEM)
sources.title: Leading US automotive OEM Automated bolt torquing — Micropsi Industries
sources.claim: Seven robots with AI-vision guidance and automatic torque wrenches were deployed at a US automotive OEM assembly station to locate and tighten bolts despite X/Y/Z variance in bolt position, inconsistent parts, and unstable lighting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production bolt torquing with part-position variance. It substantiates the 'anchor' element — autonomous location and torque-controlled tightening of fasteners on parts that are not perfectly presented — at a fixed station on a production line, i.e., E1-style structured presentation.

sources.system: Electroimpact robotic OSI-Bolt installation system
sources.date: 2015 (SAE technical paper; systems in production use since)
sources.title: Electroimpact whitepaper: automated solution for installing OSI-Bolts (2015-01-2512)
sources.claim: Electroimpact's robotic systems automatically drill and install structural bolts in large aerospace assemblies, measuring stack thickness and recording torque/angle to verify each installed fastener meets engineering requirements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated drilling and structural fastening of large, precisely located workpieces in metrology-referenced assembly cells. Comparable precision and fastener-torque verification to anchoring machinery, but demonstrated only in fenced, purpose-built aerospace cells (E1).

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Hilti Unveils Semi-Autonomous Overhead Drilling Robot, Called Jaibot — Construction Junkie
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a semi-autonomous mobile robot that locates and drills overhead anchor holes on construction sites from a BIM/CAD layout; it requires an operator for setup, transport and field supervision and it does not set anchors or install, align or level equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling anchor holes on real construction sites. It is the closest in-situ (E3) capability found, but it performs only one sub-step of the task, needs operator setup and repositioning, and never handles, aligns, levels or bolts down machinery — so it cannot support a positive E2/E3 judgment.

tasks.label: Load machines onto trucks to prepare for transportation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Machinery-moving/millwright crew loads a disconnected production machine (CNC machine, press, pump skid, generator) out of a customer's operating plant: rig it with slings or forks, skate it to the dock or yard, hoist it onto a flatbed or step-deck with forklift/gantry/crane, position it for axle weights and block it. Layout, clearances and lift points differ site to site, but the plant is a controlled industrial facility.

OEM/fabricator shipping bay: repeated outbound loading of newly built machines and skidded modules onto flatbeds or vans using the plant's overhead crane, lifting beam, or heavy forklift. Known load geometry, marked lift points, dedicated loading bay, dunnage and blocking per a standard shipping procedure.

Outdoor construction/industrial jobsite: loading equipment and machines (compressors, generators, rooftop HVAC units, pumps, small excavators, hoists) onto lowboys and trailers with a boom truck or mobile crane. Uneven ground, weather, overhead hazards, site layout changing week to week, no fixed dock.

Live-event/entertainment loadout at a venue loading dock: chain motors, hoists, truss, staging machinery and rolling road cases loaded into 53-ft trailers to a truck pack plan, under time pressure, with ramps and forklifts in a standard venue dock.

Shipyard, heavy-fabrication or port yard: marine machinery, fabricated modules and heavy components rigged with a gantry or mobile crane and set onto trucks/trailers in a controlled, paved yard with standard lifting gear and marked lift points.

Logging yard or remote resource site: loading self-propelled forestry/heavy machines (loaders, processors, yarders) onto lowboy trailers at a landing or roadside - rough terrain, no dock, machine walked or winched onto the deck and chained down.

sources.system: Actiw LoadMatic (Automated Truck Loading System)
sources.title: LoadMatic | Automated Truck Loading for Unmodified Trailers
sources.claim: Actiw LoadMatic (Joloda Hydraroll) is a commercially installed, fully automated truck-loading system that pushes a complete load of palletised or palletless industrial goods into regular unmodified trucks, trailers and containers from a fixed loading station in minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated loading of heavy industrial goods into road trailers. It transfers because the accepted output is the same (the unit placed and positioned in the truck's cargo space) and, under the E1 counterfactual, the machine arrives fixtured on the loading plate exactly as this purpose-built station presents its work. It does not cover rigging an as-found machine off a plant floor.

sources.system: Actiw LoadPlate
sources.title: LoadPlate | Automatically Load 40ft Containers in 5 minutes!
sources.claim: Actiw LoadPlate loads complex/project cargo weighing up to 30 tonnes into unmodified containers, trucks and trailers in a single automated push cycle; the cargo is first set onto the plate by forklift or crane.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated loading of heavy, irregular 'project cargo' (steel plate, long timber, machinery-class units) into trucks and containers. Weight class and irregularity match a rigged machine, and the forklift/crane placement onto the plate is precisely the fixtured presentation the E1 counterfactual grants.

sources.system: SlipBot / SlipLift autonomous trailer loading robots
sources.title: SlipLift Autonomous Trailer Loading Platform
sources.claim: Slip Robotics' SlipBot robots autonomously load and unload full trailer loads of freight at plant and warehouse docks in about five minutes and are in 24/7 production use at manufacturers including John Deere, GE Appliances, ... and Valeo.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of heavy pre-formed loads into over-the-road trailers at manufacturing docks. It substantiates the truck-loading step only when the load is already presented on the robot platform (an E1 fixtured presentation); the robots do not rig or lift a machine from a floor.

sources.system: FoxBot Mk3 autonomous trailer loader/unloader
sources.title: Fox Robotics Announces New Autonomous Forklift
sources.claim: The FoxBot Mk3 autonomous forklift picks, moves and loads or ... at dock operations; FoxBots are deployed in Walmart distribution centers and have performed millions of autonomous pallet moves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous forklift truck-loading inside a structured facility. It demonstrates unattended pick-and-load of standard palletised unit loads only; machine-class loads (multi-ton, no fork pockets, sling lift points, custom blocking) are outside its demonstrated envelope, so it does not carry these instances at E2.

sources.system: Automated crane system with Cephas control
sources.title: US steel mill installs fully automated cranes system - Hoist
sources.claim: A US steel mill runs three 190-ton automated overhead cranes that autonomously grab, move and place ~28-ton coils and stage them for shipment inside a gated, lockout-protected yard from which personnel are excluded; coils leaving the facility are placed so a forklift can handle them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended crane lifting and precise placement of multi-ton loads. It shows the heavy-lift portion of machine loading is automatable inside a fenced, purpose-built bay with a standard engagement device, but the source notes the final handoff for shipment is still made by forklift, so it does not cover as-found rigging or truck securement.

sources.system: Kalmar AutoStrad automated straddle carrier (automated truck handling)
sources.title: Automated truck handling: The last link in terminal automation
sources.claim: At Patrick Terminals, Kalmar AutoStrad automated straddle carriers place and pick containers on road trucks autonomously, closing the step of terminal operation that had previously required manual intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of ~30-tonne units onto road trucks inside an institution-controlled facility. Transfer is limited to standardized units engaged by a spreader at fixed corner castings; a machine requires sling selection, center-of-gravity judgment and blocking, which this system does not perform.

tasks.label: Attach pulleys and blocks to fixed overhead structures, such as beams, ceilings, and gin pole booms, using bolts and clamps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Manufacturing/industrial plant maintenance: rigger works from a scissor lift or platform 5-10 m up inside an operating plant, selects an overhead I-beam, hangs a snatch block or sheave using a beam clamp or through-bolts, torques the clamp screw/bolts, adds a safety shackle and secondary retention, then verifies the load path before a machinery move or equipment lift.

Construction project: rigger at height on structural steel, a concrete deck, or a gin pole boom attaches blocks/sheaves with bolts, beam clamps or shackles for material hoisting; layout differs site to site, access is by ladder, lift or climbing the steel, and weather, debris and other trades are present.

Entertainment rigging: rigger on a theatre gridiron, catwalk or arena roof steel attaches blocks/pulleys and head/loft blocks to overhead beams or trusses with beam clamps, bolts, shackles and safety cables, working to a show plot under tight load-in time pressure.

Shipyard / aboard ship: rigger attaches blocks to deckhead structure, padeyes, masts or cargo gear inside confined, congested compartments or on deck, using bolts, clamps and shackles, often overhead in awkward postures with limited access.

Logging yard / yarding operation: rigger attaches blocks (skyline, guyline, haulback blocks) to a gin pole boom, tower/yarder or spar with bolts, clamps and shackles, outdoors on uneven ground in variable weather, sometimes climbing the pole or working from a boom.

sources.system: Zeman SBA (Steel Beam Assembler) robotic assembly/welding line at Prospect Steel
sources.developer: Zeman Bauelemente (supplied in the US via Peddinghaus)
sources.title: Automated fitting and welding becomes reality for Prospect Steel
sources.claim: Zeman Steel Beam Assembler robotic line in a structural steel fabrication shop: an assembly robot picks steel attachments (stiffeners, plates, brackets) from a parts table in any orientation, scans and positions them precisely on a fixtured, conveyor-fed structural beam while welding robots fasten them; runs automatically once the operator commences the job.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching a steel fitting to a structural beam. It transfers to attaching a block/pulley to a beam in a purpose-built cell because the objects (steel beam, tens-of-kg steel attachment), the placement precision, and the fixtured presentation of the beam are comparable; only the fastening method (weld rather than bolt/clamp) differs, which items 1 and 2 cover.

sources.system: Vision-guided robotic bolt-tightening station (Sick TriSpector1030 / Photoneo PhoXi 3D sensors)
sources.developer: INESC TEC with automaker (reported in ASSEMBLY)
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines
sources.claim: A 3D-vision-guided six-axis robot performs torque-controlled bolt tightening of rear axle dampers to the underside (overhead orientation) of vans on a moving automotive assembly line, compensating for workpiece position variation with 3D perception of the attachment structure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torquing structural bolts on an overhead-oriented attachment point. It transfers because the rigger's block attachment ends in torqueing bolts or a clamp screw at a defined attachment point; the robot locates the attachment structure by 3D vision and tightens to specified torque in a station-based (E1) setting.

sources.system: Electroimpact automated wing panel drilling/fastening machines (HAWDE and panel riveting cells)
sources.developer: Electroimpact (for Airbus A380 wing panel production)
sources.title: Automating Wing Panel Assembly | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Electroimpact automated wing-panel machines in fixtured aerospace workcells drill, probe and install structural fasteners (bolts, lockbolts, collars) into large structural assemblies with virtually no manual labor, each cell built around machine and fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated installation and setting of structural bolts into a fixtured metal structure. It transfers to bolting a block to a fixtured beam because hole location, bolt insertion and collar/nut installation to a structural spec are the same operations the rigger performs with bolts, in a purpose-built fixtured cell.

sources.system: Hilti Jaibot
sources.title: Hilti's Overhead Drilling Robot Brings Further Automation to the Jobsite | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Hilti Jaibot is a commercially sold, semi-autonomous jobsite robot that autonomously drills overhead anchor holes in concrete ceilings from BIM data on real construction sites, but it only drills and marks; a worker still sets anchors and installs any hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead hole drilling on a construction site. Cited to bound the in-situ frontier: the most mature construction-site overhead robot drills only and does not lift, position or fasten load-rated hardware to beams, so it cannot substantiate E3 or E2 completion of this task.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E. (Robotic Installation System for Elevators, ABB IRB 2600 arm)
sources.date: 2020 first operational deployment; in use through 2026
sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators | Schindler Global Large Projects
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E. is a self-climbing robotic system that autonomously measures, drills and installs around a thousand anchor bolts in high-rise elevator shafts, running around the clock with an on-site operator for quality control; it works on flat concrete shaft walls and installs anchors only, not load-rated blocks or clamped fittings on beams.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ autonomous anchor installation in a building. Cited to bound the frontier: it operates inside a purpose-adapted, self-climbing rail platform in a uniform concrete shaft and installs bare anchors, so it does not substantiate positioning and clamping/bolting a heavy pulley block on arbitrary overhead beams at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Fabricate, set up, and repair rigging, supporting structures, hoists, and pulling gear, using hand and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field setup and field repair of rigging on a construction, heavy-haul, utility or logging-yard job site: selecting and assembling wire-rope/chain/synthetic slings, shackles, spreader bars, snatch blocks and tag lines to a specific load; hanging and reeving chain falls, come-alongs and tirfors from beams, hooks or anchor points, often at height or on uneven ground; cutting, wrapping, seizing and clamping cable and replacing damaged components with hand and power tools; weather, clutter and one-off geometry differ every lift.

Rigging setup inside a manufacturing plant, powerhouse or shipyard for a machine move or equipment installation: bolting or clamping beam trolleys and chain hoists to overhead structure, installing padeyes/lifting lugs and sheave blocks, reeving cable through blocks, building cribbing and jacking supports, torquing fasteners and adjusting turnbuckles with hand and power tools in and around existing equipment.

Entertainment rigging in an arena, theatre or studio: assembling truss sections and ground-support towers with pins and clips, hanging chain motors and bridles from steel or grid beams, fabricating and terminating steel cable slings (nicopress/deadhang), installing shackles and safeties overhead on a ladder, lift or beam, then testing and adjusting the system before the show.

Rigging-shop fabrication of lifting assemblies: measuring and cutting wire rope or chain to length, forming Flemish eyes and pressing swage sleeves, assembling chain slings with master links, coupling links and hooks, sewing/assembling synthetic sling hardware, proof-load testing on a test bed and tagging the finished assembly to spec.

Inspection and repair of hoists, winches, blocks and pulling gear in a shop or maintenance bay: disassembling a chain hoist or lever puller, diagnosing worn brakes, load chain, sheaves and bearings, replacing parts, relubricating and reassembling, then load-testing and documenting the repair with hand and power tools.

Shop fabrication of supporting structures and below-the-hook steel: cutting, drilling, fitting and welding plate and structural sections into spreader beams, lifting frames, brackets, dunnage stands and anchor weldments to a drawing, then cleaning up and preparing the assembly for load test.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 robotic welding cells (Obsidian AI)
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 robotic welding cells autonomously scan, fit up and weld steel parts in fenced fabrication-shop cells and are commercially deployed across the US and Canada; this covers the welding/fitting of fabricated steel supporting structures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic structural-steel welding. A rigger's shop fabrication of supporting structures (spreader beams, lifting frames, brackets) is cut-fit-weld work on the same plate and structural sections; Path's cells handle varying fit-up and parts up to 70 ft in a purpose-built cell, so performance carries to that fabrication instance at E1.

sources.system: Voortman V630 CNC beam drilling line with gripper truck / VB saw and MSI material handling
sources.title: Voortman V630 | CNC Beam Drill Line | Voortman Steel Machinery
sources.claim: Voortman CNC beam drilling/sawing lines cut, drill and mill structural profiles with automatic material handling and can run autonomously with a single operator supervising, covering the cutting and hole-making steps of fabricating steel supporting structures in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated structural profile cutting and drilling. It supplies the cut-to-length and hole-making portion of fabricating a rigger's supporting structure; same steel sections and tolerances, in a fixtured conveyor-fed line (E1).

sources.system: Elebia evo5–evo25 automatic crane hooks and hookbot
sources.title: EVO 5 and EVO 25 Crane Hook | Smart Solutions | Elebia
sources.claim: The nearest commercial technology for attaching and releasing rigging to loads is the Elebia evo automatic crane hook, which closes and releases on the sling or master link only when a human presses a button on a remote control; there is no autonomous system that selects, assembles or installs rigging gear.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hooking on / attaching lifting gear to a load. It is the closest fielded system to a rigger's setup work, but it is remote-operated and only actuates a dedicated hook; it does not assemble, install or repair rigging, so it supports no positive judgment.

sources.system: Roborigger / SMCC autonomous tower crane
sources.title: Sumitomo Mitsui Construction teams with Roborigger to develop autonomous tower crane - Roborigger
sources.claim: Roborigger's crane-suspended device provides load orientation control and remote release and has been integrated into an autonomous tower crane trial on a Tokyo construction site, but it manipulates the suspended load rather than fabricating, setting up or repairing rigging gear.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crane load handling on a construction site. It shows crane motion and load rotation can be automated, but the rigging itself (slinging, hoist installation, gear repair) is still done by human riggers, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.system: Talurit LKA 28-PS automatic cutting machine and 500T swager; Wirop swaging presses
sources.title: TALURIT LKA 28-PS and 500T Swager: the slingmakers dream − Products − LRW Media
sources.claim: Wire-rope sling fabrication equipment on the market consists of operator-fed cutting and swaging machines, with the rigger handling the rope and sling around the machine; no robotic cell performs the full sling-making sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (sling fabrication): the state of the art is a human slingmaker feeding automatic cutting and swaging machines, so the fabrication instance is not completed by a robotic system even in a purpose-built shop.

tasks.label: Clean and dress machine surfaces and component parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rigging/maintenance shop bench work on small rigging hardware and machine component parts: degreasing shackles, hooks, pins, sheave wheels, turnbuckles and block parts, wire-brushing rust and scale, filing/stoning burrs, nicks and galled spots off bearing and mating surfaces, then oiling and reassembling. Parts are loose, carried to a bench, mixed sizes and one-off items.

Plant or shipyard machine shop: cleaning and dressing larger machine components that have been removed for a move, overhaul or reinstallation — winch and hoist drums, sheave wheels, gear housings, bedplates, machined mounting pads and shaft journals. Descale/blast off rust, wipe grease, then dress burrs and high spots on machined surfaces so the part will seat.

In-place work on installed machinery in a plant or on a vessel's deck: wiping down and dressing the surfaces of a crane, hoist, press, or deck winch where it stands — grease-caked drum flanges, brake surfaces, guide rails, keyways — reaching overhead, in confined spaces, alongside other running equipment and workers.

Outdoor construction/industrial job site: before rigging and bolt-up, cleaning and dressing the surfaces of components staged in the laydown area — wiping mud, grease and preservative off faying surfaces and flanges, wire-brushing rust from pin bores and lug faces, dressing burrs on pins, shims and machine soleplates. Weather, dirt, uneven ground.

On-location entertainment venue or logging yard: cleaning and dressing rigging components in service — theater grid blocks, sheaves, chain-hoist bodies and hooks; logging blocks, guy-line hardware and shackles at a landing. Grit, pitch and grease removed, sheave grooves and hook throats dressed, parts inspected and lubricated.

sources.system: PushCorp force-compliance devices / servo spindles on robotic deburring cells
sources.title: Robotic Deburring & Automated Material Removal Applications - PushCorp
sources.claim: Commercial robotic deburring systems use force-controlled end-of-arm tooling on industrial robot arms to automatically remove burrs and ... metal parts inside a workcell, with more consistent pressure and finish than manual operators.
sources.transferJustification: Deburring/edge dressing of metal components is the 'dress' half of the task on comparable objects (machined, cast steel parts) at comparable precision; it is performed in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Smart Finishing Robotic Workcell (Argus OS, Zivid 3D cameras)
sources.title: Case Study - Cohesive Robotics Surface Finishing Work Cell (Zivid)
sources.claim: Cohesive Robotics supplies autonomous AI- and 3D-vision-equipped finishing workcells that grind, sand, polish and deburr complex metal parts for high-mix, low-volume fabrication shops, i.e. handling part-to-part variability rather than a single fixed part.
sources.transferJustification: Grinding/sanding/polishing/deburring of varied metal parts in a cell is the same surface-conditioning and dressing operation on comparable objects; 3D scanning removes the need for per-part programming.

sources.system: Scan&Sand autonomous robotic sanding cell
sources.title: Scan&Sand helps automate labor-intensive ambulance manufacturing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Sand autonomous sanding cells are deployed in production at manufacturers (e.g., Life Line Emergency Vehicles, BetterWay Products); the system scans an object and sands ... is built for high-mix work with great variation in piece shape and size.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous scan-then-abrade surface conditioning of one-off workpieces demonstrates the perception-and-path-generation capability needed to clean and dress varied, unprogrammed component surfaces in a cell.

sources.system: Blastman B20C / B20S blast cleaning robots in robotized blast rooms
sources.title: BLASTMAN BLAST CLEANING ROBOTS IN DIFFERENT INDUSTRIES - Blastman Robotics Ltd
sources.claim: Blastman robots installed in purpose-built blast rooms blast-clean heavy cast and fabricated steel components — up to 200 tonnes — in a fully automated process, removing corrosion, scale and residues, then blowing off abrasive dust.
sources.transferJustification: Blast cleaning of large rusty steel castings and weldments is the 'clean' half of the task on objects of the same class and size as winch drums, sheaves, bedplates and rigging hardware, performed with the work brought into the machine's chamber.

sources.system: CleanTech robotic laser cleaning workcells / CleanTech Titan FX
sources.title: How Laser Cleaning Robotic Workcells Pick up the Pace on the Shopfloor - New Equipment Digest
sources.claim: Enclosed robotic laser cleaning workcells (e.g., Laser Photonics CleanTech systems, including large-format units with a 6 x 12 ft envelope) automatically remove rust and contamination from components and condition the surfaces, at higher volumes than manual methods.
sources.transferJustification: Rust/grease removal and surface conditioning of metal parts in an enclosed cell is directly the 'clean' element of cleaning and dressing machine surfaces and component parts.

sources.system: FANUC material removal robots with ATI compliant tooling
sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC supplies production robots for material-removal work including deburring and polishing, using radially compliant tooling to maintain consistent contact and uniform results on parts such as wheels and crankshafts.
sources.transferJustification: Robotic deburring/polishing of machined metal components matches the dressing operation on comparable steel parts at comparable precision, inside a fenced industrial cell.

tasks.label: Install ground rigging for yarding lines, attaching chokers to logs and to the lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Breaking out on a steep-slope highlead / standing-skyline cable unit: rigging crew member walks a clearcut cutover of stumps, slash and mud, drags 20-30 lb wire-rope chokers off the butt rigging up to 50-100 ft laterally, passes each choker under or around felled-and-bucked logs, seats the nubbin in the bell, clears out and radios the yarder engineer for the turn.

Skyline unit with a motorized/slack-pulling carriage: crew pulls chokers laterally from the carriage skidding line to two or three logs of mixed size on broken ground, chokes each, hooks chokers to the carriage line, signals for slack-out/inhaul; several turns per hour in rain, dust or cold.

Rigging up and road changes: pulling strawline/haywire through the brush, hanging corner and tail blocks on stumps and standing trees, wrapping straps and shackling anchors, setting tailholds and guylines, then moving the whole ground rigging to the next yarding road.

Ground-based work on gentler terrain: choking logs behind a cable skidder winch or a small tower/mini-yarder in a thinning or woodlot, walking the line out, hooking two to four logs per drag, unhooking at the skid trail.

Landing / deck work: chaser unhooks chokers from turns arriving at the landing, untangles and re-hangs chokers on the butt rigging or carriage, re-chokes hung-up or decked logs for the loader or for a re-pull with the yarding line.

sources.system: APEX HY202 Smart Yarder with APEX electric grapple carriage (ATL / APPM / Mana Logging, FGR programme)
sources.developer: Applied Teleoperation Ltd with AP Plant & Machinery and Forest Growers Research
sources.title: Teleoperation to improve safety and productivity and address labour shortages - fgr.nz
sources.claim: The most advanced cable-yarder automation in commercial development (APEX HY202 Smart Yarder with electric grapple carriage, NZ) has automated inhaul and outhaul of the line, but the attachment of stems to the carriage is still commanded by a human operator in another machine; no autonomous choker setting or autonomous log attachment in the cutover is demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching logs to a yarding line by grapple instead of choker. Cited to show that even the most automated cable-yarding system leaves the log-attachment step under human control in the cutover.

sources.system: Falcon Claw motorised grapple carriage
sources.developer: DC Equipment (Falcon Forestry Equipment), New Zealand
sources.title: Hydraulic Log Grapples & Carriages | Timber Grabbers & Loaders - Logging Equipment
sources.claim: The commercial substitute for manual choker setting on steep slopes is a motorised grapple carriage that is remote-controlled by a human operator, not an autonomous machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connecting logs to the yarding line in place of chokers. Shows the field-proven alternative to a choker setter is continuous remote control, which cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

sources.system: Grapple carriages / swing yarders on steep terrain
sources.developer: New Zealand Institute of Forestry (review of steep terrain mechanisation)
sources.title: Mechanising steep terrain harvesting operations - NZIF
sources.claim: Grapple-based cable yarding is the industry's route to removing choker setters from the hillside, i.e. the manual choker-setting task is eliminated by mechanisation rather than performed by a robot.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the same task: the mechanised alternative replaces chokers with an operator-controlled grapple, so no cited field system performs the choker-setting instance autonomously.

sources.system: SLU/Luleå unmanned forwarder platform (first experimental unmanned forestry machine)
sources.developer: La Hera et al., Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences / Luleå University of Technology
sources.title: Exploring the feasibility of autonomous forestry operations: Results from the first experimental unmanned machine
sources.claim: An experimental unmanned forestry machine autonomously detected, grasped and loaded full-size logs outdoors, but only in a simplified, prepared test environment and as a research demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously attaching logs to an extraction machine (grapple grasp and load). Comparable objects (full-size logs) and coarse precision, but demonstrated only in a simplified, machine-prepared outdoor test area, so it supports at most an E1-style prepared setting.

sources.system: Automated log grasping forwarder (stereo-camera target-point identification with boom-tip control)
sources.developer: Semberg, Nilsson et al., Skogforsk / Troëdsson teleoperation laboratory, Sweden
sources.title: Real-time target point identification and automated log grasping by a forwarder, using a single stereo camera for both object detection and boom-tip control
sources.claim: Real-time automated log grasping by a full-scale forwarder crane using a stereo camera was demonstrated in a prepared teleoperation-laboratory test yard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine attachment of logs to a lifting device without a person at the log. Same objects (logs) and coarse precision; the tests ran in a prepared laboratory test yard, supporting a purpose-built (E1) setting only.

sources.system: Signode BPX compression strapping system (and BRP fully automatic steel strapping machine)
sources.date: 2022-11 (product line, in commercial use for years)
sources.title: Application-Specific Strapping Machines | Signode
sources.claim: Fully automatic strapping machines commercially installed on lumber lines pass and tension a steel or PET band completely around wood packages and seal it, with the load presented by the conveyor/compression platen and no human at the package.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: encircling wood (lumber packages) and round stock with a tensioned steel band and securing it — the mechanical analogue of applying a choker hitch to a log. Comparable object class and coarse precision, but only where the workpiece is fixtured and presented on a purpose-built line, i.e. E1.

roles.title: Signal and Track Switch Repairers
roles.description: Install, inspect, test, maintain, or repair electric gate crossings, signals, signal equipment, track switches, section lines, or intercommunications systems within a railroad system.

tasks.label: Inspect and test operation, mechanical parts, and circuitry of gate crossings, signals, and signal equipment such as interlocks and hotbox detectors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic (monthly/quarterly) FRA-required inspection and test of a highway-rail grade crossing warning system at a public road crossing: observe a gate/light/bell activation cycle, time warning and gate descent, measure lamp voltage and flash rate, perform ground tests at the instrument case with a voltmeter, test standby power and AC cut-out, check gate mechanism, counterweights and linkage for wear, and record results. Outdoors beside live road traffic, in all weather; layout differs at every crossing.

Inspection and testing of wayside signals and their instrument cases along mainline right-of-way: verify aspect display and lamp/LED voltage on mast or cantilever signals, shunt and test track circuits, check relays, batteries and chargers, insulation, arrester and ground tests, plus visual check of mechanical parts. Trackside in ballast, brush, mud or snow under train protection rules; each location differs.

Inspection and testing at an interlocking or control point: switch machine/point detector operation and obstruction test, lock rod and point gap checks, correspondence between machine, signal aspects and interlocking logic, and testing of vital circuits and relays in the relay house. Field junction location, outdoors, with widely varying equipment vintages and layouts.

Inspection, calibration check and functional test of a wayside detector installation (hot bearing/hotbox detector, dragging equipment detector, wheel impact detector): clean and align scanners, verify transducers and gating, check calibration against a reference heat source, test alarm/announcement circuits and communications. Trackside in open country.

Inspection and testing of signal apparatus inside a railroad-controlled yard, terminal or transit facility: dwarf signals, yard switch machines and hand-throw electric locks, retarders, and yard-road crossing gates; test operation, mechanical parts and circuits and note defects. Paved, access-controlled premises but with active switching movements.

Bench inspection and testing of signal equipment brought into a signal shop or test room: periodic verification of vital relays, crossing predictors, code units and circuit boards on test racks — contact and coil measurements, insulation, pick-up/drop-away and timing checks, mechanical condition of armature and contacts — with pass/fail tagging and records.

sources.system: NS1 Relay Test Bench (NS1-Manager)
sources.title: Our Catalog - LEIC
sources.claim: Commercial automated test bench that verifies railway vital signalling relays to national standards, running the test sequence and measurements under machine control once the relay is placed in the rack.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop verification of vital signalling relays. A signal relay is 'signal equipment' whose operation, mechanical parts (armature, contacts) and circuitry the worker tests; the bench exercises and measures exactly those properties with the item presented fixtured, as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: NS1-safety Relay test bench
sources.title: NS1-safety Relay test bench – Station One
sources.claim: The same bench performs the specific electrical/mechanical measurements a relay test requires: insulation, contact resistance, coil resistance, switching time and switching current.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: documents that the automated bench covers the full periodic test content for a relay rather than a sub-step.

sources.system: ANYmal
sources.title: Transforming Rail Operations Through Automated Robotic Inspection
sources.claim: Legged robot performs autonomous inspection rounds inside a rail maintenance facility, but the work is camera/sensor observation of wagons, not electrical or functional testing of equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds in a railway facility (E2). Establishes that the deployed rail-robotics frontier is visual/sensor observation; it does not carry over to probing circuits, operating gates or testing signal mechanisms.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit / Autowalk
sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Commercially deployed quadruped runs autonomous industrial inspection missions reading gauges, indicator lights and thermal/acoustic signatures; it does not make contact electrical measurements or actuate equipment under test.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds in structured industrial plants. Shows available inspection robots observe instruments rather than performing meter probing, shunt/ground tests, or operating gates and switch machines, so capability does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: Robotic-arm signalling test environment
sources.title: Automated Testing in Railways: Leveraging Robotic Arm Precision and Efficiency for Superior Customizability and Usability Test Case Execution
sources.claim: Research robotic arm used to execute functional test cases on railway signalling (onboard SIL4) equipment in a purpose-built test environment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic execution of functional tests on signalling equipment in a lab. Supports only interface actuation of bench-mounted equipment in a purpose-built rig, not field inspection of wayside mechanisms and circuits.

sources.system: LiDAR-based automated grade crossing survey system
sources.developer: US Federal Railroad Administration, Office of Research, Development and Technology (with university partner)
sources.title: Stationary automated signaling equipment inspection system using lidar (US 10,094,657)
sources.claim: Automated grade-crossing survey developed for FRA measures gate positions and light aiming with lidar from a survey vehicle; sensing only, with no operational or circuit testing, and the platform is human-driven.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated survey of grade crossing signal geometry. Treated as non-supporting: autonomy is unclear (vehicle-borne survey) and it measures alignment only, omitting warning-time, ground, standby-power and mechanical tests.

tasks.label: Inspect electrical units of railroad grade crossing gates and repair loose bolts and defective electrical connections and parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine periodic (monthly/quarterly) inspection of the gate mechanism and flashing-light units at a public highway-rail grade crossing: open the mechanism housing at the roadside mast, inspect wiring, contacts and terminal lugs, check lamp voltages and gate motor circuit, tighten loose bolts on the mechanism, mast and arm hardware, and re-make loose or corroded electrical connections. Done in live road traffic, in all weather, on ballast/shoulder next to an active track.

Inspection and servicing of the electrical units inside the crossing control case/bungalow at a public crossing: relays, terminal boards, surge panels, cable posts and battery bank; torque terminal screws, clean and repair corroded or loose connections, and replace a defective plug-in relay, lamp module, or battery. Locked wayside enclosure, cramped, dusty, temperature-extreme, trackside.

Trouble call on a malfunctioning crossing (false activation, gate fails to descend, lights out): diagnose an unknown fault distributed across gate motor and contacts, wayside wiring, buried cable, relays and track circuits, then repair or replace the defective part and re-test the warning system. Often at night or in storms, under time pressure, with trains and road traffic present.

Repair after damage: gate arm knocked down by a vehicle, or lightning/storm damage to the crossing electrical units; assess damage, replace gate arm/mechanism parts and damaged conductors, re-secure loosened bolted hardware, realign and re-test. Roadside, debris present, variable damage, possible flagging protection.

Same electrical-unit inspection and bolt/connection repair at a crossing inside railroad- or plant-controlled premises (rail yard crossing, industrial lead, private crossing within a facility), where access is controlled, road traffic is minimal and layout is more uniform.

sources.system: MIRAI AI-vision + Universal Robots cobot with automatic torque wrench
sources.developer: Micropsi Industries (with a North American automotive OEM)
sources.title: Leading US automotive OEM — Automated bolt torquing | MIRAI Use cases
sources.claim: Micropsi Industries' MIRAI AI-vision system runs seven Universal Robots cobots with automatic torque wrenches that autonomously locate and torque bolts on a moving human-designed assembly line despite positional, lighting and part variance, at near-100% success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production bolt tightening. Transfer to 'repair loose bolts' on a fixtured crossing-gate electrical unit is direct — same objects (threaded fasteners), same tool (torque wrench), and the system already copes with bolt-position and lighting variance rather than fully rigid presentation.

sources.system: Inbolt GuideNOW vision-guided screwdriving/fastening
sources.title: Inbolt – the pioneer in 3D vision and AI for robotic guidance – goes global as it expands into the US and Japan
sources.claim: Inbolt's 3D-vision AI guides industrial robots (ABB, FANUC, Universal Robots) for screwdriving and fastening and is in production use in more than 50 factories, with tens of millions of autonomous robot cycles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided robotic screw driving/fastening on production parts. Same manipulation and torque-control demands as tightening loose bolts and terminal screws on an electrical unit presented in a fixture.

sources.system: Averex robotic wiring centre
sources.title: Rittal Forms New Business Unit To Support Customized Enclosure Production
sources.claim: Kiesling/Rittal's Averex robotic wiring centre performs fully automated wiring of control-cabinet mounting plates — cutting, crimping, routing and connecting wires into device and terminal-block connections to standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated making of screw-terminal electrical connections in control enclosures. A grade-crossing case is a control enclosure with the same terminal blocks, ferruled conductors and screw connections, so remaking/tightening a defective connection on a fixtured panel is comparable in objects and precision.

sources.system: Kitov One / Kitov-CorePlus robotic inspection
sources.title: The Missing Piece of Industry 4.0: Kitov.ai Automates Visual Inspection with CAD-Based AI
sources.claim: Kitov.ai's robotic CAD-based visual inspection systems autonomously inspect assembled products and detect mechanical defects including worn, untightened or defective screws, corrosion and assembly errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated visual inspection of assembled electromechanical products. It substantiates the 'inspect the electrical unit and find loose fasteners/defective connections' half of this task when the unit is presented to a robot-mounted camera in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: NIO Power Swap Station (Gen 3/4)
sources.title: China's Nio raises US$2.6 billion bet on EV battery swapping, plans to add 1,000 stations
sources.claim: NIO's power swap stations automatically detach the bolted high-voltage battery module from a vehicle and install a replacement, completing the electrical/mechanical exchange in about three minutes without human intervention, across thousands of deployed stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated unbolting, removal and reinstallation of a heavy electrical module with power connectors in a purpose-built station. Transfers to replacing a defective electrical part (relay, battery, module) and re-torquing its bolts when the unit is fixtured in a machine cell.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Levatas AI inspection
sources.developer: Avangrid / United Illuminating with Levatas and Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Avangrid Pilots Mobile Robot Dog to Advance Substation Inspections with AI
sources.claim: Utility field robotics deployed on institution-controlled electrical premises perform visual and thermal inspection rounds only; the Spot quadruped pilot at United Illuminating substations collects inspection data and does no repair, bolt tightening or component replacement.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field analogue to wayside electrical maintenance: an autonomous mobile robot working outdoors on controlled electrical premises. It shows the state of the art in such settings is inspection/data capture, not fastener or connection repair, so it cannot support E2/E3 for this task.

tasks.label: Test and repair track circuits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled periodic test of a mainline track circuit: hi-rail or walk to the signal location, open the instrument case/bungalow, meter track relay voltage/current and feed battery, walk to the circuit limits and apply a 0.06-ohm shunt to verify shunting/drop-away, adjust feed resistors or ballast compensation, then complete the required test record. Live outdoor right-of-way, ballast walking, weather, train traffic under protection.

Trouble call on a failed or erratic track circuit (false occupancy, failure to shunt, intermittent drop): travel to the reported location, sectionalize the circuit, meter at joints and cases, hunt broken or corroded rail bonds, cracked insulated joints, low ballast resistance after rain/snow, damaged track leads or buried cable, or a foreign shunt; isolate the fault under time pressure, often at night or in bad weather.

Field repair of track-circuit hardware after diagnosis: attach or replace rail bonds (exothermic weld, pin brazing, drilled/compressed bonds), renew track leads and cable splices (sometimes digging to buried cable), replace insulated joint components or a defective track relay in the case, then retest and prove the circuit before restoring it to service. Uneven ballast, restricted work windows.

Track circuits at a highway-grade crossing: test and repair the island and approach circuits and shunting for a constant-warning-time predictor, verify warning-time operation, chase shunting problems caused by rusty rail, road salt, paved-in rail or damaged bonds inside the crossing surface, with road traffic and pedestrians present.

Bench/rack work in a signal bungalow or signal shop: test coded track-circuit transmitter and receiver modules and vital track relays on standard racks or a shop test bench, repair or swap the defective unit, adjust and retest to specification, and complete the test record. Indoor, fixed layout, standard equipment.

sources.system: ROBEL Rail Automation ROBOT / ROSPECT (FANUC arms on a rail wagon)
sources.developer: ROBEL Rail Automation GmbH with FANUC
sources.title: Robel Rail Automation Uses FANUC Robots to Repair Railway Lines - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: ROBEL Rail Automation's rail-car-mounted FANUC dual-arm system detects internal and external rail/switch defects with ultrasound, cameras and eddy-current sensing, then repairs them automatically by welding, milling and grinding; prototype systems run on European networks. Scope is rail steel and switch components, not electrical track circuits.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic system that inspects and repairs trackside infrastructure in the same right-of-way setting; cited to show the demonstrated scope is metal defect repair on rails and points, with no electrical measurement, shunting, bonding or relay work, so it does not transfer to testing and repairing track circuits.

sources.system: RIRS (rail-road amphibious robotic inspection and repair system)
sources.developer: University research consortium, published in Computers and Electrical Engineering
sources.title: An autonomous rail-road amphibious robotic system for railway maintenance using sensor fusion and mobile manipulator - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: An autonomous rail-road amphibious maintenance robot with a payload manipulator was demonstrated on a half-kilometre railway test site; navigation was autonomous, but inspection used QR-coded artificial defects and repairs were executed as pre-defined arm routines.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest research demonstration of trackside mobile manipulation for inspection-and-repair; cited to show that even the diagnostic step was staged with QR markers and the repair step was scripted, so it cannot substantiate autonomous testing and repair of a real track circuit.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit autonomous inspection
sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot performs autonomous inspection missions inside industrial facilities, collecting visual, thermal, acoustic and gauge-reading data; it reports equipment condition but does not connect test leads, apply track shunts, or make electrical repairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial inspection rounds in institution-controlled facilities. Cited to bound the state of the art: deployed autonomy covers sensor-based observation, not the metered electrical testing, fault diagnosis and hands-on bonding/relay repair this task requires, so it does not transfer.

tasks.label: Drive motor vehicles to job sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Signal maintainer drives a company pickup/service truck from the signal shop or home terminal over metro and suburban public streets (and freeway segments) to a grade-crossing warning device, wayside signal, or relay bungalow reachable directly from the roadway; daytime traffic, traffic signals, parking on a shoulder or in a crossing quadrant.

Longer run over rural two-lane paved highways and small-town streets (30-100 miles) to a rural grade crossing, hot-box detector, or intermediate signal on a territory; variable weather (rain, fog, wind), sometimes after dark, destination varies daily by trouble ticket.

Final approach off the paved road: driving the service truck down an unpaved right-of-way access road, gravel/dirt service road, farm lane or field crossing (ruts, mud, cattle guards, gates) to reach a remote bungalow, switch machine, or switch heater alongside the track.

Hi-rail service truck: drive on public roads to a designated crossing, deploy rail gear, and travel on track under dispatcher/track authority to a signal or switch location not reachable by road, then set off at the next crossing.

Driving inside a railroad-controlled property - classification yard, terminal, intermodal facility, transit shop complex - over yard roadways and internal crossings to reach an interlocking, yard switch machine, retarder, or signal case; controlled access, posted rules, mixed pedestrian/rail traffic.

sources.system: Waymo Driver (Jaguar I-Pace / Zeekr RT robotaxis)
sources.title: Waymo begins offering freeway robotaxi rides in San Francisco, LA and Phoenix
sources.claim: Waymo operates a commercial, fully driverless (no human in the vehicle needed) ride-hailing service on public city streets in numerous US metros and, since November 2025, on freeways, carrying passengers point-to-point to arbitrary destinations within its service areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless point-to-point road transport of people and their belongings. It transfers to 'drive a motor vehicle to a job site' because the vehicle covers the same public street and freeway network, chooses routes to varying destinations, and delivers occupants and payload to a curbside stop.

sources.system: Waymo Driver robotaxi fleet
sources.title: Las Vegas joins growing list of cities with fully autonomous Waymo rides
sources.claim: As of July 2026 Waymo's fully driverless commercial operation spans many US metros (Phoenix, SF, LA, Austin, Atlanta, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, Orlando) and is moving to rider-only service in Denver, San Diego, Tampa and Las Vegas.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: driverless road transport to varying destinations across large metro road networks, which is what driving a service truck from the shop to a crossing or signal location consists of.

sources.system: Aurora Driver
sources.title: Aurora Triples Driverless Network to 10 Routes and Prepares to Expand Across U.S. Sun Belt
sources.claim: Aurora runs driverless Class 8 trucks with no human on board on public highways and surface streets across Texas, New Mexico and Arizona - ten lanes and over 250,000 driverless miles since April 2025 - including night, rain, fog and heavy wind.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless long-distance freight hauling over rural interstates, state highways and surface streets. Transfers to driving a service truck long distances across a rural signal territory - same roads, same weather, same requirement to arrive at a specific destination.

sources.system: Aurora Driver
sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Aurora launched commercial driverless (empty cab) trucking between Dallas and Houston in May 2025 after closing its safety case.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that driverless operation on public roads with no occupant is a fielded commercial service, not a demo; same transfer as item 2.

sources.system: Kodiak Driver (Atlas RoboTrucks)
sources.developer: Kodiak AI (Kodiak Robotics) / Atlas Energy Solutions
sources.title: Kodiak AI CEO: 10 Driverless Trucks Running Now, Targets Long-Haul Driverless Launch in 2H 2026
sources.claim: Kodiak's driverless Class 8 trucks run with no one in the ... over Atlas Energy's network of private unpaved dirt lease roads in the Permian ..., delivering frac sand to well sites; ten such trucks were in commercial driverless service as of early 2026 with no required remote monitor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless hauling over unpaved, unmarked private dirt roads to changing well-site destinations. This is the same driving problem as the final unpaved-access-road segment of a signal maintainer's trip - no lane markings, rough surface, no institution keeping the road to a standard.

sources.system: Kodiak Driver (Atlas RoboTrucks)
sources.title: Groundbreaking 2025 Milestone: Kodiak Driverless Trucks Revolutionize Permian Oilfield Logistics
sources.claim: The first Kodiak/Atlas driverless run was a 21-mile delivery with nobody in the cab over the dirt lease road network of the Permian Basin, and the operation has since run around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as item 4: unpaved, privately maintained access roads to a field work location, driven with no human aboard.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for hauling
sources.title: Cat MineStar Command for hauling manages the autonomous ecosystem
sources.claim: Caterpillar's MineStar Command for hauling operates hundreds of autonomous haul trucks at dozens of controlled industrial sites, having autonomously hauled more than 8.6 billion tonnes of material over site haul roads shared with other vehicles and personnel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless vehicle movement over the internal road network of an access-controlled industrial site to assigned work locations. Transfers to driving a service truck inside a railroad yard or terminal, where an institution controls who and what is present.

tasks.label: Install, inspect, maintain, and repair various railroad service equipment on the road or in the shop, including railroad signal systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic field inspection, testing and maintenance of wayside signal apparatus at a signal bungalow/instrument case along the mainline: opening the case, checking batteries and chargers, performing ground and insulation tests with a meter, adjusting track-circuit shunt and relay drop-away values, cleaning and replacing relays or vital logic cards, and documenting the FRA-required tests. Remote outdoor right-of-way, ballast and vegetation underfoot, all weather, with train traffic protection required.

Inspection, adjustment and repair of a highway-rail grade crossing warning system at a public road crossing: testing flashers, bell, gate motor and arm, checking warning time and constant-warning-time predictor calibration, replacing burned-out LED units, damaged gate arms or a failed gate mechanism, in a public street with vehicle and pedestrian traffic.

Track-switch machine work on the road or in a yard: adjusting point detection and throw rods, replacing or overhauling an electric switch machine or circuit controller, lubricating and re-gauging the mechanism, testing point obstruction detection, and re-wiring the machine's terminal board, kneeling in ballast between running rails.

Emergency call-out troubleshooting of a signal system failure anywhere on the territory (dark signal, false occupancy, broken rail bond, lightning-damaged surge panel, cut cable): driving/hi-railing to the site, tracing circuits with a meter and prints, locating and repairing the fault, and restoring the system to service, often at night or in bad weather.

New installation or upgrade work: setting signal masts, foundations and instrument houses, trenching and pulling signal cable, bonding rails, terminating and wiring hundreds of wires on terminal boards, then testing and cutting the new circuits into service under a signal-work window.

Shop bench work in the railroad's signal shop: diagnosing, repairing, cleaning, calibrating and recertifying signal components (vital relays, crossing predictors, code units, LED signal heads, battery chargers) on test racks, and building up wired instrument cases for field installation.

sources.system: ROBEL Rail Automation ROBOT (robotic rail/switch welding system)
sources.developer: ROBEL Rail Automation with ProRail, Strukton Rail, VolkerRail
sources.title: ROBOT Automated Switch and Infrastructure Maintenance | Railway-News
sources.claim: ROBEL Rail Automation's ROBOT is a container-mounted robotic milling/welding system tested on the Dutch network that scans, mills, preheats, welds and re-profiles damaged rail and switch frogs in the track corridor, overseen by an operator and a helper.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-corridor repair of a track switch component (frog welding). It is the closest robotic in-track repair system found, but it works on a single large steel workpiece with a milling/welding head brought to it by rail wagon; it performs no electrical diagnosis, wiring, relay handling, gate or signal-apparatus work, so capability does not carry over to signal equipment repair.

sources.system: Spot (with IFS.ai agentic integration)
sources.title: IFS and Boston Dynamics Collaboration Combines the Power of Robotics with Agentic AI to Transform Field Operations
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities and substations, reading gauges and indicator lights and capturing thermal data, but its demonstrated field role is sensing and data capture, not tool-based repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds in institution-controlled industrial plants and substations. It substantiates autonomous visual/thermal inspection only; the signal repairer's inspections require operating equipment, meter connections and functional tests, and every instance here ends in a physical repair or adjustment Spot cannot perform.

sources.system: Locomotive-mounted autonomous track geometry measurement system
sources.title: Norfolk Southern debuts locomotive-mounted autonomous track inspection system - International Railway Journal
sources.claim: Norfolk Southern developed and deployed a locomotive-mounted ... that inspects track under load at track speed and transmits data to engineers, with no manipulation of wayside equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection of railroad infrastructure from a moving locomotive in the same rail corridor. It shows sensing can be automated, but it measures track geometry only; it neither tests signal circuits nor performs any maintenance or repair action, so it cannot complete these instances.

sources.system: Rail-road amphibious Railway Inspection and Repair System (RIRS)
sources.developer: Academic research group (published in Computers and Electrical Engineering)
sources.title: An autonomous rail-road amphibious robotic system for railway maintenance using sensor fusion and mobile manipulator - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: An autonomous rail-road amphibious robotic system with a mobile manipulator for railway inspection and repair exists only as a research prototype described in the literature.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation for railway maintenance. It is a laboratory/field research prototype with no evidence of completing signal apparatus inspection, testing or repair at worker quality, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Tighten loose bolts, using wrenches, and test circuits and connections by opening and closing gates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial
