instances.label: Scheduled inspection/maintenance of a highway-rail grade crossing warning system at a public road: the maintainer works at the roadside, checks and tightens loose bolts and nuts on the gate mechanism housing, mast, gate-arm hardware and foundation with wrenches (corroded, painted, varied sizes and access angles), then activates the crossing to run the gates down and up, verifying circuits, wire connections, lights and bell. Live traffic, weather, no fixed positioning.

Work in a wayside instrument case/bungalow and at a signal mast along the right-of-way: tighten terminal screws, lug, ground and cable connection hardware, re-torque loose bolts on the case, mast and mechanism, then test circuits by keying the crossing/signal and watching the gates open and close. Remote outdoor site, ballast, vegetation, variable weather.

Power switch machine / interlocking hardware in a railroad classification yard or terminal (railroad-controlled premises, fixed track layout, standard switch machines): tighten loose bolts on the machine, connecting and point-detector rods, then test the circuit controller and detection by throwing the switch and cycling associated gates/signals.

Emergency call-out after a gate-arm knockdown or storm damage: at night or in rain, re-secure and torque damaged or loosened bolts on arm, mechanism and mast at a roadside crossing, then repeatedly cycle the gates to confirm circuits and connections are sound before restoring the crossing to service.

Bench work in the railroad's signal shop: overhaul or repair of crossing gate mechanisms, relays and switch machine components on a workbench - tightening bolts and terminal hardware to torque and bench-testing circuits by powering and cycling the mechanism open and closed before it returns to the field.

Transit or commuter-rail property (station area, tunnel, or authority-controlled crossing) during a scheduled work window: tighten loose bolts on gate/signal equipment and test circuits and connections by cycling gates, under an operating authority that controls access and equipment standards.

sources.system: Radix Controls vision-guided lug-nut fastening cell (FANUC robot + Cognex In-Sight vision + nutrunner)
sources.title: Vision-guided robot fastens lug nuts | Vision Systems Design
sources.claim: Vision-guided FANUC robot with a nutrunner locates and torques wheel lug nuts to specification on a running automotive assembly line, handling parts that are only roughly positioned by the conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wrenching of threaded fasteners to a specified torque under vision guidance. Transfers to tightening bolts on gate/signal apparatus presented in a purpose-built cell: comparable fastener sizes, torque levels and localization problem.

sources.system: Inbolt GuideNOW with FANUC robots
sources.title: Inbolt and FANUC Pioneer Robots that Think and Act on the Fly at Moving Assembly Line Speeds
sources.claim: AI 3D-vision guidance lets standard industrial robots perform screw insertion and bolt rundown in automotive general assembly, including on parts that are moving rather than precisely fixtured.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bolt rundown. Shows current robotic fastening tolerates imperfect part presentation, which is what tightening assorted bolts on a fixtured gate mechanism requires.

sources.system: RedViking end-of-line transfer case test and assembly cell
sources.title: Test Cell Automation Soup to Nuts - RedViking
sources.claim: A purpose-built end-of-line cell with robotic part handling and test stands functionally tests assembled electromechanical units and performs final processing before acceptance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional test of an assembled mechanism. 'Testing circuits and connections by opening and closing gates' is a functional cycle test; in a fixtured cell such tests are run and pass/fail judged automatically, as here.

sources.system: Averex robotic wiring centre
sources.title: CDA Magazine - How automation became a reality
sources.claim: A commercial robotic wiring centre automatically makes wire connections to devices and terminals inside control cabinets presented in its fixture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making and securing electrical connections at device terminals. Signal instrument-case work involves the same class of terminal/lug connections, done autonomously when the panel is presented in a purpose-built station.

sources.system: Railway fastener maintenance robot platform (center-line projection distance tightness regression)
sources.developer: Research team, Chinese Journal of Mechanical Engineering (Beijing Jiaotong University and collaborators)
sources.title: Regression Method for Rail Fastener Tightness Based on Center-Line Projection Distance Feature and Neural Network
sources.claim: A railway fastener maintenance robot uses structured-light 3D sensing to judge whether in-service rail fasteners are loose and drives a torque wrench to tighten or loosen the fastener bolts to standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detecting loose fasteners and tightening them with a robotic torque wrench on weathered in-service railway hardware - the 'tighten loose bolts' half of this task, though on track fasteners rather than signal apparatus and with no circuit testing.

sources.system: Intelligent Maintenance Robot Platform for Railway Catenary
sources.developer: Shuohuang Railway Development Co. and partners
sources.title: China's First Intelligent Maintenance Robot Platform for Railway Catenary Was Launched on Shuohuang Railway
sources.claim: An intelligent catenary maintenance robot platform on the Shuohuang heavy-haul railway autonomously performs bolt fastening and geometry adjustments on overhead line hardware from a rail-borne multi-arm platform, replacing part of the manual crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bolt fastening on wayside railway infrastructure in the field. Limited to standardized catenary fittings reached from a rail vehicle and performs no circuit or gate-cycle testing, so it does not complete this task's field instances.

tasks.label: Inspect switch-controlling mechanisms on trolley wires and in track beds, using hand tools and test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled periodic inspection/test of an electric switch (point) machine at a mainline power-operated switch or interlocking: walk-in under track protection, open the machine case, check lock/throw rods, point detector contacts and wiring, run an obstruction test with gauges, measure motor current and contact continuity with a meter, check point adjustment and lubrication, record results. Outdoors on ballasted right-of-way, all weather.

Inspection round over many switches in a classification yard or transit yard: hand-throw and dual-control machines, switch circuit controllers, point detectors and connecting rods; test each with meter and gauges, clean and adjust, log findings. Fixed yard layout, standard hardware, access controlled by the railroad.

Trouble call on a failed or intermittently failing switch (loss of detection, fails to lock, slow throw): diagnose in the track bed with meter, gauges and hand tools, checking machine internals, rods, insulation, wiring and obstructions; often at night, in snow, ice, mud or heat, with trains held.

Inspection of a switch machine/mechanism in embedded street track (streetcar or light-rail switch at an intersection or grade crossing): open the pit or cover in the roadway, clear debris, test the operating mechanism and detection with hand tools and test equipment, amid traffic and pedestrians.

Inspection of an electrically operated overhead trolley-wire switch and its controlling mechanism (switch tongue, actuating coil/contactor, selector and detector wiring) from a bucket truck or platform over a street or terminal loop; check wear, contact clearance and operation with hand tools and test equipment.

Inspection of switch machines and controllers at an underground subway interlocking during a night work window: confined track bed with third rail, cables and drainage, test mechanism and detection with meter and gauges, restore for service before revenue hours.

sources.system: WAPS railway point drive test bench
sources.title: WAPS - railway point drive test bench - Hastema
sources.claim: Hastema's WAPS point-drive test bench is a purpose-built inspection rig for railway point machines (the switch-controlling mechanism) that runs an automatic check routine measuring setting/coupling/holding and point-opening forces, stroke, power rating and electrical circuit, evaluating them and issuing an inspection protocol.
sources.transferJustification: Same object and same measurements as the field task (switch/point machine: throw, coupling and holding forces, stroke, point opening, electrical circuit), performed with the unit fixtured in a workshop rather than in the track bed.

sources.system: Automated Bench Test Equipment (BTE/CABTE)
sources.title: Automated Bench Test Equipment | Wabtec Corporation
sources.claim: Wabtec supplies Automated Bench Test Equipment that applies automatically sequenced electrical/electro-mechanical stimulation to a rail electro-mechanical unit under test and provides troubleshooting down to module or sub-component level.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated testing and fault localisation of rail electro-mechanical units, the same diagnostic output a signal repairer produces, but with the unit presented to a fixtured bench.

sources.system: Felix
sources.title: An autonomous rail-road amphibious robotic system for railway maintenance using sensor fusion and mobile manipulator - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Loccioni's Felix is a self-propelled robotic kart that autonomously measures turnout and crossing geometry (rail profiles, point openings) in the track bed on operating railway networks; it does not open or electrically test the switch machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-track turnout geometry measurement. It shows autonomous measurement is possible in the track bed, but it covers only rail geometry, not the electro-mechanical switch-controlling mechanism, hand-tool work or circuit testing, so it cannot complete this task's instances.

sources.system: ANYmal
sources.title: Transforming Rail Operations Through Automated Robotic Inspection | ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot performs daily autonomous inspection missions in rail facilities such as railCare's Domat/Ems site, but its inspection is camera/thermal data capture, not hand-tool disassembly or gauge measurement of switch mechanisms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds in an institution-controlled rail facility (E2). Shows the state of field rail inspection robotics is sensor data capture, short of the manipulation and gauge measurement this task requires.

sources.system: Spot
sources.title: RATP: Inspections after dark | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: RATP uses Boston Dynamics' Spot to collect inspection data in hard-to-reach and hazardous parts of the Paris metro infrastructure; the work is sensor data capture rather than mechanism testing with tools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: metro infrastructure inspection in an institution-controlled underground setting; cited only to characterise what field rail inspection robots do (imaging), which falls short of switch-mechanism testing.

tasks.label: Replace defective wiring, broken lenses, or burned-out light bulbs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-line wayside signal: replace a burned-out lamp/LED lamp unit in a color-light signal head on a mast, bracket or signal bridge along the right-of-way. Requires hi-rail/road travel to the location, track protection, climbing, opening the hooded head, swapping the lamp in its socket, restoring focus/alignment and testing the aspect, in whatever weather and terrain the location has.

Public grade crossing: replace burned-out flasher lamps or LED units and cracked/broken roundels-lenses on crossing signals, gate-arm lights and gate tip lights, working on the road shoulder with vehicle and pedestrian traffic passing, often on uneven ballast/gravel and with the crossing kept in service.

Signal bungalow / relay case: replace defective internal wiring - trace the bad conductor, cut it out, strip, crimp and land new wire on relay-rack terminal posts or terminal blocks, tag and dress it, then test the circuit. Cramped locked equipment house with standard racks, legacy point-to-point wiring, energized adjacent circuits.

Field wiring/cable outdoors: replace a defective run of signal cable or its connections between bungalow, junction boxes, switch machine, track-circuit bonds or crossing mast - pulling/laying cable in trough or trench, splicing, landing conductors in a junction box at track level, on the open right-of-way.

Replace a broken lens, roundel, hood or background damaged by vandalism, gunshot, thrown ballast or vehicle strike on a wayside signal or crossing flasher - remove the retaining ring/screws, clear glass fragments, fit and seal the new lens, verify aspect visibility, all at the outdoor site.

Signal shop bench work: components brought in from the field (signal heads, crossing lamp units, gate mechanisms, terminal boards) are repaired at a bench - burned-out lamp units, cracked lenses and damaged internal harnesses are replaced and the unit is bench-tested before being returned to service.

sources.system: WAGO Cabinet Wiring Robot
sources.title: WAGO presents new solutions at SPS 2025 | Electronics360
sources.claim: WAGO's Cabinet Wiring Robot is a commercially offered automation cell that performs control-cabinet wiring - conductors cut, stripped, crimped and inserted at terminals on fixtured frames and mounting plates - cutting manual wiring workload by 60%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: landing prepared conductors on terminal blocks of a fixtured mounting plate. Signal relay-case wiring uses the same class of stranded conductors, crimped ferrules/lugs and screw or push-in terminals at comparable precision, so cell-based wiring transfers when the rack is brought to the machine.

sources.system: WAGO Cabinet Wiring Robot
sources.title: More Efficient Control Cabinet Wiring | WAGO
sources.claim: The same wiring robot is described by the maker as a high-precision 4.5-axis portal robot with a 12-slot tool magazine and screw bits that wires components from various manufacturers ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: screw-terminal wiring of racks. Demonstrates automated screwdriving plus conductor insertion on rack/mounting-plate hardware equivalent to a signal terminal board presented in a fixture.

sources.system: Daisy disassembly robot
sources.title: Apple's iPhone recycling robot shifts gears - Resource Recycling
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line autonomously tears down fixtured smartphones at industrial rate: robotic arms bracket each device, remove the display, freeze and punch out the battery and other components, covering 29 models, deployed in Apple facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing a glass cover/display and fastened internal parts from a device held in a fixture. Removing a cracked signal lens, hood or a failed lamp unit from a signal head presented in a fixture involves the same class of teardown motions, tolerances and glass handling.

sources.system: I.C.T automatic LED bulb assembly line
sources.title: I.C.T | LED Bulb Machine Automatic Assembly Line
sources.claim: Fully automatic LED bulb assembly lines are sold commercially and run the lamp build sequence - placement, soldering, testing, screw driving, aging ... packing - with automatic feeding and handling of bulb bodies and caps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling and seating of lamps and lamp caps plus automated screwdriving in a purpose-built line. Seating a replacement lamp unit into a fixtured signal head and re-securing its retaining screws is the same class of operation.

sources.system: UCSD twisting/sensing gripper on Fetch robot
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Tolley lab)
sources.title: How many robots does it take to change a light bulb? | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: A UCSD gripper mounted on a Fetch robot was demonstrated picking up and manipulating objects without vision, in a demonstration that included removing and replacing a light ....
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: unscrewing and re-seating a bulb. Autonomy of the demonstration is not established in the source, so it is treated as teleoperated and is not relied on for any positive judgment.

sources.system: Tianxun (2nd generation) data center robot
sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD
sources.claim: Alibaba Cloud reports a second-generation data-center robot that replaces faulty hard disks in racks without human intervention inside its data halls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: swapping a failed component inside equipment racks in a structured facility. Transfer is limited: drives are tool-free hot-swap modules in robot-designed aisles, unlike stripping, crimping and landing conductors on signal relay-rack terminals.

sources.system: In2Smart 2 Warthog autonomous inspection/repair platform
sources.developer: Cranfield University / Network Rail / Clearpath Robotics
sources.title: Cranfield and Network Rail develops autonomous rail inspection system | Robotics and Automation
sources.claim: Rail field robotics in the signalling/track environment remains at the inspection-and-research stage: Network Rail and Cranfield used a Clearpath Warthog platform in the In2Smart 2 project to develop an autonomous rail inspection and repair system.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (rail right-of-way) and adjacent task (field inspection/repair). It shows on-track field robots are demonstrators focused on inspection, not component replacement on signals, so it does not substantiate field completion.

sources.system: State Grid live-line operation robot
sources.developer: State Grid Zhenjiang Power Supply Company
sources.title: State Grid Zhenjiang Power Supply Company deploys robot for live-line repair - Chinadaily.com.cn
sources.claim: A Chinese utility reports field use of a live-line repair robot on distribution lines that locates conductors and plans work paths, though published work on 10 kV live-working robots describes master-slave control with mixed-reality assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor conductor work at height on utility poles. Autonomy is not clearly established (comparable systems use master-slave/MR control) and the operation is a single standardized branch-line connection, so it does not substantiate outdoor signal wiring replacement.

tasks.label: Inspect, maintain, and replace batteries as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine periodic inspection/test of the standby battery bank in a wayside signal bungalow or interlocking case: measure string and individual cell voltages and charger float voltage/current, check electrolyte level and specific gravity on flooded cells, look for corrosion, bulging, heat or leakage, and record readings for FRA-required inspection records. Trackside on the right-of-way, all weather, layout and battery vintage differ location to location.

Servicing the bank found during inspection: clean corroded terminals, lugs and hardware, neutralize acid, re-torque bolted intercell and cable connections, apply anti-corrosion compound, top up flooded cells with distilled water, and adjust or verify the charger. Done kneeling in a cramped bungalow or crossing case with live low-voltage DC present.

Replacing failed cells or an entire battery bank at a wayside signal, interlocking or CTC location: isolate the charger, disconnect cable lugs, lift 60-150 lb cells out of racks (often through a narrow bungalow door), set and connect the new cells, verify polarity, float voltage and correct signal/crossing operation, and carry the old cells out for recycling. Frequently an unplanned call-out after a low-battery alarm or failure, sometimes at night.

Battery work at small remote installations: sealed AGM batteries in a grade-crossing junction case, ground box, solar-powered switch-heater, hot-box detector or remote switch location beside a public road or in open country - test, swap and reconnect small batteries with traffic passing and track protection in force.

Indoor work at railroad facilities: capacity/load-testing and stocking batteries on the bench in the signal shop, and replacing standby/UPS cells in a control point building, relay room or dispatcher office where the layout is fixed and access is controlled.

sources.system: NIO Power Swap Station 4.0
sources.title: NIO Power Swap Station 4.0 Now Operational - News | NIO
sources.claim: NIO Power Swap stations perform the complete removal and installation of a heavy vehicle traction battery - unbolting the pack, extracting it, seating and re-fastening a charged pack and verifying the connection - automatically in about 2.5 minutes inside a purpose-built bay, with thousands of stations in commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: EV traction-battery exchange. Replacing a signal battery is the same physical operation - break bolted high-current connections, extract a heavy battery from a rack, seat and torque a replacement, confirm voltage/connection. The station does this on ~500 kg packs to commercial reliability with the work fixtured and presented, i.e. the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: CATL Choco-Swap / QIJI heavy-truck swap stations
sources.title: EV Battery Low? CATL Says, Just Swap It Out for a Fresh One
sources.claim: Automated battery swapping runs at commercial scale and volume across passenger-car and heavy-truck networks, with over a million machine-executed swaps in a year, evidencing worker-quality reliability of robotic battery exchange including ~1 t truck packs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated exchange of heavy battery packs. Establishes that machine removal/installation of batteries into rack-type fixtures is reliable at production volumes, the same manipulation required to change out heavy signal cells.

sources.system: Marposs in-line / end-of-line battery cell electrical test systems
sources.title: In-Line Electrical Test Of Cylindrical Battery Cells | Marposs
sources.claim: Commercial in-line battery test machines automatically contact cells and perform the electrical measurements a battery inspection consists of - open-circuit voltage, AC/DC internal resistance and insulation - with robots handling the cells and no human intervention in loading or unloading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production battery electrical testing. The maintainer's inspection is terminal-voltage, internal-resistance and insulation measurement plus recording; this system performs exactly those measurements autonomously on fixtured cells (the E1 presentation of the work).

sources.system: Robotic EIS battery testing framework (KUKA KR20 + End-of-Arm Potentiostat)
sources.developer: University of Birmingham (ReLiB/Faraday), published in Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.title: Advanced robotics for automated EV battery testing using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
sources.claim: A robot arm with a force/torque-controlled potentiostat end-effector autonomously probes the terminals of used battery modules and measures internal resistance/state of health, identifying degraded cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: state-of-health testing of aged battery modules. This is the diagnostic step of 'inspect batteries' - making physical contact with battery terminals and judging whether the battery remains serviceable - performed by a robot on batteries presented at a station.

sources.system: DeMoBat robot-based battery disassembly platform (KUKA KR QUANTEC)
sources.title: "DeMoBat": Battery disassembly for electric cars using KUKA robots | KUKA Germany
sources.claim: An industrial robot performed the servicing/teardown steps on used, varied battery packs - unscrewing fasteners, opening sealed joints and disconnecting cables - under sensor-based real-time control in a fixtured disassembly cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of used battery packs. Signal battery maintenance and replacement consists of the same operations - loosening and tightening terminal hardware and disconnecting/reconnecting cables on aged batteries - done here by robot on fixtured packs of varying design.

sources.system: Automated laser cleaning for battery production
sources.title: Laser Cleaning in Battery Production - raylase
sources.claim: Fully automated laser cleaning systems remove oxide and contaminant layers from battery busbars and terminal contact surfaces in production, the machine equivalent of cleaning corroded battery connections before re-torquing them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparation/cleaning of battery contact surfaces. Terminal cleaning by the maintainer removes oxide and corrosion from the same kind of metal contact surfaces; the laser cell does this autonomously on components presented at a fixtured station.

tasks.label: Record and report information about mileage or track inspected, repairs performed, and equipment requiring replacement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Lubricate moving parts on gate-crossing mechanisms and swinging signals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine periodic lubrication of a highway–rail grade crossing gate mechanism at a public road crossing on a mainline: signal maintainer opens the mechanism case at the mast, wipes and greases the gear train/sector gear, escapement and clutch, oils the arm pivot, counterweight arms and linkage, checks the gate operates freely. Done roadside during a monthly/quarterly inspection with road traffic passing and trains running; weather and ground taken as found.

Same greasing work at a rural or remote crossing reached by hi-rail truck or pickup: unpaved shoulder, ballast and vegetation underfoot, mud, snow or heat, insects and wasp nests in the mechanism housing, no lighting, mechanism often old and caked with hardened grease and dirt that must be cleaned off before relubrication.

Urban/high-traffic crossing with four-quadrant gates plus pedestrian gates: several gate mechanisms and pedestrian gate arms lubricated in a street environment with cars, pedestrians, tight clearances, a short work window and traffic control in place.

Lubrication of moving parts on swinging/movable signal apparatus: semaphore or wig-wag style signal pivots and bearings, movable-bridge signal and gate apparatus, gate arm hinge/knuckle and adjustable-arm joints — often reached from a ladder, platform or bucket at height on a mast or bridge.

Shop/bench service: a crossing gate mechanism or signal mechanism is removed from the field and overhauled in the railroad signal shop — disassembled, old grease cleaned out, gears/bearings/pivots repacked with the specified lubricant, reassembled and function tested on a bench with standard shop tooling.

sources.system: DOPAG automated greasing production cell (6-axis articulated robot with lubriLine spray/shot dispensing valves)
sources.title: Automated greasing with DOPAG dispensing valves — Valve World
sources.claim: A commercially supplied production cell uses a 6-axis articulated robot with metered spray and shot valves to apply grease to specified interior and exterior surfaces of gearwheels presented in workpiece carriers — automated, repeatable multi-point grease application on fixtured mechanical parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grease metering onto gears in a fixtured production cell. Transfer: lubricating a crossing-gate mechanism's gear train and pivot points is the same operation — a metered quantity of grease placed on known points of a rigid metal mechanism — and under the E1 counterfactual the mechanism arrives fixtured in a carrier exactly as the gearwheels do.

sources.system: DAV Tech robotic grease-damping dispensing bench (Universal Robots UR5 + DAV Tech GP pump)
sources.title: Universal Robot UR5 Cobot for Volumetric Dosing of grease Damping — DAV Tech
sources.claim: A commercially sold robotic dispensing bench pairs a UR5 collaborative robot with a positive-displacement pump to dispense metered damping grease onto mechanical components, with automatic weighing and part identification for process verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic volumetric grease dosing onto mechanical assemblies at a fixed bench. Transfer: greasing pivots and bearing surfaces of a gate or signal mechanism requires the same controlled placement of a measured grease quantity on identified surfaces of a part held in a known position, which is what this cell does at production quality.

sources.system: Motoman robotic grease-dispensing machine
sources.developer: Yaskawa Motoman (integrator cell shown by Machinery Lubrication)
sources.title: Automation Drives Grease-dispensing Machine — Machinery Lubrication
sources.claim: An industrial cell uses a Motoman robot to assemble a part and then apply lubricating grease to ... separate contact surfaces on it, with parts presented by a vibratory bowl feeder.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of grease to several distinct contact surfaces on a workpiece in a purpose-built cell. Transfer: the lube points of a gate mechanism (gear faces, pivots, bushings) are likewise a small set of fixed locations on a part; with the part presented in a known pose the same dispensing motion suffices.

tasks.label: Clean lenses of lamps with cloths and solvents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline wayside signal: technician reaches a mast, bracket or cantilever-mounted color-light head along the right-of-way (hi-rail truck or on foot over ballast), climbs the mast or ladder, opens the hood/door, and wipes the outer and inner faces of each lens/roundel with a cloth and approved solvent, then verifies the aspect. Weather, dust, insects and remote rural locations; live-track protection required.

Grade-crossing warning devices at a public road crossing: wiping the lens faces of flashing-light units, backlights, gate-arm lights and cantilever-mounted heads with cloth and solvent, working from a ladder or bucket beside moving road traffic; roadside grime, road film and salt.

Rail yard / interlocking: cleaning lenses of dwarf signals, switch-position indicators and switch lamps low to the ground amid ballast, points and standing cars, often oily film and dust; railroad-controlled premises with fixed equipment types.

Transit or commuter rail tunnel and station wayside signals: wiping brake-dust film off signal lens faces during night work windows in a third-rail/confined tunnel environment; agency-controlled, fixed layout, standard signal hardware.

Signal shop / maintenance facility bench work: lamp units, roundels, lenses and reflectors removed from service are cleaned with solvent and lint-free cloth on a bench before reassembly, lamp replacement and photometric/aspect testing.

sources.system: LCU Modulo (with HRA/PRA loading robots), Schneider Optical Machines
sources.title: LCU modulo - Lens Cleaning - Modulo - SCHNEIDER Optical Machines
sources.claim: Schneider Optical Machines' LCU Modulo is a commercially sold, fully automated inline lens-cleaning cell that removes fingerprints and residues from glass/plastic lenses using chemicals and brushes, with robotic loading (HRA) and unloading (PRA) that fixture and orient each lens; output must meet coating-grade cleanliness.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cleaning of optical lenses with cleaning chemicals and gentle brushes/wipers instead of a hand-held cloth. Objects (glass lens elements), the solvent-plus-mechanical-wipe method, and the acceptance criterion (an optically clean, unscratched lens surface) are comparable to, and stricter than, wiping a signal roundel; the work is presented fixtured and robot-loaded, i.e. a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Ecoppia E4 / H4 solar panel cleaning robots
sources.title: One Million Solar Panels Later, Ecoppia Robots Keep On Cleaning
sources.claim: Ecoppia's E4/H4 robots autonomously clean the glass cover surfaces of utility-scale PV modules with soft microfiber and airflow, running nightly on rails installed along panel rows at outdoor solar plants; deployed across more than a million panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine wiping of a soiled glass optical surface with a microfiber cloth element to restore light transmission, judged by the same functional criterion as a signal lens (light output). It runs unattended at production quality, but only where the surface is presented to a machine on purpose-built rails.

sources.system: Ozmo
sources.title: Skyline Robotics deploys Ozmo window cleaning robot in New York City - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Skyline Robotics' Ozmo, a robot-arm façade-cleaning system operated from a building's roof rig, has been deployed commercially to wash the glass of a 45-story New York office tower, with a human operator supervising from the rooftop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing glass at height on outdoor infrastructure. It shows the state of deployed at-height glass cleaning is large flat pane washing from a building-mounted rig; it does not cover reaching into a signal hood to wipe a small lens, so it substantiates façade-scale work only.

sources.system: Multihog Runway Light Cleaner
sources.title: Runway Light Cleaner - tractor-mounted runway light cleaner
sources.claim: Cleaning the lenses of in-service lamps in a controlled outdoor transport facility (an airfield) is still done with a human-operated, tractor-mounted attachment rather than an autonomous robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning installed lamp lenses in situ at an institution-controlled outdoor facility. It is a human-driven machine, so it cannot support a positive judgment; it indicates that in-situ lamp-lens cleaning in E2 settings has not been automated.

sources.system: pi-0.5 (π0.5) mobile manipulator
sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 vision-language-action model drives a mobile manipulator to perform cleaning tasks such as tidying and wiping in previously unseen homes, but success is not reliable on the first attempt; it is a research demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cloth/sponge wiping and cleanup by a general-purpose mobile manipulator in unstructured settings. Cited to show that dexterous wiping outside purpose-built setups remains at research reliability, well below the acceptance standard for signal maintenance, and does not address mast climbing or signal-hood access.

roles.description: Help installation, maintenance, and repair workers in maintenance, parts replacement, and repair of vehicles, industrial machinery, and electrical and electronic equipment. Perform duties such as furnishing tools, materials, and supplies to other workers; cleaning work area, machines, and tools; and holding materials or tools for other workers.

tasks.label: Install or replace machinery, equipment, and new or replacement parts and instruments, using hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Manufacturing/processing plant: helper works with a millwright or industrial mechanic setting up NEW machinery and equipment — unpacking, assembling subassemblies on the shop floor, bolting motors, drives, guards, brackets and instruments onto machines and skids with wrenches, impact guns and torque tools; new standard parts staged nearby.

Plant or facility: in-situ replacement of a failed/worn component on already-installed production machinery (electric motor, bearing, gearbox, pump, valve, drive belt) — working overhead or in confined access, breaking loose corroded or damaged fasteners, pulling the old unit, fitting and aligning the replacement.

Vehicle or fleet service bay: routine bolt-on part replacement on a car/light truck on a lift or in a bay — wheel and tire assemblies, batteries, filters, lamps, belts, accessory parts — under a technician's direction, using impact wrench, torque wrench and hand tools.

Customer site (private home or small business): helper assists an HVAC/appliance/plumbing service crew installing or replacing equipment tied into the building's existing systems — furnace, condensing unit, water heater, well pump, appliance — layout differs house to house, tight closets/attics/crawlspaces.

Institutional facility data hall or equipment room: replacing failed IT/electronic hardware and installing new units in standard racks — swapping drives, modules, power supplies, blades — fixed aisle layout, institution-controlled premises.

Plant or commercial building: mounting and replacing field instruments and electrical components — pressure/temperature transmitters, sensors, relays, contactors, wiring devices — on machines, control panels and enclosures using hand tools and powered screwdrivers.

sources.system: IBG Automation automated wheel assembly system (KUKA robots + Matrox Iris GT smart cameras)
sources.title: GER - Automated wheel assembly process in 54 seconds
sources.claim: Two vision-guided six-axis KUKA robots pick wheel bolts and rims from supply stations and screw wheels onto car bodies moving on the assembly line, with smart cameras locating the rim/bolt circle; full cycle about one minute per vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing wheels on an assembly line. It is the same physical act as the task's 'install new or replacement parts using power tools' — locating a bolt circle by vision, presenting a heavy part, and running threaded fasteners to torque — on a workpiece presented in a fixtured station.

sources.system: Robotic bolt-tightening station with 3D vision (Sick TriSpector1030 / Photoneo PhoXi)
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: In a car factory, a vision-guided robot with 3D sensing tightens the bolts fastening rear axle dampers to a van undercarriage, coping with vehicle position variation on the conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered fastening of a chassis component. Shows robots meeting production torque/precision requirements on parts installed with power tools in a fixtured, purpose-built station, the E1 counterpart of a helper running an impact/torque wrench.

sources.system: Tightening Cell Robotics (TCR)
sources.title: Do Tightening Cell Robotics require full automation? - Atlas Copco USA
sources.claim: Atlas Copco sells turnkey robotic tightening cells that combine robots with tightening tools and controllers so each joint is fastened to specification with traceability, marketed as complete automated fastening stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated threaded fastening in assembly cells. Directly comparable to the task's use of power tools to install equipment and parts, with the workpiece fixtured and fasteners presented as a purpose-built cell would present them.

sources.system: RoboTire System
sources.developer: RoboTire Inc. (Detroit; filed Chapter 7 in Jan 2024)
sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: RoboTire's robotic bay, installed and operating in Discount Tire retail stores, removes, lifts and installs tire-and-wheel assemblies on customer vehicles, changing four tires in under 25 minutes with store technicians overseeing the system.

sources.system: NIO Power Swap Station 4.0
sources.title: NIO Power Swap Station 4.0 Now Operational - News | NIO
sources.claim: NIO's fourth-generation Power Swap Stations automatically remove a vehicle's bolted battery pack and install a replacement in 144 seconds with the user initiating from the car; 2,432 stations were installed as of June 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated swap of a bolted vehicle battery pack. It is the replacement half of this task — unfastening and lifting out a heavy used component and fitting and re-fastening a replacement — performed at commercial reliability in a purpose-built station with the vehicle presented in a known pose.

sources.system: Tianxun (2nd generation) data center robot
sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD
sources.claim: Alibaba says its second-generation Tianxun data center robot replaces faulty hard disks in racks without human intervention, completing inspection, fault location and disk replacement in about four minutes, in operation at five of its data centers.

tasks.label: Examine and test machinery, equipment, components, and parts for defects to ensure proper functioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant-floor condition check of installed production machinery while assisting a maintenance mechanic in a factory: walk up to conveyors, pumps, motors, gearboxes; look for leaks, worn belts and loose guards; listen for abnormal noise; feel/check for hot bearings; read local gauges; report defects found. Institution-controlled industrial premises, standard assets, scheduled access.

Vehicle repair shop or fleet garage: helper performs a multi-point/courtesy inspection of a customer vehicle on a lift or in a bay — tire tread and damage, brake wear, undercarriage and underhood leaks, exhaust and suspension condition, lights, fluid levels, battery/charging check — and records defects on the shop's inspection form.

Shop bench test of a removed component or part (small motor, pump, valve, solenoid, circuit board, power tool): clamp or fixture it, run continuity/insulation/voltage checks with a meter, pressure- or run-test it on a stand, compare readings to spec, judge pass/fail or scrap.

Field service call at a residential customer site alongside a technician: operate the installed furnace, AC condenser, water heater or appliance; take temperature, pressure, airflow and electrical readings with gauges and meters at service ports and terminals; inspect wiring, filters and coils; identify the defective part. Home layouts vary; cramped attics, crawlspaces, closets.

Customer-site equipment check at a commercial or institutional building (mechanical room, boiler room, rooftop unit, electrical room): visual, thermal and noise check of pumps, motors, fans and panels; verify equipment runs correctly and flag leaks, hot spots and vibration for the technician.

Routine preventive-maintenance rounds inside the employer's own facility plant room / utility area: follow a fixed route, record gauge and meter readings on a checklist, spot leaks, overheating, and abnormal vibration or noise, and log defects into the maintenance system.

tasks.label: Tend and observe equipment and machinery to verify efficient and safe operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Manufacturing/processing plant floor: while production machinery (presses, conveyors, gearboxes, motors, packaging lines) runs, the helper stays with the equipment and the mechanic — watching for overheating, leaks, smoke, jams and unusual noise or vibration, reading gauges and panel indicators, and alerting the mechanic or stopping a machine when something is off.

Plant/building utility spaces (boiler and chiller rooms, air-compressor rooms, pump houses, electrical rooms): periodic tending rounds — reading pressure/temperature gauges and sight glasses, logging readings, checking for air, water, oil and refrigerant leaks, listening for bearing noise, and reporting anomalies to the technician.

Vehicle or heavy-equipment repair shop: after a repair the helper runs the engine, hydraulics or drivetrain at the mechanic's direction on the shop floor, lift or dyno, watching gauges and warning lights and observing for leaks, smoke and abnormal noise until the mechanic accepts the job.

Outdoor jobsite or field location (construction site, utility yard, plant outbuildings): monitoring running support equipment — generators, air compressors, dewatering pumps, lifts — during operation, checking readings and condition and flagging faults or unsafe conditions to the crew; layout and conditions differ site to site.

Customer premises (home or light-commercial site) during startup/commissioning of newly installed or repaired equipment (furnace, rooftop unit, compressor, shop machine): the helper runs and watches the unit while the installer checks it — observing pressures, temperatures, noise and leaks to verify safe, efficient operation.

tasks.label: Adjust, connect, or disconnect wiring, piping, tubing, and other parts, using hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential / light-commercial service call: helper assists an HVAC, appliance or plumbing tech at a customer's house — disconnects the old unit's water/refrigerant/gas tubing and line-voltage and control wiring, then connects the replacement, working in a closet, attic, crawlspace or beside a condenser pad with hand tools, tube cutters/flaring tools, cordless drivers and torque wrenches. Fittings are corroded or non-standard, access is tight, layout differs house to house.

New construction or renovation rough-in: helper on a construction floor pulling wire into conduit and boxes, cutting and joining pipe and tubing (PVC, copper, PEX), landing conductors on devices and panels per plan, on ladders and in ceilings amid other trades, debris and changing conditions.

Industrial plant / facility maintenance: helper works with a millwright or maintenance electrician inside a factory or building plant room, disconnecting and reconnecting motor leads and conduit, hydraulic/pneumatic tubing, coolant hoses and couplings on a machine being repaired in place, using wrenches, impact drivers and torque tools in cramped, greasy, partially disassembled equipment.

Vehicle/fleet service bay — wheels and bolted assemblies: helper removes and reinstalls wheels and other bolted parts with an impact wrench and torque tool on cars and light trucks lifted in a standard bay.

Vehicle/fleet service bay — under-hood/under-vehicle disconnections: helper disconnects and reconnects battery cables, coolant and fuel hoses, brake and A/C lines, ground straps and wiring-harness connectors on varied vehicle models during an engine, transmission or accessory repair.

Repair-shop bench work: helper at a motor/pump/equipment rebuild bench connects wiring leads to terminal blocks and connectors, fits tubing and threaded fluid fittings, and torques fasteners on a component held in a vise or stand, following the mechanic's direction.

tasks.label: Clean or lubricate vehicles, machinery, equipment, instruments, tools, work areas, and other objects, using hand tools, power tools, and cleaning equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine cleaning of a maintenance shop, garage bay, or plant maintenance area: sweeping and machine-scrubbing open concrete floors of dust, grit and oil film, plus hosing/foaming or blowing down the exteriors of machines, frames, guards and conveyors in place before or after a mechanic's work.

Detail cleanup of the immediate job site after or during a repair: collecting scrap metal, packaging, used rags and absorbent, soaking up an oil or coolant spill beside a machine, wiping the bench, and cleaning and stowing the mechanic's hand tools in their proper places in a cluttered bay.

Cleaning removed parts and components at the bench: loading them into a solvent or aqueous parts washer, wire-brushing carbon and gasket residue, spraying degreaser, blowing dry with compressed air, then laying them out clean for the mechanic to reinstall.

Lubricating vehicles and machinery: hitting chassis, bearing, pin and bushing grease fittings with a grease gun, oiling chains, slides and linkages, and topping off oilers and lube reservoirs on shop or plant equipment according to a lube chart.

Washing and degreasing vehicle and heavy-equipment exteriors at a fleet garage, dealership or wash bay: pressure-washing trucks, buses, mowers or construction machines, steam-cleaning undercarriages and engine bays, then drying and wiping down.

Cleaning installed equipment in the field at a customer's premises: chemically cleaning an HVAC condenser or evaporator coil on a rooftop or beside a house, vacuuming out a furnace burner compartment, wiping an appliance down, then cleaning up debris in the home or on the jobsite.

tasks.label: Hold or supply tools, parts, equipment, and supplies for other workers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial plant maintenance runner: a millwright working on a downed conveyor radios for a specific bearing, gasket set and a torque wrench; the helper walks to the maintenance storeroom, finds the items among thousands of SKUs, and carries/carts them to the machine on the plant floor (forklift traffic, oil, mezzanines).

Stand-by assistant at the machine during a plant repair: the helper stays at the mechanic's elbow inside/around the equipment, hands wrenches, sockets and fasteners as they are called for, holds a guard, cover, shaft or gasket in position while the mechanic bolts it, and holds the drop light where the mechanic is looking.

Vehicle repair bay: helper works beside a technician at a lift or under an open hood, passing tools as requested, retrieving a part from the parts counter mid-job, and holding an exhaust section, splash shield, harness or trim panel in place while the technician fastens it.

Field service at customer premises (residential furnace/AC change-out, restaurant equipment, small commercial site): helper hauls tools, refrigerant, fittings and duct from the truck into a basement, attic or roof, hands tools up a ladder to the installer, and holds ductwork, conduit or a fixture overhead while it is secured.

Active construction / new-installation site: helper stages and carries equipment, material and power tools across an unfinished, cluttered site to installers, and braces pipe, strut or a panel while the installer fastens it.
Parts room / shop staging: pulling the day's parts, consumables and tools per work orders, kitting them onto carts or into bins, and restocking service trucks at the start and end ... the shift.

tasks.label: Diagnose electrical problems and install and rewire electrical components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial/commercial facility: helper works with a maintenance electrician or industrial mechanic installing and rewiring electrical components on de-energized machinery — mounting contactors, relays, sensors and terminal strips on DIN rail, pulling conductors through conduit/wireway, landing and torquing wires on terminal blocks and motor leads, labeling circuits.

Maintenance/repair shop bench: helper builds or rewires an electrical assembly off the equipment — a small control panel, a wiring harness, a motor junction box, replacing damaged connectors and pigtails — then verifies the finished assembly with continuity/insulation checks before it goes back into service.

Vehicle repair bay: helper assists a technician diagnosing a vehicle electrical fault (no-start, dead lighting circuit, intermittent sensor) — load-testing the battery, back-probing connectors under the dash and in the engine bay, tracing a chafed harness — then replacing the failed switch/relay/sensor and splicing or re-terminating the wiring.

In-situ troubleshooting inside the plant or building: helper assists in locating an electrical fault in installed equipment or building circuits — checking fuses and breakers, metering voltage/continuity at panels, junction boxes and disconnects, tracing conductors through congested enclosures — and then swaps the failed device and re-lands its wires.

Field work at a home, light-commercial site, or building under construction/renovation: helper installs and rewires electrical components under a journeyman's direction — mounting boxes and fixtures, pulling and terminating cable to receptacles/switches, wiring a replacement HVAC control board or thermostat — in a space taken as found.

sources.transferJustification: Directly the 'install and rewire electrical components' half of the task: same objects (stranded wire, ferrules, push-in terminals, DIN-rail devices) and same termination precision a helper provides, but with the panel fixtured inside a purpose-built machine (E1).

tasks.label: Disassemble broken or defective equipment to facilitate repair and reassemble equipment when repairs are complete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tire/wheel service in a vehicle service bay: helper removes wheel assemblies from a customer car (breaking loose lug nuts of varied pattern and condition), hands the wheel off for tire or brake work, then reinstalls and torques the wheels. Shop-controlled bay, vehicles arrive as found.

Other vehicle component work in a repair shop: under a mechanic's direction the helper strips down an alternator, starter, water pump, brake caliper, exhaust or accessory drive on the vehicle or on a bench, dealing with rusted/seized fasteners, hidden clips and harness connectors, then reassembles after the repair.

In-plant industrial machinery maintenance: helper unbolts guards and couplings, pulls a failed pump, gearbox, electric motor or conveyor drive, strips it on the maintenance bench (housings, bearings, seals, keyed shafts), then reassembles it after the mechanic replaces parts. Factory floor, standard equipment, plant-controlled premises.

Bench repair of small electrical/electronic equipment and small appliances in a shop: opening housings, backing out many small screws, releasing clips, unplugging ribbon/board connectors, removing boards, motors or batteries, and reassembling the unit to working condition after the technician's repair.

Field service at customer premises (homes, small businesses): helper opens and disassembles installed equipment in place — furnace/AC condenser panels and blower assemblies, water heaters, washers/dryers, pumps, light electrical gear — in cramped basements, closets or rooftops, then reassembles it after the repair.

Heavy or outdoor equipment in a field or yard: helper breaks down loader/tractor/truck assemblies (hydraulic cylinders, final drives, track components, brake drums) with large, mud-caked, corroded fasteners under weather and with limited access.

tasks.label: Position vehicles, machinery, equipment, physical structures, and other objects for assembly or installation, using hand tools, power tools, and moving equipment.

instances.label: Industrial plant maintenance: helper rigs a motor, pump, gearbox, blower or conveyor section with a chain hoist or forklift, lands it on its baseplate/skid amid existing piping and guarding, roughs in alignment, shims, and starts/torques mounting bolts with hand and power tools while the mechanic directs.

Vehicle/fleet repair shop: helper spots the vehicle in the bay and on the lift, then positions heavy components for installation - transmission on a jack, engine on a hoist, differential, exhaust, wheels - lining up bolt holes and running fasteners with impact tools.

Commercial/institutional building service: helper moves a rooftop unit, air handler, boiler, pump or water heater on dollies through corridors and doorways, sets it on a curb, pad or stand in a mechanical room or roof, squares it up and bolts/anchors it in place.

Residential / light-commercial field install: helper carries and positions appliances, water heaters, condensing units, garage-door hardware or small structures inside an occupied home - stairs, tight closets, uneven yards, furniture and occupants present - and secures them for the installer.

Outdoor/field heavy equipment: helper works with crane, forklift or gin pole to rig and position varied equipment - generator, transformer, tank, pump skid, structural steel member - onto a foundation or frame at an industrial yard or job site, guiding, aligning and bolting it down.

Outdoor field site, standardized repetitive structural members: helper stages and positions large numbers of identical members (e.g., steel H-pile foundations, racking posts) at surveyed locations on a prepared field site for a solar/utility installation.

tasks.label: Transfer tools, parts, equipment, and supplies to and from work stations and other areas.

Aisles are shared with walking workers and forklifts.

Same plant, item-level errand: a millwright radios for a specific bearing, a gasket kit, a box of fasteners and two named hand/power tools; the helper locates them on crib shelves and in drawers, carries them to the machine and hands them to the technician, then returns the unused items.

Vehicle/equipment repair shop (auto or truck fleet garage, heavy-equipment shop, aviation MRO): helper moves parts, batteries, tires, fluid containers, jacks and rolling tool carts between the parts room, receiving door and service bays, around lifted vehicles, air hoses and technicians.

Field service call at a customer's premises (private home or small commercial building): helper unloads tool bags, a ladder, hoses, refrigerant/parts from the service van, carries them across a yard or through the building to the work location (basement, attic, roof, closet), then reloads everything at job's end.

Institutional building maintenance (hospital, university, hotel, large office): helper draws filters, lamps, hardware, paint and hand tools from the central maintenance shop or stockroom and carts them through corridors and elevators to the mechanical room or work site, returning surplus and tools afterward.

Active construction or new-equipment installation site: helper hauls conduit, pipe, fittings, gang-box tools, hoists and consumables from a laydown yard or staging trailer across an unfinished site with uneven ground, mud, debris, temporary stairs and changing layout.

Auto/light-truck shop helper doing the wheel/tire portion of service work: lifting the vehicle, breaking loose and removing lug nuts, pulling wheels for rotation or tire replacement, mounting/balancing on shop equipment, remounting and torquing to spec in a service bay.

Auto/truck shop helper on the rest of vehicle service: draining oil and swapping filters, replacing batteries, belts, hoses, brake pads and rotors, holding components while the mechanic works, retrieving parts and tools, cleaning parts and the bay. Manufacturing/industrial plant maintenance helper assisting a millwright or maintenance mechanic on machinery in place on the floor: tearing down a guard/drive, cleaning and inspecting parts, replacing belts, chains, bearings, seals and filters, greasing, re-torquing and adjusting tension/alignment, then testing the machine.

Institutional facility maintenance aide (school, hospital, hotel, apartment complex, municipal shop): assisting the mechanic in mechanical rooms and equipment areas — servicing rooftop units and pumps, changing filters and belts, greasing motors, adjusting door closers and small appliances, fetching parts and tools, cleaning equipment.

Shop bench work maintaining the shop's own tools and worn tooling: cleaning and inspecting tools, sharpening/regrinding worn cutting edges, drill bits and blades, replacing worn consumable tooling and tips on shop machines, adjusting and testing them before return to service.

tasks.label: Design, weld, and fabricate parts, using blueprints or other mechanical plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant/industrial maintenance shop bench work: from a sketch, shop drawing, or blueprint the helper fabricates a simple steel weldment (machine guard, mounting bracket, support stand, gusseted plate) — cut angle/plate stock, drill, fit up, MIG weld, grind. Indoor shop with welding table, clamps, bandsaw, grinder.

Fabricating a replacement part to dimensions on a mechanical plan: turn a bushing or spacer, mill/drill a mounting plate, plasma or laser cut a shim, wear plate, or flange to a hole pattern, deburr and check dimensions. Done in the shop on machine tools and cutting equipment.

In-place weld repair/modification on installed equipment on the plant floor: weld a cracked conveyor frame member, re-attach a broken bracket on a press or hopper, add a stiffener where a plan calls for it — welding in position (vertical/overhead), around guards, piping, and obstructions, with a portable welder and a fire watch.

Vehicle/fleet or mobile-equipment repair shop: fabricate a part at the bench per a drawing or spec — exhaust hanger, bumper/step bracket, wear plate, trailer crossmember section — cutting, forming, and welding steel stock to size before it is fitted to the unit.

Field fabrication at a customer site, plant yard, or construction site: measure in place, cut and weld a support, handrail section, guard, or pipe hanger in position outdoors or in a cramped mechanical space, with variable footing, weather, wind, and access.

tasks.label: Assemble and maintain physical structures, using hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop/bench assembly: in the maintenance shop or fabrication bay, the helper builds frames, brackets, machine-guard panels, skids, stands and carts from cut parts and hardware staged on a bench, using cordless drills/drivers, impact wrenches, rivet guns and clamps.

Kit assembly inside the facility: putting together flat-pack/knock-down pallet racking, shelving, workbenches, lockers, tool cabinets and storage units delivered to the plant, following printed instructions with hand and cordless power tools.

In-place erection in the plant: bolting up conveyor sections, machine bases, safety guarding and fencing, equipment platforms, mezzanine railings and pipe/duct support steel around existing machinery — rigging and lifting members, aligning, shimming, drilling and anchoring to floors and existing steel; includes throwing up the temporary staging or scaffold needed for the job and stripping it afterward.

Repair/maintenance of existing structures on the premises and grounds: doors and frames, handrails and stair treads, gates, fences, partitions, damaged machine guards, roof/wall penetrations and patches — assessing as-found damage, cutting and fitting replacement pieces, and refastening in situ with saws, grinders and drivers.

Varied field/customer-site mounting: at rooftops, mechanical rooms, crawl spaces, residences and commercial buildings, laying out and mounting a handful of supports, brackets, unistrut runs or equipment stands into concrete, masonry, wood or steel — often from a ladder or lift, in cluttered or confined space, working around existing services.

High-volume, laid-out anchoring work on a large project: installing dozens to hundreds of identical brackets/anchors/hangers to a surveyed layout along open floors, decks or slab edges — drill, blow out hole, set anchor, seat bracket, torque to spec, log the result.

tasks.label: Prepare work stations for use by mechanics and repairers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership or independent auto/light-truck shop: before the next repair order, the helper preps the service bay — sweeps debris and spilled fluid from the previous job, wipes the bench and tool cart, positions jack stands, drain pan, creeper and wheel dolly, sets fender/seat covers, checks the air hose and lift, and stages the job's parts and fluids by the vehicle. Bay is cluttered with cords, hoses, carts and a vehicle.

Plant or industrial maintenance shop: prep a bench/stall for a machine or motor repair — clear and clean the bench top of chips, oil and the last job's leftovers, gather the specific hand tools, torque wrench, pullers, micrometers and gauges the mechanic requested, fetch replacement parts from the crib, set the vise and parts washer, lay out the LOTO kit, prints and manual.

Staging run inside a shop or plant: the parts department/storeroom has pulled the parts for a scheduled job; the helper transports parts, filters, fluids and shop supplies along fixed indoor routes and leaves them staged at the technician's bay or bench, then returns cores/empties. Institution-controlled premises, marked aisles.

Electronics/electrical equipment repair bench (service depot, shop lab): prep the bench — ESD mat and wrist strap laid out, soldering/rework station and hot-air gun set up and powered, meters, test leads, scope probes and fixtures positioned, component/hardware kit for the unit staged, work order and schematic placed.

Field/on-site job (HVAC, elevator, electrical, construction trailer, roadside or customer-plant service call): set up a temporary work station in an as-found space — unload the truck, lay drop cloths, position a portable bench/table, ladders, task lighting, cones or barrier tape, run the extension cord, and lay out the tools and materials for the mechanic.

tasks.label: Monitor and adjust operations of geothermal power plant equipment or systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room / SCADA shift surveillance of a geothermal unit: watching trends and alarms for the turbine-generator, steam/brine supply, non-condensable gas removal, cooling water and injection systems, and making adjustments through the control system (unit load, injection or feed pump speed, level and dosing setpoints), logging readings each hour.

Routine field surveillance round through the plant and wellpads: walk the turbine hall, pump and heat-exchanger skids, cooling tower, separators and wellhead pads; read local gauges and sight glasses, check bearing temperatures, vibration and pump noise, look for steam/brine leaks and scaling, and record/report findings. Hot piping, H2S, stairs, grating, outdoor weather.

Hands-on field adjustment of flows and pressures: throttling manual valves and handwheels at wellheads, separators, injection lines and cooling-tower makeup on control-room direction or round findings, then verifying resulting flow, pressure and level at local instruments.

Unit startup, shutdown or major load change: local valve line-ups, starting and stopping pumps and fans at local panels, turbine warm-up, roll and synchronization, coordinating each step with the control room and confirming equipment response in the field.

Abnormal condition or trip response: investigating an alarm (scaling-induced pressure drop, pump cavitation, high NCG, cooling-tower fan trip, low well flow), diagnosing in the field, swapping to standby equipment, resetting local devices, adjusting the process to restore output, and documenting the event.

It acts on the physical process only through purpose-built installed instrumentation and actuated control valves, i.e. a machine-built loop, which is why it supports E1 rather than the human-facing plant environment.

tasks.label: Identify and correct malfunctions of geothermal plant equipment, electrical systems, instrumentation, or controls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential ground-source heat pump service call: homeowner reports no heat/no cool or high bills. Technician works in a basement, utility closet, garage or crawlspace of a house never seen before; checks thermostat and low-voltage control wiring, unit lockout codes, contactor/capacitor, compressor and reversing valve, refrigerant pressures, loop flow and circulator pump, desuperheater; then corrects the fault (replace capacitor/contactor/sensor/circulator, purge air from loop, repair wiring, adjust charge) and verifies operation.

Commercial/institutional GSHP building (school, office, multifamily, hotel): one or several distributed water-source heat pump units fault out, or the central loop pumps/valves/BAS controls misbehave. Technician traces the fault across mechanical room equipment, above-ceiling units, and the building automation system, then corrects it (replace compressor contactor, control board, actuator, flow switch, reprogram BAS points) during occupied hours.

Utility-scale geothermal plant, mechanical equipment malfunction: brine/production/injection pump vibration or seal leak, cooling-tower fan gearbox, motor-operated valve sticking, heat-exchanger fouling/scaling, condenser or NCG system trouble. Technician diagnoses from vibration/thermal/process data and field inspection outdoors on pipe racks and platforms (hot brine, H2S, scale), then performs LOTO and repairs or replaces the component.

Utility-scale geothermal plant, electrical malfunction: motor won't start, MCC starter or VFD fault, tripped breaker, ground fault, failed transformer/switchgear component, damaged terminations or heat-traced circuits. Technician isolates and locks out, tests with multimeter/megger/thermography, identifies the failed device, replaces contactors/fuses/relays/wiring, and returns the circuit to service.

Utility-scale geothermal plant, instrumentation and controls malfunction: pressure/level/flow transmitter reading wrong, plugged impulse line, failed RTD/thermocouple, control-valve positioner hunting, PLC/DCS I/O card or loop wiring fault. Technician performs loop checks, calibrates or replaces the field device, corrects control logic/setpoints, and verifies the loop from the control room.

Indoor/covered plant areas with grating, stairs, H2S risk.

Control-room data collection and recording: technician monitors SCADA/DCS screens and local control panels, records hourly/daily generation, steam and brine flows, injection totals, wellhead trends into shift logs and operating reports, flags out-of-range values. Fixed workstation inside a controlled plant control room.

Well-field round: technician drives/walks a route across the operator-controlled field to production and injection wellheads, separators, silencers, steam lines and injection pumps; records wellhead pressures and temperatures, flow/level readings, pump amps, H2S monitor readings, and notes leaks or scaling. Outdoor, gravel pads and lease roads, all weather.

Geochemical sampling round: technician collects brine, steam-condensate and non-condensable-gas samples at sampling ports (purge line, cool through a coil, filter, preserve, bottle, label), measures field pH/conductivity/temperature, records sample IDs and chain-of-custody, and delivers samples for analysis. Hot, pressurized fluid at plant and wellhead sample points.

Well tests and special surveys: rig up portable test equipment at a wellhead, install or retrieve memory pressure/temperature gauges or run PTS/wireline surveys, monitor lip-pressure/weir-box or tracer flow tests over hours, and record the resulting test data. tasks.label: Perform pre- and post-installation pressure, flow, and related tests of vertical and horizontal geothermal loop piping.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-installation pressure test of loop pipe as delivered/prefabricated: technician caps or plugs the ends of a coiled HDPE U-bend vertical loop assembly (or a horizontal loop coil), connects a hand/electric test pump or air source, pressurizes to spec (e.g., ~100 psi), holds and watches the gauge for a set period, checks the fused U-bend and joints, and records pass/fail before the loop is inserted or laid. Done on the ground at the drill/job site or in a shop staging area.

Post-insertion verification of vertical loops: after the U-bend is pushed into a 200-500 ft borehole and grouted, the technician re-pressurizes and holds the circuit, then after the pipe tails are fused into the header in a muddy header pit, hydrostatically tests the assembled header/circuit and inspects each butt-fusion joint before backfill. Outdoor residential/commercial yard, weather and mud.

Horizontal loop trench testing: technician pressure-tests each trench circuit with a hydrostatic test pump while the pipe lies in an open 6-8 ft trench, walks the trench inspecting pipe and joints, then re-tests after backfill to confirm no damage. Uneven excavated ground, spoil piles, variable site layout.

Post-installation flush, purge and flow test at the flow center: technician cam-locks flush-cart hoses to the purge ports in a home basement or utility room, flushes the whole loop field at high velocity to strip air and debris, adds antifreeze, verifies flow rate (gpm) and pressure drop across the heat pump using P/T ports, sets static loop pressure, and logs the readings.

Commercial/institutional loop field (school, campus, multifamily) under construction: dozens of borehole circuits terminated in header vaults; technician pressure-tests each circuit and the assembled headers per spec, flow-balances and verifies gpm per circuit at the mechanical room manifold, and completes documented test reports for the commissioning agent.

Shop/bench work in the plant instrument shop: calibration and certification of removed or spare transmitters, gauges, RTDs/thermocouples and pressure switches against reference standards, plus bump-testing and calibration of the portable H2S/multigas detector fleet and shop test equipment, with certificates and CMMS records.

Control-system hardware maintenance in the control room / MCC / field junction cabinets: replacing failed PLC-DCS I/O modules, power supplies, UPS batteries, relays and network gear; re-terminating and labelling wiring; restoring configuration and performing point-to-point loop checks and functional tests after replacement. Indoor, climate-controlled, energized-equipment precautions.

Turbine/generator and rotating-equipment monitoring and protection electronics: setting proximity/vibration probe gap voltages and verifying monitoring racks, replacing thermocouples/RTDs and speed pickups on the turbine and pumps, and function-testing trip/protection channels and annunciation during outages. Work is at the machine on skids and platforms, often during a short outage window.

instances.label: Outage/upgrade work in the plant electrical room: install or replace protective devices (microprocessor relays, molded-case or MV breakers, fuses, ground-fault modules) in a switchgear lineup, MCC or relay panel — mount on the plate/DIN rail, run and land control wiring on terminal blocks, land CT/PT leads, torque and label terminations, and point-to-point check the wiring against drawings.

Scheduled protective-relay testing and calibration in the plant relay room: isolate the relay with test-switch links, connect a secondary-injection test set, verify pickup/timing/differential and trip-contact operation, adjust or reload settings, prove the trip path to the breaker, then restore links and document the test.

Circuit-breaker and MCC-bucket maintenance in plant switchgear rooms: rack out the breaker, inspect and clean primary/secondary contacts and arc chutes, check the trip unit and auxiliary/trip circuits, do contact-resistance and insulation-resistance tests, lubricate the mechanism, rack in and verify closing/tripping.

Outdoor switchyard and transformer-protection work at the plant, in weather and in an H2S-corrosive geothermal atmosphere: install/replace surge arresters and CTs, land and torque high-current connections, inspect and repair grounding conductors and connections, clean corroded terminals, and check protection wiring back to the control building.

Troubleshoot and repair after a protection operation or nuisance alarm: read relay targets and event records, inspect wiring, CT circuits, aux contacts and fuses across the plant, locate the failed component, replace it, retest the protection function and restore the unit to service under time pressure.

Residential or small-commercial geothermal heat pump job: install and verify the unit's electrical protection — dedicated breaker in the load center, fused disconnect at the equipment, surge protector, overload/contactor checks and equipment bonding/grounding — in a basement, garage or small mechanical room with as-found layout and clearances.
