tasks.label: Prepare newly installed geothermal heat systems for operation by flushing, purging, or other actions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family residential new install: in the basement/utility room the tech connects a flush cart to the flow center's boiler-drain purge ports, flushes the ground loop both directions at ~2 ft/s until air-free, cleans the cart filter, injects antifreeze to the design freeze point, sets loop static pressure, purges the heat-pump side, then starts the unit and verifies flow and pressure drop.

Residential job with awkward access: flow center in a crawlspace, garage, closet or outdoor cabinet; hoses and purge tank staged outside in cold or wet weather; cramped, poorly lit working position, improvised water supply, tools and antifreeze drums carried in.

Loop field purge at an active jobsite: each borehole or horizontal circuit is flushed and pressure-tested at the header pit/vault or at fused purge tees before the header is tied in; muddy trench, temporary water supply, circuits handled one at a time, results logged.

Commercial/institutional building (school, office) mechanical room: large multi-circuit water-source heat-pump loop flushed circuit-by-circuit with a high-capacity purge pump, glycol/chemical treatment injected and verified, strainers cleaned, air vents bled, readings documented for the commissioning agent.

Return visit after startup: residual air pocket or low flow reported (gurgling pump, high pressure drop); tech re-connects the flush cart, re-purges the loop, bleeds high points, tops off fluid and pressure, rechecks antifreeze concentration and flow, and re-verifies operation.

sources.system: Manual flush-cart purging procedure (geothermal commissioning)
sources.developer: Building Commissioning Association / Strategic Energy Solutions
sources.title: Geothermal System Commissioning | BCxA Building Commissioning Association
sources.claim: Baseline for the task as humans do it: after piping is installed the geothermal ... are flushed with water and purged of trapped air using a flush cart delivering high sustained flow; entirely a manual hookup-and-monitor procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Baseline description of the rated task itself; non-robotic, cited only to fix what completion requires.

sources.system: Automated coolant fill adapter tools / fluid fill systems

sources.claim: Commercially supplied automated coolant fill stations on vehicle production lines clamp onto the circuit's port and then run a hands-off machine cycle that evacuates the circuit (removing air), fills it with water/glycol coolant, performs vacuum and pressure leak tests, and levels to the target volume.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing a newly assembled closed liquid loop for operation by purging air and charging glycol antifreeze, then verifying leak-tightness. Same fluid class and same air-removal/charge/pressure-verify sequence, machine-controlled in a purpose-built station.

sources.system: VTech Pre-Vac 40 Automatic Pre-Evacuation System
sources.title: Advanced Pre Evacuation Systems | VTech Process Equipment
sources.claim: PLC-controlled automatic pre-evacuation systems used on HVAC/R production lines (listed applications include heat pumps and chillers) run an unattended evacuation cycle on a newly assembled circuit followed by an automatic vacuum-decay leak test, using preset per-model vacuum parameters.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: purging a newly built heat-pump fluid circuit before it is charged and put into operation, with automatic verification that no air or leak remains — the machine side of the rated task, executed unattended in a fixtured line station.

sources.system: KEDA hydraulic flushing unit (PLC flushing rig)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: flushing a newly installed piping circuit clean before commissioning — the same high-velocity debris-and-air sweep a geothermal flush cart performs, here run as an automatic machine cycle on pre-connected ports.

sources.system: Robofuel autonomous refuelling
sources.title: Robofuel Autonomous Refuelling | Scott Automation
sources.claim: A vision-guided robot autonomously locates a truck's fuel receiver, couples the nozzle and pumps fluid with no person handling the hose, deployed outdoors at mine sites in hot, dusty, cold and wet conditions with only remote supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step: autonomously mating a hose/coupler to a fluid port and transferring fluid in an industrial yard. Substantiates automated hookup only; it performs no valve sequencing, air-purge judgement, antifreeze dosing or system startup.

sources.system: Review of robotics for HVAC applications (101 studies, 2005-2025)
sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Jiang, Li, Delgoshaei, Liu, Hong), Building and Environment
sources.title: Robotics for HVAC applications: A critical review and future perspectives
sources.claim: A 2026 peer-reviewed review of 101 studies on robots in HVAC finds the work concentrated on inspection, maintenance and indoor monitoring, with installation/retrofit little explored; no robotic system is reported that commissions hydronic systems in buildings.
sources.transferJustification: Survey evidence bounding the state of the art for robots working on HVAC systems inside buildings; supports the negative judgments at E2/E3, not any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Weld piping, such as high density polyethylene (HDPE) piping, using techniques such as butt, socket, side-wall, and electro-fusion welding.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential ground-loop install at a private home: socket-fusing 3/4"–1-1/4" HDPE loop pipe, u-bends, tees and insert fittings, plus small butt-fusion joints, done at the trench edge or in a shallow pit in the yard; dirt, wind, cold, uneven ground, layout differs house to house.

Commercial/institutional bore-field or large loop-field on an active construction site: butt fusion and electrofusion of 2"–8"+ HDPE headers and reducing tees in open trenches and header vaults, pipe dragged in by machine, joints made in and beside the ditch alongside other trades.

Prefabrication in the contractor's shop or fenced staging yard: cutting and fusing header/manifold assemblies, vault assemblies and pipe spools on a bench- or frame-mounted fusion machine at a fixed workstation with power, lighting and stock pipe on racks.

Inside a building mechanical room or at a geothermal/district-energy plant: fusing HDPE transition, supply/return or brine piping in a confined equipment room or plant yard, tying into existing piping with limited clearance and standard facility conditions.

Repair/tie-in of an existing buried loop or header: cutting out damaged pipe and making an electrofusion coupling or butt-fusion repair in a small, wet, muddy excavation, requiring scraping/cleaning of aged pipe and awkward joint access.

tasks.label: Test water sources for factors, such as flow volume and contaminant presence.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential site assessment for an open-loop / standing-column well geothermal heat pump at a private home: technician measures well yield in gpm (bucket-and-stopwatch or clamp/inline flow meter at the hose bib or pitless adapter, with a drawdown/recovery check), then draws a sample and runs field kits and handheld meters (pH, hardness, iron, TDS, sediment) or bottles it for a lab, to judge whether the well can feed the heat pump. Cramped basement/yard, non-standard plumbing, weather, homeowner present.

Supply-well testing for a commercial or institutional open-loop / standing-column system on a construction or retrofit site: a longer constant-rate pump test with flow meter and water-level logging, plus multiple bottled samples for lab analysis (chlorides, hydrogen sulfide, iron/iron bacteria, hardness, TSS) taken alongside the well driller. Muddy, changing site with temporary power and hoses.

Service or commissioning call on an installed well-water/open-loop heat pump: technician cracks sample ports on the strainer or heat exchanger, tests the source water and loop water for scaling/fouling indicators (hardness, iron, pH, conductivity), and verifies flow through the unit with a flow meter or P/T-port pressure-drop readings, in a home or small commercial mechanical room.

Routine water sampling round at a geothermal power plant: collect brine, condensate, cooling-tower and injection-water samples at designated sample points around the plant (some hot, taken through cooling coils), take field temperature/pH/conductivity readings, verify or read production and injection flow rates, then label, log and deliver the bottles.

Bench analysis of collected water samples in the plant or service-company laboratory: hardness/alkalinity titrations, photometric silica and chloride tests, conductivity and pH, recording results against limits and flagging exceedances (e.g., scaling or corrosion risk).

sources.system: Skalar SP2000 robotic water analyzer (with MACHEREY-NAGEL)
sources.title: New robot for fully automatic water analysis | Envirotec
sources.claim: Skalar/MACHEREY-NAGEL SP2000 is a commercial robotic water analyzer that takes field sample bottles loaded straight into racks and autonomously decaps, mixes, dispenses, titrates and measures oxygen, pH, alkalinity, colour, conductivity and turbidity overnight in drinking, surface and waste water, then recaps and returns the bottle.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content as the technician's water test (contaminant/quality parameters on a water sample), but with the sample presented to the machine in a rack rather than collected in the field.

sources.system: Metrohm 815 Robotic USB Sample Processor XL + 836 Titrando
sources.title: The Analysis of Water Hardness by Automated Titration (Labmate Online / Metrohm UK)
sources.claim: Metrohm's 815 Robotic USB Sample Processor combined with a Titrando forms a commercially sold, fully automated water-analysis system that performs conductivity measurement, alkalinity determination and water-hardness titration on racked samples with a robotic arm and dosing devices.
sources.transferJustification: Hardness and alkalinity are exactly the parameters a geothermal technician tests on well water for scaling risk; the robotic sample processor performs the same wet-chemistry test on a presented sample.

sources.system: Hach AP3900 Laboratory Robot
sources.title: Laboratory robot delivers cost effective, fully automated water analysis | Envirotech Online
sources.claim: The Hach AP3900 Laboratory Robot is a commercial automated laboratory system that handles multiple water samples and runs multiple analyses (COD, total P, total N, ammonium, nitrate, nitrite) including sample preparation and data management.
sources.transferJustification: Same class of work: automated wet-chemistry contaminant testing of water samples presented to the machine, in place of a technician running bench tests.

sources.title: 6712 Full-Size Portable Sampler | Teledyne ISCO
sources.claim: Teledyne ISCO 6712 portable automatic samplers are widely deployed machines that pump water from a source through an intake line and distribute measured aliquots into bottles on a programmed, flow-paced or sensor-triggered basis, without an operator present.

sources.claim: In oil and gas production, well flow testing is routinely automated: a multiport flow selector with actuated control automatically diverts one well at a time from a piped manifold into a multiphase flow meter that measures the water, oil and gas flow rates, removing the need for manual valve operation at remote sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = measuring the flow volume a well delivers. The machine performs the flow-rate determination the technician makes by hand, once the source is plumbed into the test skid (an E1 presentation of the work).

sources.title: On-Line Water Chemistry Analyzers | METTLER TOLEDO

tasks.label: Install, maintain, or repair ground or water source-coupled heat pumps to heat and cool residential or commercial building air or water.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential ground-source heat pump installation or replacement: set the packaged unit in a basement/utility closet, connect ground-loop supply/return piping, hydronic or duct connections, condensate, line-voltage power and thermostat wiring, purge/pressure-test the loop, charge/verify refrigerant, start up and commission the system in an occupied private home.

Residential service/maintenance call on an existing GSHP: diagnose a homeowner complaint (no heat, poor performance, fault code), check loop pressure, flow and antifreeze, refrigerant pressures/superheat, clean coil and change filter, tighten/replace electrical components, swap a failed circulator, contactor, blower motor or control board in a cramped mechanical closet.

Commercial water-source/ground-source heat pump installation during new construction or tenant fit-out: hang ceiling-plenum WSHP units on threaded rod, tie into riser piping with valves and hoses, connect ducted supply/return, power and BAS controls, in an active construction/fit-out site with other trades present.

Maintenance and component repair on GSHP/WSHP equipment in the mechanical rooms and ceiling spaces of an operating commercial or institutional building (school, office, multifamily): scheduled PM, strainer and filter service, loop water treatment checks, pump seal and valve replacement, compressor or control troubleshooting, coordinated with facility staff.

Loop/water-source side work outdoors at the site: connect header piping in the loop vault or trench, HDPE heat-fusion joints, penetrate the building wall, flush/purge the loop with a purge cart, verify flow and pressure drop, add antifreeze, in variable weather and mud.

sources.system: HVAC robotics research corpus (101 reviewed systems/studies)

sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the HVAC lifecycle including heat pump installation, maintenance and retrofit; establishes that no fielded robot performs these whole tasks.

sources.claim: Hilti Jaibot, a commercially deployed MEP jobsite robot, drills ceiling anchor holes from BIM data but is driven into position by a human operator and performs only that single sub-step of mechanical installation.

sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye automates pipe welding inside fabrication shops (a purpose-built shop setting), covering steel pipe spool joints only, with a welding operator present.

sources.transferJustification: Covers the construction/MEP trades that include heat pump installation; documents that no robot performs multi-step mechanical equipment installation.

tasks.label: Integrate hot water heater systems with geothermal heat exchange systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential retrofit: tie a geothermal heat pump's desuperheater into an existing electric or gas water heater in a home basement or utility closet — route and secure double-wall heat-exchanger lines through joists and around existing ducts, mount and wire the desuperheater circulator, connect to the tank drain and cold inlet with press/sweat/threaded fittings, add a mixing/tempering valve, purge and pressure/leak test, and verify hot-water temperature rise.

New residential construction/mechanical room build-out: set a preheat (buffer) storage tank beside the geothermal water-to-water unit, run and insulate primary/secondary piping between heat pump, tank and existing water heater, install pumps, isolation valves, expansion tank and flow center connections, wire aquastats/controls to the heat pump, fill/purge, test to code and commission with owner setpoints.

Small commercial or institutional building (school, clinic, office) mechanical room: integrate a water-to-water geothermal heat pump with domestic hot water storage tanks via a double-wall plate heat exchanger — hang and braze/groove larger-diameter piping, set pumps and mixing station, land control points to the BAS, insulate, pressure test, disinfect and commission alongside other trades.

Large commercial, multifamily or campus/district geothermal plant: tie heat-recovery domestic hot water production into the central plant — connect buffer tanks and heat exchangers to loop headers, install circulators and controls, coordinate with plant sequences, balance flows, and commission/document the DHW heat-recovery integration.

Service call on an occupied home or small building: diagnose a failed or poorly performing existing water-heater/geothermal integration (dead desuperheater pump, air-bound or reverse-piped lines, scaled heat exchanger, mis-wired control), re-pipe or replace components in cramped existing space, refill/purge, retest and re-commission.

sources.system: HVAC robotics literature corpus (101 reviewed systems/studies)
sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / Building and Environment (Jiang, Li, Delgoshaei, Liu, Hong)
sources.title: Robotics for HVAC applications: A critical review and future perspectives
sources.claim: A 2026 peer-reviewed critical review of 101 robotics-for-HVAC studies (2005-2025) finds robotic work concentrated in inspection, maintenance and monitoring, with installation/retrofit tasks — the category that covers plumbing a water heater into a heat-pump/heat-exchange system — among the least explored, i.e. no demonstrated end-to-end installation robot.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the HVAC/hydronic installation domain of this task; establishes that no fielded robot performs installation/retrofit of HVAC-hydronic equipment end to end, in any setting.

sources.system: Construction task robots (rebar-tying robots, MEP ceiling-drilling robots)
sources.title: Humanoid robots in the construction industry: A future vision
sources.claim: As of late 2025, construction-site robots (including for mechanical/electrical/plumbing work) are limited to single narrow tasks such as rebar tying or ceiling drilling; no system performs multi-step trade installations such as piping and commissioning equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related trade work (jobsite MEP installation). Capability is confined to one repetitive operation (drilling anchor holes, tying rebar); it does not carry over to routing, fitting, sealing, wiring and commissioning a water heater/geothermal heat-exchange tie-in.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR / SWR-TIGMIG, NovEye Autonomy)
sources.title: Novarc unveils dual-process spool welding robot for fabricators
sources.claim: Commercial fab-shop robots weld pipe spools autonomously once the pipe is loaded into a positioner, showing that only the welding pass on fixtured steel pipe is automated in a purpose-built shop — not the assembly, fitting, valving, wiring or commissioning of a hydronic system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = joining pipe. Transfer fails: the SWR welds a single fixtured steel joint presented by an operator in a positioner, while this task requires selecting, cutting, routing, fitting and sealing copper/PEX/steel lines, mounting pumps and tanks, wiring controls and leak-testing/commissioning a complete DHW-geothermal tie-in.

sources.claim: A 2025 robotics research roadmap identifies autonomous pipe-fitting for heat-pump and boiler installation as an open opportunity rather than an existing capability, confirming installation of such systems is not currently robot-performed.
sources.transferJustification: Same domain (heat-pump hydronic installation). Cited only as a statement of an unmet research need, not as evidence of capability; it does not support any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Determine the type of geothermal loop system most suitable to a specific property and its heating and cooling needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Dig trenches for system piping to appropriate depths and lay piping in trenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential retrofit, existing home: excavate horizontal ground-loop trenches (typically 4-10 ft deep, hundreds of feet long) in an occupied backyard with lawn, landscaping, fencing, septic field and buried utilities; mini-excavator/backhoe work plus hand shoveling at locates, then uncoil 300-600 ft HDPE loop rolls, walk/place them on the trench bottom without kinks at required separation, bed with sand/spoil.

New-construction single-family or light-commercial lot: open, graded, obstruction-free ground; long parallel trenches cut with a chain trencher or full-size excavator to design depth and grade; two to six HDPE loop pipes (or slinky coils) laid per trench, spaced and bedded, before backfill.

Header/service trench connecting the loop field or vertical borefield to the building: shallow-to-deep run crossing driveway, sidewalk or patio (saw-cut), hand digging along the foundation, sleeve penetration into the mechanical room, careful routing of supply/return pipe pairs through congested ground near other utilities.

Commercial/institutional site (school, office, multifamily campus): trenching across lawns and parking areas for a larger loop field or borefield header, coordination with other trades and utility locates, deeper/wider trenches with shoring or benching, fused HDPE header assemblies lowered and laid in the trench.

Geothermal plant or district-energy facility yard: trench runs for system piping between wellheads, separators and plant equipment inside the fenced facility; rocky or compacted ground, pipe supports/bedding, larger-diameter carrier pipe set into the trench with a machine and hand-guided into position.

sources.system: Exosystem (autonomous trenching)
sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit makes standard excavators dig trenches fully autonomously to a design file on utility-solar jobsites; the machine produces the trench, while placing the pipe/cable inside remains separate work performed by crews.
sources.transferJustification: Substantiates only the excavation half of this task (trench to specified depth/grade in open ground); it does not substantiate the pipe-laying half, which the source frames as separate work done inside the finished trench.

sources.system: Exosystem
sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: The Exosystem is a commercially sold retrofit; an uploaded CSV of depth/grade parameters drives fully autonomous digging with nobody in the cab, supervised from a cloud console.
sources.transferJustification: Trenching for buried utility conduit is closely comparable to trenching for geothermal loop piping (same machines, depths, soil), but the evidence covers digging only, not laying pipe in the trench.

sources.system: Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators
sources.title: Kawasaki Develops "Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators"
sources.claim: Kawasaki demonstrated an autonomous excavation controller that plans from 3D design data and LiDAR terrain sensing and autonomously dug a trench, levelled the trench floor and compacted, in company verification testing at a test site.
sources.transferJustification: Shows autonomous trench excavation and floor preparation at a prepared test site; no pipe handling or pipe placement is claimed, so it cannot substantiate completion of the full task.

sources.system: HEAP (Hydraulic Excavator for an Autonomous Purpose)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Robotic Systems Lab / Gramazio Kohler Research)
sources.title: Autonomous excavator constructs a six-metre-high dry-stone wall | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's HEAP autonomously grasped and placed multi-tonne boulders to build a 65 m dry-stone wall in an autonomously excavated landscape — the most advanced demonstrated autonomous object placement by an excavator, but with rigid stones, not flexible HDPE loop pipe laid to a trench bottom.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grasp-and-place of heavy objects by an excavator. It bounds current capability — rigid boulders placed in the open — and does not transfer to uncoiling and seating flexible HDPE loop pipe in a narrow trench at required depth and spacing.

sources.system: Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES)
sources.title: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES): From Innovation Funding to Field Trials
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System performed field trials on a gas network, autonomously coring and vacuum-excavating keyholes in roadways; even this advanced field system covers excavation and fitting work on existing pipe, not installation of new pipe runs in trenches.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic street excavation over buried utilities. Cited to show the state of the art in field excavation robotics; autonomy of the manipulation steps is not established, so it supports no positive judgment.

sources.system: Horizontal ground-loop installation practice (non-robotic reference)
sources.title: Geothermal Ground Loop FAQs - Dandelion Energy
sources.claim: Context for what the task requires: horizontal geothermal ground loops are installed by digging long trenches several feet deep and then installing the plastic loop pipe in them — a two-part job whose second part is manual pipe handling.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only to define the accepted output of the task (trench dug to depth plus loop pipe installed in it) against which robotic capability is measured.

tasks.label: Apply coatings or operate systems to mitigate corrosion of geothermal plant equipment or structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ field coating at a geothermal power plant: technician preps and recoats corroded steel — brine/steam piping, wellhead trees, separator and tank exteriors, structural steel and handrails. Hand/power-tool cleaning or spot abrasive blasting, masking, priming and topcoating with epoxy/polyurethane or high-temp coatings, often from ladders, lifts or scaffolding, around congested piping in an H2S/hot-brine environment; dry-film-thickness checks before sign-off.

Shop coating of components removed for maintenance at the plant's maintenance shop: valves, pipe spools, pump casings, heat-exchanger parts and brine-line sections are blasted or degreased on a bench or in a booth, given anti-corrosion coating or lining, cured, and inspected before reinstallation.

Operating the chemical corrosion/scale-inhibitor treatment system: watching injection rates, brine chemistry, pH and online corrosion-probe data at wellheads, brine lines and cooling water, and adjusting metering-pump dosing setpoints to hold inhibitor concentration within spec.

Physical servicing of the corrosion-control chemical system: swapping and refilling inhibitor totes and drums, connecting suction lines, calibrating and rebuilding metering pumps, clearing plugged injection quills, and installing or pulling corrosion coupons and probes from access fittings for lab evaluation.

Cathodic protection work on well casings, buried brine/injection lines and tank bottoms: taking rectifier voltage/current readings and structure-to-soil potential surveys with test leads across the wellfield, adjusting rectifier taps, and replacing depleted sacrificial anodes or damaged test-station wiring.

Corrosion mitigation on residential/commercial geothermal heat pump installations at customer sites: flushing and charging ground loops with inhibited antifreeze, testing and dosing loop/condenser water for corrosion inhibitor, treating or coating exposed line sets, flanges and outdoor equipment in basements, mechanical rooms and yards of varying layout.

sources.system: Omnirobotic AutonomyOS / OmniBrain (with FANUC, ABB paint robots)
sources.title: A Software Platform for Self-Programming, Autonomous Robotics | Products Finishing
sources.claim: Omnirobotic's AutonomyOS lets standard FANUC/ABB spray robots perceive parts with 3D vision and generate their own spray motions in paint and powder cells, running without per-part programming in production finishing shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of industrial protective coatings to fixtured steel parts in a booth. Same coating chemistries (epoxy primers, polyurethane topcoats), same workpiece class (steel components and spools) and film-thickness precision as recoating geothermal plant components.

sources.system: Omnirobotic Shape-to-Motion
sources.title: Omnirobotics' Shape-to-Motion Tech Supports Wide Variety of Spray Processes | Products Finishing
sources.claim: The same Shape-to-Motion technology drives autonomous surface preparation as well as coating: robots that see, plan and execute painting, powder coating and sandblasting on high-mix parts using existing industrial robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive blasting plus coating of parts in a cell, covering the surface-prep half of the corrosion-coating instance on comparable steel workpieces.

sources.system: Qlayers 10Q tank coating robot
sources.title: Storage Tank | Qlayers
sources.claim: Qlayers' 10Q magnetic crawler has coated storage tanks at terminals worldwide since 2020, but it is a semi-automatic machine driven from the ground by remote control and requires a three-person operating crew present at all times.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (field application of protective coating to industrial tanks at an institution-controlled facility); cited as evidence that in-situ coating robots remain operator-driven.

sources.system: PaintJet Bravo
sources.title: PaintJet puts robots to work in construction and maintenance as labor shortage drags on | CNBC
sources.claim: PaintJet's Bravo lift-mounted painting robot coats large industrial and commercial exteriors, but operators on the ground drive both the lift and the spray end effectors by remote control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: large-surface field coating of built structures; cited to show that field coating robots are remote-controlled rather than autonomous.

sources.system: Apellix Spray-Painting Drone
sources.title: Apellix Launches New Beta Program for Spray-Painting Drone - DRONELIFE
sources.claim: Apellix's Spray-Painting Drone applies high-performance corrosion-inhibiting coatings to structures in the field, but is described as a semi-autonomous, pilot-flown platform in a limited beta program.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (aerial application of corrosion-inhibiting coatings to industrial steel); cited as evidence that field coating is at best semi-autonomous with a pilot.

sources.system: Chemical injection skids / packages (PLC-SCADA controlled inhibitor dosing)
sources.title: Why Chemical Injection Skids Are Critical for Corrosion Control in Oil & Gas Pipelines
sources.claim: Commercial chemical injection skids — chemical tanks, metering pumps, flow meters, injection quills and PLC/SCADA control — dose corrosion inhibitor into pipelines continuously and automatically, with sensors and PLCs monitoring flow, tank level and pump performance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating an inhibitor injection system to mitigate corrosion of process piping. Same machine class (metering pumps, quills, PLC controllers) and same duty as inhibitor dosing on geothermal brine and cooling-water lines.

sources.system: Automatic phosphate corrosion-inhibitor feed and control systems
sources.developer: water utility chemical feed system vendors (as described by Treatment Plant Operator magazine)
sources.title: Phosphate Corrosion Control in Drinking Water | Treatment Plant Operator
sources.claim: Drinking-water utilities run automatic corrosion-inhibitor (phosphate) feed systems in which online measurement and automatic feed hold the inhibitor dose at a setpoint despite flow variation, without an operator adjusting the pump.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop operation of a corrosion-inhibitor dosing system based on online chemistry measurement — the same control duty a geothermal technician performs on brine and cooling-water inhibitor injection.

sources.system: ANYmal
sources.title: Robotic inspection in Power & Utilities - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot performs autonomous inspection rounds in power and utility plants — thermal, acoustic and visual checks on pumps, valves and heat exchangers — but its deployed role is data collection, not manipulation or coating work.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterise what autonomous robots actually do inside power plants (rounds are inspection-only), supporting negative judgments on hands-on chemical handling and cathodic-protection field work.

tasks.label: Backfill piping trenches to protect pipes from damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrofit residential horizontal ground-loop job at an occupied home: after the HDPE loops are laid and pressure-tested in 4-6 ft trenches, the technician backfills the backyard trenches with a mini-excavator/backhoe — shading the pipe first with rock-free fine soil or sand, pushing spoil back in lifts, water-settling/tamping, and restoring lawn grade — while working around fences, trees, sprinkler lines, and existing buried utilities.

Residential vertical-borehole system: short trenches from the bores to a header pit and to the foundation wall penetration are backfilled. Requires careful sand bedding around the fused header manifold and the entry sleeve, hand shoveling and tamping close to fittings and the house wall, then bulk spoil replacement and grade restoration.

New-construction residential lot, open and machine-accessible before landscaping: loop-field and supply-line trenches are backfilled with a skid steer/excavator, pipe shaded with screened material, spoil pushed back and rough-graded; tolerances looser because finish grading and landscaping follow.

Commercial/institutional loop field (school, campus, office) under general-contractor control: long header and circuit trenches backfilled after inspection and pressure test, using specified bedding/select fill, placed and compacted in lifts to spec with plate compactors/rollers, with density testing and inspector sign-off before final cover.

Tight-access or repair backfill: a small hand-dug excavation over a leaking loop, a fused repair coupling, or a narrow side-yard run between house and fence; material carried in by wheelbarrow, placed by shovel around exposed fittings and hand-tamped without disturbing or point-loading the pipe.

sources.system: Kawasaki Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators
sources.title: Kawasaki Develops "Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators", Achieved "Autonomous Operation" for Trench Excavation at Construction and Civil Engineering Sites
sources.claim: Kawasaki's Autonomous Excavation System autonomously excavated a 2 m x 0.6 m x 10 m trench from 3D design data and LiDAR terrain sensing, and in the same verification testing autonomously leveled the trench floor and performed compaction work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trench excavation, in-trench floor leveling and compaction to a 3D design. Backfilling is the inverse movement of the same soil into the same trench geometry with the same machine and controller, at the same (0.1 ft class) precision; the compaction step the backfill requires was itself demonstrated. It transfers only where the pipe's position is known/fixtured and the fill is pre-screened, i.e. a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: A4CSEL (automated bulldozers, vibratory rollers, dump trucks)
sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL automated fleet — vibratory rollers, bulldozers and dump ... — has been used in production at dam sites, placing and compacting embankment fill in lifts around the clock (more than ten automated machines at Naruse Dam since FY2020).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement and lift-by-lift compaction of earth/CSG fill to a design surface. Trench backfill is the same operation at smaller scale — spread fill in lifts, compact to spec. The site is explicitly reorganized as a machine-dedicated 'factory' work zone with no fragile buried object present, so the transfer holds only for the bulk-fill-and-compact part in a machine-structured setting.

sources.system: Cat CS12 autonomous soil compactor
sources.title: CONEXPO: Caterpillar to demo autonomous compactor – and AI Assistant goes live
sources.claim: Caterpillar demonstrated a CS12 soil compactor operating autonomously with no one in the ... at its purpose-built Operator Stadium demonstration area at ConExpo 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned soil compaction. Compaction of the backfill in lifts is a required element of accepted trench backfill; the demonstration is in a purpose-built demonstration arena, supporting the compaction element at E1 only.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem (autonomous trenching excavator)
sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem performs fully autonomous trenching on utility-scale solar construction sites to 0.1 ft accuracy, but the company positions backfill and compaction as work still done by human crews that its evenly spaced spoil piles make easier.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: the only commercially deployed autonomous trenching product on open construction sites automates the dig, and explicitly leaves backfill and compaction to human crews — evidence that unstructured-site autonomous backfill over laid pipe is not offered.

sources.system: Bedrock Operator (autonomous excavator retrofit kit)
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics announces autonomous excavation milestone - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics' retrofit autonomy kit ran large excavators in supervised autonomy on a 130-acre manufacturing-facility site with Sundt Construction, moving over 65,000 cubic yards by ... dump trucks; the demonstrated work is mass excavation and truck loading, not backfilling over installed pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bulk earthmoving on an open construction site. It shows machine-scale soil handling at E3 but does not cover placing bedding around a laid, fragile pipe, so it does not substantiate completion of this task at E2/E3.

sources.system: Autonomous excavator backfilling trajectory planner (imitation learning + optimization)
sources.developer: Sumitomo Heavy Industries, Technology Research Center
sources.title: Development of a Highly Efficient Trajectory Planning Algorithm in Backfilling Task for Autonomous Excavators by Imitation of Experts and Numerical Optimization (JRM Vol.36 p.263)
sources.claim: Sumitomo Heavy Industries researchers developed trajectory planning for the backfilling task with autonomous excavators; against expert operators the method's error from the target shape was about 66% larger and it moved about 58% of the soil per motion.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on the task: autonomous excavator backfilling. It confirms backfilling is an active but still below-expert R&D capability, supporting a positive judgment only in a highly structured setting and a negative one for found-ground sites.

tasks.label: Operate equipment, such as excavators, backhoes, rock hammers, trench compactors, pavement saws, grout mixers or pumps, geothermal loop reels, and coil tubing units (CTU).

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential heat-pump install: run a compact excavator/backhoe in a homeowner's yard to dig and backfill 4-6 ft horizontal loop trenches and the entry pit through the foundation wall; tight access between house, fence, septic and driveway, unmarked utilities, lawn/landscaping to protect, roots, mud and rain.

Large open loop field: run a full-size excavator/backhoe across a staked, surveyed open parcel (school campus grounds, industrial yard, plant site, solar/large commercial lot) digging long parallel loop trenches and header trenches to grade, stockpiling spoil and backfilling, with room to maneuver.

Rock and pavement work: break ledge and boulders along the trench line with an excavator-mounted hydraulic hammer, and cut/remove asphalt or concrete driveway, sidewalk and parking-lot sections with a walk-behind pavement saw before trenching, then remove slab pieces.
Backfill and compaction: bed loops in sand, backfill in lifts, and compact with a trench compactor, plate compactor or small roller over trench runs and the loop field, restoring grade and surface.

Vertical borefield support: batch and mix bentonite/silica grout in a grout mixer and pump it through a tremie hose to grout boreholes bottom-up as U-bend loops are set; handle geothermal loop reels, unspooling and feeding HDPE loop pipe into bores and trenches.

Geothermal power plant well field: operate a coil tubing unit or similar well-service equipment at a plant-operated well pad (rig up on wellhead, run coil in and out of hole for cleanout/scale removal, monitor weight and pressure while pumping), plus support equipment on plant grounds.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem (autonomous excavator trenching)
sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit converts standard excavators into autonomous trenching machines, sold commercially to contractors for utility and solar trenching.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cable/utility trenching. Same machine class (hydraulic excavator), same product (a graded trench of specified depth and width with spoil placed alongside) as a geothermal horizontal-loop or header trench.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem excavators (used by Bechtel)
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Excavators Remove 65,000 Cubic Yards of Dirt on Southwest Project | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: A major contractor has used Built Robotics' autonomous excavators for production trenching on solar construction projects in Texas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: buried-cable trenching on an open construction site; the trench geometry, soils and machine are the same as for a geothermal loop field trench.

sources.system: Bedrock Robotics autonomy retrofit for 20- to 80-ton excavators
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Announces Supervised Autonomy Testing on Active Construction Sites in Move Towards Commercialization
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics' autonomy kits performed mass excavation on active US construction sites, moving over 65,000 cubic yards on a ... site under supervised autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk excavation and truck loading with the same excavators geothermal crews use; establishes autonomous digging to plan on as-found earthwork sites, though not confined-space or utility-crossing work.

sources.system: Gravis Robotics autonomy kit / Copilot for excavators
sources.title: Gravis Robotics raises $23 million to accelerate global rollout of autonomous earthmoving technology
sources.claim: Gravis Robotics' autonomy kits performed large-scale autonomous excavation on an active airport infrastructure construction site in the UK.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous earthmoving/excavation on a managed institutional site (airport), showing the same excavator work performed autonomously within a controlled, surveyed facility.

sources.system: Gravis Robotics Copilot / autonomy platform (Hitachi, Develon excavators)
sources.title: Gravis Robotics expands into US with AI-powered autonomous construction equipment
sources.claim: Gravis-powered excavators are in production use with contractors for earthmoving, trenching and grading across multiple countries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trenching and grading with retrofit kits on standard excavators — the same equipment and output specification as geothermal loop trenching.

sources.system: Dynapac CA 5000 with Trimble Earthworks Grade Control Platform for Autonomous Compactors
sources.title: Self-driving soil compactors take a step closer to market
sources.claim: A fully autonomous soil compactor completed 37 hours of real ... alongside a manned fleet on a live earthworks construction site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soil compaction to a surveyed plan — the same output (compacted lifts to specification) that geothermal crews produce when compacting backfill over loops, though with a full-size roller rather than a trench compactor.

sources.system: XCMG unmanned road construction fleet (autonomous tandem rollers, pavers)
sources.title: XCMG deploys driverless rollers, pavers on highway project | Equipment World
sources.claim: An unmanned fleet of ten autonomous tandem rollers and ... pavers carried out compaction and paving on a live highway maintenance project.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless compaction within a managed work zone; supports autonomous compaction to plan, but with full-width rollers on prepared mats rather than narrow trench backfill.

sources.system: SLB automated coiled tubing conveyance (autonomous well intervention)
sources.title: Coiled Tubing Autonomous Conveyance Improves Consistency of Offshore Intervention Operations | SLB
sources.claim: Coiled tubing conveyance was automated for offshore interventions in the North Sea, with the system controlling running speed and reacting automatically to anomalies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coiled tubing running in and out of hole during well intervention — the same equipment class a geothermal technician runs, but only the conveyance sub-step is automated; rig-up and job execution remain crew work.

sources.system: Normet Xrock Autobreaker
sources.title: Normet Xrock launches the world’s first autonomous rock-breaking system, Xrock Autobreaker
sources.claim: A fully autonomous rock-breaking system for hydraulic breaker booms is commercially available, but only for fixed grizzly and crusher-station installations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hydraulic hammer operation, but on loose oversize rock delivered to a fixed boom over a grizzly — not in-situ ledge breaking along a trench line, and it covers no pavement sawing.

sources.system: Advanced Construction Techniques automated mobile grout batching plant
sources.title: Automated Mobile Batching Plant | Advanced Construction Techniques
sources.claim: Automated grout batch plants proportion, mix and discharge grout under computer control while pumping is monitored from a control room, with crews stationed at the boreholes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated mixing and pumping of cement/bentonite grout, the same materials and equipment class as geothermal grout mixers/pumps; however hose and tremie handling at the borehole remains manual.

tasks.label: Inspect materials, products, or equipment to detect defects or malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Line walk during a shift in a running plant (plastics, metal fab, food/beverage, electronics): supervisor pulls in-process units off the line or picks them from a bin and checks them visually/tactilely against a boundary sample — scratches, burrs, short shots, weld appearance, fill level, label/print quality — deciding whether the line keeps running.

Quality bench / near-line check of a sampled part: supervisor measures critical dimensions with calipers, micrometers, go/no-go gauges or a gauge fixture, checks fit and function, records results and signs off a first-article or lot acceptance.

Equipment condition walkthrough of the department: check machines, motors, pumps, hydraulics, conveyors, belts, guards and gauges for leaks, overheating, abnormal noise or vibration, and wear; log findings and raise maintenance work orders.

Incoming material / component inspection at receiving or line-side: verify a delivered lot against spec (gauge, color, moisture, foreign material, damage, count), sample-check pieces, accept, quarantine or reject.

Investigation of a defect spike or machine malfunction: supervisor stops or observes the machine, opens guarding, inspects tooling/die/fixture/nozzle and the affected product to find the cause, and decides whether to keep running, adjust, or call maintenance.

sources.system: Koh Young Zenith 3D AOI
sources.title: Optical Inspection System Guide | Koh Young America
sources.claim: Koh Young 3D automated optical inspection systems are commercially installed at large scale on SMT production lines and detect assembly/solder defects in-line, with parts presented on a conveyor to a fixed inspection station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-line product defect inspection normally done by human inspectors/supervisors pulling boards off the line. Same objects (produced units), same defect classes (missing/misplaced parts, cosmetic and joint defects), same accept/reject output, in the same factory, so performance carries over to the supervisor's in-process product check when units are presented to the station.

sources.system: HEUFT InLine II empty container inspector with flip rejection
sources.title: Space-saving empty bottle inspection | HEUFT
sources.claim: HEUFT inline container inspectors are installed in operating breweries and inspect every single container automatically for glass defects, foreign objects ... quality defects, rejecting faulty ones without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: 100% in-line product/container inspection replacing the manual spot checks a beverage-plant supervisor performs on units taken off the line; same objects, same defect classes, same accept/reject decision, in the same production facility.

sources.system: Flex-Inspect Platform (robot arms + MVTec HALCON)
sources.developer: Vista Solutions Inc. / MVTec Software GmbH
sources.title: Fully Automated Inspection of Underbody Trays with Machine Vision | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Vista Solutions' Flex-Inspect platform uses robot-mounted cameras and MVTec HALCON to perform full automated dimensional and feature inspection of automotive underbody trays, replacing manual spot-check inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional/feature inspection of a fabricated part that a supervisor would otherwise check by eye and gauge; comparable objects (sheet-metal/composite automotive parts), comparable precision (width, depth, thickness measurement), same factory setting.

sources.system: Mitutoyo robotic measurement cell with MiSTAR CMM
sources.title: Robotic measurement cells removes bottleneck in parts inspection process | Engineer Live
sources.claim: A robotic measurement cell combining an articulated robot, a shop-floor CMM and a pallet store was installed at manufacturer Meca-Precis and now performs sampled part dimensional inspection with the operator only loading pallets from outside the cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dimensional verification of sampled production parts, the same output the supervisor produces with calipers/gauges at a quality bench, at equal or better precision, with the part fixtured on a pallet as a purpose-built cell would present it.

sources.system: Spot with Spot CAM+IR / Orbit
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in an operating process plant, including anomaly detection, thermal inspection and analog gauge reading, navigating the whole 40-acre facility and docking to recharge between routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment condition inspection rounds; the supervisor's equipment walkthrough looks for the same malfunction signatures (hot spots, leaks, off-normal gauge readings) on the same class of plant equipment.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) at AB InBev Leuven brewery
sources.title: Robotic dog spots problems in brewery | Logistics Matters
sources.claim: At AB InBev's Leuven brewery Spot runs repeated inspection rounds across ten packaging lines and found roughly 150 equipment anomalies (mostly compressed-air and gas leaks) in six months, cutting repair turnaround.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: predictive-maintenance inspection rounds in a packaging plant, i.e. exactly the supervisor's equipment-inspection duty (detect malfunctions on production machinery) in a human-built production facility, at higher frequency than a human round.

sources.system: ANYmal / ANYmal X
sources.title: Automation and digitalization with ANYmal the case at BASF - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal legged robots operate autonomously inside BASF's chemical production plant, reading gauges, taking acoustic measurements ... thermal-scanning for hotspots on multi-floor human-built plant terrain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operator inspection rounds in a process plant; the malfunction cues (gauge values, pump/compressor acoustics, thermal hotspots) are the same ones a production supervisor checks on plant equipment, in an unmodified human work facility.

sources.system: TOMRA 3A / TOMRA 5B optical sorters
sources.title: TOMRA 3A optical food sorting machine | TOMRA
sources.claim: TOMRA optical sorters inspect incoming raw agricultural material in-line at high throughput and eject foreign material and defective product without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: incoming raw-material inspection at a food plant — checking a delivered lot for foreign material and defective product and rejecting it — which is the supervisor's receiving-inspection judgment, executed continuously on material presented on a conveyor.

sources.system: Microtec Goldeneye 300 Multi-Sensor Quality Scanner with GradeView
sources.title: Defect detection performance of automated hardwood lumber grading system - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A Microtec Goldeneye multi-sensor scanner with GradeView software graded 9,454 rough hardwood boards in a working sawmill, locating and classifying defects with 92.2% on-grade accuracy versus NHLA-trained human graders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inspection and grading of incoming raw material (lumber) for defects, benchmarked directly against trained human graders; same material, same defect taxonomy, same accept/grade output as a mill supervisor's material inspection.

instances.label: Machine shop / metalworking: supervisor sets up a CNC mill or turn-mill for the next job — mounts and indicates workholding (vise, chuck, soft jaws), loads and presets cutting tools, sets work and tool offsets, runs a first article and tweaks offsets until parts hold tolerance.

Stamping or molding: supervisor leads/performs a die change on a press or a mold change on an injection or blow molding machine — unclamping and pulling old tooling, staging and setting new tooling, connecting water/hydraulic/ejector lines, setting shut height or clamp/process parameters, then tuning first shots.

Packaging/filling line: supervisor performs or directs a size/SKU changeover — swapping or adjusting format parts (starwheels, timing screws, guide rails, formers), adjusting conveyors, labeler and coder settings and sensors, then running test containers and fine-tuning.

Food, beverage or chemical processing: supervisor sets up and adjusts process equipment (slicers, formers, fillers, mixers, ovens) including reassembly of sanitary parts after wash-down, blade/nozzle changes, and adjusting settings for variable raw material (fat content, temperature, viscosity).

Assembly / welding operations: supervisor sets up workstation and cell tooling for a model change — swapping or reconfiguring fixtures and jigs, changing robot end-effectors or weld tips, setting torque tools and presses, and verifying fit on a trial unit.

Mid-run adjustment and troubleshooting on general or legacy equipment: supervisor responds to drift or a stoppage — clearing a jam, realigning a guide or feeder, adjusting belt/web tension, shimming or squaring a component, tweaking temperature or feed on aging machinery until output is back in spec.

tasks.label: Inspect or test installed units, parts, systems, or assemblies for fit, alignment, performance, defects, or compliance with standards, using measuring instruments or test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fit and alignment check of a structural subassembly just installed in the jig on the final/major assembly floor: measuring gap and flush, step, contour conformance, hole position and edge margin between skin panels, doors, ribs, spars or control surfaces, using feeler gauges, scales, portable scanners or a laser tracker, and recording the results against the drawing tolerances.

Inspection of drilled holes and installed fasteners over a panel or joint: hole diameter, countersink depth, stack thickness, fastener head flushness/protrusion, correct fastener type and grip, sealant condition — hundreds to thousands of features per shift, checked with gauges, flushness meters and go/no-go tooling.

Surface/skin condition inspection of an assembled airframe section or completed unit at the station (pre-paint or pre-delivery walk): scanning skins and fairings for dents, scratches, tool marks, protruding fasteners, finish and sealant defects, and mapping/reporting any damage found.

Functional/operational test of installed systems in the airframe: flight-control rigging travel with protractors and rig pins, cable tension with a tensiometer, hydraulic/pneumatic pressure and leak checks, electrical continuity/bonding checks on installed harnesses, and operating installed units to verify performance, hooking up test equipment in the aircraft.

Restricted-access and confined-space inspection: entering or reaching into wing boxes, fuel tanks, fuselage crowns, wheel wells or behind installed panels with lights, mirrors and borescopes to verify installation, sealant fillets, clearances and absence of damage or FOD.

Configuration and workmanship verification against drawings and specs after installation: correct part and hardware numbers, presence of cotter pins/safety wire/torque stripes, clamp spacing and chafing clearances, FOD removal, then buying off the operation and writing up any nonconformance.

tasks.label: Assemble parts, fittings, or subassemblies on aircraft, using layout tools, hand tools, power tools, or fasteners, such as bolts, screws, rivets, or clamps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Drilling, countersinking, deburring and riveting/lockbolting skins, stringers, doublers and splice straps onto structural panels (wing panels, fuselage panels, control-surface skins) held in a shop-floor assembly jig; NC/template-defined hole patterns, tight edge-distance and countersink-depth tolerances, sealant wet-installed fasteners, two-sided work with bucking bar or squeeze riveter.

Bench/fixture build-up of small subassemblies (rib and clip assemblies, intercostals, doors, brackets, control-surface details): laying out and transferring hole patterns with drill templates and layout tools, drilling, deburring, clecoing, then riveting/screwing the detail parts together to a shop-order sequence.

Attaching repetitive standard fittings to major structures on the shop floor — frame clips, shear ties, rib posts, stringer splices, stiffeners — drilling through the stack and installing rivets, lockbolts or Hi-Loks on accessible surfaces of a spar, panel or fuselage barrel held in tooling.

Installing large or complex machined fittings and hardware in awkward, blind or confined locations: crawling into wing-box bays and fuselage crown/gear bays to install brackets, nutplates, angles and gear/hinge fittings, measuring and installing shims, running blind fasteners overhead, and torqueing bolts by feel through small access holes.

Major-component join: aligning and mating fuselage sections, wing-to-body, or empennage to fuselage, then match-drilling, countersinking, sealing and installing the joint fasteners at the splice with laser-measured positioning.

Installing systems and rigging hardware on the airframe: cushioned clamps and support brackets for hydraulic/pneumatic tubing and wire bundles, routing and securing control cables, pulleys and pushrods, screwing and safety-wiring hardware in cluttered, already-populated interior zones.

tasks.label: Mark identifying information on tubing or cable assemblies, using etching devices, labels, rubber stamps, or other methods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Harness shop of an aircraft/rotorcraft plant: applying the identifying legend (wire number, gauge, circuit code) along individual wires and coax before harness build-up, using a UV laser wire marker or hot-stamp printer, per the wire list and spec, then cutting to length and kitting.

Bench/harness-board work: fitting pre-printed heat-shrink identification sleeves over conductor and connector ends, shrinking them, and wrapping self-laminating labels or cable tags on completed cable/harness assemblies and bundle breakouts.

In-situ on the aircraft during installation: applying identification labels, tape markers or stamped tags to tubing runs and wire bundles already installed in the fuselage, wing, wheel well or under floor — confined, overhead and awkward positions, position varying with the routing found.

One-off, prototype or rework marking at a workbench: hand stamping, engraving pen or vibro-etch of a part/serial number on a repaired or replacement tube or cable assembly of odd size, plus filling out and attaching an identification tag.

tasks.label: Adjust, repair, rework, or replace parts or assemblies to ensure proper operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fastener rework on a structural assembly on the shop floor: an inspection tag or squawk identifies bad fasteners (smiling/upset rivets, sheared heads, out-of-round or oversized countersinks, wrong grip length) in a skin/stringer or frame joint; the assembler drills out the fastener without damaging the hole, inspects and reams the hole to the next oversize per the disposition, deburrs, applies wet sealant, installs and upsets/swages the replacement or oversize fastener, and verifies head flushness and grip.

Removing and replacing a defective or damaged structural detail or skin panel found nonconforming during build (cracked/mis-machined fitting, bracket, doubler, or a mislocated skin): defasten the part, remove it, fit the replacement to the existing substructure, match-drill and countersink the hole pattern, seal, and refasten to spec.

Fit-up rework on mating parts that will not come to tolerance: measure the gap between mating flanges/skin and substructure, file/trim/grind the interfering part or a clip, fabricate or select and install liquid or peelable shims, sometimes elongate or re-drill holes, then pull the joint up with clamps and verify gap, edge margin, and contour.

Systems rework inside the installed airframe after a functional or leak check: crawl into a wing box, wheel well, or fuselage crown to replace a leaking hydraulic fitting or tube run, re-route and re-clamp a wire bundle or duct, replace a chafed hose, a damaged clamp/bracket or a seal, then re-test in confined, awkward-access space.

Rigging and adjustment of movable assemblies to make them operate correctly: install rigging pins/fixtures, adjust turnbuckles and cable tension, set push-rod end lengths, adjust hinge/latch/actuator stops and door fit, then run travel and operation checks against the rigging chart and re-adjust until within spec.

Surface, sealant and finish rework on structure: scrape out and re-apply nonconforming fillet or faying-surface sealant (including fuel-tank seals), blend out scratches, mismatches and tool marks to allowable depth, re-apply primer/chem-film touch-up and re-inspect the finished surface.

sources.claim: Boeing abandoned its Fuselage Automated Upright Build robots that drilled and filled fasteners on 777/777X fuselages in the factory, returning the work to mechanics with semi-automated flex-track tools because the robotic solution produced more hand work and rework.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant negative evidence: the largest attempt to run autonomous drilling/fastening robots on airframes as they sit on a human assembly line was withdrawn for quality and rework reasons, so on-line (E2) robotic structural work is not substantiated.

sources.system: Encore aerospace robotic sanding system

sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic surface preparation of aircraft skins. It transfers to the abrasive portion of surface rework (blending and refinishing skin surfaces) on the same substrates with controlled material removal.

sources.system: SwRI adaptive robotic sanding / surface processing system
sources.title: Enabling Adaptive Capabilities for Robotic Sanding Systems
sources.claim: Southwest Research Institute demonstrated an adaptive robotic sanding system that scans the workpiece (an aircraft propeller blade region), builds a mesh and plans the sanding path on the as-found geometry rather than a fixed program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is scan-driven localized abrasive processing of an aircraft part. Rework requires working to as-found, non-nominal geometry, which this demonstrates for the blend/refinish portion of surface rework.

tasks.label: Attach brackets, hinges, or clips to secure or support components or subassemblies, using bolts, screws, rivets, chemical bonding, or welding.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Panel/subassembly stage in an airframe plant: riveting shear ties, frame clips, nut plates and small support brackets onto fuselage skin panels, stringers and frames held in a jig at a bench or panel station — drill, countersink, deburr, wet-install with sealant, squeeze or blind rivet, hundreds of small identical hardware items per shipset.

Systems-installation stage inside a closed structure: crawling into a joined fuselage barrel, wing box, under-floor bay or empennage to install clips, clamps, cable-tie mounts and support brackets that carry wire harnesses, ducts and hydraulic lines — confined, overhead, cluttered access, working off platforms, using screws, blind rivets or bonded mounts, positions often adjusted to as-built routing.

Major-structure stage in a large assembly jig: bolting hinges, hinge fittings, actuator brackets and support fittings onto wings, control surfaces, doors, flaps and empennage — heavier hardware, shim/fit-up to tolerance, drill/ream to size, Hi-Lok bolts and collars or torqued nuts, sealant, alignment checked against the jig.

Chemical bonding: attaching clips, cable-tie bases, standoffs and small brackets by adhesive to composite skins, interior panels and structure — surface prep/abrade, primer or two-part adhesive, accurate placement, hold or fixture through cure, on parts staged at a bench or on the aircraft.

Welding brackets and fittings onto metallic structure — sheet-metal/tubular assemblies, ducting, engine-area and missile/space-vehicle structures — tacking and TIG/MIG welding small brackets to a fixtured weldment in the sheet-metal or weld shop, with weld quality inspected.

tasks.label: Assemble prefabricated parts to form subassemblies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skin-panel subassembly on an airframer/tier-1 factory floor: aluminum or composite skin plus stringers/frames/shear ties built up in a jig — locate parts, temporarily clamp/cleco, drill and countersink, deburr, apply sealant, install slug rivets or lockbolts and collars, shave/inspect heads. Parts are prefabricated and drawings/NC data define hole patterns.

Structural framework subassembly: spars, ribs, bulkheads, floor grids, door frames, stabilizer/wing-box sections joined in tooling — position detail parts to jig locators, shim gaps, drill/ream to tolerance, install bolts, Hi-Loks and collars, torque and inspect. Heavy parts, overhead cranes and hoists, factory bay setting.

Small detail/bench subassemblies: brackets, clips, fittings, hinges, doublers, nutplates and bushings added to sheet-metal or machined details at a bench or small fixture — drill/countersink, apply corrosion-inhibiting sealant, set solid or blind rivets, drive screws to torque, stamp/serialize. High part-number variety, small batches, includes missile and space-vehicle detail parts.

Systems subassemblies: building wire-harness bundles on a layout board (routing, lacing, connector/backshell assembly), hydraulic/pneumatic tube-and-fitting assemblies, control cable/rigging assemblies with turnbuckles and swages, valves and components mounted on brackets — flexible, deformable materials, hand-fit routing, torque and leak/continuity checks.

Interior, secondary-structure and soft-goods subassemblies: ducting sections, insulation blankets, honeycomb/trim panels with inserts and fittings, galley/lavatory/seat structural modules, fairings — bonded and mechanically fastened, flexible or delicate materials, cosmetic acceptance criteria, low volume and many configurations.

tasks.label: Clean aircraft structures, parts, or components, using aqueous, semi-aqueous, aliphatic hydrocarbon, or organic solvent cleaning products or techniques to reduce carbon or other harmful emissions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Solvent wipe of local faying surfaces, bond lines, fastener rows and sealant areas on a large airframe assembly held in a jig on the shop floor: assembler uses lint-free cloths wetted with MEK/IPA/aliphatic naphtha immediately before applying sealant, adhesive, primer or tape, reaching around clamps, tooling and adjacent installed hardware, with other mechanics working nearby.

Cleaning and degreasing of detail parts before installation: brackets, fittings, clips, tube ends, bulk fasteners and shims wiped or immersion/spray cleaned with aqueous or solvent cleaners at a bench, sink-on-drum, ultrasonic tank or parts washer in the shop, then dried and staged for the build.

Post-drilling / post-fit cleanup of structure: removing swarf, chips, cutting fluid, marker and coating residue from drilled holes, hole edges and mating surfaces of skins, spars and ribs by vacuum and solvent wipe so surfaces meet bonding/sealing cleanliness spec before fastening.

Degreasing/washing of large assembled structures or airframe exteriors before coating, sealing or delivery: wing skins, fuselage panels or a complete airframe cleaned with aqueous detergent or solvent cleaner in a paint-prep booth or wash hangar, working from stands or a lift over large areas.

Cleaning inside confined interior spaces: wing box / integral fuel tank bays, fuselage crown and bilge, removing shavings, debris and squeezed-out sealant and solvent-wiping around ribs, stringers and fasteners while working through access panels in a respirator/protective suit.

tasks.label: Align, fit, assemble, connect, or install system components, using jigs, fixtures, measuring instruments, hand tools, or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aerostructure plant, panel/shell station: assembler loads skin panels, stringers and frames into a jig, checks fit with gauges/laser, tacks, then drills, countersinks, seals and rivets the joint rows with power tools; output must meet hole-quality, countersink-depth and edge-margin specs.

Major-component join bay: mating fuselage sections to each other and to the tail/wings on positioners, aligning with laser tracker/measurement targets, shimming gaps, then drilling, sealing and installing thousands of fasteners in the orbital/longitudinal joints.

Systems installation inside the airframe: crawling into fuselage crown/floor, wing bays, wheel wells and cockpit to install brackets, clamps, wire harnesses, hydraulic/fuel tubing, ECS ducts and connectors; route, clip, torque B-nuts, mate connectors in confined, cluttered space with restricted access.

Mechanical equipment installation and rigging: hanging flight-control surfaces and doors on hinges, installing actuators, landing gear and linkages with hoists, then aligning, shimming, pinning and rigging cables/rods to travel and tension specs with measuring instruments.

Bench/jig subassembly: building smaller structural subassemblies (ribs, spars, doublers, small skin panels, floor and bulkhead details) fixtured at a workstation, drilling, deburring, sealing and riveting/bolting with hand and power tools, then dimensional check.

tasks.label: Cut, trim, file, bend, or smooth parts to ensure proper fit and clearance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench edge work on loose detail parts in the assembly shop: deburring drilled holes, breaking and filing sharp edges, sanding out scratches or high spots on aluminum clips, angles, doublers and small machined fittings so they seat flush before installation. Part can be clamped in a vise or laid on a bench; the amount to remove is set by drawing/standard.

Trim-to-fit of panels, skins, fairings, composite parts and custom shims/fillers: the edge line or gap is taken from the mating structure (scribe, template, or measurement), then the part is cut, routed, sawn, filed and sanded to that line at a bench or saw/router, usually with one or two test fits.

Open, accessible dressing on the structure itself while it sits in the assembly jig: sanding or grinding a skin/spar edge, easing a fay surface or panel edge, blending a high spot on an exterior surface so a mating part clears. Surface is exposed and reachable from outside the assembly.

In-place fit adjustment in confined or awkward positions: reaching inside a wing box, fuselage crown, wheel well or behind installed systems to file, scrape, grind or sand an interfering bracket, clip, hole edge or fitting found binding at trial fit; interference is diagnosed by feel and repeated try-fits, in cramped, overhead or blind access.

Bending/forming to fit: bending or tweaking tubing and conduit runs, clips, brackets, shims and control/rigging hardware with hand tools, small brakes or benders so parts align, clamp up without preload and hold required clearance to adjacent structure.

Cutting and trimming soft or nonmetallic parts to fit: seals, gaskets, insulation blankets, edge trim, chafe tape, grommets and duct liners cut to length/shape with shears or knife and smoothed, so the installed part fits its cavity and clears surrounding structure.

sources.system: Unison all-electric CNC tube bending machines

sources.claim: Fully automated CNC tube bending machines are supplied for aerospace tube production, bending hydraulic and control tubing to programmed multi-plane geometry.
sources.transferJustification: Bending tube and conduit so a run fits its routing and clears structure is the 'bend parts' element; automated benders produce that geometry from measured or nominal bend data with the tube loaded into the machine.

sources.system: Zund digital cutting systems (S3/G3 flatbed cutters)

tasks.label: Clean, oil, or coat system components, as necessary, before assembly or attachment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At an assembly bench/station in an airframe plant, the assembler preps small system hardware before installing it — solvent-wiping fittings, bearings, bushings, tube ends, brackets and connectors with lint-free cloth and IPA/MEK, blowing out swarf and chips, applying anti-seize or a light oil film. Mixed part types arrive in kits and totes; the worker decides 'as necessary' which item gets which treatment.

Applying sealant / faying-surface compound / adhesive to system and structural parts before mating them (bead on a bracket or beam flange, wet-install of fasteners, rivet encapsulation, sealing a system penetration). The part is held in a jig or on the airframe at a station; bead size, coverage and tack/cure time are spec-controlled and inspected.

Coating parts and mating surfaces before attachment — brushing or spraying chromate/epoxy primer, corrosion-inhibiting compound or touch-up on machined details, fittings and skins, typically in a spray booth or designated coating area, with film thickness and coverage inspected.

Oiling/greasing mechanical system components before installation — packing bearings, greasing bushings, control-cable pulleys, actuator rod ends, hinge pins and landing-gear pins with specified aerospace grease, applying a metered amount to defined surfaces and wiping excess.

In-situ cleaning and coating in confined or awkward locations during assembly — vacuuming/wiping swarf and cleaning hole edges inside a wing box, fuselage joint, wheel well or bulkhead bay, then applying sealant or corrosion-inhibiting compound to the joint before the fastener or component goes in.
