tasks.label: Lay out and examine metal stock or workpieces to be processed to ensure that specifications are met.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Layout on structural profiles in a fabrication shop: worker reads shop drawings and marks hole centers, cut/cope lines, and the locations of clips, stiffeners and connection plates on beams, columns, channels and angles staged on sawhorses or a layout table, using tape, square, soapstone/scribe and punch.

Layout on plate and sheet stock: worker nests parts on a plate, snaps/scribes cut lines, marks hole centers, bend lines, part outlines and piece marks, and confirms the plate is large enough and of the right thickness/grade for the parts to be cut from it.

Examining incoming metal stock before processing: checking the received beam/plate/tube against the bill of material for size, grade/heat number, length, straightness/camber, mill tolerances, and surface condition (scale, pitting, gouges, laminations, rust) and rejecting non-conforming material.

Dimensional check of already-processed workpieces before fit-up: verifying lengths, bevels, squareness, hole diameters and hole spacing on parts coming off the saw, drill line or plasma table against the detail drawing, using tape, square, calipers and hole gauges.

Layout and check-out of a large built-up assembly in the shop's fitting bay: marking fitting locations along a long girder, truss chord or column and verifying overall dimensions, camber/sweep and squareness of the laid-out member against the erection/detail drawing before tacking.

Field or yard layout and verification: at an erection site or open storage yard, checking delivered or already-positioned members against erection drawings and marking field-drilled hole locations, splice lines or trim cuts in weather, on uneven ground, with the piece in place.

instances.label: Thermal cutting of plate and structural shapes in a steel fab shop: crane/rack the plate onto a CNC plasma or oxyfuel table (or laser for lighter gauge), load or verify the nest program, set gas/height-control parameters, run the cut, then break out parts, remove slag and stage them. Mixed job-shop work, sparks and dust, shop cranes and other workers around.

Press-brake and plate-roll forming: pick tooling for the job, load punch/die, set backgauge and bend program, bend a first article, check angle and flange dimensions, then run the lot - from small brackets and gussets to long heavy plate panels needing two-hand or hoist support; also rolling plate or angle to a radius template.

Cutting stock to size and punching: band-saw or cold-saw cutting beams, angle, channel and bar to length; shearing plate/sheet on a squaring shear; ironworker punching of bolt holes and notching/coping of angle and flat bar. Setting stops, gauges and punch/die sets; deburring and marking pieces.

Hole making by drilling: setting up a drill press, radial drill or CNC beam/plate drill line to drill and tap bolt holes in beams, base plates, gussets and clip angles - clamping the workpiece, selecting speed/feed and coolant, changing bits, checking hole location against the shop drawing.

Grinding and edge work: pedestal, belt or hand-held grinders to deslag and bevel thermally cut edges, weld-prep joints, dress welds flush, and deburr punched or sheared parts before fit-up or paint; parts range from small clips to large weldments handled on a bench, cart or the shop floor.

Field/erection-site or laydown-yard use of portable fabricating equipment: magnetic-base drill, portable band saw, hand-held oxyfuel/plasma torch and grinder to trim, drill, ream and dress structural pieces during fit-up - often on partly erected steel, at height or in tight quarters, with weather and no fixed setup.

tasks.label: Position or tighten braces, jacks, clamps, ropes, or bolt straps, or bolt parts in position for welding or riveting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Structural steel fab shop: fitter reads the piece drawing/layout marks on a beam or column, positions connection material (shear clips, gussets, base and end plates, stiffeners) from a cart of cut parts, holds it square with C-clamps, magnets or a dog, checks dimensions, and tack welds it in place for the welder.

Built-up member work in the shop: web-to-flange fit-up of plate girders and built-up I/box sections and similar repeating heavy sections — squaring web to flange, closing gaps with clamps/screw jacks, and tacking before submerged-arc weld out.

One-off heavy or large custom weldment in an open shop bay: crane-set members on horses, out-of-square or warped plate pulled into line with hydraulic jacks, come-alongs, wedges, strongbacks and bolt straps; fitter judges where to force, shims, bolts temporary braces, then tacks.

Repetitive production run: loading cut/formed parts into a jig or welding fixture, seating locators, closing clamps, verifying fit, and presenting the clamped assembly for robotic or manual welding (equipment frames, brackets, chassis, tank and plate subassemblies).

Shipyard / heavy-plate panel shop: positioning longitudinal and transverse stiffeners, webs and brackets on a bulkhead or deck panel, pressing them down against the plate with magnets, dogs and wedges or a pressing beam, and tacking them for automatic welding.

Field/site work: at an erection or repair site, hanging and drift-pinning members, bolting parts in position, installing temporary bracing and jacking/plumbing the assembly before final bolting, welding or riveting.

tasks.label: Lift or move materials and finished products, using large cranes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fab shop, overhead bridge crane on radio pendant: fitter slings or magnets raw stock (plate, wide-flange beam, angle, tube, bundles) out of racks or the laydown area and flies it across the bay to a saw, drill line, burn table or layout table, walking the load past machines, columns and other workers.

Fab shop, moving a fabricated assembly in process: rigging a multi-ton weldment (column with attachments, truss section, frame, awkward center of gravity) to lifting lugs with slings and shackles, sometimes a tandem two-crane pick, and moving it to the next fitting station, the blast/paint bay or a finished-goods rack with a spotter signalling.

Fit-up assist: using the crane to lift, hold and inch a member (beam, plate, gusset) into position against a mating part while the fitter aligns it to layout marks and tack welds it, with repeated small hoist/trolley corrections under hand signals before the load is released.

Receiving bay / yard: unloading incoming steel deliveries from flatbed trucks with an overhead or gantry crane — chains or magnets on bundles of beams and plate, removing banding and dunnage — and stacking the stock into racks or the outdoor laydown area, in whatever weather.

Shipping yard: loading finished fabricated products onto trailers or rail cars with a crane, setting pieces on dunnage in a required sequence and orientation for the erector, with a worker guiding placement and then chaining/strapping the load.

Off-site / field variant: a fabricator-fitter working with a mobile or crawler crane at an erection or customer site or a congested outdoor yard, moving and setting fabricated assemblies onto supports amid uneven ground, wind, delivery traffic and other trades.

tasks.label: Set up face blocks, jigs, and fixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Job-shop weldment fixture: on a steel platen or layout table in a structural fab shop, the fitter works from a shop drawing/3-D model, snaps or scribes layout lines, positions face blocks, angle stops and clamps to dimension, squares and checks diagonals, and tack-welds the stops to the table so the weldment can be fitted; one-off or small-batch work, parts 10-200 lb.

Large floor jig for a big assembly (roof truss, plate girder, frame, tank shell): heavy blocks, cribbing and dogs set with an overhead crane on the shop floor plate, leveled and shimmed to establish camber and elevation over 20-60 ft, tack-welded down, then checked with tape, level and string line.

Production fixture setup/changeover in a robotic welding cell or on a welding positioner: mount or swap the fixture plate, install locating pins, stops and toggle/pneumatic clamps for the next part number, adjust to the setup sheet, and prove out with a first-article check.

Bench-scale fixturing for repetitive small parts: build a fixture on a modular welding table (Siegmund/Fixturepoint style) using stops, squares, magnets and toggle clamps, set to drawing dimensions and checked with square and calipers before the run.

Field or erection-site fit-up aids: setting temporary jigs, strongbacks, dogs, wedges and clamps on a job site, barge, or during shipyard/outfitting work, with uneven footing, weather, and no fixed layout.

tasks.label: Align and fit parts according to specifications, using jacks, turnbuckles, wedges, drift pins, pry bars, and hammers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Structural steel fab shop: fitter takes a rolled beam or column off the rack, works from shop drawings, and lays out and fits connection material (shear tabs, clip angles, end plates, stiffeners, base plates, gussets); squares parts, taps them into line with hammer and drift pin, clamps, and tacks them for the welder.

Built-up members and heavy weldments in the shop: assembling plate girders and box/heavy columns - aligning web to flanges, setting stiffener and doubler plates, using clamps, wedges, jacks and come-alongs/turnbuckles to pull heavy or slightly distorted plate into line before tacking; overhead crane assists.

Heavy plate panel work for barges, ships and heavy equipment structures: fitting longitudinal and transverse stiffeners, webs and brackets to flat panels and bulkheads; pulling plate down with dogs and wedges, driving stiffeners tight with sledge and pry bar, tacking to layout marks.

Tank, pressure-vessel, stack and duct fabrication: aligning rolled shell courses and longitudinal/girth seams, matching edges and hi-lo with jacks, wedges, fit-up clamps and dogs; fitting heads, nozzles and rings on rollers before tacking.

Miscellaneous / architectural metal shop: one-off stairs, handrails, ladders, gates, platforms and frames of tube, angle and light plate; parts laid out on a welding table or simple jig, squared with square, level, clamps, pry bar and hammer, then tacked.

Field fit-up at the erection or installation site: aligning members already hung by crane - drawing bolt holes into line with drift pins and spud wrench, plumbing and squaring frames with turnbuckles, come-alongs, jacks and wedges, shimming bases - on an open, weather-exposed, uncontrolled site.

tasks.label: Hammer, chip, and grind workpieces to cut, bend, and straighten metal.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fab-shop bench/table work: grinding dross and slag off plasma- and oxy-fuel-cut plate parts, deburring, breaking and beveling edges, dressing cut ends. Mixed geometries, one-offs and small batches, parts moved by hand or hoist.

Grinding weld beads, spatter and tack remnants flush and chipping slag on medium-to-large fabricated weldments (beams with clips/stiffeners, frames, platforms, skids) sitting on horses or the shop floor; varied geometry, reaching and awkward postures.

Fit-up persuasion during assembly: sledgehammering, wedging, dogging and jacking misaligned members, tabs, gussets and flanges into alignment (bending them as needed) before and between tacks, judged by feel, gap gauge and eye.
Straightening/leveling parts and members brought back into tolerance after cutting or welding, using a shop press, straightening machine or leveler on parts brought to the machine.
Heat-and-hammer (flame) straightening of a warped welded assembly on the shop floor: torch heat patterns plus sledge blows, iterated by eye and feel until the member is true.
Field/erection-site touch-up: grinding welds and cut edges, chipping slag and scale on members at the job site or on erected steel, outdoors, on scaffolding or lifts, weather-exposed.

instances.label: Fab shop floor: fitter builds an expedient holding jig for a repeat weldment — reads the drawing, picks scrap angle/plate, measures and squares locating stops on a welding table or platen, tack welds them down, trial-fits a part, adjusts and re-tacks until the part sits to print.

Fab shop: fitter designs and builds a durable, repeatable welding/drilling fixture — sizes a steel base frame, cuts angle/tube/plate to length (saw, torch, grinder), drills holes, sets locators and stops, squares and levels the assembly, welds it out, and checks dimensions before release to production.

Fab shop: fitter designs and makes a flat full-size template/pattern (sheet steel, plywood, or heavy paper) of a part profile or bolt-hole pattern — lays it out with tape, square, scribe and compass, cuts with shears/jigsaw/torch, files edges, punches holes, marks and stores it for repeat marking of parts.

Fab shop: an existing jig/template no longer yields in-tolerance parts (worn, bent, heat-distorted, or the part changed). Fitter diagnoses the error, grinds or cuts off old stops, shims/re-positions locators, drills new holes, re-squares and re-tacks, then re-qualifies with a trial part.

Erection/installation site or customer plant: fitter field-measures as-built conditions (existing anchor-bolt pattern, opening, mating flange) and makes a template on the spot from cardboard/sheet, or tacks up a temporary alignment jig from scrap to hold members during fit-up, working amid other trades on uneven, uncontrolled ground.

Shop localized heat treatment of a part: flame-hardening a wear surface, annealing/softening a section for machining or bending, tempering, or localized stress relief of a small weldment, judged by temperature indicators and controlled cooling.

sources.claim: Penna Flame Industries, a commercial heat treater, has run robotic flame hardening cells since 2008 that flame heat-treat fixtured steel products such as gears, ... and rings under program control.
sources.transferJustification: Flame hardening is itself torch heat treatment of steel parts: the robot carries a gas flame head over fixtured steel and takes it to a specified metallurgical temperature, the same physical act as the fabricator's torch heat treating.

sources.system: Penna Flame robotic flame hardening cell with indexing table and IR pyrometers
sources.title: Flame Hardening Gears | Thermal Processing Magazine
sources.claim: In the robotic cells, parts are loaded on an indexing table coordinated with the robot, and preheat, austenitizing and residual temperatures are monitored with laser-sighted infrared pyrometers, giving closed-loop temperature control of the flame process.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates that a robot can hold a specified flame-heating temperature on fixtured steel with pyrometer feedback, which is the control problem in preheating and localized heat treating of fabricated steel parts.

sources.system: Robotic flame hardening bay (three programmed robots)
sources.developer: Penna Flame Industries (reported in Gear Solutions)
sources.title: Flame Hardening | Gear Solutions Magazine
sources.claim: A commercial flame-hardening operation routes parts needing intricate or selective heating to a robot bay where three programmed robots selectively heat only the designated areas of each part.
sources.transferJustification: Selective flame heating of chosen areas of a steel part is the same act as torch heat treating a specific zone of a fabricated part; comparable steel workpieces, flame tooling and temperature precision.

sources.system: KUKA robotic oxyacetylene (flame) process cells
sources.date: accessed 2026 (product page, technology in commercial use for years)
sources.title: Oxyacetylene cutting | KUKA Global
sources.claim: KUKA supplies robot cells for automated oxyacetylene torch work on steel of varying thickness, with automatic ignition and flame monitoring making the process reproducible without manual preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic oxy-acetylene cutting rather than heating, but it uses the identical tool (robot-mounted acetylene torch with automatic ignition and flame monitoring) on the same heavy steel workpieces in a fenced cell, establishing that a robot can carry and control an acetylene flame over a fixtured structural part.

sources.system: HHI curved shell-plate forming robot system
sources.title: Hyundai Heavy reports breakthrough in shipbuilding robotics - Marine Log
sources.claim: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries deployed a 6-axis articulated robot system that automatically generates heating lines and thermally forms three-dimensionally curved ship shell plates, validated in shipyard production for over a year.
sources.transferJustification: Line heating / heat forming of steel plate is the same skill as torch heat bending and flame straightening: measure the plate, decide where and how much localized heat to apply, and apply it robotically until the geometry meets the target.

sources.system: HHI curved shell-plate forming robot system
sources.title: Hyundai Heavy to use robots in ship construction - SAFETY4SEA
sources.claim: The HHI plate-forming robot replaces work previously done by hand with flame heating; the unmanned system pairs a multi-joint arm with a high-frequency induction heating head rather than a gas torch.
sources.transferJustification: Heat source is induction rather than acetylene, but the work performed (localized thermal shaping of steel formerly done manually with a flame) and the output accepted by the yard are the same; flame delivery by robot is separately evidenced by the KUKA and Penna Flame items.

sources.system: HHI curved forming robot system (곡 성형 로봇 시스템)
sources.title: 현대중공업, 조선업계 최초 선박 건조에 '로봇' 활용 - 인사이트
sources.claim: Korean trade coverage states the robot system standardized and automated the curved-forming work that operators previously did by hand with flame heating, using a 6-axis robot with high-frequency induction heating and automatic heating-line generation.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms the robot took over manual flame-heating work (heat forming of steel plate), the closest production analogue to torch heat bending and heat straightening by structural fabricators.

tasks.label: Straighten warped or bent parts, using sledges, hand torches, straightening presses, or bulldozers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fabrication shop: warped small/medium flat parts, bars and angles coming off laser/plasma/flame cutting or after welding are straightened/flattened on a hydraulic straightening press, arbor press or leveler, checked against a straightedge or surface table and re-worked until flat.

Fabrication shop: angular/weld distortion in a welded beam, plate girder or stiffened panel is removed with vee heats and strip heats from an oxy-fuel hand torch (sometimes with restraint clamps), temperature judged by color, flatness checked with a straightedge or string line.

Fabrication shop: distortion in an irregular weldment (frame with brackets, gussets, tubes, machined faces) is flame-straightened by eye — heat locations chosen ad hoc around obstructions, part re-checked in a fixture or against layout marks.

Fabrication shop: heavy rolled beams, columns and welded girders are crane-handled onto a horizontal 'bulldozer'/gag press or straightening rolls to remove sweep, camber or flange tilt, measured with a string line or tape.
Fit-up table/shop floor: bent tabs, clips, lugs, flanges and misaligned edges are 'persuaded' back with a sledge, hand hammer, dolly or wedge during assembly, judged by fit against the mating part.

Field/erection or repair site: a bent member or damaged flange is straightened in place using a portable torch, jacks, come-alongs and chain falls, on staging or at ground level, in weather and around other trades.

sources.system: ARKU FlatMaster / FlatJack precision leveler
sources.date: 2025 (product line in market for years; page retrieved 2026-07)
sources.title: FlatMaster® | Leveling of Sheet Metal & Heavy Plate | ARKU
sources.claim: ARKU FlatMaster precision roller levelers are commercial machines that flatten warped punched, laser-cut and plasma-cut parts and heavy plate up to 60 mm thick in seconds, with an optional FlatJack system that automatically measures flatness on the leveler.

sources.system: ARKU part leveler at Louis Industries
sources.title: The importance of material flatness in metal fabricating - The Fabricator
sources.claim: A US metal fabricator (Louis Industries, Paynesville, MN) installed an ARKU leveling machine specifically to deal with warped cut parts, replacing manual straightening work in its shop.

sources.system: KOHLER Peak Performer part leveling machine
sources.title: KOHLER Peak Performer part leveling machine ensures level and low-stress metal sheets
sources.claim: KOHLER Peak Performer part leveling machines are installed at fabricators (e.g., Gorasia, Lucy Group) and level laser-cut sheets and parts, removing warp and internal stress before welding and assembly.

sources.system: MAE M-AH automatic straightening machine (RICOS control)
sources.developer: MAE Maschinen- und Apparatebau Götzen GmbH
sources.title: Efficiently integrating the straightening of gear shafts in a production line – with the M-AH automatic straightening machine from MAE
sources.claim: MAE automatic straightening machines measure a workpiece's run-out/shape error and apply computed straightening strokes in a closed loop inside an automated production line, including variants with automated loading and light-curtain guarding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic press straightening of shafts/bars rather than fabricated structural bar. Same operation (measure deviation, apply plastic bending strokes on a press, re-measure to tolerance) on comparable steel sections, so performance carries to press-straightening of bent bar and profile stock in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Automated straightening machine at HAI (Hammerer Aluminium Industries)
sources.developer: reported by Light Metal Age / machine supplier
sources.title: Straightening Complex Aluminum Profiles - Light Metal Age Magazine
sources.claim: An automated straightening machine is in production use at Hammerer Aluminium Industries straightening complex structural extrusions (an EV sill/longitudinal beam) to tolerances beyond standard extrusion capability.

sources.system: SMS CRS 2000-9H compact roller straightener
sources.title: SMS group, Yamato Steel Commission Japan's First CRS® Roller Straightener - AIST
sources.claim: SMS group commissioned a CRS compact roller straightener at Yamato Steel's heavy section mill that straightens heavy structural sections and sheet piles by ..., correcting distortion consistently.

sources.system: Danieli 60-t off-line long-product straightener
sources.title: Danieli heavy-duty straightener in operation at Topy, Japan
sources.claim: A Danieli heavy-duty off-line straightener operating at Topy Industries straightens a mix of structural long products including angles, grating beams and deformed flats away from the rolling line.

sources.system: H/T-beam 3-in-1 assembly-welding-straightening machine (flange straightening machine)
sources.developer: ZMDE / BCAM / WUXI ABK (Chinese steel-structure equipment builders)
sources.title: H Beam Assembly Welding Straightening Machine Complete Guide - ZMDE Steel Machinery
sources.claim: Integrated H-beam assembly/welding/straightening lines used in steel structure fabrication include a straightening station that automatically corrects flange angular distortion caused by welding, immediately after the welding pass.

sources.system: Automatic line-heating robot for curved shell plate formation
sources.developer: Seoul National University / Korean shipyard (Journal of Ship Production and Design)
sources.title: A Comprehensive Line-Heating Algorithm for Automatic Formation of Curved Shell Plates
sources.claim: A line-heating robot system computes heating locations and speeds from measured versus target plate shape, positions the heater and measurement devices, heats the plate and re-measures it; the system was evaluated on diverse plates and used in actual shipyard fabrication.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heat forming of hull plate rather than heat straightening of a warped weldment. Identical physics and tooling (localized torch/induction heating to induce plastic shrinkage), identical control loop (3D shape measurement, computed heat pattern, re-measurement), comparable steel plate thicknesses, so it transfers to removing unwanted curvature/warp.

sources.system: Gantry-robot induction line-heating plate forming system
sources.developer: Korean research group (Journal of the Society of Naval Architects of Korea)
sources.title: A Study on the Concave Type Hull Plate Forming using Induction Heating System
sources.claim: A gantry-robot automatic heating system with a high-frequency induction heater and automatic measurement was built and applied to form concave hull plates of the type used in ship manufacturing, replacing manual gas heating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: induction line heating for plate forming rather than flame straightening. Same heat-shrinkage mechanism, same automated measure-plan-heat loop on ship steel plate, so it substantiates machine-controlled heat straightening of plate-like weldments in a fixtured cell.

tasks.label: Erect ladders and scaffolding to fit together large assemblies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Structural fabrication shop: a fitter rolls out and erects a mobile frame-scaffold tower (2-4 frames high) beside a large weldment such as a 20-ft truss, tank shell or equipment frame - setting base plates/casters and outriggers, pinning frames and cross braces, laying deck planks and guardrails, leveling and plumbing, then repositioning the tower repeatedly as fit-up moves along the assembly.

Shop floor: fitter carries and sets portable step or extension ladders against or beside a large assembly to reach an upper joint for fit-up or tacking - choosing a spot on a floor cluttered with material and leads, footing the ladder at proper angle, securing the top, and moving it several times per shift.

Heavy-fabrication bay or fenced fab yard: crew erects multi-lift system scaffold (ringlock/tube-and-clamp) fully around a very large assembly (pressure vessel, ship block, bridge girder) - hundreds of standards, ledgers, braces, base jacks on mudsills, internal ladder accesses, planking, guardrails and toeboards, ties to the structure, and a competent-person inspection tag before use.

Field erection / customer plant site: fitter erects ladders and a small scaffold around a field splice outdoors - uneven or graded ground, weather and wind, other trades and traffic present, layout unknown until arrival, scaffold adapted to whatever the structure and ground allow.
After fit-up: dismantling the scaffold and ladders, passing down and stacking/banding frames, braces and planks, hauling them back to the rack or trailer and clearing the work area in the shop.

sources.system: Automated Structures Assembly Laboratory (ASAL) robotic truss assembly system
sources.title: Robotic Assembly of Truss Structures for Space Systems and Future Research Plans
sources.claim: An industrial robot with a special end-effector and machine vision autonomously assembled and disassembled an 8-meter structure of 102 tubular truss members plus 12 panels inside a purpose-built assembly facility, with members presented from fixtured canisters on a motion base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: building a large modular frame structure from standard tubular members with pinned/quick-connect joints. Erecting frame scaffolding is the same class of work - bulky steel members, coarse (centimetre) tolerances, repeated pin/latch connections - and the demonstration is exactly the E1 case where members are presented to the machine in known fixtured positions.

sources.system: Weaver Workcell / Toggle RLS
sources.title: Toggle Robotics | LinkedIn
sources.claim: Robotic workcell autonomously assembles large steel bar structures (rebar cages, mats, column cages) from standard steel members in a purpose-built offsite production facility, guided by 3D vision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of large three-dimensional steel-member structures in a purpose-built cell. Scaffold erection joins comparable heavy steel members at comparable coarse tolerances; the Toggle cell shows such member handling and joining is production-reliable when the work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: Toggle production system
sources.title: Robots tie rebar at startup Toggle | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Toggle's system fabricates and assembles steel rebar assemblies with industrial robots as a production process used on real construction projects.
sources.transferJustification: Context only for commercial maturity of robotic steel-member assembly in a purpose-built facility; autonomy is not established in this source, so it is not relied on for a positive judgment.

sources.system: LIFTBOT
sources.title: Liftbot, help at height (Techint)
sources.claim: The only fielded scaffolding robot is a robotic hoist that carries scaffold components up and down the scaffold for human erectors; it is remotely operated and does not itself assemble, level, brace or plank the scaffold.

sources.system: Kewazo scaffolding robot (LIFTBOT predecessor)
sources.title: Engineers Develop The World's First On-Site Scaffolding Robot | ScaffMag
sources.claim: Kewazo's on-site scaffolding robot delivers scaffold materials to human workers; the erection itself remains manual, so no deployed system completes scaffold erection in a plant or site setting.

tasks.label: Preheat workpieces to make them malleable, using hand torches or furnaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fab shop: welder/fitter preheats the joint zone of a heavy structural weldment (thick plate, heavy beam-to-column joint, base plate) with an oxy-fuel rosebud hand torch to a WPS-specified temperature (e.g., 150-350 F), verifying with temp sticks or IR gun, before tacking/welding. Part sits in a fixture, on horses, or on the floor.

Fab shop: worker heats a small-to-medium part (angle, bar, gusset, rod, plate strip) with a hand torch or in a shop furnace/forge until malleable, then bends, forms or hammers it to shape in a jig, brake or vise.

Fab shop: worker loads stock or parts into a gas-fired oven, electric preheat furnace, or induction heater, sets/monitors soak temperature, and retrieves the hot workpiece for the next forming or welding operation.
Fab shop: planned flame heating of a large plate or member (line/strip heats along a laid-out pattern) to curve or camber it to a specified shape, with layout marks and template checks.

Fab shop: heat straightening / distortion correction of an already-welded assembly - the worker diagnoses where the piece is out of tolerance, chooses spot, line and vee heat patterns on the fly, and heats with a rosebud, rechecking with straightedge and squares between heats.

Field or erection site (bridge repair, plant retrofit, outdoor yard, ship in drydock): worker preheats a member or joint in place with a portable torch rig, working at height or in confined access, under variable weather and with no fixed layout.

sources.system: Inductoheat / Inductotherm Group robotic induction heating and bar-end heating systems
sources.title: Automation of Induction Heating Systems for Billets and Other Unique Shapes - Inductotherm Group
sources.claim: Commercial induction heating cells use a six-axis robot to load steel bars into heating coils, position the correct heat length, then extract the heated bar and transfer it to the forming press, with the robot performing all handling automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heating steel stock in a coil/furnace to forming temperature. Same purpose as the rated task (bring a steel workpiece to a controlled temperature so it can be worked), same objects (steel bar/billet), and tighter temperature control than a 150-350 F weld preheat.

sources.system: KUKA robot with Pickit 3D vision at Colin Milas forge
sources.title: Kuka robot picks billets and feeds an induction oven - Pickit 3D
sources.claim: A production forge feeds its induction furnace with a vision-guided KUKA robot that picks billets from a bin and places them on the infeed conveyor at the furnace cycle rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: charging a furnace with workpieces to heat them for forming. This is the handling half of the rated furnace-preheat instance, on comparable steel stock, performed autonomously in production.

sources.system: Brooks Forgings robotic forging cell (FANUC six-axis robots + induction heating)
sources.title: Robotic Forging Services | Automated Upset & Counterblow | Brooks Forgings Ltd
sources.claim: A UK forging company runs FANUC six-axis robotic forging lines in which the whole sequence, from induction heating of raw billets ... forging strike, is executed automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heating steel stock until malleable and delivering it hot to a forming operation - the same start-to-accepted-output chain as the rated task, on structural-grade steel, run unattended in a fenced cell.

sources.system: Induction bending machines (Hines Bending Systems; comparable Inductaflex CNC benders)
sources.title: Heat Induction Bending | What Is Induction Bending? | Hines Bending
sources.claim: Hot induction bending machines automatically heat a narrow band of a pipe or structural section to bending temperature with a coil and form it to the programmed radius under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locally heating a structural section until malleable and immediately forming it. Same physical objective as torch preheating for bending, on heavier sections and with closed-loop temperature control.

sources.system: IHI-alpha and iCALM line heating plate robots
sources.developer: Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries; Seoul National University
sources.title: Study on Double-Curvature Metal Plates Sequential Forming with Heat-Assisted Incremental Bending Based on Minimum Energy Method (Metals, MDPI)
sources.claim: Automated line-heating plate robots that apply controlled heat along programmed lines to form large steel hull plates were developed by IHI ('IHI-alpha') and Seoul National University ('iCALM'), improving on manual torch work, though plate accuracy remains imperfect.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: flame/line heating of large steel plate to make it locally malleable and change its shape - the same tool (gas heating head), the same workpieces (heavy steel plate) and the same temperature-judgment problem as manual torch heat forming.

sources.system: IHI-alpha / IHIMU-alpha automated steel plate bending (line heating) system
sources.date: circa 2011 (IHI Technical Report); system in use since 1997
sources.title: "IHIMU-a" A Fully Automated Steel Plate Bending System for Shipbuilding (Semantic Scholar record)
sources.claim: IHI's automatic plate bending system using line heating has been used on plates for ships actually under construction since its 1997 introduction, with a later fully automated version handling the whole process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated flame heating of heavy steel plate on a shipyard forming bed to make it malleable and shape it; establishes production maturity of machine-controlled torch heating of large workpieces.

sources.system: Path Robotics Rove (Obsidian physical AI on a quadruped)
sources.title: Path Robotics Launches Rove, Bringing Mobility to Welding Automation Powered by Physical AI
sources.claim: Path Robotics launched Rove, a quadruped-mounted autonomous welding system aimed at large assemblies and immovable structures ... shipyards and heavy industry, with early adopters beginning use.
sources.transferJustification: Considered as the closest mobile-in-facility system: it performs arc welding, not flame or induction preheating, and no source shows it carrying a heating torch or holding a workpiece at a preheat temperature, so it does not transfer to this task.

tasks.label: Install boilers, containers, and other structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fabrication shop: fitting and installing components (stiffeners, gussets, brackets, base plates, nozzles, access doors) onto/into a larger fabricated structure such as a frame, hopper or tank body — crane handling, layout to prints, clamping, squaring, tack welding, final securing.

Fabrication shop: assembling a container/vessel/boiler drum from rolled shell courses, heads and internals — aligning seams on positioners/rollers, fitting heads to can sections, fitting saddles and lugs, seam welding to code.

Field: setting and installing a packaged boiler or pressure vessel in an industrial plant or building mechanical room during new build or retrofit — rigging into a congested existing space, leveling on a foundation, anchoring, fitting supports, platforms and breeching brackets.

Field: erecting/installing outdoor tanks, silos, bins, hoppers and their support frames at industrial or construction sites — landing sections with a mobile crane, plumbing and aligning, bolting and welding shell/leg connections in weather.

Field: installing miscellaneous structures at customer sites — equipment platforms, stairs, handrails, machine guarding, duct and pipe supports — measuring to as-found conditions, cutting and drilling to fit, anchoring to existing steel or concrete, welding out.

sources.system: Zeman SBA (Steel Beam Assembler) Compact
sources.title: Zeman - SBA Compact
sources.claim: Zeman's Steel Beam Assembler is a commercial robotic cell in which a parts robot positions attachment parts to their exact weld location from the 3D model and a tack/weld robot fully automatically assembles and welds them onto structural beams.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fit-up and attachment of plates, stiffeners and brackets onto structural members. Same objects (heavy structural steel weldments), same fit-up precision, and it is the shop 'install parts into a structure' step; only the environment (a fixtured cell) differs.

sources.system: Zeman SBA robot at CPE Construction
sources.title: ZEMAN Steel Beam Assembly (SBA) Robot
sources.claim: A structural steel fabricator installed and commissioned a Zeman SBA robot in production in 2024, where robotic arms position and weld stiffeners, brackets and other components ... beams.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: real production deployment of robotic positioning and securing of components onto fabricated structures, the shop form of this task.

sources.system: Robotic Beam Constructor / stiffener mounting and panel gantries
sources.title: Robotic Cutting & Welding Automation for Structural Steel
sources.claim: Kranendonk's Robotic Beam Constructor automates assembly and welding of structural ..., using scanning to position stiffeners accurately and attach them, with minimal operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement and joining of heavy steel members and stiffeners in shipyard/heavy-steel panel and block assembly — the same positioning-and-securing operation on comparable large weldments, performed in purpose-built gantry cells.

sources.system: ABB IRB welding robot line at CIMC container plant
sources.title: ABB welding robots boost productivity for cargo container producer (IFR case study)
sources.claim: A cargo container manufacturer runs a production line with 65 ABB welding robots assembling and welding container base frames, ends and general assembly areas.

Comparable objects (large steel containers), comparable fit-and-weld precision; substantiates that container structures can be assembled and secured by robots when work is presented in a purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Fully automatic marriage (decking) stations
sources.title: Fully and semi automatic marriage stations - ROFA Industrial Automation Group
sources.claim: Automotive final-assembly 'marriage' stations that merge a heavy drivetrain/chassis module with the body and fasten it are offered and operated in fully automatic form.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated setting of a heavy assembled unit onto its mounting structure and fastening it. This is the machine-environment analogue of setting a boiler/vessel onto a base and anchoring it: heavy module, positional alignment to mounting points, automatic fastening, all with the work fixtured and presented.

sources.system: Robotic arc welding cells at A.O. Smith
sources.title: Making the move from hard automation to robotic welding
sources.claim: A water heater manufacturer converted tank (container) production to robotic arc welding cells, welding tank bodies and fittings in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly/joining of pressure-holding tanks in fixtured cells; comparable containers and weld-quality requirements to shop container/vessel build-up.

sources.system: Robo-Welder (Shimizu Smart Site)
sources.title: Shimizu Begins Collaborating People and Autonomous Robots at Construction Site, Toranomon-Azabudai Project
sources.claim: Shimizu deployed the autonomous Robo-Welder to weld massive steel columns at an actual high-rise construction site; columns and beams are lowered into position by a separate crane system and human crews before the robot welds the joints.

sources.title: It's Time To Think Differently About Automated Welding for Pressure Vessels
sources.claim: Pressure-vessel fabricators use PEMA assembly stations and large positioners to cut joint fit-up time and to fit heads to can sections, but the station is run with an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fit-up and joining of pressure-vessel/boiler shell sections and heads. Operator-assisted, so treated as non-autonomous supporting context only.

emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Fiberglass Laminators and Fabricators
roles.description: Laminate layers of fiberglass on molds to form boat decks and hulls, bodies for golf carts, automobiles, or other products.

tasks.label: Release air bubbles and smooth seams, using rollers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boat plant, open-mold hull or deck: after chopper-gun spray-up or hand-laid mat/roving, the laminator works the large, mostly smooth/convex mold surface with grooved aluminum and finned rollers to expel entrapped air, wet out the glass and flatten ply overlaps before gel; mold sits in a lamination bay, often on a rotating fixture, resin gel time sets the pace.

Production line for small-to-medium standardized parts (tub/shower units, spa shells, truck fairings, golf-cart and RV body panels, small boat components): repetitive rollout of one or two plies over an identical open mold on a stand or carousel, same laminate schedule every cycle.

Confined and geometrically awkward rollout: tabbing stringers, bulkheads and hull liners inside a cured hull, hull-to-deck seams, corners, radii, deep recesses and overhead/vertical surfaces; worker reaches into the part with long-handled and corner rollers and judges by sight and feel where air remains.

Large industrial composite parts in a plant: wind-blade shell/root laminates, FRP tanks, pipe and duct wraps, architectural panels - very large open molds or mandrels, thick multi-ply glass laminates rolled out in sections by a crew.

Repair, refit, prototype and one-off custom work: boat repair yard, RV/truck body shop, custom composites shop or on-site tank/pipe repair; patch or scarf laminate rolled onto a variably shaped, previously built structure in whatever position it happens to sit.

sources.system: BOSMAL Robotic Station for Automated Hull Lamination
sources.developer: BOSMAL Automotive Research and Development Institute (Poland)
sources.title: Yacht Lamination Automation | Robotic Station | BOSMAL
sources.claim: BOSMAL offers a fenced 6-axis robotic station whose primary function is rolling out saturated fiberglass laminate on yacht hull molds with a force-instrumented roller head to remove air bubbles; molds are mounted manually on rotary positioners inside a full safety enclosure with the robot on a linear track.

sources.system: Cevotec SAMBA / Fiber Patch Placement 'Robotic Lamination'
sources.title: Robotic Lamination: Enabler to increase lay-up rates of complex aerostructures - Cevotec
sources.claim: Cevotec's SAMBA Fiber Patch Placement systems perform 'Robotic Lamination' in a robotic cell: the robot presses and rolls plies onto molds with controlled compaction, including on shoulder transitions, concave sections, steep edges and small radii, explicitly to minimize air enclosures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated ply lay-up onto molds. The de-airing action is the same physical operation as hand rollout - a compliant roller pressed against plies on a mold surface with controlled force to conform the ply and expel entrapped air - performed on curved production molds in a robot cell.

sources.system: Robotic AFP/ATP compaction rollers (survey of robotic CFRP manufacturing)
sources.title: Application of robotic manipulation for carbon fiber reinforced polymers manufacturing - A survey - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Robotic composite lay-up heads use conformable silicone/rubber compaction rollers that follow intricate mold contours, promote resin flow between plies and remove air bubbles introduced during placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fiber/tape placement. The compaction roller performs the same de-airing/consolidation function as a laminator's hand roller, against a mold, and is the accepted quality-critical step for void control in these machines.

sources.system: Automated Fiber Placement machines (Hercules/Ingersoll/Electroimpact lineage)
sources.title: Automated fiber placement: A review of history, current technologies, and future paths forward - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Automated fiber placement machines, which consolidate plies with compaction rollers, have been commercially available since the late 1980s and are implemented in production by aerospace manufacturers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated lay-up with roller consolidation. Establishes that roller-consolidation lay-up runs in real production, in dedicated machine cells, at aerospace quality levels.

sources.system: KADO x IEC FRP spray-up automation with Kawasaki KJ264 explosion-proof robot
sources.developer: KADO Co. / IEC Co. / Kawasaki Robotics
sources.title: At the Forefront of FRP Automation: Spray-Up and Cutting Process Innovations Pioneered by KADO x IEC | Kawasaki Robotics
sources.claim: KADO and IEC automated open-mold GFRP spray-up of Kawasaki jet-ski parts using an explosion-proof Kawasaki coating robot, achieving stable automated operation on the shop floor - showing wet glass/resin open-mold work running in a purpose-built robot cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic open-mold spray-up of chopped glass and resin. Shows that the same molds, materials and explosive-atmosphere constraints are handled by robots when the mold is fixtured in a dedicated cell, supporting the E1 environment for the rollout step.

sources.system: Bavaria Yachts gelcoat spraying robot (hull moulds, series production hall)
sources.title: The lamination of a yacht: layer by layer | BAVARIA YACHTS

tasks.label: Spray chopped fiberglass, resins, and catalysts onto prepared molds or dies using pneumatic spray guns with chopper attachments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Marine plant lamination bay: sprayer applies skin coat and successive chopped-glass/resin/catalyst laminate layers into a large boat hull or deck mold (20-80 ft) sitting on a cradle in the shop, walking around and inside the mold, controlling thickness and glass content by pass and feel; repeated on a small set of recurring hull/deck tools.

High-volume leisure/sanitary parts: pool shells, spa and tub shells, shower bases sprayed with a chopper gun over gel coat and barrier coat, molds on carts, turntables or a moving line inside a ventilated spray station; the same handful of standard shapes runs repeatedly to a fixed laminate schedule.

Job-shop / OEM medium parts: truck caps, tanks, ducts, planters, flat and lightly contoured panels, transit and equipment covers; short runs with frequent mold changes, molds set on stands or tables in a curtained spray area of a composites plant.

Complex molds and detail work: spraying deep narrow recesses, lockers, undercuts and flange returns, and spraying over foam cores, rib/stiffener formers, inserts and hardware the crew has just placed in the mold; requires working the gun into confined areas and adapting to where the cores actually sit.

One-off, rework and away-from-the-line work: prototype or single custom molds, patching thin or dry spots and rework areas on parts, and occasional on-site spray-up such as lining an installed tank, pond or pool at a customer location, where surface and access are taken as found.

tasks.label: Mix catalysts into resins, and saturate cloth and mats with mixtures, using brushes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production boat/pool/tank plant: laminating a large open mold (hull, deck, pool or tank shell). Worker batches catalyzed polyester/vinylester in buckets, lays chopped strand mat and woven roving into the fixed mold, and wets the plies out with brushes and rollers, working to gel-time limits over a large curved surface.

Composites shop making small/medium repetitive open-mold parts (shower pans, spa/bath shells, hatches, liners, tanks, golf-cart or vehicle body panels): small resin batches catalyzed at the bench, cloth/mat pieces cut to pattern and brushed out in standard molds, many parts per shift.

Secondary/structural lamination inside a hull or deep mold cavity: tabbing stringers, bulkheads, transom cores and hull-deck joints with glass tape and mat, brushing catalyzed resin into corners and confined interior spaces at awkward angles, geometry varying part to part.

In-plant rework and repair: grinding out voids, dry spots, blisters or damage on a demolded part, cutting one-off patch plies, mixing a small catalyzed batch in a cup and brushing the plies onto the ground-out, one-of-a-kind repair area.

Off-site/field wet layup: repairing a boat in a yard or slip, lining or patching a tank, duct or pipe in place; resin catalyzed on site in small batches, cloth and mat brushed onto vertical/overhead surfaces under uncontrolled ambient conditions.

sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic spray-up laminating) substantiates machine mixing of catalyst into resin and deposition of the catalyzed mixture to wet out glass reinforcement in a full-size open mold, i.e. the same wetted-laminate output this task produces by brush; the reinforcement arrives chopped rather than as pre-placed mat, but resin chemistry, mold size and quality standard are the same.

sources.transferJustification: Resin spray-up and chopped lamination cells perform the catalyzed-resin application/wet-out step of open-mold laminating in marine and sanitary-ware production, the same output as brush saturation of mats in those industries.

tasks.label: Check completed products for conformance to specifications and for defects by measuring with rulers or micrometers, by checking them visually, or by tapping them to detect bubbles or dead spots.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boat plant: after demold, a laminator checks a large FRP hull, deck or liner - walks the part inside and out, eyeballs the gelcoat for pits, blisters, print-through and dry spots, taps the laminate with a coin/hammer to find voids and dead spots, and checks key dimensions and laminate thickness with tape, ruler or gauge before the part moves to rigging.

Production/trim line for medium molded parts (golf cart and vehicle body panels, truck caps, tubs/showers, small tanks, ducts): worker measures thickness and features with ruler, calipers or micrometer against a spec sheet, scans the surface visually for wrinkles, porosity and resin-rich/dry areas, taps suspect zones, and passes or tags the part.

High-spec structural laminates (wind blade shells/spar caps, aerospace and defense parts): documented inspection to a written spec - full-coverage check of bond lines and laminate for voids/delamination (tap or instrumented equivalent), plus dimensional/thickness verification, with a recorded inspection report before release.

Finishing/repair bay: final cosmetic QC of gelcoated parts after trim, patching and buffing - comparing surface finish to boundary samples, checking that repaired/filled areas are sound and blended, tapping over patches, and marking anything needing rework.

Very large or awkward finished products checked in place on the shop floor (bus/RV body shells, large FRP tanks, pool shells, hulls with liners installed): inspector climbs into or under the part, taps overhead surfaces and inside corners, and measures in confined, obstructed spaces with a tape.

tasks.label: Pat or press layers of saturated mat or cloth into place on molds, using brushes or hands, and smooth out wrinkles and air bubbles with hands or squeegees.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boat plant, large open female hull/deck molds (6-20 m): laminator drapes pre-cut chopped-strand mat and woven roving saturated with catalyzed polyester into the mold, pats it into chines, corners, keel and stringer pockets by hand/brush, then works out wrinkles and air with laminating rollers and squeegees before gel time.

General FRP job shop, contoured open molds of moderate size (truck caps, golf-cart and utility-vehicle body panels, ducts, tank heads): worker lays wet-out mat/cloth plies into the mold, presses them into radii and flanges, and rolls out bubbles; mold changes several times a week.

Flat or near-flat panel and sheet lamination (wall/liner panels, flat stock, simple tray molds) on tables or shuttle molds: mat is rolled out, resin/chop applied, and the laminate rolled/squeegeed flat and de-aerated in repetitive runs.

Bath/pool/spa plant: tubs, shower pans and pool shells; chopped glass and resin sprayed or mat placed into the mold, then the wet laminate is rolled out by hand to consolidate it and remove air, with extra mat pressed into corners and reinforcement zones between spray passes.

Engineered ply-schedule laminates on contoured tooling of a few metres (transit-vehicle panels, radomes/ducts, blade sub-preforms, high-spec tooling): pre-cut resin-impregnated or wet-out plies laid in a specified order and orientation on the tool, debulked and smoothed wrinkle-free to a documented standard.

Repair, rework and field/on-site lay-up: patching a damaged hull in a repair bay or at a dock, relining a tank or duct in place, one-off prototype molds; geometry and access differ every time and the setting is not kept to a production standard.

tasks.label: Select precut fiberglass mats, cloth, and wood-bracing materials as required by projects being assembled.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production boat plant: laminator working a hull or deck mold pulls the precut chopped-strand mat, woven roving and cloth plies for that part from the kit cart/rack staged by the cutting room, checks ply type and sequence against the layup schedule, and stages them at the mold.

Mid-volume composites shop (truck caps, tubs/showers, tanks, golf-cart and vehicle body panels): worker selects the precut mat and cloth pieces called out on the process sheet for the specific mold from stacked, labeled kits at the cutting/kitting area and carries them to the layup station.

Selecting wood-bracing and core materials: precut plywood stringers, transom panels, bulkheads and blocking (plus balsa/foam core sheets) picked from cut-parts racks per the part being assembled and staged at the mold.

Custom or low-volume shop with mixed jobs: worker selects among several precut ply kits and offcuts of different weights/weaves for a one-off or small-batch part, matching material to the job traveler and reserving extra pieces for build-ups.

Field/yard work: laminator doing a repair or fit-out at a boatyard, dock or customer site selects mats, cloth and wood bracing from truck stock or a temporary material stash under uncontrolled conditions.

sources.system: Airborne Automated Kitting / Automated Ply Placement

sources.claim: Airborne's Automated Kitting is a commercial robotic cutting-room system that takes cut composite plies off the cutter, sorts them into the correct kit for the part and sequences them in laminating order, handling prepreg, dry fibre and thermoplastic materials.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same work as the rated task: choosing the correct precut fabric plies for the part being laid up and staging them in build order; the robot does it from digital nest/kit data in a cutting-room cell.

sources.system: Airborne Automated Kitting solution at GKN Fokker

sources.claim: The robotic kitting platform was contracted for and installed at GKN Fokker's plant; the cell picks, places and sorts cut composite plies, with vision that identifies any random ply presented, and a second phase adding automated picking from the nest.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects (limp cut composite plies) and same purpose (sorting the right plies into the kit for a given part) as the rated task, executed in an industrial cell.

sources.transferJustification: Robotic identification and handling of individual precut dry fabric plies in a production cell — the picking and verification core of selecting the right precut mats and cloth for a part.

sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates robust robotic grasping of limp precut fabric plies of the kind a laminator selects, in a fixtured production cell.

tasks.label: Bond wood reinforcing strips to decks and cabin structures of watercraft, using resin-saturated fiberglass.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume production boat plant: bonding plywood/wood reinforcing strips (hatch-edge cleats, hardware backers, deck core inserts) into an open deck or cabin-liner mold at the same, repeated locations on every unit. Worker beds the strip in resin/putty, lays resin-saturated mat or tape over it, and rolls out air. Same part geometry every cycle; mold sits in the lamination bay.

Bench/subassembly work in the same plant: bonding wood strips and backing pads to small, largely flat or gently curved components (hatch covers, deck panels, seat bases, liner sections) lying on a work table or simple fixture, laminated over with resin-wet fiberglass and rolled out. Repetitive, accessible from above.

Tabbing wood cleats/reinforcing strips inside an assembled hull/cabin structure after the deck or liner is set: worker climbs through a hatch into a confined cabin, works overhead and on vertical surfaces, hand-cuts and wets out tape, and rolls it onto irregular, partly obstructed joints.

Custom or semi-custom yacht builder, one-off or very low volume: wood reinforcing strips scribed and hand-fitted to a unique cabin structure per drawings, bedded and overlaminated with resin-saturated cloth; geometry differs from boat to boat and fit-up is judged by eye and feel.

Repair/refit at a boatyard: bonding new wood reinforcing strips into an existing boat's deck or cabin (rotted core replacement, new hardware backers), working around existing structure, finishes and furniture, in tight access with hand-mixed resin and wet-out cloth.

sources.system: ROBOSTRAT robotic spray-up range (Magnum Venus Products Europe)
sources.title: Robotics - Magnum Industries Europe Ltd t/as; Magnum Venus Products
sources.claim: Commercially sold robotic chop-and-spray systems apply resin plus chopped fiberglass (i.e., resin-saturated fiberglass) to complex-shaped composite parts at production rates, using programmed robot paths in spray enclosures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray-up lamination. The bonding laminate over a wood strip is the same material (chopped glass wetted with catalyzed resin) applied to the same class of open molded marine parts, so the material-application step of this task is already robotized on comparable geometry.

sources.system: Lesta LECROB self-learning spraying robots with 'fiberglass package'
sources.title: Automation systems for fiberglass, glass fiber, and gelcoat spraying - IPCM
sources.claim: Robot manufacturers supply dedicated fiberglass/gelcoat spraying robot packages with chopper dosing and resin valve control that are used in production composite plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of resin and chopped glass in a booth. Same consumables and same deposition control needed to lay resin-saturated fiberglass over a wood strip; substantiates that the wet-laminate application step is a fielded robotic capability.

sources.system: Bavaria Yachtbau gelcoat spraying robot
sources.title: The lamination of a yacht | BAVARIA YACHTS
sources.claim: A production boatbuilder runs a CNC-controlled robot that sprays material inside hull molds moving along its lamination line, i.e., robots already apply coatings/material to boat moldings presented on a purpose-built line.

tasks.label: Trim excess materials from molds, using hand shears or trimming knives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large open mold (boat hull or deck, tub/shower, tank, RV/truck fairing) on the shop floor: after layup, while the laminate is green/gelled, the worker leans over or into the mold and runs a trimming knife along the mold flange or trim line, peeling away the wet glass overhang before full cure. The mold sits wherever it is staged in the plant; sticky resin, fumes, and a cut line judged against the mold edge.

Small-to-medium parts in open molds staged on carts, racks or turntables (golf-cart body panels, hatches, covers, seat pans, pool steps): worker trims the excess laminate overhang and squeeze-out at the mold rim with hand shears or a hook knife at a workstation, then passes the mold on. Repetitive, many molds per shift.

During layup: cutting and trimming the reinforcement itself to the mold - shearing mat, woven roving, chopped strand or prepreg plies to fit contours, cutting darts at corners, and trimming ply overhang past the mold flange with shears before or during wet-out.

After demold: knife/shear trimming of cured flash, fins and ragged edges from the part's perimeter and openings, working at a bench, on a trim fixture, or with the part supported on a stand, before routing and sanding.

Custom, prototype or repair work in a small job shop: one-off or very-low-volume parts on hand-built or worn molds with no CAD model, non-standard trim lines set by eye or by a scribe mark, and frequent geometry changes between jobs.

tasks.label: Apply layers of plastic resin to mold surfaces prior to placement of fiberglass mats, repeating layers until products have the desired thicknesses and plastics have jelled.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Series production boat plant: worker applies catalyzed gel coat and then resin skin/barrier coats into a large open hull or deck mold staged in a layup bay or spray area, building to a specified mil thickness in multiple passes and waiting for each coat to gel before the next; molds are repeat production tooling.

Pool, tank, bath/shower, RV or truck-part plant: repeat molds of moderate size move through a fixed sequence of stations; worker sprays gel coat, then barrier/skin resin coats, checking thickness and gel state between layers before mats are laid.

General shop bay: worker applies catalyzed resin by brush, roller or hand-held gun to small or intricate molds and detail areas (tight radii, flanges, corners, cored zones, small parts and tooling), repeating coats until the required thickness is reached and the resin has jelled.

Large custom or low-volume part (big yacht hull, one-off architectural/industrial mold): worker climbs into or works around a deep unique mold, applying resin coats over long cycles on tooling that may be used only once or a few times.

Small custom job shop or off-site work: mold set up in a cluttered, non-standard space or at a customer's site/outdoors, with variable temperature and humidity affecting gel time; worker applies successive resin coats under conditions kept to no fixed standard.

tasks.label: Inspect, clean, and assemble molds before beginning work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boat plant, large open mold: a 20-40 ft hull or deck mold sits on a rolling cart or rotisserie in an open lamination bay. Worker walks the mold, inspects the polished gelcoat tool surface for scratches, wax buildup and cured resin flash, wipes it down with solvent/tack rag, applies and buffs several coats of release wax or PVA, then bolts or clamps on flange extensions, transom and hatch inserts before layup begins.

Small-to-medium production molds (tubs and shower pans, golf cart and truck body panels, tanks, RV components) staged on racks or tables in an open shop. Worker inspects the mold face, blows/wipes off dust and residue, applies or sprays release agent, and installs inserts, plugs or clamps the two mold halves together before spray-up or hand layup.

Closed-mold RTM/infusion tooling: worker inspects both mold halves and the sealing gaskets/O-rings, scrapes and cleans cured resin from flanges, applies semi-permanent release, installs cores or inserts, bolts/clamps the halves and verifies the vacuum seal before injection.

Remediation found during pre-work inspection: a scratch, pinhole, chip or wax build-up on the mold face must be sanded, patched with gelcoat/filler, cured, re-sanded, polished back to a mirror finish and re-waxed before the mold can be used.

Oversized or one-off tooling assembled from sections (pool, tank, custom architectural piece) in a yard, temporary bay or at a customer site: sections trucked in and set on stands, aligned and shimmed, bolted, joints taped and faired, then cleaned and waxed. Layout and lighting differ every time.

tasks.label: Cure materials by letting them set at room temperature, placing them under heat lamps, or baking them in ovens.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-mold FRP part just hand-laid or sprayed on its mold (boat hull or deck, tank, tub/shower, cart body) is left to cure at ambient shop temperature in the layup/cure bay: the mold on its dolly or stand stays put or is rolled to a staging area, the laminator watches gel and exotherm, and checks tack-free state or Barcol hardness before the part is released to demold or the next ply. Shop floor shared with other laminators, forklifts and overhead cranes.

Small to medium laminated, bonded or gel-coated parts are racked on carts or shelves and baked in a batch curing oven: worker loads the rack, closes the door, sets the recipe (temperature ramp and soak) per the work order, monitors it, then unloads after the cycle and stages the hot parts to cool. Composite shop with standard equipment and fixed layout.

Localized accelerated cure of a patch, gel-coat repair, bonded joint or putty fill using portable heat lamps or infrared panels: worker positions the lamp(s) at the right stand-off over the area, watches surface temperature and scorch risk, repositions to cover the whole area, and checks hardness at the end. Done at a bench or alongside a large part in the shop.

Large part or loaded tool (big marine part, hull section, tub/shower shell on a support fixture, large panel, tooling) is moved by cart, tug, forklift or crane into a walk-in oven or heat tunnel, positioned for airflow, run through a post-cure cycle and removed. Plant with an institution-controlled layout and dedicated cure area.

Vacuum-bagged prepreg or wet-layup part cured under heat and pressure in an autoclave or heated press: hook up vacuum lines and thermocouples, verify bag integrity, roll the tool cart into the vessel, run the certified cycle, then unload and debag. Higher-spec composite/aerospace shop.

Cure done away from the production shop: a laminated repair on a boat in a marina slip or yard, or a part finished at a customer site, cured at ambient or with a portable heater/lamp under a tarp, with weather, dust and variable temperature and humidity to manage.

tasks.label: Apply lacquers and waxes to mold surfaces to facilitate assembly and removal of laminated parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large open molds (boat hull or deck, pool shell, truck/RV body panel, tank half) sitting on stands or dollies in the layup bay of a composites plant. Worker cleans the mold, applies paste wax or semi-permanent release by rag/orbital pad over tens of square meters including deep concave areas, buffs to a haze-free shine, repeats coats.

Small-to-medium molds (hatches, consoles, seats, shower pans, golf-cart or ATV panels) prepared on benches, carts or a carousel in a high-mix shop: wipe or spray on wax/semi-permanent release, buff off, mask flanges and parting lines.

Spray application of PVA release lacquer or a semi-permanent sealer with a spray gun over an already waxed mold in a prep area or booth, achieving an even, continuous, pinhole-free film before gelcoat.

Between-pull touch-up on production molds in a high-volume line (bathware, pool, small-parts carousel): one quick coat of release re-applied and lightly buffed on the same tooling many times per shift.

Break-in of a new or freshly repaired/refinished mold: applying sealer/lacquer and multiple wax coats with cure intervals, detail-buffing corners, radii and undercuts, and inspecting the surface for hazing, missed spots or contamination before the first pull.

tasks.label: Repair or modify damaged or defective glass-fiber parts, checking thicknesses, densities, and contours to ensure a close fit after repair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cosmetic blemish repair on freshly demolded parts inside the plant's finish/repair bay: scratches, dust nibs, sags/runs, dull spots and light print-through in the gelcoat of boat decks, tubs, RV/truck panels. Worker locates the blemish, sands it out with progressively finer abrasives and buffs back to gloss, checking that the gelcoat film is not cut through and that the contour still matches the surrounding surface.

In-plant repair of defective laminate requiring material to be put back: air voids, dry spots, blisters, resin-starved corners, holes or openings cut in the wrong place. Worker grinds/cuts out the defect, wets out and lays in glass plies or fills with putty, cures, grinds flush, sprays or brushes patch gelcoat, blends and buffs, and checks laminate thickness and contour against spec.

Subtractive modification of a part so it fits its mating assembly: trimming flanges, routing or enlarging openings, grinding down high spots and mold-line mismatch on hulls, caps, doors and hatches, then offering the part up or using a template/fixture to confirm a close fit. Plant floor, part on a cart, buck or trim fixture.

Repair-shop/boatyard repair of customer-damaged fiberglass: punctures, cracks, delamination and transom/stringer damage on hulls and decks. Worker assesses damage extent (tap test/moisture/thickness), bevels or scarfs the area, lays up successive plies to restore thickness and density, fairs the contour, matches and sprays gelcoat, wet-sands and buffs.

On-site/field repair away from the shop: RV sidewalls and truck bodies at a dealer lot, fiberglass tanks/ducts at a customer plant, a boat in a slip or on a trailer. Variable access, ladders or staging, ambient temperature and humidity affecting cure, damage of unknown extent, cosmetic match expected.

Repair and refinishing of production molds/tooling in the plant: filling gouges, chips and crazing in the mold's tooling gelcoat, re-establishing the exact contour and parting-line fit, then wet-sanding and polishing the mold surface to a mirror finish and re-waxing before the next pull.

tasks.label: Mask off mold areas not to be laminated, using cellophane, wax paper, masking tape, or special sprays containing mold-release substances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repeat-production open mold (shower pan, pool step, tank half, small boat deck) staged at a prep/spray station in an FRP plant: worker sprays a mold-release/PVA parting film over the mold face and over the flange areas that must stay resin-free, controlling coverage boundaries so nothing outside the part area bonds.

Repeat-production mold in an FRP plant: worker applies masking tape along the mold flange, parting line, and around cutout/hatch boundaries before gelcoat and layup so those areas are not laminated; long straight and gently curved runs on a smooth gelcoated tool.

Large boat hull or deck mold sitting on its cradle on the shop floor: worker climbs in and does the whole prep — wax/semi-permanent release, PVA spray, tape on flanges, and paper or film taped over hardware bosses, inserts and previously laminated sections — with mold geometry and clutter varying bay to bay.

Masking selected mold regions with sheet material: cellophane, wax paper, or plastic film cut to shape, laid over cores, insert pockets or bonded-in areas, and taped down so resin does not reach them.

One-off, prototype, or repair tooling in a custom shop: plug or short-run mold whose geometry differs every time, masked ad hoc with tape, paper and release spray according to the fabricator's judgment.

tasks.label: Check all dies, templates, and cutout patterns to be used in the manufacturing process to ensure that they conform to dimensional data, photographs, blueprints, samples, or customer specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boat/RV or bath-fixture plant: before a run, the laminator pulls the plywood/MDF/plastic trim and cutout templates for a part (hatch openings, hardware hole patterns, trim lines) and verifies outline dimensions, hole locations and squareness against the shop blueprint with tape, rule and square, checking for wear, chipped edges or warp, then approves the template or tags it for rework.

Cutting room of a composites plant: check the cloth/core cutting patterns (mylar, cardboard or nested digital cut files' hard patterns) for each ply against the ply schedule and part drawing before fabric is cut into kits — verifying pattern outline, ply-count markings and orientation marks.

Mold shop / layup bay: verify a small-to-medium die or mold (1–3 m: golf-cart body panel mold, hatch mold, shower-pan mold, kick-off flange) against blueprint dimensions or a master before layup — checking flange widths, key openings and overall surface geometry for distortion after repeated pulls.

Custom or repair job shop: a pattern or template has been made from a customer's sample part or from photographs with only partial dimensional data; the worker checks the template by test-fitting it on the sample/part and against whatever specifications exist, judging whether the fit and profile are acceptable for the customer.

Large tooling: check full-size layout templates or large molds (over 3 m — deck templates, hull-side patterns, long stringers or a large one-piece mold) against loft drawings by laying them out on the floor or on the mold and measuring key stations and diagonals.
