tasks.label: Check products for quality, and identify damaged or expired goods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale/industrial bakery plant: the baker walks the line during a run, pulling loaves, buns, cookies or tortillas off the oven-discharge and cooling conveyors, judging bake color, volume, shape, scoring, topping coverage and breakage against spec, and checking finished packs for seal, weight and correct date code; out-of-spec units are pulled and the finding logged.

Retail in-store bakery (supermarket, donut shop, cafe): opening/closing walk of the display case and packaged bakery shelf — checking loaves, donuts, pastries for staleness, crushing, collapsed or damaged product, reading the date stickers on bagged items, and identifying goods past their pull date for markdown or disposal.

Small artisan/craft bakery or hotel-restaurant pastry kitchen: checking each rack as it comes out of the oven — crust color, oven spring, scoring, under- or over-bake, cracked or collapsed items — sometimes tapping, squeezing or cutting a sample loaf, and setting aside defective pieces before the goods go to the front.

Large bakery's receiving dock and racked ingredient/finished-goods warehouse: verifying incoming pallets of flour, sugar, fats, fillings and packaging — reading lot codes and expiration dates, spotting torn or crushed cases and leaking containers, confirming FIFO rotation of stored stock.

Small bakery or in-store bakery storage check: walk-in cooler, freezer and dry-store shelves — smelling and looking at dairy, eggs, fillings and fruit for spoilage, reading dates on tubs and cartons, checking flour and sugar sacks for tears, damp or pest damage, and rotating stock.

Final check of decorated and specialty items before boxing or sale: sheet cakes, cupcakes and custom cakes inspected for icing coverage and finish, decoration placement and lettering, structural integrity and match to the order spec; damaged or off-spec items rejected or redone.

tasks.label: Check equipment to ensure that it meets health and safety regulations, and perform maintenance or cleaning, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail bakery / in-store (grocery) bakery / restaurant bakeshop: end-of-shift or between-batch clean-down of production equipment in place - scraping and wiping the planetary or spiral mixer, bowl guard and beater, dough sheeter rollers and scrapers, divider/rounder, bench surfaces and scale, and the flour-dusted area around them, then sanitizing food-contact surfaces to code.

Wash-up of removable items and equipment parts: mixing bowls and hooks, sheet pans, bread pans, muffin tins, cooling racks, dough boxes, cutters, piping tips and utensils - soaking/scrubbing baked-on grease, running items through a warewasher or pot sink, drying and racking.

Ovens, proofers and hoods: brushing crumbs and carbon from deck/rack/convection oven interiors and racks, cleaning oven doors, steam tubes and drip trays, wiping the proofer interior and trays, pulling and cleaning hood filters, and confirming the oven holds temperature afterwards.

Wholesale/industrial bakery plant: cleaning and sanitizing production line equipment at changeover or during the sanitation window - hosing/foaming/sanitizing mixers, troughs, conveyors, dividers, moulders and depositors, dry-cleaning flour-handling equipment, and returning the line to pre-op condition.

Retail/in-store bakery: routine check that equipment meets health and safety rules - verifying blade and bowl guards and interlocks, cords and gaskets, slicer and mixer condition, verifying oven/proofer/cooler temperatures with a thermometer, checking for residue, pests and damage, and recording findings on a sanitation/HACCP log.

Wholesale bakery plant: routine inspection round of production equipment - reading gauges and temperatures, checking for bearing or drive faults, thermal checks, spotting leaks, spills and guard issues, and logging results for maintenance and food-safety records.

tasks.label: Adapt the quantity of ingredients to match the amount of items to be baked.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Artisan/retail bakery: baker takes the day's forecast or standing wholesale orders (e.g., 60 sourdough loaves instead of yesterday's 40), converts the formula's baker's percentages to a new total flour weight, and works out the scaled water, salt, levain, and yeast figures for the batch sheet.

Custom cake/pastry order: baker scales a base recipe to a nonstandard pan size, tier count, or serving count (e.g., a 3-tier wedding cake, or half a sheet-cake recipe), computing batter volume per pan and the matching quantities of filling, buttercream, and glaze.

Wholesale/commercial production bakery: production baker or scheduler converts the order book into batch counts constrained by mixer and proofer capacity, rounding to whole batches and computing total ingredient draw per formula in the bakery's production/ERP system.
In-store supermarket or foodservice bakery: baker adjusts pre-mix bag counts, scoop counts, and pan quantities against par levels and same-day order slips for thaw-and-bake or scratch-mix items.

Mid-shift adjustment: rush add-on order, ingredient shortfall, or leftover dough/batter requires recomputing a partial batch or a substituted-ingredient quantity on the fly so the finished count matches what was promised.

tasks.label: Place dough in pans, molds, or on sheets, and bake in production ovens or on grills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial/wholesale plant bakery: pan bread, buns or rolls. Divided and moulded dough pieces are panned into strapped pans or onto trays, run through a proofer and a tunnel/travelling oven at hundreds to thousands of pieces per hour; the baker sets programs, monitors panning and bake, and clears jams.

Retail/artisan bakery back-of-house: hand-shaped sourdough, baguettes and rustic loaves transferred from bannetons/couches onto peel boards or sheet pans, scored, loaded into a steam deck oven with a peel or loading belt, bake watched and pulled by color/feel; mixed product sizes through the morning.

Supermarket in-store bakery: frozen or par-baked dough pieces taken from the freezer, arranged on standard sheet pans, pans racked on a rolling rack, rack rolled into a rotating rack oven, program selected, product pulled and moved to cooling/display; staff and shoppers moving through the area.

Cookies, muffins, pastries and cakes in a retail bakery or commissary: dough scooped/deposited or portioned onto lined sheet pans or into muffin/cake molds at set spacing, pans loaded into a convection or rack oven, trays rotated, doneness judged.

Restaurant/foodservice baking: pizza dough stretched onto screens/peels and loaded into a deck or conveyor oven, or flatbreads/tortillas/griddle doughs cooked on a grill or griddle, turned and pulled to order during service.

tasks.label: Observe color of products being baked, and adjust oven temperatures, humidity, or conveyor speeds accordingly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket / in-store bakery bake-off: baker runs frozen par-baked breads, rolls, cookies and muffins through rack or convection ovens on preset programs, glances through the door glass or opens it mid-bake, and extends time, bumps temperature or adds steam when a rack is browning too fast or too pale.

Independent retail bakery / bakery-cafe daily production: croissants, baguettes, rolls, cookies and sheet cakes in convection and deck ovens; the baker watches crust and top color, then trims temperature, steam/vent and time between loads as the oven heat drifts through the morning.

Artisan bakery hearth breads: large sourdough and rye loaves in a steam-injected stone deck oven; the baker judges crust color loaf by loaf through the window, opens the damper to dry the chamber, drops deck temperature, and rotates or shifts loaves to even out browning.

Wholesale/industrial bakery plant: bread, buns, cookies or crackers travel on a band through a multi-zone tunnel oven; the operator watches bake color across lanes at the oven exit and trims zone temperatures, steam/humidity extraction and band speed at the control panel.

Restaurant, hotel or institutional pastry kitchen: cakes, quick breads, cookies and pastries baked in convection or combi ovens, often mixed loads on several racks; the cook checks color and doneness partway through and adjusts temperature or moves pans.

Specialty and delicate items: macarons, meringues, custom cake layers, pies with fluted crusts, and first runs of new recipes, where acceptable color is idiosyncratic and the baker makes item-by-item calls on temperature, humidity and time.

tasks.label: Set time and speed controls for mixing machines, blending machines, or steam kettles so that ingredients will be mixed or cooked according to instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale/industrial bakery plant: the baker/mixer operator sets mix time and low/high speed steps on a horizontal or spiral production mixer (e.g., 300–2,000 lb bread dough batches) per the plant formula card or HMI recipe, targeting dough temperature and development; work is in a production mixing room with bowl hoists and ingredient lines.

Supermarket/in-store bakery: baker sets the speed dial and timer on a 20–60 qt planetary mixer for icing, batters, cookie dough, or sweet dough per a recipe card, stopping to scrape the bowl and change speed between stages during a morning production run.

Small independent/artisan bakery: baker sets first speed/second speed times on a spiral mixer for bread and enriched doughs, then adjusts remaining mix time by feel and dough temperature (flour lot, water temp, room temperature vary day to day).

Pastry/institutional kitchen: baker sets time, temperature, and agitator speed on a steam kettle or automatic braising pan to cook fruit fillings, custards, glazes, or syrups to a specified endpoint, then holds or discharges the batch.

Blending/batching station in a bakery or bakery-mix operation: baker sets blend time and speed on a ribbon blender, dry-mix blender, or batter/cream blender to combine dry ingredients, fillings, or icings to formula before they go to the line.

tasks.label: Combine measured ingredients in bowls of mixing, blending, or cooking machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale/artisan bakery production floor: baker tips scaled flour (25 kg bags or bin), metered water/ice, salt, yeast and a bucket of preferment into a spiral or horizontal mixer bowl, several batches per shift, on a wet, floury floor shared with other staff.

Industrial plant bakery mixing room: mixer operator charges a 1,000+ lb mixer — bulk flour and sugar from silos/day bins, metered water and ice, plus pre-scaled minor ingredients hand-added from bags and totes on a schedule tied to the divider line.

Supermarket in-store bakery back room: baker cuts and dumps a 50-lb bag of cake/donut/bread mix into a floor planetary mixer bowl, adds measured water, oil and eggs from jugs, then attaches the bowl and starts the mixer; several different mixes per morning.

Small retail bakery, cafe or restaurant pastry station: many small varied batches (cookie dough, buttercream, batter, meringue) combined in a 12–20 qt planetary bowl from deli containers, blocks of butter, cracked eggs and small scaled bags; recipes and sequence change constantly.

Institutional bakery (school district commissary, hospital or correctional kitchen): scheduled sheet-cake/roll batches combined in a 60–80 qt floor mixer from cases of pre-scaled mix and metered liquids, standard equipment and fixed daily production plan.

tasks.label: Check the quality of raw materials to ensure that standards and specifications are met.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-store/retail bakery (supermarket or independent shop): a mixed delivery arrives at the back door — sacks of flour and sugar, cases of eggs, tubs of shortening/icing, chilled butter and cream. Baker opens cases, checks packaging integrity, date codes, chill temperature, cracked or soiled eggs, torn or wet sacks, and accepts or rejects the load.

Bench check of dry ingredients immediately before mixing: flour/sugar/cocoa scooped or tipped out, checked for lumping, caking, off odor, discoloration, insect fragments or weevils, foreign material, and conformity to the specified grade before it goes into the mixer.

Functional/sensory check of fats, liquids and leaveners: butter or shortening temperature and plasticity by feel, cream/milk smelled and tasted for souring, yeast proofed in warm water to confirm activity, chocolate/couverture checked for bloom and tempering behavior.
Fresh produce and fillings check: cases of berries, apples, bananas, or cut fruit examined for mold, rot, bruising, ripeness and size before use in pies, tarts and decorating.

Wholesale/industrial bakery incoming lot inspection: a bulk flour tanker or pallet lot arrives; a representative sample is drawn, moisture/protein/ash checked against spec and the certificate of analysis, foreign material and infestation screened, and the lot released to a silo or quarantined.
Dry-store and walk-in stock check: walking the ingredient store to verify date codes and stock rotation, spotting swollen, leaking or damp packaging, pest evidence, and pulling out-of-spec stock.

sources.claim: TOMRA's commercial optical sorters inspect and physically eject defective berries and fruit — mold, decay, unripe fruit, bruising, foreign material — on processing/packing lines, running autonomously at line speed.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content as a baker's fruit-quality check (mold, rot, unripe, foreign material), performed on the same raw materials, but with the fruit presented on a purpose-built sorting line.

sources.transferJustification: Directly the raw-material quality check a baker/miller performs on incoming grain and dry ingredients (discoloration, insect damage, foreign material), but with material presented in a flowing stream to the machine.

tasks.label: Roll, knead, cut, or shape dough to form sweet rolls, pie crusts, tarts, cookies, or other products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale/industrial bakery plant: baker tends the makeup line producing high-volume standard items — dough sheeted, divided, rounded, moulded into loaves and buns, croissant dough laminated/cut/rolled, cookie dough deposited or wire-cut, pie shells pressed. Supermarket in-store bakery: baker works from mixes, pre-portioned or frozen dough — cutting and panning cookie dough, rolling and fitting pie/tart shells, forming sweet rolls and dinner rolls, running a bench sheeter or divider/rounder, during retail hours in a fixed-layout back-of-store bakery.

Restaurant, hotel or institutional pastry station: small varied batches changing daily — rolling pie crusts and tart shells into assorted pans, cutting cookies, shaping sweet rolls and turnovers — on a shared kitchen bench amid other cooks, with frequent product changeovers.

Custom and decorative hand shaping to order in a retail bakery: braided challah and holiday loaves, woven lattice pie tops, hand-formed novelty and seasonal shapes, sculpted or crimped decorative edges, produced in small numbers to a design set that day.

Commercial bakery or grocery commissary batch finishing station: worker rolls racks of sheet pans/trays of baked cookies, scones, brownies or buns to a bench and drizzles/spreads icing or glaze on each piece, returning trays to racks; hundreds of pieces per rack, repetitive, done alongside other staff.

In-store supermarket bakery: base-icing and smoothing buttercream on round and sheet cakes with a spatula/turntable (thawed shells or freshly baked layers), plus icing thaw-and-sell items; 10-40 cakes per shift, standard pan sizes, staff and carts moving through a small back room.

Retail/artisan bakery or pastry shop: brushing egg wash on trays of hand-shaped croissants, breads and danish before bake; brushing apricot glaze on fruit tarts; drizzling icing on cinnamon rolls; many SKUs, small batches, frequent changeovers, hand-formed items of varying size on shared benches.

Restaurant, hotel or institutional pastry kitchen: à-la-carte and small-batch finishing — brushing butter or syrup on rolls and cake layers, pouring/spreading glaze or ganache on individual desserts and entremets — done at a crowded shared kitchen station, on demand, on varied plated or racked items.

tasks.label: Order or receive supplies or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small retail or in-store bakery, pre-order stock check: before the twice-weekly order the baker walks the dry store, walk-in cooler and freezer, counts flour, sugar, butter, fillings, boxes and liners against par levels and the coming production schedule, then submits the order to a distributor by phone, order guide or web portal.

Independent retail bakery / restaurant pastry kitchen, receiving a mixed distributor delivery at the back door (no dock): 20-40 line items hand-stacked on a two-wheeler - 50 lb flour and sugar sacks, cases of butter, eggs and cream, pails of filling, cartons of packaging. Baker checks each line against the invoice, inspects for damage and cold-chain temperature, signs, then hand-carries and stacks the goods into dry storage, cooler and freezer with FIFO rotation.

Supermarket in-store bakery: a pallet or rolltainer of frozen dough cases, icing pails, cake boxes and film arrives from the store's receiving dock; the bakery clerk verifies items against the invoice/order guide, breaks the load down, wheels cases through the backroom into the bakery freezer, cooler and dry rack, and rotates existing stock.

Wholesale/commercial bakery plant warehouse: an inbound truck delivers pallets of flour, sugar, shortening and packaging (or a bulk flour tanker); the receiver checks the bill of lading, lot codes and COA, unloads pallets with a forklift, inspects for damage and pest/temperature issues, records receipt into the inventory system and puts pallets away in warehouse racking or the cooler.

Receiving equipment and non-ingredient items: a crated 60-qt mixer or new proofer part, a bundle of sheet pans, or parcels of decorating and cleaning supplies arrive; the baker uncrates and unpacks, inspects for damage and completeness against the packing slip, reports shortages or damage to the vendor, and moves the item into position in the shop or stores it.

sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously traverses store aisles and captures real-time shelf-level data on ... and placement; it is deployed across 17 Harmons grocery stores and feeds replenishment workflows, replacing manual stock verification by associates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inventory verification driving replenishment in a grocery store. The physical part of a baker's ordering instance is exactly this - traversing the storage area and establishing what is on hand and below par so the order can be generated.

sources.system: Symbotic system
sources.title: Walmart to Expand Deployment of Symbotic Supply Chain Automation to 25 Distribution Centers - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Symbotic's robotic system, deployed in Walmart regional distribution centers, automates intake, storage, sorting and palletizing of cases inside a purpose-built automated storage structure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated goods intake and putaway to storage. Provides the storage-side completion of a receiving instance when cases are presented to the machine in a purpose-built structure.

tasks.label: Operate slicing or wrapping machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale/industrial bakery: baker-operator runs an inline bread slicer-bagger on a pan-bread packaging line. Cooled loaves arrive on conveyor from the cooler; the machine slices, bags and closes them; the operator monitors slice quality and bag seal/closure, keeps bag wickets/clip stock supplied, and clears occasional jams or crushed loaves.

Wholesale/commissary bakery: operating a wrapping machine (horizontal flow wrapper, overwrapper or tray sealer) for buns, cookies, cakes or pastries — product presented on trays/belt is loaded into the wrapper infeed, film reel and seal settings monitored, seals and pack appearance checked, rejects removed.

Supermarket in-store bakery: baker takes cooled loaves off a rack, hand-feeds them one at a time into a countertop reciprocating/gravity slicer, bags each loaf, applies a Kwik-Lok tag or twist tie and price label; mixed loaf types and sizes, shared bench, other staff and customers nearby.

Retail/artisan bakery or bakery counter: slicing crusty, irregular artisan loaves (boules, batards, seeded breads) to order at the counter or in small batches, at varying slice thickness, then bagging and tying for the customer.

Changeover/setup on the slicer or wrapper between products: adjust blade spacing/slice thickness, infeed guides, bag or film size, seal temperature and scoop/bag tension; thread a new film reel or load bag wickets; run and check first pieces before releasing the run.

End-of-run cleaning, sanitation and minor maintenance of the slicer/wrapper: remove crumb build-up, clean and de-gum blades, change or tension a broken blade, wipe/wash down guarding and sealing jaws to food-safety standard.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR10 cobot with Soft Robotics mGrip gripper, integrated by Revtech Systèmes at Boulangerie La Fabrique
sources.developer: Universal Robots / Soft Robotics / Revtech Systèmes
sources.title: How a Canadian bakery automated its bread packaging line
sources.claim: A deployed robotic packaging cell at an artisan bakery picks baked loaves of varying shape and size off a conveyor and loads them into a bagging machine, triggered automatically by a photoeye and PLC (no operator in the loop).
sources.transferJustification: Directly the bagging half of the task, with artisan loaves that 'vary a lot in shape and dimensions'; the robot performs the loaf-handling into the packaging machine that the human operator otherwise does.

sources.system: Schubert TLM line with F4 pick-and-place robots and Flowmodul flow-wrappers at More Than A Bakery, Versailles, KY
sources.title: Efficient Packing Line Fuels Bakery Growth | Baking Business
sources.claim: A US wholesale bakery has run a fully automated flow-wrapping line since spring 2024 in which vision-guided pick-and-place robots feed four integrated flow-wrapping modules at >1,700 products/min, replacing operators who previously fed the packaging equipment by hand.

sources.system: AMF PackTech Combo 75S Bread Slicer & Bagger
sources.title: AMF PackTech Combo 75S Bread Slicer & Bagger
sources.claim: Commercially sold combination bread slicer/bagger automates the whole slice-and-bag operation for a variety of loaves and bag sizes, with recipe-driven automatic pre-operational adjustment of guides, blade spacing, infeed phaser, ... scoop opening.

sources.system: AMF PackTech Combo 75S Bread Slicer & Bagger
sources.title: Automated Packaging in Industrial Bread Bakeries - AMF Bakery Systems
sources.claim: The same slicer/bagger performs product changeover automatically within about a minute, recalling preset recipes and blade spacing so setups are consistent from crew to crew.

sources.system: Syntegon (Bosch Packaging) Delta robot feeding Pack 102 flow wrapper
sources.title: Product handling systems evolve | Snack Food & Wholesale Bakery
sources.claim: Vision-guided delta robots pick baked goods directly from baking trays and place them into the infeed chain ... a horizontal flow wrapper, automating the wrapper-loading step.

sources.system: Bakisto (FANUC cobot + WIESHEU TrayMotion oven + Wanzl BakeOff i)
sources.title: Robots in the Bakery | IFR case study
sources.claim: The most advanced in-store (supermarket) bakery robot shown to date is a prototype cobot that loads/unloads baking trays and stocks display compartments; it does not slice or bag bread, and it was presented as a trade-show prototype rather than a deployed system.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest in-store-bakery (E2) robotic system; it handles trays and display stocking, not slicing or wrapping, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at E2.

sources.system: JAC SWIFT / VARIA / SELF in-store bread slicers
sources.title: Automated slicers help instore bakeries 'level up' | Supermarket Perimeter
sources.claim: In-store bakery slicing remains a human- or customer-fed operation: retail slicers are designed for a person to load each loaf, with self-service models letting customers slice and bag their own bread.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the in-store variant of the task and that no robotic loaf-handling exists there; used only to bound the E2 judgment, not to support one.

tasks.label: Develop new recipes for baked goods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Artisan/retail bakery: head baker develops a new bread or laminated pastry — sets a concept, writes baker's percentages, mixes and ferments small trial doughs on shop equipment over several days, judges dough handling, crumb, crust, flavor and aroma by hand and by tasting, adjusts hydration/fermentation/inclusions, and finalizes a scalable formula and process sheet the shop can produce daily.

Supermarket or franchise in-store bakery: baker creates a seasonal or limited-time item by varying a corporate base formula or scratch/frozen dough (new flavor, filling, topping, decoration), test-bakes a few trays in the store's ovens, gathers manager and customer feedback, checks cost and available SKUs, and documents the finished recipe and bake schedule.

Wholesale/industrial bakery R&D test bakery: product-development baker formulates a new item to a brief (cost, clean label, shelf life, allergen limits), runs bench trials and pilot-line trials, uses lab instruments (dough rheology, water activity, texture) plus tasting, iterates the formula and process, presents to a sensory panel, then scales it to the plant line.

Cottage/home-based bakery, caterer or food-truck baker: develops a custom or dietary-restricted recipe (e.g., gluten-free or vegan wedding cake flavor) in a home or rented kitchen with non-standard equipment and whatever ingredients are on hand, iterating over trial bakes and client tastings until the client approves.

Restaurant/hotel pastry kitchen: pastry chef develops a new dessert, viennoiserie or house bread for the menu, improvising with kitchen ingredients between services, adjusting sweetness, texture, plating and pairing through repeated tastings with the executive chef, and writing the final spec for line cooks.

sources.system: BakeBot (Willow Garage PR2)
sources.title: A Robot That Bakes Cookies — CCC Blog
sources.claim: MIT CSAIL's BakeBot (PR2) baked cookies autonomously in a lab kitchen, but it executed a hard-coded recipe: it located ingredients by vision and mixed, portioned and baked according to fixed instructions, with no ability to invent or iteratively revise a formula.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic execution of a baking recipe in a laboratory kitchen. It bears on recipe development only as the test-baking step; the system cannot generate a formula, evaluate it against sensory targets, or revise it, so it does not carry over to the whole task.

sources.system: Cambridge robot chef (Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory)
sources.title: Taste of the future: robot chef learns to 'taste as you go' | University of Cambridge
sources.claim: The Cambridge/Beko robot 'chef' used a salinity probe on a robot arm to assess seasoning of scrambled-egg dishes at chewing stages, and an earlier version tuned omelettes using human tasters' feedback; it is a laboratory demonstration limited to one taste dimension of simple cooked dishes, not autonomous development of new baked-goods recipes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop robotic tuning of a cooked dish using instrumental taste feedback. It is the nearest published analogue to recipe iteration, but it optimizes salt level in a fixed simple dish under lab conditions, with no dough handling, baking, or multi-attribute sensory acceptance.

sources.system: Milli-fluidic robotic formulation platform with TSEMO active learning
sources.developer: Academic food process engineering group (Innovative Food Science & Emerging Technologies)
sources.title: Optimization of complex food formulations using robotics and active learning - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A milli-fluidic robotic platform performed fully automated dosing, mixing and analysis of liquid food formulations in a closed loop with a multi-objective optimization algorithm, optimizing whey-protein aggregation against turbidity/viscosity targets in a laboratory — automated formulation of liquid model systems, not creation of an accepted baked-goods recipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous closed-loop formulation optimization in a purpose-built lab. It handles pumpable liquids optimized to instrument-measured physical targets; it does not mix or ferment dough, bake, or judge eating quality, so it does not substantiate whole-task bakery recipe development.

sources.system: BreadBot
sources.title: Bread-baking robot charms customers at local store | Tri-Cities Area Journal of Business
sources.claim: Deployed automated bakery machines such as Wilkinson Baking Company's BreadBot produce loaves unattended in grocery stores from pre-supplied bread mix, running a fixed set of programmed varieties; the machine reproduces recipes rather than developing them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended commercial bread production in a retail store. It shows that deployed bakery automation is fixed-recipe execution from prepared mixes, which does not transfer to conceiving and iterating a new formula.

sources.system: AI recipe/flavor development software in food R&D (McCormick flavor AI, Unilever digital recipe testing)
sources.title: AI startups want to crack open the recipe book in Big Food's test kitchens - CNBC
sources.claim: In large food companies, AI is used for digital recipe screening and flavor development while the physical trial work remains in human-staffed test kitchens; the reported systems are software, not embodied machines that mix, bake and evaluate trial batches.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the same task in industrial R&D: the automation in use is software-only and therefore cannot support a positive robotic judgment; the physical bench and pilot trials are still executed by human product developers.

roles.title: Butchers and Meat Cutters
roles.description: Cut, trim, or prepare consumer-sized portions of meat for use or sale in retail establishments.

tasks.label: Prepare and place meat cuts and products in display counter to appear attractive and catch the shopper's eye.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket self-service multideck meat case: butcher/meat cutter wheels a cart of freshly wrapped foam trays (ground beef chubs, chicken packs, pork chops, case-ready steaks) onto the sales floor, loads them into the open refrigerated case by planogram, fronts and faces the packages, rotates older product forward, and pulls out-of-date or leaking packs. Done during store hours around shoppers, in a cold, wet-floor department.

Full-service glass display counter at a supermarket or grocery meat department: arranging loose fresh cuts (ribeyes, chops, roasts, ground beef mounds, poultry pieces) on stainless display pans, fanning/shingling cuts so the eye of the steak shows, spacing pans, adding parsley/garnish and price cards, and refilling gaps through the day as customers buy from the case.

Value-added/further-processed items prepared for display: skewering kabobs, marinating or seasoning cuts, stuffing chicken breasts or pinwheels, coiling fresh sausage, then laying these items out on trays or in the case as an eye-catching feature group.

Weekend/holiday feature and promotional display build: bulk-stacking value packs, family packs, whole turkeys, prime rib roasts or grilling bundles into the case ends, bunkers or an endcap display, arranging by price point, and setting POS signage and ad tags.

Independent/whole-animal butcher shop counter: a small shop where the day's available cuts vary with what carcasses were broken, and the butcher lays out an entirely new counter each morning — steaks, house sausages, charcuterie, offal, marinated items — changing composition and layout to match stock and to draw walk-in customers.

sources.system: Marel RoboBatcher Flex for Meat
sources.title: RoboBatcher Flex for Meat | Marel
sources.claim: Marel's RoboBatcher Flex is a commercial robotic cell that batches and places whole-muscle meat portions (e.g., boneless pork chops, striploin steaks) into retail trays with controlled 'styling' — i.e., the attractive, repeatable arrangement of cuts in the presentation pack.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tray styling of retail meat portions on a packing line. It handles the same objects (raw whole-muscle cuts) with the same objective as the task's core act — laying cuts into a presentation pan so the arrangement looks right to a shopper — at the same precision, differing only in that the pan is presented on a fixtured conveyor rather than in a store case.

sources.system: Marel RoboPacker for Meat
sources.title: RoboPacker for Meat | Marel
sources.claim: Marel's RoboPacker is a commercial robotic catch-weight tray packer for meat whose selling point is gripper technology that produces good 'styling' (product appearance) in the finished tray.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of variable-weight meat pieces into retail trays. The appearance of the packed tray is the acceptance criterion, as it is for a display pan, and the objects (soft, variable, wet raw meat) are identical.

sources.system: JLS Automation Osprey
sources.title: Tray Loading | JLS Automation
sources.claim: JLS Automation's vision-guided Osprey pick-and-place robot loads wrapped meat trays (MAP trays and vacuum-skin packs) at high speed into cases according to a specified placement and orientation, including shingling them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided loading of overwrapped retail meat packages into an ordered, oriented array. This is the same manipulation as loading a self-service case shelf — same objects (film-wrapped foam/VSP meat trays), same requirement that labels face out and packs sit in a neat pattern — with the receptacle fixtured instead of a store shelf.

sources.system: JLS Automation Talon
sources.title: JLS Automation showcases integrated patty packaging system at IPPE | The National Provisioner
sources.claim: JLS Automation's hygienic Talon robot performs primary loading of raw protein (patties) directly into retail trays on a tray-sealing line, shown as an integrated commercial system at the 2025 IPPE trade show.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: gentle robotic placement of raw meat items into a retail tray. Ground/formed meat products are among the items a butcher lays into a display pan; the handling delicacy and placement accuracy required are comparable.

sources.system: Pintro Fully Automatic Skewer Machine (Pick & Skewer)
sources.title: Fully Automatic Skewer machine - PINTRO EN
sources.claim: Fully automatic skewering lines commercially produce kabobs by threading raw or marinated meat and vegetables from feed conveyors onto skewers, i.e., the preparation step for value-added display items is machine-executed on a fixtured production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly of skewered value-added meat products. It covers the 'prepare' half of preparing kabobs for display; the subsequent laying-out into trays is covered by the Marel/JLS tray-styling evidence for the same product class.

sources.system: TX SCARA (with GORDON AI)
sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores | NVIDIA Blog
sources.claim: The only manipulation robot deployed at scale on a retail sales floor for restocking a refrigerated display is Telexistence's TX SCARA, which is rail-mounted and restocks bottles and cans only, using cameras and AI to decide what to replenish; it does not handle fresh meat packages.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the in-store (E2) case: the only proven store-floor restocking robot works on rigid, uniform bottles and cans on a fixed rail, not on floppy overwrapped meat trays requiring date rotation and appearance-driven arrangement, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: Simbe Tally
sources.title: New robotic capability lets retailers remotely monitor store shelves | Grocery Dive
sources.claim: Retail-floor robots deployed across US grocery chains (Simbe Tally) are sensing-only: they navigate aisles and photograph shelves to report out-of-stocks, with no arm and no ability to place product.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a negative bound on E2: the widely deployed US grocery-floor robot performs no manipulation, so it cannot fill or dress a meat case.

sources.system: Mobile-manipulator supermarket stocking system (ROS2 / Nav2 / YOLO+SAM2)
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: End-to-End Algorithmic Control of a Mobile Manipulator for Supermarket Stocking and Fronting (arXiv:2509.11740)
sources.claim: Autonomous shelf stocking and fronting inside a supermarket by a mobile manipulator remains a research-stage integration problem, with human traffic, tight aisles and varied product geometry cited as unsolved challenges.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a negative bound on E2: in-store autonomous stocking is a demo, not a worker-quality deployment, and the paper does not address fresh-meat packages or display merchandising.

tasks.label: Wrap, weigh, label, and price cuts of meat.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket meat-department back room / prepack station: butcher arranges freshly cut steaks, chops and roasts on foam trays, runs each tray through a hand or automatic film wrapper, weighs it on the scale-printer, applies the weight/price/UPC label, and carries the packs out to the display case. Mixed cuts, changing sizes, wet washdown room, staff moving through.

Store or club-store bulk packaging: ground beef into chubs or family packs, value packs and vacuum-sealed subprimals/roasts; product bagged or tray-sealed, weighed on a catch-weight scale, priced and labeled, then boxed or cased for the display.

Service counter at a supermarket or independent butcher shop: customer asks for a given quantity or number of cuts; butcher weighs the portion on the counter scale, wraps it in butcher paper or film, prints the weight/price label, sticks it on, and hands the parcel over during a queue.

In-plant case-ready / further-processing packaging line: portioned steaks, chops or ground product conveyed to tray loading or thermoforming, sealed, then run through an inline weigh-price labeler at high rate; cartons weighed and labeled for shipment to stores.

Custom-exempt or locker plant / game processing: whole-animal customer orders cut into varied packages, wrapped in freezer paper or vacuum bags, weighed, hand-labeled with cut name, date and customer name, then boxed and sorted per customer for pickup.

sources.system: Ishida WM-Ai / WM-Nano automatic wrapper (Rice Lake Retail Solutions)
sources.title: Wrappers | Rice Lake Weighing Systems
sources.claim: Ishida WM-Ai and WM-Nano automatic tray wrappers, sold through Rice Lake Retail Solutions, tare the tray, weigh the meat, apply stretch film and apply the weight/price label automatically at up to 35 packs per minute; they are installed in supermarket back rooms and prepack stations, with the operator placing trays on the infeed conveyor.

sources.system: Ishida WM-Ai automatic wrapper
sources.title: Wrappers | Rice Lake Weighing Systems (customer use cases)
sources.claim: WM-Ai automatic wrappers are in daily use in retail meat departments, e.g. Sun Foods and Dragon Star ... in Saint Paul, Minnesota, wrapping the store's cuts of meat.

sources.system: RoboBatcher Flex (Meat)
sources.title: RoboBatcher Flex for Meat | Marel
sources.claim: Marel/JBT RoboBatcher Flex for Meat weighs and vision-inspects each incoming portion and uses robot arms to place boneless pork chops or striploin steaks into retail trays to fixed-weight targets and pre-programmed styles, at up to 240 portions per minute, in meat processing packing lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: weight-batching and tray-loading of retail meat portions. It covers the weighing and tray-presentation steps of this task on the same objects (raw steaks/chops of varying size) at retail-pack precision, immediately upstream of sealing and labeling.

sources.system: JLS Talon primary loading system (with Smart Vision Works SiftAI)
sources.title: Robot and Cobot Technology Transform Food Operations | Food Engineering
sources.claim: JLS Automation's vision-guided Talon pick-and-place robot loads raw proteins, including steaks, into thermoformed packs, MAP or foam trays, flow wrappers and vacuum skin packs in washdown food plants; a working line loading steaks into a thermoformer with AI cut recognition was shown at IPPE 2023.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic loading of raw meat cuts into the retail package that is then sealed. This is the 'wrap' step of this task on identical objects (raw steaks) with retail-pack placement accuracy, in the same washdown setting.

sources.system: Automatic weigh, price, labeling systems (Bizerba, Ishida, Marel and others)
sources.title: Processors embrace automation in weighing & labeling | The National Provisioner
sources.claim: Automatic weigh-price-label machines are standard, increasingly fully automatic equipment in case-ready meat plants and deli packaging, running catch-weight product at more than 150 packs per ..., applying labels top and bottom with vision verification of label presence, position and print.

sources.system: Bizerba GLM-I 170 / GLM-Emaxx automac weigh price labelers
sources.title: High-end modular weigh price labeling system | Bizerba GLM-I 170
sources.claim: Bizerba GLM-I series modular weigh price labeling systems automatically weigh and label pre-packaged variable-weight food (meat, cold cuts) in industrial food operations, and the GLM-Emaxx automac is combined with packaging machines for supermarket-destined variable-weight meat packs.

sources.system: CRYOVAC AutoLoad R2 Robotic Bag Loader / automated bag loaders
sources.title: CRYOVAC Equipment – Automatic Bag Loaders – Sealed Air
sources.claim: Sealed Air's CRYOVAC AutoLoad R2 robotic bag loader automatically inserts heavy products such as primal meat cuts and roasts into vacuum bags ahead of vacuum sealing, as part of integrated lines that also include label printers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bagging of bulk/primal meat before vacuum sealing. It is the wrapping step for bulk cuts on the same objects, feeding the vacuum sealer and weigh-price labeler that finish the pack.

sources.system: KUKA meat processing robot automation
sources.title: Automated solutions for meat processing | KUKA Global
sources.claim: KUKA supplies robot lines for meat plants that portion-package meat into plastic trays, thermoform packs or tubular bags, seal them, label them correctly for the supermarket, and then case-pack the labeled packs.

tasks.label: Cut, trim, bone, tie, and grind meats, such as beef, pork, poultry, and fish, to prepare in cooking form.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket / big-box retail meat department: cutter opens boxed beef and pork subprimals (strip loins, top rounds, pork loins, briskets), trims fat and silverskin on a cutting table, cuts steaks/chops/roasts by eye and on a band saw, and grinds accumulated trim into ground beef at a target lean point, to the chain's cut specs and case plan.

Retail poultry and fish work: cutting whole chickens into 8-piece packs, boning breasts and thighs, skinning, and filleting/portioning fish (salmon, cod) for the service case; species and sizes vary through the day.

Wholesale/industrial fabrication floor (packing house, case-ready plant, further-processing plant): high-volume repetitive boning and trimming at a station on a moving line - pork hams and shoulders deboned, loins boned, lamb/pork primals broken, trim sorted to grinders.

Specialty/custom butcher shop, pork and lamb: breaking hanging half carcasses into primals and retail cuts, deboning shoulders and legs, tying rolled roasts and porchetta with string, grinding trim for sausage.

Specialty shop / small locker plant, beef: breaking hindquarters and forequarters, boning chucks, rounds and ribs into customer-specified cuts (varying thickness, roast sizes, bone-in vs boneless) for individual custom-kill orders, then tying roasts and grinding the balance into hamburger.

Foodservice/institutional butcher (restaurant, hotel, club store, commissary kitchen): trimming whole beef tenderloins, ribeyes and pork loins, cutting steaks and cutlets to portion weight, tying roasts, grinding trim for burgers, in a stainless prep area shared with cooks.

sources.system: HAMDAS-R / HAMDAS-RX and WANDAS-RX deboning robots
sources.date: 2024 (in plant use since the 2010s; page current 2024-2025)
sources.title: Deboning machines | Products | MAYEKAWA Global (MYCOM)
sources.claim: Mayekawa's HAMDAS-R/RX is a six-axis robotic machine that automatically debones pork hams (about 500/hour) after pre-cutting, using auto-measurement and image processing; WANDAS-RX does pork shoulders. Used in pork plants.
sources.transferJustification: Same task elements (boning and trimming pork legs/shoulders with knives) as a butcher performs, but executed in a fixtured machine cell rather than at a human bench.

sources.system: HAMDAS-RX; Scott Automation robotic scribing saw
sources.title: A review of robotic and automated systems in meat processing (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review confirms HAMDAS-RX performs automated pork ham deboning including hipbone/tailbone extraction and left/right discrimination, and that Scott's robotic scribing-saw systems cut beef using sensing of position and shape.

sources.system: Scott Automation LEAP primal/middle/forequarter lamb cutting system
sources.title: One giant LEAP for robo meatworks - Farmers Weekly
sources.claim: Scott Automation's LEAP primal, middle and forequarter system - X-ray and vision guided robotic cutting cells - was installed and commissioned in Silver Fern Farms' Finegand lamb plant, automating primal and subprimal cutting of lamb carcasses (humans still bone hindquarters).
sources.transferJustification: Breaking carcasses into primals and subprimals is the cutting/boning work of a butcher, here performed autonomously in enclosed robotic cells on a boning-room line.

sources.system: I-Cut 55/56/130 portion cutters in case-ready whole muscle steak line
sources.title: Case-ready Whole Muscle Steak Line | JBT Marel
sources.claim: JBT Marel supplies commercial case-ready whole-muscle steak lines in which an I-Cut vision-controlled portioning machine slices primals into fixed-weight retail steaks for supermarket packs.
sources.transferJustification: Produces exactly the retail-cut output a supermarket meat cutter produces (fixed-weight steaks from subprimals), but with the primal conveyed into a scanning/cutting machine.

sources.system: MARELEC PORTIO B bone-in portion cutter
sources.title: Portion Cutter PORTIO B - MARELEC
sources.claim: Marelec PORTIO B is a commercial fixed-weight portion cutter that scans bone-in pork loins with three camera/laser units and cuts them into bone-in chops of target weight.
sources.transferJustification: Bone-in chop cutting on a band saw is a core retail butcher operation; this machine performs the same cut automatically on a fixtured infeed.

sources.system: Collaborative meat-cutting robot arm (Losey et al.)
sources.title: Safely and autonomously cutting meat with a collaborative robot arm (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: A Virginia Tech system used a 6-DoF collaborative arm with knife instrumentation and vision to autonomously slice pork loins into chops, trim fat, and cube meat after a human placed the meat; industry experts rated performance on average as adequate.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task's operations (slicing chops, trimming fat, cubing) on retail-scale pork loins, though at proof-of-concept quality and with the workpiece presented to the arm.

sources.system: ACM-NT automatic cut-up and automated in-line deboning systems
sources.title: Poultry Processing Tech: Innovative automation | MEAT+POULTRY
sources.claim: Marel/JBT Marel supplies automated in-line poultry cut-up (ACM-NT) and deboning systems that convert whole birds into parts and boneless breast/thigh fillets in commercial poultry plants.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting whole chickens into parts and deboning them is the poultry portion of this task; here done autonomously on shackle lines.

sources.system: BAADER 189 Pro / 192 filleting machines; Marel FleXicut
sources.title: BAADER Showcasing Future-Ready Fish Processing Solutions at Seafood Processing Global (SPG) 2024
sources.claim: BAADER whitefish filleting machines (e.g., 189 Pro, 192) automatically head, gut and fillet fish, and Marel's X-ray-guided FleXicut waterjet system automatically pinbones and trims fillets in commercial plants.
sources.transferJustification: Filleting and pinboning fish is the fish element of this task; these machines do it automatically on a conveyed, fixtured infeed.

sources.system: Weiler Dominator 14 mixer grinder with inline fat analysis
sources.title: Provisur's Weiler Mixer Grinder Dominator 14 Can Now Have an Inline Reclaim System | Food Engineering
sources.claim: Provisur's Weiler Dominator mixer/grinders run automated grinding with inline fat analysis that adjusts lean/fat additions to hit target grind specifications; in use at commercial beef processors such as FPL Food.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'grind meats' element to a target lean point, the same output a butcher's grinder produces.

sources.system: Inox Meccanica automatic tying machines; TIPPER TIE TN2004/TN3004 netting-clipping systems
sources.title: Automatic Meat Tying Machines - Perfect for String Tying | Inox Meccanica
sources.claim: Automatic string-tying machines commercially tie roasts, porchetta and loins with continuous or single-knot loops; Tipper Tie TN-series machines automatically net and clip whole-muscle products.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'tie' element of the task on the same products (rolled roasts, loins) a butcher ties by hand.

sources.system: LEAP4Beef automated beef boning program
sources.developer: Scott Automation & Robotics with AMPC/MLA/JBS Australia
sources.title: World's first fully-automated beef boning program a step closer - Beef Central

tasks.label: Prepare special cuts of meat ordered by customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket service counter: a customer asks for four ribeyes cut 1.5 inches thick (or a specific weight) off a boneless subprimal. The cutter pulls the loin from the cooler, trims the fat cap to spec, slices the steaks, weighs, wraps and labels them while the customer waits.

Bone-in special order needing the band saw: thick-cut bone-in pork chops, T-bones/porterhouses off a short loin, cross-cut beef shanks, short ribs cut flanken-style, or soup/marrow bones cut to length. Sawing through bone to a requested thickness without shattering bone or leaving dust on the meat.

Custom grind and cube orders: chuck ground fresh to order at a requested lean point, a custom brisket/short-rib burger blend, stew meat cubed to a stated size, or kabob cubes trimmed of gristle from a whole muscle.

Poultry and other proteins to order: deboning chicken thighs or a whole bird, spatchcocking, skinning and trimming breasts, cutting a turkey breast in half, portioning a fish/pork tenderloin, for a customer waiting at the counter.
Presentation trimming: frenching a rack of lamb or pork, or cleaning the rib bones on a standing rib roast so the bones are bare to a set length for a customer's holiday order.

Complex bespoke work: crown roast tied from two frenched racks, butterflied leg of lamb, pocketed/stuffed and netted rolled roast, seam-boning an odd cut for an ethnic or whole-animal order, or splitting and reworking a primal to an unusual customer specification.

tasks.label: Receive, inspect, and store meat upon delivery to ensure meat quality.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket/grocery meat department: a distributor truck arrives at the store's back dock with a mixed load of vacuum-packed boxed subprimals and case-ready trays on carts/pallets. The cutter counts cases against the invoice, probes/IR-checks product temperature, inspects boxes for crushing, leaks, purge, off-color and dates, accepts or rejects items, then hand-stacks the cases into the walk-in cooler in FIFO rotation and logs receiving temperatures.

High-volume store or warehouse club: full pallets of case-ready/frozen meat delivered on a pallet jack or forklift; verify pallet count and labels against the manifest, check trailer and product temperature, look for thawed/leaking cases and damaged stretch wrap, then move the pallet into the refrigerated holding room and stage/rotate it.

Independent butcher shop or specialty market: primals in boxes, or hanging beef/pork sides, delivered at a narrow back door or curb; carry or rail-hang the product into the cooler, judge quality by sight and smell (color, bloom, fat cover, marbling, odor, bone condition), reject substandard product with the driver, and hang/stack for aging or rotation.

Foodservice/institutional meat cutter (hotel, restaurant group, commissary, college dining): receipt at a shared dock, HACCP receiving log with probe temperatures per item, check-in against the purchase order, credit/reject paperwork with the driver, and put-away into a walk-in cooler/freezer with date labeling and rotation.

Non-standard receipt: a local farm or small supplier's van pulls up at the curb or the product is picked up off-site; mixed, variably packaged and often unlabeled cuts in coolers or totes; count against a handwritten sheet, judge temperature and freshness by hand and smell, then carry the product inside and store it.

tasks.label: Shape, lace, and tie roasts, using boning knife, skewer, and twine.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket back-room meat department: butcher takes boneless subprimals (pork loin, eye of round, chuck/shoulder), trims with a boning knife, rolls fat cap out, and ties a series of twine loops plus a lengthwise tie at set intervals, producing 6–30 uniform rolled roasts per shift for the retail case. Cold, wet, tiled cutting room with a standard block/table and saw; sizes and shapes vary piece to piece.

Case-ready or further-processing plant: production run of uniform rolled roasts (roast beef, boneless ham, pork loin roast) laid up and secured with twine or elastic netting at line rate, hundreds to thousands per shift, to a spec diameter and tie spacing.

Independent butcher shop or small locker plant, custom order: boned leg of lamb or pork shoulder rolled and tied, porchetta-style or stuffed-and-rolled loin, bacon-wrapped roast; sizes vary with the customer's order and the carcass, done a few at a time between other counter work.

Structural/bone-related tying: rib roast tied back against its own chined rib bones, tenderloin tail folded and tied under, boned leg tied around the cavity left by the bone — the twine must be placed relative to bones and cavities, not just around a cylinder.

Presentation specialties, mostly seasonal: crown roast of pork or lamb formed from frenched racks and laced with twine and skewers, or a stuffed pocket roast closed with skewers and laced shoelace-style; low volume, high visual standard.

tasks.label: Supervise other butchers or meat cutters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Head meat cutter in a supermarket meat department directs 2-4 cutters and wrappers: assigns the daily cut list and case-fill priorities, checks the appearance and portioning of finished trays, tells a cutter to re-work or re-price an item, and reassigns people as customer demand shifts.

Cut-floor or fabrication-room supervisor in a meat processing/packing plant oversees a line crew: monitors line pace and yields, spot-checks trim quality and knife technique, enforces sanitation/HACCP and PPE rules, and calls out corrections during the shift.

Owner or lead butcher in an independent retail shop oversees an apprentice or junior cutter: watches a breakdown, verbally corrects technique and yield, assigns which primals to work next, and approves the finished product before it goes into the case.

Administrative supervision away from the block: writing schedules and break rotations, running crew huddles, delivering performance feedback and discipline, documenting safety and food-safety training, and coordinating staffing with the store or plant manager.

Lead cutter in a warehouse-club or grocery-fulfillment meat room coordinates a small crew against production quotas, resolves equipment or supply problems with other departments, and signs off on output volumes and shrink.

tasks.label: Cure, smoke, tenderize, and preserve meat.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket meat department back room: cutter mechanically tenderizes/cubes beef rounds, chucks or pork cutlets on the department's cuber/tenderizer, hand-feeding irregular pieces one at a time between other cutting jobs, catching output and staging it for trays.

Retail meat department or butcher shop value-added program: seasoning/marinating portions (marinated chicken breasts, rubbed pork chops, kabob meat, fajita strips) by applying rub or marinade, hand-mixing or small-tumbling, holding to absorb, then dating for the case.

Preserving fresh cuts in a retail/shop cooler: vacuum-sealing or over-wrapping cuts, dating and labeling, blast-chilling or freezing sub-primals and trim, and rotating stock so product holds its shelf life.

Small butcher shop or custom/locker processor: curing and smoking a batch (bacon bellies, hams, snack sticks, jerky) - mixing and applying/injecting cure, resting, racking or hanging on smoke sticks and trolleys, loading the smokehouse, running the smoke/cook cycle to a target internal temperature, unloading and chilling.

Larger further-processing/deli operation supplying retail: brine-injecting and tumbling whole-muscle hams, turkey breast or corned beef, stuffing/netting, hanging on smoke sticks, running the automated smokehouse cook-and-smoke cycle, then chilling for slicing.

tasks.label: Use knives, cleavers, meat saws, bandsaws, or other equipment to perform meat cutting and trimming.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Poultry plant debone/cut-up station: worker at a moving line (cones, shackles or conveyor) uses knife/scissors to remove breast fillets, tenders and thigh/leg meat and trim fat, cartilage and bone bits at 30-40 pieces per minute, chilled wet floor, spec yields.

Beef/pork packing plant: breaking chilled carcasses and sides into primals with a powered saw or knife on the rail/fabrication line - splitting, quartering, rib scribing, loin/leg separation - with carcass weights and conformation varying widely piece to piece.

Beef/pork trim line: hand-trimming boneless primals and trimmings to spec on a conveyor - removing fat to a target lean point, seam-cutting, cutting out bruises, glands, bone chips and defects from irregular pieces arriving in random orientation.
Seafood plant: filleting and trimming fish (salmon, cod, catfish, tilapia) - heading, filleting, skinning, pinbone and belly-flap trimming, portioning to fixed weight on an in-line processing line.
Shellfish/specialty seafood: hand-picking blue crab meat, shucking, or hand-cutting oddly shaped species with a knife at a picking table, judging lump/claw grades by feel and sight.

Grocery/warehouse-club meat room: cutting boxed subprimals into retail steaks, chops, roasts and stew meat with knife and bandsaw, trimming fat to store spec, cutting whole birds and fish for the case, in small mixed batches through the day.

tasks.label: Weigh meats and tag containers for weight and contents.

tasks.label: Inspect meat products for defects, bruises or blemishes and remove them along with any excess fat.

instances.label: Poultry further-processing plant, deboning/trim line: worker inspects each breast fillet, tender, thigh or wing arriving on a belt or cone line and cuts out bruises, blood spots, bone and cartilage fragments and off-color meat, trims skin and excess fat, at roughly 30-40 pieces per minute in a chilled, wet room.

Beef or pork fabrication floor: worker at a boning/trim table or conveyor trims external fat to a specified thickness on subprimals and trimmings with a knife or Whizard trimmer and cuts away bruises, blood clots, bone dust/chips, glands and visible contamination before the piece is vacuum-packed or ground.

Standardized fat/rind trimming station in pork processing: loins presented one at a time to be derinded and fat-trimmed to a specified rind thickness, or pork bellies trimmed to shape/spec before bacon slicing; product is uniform and moves in a single stream.

Seafood plant fillet trimming line (salmon/trout, cod/pollock): worker at a trimming table removes belly flap and belly/back fat, dark membrane, remaining pin bones and surface blemishes (melanin spots, blood) from machine-filleted fillets to a defined trim grade.

Bench hand-trimming of irregular seafood (catfish fillets, tuna loins, crab sections, dressed whole fish): worker inspects for bruising, bloodline, parasites/blemishes and belly fat and removes them with a knife; product size and shape vary widely piece to piece.

Retail grocery meat/seafood department or butcher shop back room: worker at a cutting block trims fat and cuts blemishes, bruises and discolored areas from beef, pork, lamb, poultry and fish of many different cuts and species in small lots before cutting and traying product for the display case.

Grocery store or small wholesale butcher back room: worker breaks boxed subprimals into retail cuts, trims fat and silverskin, cuts chops/steaks and cuts up poultry and fish in small, mixed, frequently changing lots for tray packing and the service case.

instances.label: Poultry processing plant, cut-up/deboning line: worker takes graded parts (breast fillets, tenders, wings, drums) off the line and places them into the specified totes, trays or boxes by product code, with off-spec pieces and trim going to separate byproduct containers; cold, wet, high line speed.

Seafood processing plant: fillets and portions sorted by size/grade into pans, totes or waxed boxes, with frames, skins, roe and trim diverted to byproduct containers; boxes lidded/sealed and sent to icing or freezing.

Supermarket meat room, small butcher shop or custom-exempt plant: cut portions placed on foam trays or into vacuum bags, sealed on an over-wrapper/vacuum sealer and labeled; scraps and bones separated into grind and rendering containers; small batches, frequent product changes.

Meat plant floor bulk handling: fetch combos, totes, carts or pallets of primals/trim from the cooler or staging area and deliver them to cutting and trim stations, then take away filled containers of trimmed product to the next department.

Supermarket / warehouse-club meat department: go into the walk-in cooler, find and pull the specified boxed primal or case of poultry/pork from a mixed stack, carry it to the cutting room block, and distribute cut, wrapped product to the display case, to co-workers, or to a waiting customer's order.

Small independent butcher shop, custom locker or deer-processing plant: identify the individual customer's carcass, quarters or game animal on the cooler rail, bring it into the cutting room, and keep the cuts distributed to the right order for pickup.

Seafood processing plant or retail fish market: obtain the specified fish (species/size lot) from ice bins, totes or the chill room and distribute it to trimming/filleting stations or the retail counter.

instances.label: Large beef plant fabrication floor: worker at a moving conveyor/table knife-trims fat, sinew, bone dust, bruises and glands from beef subprimals (chuck rolls, rounds, plates, briskets) to spec and throws the lean pieces onto the trim belt feeding the hamburger program. Chilled (~40F); pieces vary in size, fat cover and defects; 10-20 s per piece.

Beef/pork trim line and grind room: worker works incoming boxed or belt-fed trim, picks out bone chips, cartilage, gristle and off-color pieces, sorts lean vs fat to hit chemical-lean targets (e.g. 50s/85s), and charges grinders/blenders that produce bulk hamburger meat into combos or chubs.

Pork plant boning/trimming station: worker debones and trims hams, picnics, butts and bellies, producing retail cuts plus lean and fat trimmings destined for ground pork/sausage batter; fixed conveyor or table station, powered or hand knife.

Poultry plant deboning/trim station: worker debones and trims breast fillets, thighs and drums on a cone or belt line, harvesting tenders and trim used for ground chicken, nuggets and patty meat; high line speed, standardized bird size.

Supermarket, warehouse-club or small butcher/custom shop meat room: worker trims chucks/rounds and accumulated case trim, runs it through a table grinder (often twice), mixes to fat target, forms patties or fills trays, weighs/labels, and breaks down and sanitizes the grinder between runs; small batches, frequent product changes.

tasks.label: Clean and salt hides.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large beef packing plant hide cellar/hide house: green cattle hides arrive from the hide puller by chute or conveyor; the worker pulls manure tags, scrapes/trims residual fat, flesh and loose meat from the flesh side, then the hide is washed and cured with salt (dry-salt pack or saturated brine) and folded/stacked on pallets for the tanner. High volume, chilled wet room, hides 25-40 kg each.

Small custom-exempt or local slaughterhouse / locker plant: a few beef hides per day; the worker spreads each hide hair-side down on a concrete floor or table, knifes off remaining flesh, fat and dirt, spreads coarse salt over the whole flesh side and rubs it into edges, neck and legs, then folds and stacks the hide in the curing area for the hide buyer.

Sheep/lamb pelts or hog skins at a small plant: pelts trimmed of tags and flesh, salted (spread with dry salt or tumbled in salt) and stacked/piled to cure before pickup; smaller, thinner, wool- or hair-on stock handled in batches.

Deer/game processing shop in hunting season: hunter-delivered, field-dressed hides in variable condition (dirt, burrs, blood, knife cuts, uneven skinning); the worker scrapes off meat and fat, salts the flesh side heavily and stacks hides on pallets or in barrels for a hide buyer; work is bursty and seasonal.

On-farm, mobile-slaughter or outdoor-shed hide handling: hide laid over a rack, pallet or barn floor as found, cleaned of manure and flesh with a knife, salted and stacked; no fixed layout, ambient weather and lighting.

sources.system: Smarthides salt spreading machine (salting line)
sources.title: salting machines - Smarthides
sources.claim: Smarthides (Machinefabriek Geurtsen) builds commercial salt-spreading machines for raw cattle hides: hides enter on an infeed belt, a salt head doses an adjustable amount of salt over each hide, and the salted hides are loaded onto a pallet, with excess salt automatically recovered and recirculated - the salting step done by machine in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: Conveyorised hide house line (hide washing machine, combination flesher/demanurer, brine curing raceways) - Union Hide Company, Modesto CA
sources.developer: Union Hide Company / hide-trade equipment builders
sources.date: 2012 page describing long-standing US practice (raceway cure used at UHC since 1963)
sources.title: Union Hide Company : Process
sources.claim: Industry description of modern packinghouse/hide-processor practice: whole-hide combination fleshing and demanuring machines and rotary-screen hide washing machines clean green hides, and conveyors move hides through washers, the flesher and into and out of the ... curing tanks, so cleaning and salt curing are performed by conveyor-linked machinery rather than by hand.

sources.system: Hide curing raceway (paddle brine vat)
sources.developer: hide industry equipment described in patent US5435808
sources.date: patent 1995, describing standard industry raceways in continuing use
sources.title: US5435808A - Hide raceway treatment and improved method of curing hides - Google Patents
sources.claim: The hide-curing raceway - an oval paddle brine vat used throughout the hide trade - both physically removes remaining fat and organic material from hides and cures them with salt in roughly 16-24 hours, i.e. one purpose-built machine performs the clean-and-salt function on green hides.

sources.system: SCE Hide Processor

sources.claim: MHM Automation (SCE) sells a commercial inclined-axis Hide Processor drum used on cattle hides, pigskins and woolly sheepskins that performs the wet operations from soaking through curing, with either dry salting or ..., under load-cell-based process control.
sources.transferJustification: Cited for sheep pelts, pigskins and (by transfer) deer hides: the machine is specified for woolly sheepskins and pigskins, the same class of floppy hair-on raw skins as deer hides, cleaned by soaking/tumbling and preserved by the identical dry-salt or brine cure.
